_meta.source: Anchoring research workflow: round 0 (8 lenses), round 1 gap research (7 lenses) and round 2 gap research (G0 orphaned files, G7 chart-conditioned Epēshu, G8 seam clip, G9 era sheets), static analysis of the HEAD export and fetched primary sources, two independent verifier checks per item. No browser was run.
_meta.key_distinction: REGISTRATION (where art or geometry sits relative to the atlas coast, rivers, roads and ring-dots) fixes misalignment. The RENDERING MEDIUM (raster vs vector) brings crispness past the stretched image, interactivity and shared road vertices. A vector city placed through the same cityBox misaligns exactly as the raster does.
_meta.status_rule: survived = 2/2 checks held; disputed = 1/2; refuted = 0/2. Only survived and disputed items are findings (finding:true). Where a check corrected an item, the section summaries carry the corrected text.
_meta.id_rule: Item ids are '<lens-prefix>:<raw id>' because raw ids collide across lenses (several C1s). Prefixes: shift, ties, canon, sim, reg, vlod, vec, refs, own-atlas, own-sim, gap-anchor, gap-coasts, gap-print, gap-consumers, gap-mobile, gap-vecbudget, gap-refs, gap-G0, gap-G7, gap-G8, gap-G9. The dossier cites the round-2 items bare (G0-1, G7-9, G8-4, G9-2). Round-2 ids are normalised to their G<n>-<m> stem because sections supplied some in long form (e.g. G7-3-feature-budget, G9-1-era-sheets-are-recoloured-copies); raw_ids keeps every form.
_meta.counts_rule: counts are over unique items; an item cited by several sections is counted once. Per-section row tallies are in rows_by_section.
_meta.prior_record_rule: items[].prior_record is the full earlier record (proposer text, mechanism, magnitude, fix, evidence, verifier votes and texts) for the 299 round-0/round-1 items and the 2 tie sets. The 53 round-2 items (G0, G7, G8, G9) exist only as their section summaries. items[].summaries holds per-section summaries where the sections worded an item differently.
_meta.shift_major_rule: shift source with status survived or disputed and at least one major severity vote (computed, section 1.1)

section_headlines.1-shift: The owner's 'things shift' comes mostly from fixed registration errors that zoom magnifies: anchors sitting on labels (45 move / 2 keep / 4 owner calls over 138), the Summarch literal, the Hordon/Maeges duplicate, two canon charts placed by a footprint box, a two-sided Epēshu seam, and unregistered gates, sea sides and rivers in the generated plans. Unrequested lifecycle motion (maxZoom ease-down, catchment pops, hot-swaps, ensureArrival teleports) and presentation timing add to it. Only svg-css-scale-bloom and gen-jank-frame-drops depend on the rendering medium, so a vector city placed through the same cityBox would misalign exactly as the raster does.
section_headlines.2-registration: City art drifts on zoom for one reason: a fixed, unfitted cityBox placement (anchor dot plus a FOOT_R class size) that 2^(z-4) magnifies, not drift in the medium. The fix is registration: re-snap 45 anchors to their printed rings, move Summarch 20 px onto its ring, give Epēshu a policy-chosen translate+scale override that all five placement consumers read, and ship it with a stored print-land clip and a sea fill. A vector city placed through the same box misaligns exactly as the raster does.
section_headlines.3-vector: Every vector precedent already in the repo (the shipped Sun Road polyline, the chart-conditioned Epēshu prototype, the genCityCanvas plan) misaligns exactly like the raster when placed through cityBox, so registration (anchors, a per-city translate+scale record, a print-derived seam clip and sea fill) ships first and medium-blind, and the vector city is a later, owner-gated medium upgrade (crispness on phones from z8.3, hit geometry, shared vertices) with a measured budget: skeleton trace ~24 KB gzip fits, full-building Epēshu (177k vertices) or the seeded prototype (29k vertices, ~1.2 s build) needs LOD and phone timing.
section_headlines.4-references: Every reference we could read stays anchored on zoom because its detail is registered into one frame. The atlas already has that frame (CRS.Simple atlas px at NZ=4), but cityBox places canon city art by kind rather than by what the art shows. The fix is a stored per-city transform that every consumer reads; changing the rendering medium does not fix it, and even the best policy placement for Epēshu (0.6x+3E) leaves about 3.6 atlas px rms of coast misfit in both directions.
section_headlines.5-ownership: Nobody owns registration of city art today. The evidence supports a standalone atlas registration item: one per-city record read by bounds, POIs, wash, cap and fly target, reaching Filigree 2 through a README §7 row and landing after Mobile 9/14 and before Filigree 3. The vector city comes later as a separate item, and the sim stays out of the first cut.

_meta.dedup_rule: owner_questions, measure_probes and open_questions are deduplicated from the section lists; each entry names the raw indices it merges, and the verbatim section lists are kept in *_raw.
_meta.probe_rule: Probes run in a later session after Mobile 5 lands, on a HEAD copy served by the probing session's own server on a port other than 8544; never tools/mobile-capture.js, never beside a mobile capture.

items.summary: REGISTRATION (data): 39 city anchors (37 in city-anchors.json plus the Summarch and Penthelon literals in meshedWorldInit) sit more than 5 atlas px from their printed ring-dot marker, mostly on their own label text (overall median 1.0, p90 35.4, off-dot median 26.4, max 112.8), and cityBox, washMake, sampleCityMask, cityApproaches, nearestCity, buildWorldPOIs and the flyIntoCity target all centre on that anchor, so the plan lands off its dot whatever the rendering medium.

votes.corrected:
REGISTRATION, confirmed against the HEAD export, with a few corrections.

The code path is as claimed. In maps-site/index.html everything below is centred on CITY_ANCHORS[k].atlasX/atlasY:
- cityBox(a,w,h) gives a box centred on the anchor. The overlay bounds, worldPOICoord and buildWorldPOIs all go through it.
- sampleCityMask takes a window centred on the anchor, ox=(atlasX-1.35*rW)*2.
- cityApproaches uses segCircleHits around the anchor with radius 2.5*footR.
- nearestCity picks the closest anchor and accepts it only within 3*footR. worldCityUpdate uses it. Above z6.5 it runs ensureCityGen/ensureCityOverlay; overlayOpacity is above 0 from z6.8. With no near city, setMaxZoom(Z_OPEN_MAX=8) caps the zoom.
- flyIntoCity flies to dest=px(a.atlasX,a.atlasY). #chart= and Descend both go through it.

The clickable glyph is built in buildMarkers at px(m.x,m.y), and flyToMarker uses m._mk.getLatLng(), so both use the maps_markers.json position. tools/build-gazetteer.js adds markers first and uses an anchor only when no marker has that name. The tier-d CSS hides the marker panes from Z_TIER_D=7.5.

Numbers I measured (name-folded match to Settlements markers, plus the two hard-coded overrides):
- 39 anchors are more than 5 px from their marker.
- Median 1.0 px, p90 35.4 px.
- Damoklir 69.1, Paga 68.6, Pontoron 67.5, Zhomphek 64.5, Philider 58.0, Permūr 53.0, Līrider 42.7, Hordon 42.7, Dargan 42.4, Lek Zagrok 38.3, Drāmūz 36.3, Penthelon 112.8, Summarch 19.9.

What z5 tile crops show:
- Anchor sits on its own label with the marker on the ring-dot: Damoklir, Pontoron, Zhomphek, Philider, Ion Ephel, Clickerhall-by-Goblin-Hole, Cyrikon, Sūl, Hemdok Laego, Aldrakhar, Gel.
- Drāmūz is the reverse case: the anchor is on the dot and the marker is in the sea.
- Sokundo, Kanae, Tamaron and Lepon the Old have anchors about 6-8 px off their dots.
- Shengo's anchor sits on the 'O' of a region label.
- Kolens and Sjefenhold have anchor equal to marker (0 px), and both points are on blank parchment. This is a separate no-dot issue, not an offset.

Corrections:
(a) Tamaron is not marker-less. It has a Settlements marker (minor, mag) at 1659,1556 on the dot, 7.8 px from the anchor. Lepon the Old also has a marker, named 'Lepon', at 1145,1427 on the dot, 7.0 px away. Only Sokundo, Kanae and Shengo truly lack a same-name marker.
(b) Paga's anchor sits on the neighbour's label ('…thelon' of Penthelon), not its own. Paga's marker is also off the dot: it sits on the 'P' of the Paga label, about 15 px from the ring-dot. So 'markers sit on the dots' has two exceptions, Drāmūz and Paga.
(c) Penthelon is not justified. Its anchor is hard-coded in meshedWorldInit at 1962,644, with a comment saying the wiki marker 'floats in the lake'. The tiles show the marker at 1942,755 sitting exactly on the Penthelon ring-dot on the Five Fingers shore. The anchor is 112.8 px north in open ground and water. Penthelon should move to the marker, not be kept with an offDot reason.
(d) Summarch (523,58) is also hard-coded in meshedWorldInit. It sits on the coastline 19.9 px west of its dot (542,52). Fixing Summarch and Penthelon therefore needs a code edit in meshedWorldInit (not a pinned function); a data-only change cannot fix them.
(e) Hordon's anchor (1139,1730) is identical to Maeges' anchor and sits on the Maeges dot, 42.7 px from Hordon's own dot. That is more than 3*14=42, so a view centred on Hordon's dot is uncharted. On the exact tie, nearestCity's strict d<bd keeps whichever key comes first: Hordon, at line 213 versus Maeges at line 1050. So the Maeges dot shows Hordon's harbour-town plan, and zooming never selects Maeges. This is already queued as filigree R21.
(f) Settlements whose dot lies outside their own catchment (more than 3*FOOT_R) number 17, not 16: 15 villages including Penthelon, plus Ion Ephel (ruin, 31.3 > 24) and Hordon (town, 42.7 > 42).

Magnitude on screen: anchor-to-marker distance x9.85 at z7.3 (2^3.3) gives about 77-681 px, or 1111 px for Penthelon. At a village's cityMaxZ of 10.83 (GEN_SIZE 2048 over 18) the factor is x113.8.

Fix: snap atlasX/atlasY to the ring-dot.
- Use the marker x,y where the marker is on the dot.
- Hand-measure Paga, Sokundo, Kanae, Shengo and Hordon on z5 tiles.
- Leave Drāmūz's anchor where it is and fix its marker instead.
- Edit the meshedWorldInit overrides for Summarch and Penthelon.
- Add a lint for anchor-to-marker offsets over 3 px.

Rendering vector instead of raster does not fix this: a vector city placed through cityBox would misalign the same way.
votes.reason: The code path exists and runs exactly as stated. On these offsets, cityBox, sampleCityMask, cityApproaches, nearestCity, buildWorldPOIs and flyIntoCity all centre on the anchor, while the marker glyph, flyToMarker and the gazetteer use the marker x,y. I recomputed the distances from city-anchors.json against maps_markers.json and got 39 over 5 px, median 1.0 and p90 35.4, matching the claim. Crops of the z5 tiles confirm that anchors sit on their labels and markers on the dots for 11 sampled cities, plus Drāmūz as the reverse case. The claim is partly wrong in five places. VECTOR_INDEPENDENT: true. This is registration. cityBox, washMake, sampleCityMask (window centred at atlasX-1.35*rW), nearestCity and flyIntoCity (dest = px(a.atlasX, a.atlasY)) all key on the anchor, so a vector plan placed through the same anchor would land in the same wrong place. These values are measured from the old point, so moving only x,y leaves the harbor water misplaced. Fixing Summarch, or recording Penthelon's offDot reason, means editing that file (not a pinned function, but it is the mid-flight Mobile lane's file). votes.corrected: REGISTRATION (not a rendering-medium issue; a vector city placed through the same anchor would miss the same way). In maps-site/index.html, meshedWorldInit hard-codes CITY_ANCHORS['Summarch']={atlasX:523,atlasY:58,kind:'town',harbor:false,sea:null} under the comment "two extra anchors sourced from maps_markers (spec §A.2)". The comment is wrong. maps_markers.json (and gazetteer.json) put Summarch at (542,52). The literal (523,58) is the party-route.json first-visit 'Summarch' point, whose note is the Hagar/Hooded Man note and is NOT marked 'Approximate' (the 'Approximate' notes are on the East-West Road entry and the second Summarch visit at 545,80). It is also the factions.json Allhammers seat {x:523,y:58}. city-anchors.json has no Summarch entry and nothing mutates the anchor later. cityBox (town FOOT_R 14, image 3072x2859, so hw 14 and hh 13.03) gives an overlay box of x 509-537, y 45.0-71.0. ensureCityOverlay uses exactly that box for the L.imageOverlay, buildWorldPOIs/worldPOICoord project the 9 chart POIs through it, and washMake centres the radial wash on (523,58). On the z5 tiles the printed double ring has its centroid at about (541.5, 49.8), with the outer ring spanning x about 537-546. So the whole ring sits outside the box, tangent to its east edge, with the centre about 4.5 px past it. The box is instead centred on the solid black line (a river by the cartographic key) at x about 523-531, just west of the ring, with the dotted road running south from the ring. Offsets: 19.9 atlas px from the marker and about 20.2 px from the ring centroid, about 1.42 footprint radii. On screen that is about 197 px at z7.3, about 318 px at z8, and about 1546 px at the fly target 10.28 (cityMaxZ 10.78 minus 0.5, x77.7). When it fires: worldCityUpdate at z>6.5 while Summarch is nearest (nearestCity threshold is 42 px, so a reader centred on the real dot still gets Summarch), through the 6.8-7.8 crossfade and deeper; also flyIntoCity via #chart=Summarch (handleHash, then isFlyInCity) or the 'Descend into' button, with dest=px(523,58). What the reader sees: during the crossfade the ring stays visible just east of the chart. At depth (base 0.12) the dot lies under the wash fringe, about 32% alpha at a normalised radius of about 0.86, so a reader zoomed on the dot sees faint washed parchment beside the chart's east edge. Cheap fix: set the anchor to the dot ({atlasX:542,atlasY:52}, or the measured ring at about 541.5,50), ideally by moving Summarch into city-anchors.json and deleting the hard-code.
votes.reason: Verified in maps-site/index.html (HEAD export): meshedWorldInit has the literal and the misleading 'sourced from maps_markers' comment. cityBox, ensureCityOverlay (imageOverlay bounds), buildWorldPOIs/worldPOICoord, washMake, nearestCity (3*footR = 42 px), worldCityUpdate (z>6.5), flyIntoCity (dest px(a.atlasX,a.atlasY), target cityMaxZ-0.5 = 10.28) and handleHash (#chart then flyIntoCity) all behave as the claim says. No other code writes CITY_ANCHORS['Summarch'], and city-anchors.json lacks Summarch. maps_markers.json and gazetteer.json have Summarch at (542,52). party-route.json's (523,58) Summarch entry matches the literal, as does the factions.json seat. chart-pois.json has 9 Summarch POIs. I sampled the z5 tiles (tile floor(2x/256)): the ring centroid is (541.5, 49.8) and the ring spans x about 537-546, so it lies fully outside the box (x1 = 537). Corrections to the claim: (1) the (523,58) party-route point is not marked 'Approximate'; (2) the ring-centre offset is about 20.2 px, not about 18, and z8 is about 318 screen px, not 290; (3) the solid line under the box is a river by the cartographic key, so the 'over the coast and hatched realm' wording and the 'water IoU 0.01' figure were not independently verified; (4) the whole double ring sits outside the box rather than 'peeking out', and at depth it is half-hidden under the wash fringe (about 32% alpha over base 0.12). None of these change the verdict. The chart and its POIs sit about 20 atlas px (1.4 footprint radii) west of the town, which is plainly visible at the table: major.

votes.corrected:
The claim is right up to the post-landing yank. It leaves out ensureArrival, which changes the end state.

Data: city-anchors.json has Hordon {1139,1730,town,harbor:true} at key index 22 and Maeges {1139,1730,village,prov:trace} at index 127. They are the only duplicate pair among the 136 anchors. Hordon's own mag marker in maps_markers.json and gazetteer.json is at (1124,1690), 42.7 atlas px NW. Maeges' marker is at (1139,1731).

Selection: nearestCity (maps-site/index.html) uses a strict `if(d<bd)` in insertion order. The two anchors are always the same distance from any centre, so Hordon wins every time. worldCityUpdate, which runs on 'zoomend moveend', never selects Maeges: not for generation at z>6.5, not for the pre-warm at z>5.6 within 6x14=84 px, not for maxZoom, and not for the overlay.

Cold #chart=Maeges link (handleHash -> isFlyInCity -> flyIntoCity; ATLAS.descend and the 'Descend into' button take the same path):
1. ensureCityGenNow('Maeges') registers the village plan synchronously (GEN_SIZE 2048).
2. setMaxZoom(cityMaxZ = 4+log2(2048/18) = 10.83), ensureCityOverlay('Maeges'), then flyTo(dest, 10.33, 1.4 s).
3. At landing, zoomend/moveend call worldCityUpdate, which picks Hordon. CITYREG['Hordon'] is null because sampleCityMask waits on Image onload, so it is async. allowed is therefore Z_OPEN_MAX = 8.
4. Leaflet's setMaxZoom calls setZoom(8), which animates because dz 2.33 is under zoomAnimationThreshold 4 (about x5.0). ensureCityOverlay(null) removes Maeges' plan at once.
5. When Hordon's mask lands: genCityCanvas -> registerCityOverlay -> worldCityUpdate raises maxZoom to 10.19 and shows Hordon's town plan (r 14, x1.56 box) centred on Maeges' dot.
6. About 1700 ms after flyIntoCity, ensureArrival sees getZoom() 8 < target-0.5 = 9.83. It calls setView(dest, 10.33, {animate:false}), which _limitZoom clamps to the current maxZoom. If Hordon has registered by then, the map snaps back in to 10.19 on Hordon's plan, with no animation. If not, the clamp holds it at 8 and it retries at about 3.4 s and 5.1 s.

So the reader does not stay zoomed out. The sequence is: arrive on Maeges, yank out to 8, then snap back in to about 10.19 on the wrong town's plan.

Warm branch (Hordon already registered, the usual case when 'Descend into Maeges' is clicked from a card nearby, because the z>5.6 pre-warm and the z>6.5 generation both target Hordon): at landing the plan swaps to Hordon's with a small eased zoom from 10.33 to 10.19. ensureArrival then sees 10.19 >= 9.83 and does nothing more.

Either way a Maeges link ends on Hordon's plan, 42.7 atlas px from Hordon's dot. That is about 421 screen px at z7.3, 683 at z8 and about 3.1k at z10.19.

Cheap fix as claimed: move Hordon's anchor to its own dot, (1124,1690) or the corrected marker. Optionally, flyIntoCity could pin the destination key so nearestCity/worldCityUpdate prefer it after landing. That is pure logic and keeps determinism. The fix is the same for a vector city: registration, not the rendering medium.

- vector_independent=true is correct. A vector city that goes through the same `cityBox` gets the same centre-plus-uniform-scale placement, so registration is the fix and the medium is not.

CHEAP FIX, corrected:
(1) `washMake` does NOT fully follow a fitted `cityBox`. Its bounds are px(a.atlasX±box.hw*1.7, a.atlasY±box.hh*1.7). It reads only hw/hh from `cityBox` and centres on the anchor dot, not on the box centre. A fit with scale 0.80 therefore shrinks the wash, but the fit's (+4,+4) shift and the rotation do not move it. Fixing that means editing `washMake`, which UG3 forbids ("the diff touches none of ... washMake"). The options are:
- accept a wash that is off-centre by about 4 atlas px (it is a 1.7x soft radial, so this is tolerable);
- have `cityBox` return a box centred on the fitted cx,cy while the anchor dot stays where it is (this still leaves the wash on the dot);
- move the anchor itself (a.atlasX/Y in city-anchors.json), which is the separate anchor fix.
State this. Do not claim the wash follows.
(2) `cityMaxZ` and the flyIntoCity `dest` do not call `cityBox`. `cityMaxZ` uses footR directly, so a 0.80 fit puts the "1 image px ≈ 1 screen px" zoom off by log2(1/0.8)=0.32. Have `cityMaxZ` read the fit scale; it is not pinned. `dest` stays at the anchor dot. The calls that DO go through `cityBox` are `worldPOICoord`, `buildWorldPOIs`, `ensureCityOverlay` and `washMake` (half-size only).
(3) Rotation through a pre-rotated canvas changes w and h to the rotated bounding box (about 3100x3300 at -5 deg). `cityBox` and the POI transform then need the pre-rotation size plus the rotation, or the POIs drift.
`registerCityOverlay` with a canvas re-encodes it through toDataURL (webp/png). That creates a second multi-MB copy of the DM art and a large decode/encode on mobile, which contradicts "do not duplicate the 2.1 MB overlay". The safer route is an offline pre-rotated or warped JPG with provenance kept, or putting the translate/scale fit only in bounds and leaving rotation to the warp stage.
(4) The rest is correct:
- Fit data is canon-only, with fall-back to the footprint box, so genCityCanvas, sampleCityMask, cityCanvasSha and the procedural cities are untouched. sampleCityMask uses footR, not `cityBox`.
- `washMake` source is unchanged, so its UG3 atlas_fn_sha stays unchanged.
- Fit data is static JSON, so determinism is not at stake.
- Desktop and mobile baselines for Epēshu and Summarch change and need declaring. Mobile lane 5-9 is mid-flight in maps-site/index.html, so the edit to `cityBox` and `cityMaxZ` must be sequenced after it or declared in its unit.
- The order is: anchor fix, then this registration, then edge feathering.

items.summary: Rendering that makes REGISTRATION errors read as motion: between z7.1 and about 7.59 both the base (>=0.32) and the overlay (>=0.30) are visible, so any art offset appears as a slide of offset x 2^(z-4) screen px; only the canon charts show a second coast, because procedural coasts come from the atlas mask.

prior_record.title: Crossfade band draws the atlas and the art at once, so every registration error reads as motion
prior_record.anchor: baseOpacity(z) (1 to 0.12 over z6.2-8) / overlayOpacity(z) (0 to 1 over 6.8-7.8) / worldOpacityUpdate; washMake f=1.7 radial wash in pCityWash
prior_record.mechanism: Working as intended; RENDERING that amplifies every REGISTRATION error. Between z7.1 and 7.6 the base is >=0.32 and the overlay >=0.3 (z7.3: base 0.46, overlay 0.5), so two coastlines and two road networks show together and their relative weight changes with zoom. Outside the box the 1.7x wash fades to 0 at its rim and beyond it the 0.12 base ghost continues with its own coast and roads; the canon JPG has a hard rectangular edge. Pure scale is anchored correctly; it is the content that differs.
prior_record.fires_when: Every descent or ascent through z6.8-7.8 near an anchored city, and at the box/wash edge at deep zoom.
prior_record.visible_effect: The coast, roads and town 'slide' from the atlas position to the art position as you zoom (the owner's 'things shift'); at the box edge the art stops and the ghost continues offset.
prior_record.magnitude: Both layers >=30% visible across dz ~0.5 (z7.1-7.6). Perceived shift = registration offset x 2^(z-4): Epēshu coast mean 6.1 px = 60 screen px at z7.3 (113-200 px by the other measurement); a label-anchored village (26 px median) = 256 px.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Fix registration first (anchor-on-label, canon-art-fit-by-box). The ramp itself can be narrowed to ~0.4 zoom or made complementary so overlay+base contrast stays constant, but that only hides the error; optionally feather the canon edge.
prior_record.fix_risks: Ramp constants are look-owned by the filigree (R3 painted city on the overlay ramp) and living-chart tracks; baseOpacity/overlayOpacity are not UG3-pinned, washMake is. Desktop visual identity changes.

votes.corrected:
Mechanism confirmed in maps-site/index.html, with five corrections. It is working as intended: RENDERING that turns every REGISTRATION error into apparent motion. The constants match the claim: baseOpacity(z) = 1 → 0.12 linearly over z6.2–8, and overlayOpacity(z) = z − 6.8, clamped to 0..1 over z6.8–7.8. worldOpacityUpdate runs on 'zoom zoomend moveend' and applies baseOpacity to curBase and overlayOpacity to both CITYVIEW.overlay (pane pCity, z450) and CITYVIEW.wash (pane pCityWash, z449). washMake builds a radial-gradient imageOverlay over cityBox × f=1.7, centred on atlasX/atlasY. Its alpha is .94 out to r=.5, .5 at r=.78 and 0 at r=1, so at the box edge (r≈.59) it is about .80. Pure scale is anchored correctly, because Leaflet's ImageOverlay is bounds-pinned. What differs is the content inside cityBox.

(1) The two in-box layers are never both strong across z7.1–7.6. The wash sits under the art, rides the same ramp and covers the base, so inside the box the base's effective weight is b·(1−a)·(1−0.94a), not b. Values: z6.9 ≈ .54 base vs .10 art; z7.0 ≈ .40 vs .20; z7.1 ≈ .28 vs .30 (equal weight); z7.2 ≈ .19 vs .40; z7.3 ≈ .12 vs .50 (not .46); z7.4 ≈ .07; z7.6 ≈ .02. So the true in-box double image is about z6.9–7.3, a span of about 0.4 zoom. The raw-opacity statement 'both ≥30% over z7.1–7.6' holds only in the wash ring outside the art, where the wash falls from .5 to 0, and beyond the wash rim, where the base continues alone at its ramp value and settles at a 0.12 ghost by z8.

(2) There is a third registration in the band, and it pops off at z7.5. Atlas settlement and region markers and labels (TYPE_STYLE 'Settlements' → pSettle 624, pMajor 620, pMinor 626, plus pWater 618) sit ABOVE pCity at full opacity over the half-transparent art. They are removed only by `.map-tier-d … {opacity:0!important}` at Z_TIER_D=7.5, and those panes have no transition. The printed town dot and label therefore sit over the art's own town until z7.5 and then vanish instantly. This is the most visible 'two towns' cue for label-anchored cities. pWay (414) and pRouteLine (415) sit under the wash and fade with the base.

(3) The hard rectangular edge applies to canon art only, namely art/overlay-*.jpg (opaque JPG). registerCityOverlay exports procedural canvases as webp/png 'to keep the vignette's alpha', so generated plans have feathered edges.

(4) Corrected fires_when. worldCityUpdate runs only on zoomend/moveend. It tests nearestCity against the map CENTRE (dist ≤ 3·footR) and calls ensureCityOverlay only when z > 6.5. The crossfade therefore fires when the view centre is near an anchor, not whenever a city is merely on screen. A single pinch or zoom gesture carrying z ≤ 6.5 straight past 7.8 shows no art crossfade at all: the overlay is created at release at its ramp value (a pop), while the base fade still rides 'zoom'. Wheel steps each end in zoomend, so they do crossfade, but stepwise. In Leaflet 1.9, _animateZoom calls _move at animation start, so getZoom() returns the target and opacity jumps per step. The `.leaflet-pCity-pane{transition:opacity .25s}` rule does not smooth this, because setOpacity writes the img or tile-container element, not the pane. flyIntoCity calls ensureCityOverlay eagerly before the flyTo, so flies do get the continuous crossfade.

(5) The perceived offset in screen pixels is the registration offset in atlas pixels × 2^(z−4) (NZ=4). The figures 6.1 → ~52–60 screen px at z7.1–7.3 and 26 → ~224–256 px are arithmetically right, but the 6.1 px and 26 px inputs come from other findings and were not re-measured here.

vector_independent=true stands: a vector city placed through the same cityBox crossfades over the same misregistered content. Cheap fix: fix registration first. Then narrow or make complementary the a/b ramps, ideally deriving the in-box base weight from the wash, and fade pSettle/pMajor/pMinor across the band instead of the 7.5 pop. Either change only hides the error. Optionally feather the canon JPG edge. Fix risks are as stated: washMake is UG3-pinned, baseOpacity/overlayOpacity are not, and the ramp and tier-d look belong to the filigree and living-chart tracks.

The mechanism holds. The magnitude and the fix need correcting.

RAMPS (recomputed from maps-site/index.html, function baseOpacity and function overlayOpacity). Base = 1 - (z-6.2)/1.8*0.88. Overlay = z-6.8. At z7.1: base 0.56, overlay 0.30. At z7.3: base 0.462, overlay 0.50. At z7.6: base 0.316, overlay 0.80. Base stays >=0.32 until z~7.59, so both layers are >=30% from z7.1 to z~7.59 (dz~0.49). This matches the claim. The wash (washMake, f=1.7) also rides overlayOpacity. Its gradient is .94 out to 0.5 of its radius (0.85 hw), .5 at 0.78 (1.33 hw) and 0 at the rim (1.7 hw), so box corners near 1.41 hw get less than half a mat. In the same band, Z_TIER_D=7.5 (map-tier-d) hard-hides the vector ways, settlements and water. So the double image is raster atlas vs art, and the vector ink pops at 7.5. It is a cross-dissolve: two fixed ghosts whose weights trade, not a continuous slide. Separation on screen = registration offset (atlas px) x 2^(z-4) (x9.85 at z7.3).

MAGNITUDE corrections:
(a) "Two coastlines" applies only to the canon charts (Epēshu, Summarch). A procedural plan's land/water comes from sampleCityMask, which reads the same z5 tiles around the same anchor. Its coast is co-registered with the atlas, up to mask resolution. For procedural cities the visible double is the printed ring-dot, label and roads against the plan's centre and streets: stub gap median 3.8, max 14.5 atlas px, so ~37-143 px at z7.3.
(b) "Epēshu coast mean 6.1 px" was not reproduced (the canon-registration finding: coast residual 6.1/16.8 and the similarity fit not reproduced). What is reproduced: water IoU 0.36, 26% of the box disagreeing, a coast tilt difference of ~25 deg, and road exits ~7 atlas px apart (~69 px at z7.3). Quote those, not 60 px or the unsourced "113-200 px".
(c) "26 px" is the median of the 39 anchors more than 5 px from their same-name markers (range 7.8-69.1). It is not a village median. Corrected: 77-681 screen px at z7.3, median ~256, and only for those off-dot anchors (most anchors are within 1 px).

vector_independent = true holds. A vector city placed through cityBox ghosts against the raster base exactly as the raster art does.

CHEAP FIX corrections:
- Registration first is right.
- Re-anchoring on the label/marker moves a.atlasX/Y. That changes the region sampleCityMask reads and so the genCityCanvas output. cityCanvasSha hashes Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae, and Tamaron is a 7.8 px off-dot anchor, so moving it breaks UG3 cityCanvasSha vs B0. It must be a declared, owner-approved re-baseline, or exclude the pinned trio, and it is not "free".
- Ramp edits (narrowing the band, or a complementary base = 1 - overlay) touch only baseOpacity/overlayOpacity, which are unpinned. washMake's source hash is unchanged because it calls overlayOpacity by name. Determinism is unaffected. But a complementary ramp still gives 50/50 at the midpoint, so it does not remove the double image. Only shortening the overlap shrinks it, and either way it only hides the error.
- Feathering the canon edge must be done on the JPG or with a CSS mask on the overlay element. Doing it inside washMake (or genCityCanvas) breaks the UG3 atlas_fn_sha pin.
- Every one of these edits lands in maps-site/index.html while the mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) is mid-flight there. It changes desktop identity, and the look is owned by filigree (slice C, the painted city on the overlay ramp) and living-chart (zoom-through). Schedule it after the lane, not as a drive-by.

The mechanism is real and fires as described. In maps-site/index.html, the map options set zoomSnap:0, zoomDelta:.25, wheelPxPerZoomLevel:80 and wheelDebounceTime:20, and then map.scrollWheelZoom.disable() is called. So the wheel knobs do nothing, and zoomDelta matters only to the +/- buttons and keyboard. The IIFE's mc.addEventListener('wheel',...,{passive:false}) works like this:
- deltaMode 1 multiplies the deltas by 33, and deltaMode 2 multiplies them by the viewport height.
- wheelish = deltaMode!==0 || (dx===0 && |dy|>=60 && Number.isInteger(dy)). A non-ctrl, non-wheelish event goes to panBy and does not zoom.
- Otherwise k = ctrlKey ? 0.018 : 0.0045, step = clamp(-dy*k, -1, 1), and the target is clamped to the live getMinZoom/getMaxZoom.
- It then calls map.setZoomAround(cursorLatLng, target, {animate:false}).

The vendored leaflet@1.9.4 confirms the rest:
- setZoomAround passes {zoom:{animate:false}} to setView. setView calls _stop() and then _tryAnimatedZoom, which returns false because animate===false, so the result is _resetView.
- _resetView runs _moveStart, then _move (fires 'zoom' and 'move'), then _moveEnd (fires 'zoomend' and 'moveend').
- So every wheel event is one instant rescale, with no CSS transition. 'zoom' drives worldOpacityUpdate and updScale; 'zoomend' and 'moveend' drive worldCityUpdate (ensureCityGen, setMaxZoom, ensureCityOverlay), updTier and the #view hash write.
- The zoomSnap save/restore around setZoomAround does nothing, because zoomSnap is already 0 and _limitZoom rounds only when the snap value is truthy.

Magnitudes:
- One 100-px or 3-line notch gives dz 0.45 (x1.366). baseOpacity steps about 0.22 per notch and overlayOpacity about 0.45, so the 6.8-7.8 crossfade takes about 2.2 notches.
- A ctrl-wheel event with |dy| >= 56 saturates at dz 1 (x2). Mac pinch deltas of roughly 1-10 give dz 0.02-0.18 per event, which looks near-continuous.

Corrections and additions to the claim:
1. The atlas has no custom pinch handler. "As the pinch handler does" can only mean Leaflet's built-in TouchZoom, which calls map._move(..., {pinch:true, round:false}) every rAF frame and _animateZoom or _resetView at the end. That is the pattern to copy.
2. Anchoring to the cursor is exact except near the frame edge. setView runs _limitCenter against maxBounds (viscosity 1.0), which can push the centre off the cursor-anchored point.
3. Side effects of setView: its _stop() cancels a running flyTo (flyIntoCity), and ensureArrival then hard-lands the view about 1.7 s later. While setMaxZoom's "ease down" (an animated setZoom) is running, _animatingZoom makes _tryAnimatedZoom return true, so wheel events in that window are silently swallowed.

None of this changes registration. Overlay, base and wash stay locked to the cursor and to cityBox; only the scale, crossfade and city-swap cadence move in steps. Vector-independent: a vector city would step the same way.

When the tiles' onload finishes, the ensureCityGen callback sees reg.prov==='invented' and reruns genCityCanvas with the mask. registerCityOverlay then calls overlayCache.delete(key) and, because CITYVIEW.name===key, runs ensureCityOverlay(key) to hot-swap. That removes the old imageOverlay and adds a new data-URL overlay, plus a new wash. Leaflet does not crossfade, so for a moment there is no plan while the new image decodes.

With the mask, the plan changes in these ways:
- For drawWater cities, MK=mask when mask.water is true, so inWater uses wAt (the atlas coast) instead of the compass half-plane at shoreDist. The inWater/inLand-gated `continue`s skip later R() draws (fields, buildings, quays, the waterfront node, POIs), so everything after the first differing gate reshuffles.
- For the three side-less harbours (Hordon, Ion Ephel and Penthelon; Penthelon is defined in meshedWorldInit/traits), pick(COMPASS) is drawn in both runs. sv becomes mask.bear only when mask.water and mask.bear are set, and cx/cy move by 0.07*S*|sv_rand-bear| image px. In atlas px that is 0.07*2r*|Δ|, at most 0.14*2r: 3.9 for Hordon (town), 2.2 for Ion Ephel (ruin), 2.5 for Penthelon (village, unverified because whether its patch has mask.water was not checked).
- For non-drawWater cities, only LT changes GREEN and the wash tone; the layout is identical because the river RD does not depend on the mask.
- Epēshu and Summarch are canon, so ensureCityGenNow returns early and the callback skips them.
- In total there are 16 generated drawWater cities in the data. A coast actually moves only where the sampled patch has mask.water.

When it fires (corrected):
- The trigger is not a cold HTTP cache. Image onload is always asynchronous, so the synthetic plan registers first whenever MASKQ[key] has not been sampled in this page session. That covers a fresh-load #chart=City deep link (handleHash runs after meshedWorldInit), the Descend button and ATLAS.descend, with a warm cache or not.
- It does not fire if CITYREG[key] already exists: a prior visit, or the z>5.6 prewarm within 6 footprint radii.

When it is visible (corrected):
- overlayOpacity is 0 below z6.8. A simulation of Leaflet's flyTo from a world view (z≈2.7 to cz-0.5) crosses z6.8 at about 630–700 ms of the 1.4 s fly. A mask landing before that swaps invisibly, so on fast links there is usually no visible coast or street jump. The jump shows mid-fly or after arrival only on slow tiles, or when the fly starts from mid-zoom.
- The POI mis-centring happens whenever the swap happens, whatever the timing. dest and ensureArrival's setView(dest) keep the synthetic coordinate, and the moveend handler opens the POI panel there, so the camera rests off the melded roundel. At the fly target cz-0.5 (town ≈9.69), a move of up to 28 atlas px is about 1.45k screen px, not 2.0k at 10.19.

A further artifact with the same root cause: the mask callback also calls worldCityUpdate mid-fly. If z≤6.5 at that moment, ensureCityOverlay(null) removes the eagerly added overlay, and flyTo fires no zoomend or moveend until it lands. The plan therefore pops in at full opacity at the end of the fly instead of fading in during the descent.

The claimed bearing errors (Sokundo 132 deg and the rest) were not re-measured here. Magnitudes are upper bounds unless probed.

Fix surface: change only flyIntoCity, registerCityOverlay and the callback in ensureCityGen; these are not UG3-pinned. The options are to wait briefly for the mask, crossfade the swap, re-centre on worldPOICoord after the swap, and skip worldCityUpdate's overlay teardown while a fly is in progress.
votes.reason:
Read end to end in maps-site/index.html: flyIntoCity, ensureCityGen and ensureCityGenNow, sampleCityMask, registerCityOverlay, ensureCityOverlay, worldCityUpdate, nearestCity, genCityCanvas (the sv/mask.bear branch, `MK=(drawWater&&mask&&mask.water)?mask:null`, inWater's WD branch, and the inWater-gated `continue` after R() draws in the field loop and later), worldPOICoord and ensureArrival. Synthetic-first, the hot-swap and the frozen synthetic POI dest are confirmed. A data scan of city-anchors.json and city-traits.json gives 17 drawWater entries; Epēshu is canon, which leaves 16 generated, three of them side-less harbours (Hordon, Ion Ephel, Penthelon).

The claim is partly wrong in three places:
- **Trigger:** it is "mask not yet sampled this session", not a cold cache, because Image onload is always asynchronous.
- **Visibility:** the overlay sits at opacity 0 until z6.8 (about 0.65 s into the 1.4 s flyTo), so on fast links the coast jump is usually unseen. The POI centring miss happens regardless of timing.
- **Magnitudes:** they are upper bounds, and the 2.0k screen px figure uses cityMaxZ instead of the cz-0.5 fly target.

Also found: the callback's mid-fly worldCityUpdate can drop the eager overlay, so it pops in at moveend. The issue is major because a POI deep link reliably ends off its roundel, and on slow tiles a harbour's coast and streets jump visibly.

votes.corrected:
MECHANISM: confirmed, with two corrections. flyIntoCity calls ensureCityGen(key), which starts sampleCityMask, and then ensureCityGenNow(key). Because Image onload is always async, MASKQ[key].s is still 0 at that point, so genCityCanvas(key,t,a,null) registers the mask-less plan. Later the sampleCityMask callback in ensureCityGen re-registers the melded plan, and registerCityOverlay's `overlayCache.delete(key); if(CITYVIEW.name===key){...ensureCityOverlay(key);} // hot-swap` swaps it in.

(1) The trigger is the first flyIntoCity of the session on a city whose MASKQ[key] has not been sampled. An HTTP-cold cache is not required: even with every tile cached, the swap still fires a few frames later. Manual zooming never shows the synthetic plan, because worldCityUpdate only calls ensureCityGen.

(2) Penthelon (village, harbor, sea:null, defined in meshedWorldInit/traits) is a third side-less harbour. Its town centre shifts too, so it belongs with Hordon and Ion Ephel.

MAGNITUDE (recomputed): GEN_SIZE S=2048 maps to a box 2r on a side. The centre moves by `cx-=sv.x*S*0.07`, and |sv_random - mask.bear| is at most 2, so the shift is at most 0.14*2r.
- Hordon (town, r=14): 3.92 atlas px. That is 251 screen px at z10 and about 287 px at cityMaxZ = 4+log2(2048/28) = 10.19. The claim's "650+ at cityMaxZ" is wrong.
- Ion Ephel (ruin, r=8): 2.24 atlas px (about 1.6 px at 10.19... i.e. 2.24*2^(cityMaxZ-4); ruin cityMaxZ = 4+log2(2048/16) = 11, so about 287 px).
- Penthelon (village, r=9): 2.52 atlas px. Village cityMaxZ = 10.83, so about 287 px.

So the centre shift is about 0.14*2048 ≈ 287 screen px at each city's own max zoom, whatever the kind. POIs can move up to the plan diameter: 2r = S ≈ 2048 screen px at cityMaxZ for every kind (town 28 atlas px, village 18, ruin 16, capital 52 = ±26). A POI index can also land on a different place, so openWorldPOI then opens a different name. The per-city coast-bearing errors (Sokundo 132°, ...) and the count of 16 were not re-verified and need a probe that diffs genCityCanvas(key,t,a,null) against the melded plan. vector_independent=true is correct: a vector plan built through the same two-stage pipeline and the same cityBox would swap the same way.

CHEAP FIX: the proposed fix is wrong as written. Skipping ensureCityGenNow leaves CITYREG[key] unset, and flyIntoCity then returns false at `if(!reg||!a)return false`. That breaks the Descend button, ATLAS.descend and #chart= links. It also leaves cz (reg.w/h) and worldPOICoord (reg.pois) with nothing to work from.

A working version:
(a) Keep ensureCityGenNow for !drawWater cities.
(b) For drawWater traits, compute cz from GEN_SIZE (w=h=2048 is known without a plan) and start the fly toward the anchor. Then in the sampleCityMask callback, or after a timeout of about 300-600 ms (well under ensureArrival's 1700 ms), call ensureCityGenNow if no plan has registered yet. Only after that resolve worldPOICoord(key,poiN) and re-target with flyTo/panTo.
(c) The minimal option: keep today's order and, when poiN is set, re-resolve dest = worldPOICoord(key,poiN) after the hot-swap, re-pan, and re-open the POI. Add a crossfade: add the new overlay, then remove the old one on 'load'.

Touch only flyIntoCity, ensureCityGen's callback and registerCityOverlay (none is in atlas_fn_sha). That leaves the UG3 pins and cityCanvasSha unchanged, and desktop rest identity holds. Do not use trait edits as a quick fix: they change cityCanvasSha for those cities and need a rebaseline. Determinism holds: both plans stay pure functions of name and mask, and only when the swap lands depends on timing, as it does today. The 'deep links never wait' promise (MW) is weakened and must be restated. The change also touches mobile-lane and H2z fly timing, so it needs coordinating with Mobile 5-9 and living-chart.
votes.reason:
The mechanism is correct: the synthetic plan is registered in flyIntoCity before the async mask arrives, and the hot-swap in registerCityOverlay replaces it. vector_independent=true is also correct. Three things are wrong.

1. The magnitude has an error. Hordon's centre shift is 3.92 atlas px, which is about 287 screen px at its cityMaxZ of 10.19, not 650+. Penthelon, a third side-less harbour that shifts 2.52 atlas px, is left out.
2. The trigger is broader than "cold cache". Image onload is always async, so the swap fires on the first fly of every session.
3. The primary cheap fix breaks the feature. If ensureCityGenNow is skipped, CITYREG[key] is never set, so flyIntoCity returns false and cannot compute cz or worldPOICoord. The fix needs restructuring, or the minimal option of re-centring on the new POI after the swap plus a crossfade.

The pin-safety reasoning (change only the functions outside the UG3 pins) is right.

items.summary: Refuted: the remove-then-add blank decode frame exists only inside the narrow hot-swap path, not on every first visit, LRU revisit or neighbour switch, and it moves nothing.

prior_record.title: Hot-swap, LRU re-show and wash rebuilds replace the , giving a blank frame before decode
prior_record.anchor: registerCityOverlay: overlayCache.delete(key); ... ensureCityOverlay(key) -> L.imageOverlay(reg.url,...); ensureCityGen callback: if(CITYVIEW.name===key)washRefresh(key); lruPut (cap 6)
prior_record.mechanism: RENDERING. A swap removes the old overlay layer first, then adds a new L.imageOverlay whose decodes asynchronously (2048^2 WebP/PNG), so the plan area shows the 12-100% base for >=1 frame. ensureCityOverlay always builds a new wash, and in the ensureCityGen callback the wash is built twice (once from the hot-swap, then torn down and rebuilt by washRefresh). lruPut discards overlay objects so a revisit re-decodes the image.
prior_record.fires_when: The mask lands while a city is on screen (every first visit at z>6.5), revisiting a 7th+ city, any nearest-city switch.
prior_record.visible_effect: A one-frame (longer on phones) flash of bare atlas and printed label under the plan or wash.
prior_record.magnitude: Unmeasured. Probe: record rAF frames between map.removeLayer(old) and the new overlay's 'load' event and for the wash, on the pixel7 profile.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Swap after load: create the new overlay at opacity 0 and on 'load' set opacity and remove the old one, or reuse the same overlay via setUrl+setBounds. Drop the redundant washRefresh when registerCityOverlay already hot-swapped. (A synchronously drawn vector layer has no decode step.)
prior_record.fix_risks: washMake is UG3-pinned; only call sites change. cityCanvasSha unaffected. Two images are briefly resident (phone memory).

votes.corrected: RENDERING, not registration. The code is as described, but the claim says it fires far more often than it does. The facts below come from maps-site/index.html at HEAD and the vendored leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js. 1. ensureCityOverlay synchronously removes the old overlay, wash, stubs and POIs first, then adds L.imageOverlay(reg.url) and calls washMake. Leaflet's onAdd -> _initImage creates a new , sets src to the data URL and appends it. onRemove only detaches the element (T(this._image)). 2. The hot-swap branch in registerCityOverlay (if(CITYVIEW.name===key){CITYVIEW.name=null;ensureCityOverlay(key);}) runs only when the city is already registered AND is CITYVIEW when the mask lands. That is NOT every first visit at z>6.5. In worldCityUpdate, ensureCityGen(near.name) runs before ensureCityOverlay((reg&&z>6.5)?near.name:null). An invented city with no registration yet gives reg=null, so CITYVIEW.name stays null. When the sampleCityMask callback lands, registerCityOverlay does not swap and washRefresh does nothing (both check CITYVIEW.name===key). The trailing worldCityUpdate then creates the overlay fresh. The plan appears for the first time once decoded; nothing is swapped out from under it. The prewarm at z>5.6 registers even earlier. The cases that really fire are: (a) flyIntoCity (the descend button, a #chart= deep link, ANNALS descend) into an invented city whose mask has not been sampled yet. ensureCityGenNow registers the synthetic plan, ensureCityOverlay(key) shows it, then the melded plan hot-swaps in during the 1.4 s flyTo. This is the only path where the wash is built twice: washMake inside the hot-swap, then washRefresh rebuilds it from the identical cached WASHC URL, which is genuinely redundant. It is only visible if the z5 tiles land after the fly passes z6.8, since overlayOpacity is 0 below that. (b) Canon Epēshu/Summarch on the first approach past z6.5. registerCityOverlay is not called (prov canon). One washRefresh rebuilds the 256² wash to change its tone from LAND_TAN to the sampled hue. That change is intended, not redundant. 3. LRU: a cache hit re-appends the same detached . Only a city that was evicted after 6 more-recent distinct cities gets a new and a fresh decode of the data URL. The wash, by contrast, is a new on every ensureCityOverlay. 4. A nearest-city switch drops the old city's plan at once and the new city's plan appears for the first time (or its cached element is re-appended). That is not a flash under a plan that was already showing. 5. The blank frame is unmeasured and depends on the browser. It only occurs if the engine async-decodes a freshly appended large data-URL rather than decoding it at raster time. Keep the claim's probe as written. Cheap fix (still valid): call ensureCityOverlay/washMake as before but delay removing the old layer until the new one fires 'load', or setUrl on the existing overlay. Also skip washRefresh when the hot-swap already rebuilt the wash. This changes call sites only; washMake and cityCanvasSha are untouched.

This is a RENDERING glitch: the image blinks while it reloads. It is not a REGISTRATION or shift problem, because the overlay does not move. The hot-swap passes the same cityBox(a,reg.w,reg.h) bounds to L.imageOverlay, so the positional shift is 0 px. vector_independent:false is correct. A synchronously drawn vector or canvas layer has no async decode step, but a vector city would still be placed by cityBox and would not fix any alignment problem. When it fires (corrected): (a) The real case is ensureCityGen's sampleCityMask callback calling registerCityOverlay while CITYVIEW.name===key. That only happens when CITYREG[key] already existed before the mask was applied, which in practice means the synthetic plan from flyIntoCity -> ensureCityGenNow (Descend button, #chart= deep link, ANNALS descend). The synthetic overlay is on screen and the melded plan replaces it. (b) "Every first visit at z>6.5" is wrong. On an ordinary first zoom-in, the prewarm (z>5.6) and ensureCityGen run while reg is null. ensureCityOverlay(null) shows nothing, and the plan later appears fresh through worldCityUpdate, so there is nothing to blank out. (c) A nearest-city switch is not a flash under a plan. The new overlay covers a different footprint that was showing the base anyway, so it just appears late. (d) An LRU revisit only rebuilds the after the city was evicted (7th or later distinct city). A cached overlay keeps its _image across removeLayer and addTo. (e) Canon Epēshu and Summarch are never regenerated, so their chart overlays are never swapped. The swap is invisible while z<=6.8, where overlayOpacity is 0. Magnitude, recomputed: 0 px positional. Under the plan, the atlas shows at baseOpacity(z), from 1-(0.6/1.8)*0.88 = 0.71 at z6.8 down to 0.12 at z>=8. That range is 0.12-0.71, not 12-100%, and at z>=8 the frame is mostly the #map background with a faint atlas. Area: 2r world px square, or 1.7x that for the wash. For a capital (r 26, 52 world px) at flyIntoCity's target cityMaxZ-0.5 = 4+log2(2048/52)-0.5 ≈ 8.8, that is about 1448 screen px (the plan) and about 2460 px (the wash). For a town (r 14) at about 9.7, it is also about 1448 px. Duration: unmeasured; expect at least one frame, more on phones. The probe is fine. The synthetic-to-melded content change (a different land/water mask) is itself a visible pop that no swap timing removes. Cheap fix (corrected): 1. Best: in the hot-swap branch only, reuse the live overlay with ov.setUrl(newUrl) (plus setBounds if w or h changed). Under the HTML image-update rules, the old picture stays displayed until the new one is fully available. Also await ov.getElement().decode() where it exists. 2. If using two overlays: Leaflet's 'load' event fires on img onload, which does not guarantee decode. Gate on img.decode(), then setOpacity and remove the old overlay. Track the pending old overlay in CITYVIEW so that worldOpacityUpdate fades it, and so that ensureCityOverlay(null), a nearest-city switch, or enterChart removes it. Otherwise an orphan plan is left stuck on the map. 3. Skip the second wash only when the callback actually hot-swapped. Keep washRefresh for the canon/re-tone path where registerCityOverlay was not called. Call sites only: ensureCityOverlay, registerCityOverlay and ensureCityGen. None of these are UG3-pinned; the pinned set is xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask, and washMake's source must not change. cityCanvasSha, determinism and the settled-frame desktop identity are unaffected. Risks: two 2048² decoded images resident briefly on phones. Because the atlas mobile lane (Mobile 5-9) is mid-flight in maps-site/index.html, land this as a unit sequenced after or inside that lane, not concurrently.
votes.reason: I checked this against maps-site/index.html at HEAD (registerCityOverlay, ensureCityOverlay, lruPut, washMake, washRefresh, ensureCityGen, ensureCityGenNow, flyIntoCity, baseOpacity, overlayOpacity). - The mechanism is real. The hot-swap removes the old layer, then adds a new imageOverlay whose data: URL decodes asynchronously. The double wash in the ensureCityGen callback is real too: ensureCityOverlay calls washMake, then washRefresh removes that wash and builds it again. - The trigger list is wrong. "Every first visit" is false: reg is null there, so nothing is drawn. A nearest-city switch is a different footprint, so there is no flash. Cached LRU entries keep their ; only evicted ones rebuild it. - The "12-100% base" range is wrong; it is 0.12-0.71 while the overlay is visible. - The finding never says that the shift magnitude is 0 px, which takes it out of the anchoring question. - The fix as written (show on 'load') does not guarantee decode, and it would leave the old overlay orphaned if the user leaves before the load. setUrl or img.decode() closes both gaps. - The UG3, determinism and desktop-identity claims hold, since only unpinned call sites change. The fix should be sequenced with the mobile atlas lane.

votes.corrected: Mostly correct, with three fixes. It is a RENDERING/load-latency pop-in, not a registration shift: the chart's bounds come from cityBox either way, so nothing moves. Mechanism, verified in maps-site/index.html. meshedWorldInit runs registerCityOverlay('Epēshu','art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg',...) and the Summarch equivalent at init. That puts both in CITYREG with url=tv(...) (adds '?t=1') and prov 'canon'. The prewarm branch in worldCityUpdate (`else if(near&&z>5.6&&!CITYREG[near.name]&&!PREWARMED.has(near.name))`) is therefore skipped for them. Even when it runs for other cities it only calls ensureCityGen, which builds a canvas/dataURL and never fetches a URL. The z>6.5 branch calls ensureCityGen for canon cities too, but it only samples z5 tiles and does not regenerate a canon reg. No other code fetches the overlay JPEGs: grep finds no `new Image`, preload/prefetch link or serviceWorker for them. tools/build-offline-manifest.js lists art/ but no SW is registered at HEAD. The first request is made by Leaflet: ImageOverlay.onAdd calls _initImage, which sets img.src straight away and does not hide the image until 'load'. That happens when ensureCityOverlay(key) runs, which is (a) from worldCityUpdate on the first zoomend/moveend with z>6.5 and the city within 3*FOOT_R (nearestCity), or (b) at fly start in flyIntoCity, including #chart=Epēshu deep links through handleHash. The overlay gets opacity overlayOpacity(z): 0 up to z6.8, rising linearly to 1 at 7.8. Both files are baseline SOF0 JPEGs: overlay-Epeshu.jpg is 2,171,695 B at 2863x3072 and overlay-Summarch.jpg is 1,283,357 B at 3072x2859. The brief's 3072x2863 for Epeshu is transposed; the registry's w:2863,h:3072 is right. So on a slow link they paint top-down. Corrections: (1) Head start: with manual zoom the download begins only at the first zoomend past 6.5, so the lead before the fade starts at 6.8 is short or zero. One wheel or pinch gesture that ends past 7.8 adds the overlay at full opacity over a base already down to about 0.2 opacity plus the wash (a dataURL, so instant), which leaves a washed-out hole until the bytes arrive. On a fly, the download gets the 1.4 s flyTo plus the ensureArrival timer (1.7 s) and competes with the cold-load tile requests. (2) Frequency: it happens once per cold HTTP cache, not once per session. The overlayCache LRU (cap 6) keeps the L.imageOverlay and its img element, so re-adding does not refetch, and the static ?t=1 URL stays in the browser cache across sessions. (3) It is visible only when the transfer takes longer than the zoom, which means phone, hotspot or Fast-3G-class links. On LAN or broadband (about 0.3-0.5 s for 2.1 MB) it is mostly hidden by the fade. The cheap fix stands: in the prewarm branch, also handle a registered canon reg with `if(reg.prov==='canon'&&!PREWARMED.has(key)){PREWARMED.add(key);new Image().src=reg.url;}` under the same 6*FOOT_R gate. Because the URL is identical (tv'd), Leaflet's later img hits the cache. Progressive JPEG or WebP re-encodes change the bytes, so they need a TILES_V bump and an offline-manifest regen.
votes.reason: The code path exists as claimed. CITYREG entries for Epēshu and Summarch are set in meshedWorldInit before any zoom, so the prewarm guard `!CITYREG[near.name]` excludes them. votes.corrected:
MECHANISM (RENDERING / load-timing, not REGISTRATION; nothing changes position): mostly correct. In worldCityUpdate the prewarm branch `else if(near&&z>5.6&&!CITYREG[near.name]&&!PREWARMED.has(near.name))` never fires for Epēshu or Summarch. Both are registered at init by the `registerCityOverlay('Epēshu','art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg',{prov:'canon',w:2863,h:3072` and `registerCityOverlay('Summarch','art/overlay-Summarch.jpg',{prov:'canon',w:3072,h:2859` calls. MAGNITUDE (recomputed): overlay-Epeshu.jpg in HEAD is 2,171,695 B = 17.37 Mbit, so about 10.9 s at 1.6 Mb/s (the old DevTools Fast 3G, now Slow 4G), plus about 0.56 s RTT, about 11.4 s in total. For the crossfade to be complete by the time the 6.8 to 7.8 ramp finishes in about 1 s, the link needs at least 17 Mb/s. Measured fact from docs/mobile/inputs/brief.md: #chart=Epēshu settles in 5.17 s even unthrottled.

FIRES_WHEN correction: the proposed prefetch can only fire on a zoomend that lands in z5.6 to 6.5 within 6*FOOT_R of the anchor (156 px for capital Epēshu, 84 px for town Summarch). A continuous wheel or pinch through that band, or any #chart= cold load (handleHash then flyIntoCity then an immediate ensureCityOverlay), skips it. So the fix does nothing for the case the claim calls worst.

FIX as written is wrong in two ways:
(1) "In the prewarm branch" cannot work, because that branch is gated on !CITYREG. The fix needs a separate canon branch ahead of the if/else, keyed on reg.prov==='canon', with its own PREWARMED entry. For the cold-link case, the fetch has to start at registration or at handleHash time, not in worldCityUpdate.
(2) It collides with the mid-flight mobile lane. Unit A-U11 (Mobile 6, docs/mobile/units.json) owns exactly this defect (A7). It ships 720 px previews overlay-Epeshu-720.jpg and overlay-Summarch-720.jpg (each 180 KB or less) and swaps them for the full plate. Its acceptance requires that no asset over 500 KB is requested before its preview, and that the full image stays the same file with the final shot equal to R1. Prefetching the 2.1 MB full plate early would break that ordering. "WebP" (lossy) would also break "same file / final shot equals R1" and therefore desktop identity. A plain progressive re-encode changes the bytes, though not the pixels if done losslessly with jpegtran.

Correct cheap fix: do not edit maps-site/index.html now. Hand the item to A-U11. If something is wanted beyond A-U11, it should run after A-U11 lands:
- In worldCityUpdate, add a separate branch for registered canon regs with z>5.6 inside 6*FOOT_R that prefetches the 720 px preview (not the full plate) once.
- Optionally hold the overlay's opacity at 0 until its 'load' event, then rejoin overlayOpacity, so it never wipes in mid-ramp.
- If the full plate is to be progressive, convert it losslessly with `jpegtran -progressive -copy none` so the pixels stay identical.

SAFETY: none of this touches the UG3-pinned functions (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask) or cityCanvasSha, and none of it is gen code, so determinism is unaffected. The only risks are the A-U11 ordering acceptance, the "same file" desktop-identity check, mobile bandwidth (about 2.2 MB wasted on a near-miss if the full plate is prefetched), and the offline manifest from tools/build-offline-manifest.js if new preview files are added.

VECTOR_INDEPENDENT should be true in practice. The cause is load ordering of the DM's canon raster, which stays authoritative (A-U11 keeps it as the same file), and a preview or tile pyramid fixes it without any vector layer. A vector city would avoid it only by not showing the canon art. Registering a vector city through the same cityBox would also not change any alignment.
votes.reason: The diagnosis is correct: canon regs are excluded from the prewarm branch by !CITYREG, the plates are baseline JPEGs, and the overlay is added only at z>6.5 or at fly start. The magnitude is understated: 2,171,695 B at 1.6 Mb/s is about 10.9 s, about 11.4 s with RTT, not 10.5 s. The fix is unsound on two counts. As placed in the !CITYREG-gated branch it can never fire, and it never runs on the #chart cold-load path the claim calls worst, because flyIntoCity bypasses the z5.6 to 6.5 zoomend band. Prefetching the full 2.1 MB plate, or re-encoding it to WebP, conflicts with mobile unit A-U11 (Mobile 6, mid-flight). A-U11 already owns this defect (A7) through 720 px previews and requires the preview before any asset over 500 KB and the full plate to stay the same file. The fix does not risk the UG3 pins or determinism. vector_independent=false is doubtful because the canon raster stays the authoritative art and a raster preview fixes the problem.

items.summary: REGISTRATION plus presentation: generated-plan road stubs take their bearing at the 2.5r ring and are drawn radially to 1.18r at fixed opacity, so they show over bare atlas from z6.5 and end a median 4.2 atlas px (max 14.0-14.5 at Sokundo) from the drawn road; the spline is not the cause.

prior_record.title: Street-tier road stubs pop in at full opacity before the plan and end beside the world road they claim to continue
prior_record.subsystem: overlay (buildCityStubs / stub block in genCityCanvas / worldOpacityUpdate)
prior_record.anchor: buildCityStubs: L.polyline(ll,{color:'#efe6cf',weight:6,opacity:.5/.6,...pane:'pCity'}); genCityCanvas stubs: `ox=a.atlasX+Math.cos(gg.ang)*footR(a.kind)*1.18`; cityApproaches/segCircleHits on raw polyline pts; buildNamedWays crSpline(way.pts,16)
prior_record.mechanism: REGISTRATION and RENDERING. Stubs exist only for reg.prov==='invented' (canon draws none). Opacity is fixed .5/.6 and worldOpacityUpdate never touches them, so they appear the moment the overlay is instantiated (z>6.5, overlayOpacity 0 until 6.8) and vanish at <=6.5. Each stub runs radially from the exact gate to anchor + 1.18*r along the bearing where the RAW approach polyline crosses the 2.5*r ring, but the drawn world road is a Catmull-Rom spline of those points, so where the road curves the stub end misses it. Hinterland and river-walked gates (ang += 0.12 steps) add stubs whose bearing comes from no road at all (gap numbers are a lower bound). Named ways and route stay visible until tier-d (7.5), giving two roads at 6.5-7.5, and the atlas road blinks out at 7.5 leaving the stub pointing nowhere.
prior_record.fires_when: Generated cities with land approaches (13 anchors; party route + 2 named ways), z>6.5, overlapping with world lines up to 7.5.
prior_record.visible_effect: Short brown/cream stubs float over the plain atlas from z6.5 before any city shows, then form a V or sit offset against the printed or drawn road.
prior_record.magnitude: Stub-end to drawn-road gap over 29 stubs on 13 cities (10 cities / 19 road-derived stubs for one pass): max 14.0-14.5 atlas px (Sokundo, second 13.7), Nhagi 9.2, Epēshu bearing 10.6 (canon, unused), Harney 8.8-9.8; median 2.2 (raw polyline) to 3.8 (spline), p90 9.2. Screen: 18-37 px median and 112-153 px max at z7-7.4. Opacity step 0 to .5/.6 at z6.5, with overlay below 0.5 until z7.3.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Pin-free: in worldOpacityUpdate setStyle({opacity:base*overlayOpacity(z)}) on CITYVIEW.stubs layers; in buildCityStubs (not pinned) snap (x1,y1) to the nearest point on the drawn way/route spline (or APPR_POLYS land polylines) within ~2*footR and extend along the polyline instead of radially, dropping stubs with no road. Leave genCityCanvas stubs untouched. Superseded if filigree slice C pooled edges replace stubs.
prior_record.fix_risks: Editing endpoint math inside genCityCanvas would change its UG3 source hash and cityCanvasSha across profiles; the buildCityStubs route avoids both. Determinism holds (snap is a pure function of static data). Desktop look changes slightly at z>6.5.

votes.corrected:
The mechanism exists, but the claim names the wrong cause for the misalignment. It is a REGISTRATION error (and would stay one in vector): where the stub ends is computed separately from where the road actually runs.

(1) Opacity. `buildCityStubs` (maps-site/index.html) returns null unless `reg.prov==='invented'`, so canon Epēshu and Summarch get no stubs. Each stub is two `L.polyline`s in pane `pCity`: a casing `#efe6cf` with weight 6 and opacity .5, and ink `#6a4326` with weight 2.6 and opacity .6. `worldOpacityUpdate` sets opacity on curBase, CITYVIEW.overlay and CITYVIEW.wash, but never on CITYVIEW.stubs. The pane's .25s CSS transition fades the pane, not the strokes, so the step from 0 to .5/.6 is a true pop. `ensureCityOverlay` adds the stubs. `worldCityUpdate` calls it only on zoomend/moveend, once z>6.5 and `CITYREG[key]` exists (generation is async from the tiles and is prewarmed at z>5.6). The stubs come off at the first zoomend at z≤6.5. `overlayOpacity` is 0 up to 6.8 and reaches .5 only at 7.3, so between 6.5 and 6.8 the stubs sit on bare parchment. `flyIntoCity` calls `ensureCityOverlay(key)` eagerly, so on a fly-in the stubs appear at whatever zoom the flight starts from. The pWay and pRouteLine panes (named ways and the dashed party route) stay visible until `Z_TIER_D`=7.5 and then fade out over a .2s pane transition. So from 6.5 to 7.5 the stub and the world road show at the same time. The printed base road fades gradually via `baseOpacity` (about .37 at 7.5, .12 at z8).

(2) Gap. `cityApproaches` takes the bearing where the RAW polyline (party legs + named ways) crosses the 2.5·footR ring, then clusters bearings within about 14° with `mergeAngles`. In `genCityCanvas` the stub runs from the exact gate to `anchor + 1.18·footR` along that bearing. Any road that does not run radially toward the anchor between 2.5r and 1.18r misses that end point, so the error is radial extrapolation, not Catmull-Rom smoothing. Raw and spline gaps are almost the same: Sokundo 14.0 raw vs 14.5 spline; medians 4.2 vs 3.8 atlas px. The river walk (`gg.ang+=0.12`, up to 16 steps) ROTATES existing approach gates, including road-derived ones, and adds no stub, so the measured gaps are a lower bound for river cities. Hinterland is the part that ADDS stubs, through `mkGate(hb,true)` or a seeded gate flagged `appr=true`. The bearing is anchor→Epēshu or comes from the seeded gate, not from any road. This gives one roadless stub each to Aldorūs, Rēketis, Āglaz, Mīth Mirdānak, Pharzeban and Tarap, and possibly a second to Sokundo or Kanae.

(3) Counts, reproduced in node from city-anchors, party-route and named-ways. 12 anchors have land approaches. Epēshu (canon) and Lepon the Old (ruin, so `landAppr=[]`) drop out, leaving 10 cities with 19 road-derived stubs, plus 6–8 roadless hinterland stubs. Not 13 anchors / 29 stubs. Stub-end to road gap, raw/spline in atlas px: Sokundo 14.0/14.5 and 14.0/13.7; Harney 8.9 and 9.8 raw (8.6–8.9 spline); Nhagi 8.5 raw, 7.8–9.2 spline; Rhup 4.8–6.4; Epēshu 10.6 raw (canon, so never drawn). Median 4.2 raw / 3.8 spline (the claim's 2.2 raw median does not reproduce); max 14.5. At z7 (8 screen px per atlas px) that is about 30 px median and 112–116 px for Sokundo.

(4) The cheap fix stands: snap or extend the stubs in `buildCityStubs`, which is not hash-pinned, and fade them with `overlayOpacity`. It should project the stub end onto the nearest road polyline rather than only swapping raw for spline. Roadless hinterland stubs should be dropped or bent onto a real road.
votes.reason: I traced the code path end to end in the HEAD export. The main effect: at z7 the stub ends sit about 30 px (median) and up to 112–116 px (Sokundo, on the party's road out of Epēshu) away from the road they are meant to continue. The dashed route or named way is still drawn there until z7.5, so the two form a visible V or offset. The pop-in is subtler: fixed-opacity stubs appear over bare parchment between z6.5 and 6.8. My node reproduction matches the claim's headline gap numbers (Sokundo max 14.0–14.5 atlas px, second 13.7, Nhagi 9.2, Epēshu 10.6, Harney about 9), but it shows three errors in the claim. The miss comes from radial extrapolation of a bearing measured at 2.5r to 1.18r, not from the spline (raw and spline gaps are nearly equal). River-walk rotates existing stubs rather than adding them; only hinterland adds roadless stubs. The counts are wrong: 10 cities / 19 road-derived stubs plus 6–8 hinterland stubs, and the raw median is 4.2, not 2.2.

votes.corrected:
VISIBLE EFFECT: right. buildCityStubs (maps-site/index.html) draws two L.polylines per stub in pane pCity at a fixed opacity of .5 and .6. ensureCityOverlay adds them as soon as worldCityUpdate sees z>6.5. worldOpacityUpdate only fades CITYVIEW.overlay and CITYVIEW.wash, so from z6.5 to 6.8 the stubs sit over the bare atlas while overlayOpacity is 0. At Z_TIER_D 7.5 the pWay and pRouteLine panes go to opacity 0. That is a 0.5 s CSS fade, not an instant blink.

MAGNITUDE (recomputed in node). I ran the real crSpline, segCircleHits and mergeAngles code over party-route.json, named-ways.json and city-anchors.json, with FOOT_R and the stub end at 1.18*footR along the merged bearing at 2.5*footR. That gives 19 road-derived stubs on 10 cities, excluding Epēshu and Summarch. Gaps:
- Sokundo: 14.0 raw / 14.5 spline, and 14.0 / 13.7 for its second stub
- Nhagi: 9.2 and 7.8 spline
- Harney: 8.6 to 9.8
- Epēshu: 10.6 raw (canon, so no stub is drawn)
- median: 4.2 raw / 3.8 spline over the 19 (the claim's "2.2 raw" is not reproduced; it presumably counts unverified extra stubs)
- p90: 9.2

Screen size: 1 atlas px = 2^(z-4) screen px, so about 30 px median and 112 to 153 px max at z7 to 7.4. Those figures stand.

MECHANISM (corrected). The spline is not the main cause: the raw-polyline gaps are as large as the spline gaps (Sokundo 14.0 raw). The cause is a registration mismatch. The stub bearing is the mean of the crossings at the 2.5r ring (mergeAngles), but the stub is placed radially at 1.18r. Roads that are not radial, that pass by the anchor, or that merge two crossings within 0.25 rad are therefore missed near the plan. Hinterland stubs and river-walked stubs (gg.ang+=0.12) add bearings that come from no road at all.

vector_independent: true. These are stub endpoint coordinates, and a vector city placed through the same bearings misses the road the same way.

CHEAP FIX (corrected).
- (1) CITYVIEW.stubs is an L.layerGroup, which has no setStyle. In worldOpacityUpdate use `CITYVIEW.stubs.eachLayer(l => l.setStyle({opacity: l.options._b * overlayOpacity(z)}))`, storing _b = .5 or .6 in buildCityStubs. A featureGroup cannot be used with a single setStyle either, because the two bases differ.
- (2) The snap in buildCityStubs: keep (x0,y0) at the gate, set (x1,y1) to the nearest point on the drawn spline (route legs crSpline 18, ways crSpline 16) within about 2*footR, and drop stubs that have no road. This is safe because buildCityStubs and worldOpacityUpdate are not in UG3 atlas_fn_sha (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask). The stubs also never enter the canvas, so cityCanvasSha is unchanged. Determinism holds (a pure function of static data), and no mobile units touch either function.
- Caveat: the pinned genCityCanvas still paints each approach road radially from the gate out to S*0.6, which is 1.2r in atlas px, on the old bearing (`roads.push` for appr gates). A snapped stub will therefore bend away from the painted plan road. The fix shortens the stub-to-world-road gap but adds a kink at the gate.
- The full fix is to choose the gate bearing from the road's position at about 1.2r instead of at 2.5r, inside cityApproaches. cityApproaches is not pinned, but the change alters the canvas, so it changes cityCanvasSha (Sokundo and Kanae are in the hashed set). It has to wait for a re-baseline outside the mobile lane, or for filigree slice C's pooled edges.
- Desktop look changes at z>6.5. Filigree R6 asks ink to ease in over 0.25 zoom or less; the overlayOpacity ramp spans 1.0 zoom.
votes.reason: The visible effect, the unramped opacity, and the max, second, Nhagi, Harney, Epēshu and p90 gaps all reproduce from code and data. The median does not: 4.2 raw versus the claimed 2.2. The mechanism wrongly blames the Catmull-Rom spline, since the raw-polyline gaps are just as large; the real cause is a stub bearing taken at the 2.5r ring and placed radially at 1.18r. The cheap fix as written fails, because L.layerGroup has no setStyle and the two stub lines have different base opacities. The snap is pin-safe and deterministic, but it leaves a kink against the radial road that the pinned genCityCanvas paints on the old bearing. So it is a partial fix, and the full fix changes cityCanvasSha.

items.summary: REGISTRATION: buildApprPolys sees only the party route, two named ways and four sea lanes, so 11 of 136 anchors get land approaches (plus 6 with a hinterland gate) and the rest aim gates at seeded-random bearings; data/traced-roads.json is mostly lettering and is not a usable fix.

prior_record.title: Most generated plans aim gates and roads at seeded-random bearings, not at the atlas's printed roads
prior_record.anchor: buildApprPolys(route,res[13],res[12]) (party-route + named-ways + sea-lanes only); genCityCanvas: gate0=R()*Math.PI*2; data/traced-roads.json never loaded
prior_record.mechanism: REGISTRATION. Approach bearings come only from the 12-point party route, 2 named ways and 4 sea lanes. 125 of 138 anchors get none, so their gates are seeded-random (gate0 plus jitter) and in-plan roads do not continue the dotted roads printed on the atlas. maps-site/data/traced-roads.json (46 polylines traced from the atlas) is never loaded by the atlas.
prior_record.fires_when: Every generated plan without a route or named-way crossing, z6.8 and deeper.
prior_record.visible_effect: The atlas road runs into the town from the east but the plan's main road leaves north; roads jump across the crossfade.
prior_record.magnitude: Angular mismatch arbitrary (0-180 deg); at the plan edge up to 2r: 18 atlas px for a village (2.0k screen px at 10.83). Coverage 13/138 anchors with land approaches today, 56/138 with traced-roads.json.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Load data/traced-roads.json in the Promise.all and pass its polylines into buildApprPolys as class 'land'.
prior_record.fix_risks: Data and call-site only (genCityCanvas source unchanged) but every gained city's canvas changes; Tamaron gains a crossing so cityCanvasSha changes (rebaseline). Traced roads near off-dot anchors need the anchor fix first or bearings are measured from the label.

votes.corrected:
REGISTRATION (vector_independent: true). In maps-site/index.html the load Promise.all never fetches data/traced-roads.json; the file is mentioned only in docs. `buildApprPolys(route,res[13],res[12])` builds APPR_POLYS from three sources: the 12-point party-route legs plus their vias, the 2 named-ways ('Road that Walks with the Sun', 28 pts; 'The East-West Road', 4 pts) as 'land', and the 4 sea-lanes as 'sea'. `cityApproaches(key)` turns each crossing of a 2.5*footR circle into a bearing. In `genCityCanvas`, `gate0=R()*Math.PI*2` and `ga=gate0+gi/nGates*2PI+rr(-.25,.25)` fill out the gate set after the land approaches (`mkGate(b,true)`).

Coverage (replicated in node): 13 of 138 anchors (136 in the file plus Summarch and Penthelon added in meshedWorldInit) get land crossings. Three of the 13 do not use them for a generated plan: Epēshu and Summarch are canon overlays, and Lepon the Old is a ruin, so its landAppr is []. That leaves 10 generated plans with gates taken from atlas data. `hinterlandOf` adds an appr gate pointing at the parent port for 8 cities. Six of those are outside the 13 (Aldorūs, Rēketis, Āglaz, Mīth Mirdānak, Pharzeban, Tarap). That gate follows a straight bearing to the port, not the printed road, and it is not seeded-random either. So about 119 plans are fully seeded and 6 have only the port bearing. Even the 10 covered plans aim at the shipped Sun Road trace, and density-bible B-16 says that trace lies off the printed dotted road.

The visible effect is different from the claim. A non-approach gate sits at gr=coreR*1.15 when unwalled or 0.9 when walled, about 3.5 atlas px from the centre for a village. Its road runs only from the gate to the market square. The road out to the plan edge (S*0.6) and the street-tier stubs (buildCityStubs, gen.stubs) are both conditional on gg.appr. So no plan road reaches the edge, and nothing 'jumps' across it. What actually happens: the atlas dotted road runs to the dot and fades into an opaque plan that has no matching road, while the plan's main roads point wherever gate0 landed. The angular mismatch can be anything from 0 to 180 deg. The positional gap is about 2*gr, not 2r: roughly 7 atlas px for a village, about 0.8k screen px at its cityMaxZ of 10.83.

Where it is seen: the plan is opaque inside cityBox, baseOpacity drops to 0.12 by z8, and washMake covers the rim. The mismatch is therefore readable mainly in the crossfade band z6.8-7.8 (overlayOpacity 0 to 1) and faintly at the rim. It is still the owner's 'doesn't line up', most clearly for towns.

The cheap fix is unsafe as written. (a) traced-roads.json is bare [[x,y],...] arrays, and buildApprPolys keeps only entries with w.pts, so passing the file unwrapped drops all 46 chains and changes nothing. It needs mapping to {pts:p}. (b) The density-bible blazed_paths row says the chains are 'mostly lettering and islets', and B-16 says they 'lie off the printed road'. POLISH 'Traced road network (USER FLAG)' is still unchecked: text i-dots chain like roads. Loading them as they are would aim gates at lettering. The fix has to wait for that item, which re-traces the print and also re-snaps the named ways the 10 covered cities depend on.

fix_risks: the 56/138 figure with the traced roads loaded checks out. Gainers would include Tamaron (tr33), and also Mago (tr33), Drāmūz (tr40), Māmīth Māgrīn (tr0) and Istīron (tr38), which keep their existing crossings and gain more. Every gainer's gate set and canvas changes. cityCanvasSha hashes Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae (docs/mobile/README.md), so Tamaron's gain forces a UG3 rebaseline. Sokundo and Kanae do not gain. genCityCanvas source would stay unchanged, but the output changes, so the change needs a mobile gap.

A vector plan placed through the same gate0 would misaim in exactly the same way. The fix is registration data (a traced print road feeding the approach bearings), not the rendering medium.
votes.reason:
The code path exists as claimed. The Promise.all fetches 16 data files, and traced-roads.json is not among them. buildApprPolys takes only route, ways and lanes, and gate0=R()*Math.PI*2 is in genCityCanvas. Replicating cityApproaches in node reproduces the 13/138 coverage today, 56/138 with the traced roads, and Tamaron gaining tr33.
