Three parts of the claim are wrong. First, effective coverage is lower: canon overlays, a ruin, and hinterland gates change the counts. Second, the visible effect is wrong. Non-approach gates have no edge road and no stubs, so nothing continues across the plan edge. The gap is about 2*gr, not 2r, and it is visible mainly in the z6.8-7.8 crossfade. Third, the cheap fix silently does nothing, because the file has no .pts wrapper and buildApprPolys skips it. It is also unsafe, because the docs record the traced chains as mostly lettering and islets.

I rated it major because, at town scale, plan roads pointing away from the printed dotted road are exactly the misalignment the owner describes.

votes.corrected:
MECHANISM (holds): this is a REGISTRATION problem, and vector_independent=true is right. In maps-site/index.html, buildApprPolys(route,res[13],res[12]) gets its approach polylines only from party-route.json (12 points, 11 legs), named-ways.json (2 entries) and sea-lanes.json (4 entries). The Promise.all loads 16 files and traced-roads.json is not one of them. In genCityCanvas, the RNG-free approach gates come from cityApproaches(name).land. Every other gate is placed at gate0=R()*Math.PI*2 plus i/nGates*2pi plus rr(-.25,.25). A vector plan placed through cityBox would put its gates just as far off the printed road.

COVERAGE (recomputed by replaying segCircleHits at 2.5*footR over the data): there are 136 anchors, not 138 (1 capital, 17 towns, 115 villages, 3 ruins). Ruins get landAppr=[]. 11 of the 133 non-ruin anchors have a land approach today: Epēshu, Sokundo, Kanae, Tamaron, Mago, Drāmūz, Rhup, Māmīth Māgrīn, Harney, Pomos and Nhagi. The claim says 13. hinterlandOf in city-traits.json (8 cities) also gives Aldorūs, Rēketis, Āglaz, Mīth Mirdānak, Pharzeban and Tarap one non-random gate. That gate points toward the parent port, not along the printed road. So about 116 to 122 of 133 plans have only seeded-random gates. Adding the traced chains would bring coverage to 54 of 136, not 56.

MAGNITUDE: the bearing error can be anything from 0 to 180 degrees. Gate and road ends sit on a circle of radius at most r inside the 2r cityBox, so the chord at the plan edge is 2r*sin(dtheta/2). That is at most 18 world px for a village, 28 for a town and 52 for the capital. On screen it scales by 2^(z-4). In the crossfade band z6.8 to 7.8, where the base road and the plan road both show, a village gives 125 to 251 screen px and a town 195 to 390. At a village's cityMaxZ of 4+log2(2048/18)=10.83 the figure is 2048 screen px, but there baseOpacity is 0.12, so the jump is mainly seen inside the crossfade band. The claim's 2.0k figure is arithmetically right but sits at the wrong zoom for the visible effect.

CHEAP FIX (wrong, unsafe): "load traced-roads.json and pass it as class 'land'" would mis-register the plans further. The committed file holds 46 short fragments of 2 to 10 vertices and 27 to 312 px each. The filigree density bible (blazed_paths row) calls them "mostly lettering and islets". Its B-16 row says the traced-roads chains "lie off the printed road and cannot feed it before the Traced road network item". POLISH.md's LEARNINGS also notes that text i-dots and periods chain like roads. Feeding them in would aim gates at lettering strokes and islet outlines.

The safe route is the POLISH item "Traced road network (USER FLAG)". Its scope already includes "feed approach bearings". Once it ships a vetted dotted-road spline set with text masked, load that set into APPR_POLYS as 'land'. Leave genCityCanvas untouched. Gate it on the anchor-on-dot fix so bearings are measured from the true settlement ring and not from the label.

SEQUENCING and RISKS:
- (a) Determinism holds either way: it is pure static data and draws no RNG. The gate0 and rr draw count stays the same, because approach gates are RNG-free and the loop calls rr() on every iteration.
- (b) UG3: cityCanvasSha hashes Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae. Tamaron gains a traced crossing (base 2 hits, plus 1 traced), so the sha moves away from B0, and every newly covered city's plan changes. This must not land while the atlas lane (Mobile 5 to 9) is in flight. Schedule it after Mobile 9 with an explicit B0 rebaseline.
- (c) Desktop identity: desktop plans change on purpose. Declare this as an intended visual change, not a regression.
- (d) It changes maps-site/index.html, which the filigree build holds while slice C runs, so it also needs a hold check.
votes.reason: The mechanism and vector_independent=true are correct: buildApprPolys only sees the route, named ways and sea lanes, and traced-roads.json is never fetched. Most plans therefore get gates from gate0=R()*2pi plus jitter. The counts are off: there are 136 anchors, not 138, and 11 have land approaches, not 13 (plus 6 more with a hinterland gate). The traced chains raise coverage to 54, not 56. The 2.0k px figure is at z10.83, where the base is at 0.12 opacity; the visible jump is 125 to 390 screen px in the z6.8 to 7.8 crossfade band. The cheap fix is wrong. traced-roads.json is 46 short, noisy fragments, which the density bible calls "mostly lettering and islets" lying off the printed road, so feeding them as 'land' would mis-register gates. The correct input is the output of the pending "Traced road network" POLISH item. Any such change moves cityCanvasSha (Tamaron gains a crossing), so it has to wait until after Mobile 9 and be rebaselined.

items.summary: REGISTRATION (data): traits.sea.side drives the plan's sea vector even when the atlas mask has water, so active drawWater cities (Sokundo 132 deg, Tamaron 97 deg) bias centre and quays toward the wrong side and Shengo draws a compass sea on dry land; five of the nine claimed cities never draw water.

prior_record.title: Trait sea.side contradicts the atlas: compass coast, centre shift and ruin-island POI land on the wrong side
prior_record.anchor: genCityCanvas: `if(drawWater){cx-=sv.x*S*0.07;...}`; addPoi(cx+sv.x*(shoreDist+S*0.14),...,'The Island Fortress',...); inWater(): (x-cx)*sv.x+(y-cy)*sv.y > shoreOff(...)
prior_record.mechanism: REGISTRATION. sv comes from traits.sea.side even when the mask supplies the real coast. It still shifts the plan centre 0.07*S away from the stated side, biases the quay cast, draws the whole coast when there is no mask (synthetic plan, or Shengo whose patch has no water) and places the ruin's 'Island Fortress' POI along sv, whereas the drawn island uses waterNode/seaNormal when WD is set. Shengo's anchor sits on a label letter in dry land but draws a compass sea to the east.
prior_record.fires_when: Generated plans for harbor/sea cities with wrong traits, and synthetic plans before the mask lands.
prior_record.visible_effect: Sea painted where the atlas shows land (Shengo, synthetic plans); the Island Fortress marker on land away from the drawn island (Lepon the Old); town centres pushed off by ~2 atlas px.
prior_record.magnitude: Bearing error trait vs mask water centroid: Aldorūs 175 deg, Medem 166, Sokundo 132, Rēketis 130, Lepon the Old 115, Perōna 115, Epēshu 114 (canon, unused), Tamaron 97, Pharzeban 76. Centre shift 0.07*2r: 1.96 (town), 1.12 (ruin). Lepon Island Fortress POI 3.4 px east of anchor while the island lies ~115 deg away; Shengo sea covers ~east half of its 18-px footprint.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Data: set traits.sea.side to the dirName of the mask bearing or null it for harbors (so mask.bear is used); remove Shengo's sea (distPx 2 on dry land) after moving its anchor to its dot.
prior_record.fix_risks: Changes cityCanvasSha for Sokundo and Tamaron (rebaseline); pinned function sources untouched. The r-b<=54 classifier misreads grey-green inland regions as water, so derive sides only for real-coast cities, checked by eye.

votes.corrected:
REGISTRATION (the problem is where the plan's water and city parts sit relative to the atlas coast. The medium does not matter: a vector plan fed the same sv would place things the same way). In genCityCanvas (maps-site/index.html), `var sea=(t.sea&&t.sea.side)?t.sea.side:...; var sv=sea?compassVec(sea):null;` takes the compass side from traits. The atlas bearing mask.bear replaces it only for `t.harbor&&!(t.sea&&t.sea.side)`, so any city with a charted side keeps that side even when the sampled mask holds the real coast. sv only matters when `drawWater = !!sv && (t.harbor || distPx<=25)`. When that is true:
(1) `if(drawWater){cx-=sv.x*S*0.07;...}` moves the plan centre 0.07S away from the stated side. S spans 2r atlas px, so the move is 0.14r: 1.96 px for a town, 1.26 for a village, 1.12 for a ruin. The move is by design. The error is only its direction: a wrong side puts the centre up to 2*0.07S*sin(theta/2) away from where a correct side would, about 3.6 px at Sokundo.
(2) When the mask has water (WD), the coast fill comes from the mask and is correct. sv still steers the waterfront: castV is the sea-lane approach bearing nearest sv. waterNode is cast within ±0.8 rad of castV and then sv, and quays within ±0.55 rad of qCenter. The Quays POI text uses `sea`, so Sokundo's reads 'along the wsw water' while its water lies to the north-north-east.
(3) When there is no WD, the whole synthetic compass coast is drawn along sv. This happens in two cases. One is ensureCityGenNow's plan before the mask lands; it is replaced when the mask arrives. The other is permanent: a mask with water=false. Shengo is that case. Its anchor (1453,1735) sits on the 'O' of a spaced regional label ('H O S...') on dry land, well away from its own 'Shengo' label and dot. Patch water fraction is 0.000, yet traits say side E, distPx 2. So a synthetic sea covers about 46% of the 18-px footprint, its east half, where the atlas is land. This is the major, at-the-table effect.
(4) Ruin Island Fortress: the POI is placed at cx+sv*(shoreDist+0.14S). The drawn island uses waterNode+seaNormal*0.14S when WD is set, so the two disagree. For Lepon the Old, the claimed geometry is wrong. It has no sea lane, so castV=sv=E. The anchor sits on the coast ink, and mask water wraps just east of it, so the first eastward ray hits water. The island centre lands about 1.7 to 2 px E (slightly north-tilted, depending on seaNormal). The POI lands 3.4 px E. Both lie over mask water on roughly the same bearing, about 1.7 atlas px apart. That is about 220 screen px at the ruin's cityMaxZ 11. It is NOT on land and NOT 115 deg off.
Magnitude list: drop Aldorus, Medem, Reketis, Perona and Pharzeban. They are non-harbor with distPx 36-77 > 25, so drawWater is false and sv is inert (none has a river trait). Their bearing numbers reproduce, but they move nothing. Epeshu uses a canon overlay. The cities where sv actually acts, with trait-vs-mask-centroid error: Sokundo 132, Lepon 115, Tamaron 97, Tarap 53, Mago 44, Kanae 43, Thalbaen 23, Dramuz 21, Aglaz 15, Rhup 14, Mith Mirdanak 9, Kardunash 6; Shengo has no water at all. A test cast with only sv (no lane) found water for every one checked: Tarap through the +0.8 rad fallback; Sokundo, Tamaron, Kanae and Mago directly. Sokundo and Tamaron also have sea lanes. So no case of the waterfront disappearing was observed. Net effect: Shengo's phantom sea is major. Everything else (centre direction, waterfront bias, the wrong compass word in the Quays text, Lepon's POI 1.7 px beyond its island) is minor.
votes.reason: Every code anchor exists and fires as stated. sv comes from traits.sea.side even when the mask has water; the centre shift, the !WD compass coast and the sv-based Island Fortress POI all match the code. I reproduced buildCityMask in Python from the z5 tiles and got the claim's bearings to the degree. Shengo is confirmed: the anchor is on a label 'O', patch water is 0, and an east synthetic sea is drawn over land. A table reader would notice that. The claim overstates in three ways. Five of its nine magnitude cities never draw water (non-harbor, distPx > 25). Lepon's POI is not on land and not 115 deg from the island: the eastward cast hits water at once, and the POI sits about 1.7 px beyond the island on the same bearing. The 0.07S shift is by design; only its direction is wrong.

votes.corrected:
Mechanism holds and vector_independent=true is right: a vector city fed the same traits would place its coast, centre and POI along the same wrong sv. This is a registration problem, but it is not a per-zoom drift. The art is wrong at every zoom. Over a mask-melded plan it shows only as (a) the centre and quay bias and (b) a coast jump when a deep-linked synthetic plan (ensureCityGenNow, mask not yet sampled) is hot-swapped for the melded plan.

MAGNITUDE (I re-ran buildCityMask in Python on the z5 tiles; bearings match the claim within a few degrees):
- Only cities where drawWater is true are affected. drawWater = !!sv && (t.harbor || distPx<=25).
- Aldorus, Medem, Reketis, Pharzeban and Perona are all non-harbor with distPx 36-77, so drawWater is false. None has a 'beside' river, so sv is never read. Their 76-176 deg errors change nothing.
- Epeshu uses canon art, so its error is also inert.
- Cities whose bearing error is visible: Sokundo 132 deg (mask bearing ~20, NNE), Lepon the Old 115 (~335, NNW), Tamaron 97 (~353, N), Tarap 53 (~233, SW), Mago 44 (~44, NE), Kanae 43 (~47, NE). The claim leaves out Tarap, Mago and Kanae.
- Shengo: mask water fraction 0, so it gets the synthetic compass sea to the E. The shoreline sits about 0.64 atlas px E of the anchor (0.1055S - 0.07S, with S = 18 px), so sea covers about 46% of the 18-px footprint. Confirmed.
- Centre shift is 0.07*2rW: capital 3.64, town 1.96, village 1.26, ruin 1.12 atlas px. Measured against a shift away from the true water, the misplacement is 0.14*rW*2*sin(err/2): Sokundo ~3.6 px, Tamaron ~2.9, Lepon ~1.9, Tarap ~1.1, Kanae/Mago ~0.9.
- Lepon is mis-described. In the replicated mask the Lepon anchor itself is in water. The E cast from the shifted centre hits water about 0.6 atlas px E. The drawn island sits at waterNode + seaNormal*0.14S, about 2 px out, so it is roughly E/NE, not 115 deg away. The POI, 3.4 px E (0.214S*16 px), lands in mask water about 1-3 px from the drawn island, not on land.

FIX: the claim's fix is wrong.
- Nulling sea.side for a harbor makes line `var sea=(t.sea&&t.sea.side)?...:(t.harbor?pick(Object.keys(COMPASS)):null)` call pick(). That uses one extra R() draw before the mask.bear override, which shifts the whole mulberry32 stream: every street and building re-rolls. Synthetic (no-mask) plans would also get a random side.
- Nulling it for the non-harbors (Lepon, Tarap, Shengo) turns drawWater off and deletes their water.

Correct cheap fix: data only, in maps-site/data/city-traits.json, keeping the city-anchors.json sea fallback in sync.
- Set sea.side to the 16-point COMPASS name nearest the mask bearing (COMPASS takes 16 points; dirName gives only 8) for the drawWater cities above: Sokundo NNE, Tamaron N, Lepon the Old NNW, Tarap SW, Mago NE, Kanae NE.
- Check each by eye, because the r-b<=54 classifier can misread inland regions as water.
- No R() draws are added, so the stream stays aligned and determinism holds.
- For Shengo, move the anchor to its dot and drop sea, so no water is drawn.

SAFETY:
- No pinned function source changes (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask).
- cityCanvasSha, which hashes Tamaron, Sokundo AND Kanae, changes for all three.
- UG3 requires cityCanvasSha == B0 on every atlas unit, so this cannot land while the Mobile 5-9 atlas lane is mid-flight. It has to wait until after Mobile 9, or come with a central B0 rebaseline between units.
- It deliberately changes desktop rendering of these cities. Desktop and phone stay identical to each other.
- Making the Island Fortress POI use the drawn island's position (ifx, ify) is a genCityCanvas edit and breaks the atlas_fn_sha pin. Defer it until after the lane.
votes.reason: Checked genCityCanvas (the sea/sv/drawWater lines, shoreOff/inWater, castWater/waterNode, the island and Island Fortress addPoi), buildCityMask, ensureCityGen/ensureCityGenNow and traitsFor in maps-site/index.html, plus city-traits.json and docs/mobile/README.md (cityCanvasSha covers Tamaron, Sokundo, Kanae). I re-ran the mask bearings in Python on the z5 tiles. The centre-shift and Lepon POI-offset numbers are right. The bearing table is wrong: 5 of its 9 cities are inert because drawWater is false, and it omits the active Tarap, Mago and Kanae. The Lepon island-direction and POI-on-land statements do not match the replicated mask. The proposed fix is unsafe: nulling side adds a pick() R() draw that re-rolls the whole plan, nulling for non-harbors deletes their water, and the Kanae sha change plus the mid-lane timing against the UG3 cityCanvasSha==B0 gate are not mentioned.

items.summary: Rendering configuration: detectRetina lowers the base layer's maxZoom to 10.5, so on DPR>1 above z10.5 (villages, ruins, Summarch, reached by hand) the 0.12 base ghost disappears, visible mainly at plan and wash edges.

prior_record.title: On HiDPI screens the base atlas ghost vanishes above z10.5
prior_record.subsystem: base tile layer limits (makeBase / Leaflet detectRetina)
prior_record.anchor: makeBase: L.tileLayer(...,{maxNativeZoom:RETINA?deepZoom-1:deepZoom,maxZoom:Z_STREET,detectRetina:true}); Leaflet TileLayer initialize `maxZoom-1` on retina; GridLayer _setView/_pruneTiles `_removeAllTiles` when round(z)>options.maxZoom
prior_record.mechanism: RENDERING/config. detectRetina halves tileSize, bumps zoomOffset and lowers the layer's maxZoom from 11.5 to 10.5; above that tileZoom is undefined and every tile is pruned. The map's own maxZoom (cityMaxZ up to 11.0) goes deeper. enterChart already compensates ('detectRetina drops the tile layer's effective maxZoom by 1'); the world base does not.
prior_record.fires_when: DPR>=2 (all phones, Retina Macs) at z>10.5: villages (cityMaxZ 10.83), ruins (11.0), Summarch (10.78). Towns 10.19 and capitals are safe.
prior_record.visible_effect: The faint atlas ghost (coast, dot, roads at 0.12) disappears abruptly outside the plan's vignette, leaving flat #map parchment (#d9cba7); tiles return when zooming out.
prior_record.magnitude: Base opacity 0.12 to 0 across the whole viewport over the last 0.28-0.5 zoom levels (z10.5 to cityMaxZ).
prior_record.cheap_fix: In makeBase use maxZoom: RETINA?Z_STREET+1:Z_STREET (maxNativeZoom already caps URLs, so no 404s), or clamp cityMaxZ to RETINA?10.5:Z_STREET.
prior_record.fix_risks: Not pinned; non-retina desktop identical. Phone and desktop2x captures at z>10.5 gain the ghost (Mobile lane owns phone profiles and baselines). No determinism impact.

votes.corrected:
The mechanism is real, but the claim gets some details wrong.

How it works: makeBase builds every era base (modern, war, imperial) with L.tileLayer({maxNativeZoom:RETINA?deepZoom-1:deepZoom, maxZoom:Z_STREET, detectRetina:true}). On a HiDPI screen, Leaflet 1.9.4's TileLayer initialize (`detectRetina&&b.retina&&0<e.maxZoom?(e.tileSize=Math.floor(e.tileSize/2),...e.zoomOffset++,e.maxZoom=Math.max(e.minZoom,e.maxZoom-1)`) lowers the layer's options.maxZoom from 11.5 to 10.5. L.Browser.retina means devicePixelRatio>1, not >=2, so 1.25x and 1.5x Windows laptops count too.

GridLayer._setView computes tileZoom=Math.round(z) and sets it to undefined when it exceeds 10.5. That happens for every z>=10.5, because round(10.5)=11. With tileZoom undefined, _update returns early and no new tiles load when you pan. GridLayer._pruneTiles calls _removeAllTiles only when the raw map zoom is above 10.5. _setView prunes only on non-pinch, non-flyTo 'zoom'/viewreset events: _resetView passes noPrune=e.pinch||e.flyTo. So the tiles disappear when a wheel, button or keyboard zoom ends above 10.5, or when a pinch is released there. They do not disappear partway through a flyTo or pinch.

The map's own ceiling is separate: worldCityUpdate calls setMaxZoom(cityMaxZ). With GEN_SIZE 2048 that gives:
- villages: 4+log2(2048/18) = 10.83
- ruins: 11.0
- Summarch (town, 3072 px): 10.78
- other towns: 10.19
- Epēshu (capital, 3072/52): 9.88

So villages, ruins and Summarch can go deeper than 10.5; the other towns and Epēshu are safe. flyIntoCity flies to target=cz-0.5, which is at most 10.5, so arriving by fly never prunes. For a ruin it lands exactly on 10.5: the existing tiles stay but none load when panning. The ghost is lost only when the reader zooms in by hand past 10.5.

enterChart's comment already describes this exact rule for chart tile layers, and it compensates (maxZoom:def.maxz+1, map max RETINA?def.maxz:def.maxz+1). makeBase does not compensate.

Visible effect is much smaller than claimed. The base layer is fully removed, but around the city the wash covers it. The wash (pCityWash, 1.7x cityBox) is an opaque land tone at 0.94 out to 0.85 box half-width (hw), 0.5 at 1.33hw, and 0 at 1.7hw. The plan's own vignette dissolves between about 0.77hw and 0.97hw. Under the wash, the 0.12 ghost adds at most about 0.7% contrast. It only shows clearly beyond about 1.3–1.7hw from the anchor, which at z10.83 for a village is roughly 1300–1700 CSS px from centre. A phone centred on the city sees no change. You only notice it after panning well off the plan at z>10.5, or in the far corners of a large desktop window. There, faint coast and road lines fade to the flat #map parchment (#d9cba7) and come back when you zoom below 10.5.

The cheap fix is correct. Setting maxZoom:RETINA?Z_STREET+1:Z_STREET in makeBase makes the effective layer maxZoom 11.5. _clampZoom still clamps to maxNativeZoom 4, plus zoomOffset 1, so URLs stay at z5 and there are no 404s. Clamping cityMaxZ to 10.5 instead would cut retina zoom depth, so the makeBase change is the better option. Neither is in the pinned function set and neither affects determinism. It changes retina captures at z>10.5 only.

This is a rendering/config issue only, not registration: nothing moves or misaligns. It is the same for raster and vector cities.
votes.reason: Confirmed in the HEAD export at maps-site/index.html (makeBase, cityMaxZ, worldCityUpdate setMaxZoom, flyIntoCity target=cz-0.5, enterChart retina comment) and in vendored leaflet.js (TileLayer detectRetina maxZoom-1, GridLayer._setView round(z)>maxZoom → tileZoom undefined, _pruneTiles z>maxZoom → _removeAllTiles, _resetView noPrune on pinch/flyTo). On HiDPI (DPR>1, not >=2) the era base drops out at z>10.5. That zoom is reachable for villages (10.83), ruins (11.0) and Summarch (10.78) when zooming by hand; arriving by flyIntoCity never goes past 10.5. The visible effect is small. In the claim, the ghost vanishes across the whole viewport. In fact the 0.12 ghost sits under the city wash (0.94 opaque to 0.85hw, fading to 0 at 1.7hw) and the opaque plan core, so a centred view, especially on a phone, changes by under 1%. The loss only shows after panning about 1.3hw or more off the anchor at z>10.5. It moves nothing (not a registration shift). The suggested makeBase fix is sound and causes no 404s.

votes.corrected: Mechanism and fix are right; the magnitude and visible effect are overstated. MECHANISM (verified in vendor/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js): on retina, TileLayer initialize does tileSize/2, zoomOffset++ and maxZoom=max(minZoom,maxZoom-1), so makeBase's maxZoom:Z_STREET (11.5) becomes 10.5. maxNativeZoom (RETINA?4:5) is left alone. GridLayer _setView sets tileZoom to undefined once round(z)>10.5, i.e. z>=10.5, and _pruneTiles calls _removeAllTiles once map z>10.5. So the base tiles go away at z>10.5. Non-retina has maxZoom 11.5, which the map never passes. L.Browser.retina means DPR>1, not only DPR>=2. REACH (recomputed from cityMaxZ = min(11.5, 4+log2(max(w,h)/(2*FOOT_R)))): procedural GEN_SIZE 2048 gives village 10.83 (115 anchors), ruin 11.00 (3), town 10.19 and capital 9.30. Canon Summarch (town, 3072) gives 10.78 and canon Epēshu (capital, 3072) gives 9.885. So it fires in the last 0.28-0.50 zoom levels of villages, ruins and Summarch. MAGNITUDE (corrected): the base layer's own opacity does drop from 0.12 to 0, but on screen you barely see it. The base sits under the opaque plan: canon JPGs have no alpha, and procedural plans are opaque inside their vignette. It also sits under the washMake radial wash, which spans 1.7x cityBox at alpha 0.94 out to 0.5 of its radius and 0.5 at 0.78. At z10.5 a village plan is about 1630 CSS px across and its wash about 2770, so a phone viewport centred on the city lies inside the plan and the solid wash. There the lost light is about 0.12*(1-0.94) ≈ 0.7%, which you cannot see. On a 1440x900 Retina-Mac viewport the corners reach about 0.6 of the wash radius (alpha about 0.8), so the loss there is at most about 2.4%. The effect only becomes noticeable, as a missing coast/road ghost and plain wash or #d9cba7 instead, when you pan toward the plan's vignette edge or the wash fringe. Treat it as a subtle edge or pan artifact, not a viewport-wide vanish. It is a rendering/config issue, not a registration one. VECTOR_INDEPENDENT: true, since a vector city in the same cityBox would hit the same base drop. CHEAP FIX: makeBase maxZoom: RETINA?Z_STREET+1:Z_STREET is correct. It gives an effective 11.5 on retina, the same as desktop. URLs stay capped by maxNativeZoom, so there are no 404s. The map's own maxZoom option is set, so the layer maxZoom does not leak into map.getMaxZoom, and only the level zIndex shifts. It is per-instance via setOptions, covers all three BASES and leaves chart layers untouched. REJECT the alternative clamp of cityMaxZ to RETINA?10.5. At exactly z=10.5, round(10.5)=11 > 10.5 still leaves tileZoom undefined, so _update stops loading tiles on pan. It would also cut phone zoom depth and change the flyIntoCity/ensureArrival targets (cz-0.5), which is a mobile-lane behavior change. RISKS: makeBase is not among the UG3 atlas_fn_sha pins (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask) and does not affect cityCanvasSha. Non-retina desktop stays byte- and pixel-identical. No determinism impact. Retina/phone captures at z>10.5 change only at the plan/wash fringe. The edit lands in maps-site/index.html while Mobile 5-9 is mid-flight, so route it through the Mobile lane or wait for it, and expect phone/desktop2x baselines to need re-accepting.
votes.reason: The mechanism, the threshold (z>10.5 on retina) and the per-kind cityMaxZ reach (10.83/11.0/10.78/10.19) recompute correctly from Leaflet 1.9.4 and the code's constants. The primary fix is correct and safe. But the claimed 'whole viewport, ghost vanishes to flat parchment' magnitude ignores occlusion: the opaque plan plus the 0.94-alpha washMake wash hide almost all of the 0.12 base inside the viewport, so the drop is at most about 0.7-2.4% at normal framing and visible only near the plan/wash edges. The alternative cityMaxZ clamp to 10.5 is also wrong: tileZoom is still undefined at exactly 10.5, and the clamp changes phone zoom behavior.

items.summary: Gesture and lifecycle: Leaflet's default bounceAtZoomLimits lets a pinch overshoot the dynamic cap and snap back about the viewport centre (44 px at dz 0.5 and d=150, 75 px at dz 1), and the plan is only created after release.

prior_record.title: Pinch can overshoot the zoom limit and bounce back about the centre, and the plan is only created after the gesture ends
prior_record.anchor: Leaflet TouchZoom default bounceAtZoomLimits:true, _onTouchEnd -> _animateZoom(this._center,_limitZoom(zoom)); map.on('zoomend moveend',worldCityUpdate); worldOpacityUpdate on 'zoom'
prior_record.mechanism: RENDERING/lifecycle. Leaflet lets a pinch exceed getMaxZoom/minZoom (including the dynamic 8 and cityMaxZ) and animates back on touchend around this._center (the pinch-adjusted map centre), so the place under the fingers slides. worldCityUpdate (generation, overlay instantiation, setMaxZoom) runs only on zoomend/moveend, i.e. after the gesture, so during one continuous pinch from below z6.5 worldOpacityUpdate fades the base to 0.12 per frame while no overlay exists yet.
prior_record.fires_when: Touch pinch on phones and tablets near a city, especially before its plan exists (maxZoom then 8) or at cityMaxZ, or beyond minZoom.
prior_record.visible_effect: The view rubber-bands back after a deep pinch and the city recoils/slides sideways; the base fades to near-empty parchment, then the whole plan pops in at full opacity when the fingers lift (overlayOpacity(z)=1 for z>=7.8).
prior_record.magnitude: Overshoot unbounded during the gesture with a 250 ms snap-back; a point d css px from the centre slides d*(1-2^-dz): overshoot 0.5 at d=150 px = 44 px, dz=1 = 75 px (typical overshoot 0.1-0.5, 7-41% scale).
prior_record.cheap_fix: Set map option bounceAtZoomLimits:false. On 'zoom' events with e.pinch run a light path (nearestCity -> ensureCityGen + ensureCityOverlay, no setMaxZoom), throttled per rAF; prewarm for every anchor in view.
prior_record.fix_risks: The Mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) owns touch behaviour and is mid-flight, so coordinate; a hard stop replaces the rubber-band (mobile feel). Desktop identical. Not pinned.

votes.corrected:
There are two separate mechanisms here. Neither one is a REGISTRATION shift. Both hold with the corrections below.

(1) RUBBER-BAND (stock Leaflet, touch only). The atlas creates the map with L.map('map',{crs:L.CRS.Simple,minZoom:0,maxZoom:Z_STREET,...zoomSnap:0...}) in maps-site/index.html and never sets bounceAtZoomLimits, so the vendored default (true) applies. maps-site/index.html has no touch or pinch code of its own. The custom wheel handler covers mouse wheels and macOS ctrl+wheel and clamps to the live min/max, so desktop never bounces.
- In vendor/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js, TouchZoom _onTouchMove computes this._zoom=getScaleZoom(scale,startZoom). It clamps only when !bounceAtZoomLimits, so during the gesture the zoom can pass getMaxZoom() (8 in open country, or cityMaxZ near a registered city) or getMinZoom() (fitZoom) with no limit.
- _onTouchEnd then calls _animateZoom(this._center,_limitZoom(this._zoom)). this._center is the pinch-adjusted viewport centre, and the animation is a 250 ms CSS transform (setTimeout 250 -> _onZoomTransitionEnd).
- The snap-back zooms about the viewport centre. A point d css px from the centre contracts radially toward it by d*(1-2^-dz): 44 px at d=150 px with dz=0.5, and 75 px at dz=1. It does not slide sideways. The place under the fingers drifts toward the screen centre.
- Base tiles, the pCity overlay, the wash and the stubs all transform together through zoomanim. The overlay never leaves its cityBox, so nothing misregisters against the atlas.
- On their own these numbers mean little: every Leaflet map rubber-bands like this.

(2) LATE INSTANTIATION (atlas wiring). This is the real defect.
- map.on('zoom zoomend moveend',worldOpacityUpdate) runs every frame of a pinch. Leaflet _move fires 'zoom' whenever data.pinch is set. map.on('zoomend moveend',worldCityUpdate) does not fire until the gesture is over: no zoomend happens until _onZoomTransitionEnd -> _moveEnd, about 250 ms after the fingers lift.
- worldCityUpdate calls ensureCityOverlay(null) whenever z<=6.5, which removes the overlay. So if the last zoomend was at z<=6.5 and one continuous pinch then goes past 6.8, CITYVIEW.overlay is null for the whole gesture. Meanwhile baseOpacity(z) drops the base toward 0.12 (it reaches 0.12 at z8). The reader sees near-empty parchment.
- This does not depend on whether the city has a plan yet. Epēshu and Summarch are registered at init, so near them maxZoom is cityMaxZ, about 9.9, not 8.
- At lift, _animateZoom calls _move with the final zoom straight away, so base opacity jumps to its end value as the bounce starts. About 250 ms later zoomend -> worldCityUpdate -> ensureCityOverlay adds the plan at overlayOpacity(z), which is 1 when z>=7.8 (the image element has no fade). That is the pop-in.
- For a town with no plan yet, zoomend only starts ensureCityGen. The plan then waits on the sampleCityMask tile loads and genCityCanvas, and the callback calls worldCityUpdate, which raises maxZoom and adds the overlay. That pop-in comes later than 250 ms.
- One exception to "only after the gesture": that same async callback in ensureCityGen (if(!CHART.on)worldCityUpdate()) can run mid-pinch if a prewarm finishes during the gesture. Prewarm starts when z>5.6 and the view centre is within 6 footprint radii of the city. In that case the overlay appears and setMaxZoom runs in the middle of the gesture.

A vector plan wired through the same zoomend-only path would be just as absent mid-gesture, so this is vector-independent. Fixing it is a lifecycle job (instantiate on pinch 'zoom' and prewarm), not a registration job.
votes.reason:
I traced the claim through maps-site/index.html and the vendored minified Leaflet 1.9.4 (vendor/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js), and it checks out:
- bounceAtZoomLimits is not set in L.map('map',...), so the default (true) applies; the vendored leaflet.js has `bounceAtZoomLimits:!0`.
- _onTouchMove clamps only when !bounceAtZoomLimits.
- _onTouchEnd calls `_animateZoom(this._center,this._map._limitZoom(this._zoom),...)` with a 250 ms timeout.
- _move fires 'zoom' when `i&&i.pinch`.
- Events are wired as `map.on('zoom zoomend moveend',worldOpacityUpdate)` and `map.on('zoomend moveend',worldCityUpdate)`.
- worldCityUpdate calls `ensureCityOverlay((reg&&z>6.5)?near.name:null)`.
- The opacity curves match the claim: baseOpacity runs 1 to 0.12 over z6.2-8, and overlayOpacity is 1 for z>=7.8.
- The magnitude arithmetic is correct.

Corrections:
- The displacement is a radial contraction toward the viewport centre, not a sideways slide.
- "maxZoom then 8" applies only to towns without a plan. Canon Epēshu and Summarch are registered at init, so their cap is cityMaxZ (about 9.9).
- The overlay is missing whenever the last zoomend was at z<=6.5, whether or not the city has a plan.
- The pop-in comes about 250 ms after lift, or later for a town whose plan is still being made.
- The ensureCityGen async callback can run worldCityUpdate mid-pinch, so "only after the gesture" has one exception.

On severity: the major rating rests on mechanism 2. On a phone, a deep pinch fades the base to blank parchment and the plan then pops in at full opacity, which a reader at the table would notice. The rubber-band on its own would be minor, since it is what every Leaflet map does on touch. Neither mechanism misregisters art against the atlas, because the whole frame moves together. Both are about rendering and lifecycle, not REGISTRATION, and both would behave the same with a vector plan.

votes.corrected:
MECHANISM: confirmed against vendor/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js. TouchZoom._onTouchMove sets zoom = getScaleZoom(ratio, startZoom) with no upper limit, and clamps it only when bounceAtZoomLimits is false (the default is true). _onTouchEnd calls _animateZoom(this._center, _limitZoom(this._zoom)), which scales back about the viewport centre. The fixed point of the 250 ms leaflet-zoom-anim transition is the viewport centre, not the pinch midpoint, so the place under the fingers slides.

MAGNITUDE: recomputed, and it holds. A point d css px from the viewport centre slides d*(1-2^-dz) toward the centre: dz=0.5 at d=150 gives 43.9 px, and dz=1 gives 75 px. dz 0.1-0.5 is a 7-41% scale overshoot. The overshoot has no bound while the gesture lasts, so dz>1 is likely when the cap is Z_OPEN_MAX=8 and the reader is aiming for the city depth. For a capital, cityMaxZ = 4+log2(3072/52) ≈ 9.9.

TWO SCOPE CORRECTIONS:
(1) The cap is 8 only while registryFor(nearest) is null. If the plan was prewarmed at z>5.6 within 6*FOOT_R, maxZoom is already cityMaxZ.
(2) At z=7.8 the base opacity is 0.22, and it reaches 0.12 only at z>=8. After touchend, worldCityUpdate creates the overlay only if a plan is already registered. Otherwise ensureCityGen loads z5 tiles asynchronously, and its callback calls worldCityUpdate, which builds the overlay at overlayOpacity(z)=1. So the plan pops in at full opacity either at zoomend or shortly after it.

vector_independent=true is right. This is gesture lifecycle, not registration. A vector city rubber-bands and pops in exactly the same way, and neither medium touches cityBox alignment.

CORRECTED CHEAP FIX:
(a) Keep bounceAtZoomLimits:false. It is correct and safe. _onTouchMove then clamps to e._limitZoom and still computes _center from _pinchStartLatLng at the clamped zoom, so the pinch midpoint stays under the fingers and nothing slides on lift. It reads getMaxZoom() on every move, so if maxZoom rises mid-gesture the reader can keep pinching. It affects only the TouchZoom handler: desktop mouse, wheel and trackpad paths are unchanged (touchscreen laptops lose the rubber-band too). It edits no UG3-pinned function, and cityCanvasSha and determinism are unaffected.

(b) Drop the light path as written. ensureCityGen cannot be called "without setMaxZoom": its sampleCityMask callback ends with worldCityUpdate(), which calls setMaxZoom. If that lowers the cap below the current zoom, Leaflet does setZoom in the middle of the touch. Generating mid-gesture also runs a synchronous genCityCanvas on the 2048² canvas, plus JPEG encoding, inside the pinch. That breaks the code's own rule ('never mid-fly') and would land in the Mobile atlas lane's pinch LoAF/long-frame captures (docs/mobile/units.json, the 'night-mode pinch measured on phones' unit). Prewarming every anchor in view at z~5.6 costs unbounded CPU and memory on a phone.

Safe version:
- On 'zoom' with e.pinch, at most once per rAF, call ensureCityOverlay(near) ONLY when CITYREG[near] already exists and z>6.5. This is an instant layer add with no generation.
- Move the existing PREWARMED idle prewarm (nearest city only, within 6*FOOT_R, z>5.6) so it also runs on pinch 'zoom' events, not just zoomend/moveend.
- In ensureCityGen's callback, defer worldCityUpdate while map.touchZoom._zooming or map._animatingZoom is set; the next zoomend runs it anyway.
- Optionally ramp a newly created overlay's opacity from 0 over ~200 ms so it never pops in at 1.

None of these edits touch xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask. Every change sits in maps-site/index.html, where Mobile 5-9 is in flight, so it must wait for or be scheduled with that lane, and the pinch captures must be re-run.
votes.reason: The mechanism, the visible effect and the magnitude check out against the vendored Leaflet 1.9.4 and the atlas constants: d*(1-2^-dz) gives 43.9 px for dz=0.5 at d=150 and 75 px for dz=1, with a 250 ms snap-back. vector_independent=true is correct. Two scope details are off. The cap is 8 only when no plan is registered for the nearest city, and the base is at 0.22, not 0.12, at z7.8. bounceAtZoomLimits:false is a correct, touch-only fix that touches no pin. The rest of the cheap fix is wrong and unsafe. ensureCityGen's async callback always calls worldCityUpdate and therefore setMaxZoom, so "no setMaxZoom" can't be achieved through it. Generating mid-pinch puts a synchronous genCityCanvas on the 2048² canvas, plus JPEG encoding, inside the gesture, against the code's "never mid-fly" rule and the mobile lane's pinch long-frame captures. Prewarming every anchor in view has no bound. Because part of the fix is wrong, holds=false. Severity is minor: this is a phone-only gesture-lifecycle artifact, not the registration misalignment the owner reported.

items.summary: RENDERING MEDIUM: Leaflet's SVG renderer only CSS-scales its container during flyTo and pinch and re-projects at zoomend, so road stubs and routes balloon (stubs up to about x250 on flies into generated cities) and then snap; a stock Leaflet vector city would inherit this.

prior_record.title: Leaflet SVG vector layers (route, ways, stubs, trail) are CSS-scaled from their pre-fly projection during flyTo and pinch, then snap at moveend
prior_record.anchor: Leaflet Renderer getEvents {zoom:this._onZoom, moveend:this._update, zoomend:_onZoomEnd} -> _updateTransform (scale=getZoomScale(zoom,this._zoom)); Polyline smoothFactor 1; buildCityStubs in pane 'pCity'; flyIntoCity adds stubs eagerly via ensureCityOverlay before flyTo
prior_record.mechanism: RENDERING (medium-dependent). The per-pane SVG renderer re-projects only at viewreset/moveend. On each 'zoom' frame of flyTo or a touch pinch it CSS-scales the old drawing, so strokes, casings and dashes magnify by 2^dz, vertices stay rounded/simplified at the start zoom, and paths clipped at the old bounds (+10% padding) stay missing until redraw. Image overlays and markers re-place every frame, so vectors also drift against them. Wheel zoom is exempt (setZoomAround(animate:false) -> _resetView re-renders). Raster plans do not bloom; a Leaflet-SVG vector city would inherit it, a per-frame canvas layer redrawn on 'zoom' would not.
prior_record.fires_when: flyIntoCity (Descend, #chart deep links), flyToMarker, goWaypoint, search pick, ensureArrival path, and touch pinch, while SVG panes (or stubs) are visible.
prior_record.visible_effect: Roads, borders, route and trail thicken and blur as the camera dives and stretch their dashes, city stubs become huge bars, then snap thin at arrival; on pinch-out lines are cut at the old viewport edge until release.
prior_record.magnitude: Stroke x 2^(z-z_start): fit 2.55-2.6 to tier-d 7.5 = x30-31 (route 3 px to ~90 px; 2.4-px way to 74 px); peak flyTo 2.55 to 9.4 = x115; stubs (6-px casing) from z5 to 9.385 = x21 (126 px), from 2.6 to Sokundo's 9.69 = x137 (~690-820 px). Pinch dz=1 doubles width. Vertex error 0.5 px + simplification <=1 px, times 2^dz.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Today: add stubs on landing (moveend/ensureArrival) instead of before the fly, hide SVG panes with a 'flying' class until moveend, or give pCity its own L.canvas/renderer redrawn on 'zoom' (cheap for 2 polylines; smoothFactor:0). For a future vector city: a custom canvas/WebGL layer redrawn every 'zoom' frame with stroke widths in screen px, never stock L.svg/L.Canvas paths.
prior_record.fix_risks: Not pinned. Per-frame re-projection costs CPU on phones (Mobile lane budgets); overriding renderer internals ties code to Leaflet 1.9.4; living-chart owns fly motion; filigree owns stroke styling (slice C pooled edges). This is the key caveat for the 'vector city' proposal: stock renderers are crisp only at rest.

votes.corrected:
RENDERING (medium-dependent), transient only. It moves nothing at rest and is not the cityBox registration fault. The vendored Leaflet 1.9.4 (maps-site/vendor/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js) Renderer has getEvents {viewreset:_reset, zoom:_onZoom, moveend:_update, zoomend:_onZoomEnd} (+zoomanim:_onAnimZoom). _onZoom/_onAnimZoom call _updateTransform, which sets a CSS transform on the per-pane SVG with scale=getZoomScale(zoom,this._zoom) and padding .1. Paths are re-projected at zoomend (_onZoomEnd -> _project) and redrawn at moveend (Renderer _update fires 'update' -> _updatePaths). Both happen in the same tick at the end of a move. No vector-effect:non-scaling-stroke is set anywhere, so on every flyTo frame (map._move fires 'zoom') strokes, casings and dashes scale by 2^(z - z_start). Vertices keep their start-zoom rounding (0.5 px) and smoothFactor-1 simplification (<=1 px), both times 2^dz. The SVG extent stays the old bounds (viewport x1.2). ImageOverlay ({zoom:_reset}) and markers re-place every frame. The shapes stay registered because the transform math is exact; only the stroke weight and the small vertex error drift, and they snap back at moveend.

WHERE IT SHOWS:
(a) Route, way, lane, trail, district and realm panes (pRouteLine/pWay/pLane/pTrail/pDistrict/pRealm) are hidden at z>=Z_TIER_D 7.5 (.map-tier-d opacity:0!important, .2s fade, class toggled per 'zoom' frame by worldOpacityUpdate). Their bloom therefore peaks at about x30 when flyIntoCity starts from fit 2.55-2.6: route 3 px to about 90 px, way 2.4 px to about 73 px, way casing 5 px to about 150 px. Then they fade out.
(b) The x100+ peaks apply only to the panes that are never hidden. pCity has only a .25s opacity transition. Its city stubs are added eagerly by ensureCityOverlay(key) one rAF before map.flyTo, at opacity .5/.6, and are drawn above the city overlay. pJTrail (journey trail, weight 4) is not in the tier-d list either.
(c) Stubs exist only when reg.prov==='invented' (buildCityStubs returns null for canon Epēshu and Summarch). So the claim's "z5 to 9.385" example is wrong: 9.385 is the canon Epēshu/Summarch target, and those have no stubs. Generated fly targets are cityMaxZ-0.5 with GEN_SIZE 2048: capital 8.80, town 9.69 (Sokundo, x137 from 2.6, a 6-px casing about 820 px wide), village 10.33, ruin 10.5. From z5 to Sokundo the factor is x25.6 (about 154 px). A stub is only drawn at the start if the city lies inside the renderer bounds; otherwise it is clipped and first appears at moveend.
(d) Other flyTo callers (goWaypoint, flyToMarker, the panel flyTo helper, search/gazetteer picks) go to tierZoom/revealZoom, so dz is smaller. The x30/x115 figures belong to flyIntoCity (Descend, #chart deep links).
(e) ensureArrival does not cause the bloom: it calls setView(animate:false), which runs _resetView and redraws synchronously, so it ends a bloom.
(f) Touch pinch: _onTouchMove calls _move({pinch:true}), which fires 'zoom' and CSS-scales. On release, zoomAnimation (default on) runs _animateZoom -> zoomanim, still CSS-scaled, and the redraw comes only after the ~250 ms transition. During pinch-out, paths are cut at the old bounds until then.
(g) The custom wheel handler (scrollWheelZoom disabled) calls setZoomAround(..,{animate:false}) -> _resetView, so wheel zoom never blooms. Zoom buttons, double-click and keyboard go through zoomanim for about 250 ms (zoomDelta .25 gives x1.19; double-click gives x2).
(h) "Blur" depends on the browser. Thickening and dash stretch are certain.

VERDICT: a raster plan does not bloom. A future vector city drawn with stock L.svg/L.canvas paths would inherit the bloom; a layer redrawn on every 'zoom' frame with screen-px widths, or hiding SVG panes while flying, would avoid it.
votes.reason:
I traced the whole code path. In the vendored minified Leaflet 1.9.4, Renderer.getEvents, _updateTransform (getZoomScale applied as a CSS scale), _onZoomEnd->_project, on("update",_updatePaths), the per-frame _move in flyTo firing 'zoom', the pinch _move in _onTouchMove, and the ImageOverlay/Marker per-'zoom' resets all exist as described. In maps-site/index.html, ensureCityOverlay (which adds buildCityStubs in pCity) runs before the rAF-deferred map.flyTo in flyIntoCity. The custom wheel handler uses setZoomAround animate:false (_resetView), so wheel zoom is exempt. No vector-effect is set. pCity and pJTrail have no hiding rule, so the stubs and the journey trail are on screen for the whole dive. The core claim therefore holds.

Corrections:
- Tier-d (z>=7.5) hides the route, way, lane and trail panes, so their bloom tops out near x30.
- The "z5 to 9.385" stub example is wrong. That is the canon Epēshu/Summarch target, and buildCityStubs gives no stubs for canon cities. The generated town target is 9.69 and capital 8.80.
- ensureArrival ends a bloom rather than causing one (setView animate:false).
- After a pinch, the redraw waits for the ~250 ms zoomanim transition.
- The x30+ magnitudes belong to flyIntoCity; other fly paths have smaller dz.
- Blur depends on the browser.

Severity is major. The effect is transient, a rendering artifact that is not an at-rest misregistration, but over the 1.4 s descent the roads swell to ~90 px before fading. For generated cities, a semi-transparent stub bar hundreds of px wide sits over the city plan until the snap at moveend. A player at the table would notice that.

votes.corrected: MECHANISM (confirmed, with fixes): vendored leaflet@1.9.4 Renderer getEvents {viewreset:_reset, zoom:_onZoom, moveend:_update, zoomend:_onZoomEnd} (+zoomanim:_onAnimZoom). _onZoom -> _updateTransform CSS-scales the SVG drawn at the renderer's last _update zoom. ImageOverlay ({zoom:_reset}), TileLayer ({zoom:_resetView}) and markers re-place on every flyTo/pinch 'zoom' frame. So on flyTo and touch pinch (TouchZoom _onTouchMove -> map._move per rAF), strokes, casings and dashes grow by 2^dz and redraw at moveend. On pinch-out, paths stay clipped to the old bounds (padding 0.1). WHEEL IS NOT EXEMPT, and the claim's reason is wrong. setZoomAround -> setView has no animate:false. With zoomAnimation on, a wheel step is a 250 ms zoomanim in which SVG (_onAnimZoom), overlay, tiles and markers all CSS-scale together, then redraw at zoomend. That is coherent and brief, with no drift between layers. Soften "blur": during flyTo the base tiles are upscaled too. The vector-specific signs are stroke and dash growth plus the snap on landing. MAGNITUDE. Write it in terms of fitZoom, because fillZoom depends on map height (≈2.55 at ~800 px tall, ≈2.98 at 1080, lower on phones). (a) Route, ways, trail, lanes and districts: worldOpacityUpdate toggles map-tier-d on every 'zoom' frame. At z>=7.5 those panes go to opacity:0 !important. So the most they grow is 2^(7.5-fit) ≈ x31 (route 3 -> ~93 px, way 2.4 -> ~74 px), and then they vanish. "Peak x115" does not apply to them. (b) flyToMarker, goWaypoint, search pick and company flyTo all fly to tierZoom('c') = fit + 2(TIER_CEIL - fit)/3, about 4.85 (TIER_CEIL 6) or 4.18 (retina). That is only about x5 or x3. If the reader is already deeper, a same-zoom flyTo still zooms out and back in (van Wijk), so lines thin and show the old clip edge mid-flight. (c) Stubs exist only for prov 'invented' plans. 9.385 is the target for Epēshu, which is prov:'canon' and has no stubs. Invented plans use GEN_SIZE 2048, so cityMaxZ - 0.5 gives targets of capital 8.80, town 9.69, village 10.33, ruin 10.5. From fit 2.55 that is about x76, x140, x220 and x250. The 6 px casing reaches ~460, ~840, ~1300 and ~1500 px. From z5: capital x14 (84 px), town x26. The real peak is x~250, not x115. (d) Position jump: latLngToLayerPoint rounds vertices and the pixel origin at the start zoom (up to ~1 px combined), and the CSS scale multiplies that offset. At a town arrival (x~140) a stub can sit tens of screen px off the overlay until moveend snaps it. This is the one symptom here that an owner would read as "things shift". KEY DISTINCTION: this is about the rendering medium, not registration. It only happens in transit, plus one snap on landing. At rest nothing is misregistered, so it does not explain the resting "doesn't anchor" complaint. vector_independent:false stands: raster overlays don't bloom; a Leaflet-SVG city or a stock L.canvas city would inherit it. FIX (corrected): 1. Moving stubs to landing needs restructuring. ensureCityOverlay returns early when CITYVIEW.name===key, so worldCityUpdate at moveend would never add them. Split the stub add out of ensureCityOverlay into a guarded moveend-only step. Keep the eager overlay fade-in. 2. A stock L.canvas renderer does NOT fix it. It inherits the same Renderer._onZoom -> _updateTransform. It only works with a private override of _onZoom that calls _reset/_update each frame (ties the code to 1.9.4). smoothFactor:0 does nothing for 2-point stubs. 3. Any hide-during-flight CSS must target the svg inside .leaflet-pCity-pane, not the whole pane, because the pane also holds the overlay . Key it on zoom drift against the renderer's start zoom (e.g. |dz|>0.25) or limit it to pCity. A plain zoomstart class would make route/ways flicker on every wheel tick and hide them during every flyToMarker. 4. For a future vector city: draw it on a custom canvas/WebGL layer redrawn every 'zoom' frame, with stroke widths in screen px. SAFETY: none of this touches xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask, or the canvas pixels. UG3 atlas_fn_sha and cityCanvasSha hold. No gen code changes, so determinism holds. The at-rest view is identical, so desktop identity holds. Only the in-flight look changes. Sequence it after the atlas Mobile lane (5-9, mid-flight in maps-site/index.html). Stroke styling belongs to filigree slice C; fly motion belongs to living-chart.
votes.reason: The mechanism, the anchor and vector_independent:false all check out against vendored Leaflet 1.9.4 (Renderer zoom:_onZoom CSS scale vs ImageOverlay zoom:_reset) and maps-site/index.html (buildCityStubs in pCity, eager ensureCityOverlay in flyIntoCity). The magnitudes are wrong: x21/9.385 is paired with Epēshu, which is canon and has no stubs. Invented plans reach 8.80, 9.69, 10.33 and 10.5, so the peak is about x250, not x115. Route and ways vanish at tier-d 7.5. Marker, waypoint and search flies only reach tierZoom('c'), about x3-5. The claim that wheel zoom is exempt via animate:false is wrong. Two of the fixes don't work as written: a stock L.canvas renderer CSS-scales the same way, and adding stubs at landing is blocked by ensureCityOverlay's early return. Not pinned, no determinism or at-rest risk. This only happens in transit, so it is not a registration cause.

items.summary: Lifecycle: #view deep links are clamped because worldCityUpdate runs before handleHash and the writer rounds the centre to whole atlas px; the checks disagree on the boot cap (the holding check finds maxBounds keeps the boot centre away from every anchor so every link deeper than z8 lands at 8, Epēshu included; the dissent assumed Epēshu's 9.885 cap, giving losses up to dz 3.0 for generated ruins and up to 0.89 at Summarch), so a probe is needed.

prior_record.title: #view deep links lose their zoom (clamped by the boot or unregistered-city maxZoom, then rewritten) and round the centre to whole atlas px
prior_record.subsystem: deep link / URL state (handleHash #view, moveend hash writer, worldCityUpdate)
prior_record.anchor: handleHash: `map.setView(px(+v[1],+v[2]),+v[3],{animate:false})` run after boot worldCityUpdate; moveend writer `setHash('#view='+c.x.toFixed(0)+','+c.y.toFixed(0)+','+map.getZoom().toFixed(2))`
prior_record.mechanism: Lifecycle/serialisation. (a) At load worldCityUpdate runs before handleHash with the boot centre (EPESHU [1222,1404], 17.9 px from Epēshu's anchor), so maxZoom is Epēshu's 9.885 (or 8 elsewhere) and setView's _limitZoom clamps the link. (b) The landing moveend runs worldCityUpdate for the linked city whose plan is not generated yet (reg null), so setMaxZoom(8) eases down; when the plan registers only the cap rises and the zoom is never restored; the writer then rewrites the shared URL with the lower zoom. (c) The writer rounds the centre to integer atlas px and zoom to 0.01.
prior_record.fires_when: Opening or sharing any #view= link deeper than 9.885 anywhere, deeper than 8 at any non-Epēshu city (Summarch too); the rounding applies to every #view link.
prior_record.visible_effect: A shared street-depth view opens several levels zoomed out, the URL silently changes, and a reloaded deep view sits visibly off-centre.
prior_record.magnitude: dz up to 3.0 (x8; 3.5, x11 against Z_STREET) for generated cities; 0.6-1.6 above Epēshu's 9.885 cap; shim: #view=2014,767,10.5 landed at z8.00 (dz 2.5, x5.7). Centre rounding <=0.5 atlas px per axis: 29.5 px at 9.885, 32 px at z10, <=57-64 px at 10.83-11, 90 px at Z_STREET 11.5 (<=81 px diagonal at 10.83); zoom quantum 0.005 = 0.35% scale (~2 px at a 1200-px edge).
prior_record.cheap_fix: In the #view branch find nearestCity(x,y), call ensureCityGenNow and raise maxZoom to cityMaxZ before setView (as flyIntoCity does); skip the moveend hash write until the deep link settles; write x,y with toFixed(1-2) (or precision from zoom) and zoom toFixed(3). Parser already accepts decimals.
prior_record.fix_risks: ensureCityGenNow on boot costs a synchronous 2048^2 draw (phones) and brings the synthetic-to-melded swap. Old links stay valid; hash format gains decimals. Not pinned (genCityCanvas not modified). Mobile-capture profiles that load #view URLs change zoom and need rebaselining.

votes.corrected: The effect is real and vector-independent, and it is worse than claimed. Part (a) is wrong about the boot cap. The boot centre is not near Epēshu. maps-site/index.html sets maxBounds(contentBounds) before `map.setView(px(EPESHU[0],EPESHU[1]),fitZoom,{animate:false})`. At fitZoom (fillZoom) the atlas height fills the viewport, so Leaflet 1.9.4 setView→_limitCenter clamps the centre's y to about 1095-1130. On landscape screens it also clamps x to the half-width, about 1900-2150. The boot centre therefore lies 107-150 atlas px from the nearest anchor, outside nearestCity's 3·footR radius (78 for a capital) at every viewport I computed, phones included. So the boot `worldCityUpdate(); handleHash();` call sets maxZoom to Z_OPEN_MAX = 8, not Epēshu's 9.885. The `#view` branch `map.setView(px(+v[1],+v[2]),+v[3],{animate:false})` then runs _limitZoom, which has no snap because zoomSnap is 0, and clamps EVERY #view link deeper than 8 to exactly 8, including Epēshu and Summarch. This matches the shim result 2014,767,10.5 → z8.00. Part (b): the landing moveend runs worldCityUpdate. Epēshu and Summarch are canon overlays registered at boot by meshedWorldInit, so the cap rises at once to cityMaxZ: 9.885 for Epēshu, and 4+log2(3072/28)=10.78 for Summarch, which is not "8 because unregistered". Generated cities get their cap raised only when ensureCityGen's async sampleCityMask callback lands. In every case the zoom stays at 8 and is never restored. The moveend writer is registered after worldCityUpdate, and because location.hash still starts with #view= it calls `setHash('#view='+c.x.toFixed(0)+','+c.y.toFixed(0)+','+map.getZoom().toFixed(2))` and rewrites the shared URL with z 8.00. A #view pasted later in the same tab goes through hashchange→handleHash and is clamped by whatever maxZoom the current position allows. Part (c) is correct. The centre is rounded to whole atlas px (≤0.5 px per axis = 0.5·2^(z−4) screen px: 8 px at z8, 29.5 at 9.885, 90 at 11.5) and zoom to 0.01 (≤0.005, 0.35% scale). Because of the clamp, the rounding is latent today: a reload lands at z8, where it is at most 8 px per axis. It becomes up to 29-90 px once the clamp is fixed. Magnitude: dz up to 3.5 (11.5→8, ×11) for any city, 1.885 (×3.7) at Epēshu's cap, 2.78 at Summarch. Cheap fix still applies: in the #view branch, call nearestCity(x,y) and ensureCityGenNow(key), and raise maxZoom to cityMaxZ before setView, as flyIntoCity does. Gate the moveend writer until the link settles. Write x,y with decimals and zoom with toFixed(3).
votes.reason: Code path confirmed in maps-site/index.html. The boot order is `worldCityUpdate(); handleHash();`. The #view branch uses setView with animate:false, which runs Leaflet _limitZoom/_limitCenter with zoomSnap 0. The moveend writer calls setHash with toFixed(0)/toFixed(2), and worldCityUpdate computes allowed = reg ? cityMaxZ : Z_OPEN_MAX. One part of the claim is wrong: the boot maxZoom is not Epēshu's 9.885. maxBounds clamps the fitZoom boot centre to y≈1100, about 107-150 px from any anchor, so nearestCity returns null and the cap is 8 at every viewport. This makes every #view deeper than 8 clamp to 8, Epēshu included. Summarch is a canon overlay registered at boot, not an unregistered city. The rest holds: the zoom is never restored, the URL is rewritten lower, and the centre and zoom are rounded. A shared deep view that opens up to 3.5 zoom levels out is plainly visible at the table. The bug is in URL state, so the rendering medium (raster or vector) does not affect it.

votes.corrected:
The mechanism is right (checked in maps-site/index.html at HEAD). Boot runs `worldCityUpdate(); handleHash();` with the centre at EPESHU [1222,1404], which is 17.9 px from Epēshu's anchor (1236.1,1415), well inside 3*26. Epēshu's canon reg (w2863,h3072) gives cityMaxZ = 4+log2(3072/52) = 9.885. `map.setView(px(+v[1],+v[2]),+v[3],{animate:false})` therefore clamps to 9.885. On the landing moveend, a city with no registered plan gets `allowed=Z_OPEN_MAX` 8, and `setMaxZoom` eases down. When sampleCityMask lands, worldCityUpdate only raises the cap and never restores the zoom. The moveend writer then rewrites the hash.

**Magnitude needs three corrections.**
1. **Epēshu is not a loss.** Its own design ceiling is 9.885 (cityMaxZ), so a link deeper than that cannot be reached at Epēshu by design, and the writer can never produce one there. The claimed "0.6-1.6 above Epēshu's cap" should be dropped.
2. **Summarch does not drop to 8.** Its canon overlay is registered in meshedWorldInit before handleHash (town, 3072x2859), so its cap is 4+log2(3072/28) = 10.78. Only the boot clamp (a) applies: a link up to 10.78 lands at 9.885, a loss of dz up to 0.89 (x1.86). The cap then rises to 10.78 and the zoom is not restored.
3. **Generated cities (GEN_SIZE 2048, all 'invented') land at exactly z8.** The loss is dz = link - 8, bounded by the city's own cap:
   - town 4+log2(2048/28) = 10.19, so dz up to 2.19 (x4.6)
   - village 10.83, so dz up to 2.83 (x7.1)
   - ruin 11.0, so dz up to 3.0 (x8)
   
   The "3.5 vs Z_STREET" figure is unreachable, because no generated city's cap exceeds 11.0. The Paga shim (village at 2014,767) is consistent: 10.5 to 8.00, dz 2.5, x5.66.

In open country (no city within 3 footprint radii) links deeper than 8 fall to 8 by design (Z_OPEN_MAX), so that is not a bug.

The rounding figures are correct. Error is at most 0.5 atlas px per axis, which is 0.5*2^(z-4) screen px: 29.5 at 9.885, 32 at z10, 57 at 10.83, 64 at 11, 90 at 11.5, and 80.5 px diagonal at 10.83. The toFixed(2) zoom quantum gives at most 0.005 error, about 0.35% scale.

**vector_independent: true is right.** This is URL and lifecycle state; a vector city with an asynchronous registration step behaves the same way.

**The fix is right with refinements.** In the #view branch:
1. Parse x, y and z, then run `near=nearestCity(x,y)` on the link's coordinates, not the current centre.
2. If `near`:
   - call `ensureCityGen(near.name)` (melded, async) and then `ensureCityGenNow(near.name)` (a no-op when a reg already exists, as for Epēshu and Summarch), exactly as flyIntoCity does
   - set `cz=cityMaxZ(near.a,reg.w,reg.h)`, and `if(map.getMaxZoom()<cz)map.setMaxZoom(cz)`
3. Then call setView.

This also fixes Summarch, whose problem is the cap and not generation. With the cap raised, the following moveend's worldCityUpdate keeps `allowed=cz`, so the zoom survives. A "skip the hash write until settled" guard becomes unnecessary; if one is added, it must be a one-shot that never suppresses later writes.

Writer: change to `c.x.toFixed(1)` / `c.y.toFixed(1)` (enough for street zoom, under 9 px) and zoom `toFixed(3)`. The parser regex `[-\d.]+` already accepts decimals, and old links stay valid.

**Safety.**
- **UG3 pins:** unaffected. xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask are not touched.
- **Determinism:** unaffected. No new RNG or clock use in generation code, and ensureCityGenNow already runs on the #chart path.
- **Desktop identity:** no-hash loads are unchanged.
- **Mobile lane:** no tools/mobile-capture.js profile loads a #view URL (all its page.goto calls use plain or #s= URLs). The claimed "profiles that load #view need rebaselining" risk is moot. The real side effect is that recorded tap rows hold writer output, e.g. docs/mobile/baseline.json opened_hash "#view=1236,1417,3.30". The new decimal format changes those strings, though the scorer still classes them as 'other', so the counts hold. The edit also lands in maps-site/index.html, which the mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) is editing mid-flight, so it must be sequenced after that lane or folded into it.
- **Cost:** a synchronous 2048² draw on a cold #view load at a generated city, followed by the synthetic-to-melded hot-swap. This is the same cost flyIntoCity already pays.
votes.reason:
The mechanism is confirmed in the code, but the magnitude is wrong in two places:
- **Epēshu:** 9.885 is its own designed cityMaxZ. Links deeper than that cannot be reached or written there, so no zoom is lost.
- **Summarch:** it is canon-registered before handleHash, so it is clamped to 9.885, not 8. That is a loss of dz up to 0.89, not up to 3.

The dz-3.0 figure applies only to generated ruins. The bounds by kind are town 2.19, village 2.83 and ruin 3.0; the 3.5 figure is unreachable.

The rounding numbers and vector_independent=true are correct. The fix is sound but should take nearestCity from the link's x,y, raise the cap for every registered city (not only generated ones), and also call ensureCityGen. The skip-write step is unnecessary.

One fix risk is wrong: no capture profile loads #view URLs. The real side effects are:
- the opened_hash strings recorded in the baseline change format
- the edit has to be sequenced with the in-flight mobile atlas lane on maps-site/index.html

UG3 pins, determinism and desktop no-hash loads are unaffected.

items.summary: Refuted: a marker click never flies, so there is no lateral slide from the dot; the remaining error is anchor-on-label at arrival, and flying to the marker would strand the view off the plan.

prior_record.title: 'Descend' flies from the clicked dot to the anchor, sliding sideways
prior_record.anchor: flyToMarker: map.flyTo(m._mk.getLatLng(),...); flyIntoCity: `var dest=px(a.atlasX,a.atlasY)`
prior_record.mechanism: REGISTRATION. The place card opens from the marker, centred on the dot at tier C; Descend targets the anchor, which for label-anchored cities is the label, so the van Wijk fly contains a lateral pan equal to the anchor offset.
prior_record.fires_when: Clicking a settlement, then 'Descend into ...', for the off-dot cities.
prior_record.visible_effect: The camera drifts off the town you clicked onto its name while diving.
prior_record.magnitude: Equal to the anchor offset 7.8-69.1 atlas px: 22-195 screen px at a tier-C start of z5.5 (x2.83), growing through the dive.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Fixed by anchor-on-label. Interim: flyIntoCity uses dest = marker latlng when a Settlements marker exists within 3*FOOT_R.
prior_record.fix_risks: None beyond anchor-on-label. Not pinned.

votes.corrected:
REGISTRATION, and the same defect as anchor-on-label rather than a separate mechanism. In maps-site/index.html, a plain marker click (`mk.on('click',function(){openPlace(m);})` in buildMarkers) only opens the card. It does not fly and does not re-centre (showPanel just toggles classes). So "the card opens centred on the dot at tier C" is false for the click path the claim names. The dot-centred start only happens on the paths that call flyToMarker before openPlace: openPlaceByName, search results (`else{flyToMarker(m);openPlace(m);}`), the #place deep-link branch, the chart back-link and ATLAS.fly. flyToMarker targets `m._mk.getLatLng()`, which is `px(clampToFrame(m.x,m.y))`, at revealZoom('Settlements'), which is tier C. For a plain click, Descend (`flyIntoCity(akey,0)`) flies from wherever the view happens to be, so any pan is just the user's own framing. On every path the fly ends at `dest=px(a.atlasX,a.atlasY)`, zoom `max(z, cityMaxZ-0.5)`, which is where cityBox centres the overlay. The endpoint therefore agrees with the art. What disagrees with the art is the ring-dot.

Measured marker-to-anchor offsets: 39 of the 121 same-name pairs are more than 5 px apart, from 7.8 px (Tamaron) to 69.1 px (Damoklir). Penthelon's 112.8 px is a deliberate override. On the flyToMarker paths, the lateral component at the tier-C start is offset × 2^(zC−4). tierZoom('c') = fitZoom + 2(TIER_CEIL−fitZoom)/3 with TIER_CEIL 6 (5 on retina), which lands around z4.2-5.0, not z5.5. That gives ×1.15-2.0, about 9-138 screen px, not 22-195. The dot drifts off-centre as the dive deepens because the anchor, and the art centred on it, is off the dot. That is anchor-on-label seen in motion.

The proposed interim fix (dest = marker latlng) is harmful. It would end the fly on the dot while the overlay stays centred on the anchor. At village cityMaxZ−0.5 ≈ z10.3 (×~80), a 69 px offset is about 5.5k screen px, so the reader lands off the 18-px-wide (≈1.4k screen px) plan. The only correct fix is the data fix in anchor-on-label: move the anchors onto the ring and re-measure sea/harbor. That changes cityCanvasSha for the moved generated cities, so it needs an owner-approved rebaseline. Vector-independent: yes.
votes.reason: The code path is partly as claimed: flyIntoCity's dest is the anchor, and the anchors really are 7.8-69.1 px off the dot for 39 cities. But the stated trigger (click a settlement, then Descend) is wrong: the click handler calls only openPlace, and openPlace/showPanel never fly or re-centre. A dot-centred start happens only on the flyToMarker paths (search, openPlaceByName, deep link, ATLAS.fly). Tier C is about z4.2-5.0, not z5.5, so the start offset is about 9-138 px. The fly's endpoint matches the anchor-centred overlay, so the visible error is anchor-on-label, not a fly-specific slide. The cheap fix (dest = marker) would strand the reader thousands of px from the art at cityMaxZ. Any lateral component is mixed into a 1.4 s van Wijk zoom-pan, so as a separate effect it is subtle (minor); the underlying defect it shows is already covered by anchor-on-label.

votes.corrected:
MECHANISM (partly right, REGISTRATION): Descend calls flyIntoCity(akey,0) with dest=px(a.atlasX,a.atlasY), while the Settlements/LESSER glyph sits at the maps_markers.json x,y (both via px()). Where the two differ, the descent ends centred on the anchor, not on the glyph that was clicked. But the claimed start state is wrong. A direct marker click is mk.on('click',function(){openPlace(m);}) and does not fly. flyToMarker runs only from search, openPlaceByName, the hash and ANNALS.fly. After a plain click the opening lateral pan goes from wherever the view already was to the anchor, so its size is not the anchor offset. What the anchor offset decides is where the glyph ends up at arrival: off-centre by d*2^(target-NZ) screen px. Rendering medium does not matter: vector_independent=true is correct.
MAGNITUDE (corrected, recomputed from maps_markers.json vs city-anchors.json plus the two hard-coded anchors in meshedWorldInit): of 121 anchored cities with a same-name marker, most are 0-2.2 px. 40 have d >= 7.8: Tamaron 7.8 ... Damoklir 69.1 among lesser dots, and Hordon 42.7, Drāmūz 36.3, Clickerhall 32.9 and Ion Ephel 31.3 among major markers. Penthelon is 112.8 and was left out of the claimed range; its anchor is moved on purpose ('footprint on the charted Five Fingers shore (wiki marker floats in the lake)'). The 'tier-C start of z5.5 (x2.83)' is wrong. tierZoom('c')=fitZoom+2/3*(TIER_CEIL-fitZoom), TIER_CEIL=6 on desktop and 5 on retina. With a 900 px viewport fitZoom≈2.75, so tier C≈4.92 (x1.89) on desktop and ≈4.25 (x1.19) on retina, never above 6. That gives about 15-131 screen px at the start (213 for Penthelon) when the card came from search or a link. At arrival (target=max(z,cityMaxZ-0.5): about 10.3 for a 2048 village plan, x≈80) the glyph sits hundreds to thousands of px off-centre. It is the glyph that moves, not the city: the overlay, POIs and wash are all centred on the anchor, so the camera stays registered with the city art.
CHEAP FIX (wrong and harmful): setting dest to the marker latlng would centre the camera on the dot while cityBox, the overlay, worldPOICoord and sampleCityMask all stay on the anchor. At target zoom a village footprint is 18 world px, about 1450 screen px wide, so any offset over about 9 px pushes the plan partly or wholly off-screen. At the proposed 3*FOOT_R limit (27 px for a village) the plan would be about 2160 px off-centre, fully off a phone screen. It would also change which city worldCityUpdate treats as nearest, and it would overrule Penthelon's deliberate shore placement, which breaks the rule that registration bends art to the atlas. Correct fix: keep the fly target on the anchor, and fix the data instead. Re-register each off-dot anchor against the atlas: either move the anchor onto the glyph when the glyph is the true settlement site, or move the marker or glyph to the anchor when the anchor is the true site, as with Penthelon. Optionally, after arrival, show a short eased hand-off from glyph to footprint, within the living track. The data edit does not touch the UG3 pins (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask), but moving an anchor changes that city's genCityCanvas input mask and therefore its cityCanvasSha, so the mobile lane baselines must be re-cut centrally. flyIntoCity is not pinned. Desktop and phone stay identical, since nothing in the fix depends on the viewport.
votes.reason: The mechanism is right (dest = anchor ≠ glyph) and vector_independent=true holds. The claim fails on three points. (1) Start state: a marker click only calls openPlace and does not fly to the dot; only search, hash and API paths use flyToMarker. (2) Magnitude: tier C is about z4.9 (x1.89) on desktop and about z4.25 (x1.19) on retina, never z5.5/x2.83; the range also leaves out Penthelon at 112.8 px, and the real visible error is at arrival (glyph about x80 off-centre), not mid-dive. (3) The interim fix is unsafe: centring on the marker while cityBox, overlay and POIs stay on the anchor would push the city plan off-screen whenever the offset is more than about 9 px. The correct fix is to re-register the anchor data, which changes cityCanvasSha for each moved city but leaves the UG3 function hashes alone.

items.summary: REGISTRATION inherited: world POIs go through the same cityBox as the art, so they agree with the chart (to about 0.003 atlas px) but carry its offsets against the atlas, e.g. several Epēshu POIs over atlas sea.

prior_record.title: World POIs are registered to the image, so they inherit every art misregistration and pop in at z8
prior_record.anchor: buildWorldPOIs: px(box.x0+(p.x/pr.w)*box.fw, box.y0+(p.y/pr.h)*box.fh)
prior_record.mechanism: Working as intended: REGISTRATION to the art, not the atlas. POIs go through the same cityBox (canon poiRef 3914x4200 to 2863x3072, scale mismatch 7e-5 = 0.004 atlas px; overlay JPGs are exact resizes of the chart pyramids, correlation 0.997-0.998, shift 0.0 px), so they sit exactly on the chart's printed badges but move with its offsets relative to the atlas. They exist at z>=8 only (add/remove, see poi-band-gap).
prior_record.fires_when: z>=8 in any city with POIs; #chart=...&poi=n deep links fly to worldPOICoord.
prior_record.visible_effect: Numbered markers agree with the chart but not the atlas (e.g. Epēshu north-ward POIs over atlas sea).
prior_record.magnitude: Same as the art offsets: Epēshu mean 6.1 / max 16.8 atlas px, Summarch ~20, label-anchored cities 7.8-69.1; the Lepon Island Fortress POI is off its own drawn island (see trait-sea-side-vs-atlas).
prior_record.cheap_fix: None separate: they follow any cityBox fit automatically. Optionally fade them in over z7.8-8.2 instead of add/remove.
prior_record.fix_risks: None; the cityBox fit carries them along.

votes.corrected:
The claim holds, with three refinements. The core is right. buildWorldPOIs and worldPOICoord (maps-site/index.html) put each POI at px(box.x0+(p.x/pr.w)*box.fw, box.y0+(p.y/pr.h)*box.fh). The box is the same cityBox(a,reg.w,reg.h) that ensureCityOverlay uses for the L.imageOverlay bounds. So POIs are registered to the art (REGISTRATION), not to the atlas, and they move with every offset the art has. For canon charts the frame mismatch is negligible. In meshedWorldInit, Epēshu has poiRef 3914x4200 (detail-charts.json) and art 2863x3072 (scales 0.731477 vs 0.731429). Summarch has poiRef 4245x3951 and art 3072x2859. Either mismatch is under 0.01 atlas px, so the markers sit on the art's printed badges. Atlas check: I sampled z5 tiles at the 19 Epēshu POI world positions. Several land on atlas sea west and north-west of the ring-dot, not just to the north: Temple of Thobrauk Tegendes, Māmban, Bangeph Rock, Mount Mastery and Eelwynd. There the atlas coast runs NE-SW through the anchor and the sea lies to the W/NW.

Refinement 1, pop-in. The POI layer group is added or removed as a whole, never faded. setCityPOIVisible(z>=8) runs only inside worldCityUpdate, which fires on zoomend/moveend. ensureCityOverlay also adds the layer at instantiation when getZoom()>=8. So the markers appear or vanish at the end of a gesture or animation that crosses z8, not continuously at z8. flyIntoCity, reached from the #chart=..&poi=n hash path and from ANNALS.descend, flies to worldPOICoord and so lands on the art-registered spot.

Refinement 2, how visible the mismatch is. Whenever POIs show (z>=8), map-tier-d (from Z_TIER_D 7.5) has already set opacity 0 on the settlement, way, water, lane, district and route panes. baseOpacity is also at its 0.12 floor. The reader therefore sees POIs agree with the dominant art. The atlas disagreement shows only through the faint 12% base. The POIs add no shift of their own.

Refinement 3, generated plans. "Exactly on the art" holds only for canon charts. In genCityCanvas the ruin island-fortress POI is placed at cx+sv*(shoreDist+S*0.14). When the water mask exists (WD&&waterNode), the island is drawn at waterNode+seaNormal(waterNode)*S*0.14. So on Lepon-type ruins the POI can sit off its own drawn island, a mismatch inside the plan's own frame (the trait-sea-side-vs-atlas issue).

The cheap fix stands: any cityBox or registration fix carries the POIs along automatically. A z7.8-8.2 opacity fade could replace add/remove, driven from worldOpacityUpdate on the live zoom event.
votes.reason: I verified this in head maps-site/index.html. buildWorldPOIs and worldPOICoord use the same cityBox as the image overlay in ensureCityOverlay. The poiRef-to-art aspect mismatch for Epēshu and Summarch is under 1e-4, so the POIs ride the art, not the atlas. Sampling the atlas tiles shows several Epēshu POIs over atlas sea to the W/NW. The z8 gate is setCityPOIVisible(z>=8), which only worldCityUpdate calls (on zoomend/moveend), and it adds or removes the layer with no fade. The deep link goes through flyIntoCity to worldPOICoord. I rate it minor, not major. When POIs are visible, map-tier-d (z>=7.5) hides all the atlas vector panes and the base is at 0.12 opacity. The POIs agree with the art the reader is looking at and add no shift beyond the art's own offset. The only extra visible effect is the zoomend pop. The vector_independent claim and the fix-follows-cityBox claim are both correct.

votes.corrected:
MECHANISM (holds, registration): buildWorldPOIs and worldPOICoord in maps-site/index.html map POIs through the same cityBox(a,reg.w,reg.h) linear transform as the L.imageOverlay, normalised by poiRef. For canon cities the poiRef-to-overlay aspect mismatch is negligible: Epēshu has 2863/3914=0.731477 against 3072/4200=0.731429, a relative 6.6e-5, times fw 48.46, which is about 0.003 atlas px. Summarch has a relative 8.4e-5 times fw 28, which is about 0.002 px. So canon POIs sit on the chart's printed badges and carry the chart's offsets relative to the atlas. Procedural plans use poiRef = gen.w/h, so that mapping is exact too. POIs appear only at z>=8, and setCityPOIVisible runs only from worldCityUpdate, which fires on zoomend and moveend. They therefore pop in once a gesture or animation that crosses z8 ends, not during it.

MAGNITUDE (corrected):
(a) Epēshu: the "mean 6.1 / max 16.8" coast residual was NOT reproduced; the epeshu-canon-fit claim is disputed. The reproduced evidence is water IoU 0.36 over the box x 1211.9-1260.3, y 1389-1441: atlas sea covers 45% of the box and the art's sea 16%, so 26% of the box disagrees. That is up to roughly half the 48x52 px box in the north wards. The ties similarity fit (scale about 0.83x today, rotation about 5.4 deg, residual rms 5.0 / max 6.2) gives the residual after fitting, not today's offset.
