Quote the offset as unmeasured, with the IoU as the evidence.
(b) Summarch: the anchor sits about 20 atlas px from its ring (19.9 from the marker, 20.5 from the measured ring centre). POIs inherit this as a pure translation.
(c) Label-anchored procedural cities, 7.8-69.1 px (median about 26): this is the plan being offset from the printed ring. It is NOT an art-versus-coast misregistration. The plan's water comes from sampleCityMask over the same box, so POIs there agree with the atlas coast and simply sit beside the dot.
(d) Lepon's "The Island Fortress" POI does NOT ride the art. In genCityCanvas the island is drawn at waterNode + seaNormal*S*0.14 when the mask exists (WD). addPoi instead places the POI at cx + sv*(shoreDist + S*0.14), using the trait bearing. So the POI can sit off its own drawn island. That is a bug between POI and art inside genCityCanvas and contradicts the claim that POIs are "exactly on the art".

VECTOR_INDEPENDENT: true. A vector city placed through cityBox carries POIs identically.

CHEAP FIX (corrected):
(1) Put the per-city registration in data that cityBox reads (outside the pinned functions), so the overlay, wash, stubs and both POI paths (buildWorldPOIs and worldPOICoord, including #chart=...&poi=n deep links) all move together. This only carries POIs automatically for a translation-plus-scale fit. A rotation or affine fit (Epēshu's fit wants about 5.4 deg) cannot be shown by the axis-aligned L.imageOverlay, and the POI transform would need the same rotation added explicitly.
(2) The optional fade: add the layer at z>=7.8 and drive the pCityPOI pane opacity from worldOpacityUpdate on the live zoom event. Toggling add/remove in setCityPOIVisible alone cannot fade, because it runs only at zoomend.
(3) The Lepon island POI fix (use ifx/ify for the POI) must be made inside genCityCanvas.
votes.reason:
The mechanism is confirmed in code, and the canon mismatch of about 0.003 px recomputes correctly. The magnitude is wrong in three places, and fix_risks "None" is wrong.

Magnitude:
- Epēshu's 6.1/16.8 was not reproduced (the epeshu-canon-fit claim is disputed). Only water IoU 0.36 stands.
- The 7.8-69.1 px figure for label-anchored cities is the plan sitting off its ring. It is not art misregistered against the atlas: those plans take their water from the atlas mask, so their POIs agree with the coast.
- The Lepon Island Fortress POI is placed by a different formula from the drawn island (sv/shoreDist versus waterNode/seaNormal in genCityCanvas). So that POI does not ride the art.

Fix risks:
- Any edit to genCityCanvas changes its source hash and fails the UG3 atlas_fn_sha pin. It must land after Mobile 9 with a central rebaseline.
- The fade edits worldOpacityUpdate and setCityPOIVisible in maps-site/index.html while the atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) is mid-flight there. That risks a merge collision and a visible change on desktop that the desktop-identity captures would flag. Sequence it after the lane.
- A cityBox fit carries POIs only for translation plus scale. A rotation fit needs an explicit POI transform and a different overlay render path.
- Determinism is unaffected, because registration data is static.

items.summary: Lifecycle: ensureArrival hard-sets the view 1700 ms after flyIntoCity when the fly stalled (hidden tab or a long main-thread block), a teleport of dz about 6.4-8.2; flyTo is wall-clock timed, so short arrivals do not happen.

prior_record.title: ensureArrival hard-lands an unfinished or stalled fly with an instant setView
prior_record.anchor: ensureArrival: `if(map.getZoom()>=target-0.5){worldCityUpdate();return;} map._animatingZoom=false; map._mapPane.classList.remove('leaflet-zoom-anim'); map.setView(dest,target,{animate:false})` after setTimeout 1700, up to 2 retries
prior_record.mechanism: Working as intended (deep-link guarantee, spec MW). 1700 ms after flyIntoCity, if zoom < target-0.5 it clears Leaflet's zoom-animation flag/class and jumps synchronously, retrying up to twice. The class is ripped off mid-transition and a queued _animateZoom from an earlier setMaxZoom can still fire _onZoomTransitionEnd and _move to its stale target. A fly that ends inside the 0.5 slack is accepted short of target.
prior_record.fires_when: Throttled or background tabs, stalled flyTo, heavy main-thread work during the fly (a 2048^2 synchronous plan draw), slow phones, or after exitChart's queued zoom.
prior_record.visible_effect: The fly freezes and the view teleports to the city at depth; on mobile tiles and art pop in at once; sometimes arrival up to half a level shallower than intended.
prior_record.magnitude: Up to the entire remaining fly in one frame: from fit zoom ~2-2.7 to 9.385 (dz 6.7-7.4) plus the full lateral distance; accepted shortfall up to 0.5 zoom (x1.41). Unmeasured on devices; probe with CDP CPU throttling 6 and #chart=Epēshu.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Keep as a guarantee. Optionally only hard-land when document.hidden or no 'zoom' event fired in the last ~300 ms, or land with a short animated setView when the tab is visible; prewarm the plan before the fly (requestIdleCallback); tighten slack to 0.1.
prior_record.fix_risks: Weakening it reintroduces stranded deep links; mobile deep-link guarantee tests depend on landing by 1.7 s. Living-chart H2z owns this transition. Not pinned.

votes.corrected:
The core holds. In maps-site/index.html, `flyIntoCity` (called by `handleHash` for `#chart=City`, and by the descend button and API) starts `map.flyTo(dest,target,{duration:1.4,easeLinearity:.25})` one rAF late, with target=max(getZoom(), cityMaxZ-0.5) (Epēshu: 9.885-0.5=9.385). It also arms `ensureArrival(dest,target,0)` at the same time, outside any rAF. 1700 ms later, if CHART.on it returns. If getZoom()>=target-0.5 it only calls worldCityUpdate. Otherwise it sets map._animatingZoom=false, removes 'leaflet-zoom-anim' from the map pane and runs `setView(dest,target,{animate:false})`. That is a synchronous _resetView: the tiles re-grid and pop in, and moveend fires.

Four details in the claim are wrong.
(1) The stale-animation path is mostly the reverse of what the claim says. In vendored leaflet.js, `_onZoomTransitionEnd` is guarded by `this._animatingZoom&&(...)`. Clearing the flag therefore makes a 250 ms transition-end timer that is already pending do nothing. A stale zoom can only reach the view through a `_tryAnimatedZoom` rAF (`x(function(){..._animateZoom(t,e,!0)})`) that has not run yet. When it finally runs, it re-sets the flag and _moves to its stale target. That only happens when rAF is paused, i.e. in a background tab.
(2) There is no shallow arrival. The accept branch does not _stop() the fly. flyTo runs on wall-clock time (Date.now()) and always ends with `this._move(n,o)._moveEnd(!0)` exactly at target. The 0.5 slack (cityMaxZ-1.0) never decides the landing zoom, unless the user interrupts the fly or a maxZoom clamp cancels it.
(3) The firing window is narrow. flyTo finishes on the first frame after about 1.42 s. A visible tab therefore hard-lands only if the main thread blocks for about 280 ms or more across the fly's end. The likely case is the async `ensureCityGen` melded plan finishing and drawing or encoding synchronously in that window. The synchronous `ensureCityGenNow` draw runs before the timer starts, so it does not count. In a background tab, rAF is paused but the timer still fires (throttled), so the landing happens while the tab is hidden. On return, the queued flyTo rAF runs from the landed view to the same dest (`l=distanceTo||1` keeps it finite), so it is close to a no-op and nothing teleports in front of the reader.
(4) `exitChart` does not make ensureArrival fire. Its `setMaxZoom(s.maxZoom)` may queue an animated setZoom rAF, which is a separate 250 ms yank during the running fly. Its own setView is animate:false.

Retries are effectively dead code. The check `getZoom()<target-0.5` runs right after a synchronous reset, so a retry only arms if _limitZoom clamped target because maxZoom dropped below it.

items.summary: Lifecycle: ensureArrival is armed unconditionally, so a reader who drags or wheels during a descent is teleported to the target at 1.7 s (up to about 6.7 levels plus the pan, about 4.7 for a takeover at 300 ms), normally once, re-arming only when the hard setView is clamped.

prior_record.title: An interrupted descent is forced to finish 1.7 s, 3.4 s and 5.1 s later
prior_record.anchor: ensureArrival(dest,target,tries): setTimeout(...,1700), map.setView(dest,target,{animate:false}), tries<2; Leaflet map._stop() via _onDragStart / setZoomAround
prior_record.mechanism: Navigation policy. flyIntoCity starts flyTo in a rAF and arms ensureArrival unconditionally. Any reader gesture during the 1.4 s fly (drag, or the wheel handler via setZoomAround -> setView) cancels the fly through map._stop(); at 1700 ms ensureArrival sees getZoom()<target-0.5, clears _animatingZoom and hard-setViews to the city, and re-arms up to twice more.
prior_record.fires_when: #chart=City deep links, Descend, ATLAS.descend, whenever the reader drags or wheels during the descent (also the interrupted stall case in hard-arrival-setview).
prior_record.visible_effect: The reader takes over, then the map teleports into the city without animation, and can do it again 1.7 s later.
prior_record.magnitude: A teleport of (target - current zoom), up to ~6.7 levels (fitZoom 2.72 to Epēshu 9.385) plus the full pan to the anchor, up to 3 times. Probe: ATLAS.descend('Epēshu'), drag at t=300 ms, log moveend at 1.7/3.4/5.1 s.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Per-descent token: cancel ensureArrival on any movestart/zoomstart/dragstart not caused by the fly (listen after the first fly frame) and land only if the fly never stepped (no 'zoom' event since the kick).
prior_record.fix_risks: Must keep the background-tab guarantee (no rAF means no zoom events means it still lands). Not pinned. Living-chart H2z choreography.

votes.corrected: The forced finish is real, but the claim gets the schedule wrong. In maps-site/index.html, flyIntoCity(name,poiN) starts map.flyTo(dest,target,{duration:1.4}) inside a requestAnimationFrame and always calls ensureArrival(dest,target,0). target = max(getZoom, cityMaxZ-0.5), which is 9.385 for Epēshu (capital r26, 3072 px wide). Three reader actions cancel the fly through Leaflet's map._stop(): a mouse drag (Map.Drag _onDragStart calls e._stop()), a mouse wheel or pinch (the custom wheel handler calls setZoomAround, then setView, which calls _stop), and the +/- buttons or keyboard. A trackpad two-finger pan does NOT cancel it, because it uses panBy({animate:false}), which never calls _stop; the fly just overwrites that pan. At 1700 ms, if getZoom() < target-0.5 and CHART.on is false, ensureArrival clears _animatingZoom, drops the leaflet-zoom-anim class and calls map.setView(dest,target,{animate:false}). That is a hard jump to the anchor or POI, so the reader's takeover is overridden. The claim says this happens at 1.7, 3.4 and 5.1 s unconditionally. It does not. The re-arm check (getZoom()<target-0.5 && tries<2) runs right after the synchronous setView, so it only fires when that setView was clamped by maxZoom. The clamp does happen in the probe case: the interrupt's own moveend runs worldCityUpdate. If the view centre is then more than 3 footprint radii from any anchor (nearestCity returns null), or nearest a different city, it calls setMaxZoom(Z_OPEN_MAX=8) or that city's cap. The 1.7 s setView is then clamped to z8 on the anchor. worldCityUpdate then raises maxZoom back to Epēshu's 9.885, and 8 < 8.885 re-arms. At 3.4 s a second hard jump goes z8 → 9.385. So the usual result is one jump, if the reader stayed near the city, or two (1.7 s to z8, 3.4 s to the full depth). A third jump at 5.1 s happens only if the reader drags away again during each window. The first jump is up to about 5.3 levels (fit ~2.7 → 8) plus the full pan; the total is about 6.7 levels. A side effect, if a POI was asked for: the map.once('moveend') POI handler is used up by the interrupt's own moveend, so openWorldPOI opens before the landing.

I also checked the vendored Leaflet 1.9.4: _stop cancels _flyToFrame, Map.Drag _onDragStart calls e._stop(), setView calls this._stop(), panBy without animate does not call _stop, and setMaxZoom calls setZoom when the current zoom is above the new cap. The interrupt-then-hard-land path exists as claimed, and a reader at the table would see the view jump after they took over, so it rates major. Two parts of the claim are wrong. The re-arm is not unconditional: it only fires when setView is clamped by a maxZoom that worldCityUpdate lowered during the interrupt, so it is usually 1 or 2 jumps, not 3. And trackpad pans do not interrupt the fly. The fault is in navigation policy, not registration, and it would act the same with raster or vector city art.

SAFETY. flyIntoCity and ensureArrival are not among the UG3 atlas_fn_sha pins (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask), and cityCanvasSha is untouched. What the code does show is a large downsample. Village plans (FOOT_R 9) put GEN_SIZE=2048 over 18 world px, about 251 screen px at z7.8 (8.2x). Ruins are about 9.2x, towns (14) about 5.2x, and the capitals (26), including canon overlay-Epeshu.jpg 2863x3072 and Summarch, about 724 px (4.2x). So "1/8" applies only to villages and ruins. genCityCanvas strokes building outlines and ink at lineWidth 0.7-1.2 at 2048, which is about 0.1 screen px at z7.8, so the plan really does contain sub-pixel, high-frequency line work.

The browser scales the img through two different paths in vendored Leaflet 1.9.4. (1) Wheel, zoom-control and keyboard zoom go through _tryAnimatedZoom, then zoomanim, then ImageOverlay._animateZoom, which sets transform scale via setTransform. That runs as a 0.25s CSS transition (.leaflet-zoom-anim .leaflet-zoom-animated) and changes scale by at most about 2x per step. Then the 'zoom' event calls _reset, which sets style.width/height. (2) flyTo (used by flyIntoCity, the main zoom-through) and pinch fire 'zoom' every frame, so _reset sets a new style.width/height each frame and the img is redrawn at a new size. There is no scale transform on this path. On the wheel path the overlay is only added at zoomend/moveend by worldCityUpdate, once z is above 6.5. flyIntoCity adds it eagerly.

Whether an engine uses mip levels or plain bilinear for any of these draws is unverified and depends on the engine. Nothing in the repo shows it. If scale-dependent aliasing does happen, it can appear anywhere the downsample stays above about 2x: for a village up to about z9.8 (1:1 only at cityMaxZ 10.83), not just z6.8-8.5. Below about z7.3, overlayOpacity is 0.5 or less, so the base half-masks it.

Fix note: a downscaled copy made from the canvas output inside registerCityOverlay leaves genCityCanvas and cityCanvasSha unpinned-safe. The canon JPGs would need an image-to-canvas downscale at load. Swapping src by zoom adds its own one-frame pop. The magnitude is still unmeasured, so use the claim's own z7.50/7.55 screenshot probe, per engine and per path (wheel vs flyTo).
votes.reason: The downsample exists as stated: 2048 px over 18 world px for villages, about 8x at z7.8. Sub-pixel strokes also exist (lineWidth 0.7-1.2 in genCityCanvas), so some scale-dependent aliasing is plausible. The claim fails as stated on four points. "1/8 scale" is true only for villages and ruins; capitals and the canon Epēshu map are about 4.2x and towns about 5.2x. "Browsers resample without mipmaps during transforms" cannot be verified from the repo and depends on the engine. Leaflet uses a CSS transform scale only on the wheel/button path (ImageOverlay._animateZoom, 0.25s, at most about 2x per step). flyTo, which flyIntoCity uses, and pinch resize the img through _reset's style.width/height on every frame instead. The z6.8-8.5 window is arbitrary, since the downsample stays above 2x up to about z9.8 for villages. Most importantly, it moves no geometry: the overlay stays inside cityBox at every zoom. That makes it a RENDERING-medium artifact, not a registration or zoom-shift source. If it is real, it is at most a subtle flicker, and the opacity ramp half-masks it below about z7.3. Magnitude unmeasured.

votes.corrected:
MAGNITUDE (recomputed from constants in maps-site/index.html: NZ=4, FOOT_R, cityBox, overlayOpacity, GEN_SIZE=2048). Screen px per world px = 2^(z-4). A village box (FOOT_R.village 9, so 18 world px) is 125 CSS px at z6.8 (where overlayOpacity is 0), 177 px at z7.3 (opacity 0.5) and 251 px at z7.8 (opacity 1). The 2048 plan is therefore downsampled about 16x, 11.6x and 8.2x, or half that on a DPR-2 screen. A town (28 world px) is 390 px at z7.8, a 5.25x downsample. Epēshu is a capital (52 world px) and its overlay-Epeshu.jpg is 2863x3072, so it shows at 724 px at z7.8 (4.2x, 2.1x on retina) and 362 px at z6.8 (8.5x). The claim's "~256 px / 1/8" is right for villages at z7.8 only. The worst ratios fall where the overlay is mostly transparent. 115 of the 136 anchors are villages, so the generated plans carry the risk, not the canon art. The visible crawl is still unmeasured and depends on the browser: Chrome picks a mip level per raster scale and re-rasters on each fractional wheel step (zoomSnap 0, zoomDelta .25), so it may be mild there. The proposed probe (z7.50 and z7.55 pair, high-frequency energy inside the box) is good. Add a second pair of frames taken mid-animation, plus Safari and Firefox. This is RENDERING, not REGISTRATION: nothing moves relative to the coast or roads, and it produces no anchoring shift. vector_independent=false is correct: a Leaflet SVG or canvas vector layer is re-rendered at screen resolution after each zoom and only CSS-scaled by the step factor in between, so it does not alias, though the same cityBox would still misregister it.
FIX (corrected). A single half-resolution copy does not work. At 1024 px a village is still downsampled 4x at z7.8 and 8x at z6.8. The fix also cannot reach the URL-string art (registerCityOverlay gets no canvas for overlay-Epeshu.jpg or overlay-Summarch.jpg). And swapping the url at z8.5 reloads the img element, which causes its own pop or blink in the middle of the zoom. The safe version is a small size ladder. For a canvas plan only: drawImage the read-only genCityCanvas output once, with imageSmoothingQuality 'high', into sizes matched to the box on screen. Rough sizes: about 512 px for villages below ~z8.5, 1024 px for z8.5-9.5, and the full 2048 above. Size each rung as ceil(2*r*2^(z_swap-4)*DPR). Preload each rung's image before calling setUrl, or cross-fade two overlays, so the swap does not blink. Keep CITYREG[key].w/h at the full-resolution dimensions so cityBox and cityMaxZ stay byte-identical. Leave the canon art alone: the mobile lane's A-U11 (Mobile 6) already owns 720 px previews of exactly overlay-Epeshu/Summarch, with "registerCityOverlay literal kept" and "final shot equals R1 at max zoom". The real art also already has a tiled pyramid under charts/epeshu and charts/summarch. Safety: the UG3 atlas_fn_sha pins (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask) and cityCanvasSha stay intact only if genCityCanvas and its canvas are not modified. Determinism is unaffected because the downscale is presentation, not generation. But desktop identity is NOT automatically safe. Frames at rest between z6.8 and 8.5 would change pixels, because a pre-downscaled rung resamples differently from the browser's own mip, so this needs a desktop rebaseline. It also edits maps-site/index.html around registerCityOverlay and ensureCityOverlay while the Mobile 5-9 lane is mid-flight there, so it must be queued after Mobile 9 or folded into that lane, not landed alongside it. Memory gets lighter, not heavier: the extra rungs add 1/16 + 1/4 of the 2048 data URL, roughly a third more.
votes.reason: The mechanism (rendering medium, not registration) and vector_independent=false are right. The numbers are only half right: 1/8 holds for villages at z7.8 alone. The real range during the fade is about 16x down to 8x for villages, 5x for towns and 4x for Epēshu's art (cityBox: FOOT_R 9/14/26 world px x 2^(z-4); GEN_SIZE 2048; overlay-Epeshu.jpg 2863x3072). The cheap fix is wrong. One half-resolution copy still leaves a 4-8x downsample. It cannot apply to URL-string art in registerCityOverlay. A raw setUrl swap blinks. items.summary: Performance (medium-dependent): synchronous 2048-square genCityCanvas plus toDataURL run in the z5 tile onload (prewarm only starts fetches; deep links generate twice), so long tasks can land mid-gesture; unmeasured.

prior_record.title: Synchronous 2048^2 generation and WebP encode can drop frames mid-zoom
prior_record.subsystem: overlay (ensureCityGen callback -> genCityCanvas + toDataURL; prewarm window)
prior_record.anchor: registerCityOverlay: url=img.toDataURL('image/webp',0.85); ensureCityGen: genCityCanvas(key,t,a,m); prewarm reached only on moveend at z>5.6 within 6*FOOT_R
prior_record.mechanism: RENDERING. When prewarm missed, generation plus encode runs on the main thread in the tile-load callback while the reader pinches, wheels or flies; frames stall and the next frame applies the accumulated zoom at once. (A vector plan still needs generation but not the raster encode and decode.)
prior_record.fires_when: First approach to a city without prewarm (fast pinch, deep link), especially on phones.
prior_record.visible_effect: A hitch: the zoom freezes, then jumps.
prior_record.magnitude: Unmeasured. Probe: performance.mark around genCityCanvas and toDataURL on pixel7 and desktop profiles (4x CPU throttle), count long tasks >50 ms during a scripted pinch.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Prewarm on any 'zoom' event at z>5.6 (not only moveend) and widen the 6*FOOT_R ring; schedule rather than move to a worker.
prior_record.fix_risks: A worker/OffscreenCanvas risks cityCanvasSha (text rasterisation differs) and touches pinned code; prefer scheduling-only fixes.

votes.corrected:
RENDERING, not registration: nothing moves on the map, the frames just stall. The mechanism is real, but the claim gets the trigger and the prewarm window partly wrong.

(1) The work. genCityCanvas (GEN_SIZE=2048) builds a 2048² canvas on the main thread. It reads 2048² pixel data back more than once (the wla alpha field and the RVD/RD river fields) and writes the 2048² vignette with putImageData. registerCityOverlay then calls img.toDataURL('image/webp',0.85). Where the browser cannot encode webp (Safari), that call returns PNG and the code encodes a second time with toDataURL('image/png'), so the work doubles on iPhones. If the city is on screen (CITYVIEW.name===key), registerCityOverlay also hot-swaps the overlay: it builds a new L.imageOverlay from the multi-MB data URL. The ensureCityGen callback then calls washRefresh to rebuild the wash.

(2) When it runs. ensureCityGen does not generate on its own schedule. It runs inside sampleCityMask's done callback. That callback fires either synchronously, if MASKQ was already sampled, or in the Image onload of the last z5 tile to arrive. So the cost lands whenever those tiles arrive, which can be mid-gesture.

(3) Prewarm. worldCityUpdate is bound to 'zoomend moveend', not moveend only. Prewarm is the else-branch: 5.6<z≤6.5, the city has no CITYREG entry and is not in PREWARMED, and the centre is within 6*FOOT_R[kind] of the anchor. requestIdleCallback (setTimeout 180 on Safari) only schedules the tile kick. The generation still runs unscheduled in the tile onload, so even a prewarm hit is not an idle-time bake. At z>6.5, worldCityUpdate calls ensureCityGen directly on every zoomend/moveend.

(4) When the stall shows.
- flyIntoCity (deep link or click): ensureCityGenNow generates the synthetic plan synchronously before the fly. The rAF delay moves that cost off the fly's first tick. ensureCityGen then starts fetching z5 tiles that are not loaded at world zoom. When they land during the 1.4 s flyTo, the melded plan is regenerated, re-encoded and hot-swapped mid-fly. Leaflet's fly frame is driven by Date.now, so the view freezes, then jumps to the time-correct frame.
- Pinch: the touch move is applied on the next frame after the stall, so the zoom jumps.
- Wheel: wheel events queued during the stall are summed into one larger zoom step.

Canon cities (Epēshu, Summarch) never take this path because ensureCityGen only generates for invented or unregistered cities. The plan is cached in CITYREG for the session, so the stall hits only the first approach to each generated city.

Cheap fix. Defer the genCityCanvas, registerCityOverlay and washRefresh block inside the sampleCityMask callback until no zoom/move or touch is active: wait for zoomend/moveend plus an idle slot, then let the existing hot-swap land it. Kick tile sampling earlier and on a wider ring, but never generate during an animation. This is scheduling only. A worker/OffscreenCanvas could change text rasterisation and break the cityCanvasSha/atlas_fn_sha pins. The flyIntoCity comment "JPEG-encode" is stale: the encode is webp/PNG.

Magnitude is unmeasured. Probe with performance.mark around genCityCanvas and toDataURL, plus a long-task observer, during a scripted flyIntoCity and a pinch, on pixel7/iPhone (WebKit) and desktop profiles.
votes.reason: Checked in head maps-site/index.html. GEN_SIZE=2048. genCityCanvas does 2048² getImageData readbacks (wla alpha field, RVD/RD) and a vignette putImageData. registerCityOverlay calls toDataURL('image/webp',0.85), then toDataURL('image/png') again if the result is not webp. ensureCityGen runs genCityCanvas inside the sampleCityMask done callback, which fires from the z5 tile Image.onload. worldCityUpdate is bound via map.on('zoomend moveend',worldCityUpdate), so the claim's "only on moveend" is wrong. Prewarm is the else-branch for 5.6<z<=6.5, needs !CITYREG and !PREWARMED, and uses fr=FOOT_R*6. Its requestIdleCallback only schedules the tile kick, so generation still lands in the tile onload. flyIntoCity calls ensureCityGen then ensureCityGenNow, so the synthetic plan is generated synchronously before the rAF-delayed flyTo, and the melded regen plus hot-swap and washRefresh lands mid-fly when the tiles arrive. In the vendored Leaflet 1.9.4, the fly frame is timed by Date.now ((Date.now()-g)/y), so a stall shows as a freeze, then a jump. Touch-zoom and wheel-zoom (wheelDebounceTime 20) apply input accumulated during a stall in one step. Severity: a multi-hundred-ms freeze mid-fly or mid-pinch on first approach would be noticeable, especially on phones and Safari's double PNG encode, but it is unmeasured and once per generated city per session. Canon cities are exempt. It shifts no registration.

votes.corrected:
VISIBLE EFFECT: correct only as a TIMING artifact. It is a stall followed by a catch-up jump. It is not a registration shift: the art lands where cityBox puts it, so this is not the misalignment the owner describes. Classify it as RENDERING/perf, not REGISTRATION.

WHERE IT ACTUALLY FIRES (maps-site/index.html):
(1) The heavy work never runs in idle time. The prewarm's requestIdleCallback in worldCityUpdate only calls ensureCityGen, and that only starts sampleCityMask, which makes 'new Image()' fetches of z5 tiles. genCityCanvas plus toDataURL then run in the im.onload callback ('one()' -> cbs -> the ensureCityGen callback), at whatever moment the last mask tile arrives. That can be mid-gesture or mid-fly whether or not prewarm happened.
(2) worldCityUpdate is bound to 'zoomend moveend' only. Without prewarm, the generation is therefore queued after a gesture ends. It hits the next gesture or an in-flight flyTo only when the tiles land late.
(3) The worst case the claim misses is a deep link or flyIntoCity. ensureCityGenNow runs a synchronous 2048^2 genCityCanvas + toDataURL before the fly (the one-rAF delay only moves it out of the first tick). Then ensureCityGen's tile callback finds reg.prov==='invented' and regenerates the melded plan mid-fly: TWO full generations and encodes per deep link. registerCityOverlay's hot-swap then makes the browser decode a multi-MB data: URL during the descent.

MAGNITUDE: GEN_SIZE=2048 gives 4.19 MP per plan. Each plan costs a full canvas draw, a WebP q0.85 toDataURL (Safari/iOS cannot encode WebP, so the code encodes twice: it tries WebP, gets back PNG, then calls toDataURL('image/png') again), base64 (~1.33x the bytes), and an image decode at overlay swap. That is plausibly 10^2 ms or more per plan on a phone and up to two plans per deep link. It is still unmeasured, so keep it as 'unmeasured, plausibly >=100 ms long task'.

Fix the probe: put performance.mark/measure and the long-task observer in tools/mobile-capture.js through page.evaluate or an init script, NEVER in the page. Under UG3, maps-site/index.html must keep exactly 1 narrow and 2 wide clock tokens (performance.now at jrn.lastFrame; requestIdleCallback at the prewarm).

vector_independent=false is right: a vector plan skips the encode, base64 and decode, but it still pays for generation and adds its own paint cost.

CHEAP FIX (corrected): do NOT prewarm on 'zoom' and do NOT widen the 6*FOOT_R ring.
(a) Prewarm does not move the heavy work into idle time (see 1), so it fixes nothing.
(b) It breaks UG3. cityCanvasSha hashes the data: URL of EVERY 'invented' entry in ATLAS.cityReg after the descends to Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae. Prewarming more, or on per-frame zoom events during those flights, adds extra cities to the registry. That changes the hash against B0, and the extra set depends on fps and viewport, which breaks the across-profile equality.
(c) A new requestIdleCallback or performance.now token breaks the UG3 clock-token count.

Safe fix, scheduling only, outside the pinned functions, done in the mobile lane after Mobile 5-9 lands:
- In the ensureCityGen callback (not pinned), defer the genCityCanvas + registerCityOverlay call until the map is idle. Gate it on !map._animatingZoom, with no active pinch and no flyTo in progress; otherwise wait for the next 'zoomend'/'moveend' (map.once) and then use the existing rIC shim. This adds no new token if it reuses the one shim through a shared helper.
- In flyIntoCity, skip the melded regeneration until ensureArrival has landed, so a deep link pays for one generation during the fly, not two.

Keep toDataURL: switching to toBlob, an object URL or an OffscreenCanvas worker would empty or alter the /^data:/ registry URLs that cityCanvasSha hashes. Pixels stay a pure function of the city name, so determinism and desktop identity are preserved as long as the set of generated cities at capture time is unchanged.
votes.reason: The mechanism and anchors are broadly real (GEN_SIZE=2048, synchronous genCityCanvas plus toDataURL('image/webp',0.85) in the sampleCityMask tile onload callback). But the claim misreads prewarm: its requestIdleCallback only starts the tile fetches, and the heavy work still runs in the tile onload callback. It also misses the double generation on deep links (ensureCityGenNow, then the melded regeneration mid-fly). The proposed fix would break UG3 in two ways. cityCanvasSha hashes every invented data: URL in cityReg after the descends, and generating extra cities or using fps-dependent zoom-event triggers changes that set. A new requestIdleCallback or performance token would break the clock-token count of 1 narrow and 2 wide. The fix also would not move generation off the gesture. The effect is a temporal hitch, not a registration shift, so it is minor for the owner's alignment ask.

items.summary: Refuted: all 15 tier-d panes already fade with transition:opacity .2s, so the marks do not snap off and the proposed CSS fix does nothing.

prior_record.title: At z7.5 settlement markers, labels, roads, route and borders snap off instantly mid-crossfade
prior_record.anchor: worldOpacityUpdate: `mc.classList.toggle('map-tier-d',z>=Z_TIER_D)` (Z_TIER_D=7.5); CSS `.map-tier-d .leaflet-pSettle-pane ... {opacity:0!important;pointer-events:none}`
prior_record.mechanism: RENDERING, threshold policy. The class flips on the live 'zoom' event at 7.5 while overlayOpacity is 0.7 (base 0.39); 13-15 panes (pSettle, pWay, pLane, pRealm, pWater, pMajor, ...) go to 0 with no transition (only pTrail/pOrigin/pFaction have .2 s). The reference marks that would show whether the art lines up (ring dot, named roads) vanish at once; for label-anchored cities the glyph sits on the dot away from the plan until it vanishes. Zooming out they pop back offset from the art.
prior_record.fires_when: Crossing z7.5 in either direction.
prior_record.visible_effect: The town's clickable glyph, label, named ways, route and borders blink out or in while the plan is ~70% faded in.
prior_record.magnitude: Binary opacity 1 to 0 at dz=0 for 13-15 panes at overlay 0.70.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Add transition:opacity .25s to those panes or drive their opacity from a ramp (e.g. 1 to 0 over z7.2-7.8) in worldOpacityUpdate (pane.style.opacity).
prior_record.fix_risks: Marker and filigree subsystems own those panes (R7 nothing at rest; mobile tier rules); living-chart owns motion. CSS only, no UG3 pins; desktop and mobile captures at z7.5 change.

votes.corrected: The threshold is real, but the claim that the marks blink off instantly is wrong. In maps-site/index.html, worldOpacityUpdate runs on map.on('zoom zoomend moveend', worldOpacityUpdate) and calls mc.classList.toggle('map-tier-d', z>=Z_TIER_D), with Z_TIER_D=7.5. The `.map-tier-d .leaflet-pRealm-pane ... pRouteWp-pane {opacity:0!important;pointer-events:none;}` rule hides 15 panes: pRealm, pTrail, pRouteLine, pWater, pMajor, pMtn, pSettle, pMinor, pLesser, pOrigin, pFaction, pLane, pWay, pDistrict and pRouteWp. All 15 already carry `transition:opacity .2s ease`. Twelve get it from the tier-panes rule ('tier panes (fade reveal)': pMajor, pWater, pSettle, pMtn, pMinor, pLesser, pRealm, pRouteLine, pRouteWp, pLane, pWay, pDistrict). The other three (pTrail, pOrigin, pFaction) get it from their own rule. Nothing overrides that transition, mobile rules included. So when the zoom crosses 7.5 in either direction, every settlement glyph and its label (markers in pSettle, pMajor, pMinor, pLesser), named ways, sea lanes, the party route and its waypoints, realm and district borders, rivers and mountains fade together over a fixed 200 ms. Pointer-events go to none at once. The fade is timed in milliseconds, not driven by zoom, so it is a threshold cut rather than a ramp. Timing depends on the input. With the vendored Leaflet 1.9.4, a wheel, button or keyboard zoom is animated. Map._move suppresses 'zoom' during the animation, and _tempFireZoomEvent fires it only at the end of the transition, about 250 ms in. So the class flips at the end of the step, at whatever zoom the step lands on (0.25 to 1.0 overlay). It does not flip exactly at 7.5. The base layer and the city overlay also update in steps then. Only pinch zoom and flyTo (fly-into-city) fire 'zoom' every frame and cross exactly at 7.5, where overlayOpacity is 0.7 and baseOpacity about 0.39. The class toggles whether or not a city overlay is present. Over open country (Z_OPEN_MAX 8) every reference mark also vanishes, leaving the 0.12–0.39 base ghost. Nothing moves. When the marks come back on zoom-out they sit at their true atlas positions. Any offset from the city plan comes from the cityBox registration, not from this mechanism. Fix: half of the suggested cheap fix already exists, since the panes have a .2 s transition. The useful change is a zoom-driven ramp: set pane.style.opacity in worldOpacityUpdate, for example 1 to 0 over z7.2–7.8, and drop the !important class rule or let the inline value take its place. That keeps the reference marks fading in step with overlayOpacity so the coast and roads can be compared with the plan. It touches CSS and pane opacity only, with no UG3 pins, but it sits in panes owned by the marker, filigree (R7) and living-chart tracks, and it changes the z7.5 captures.
votes.reason: The mechanism exists, but the claim gets its behaviour wrong. All 15 hidden panes already have a 0.2 s opacity transition: twelve from the 'tier panes (fade reveal)' rule and pTrail, pOrigin and pFaction from their own rule. So the marks fade quickly rather than snapping off instantly. For wheel, button and keyboard zoom, Leaflet 1.9.4 fires 'zoom' only when the animation ends (the _tempFireZoomEvent path in Map._move and _onZoomTransitionEnd). So the threshold is applied at the end of the step, not live at exactly 7.5. Only pinch and flyTo cross at 7.5 with the overlay at 0.70. It moves no geometry. It only takes away the reference marks for a moment, and when they come back they sit at their true positions. Any mismatch with the plan is a cityBox registration issue. A sharp-eyed reader would see a brief fade-out of everything at one zoom step, which is a minor visual pop and does not shift anything.

votes.corrected:
Mechanism and magnitude, recomputed from maps-site/index.html at HEAD. worldOpacityUpdate does run `mc.classList.toggle('map-tier-d',z>=Z_TIER_D)` on the live 'zoom' event, with Z_TIER_D=7.5. The `.map-tier-d ...{opacity:0!important;pointer-events:none;}` rule covers 15 panes: pRealm, pTrail, pRouteLine, pWater, pMajor, pMtn, pSettle, pMinor, pLesser, pOrigin, pFaction, pLane, pWay, pDistrict and pRouteWp. At z7.5, overlayOpacity is 7.5-6.8 = 0.70 (correct in the claim). baseOpacity is 1-(1.3/1.8)*0.88 = 0.364, not 0.39.

The claim says the panes have no transition. That is wrong. The "tier panes (fade reveal)" rule (`.leaflet-pMajor-pane,...,.leaflet-pDistrict-pane{transition:opacity .2s ease;}`) gives 12 of the panes `transition:opacity .2s`. The other three (pTrail, pOrigin, pFaction) get it from the `.leaflet-pTrail-pane,.leaflet-pOrigin-pane,.leaflet-pFaction-pane{transition:opacity .2s ease;}` rule. So all 15 panes take a 200 ms time-based fade, 1 to 0, set off when the zoom crosses 7.5. They do not blink. The real defect is that this fade is tied to time, not to zoom. It is a step in zoom space, softened by 200 ms, so it does not follow the base/overlay crossfade. On a slow pinch or wheel zoom it still reads as a quick vanish at one zoom level. Zooming out reverses it the same way.

This is not a misalignment. No geometry moves. The markers and roads come back exactly where they were drawn. Any offset from the art is the cityBox registration error that already exists, not something this toggle causes. It is a rendering/threshold-policy issue. vector_independent=true is correct.

Corrected magnitude: 15 panes fade from 1 to 0 over about 200 ms (a time fade at a zoom step, dz=0) at overlay 0.70 / base 0.364. Positional shift: 0 px.

Fix. "Add transition .25s" changes nothing, because the panes already have .2s. The pane.style.opacity ramp as written is unsafe for three reasons:
1. An inline opacity overrides the non-!important `.map-tier-a` and `.map-tier-b` hide rules. A ramp that writes 1 below z7.2 would show the panes that tier A/B hide (pSettle, pMinor, pLesser, pDistrict, pRouteWp, pOrigin, pTrail, pFaction and others) at low zoom.
2. The `.map-tier-d` `opacity:0!important` rule beats inline styles, so the ramp only takes effect below 7.5. That leaves a ramp from 1 down to about 0.5 followed by the same step.
3. pointer-events still flip at 7.5.

A correct cheap fix multiplies by a zoom ramp only inside the band and clears it everywhere else. One way: in worldOpacityUpdate, set a CSS custom property, for example `mc.style.setProperty('--tdz', clamp((7.8-z)/0.6, 0, 1))`, used only by a new rule such as `.map-tier-c .leaflet-pSettle-pane{opacity:var(--tdz,1)}` (keep the cascade order below the tier-a/b rules). Then move the map-tier-d class to z>=7.8, so the !important rule and pointer-events:none apply only once the ramp has reached 0. Also turn off the .2s transition while the zoom is live, so the ramp tracks the zoom directly.

UG3 pins: unaffected. xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask are not touched, and cityCanvasSha does not change. Determinism: unaffected, since this is display-only and uses no RNG. Desktop identity and the mobile captures do change between z7.2 and 7.8 and at the class edge. The change also edits worldOpacityUpdate in maps-site/index.html, where the mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) is currently working, so it must be sequenced after or inside that lane. The panes belong to the filigree track (R7) and the motion to the living-chart track.
votes.reason: At HEAD, all 15 tier-d panes already have transition:opacity .2s: 12 from the tier-pane fade-reveal rule, plus pTrail, pOrigin and pFaction. So the claim's "no transition, binary 1 to 0 at dz=0" is wrong, and its cheap fix (add a .25s transition) does nothing. The claim's base opacity at z7.5 is also off: it is 0.364, not 0.39. The claimed ramp through pane.style.opacity is unsafe. prior_record.subsystem: overlay/marks (flyToMarker, flyTo(x,y,t), goWaypoint, pick, flyIntoCity POI branch + openWorldPOI -> showPanel)
prior_record.anchor: flyIntoCity: `if(poiN){var wc=worldPOICoord(key,poiN); if(wc)dest=wc;} ... map.once('moveend',...openWorldPOI)`; CSS #panel (340-px left drawer; @media (max-width:640px){#panel{height:64%}})

items.summary: Rendering: each Leaflet layer rounds its origin to whole CSS px independently, giving at most 1 CSS px hairline jitter between layers (0.0167 atlas px at z9.9); negligible.

prior_record.title: Each Leaflet layer rounds its origin to whole screen px independently, giving up to 1 px jitter between tiles, overlays, markers and vectors
prior_record.anchor: Leaflet ImageOverlay._reset (latLngToLayerPoint(...)._round(), size = difference of rounded corners); GridLayer._setZoomTransform(...).round(); Marker.update/_animateZoom .round(); Renderer._updateTransform (unrounded); Polyline _projectLatlngs (rounded, smoothFactor 1)
prior_record.mechanism: RENDERING, working as intended. With zoomSnap 0 and fractional zoom each layer carries an independent rounding error of up to 0.5 css px per axis, re-rolled every frame; overlay width/height are differences of rounded corners; markers are rounded while SVG transforms are not. Any medium in Leaflet panes inherits it; a single vector layer would round once.
prior_record.fires_when: Every zoom and pan, most visible in flyTo frames and on fractional-DPR screens (1.25, 1.5, 2.625).
prior_record.visible_effect: Hairline shimmer between plan, POIs, tiles and markers; no lasting shift.
prior_record.magnitude: <=1 css px between any two layers (marker vs true point <=0.71 px; 1.5-2.6 device px at DPR 1.5-2.625) = 2^-(z-4) atlas px: 0.016 at z10, 0.008 at z9.9. Overlay scale error <=1/2697 for Epēshu at z9.8. Negligible.
prior_record.cheap_fix: None needed. Future vector city should render in one layer (one rounding); optionally override L.Marker.prototype.update/_animateZoom to drop .round().
prior_record.fix_risks: Patching vendored Leaflet touches internals and may blur glyph edges at DPR 1. No pins.

votes.corrected:
The REGISTRATION/RENDERING split is the point here. This is a RENDERING artifact and it does not fix or cause misalignment. The rounding works as the claim describes. In the vendored Leaflet 1.9.4, latLngToLayerPoint = project(p)._round() - pixelOrigin, and pixelOrigin comes from _getNewPixelOrigin(...)._round(). ImageOverlay._reset rounds its NW and SE corners independently, so the overlay's width/height is the difference of two rounded corners. GridLayer._setZoomTransform rounds its translate to whole px; the level origin cancels out and the scale is left unrounded. Marker.update and Marker._animateZoom both use .round(). Renderer._updateTransform rounds nothing beyond the shared pixel origin. Polyline._projectLatlngs projects through the rounded latLngToLayerPoint, and _simplifyPoints then applies smoothFactor 1. With zoomSnap 0, set in the L.map options in maps-site/index.html, each layer can be off by up to 0.5 css px per axis at rest. That gives at most about 1 css px between two layers, or about 1/2699 scale error for Epēshu at z9.8 (48.46 x 2^5.8 on the short side). This is negligible.

Two parts of the claim need correcting:

(1) The claim says the error is "re-rolled every frame" and stays within 1 px. That is false for SVG vector layers during flyTo, pinch zoom, or any 'zoom'-event motion. ImageOverlay (zoom->_reset), Marker (zoom->update) and GridLayer (zoom->_resetView) recompute on every frame. Renderer.getEvents binds zoom only to _onZoom, which applies a CSS translate plus scale(2^dz) to the previous render. It re-projects only on zoomend (_onZoomEnd->_project) and moveend (_update). So during flyIntoCity's map.flyTo (1.4 s), every polyline is a stale render from the starting zoom stretched by 2^dz. The 0.5 px vertex rounding grows to 0.5*2^dz css px, the 1 px simplification tolerance grows to 2^dz px, and stroke widths grow by 2^dz too. Everything snaps back at moveend. This is a separate mechanism (stale projection plus CSS scale, not sub-pixel rounding) and should be filed as its own finding. It is visible as thick, drifting lines that snap on arrival.

Where it shows: buildCityStubs polylines in pane pCity. These exist only for procedural ('invented') plans; canon Epēshu and Summarch have none. ensureCityOverlay adds them before the flyTo starts, and they stay visible all the way down. pWay, pLane and pDistrict SVG are also affected from z2 until map-tier-d hides them at z7.5 (toggled per frame by worldOpacityUpdate). It only appears when the city is already on screen at the start of the flight. Otherwise _clipPoints leaves nothing drawn until moveend.

(2) The number "0.008 at z9.9" is wrong. 1 css px at z9.9 is 2^-5.9, about 0.0167 atlas px; 0.008 is the half-px bound. Also, a single Leaflet vector layer does not "round once". Each vertex is rounded on its own, which keeps the layer internally consistent to about 1 px. A future vector city built on a stock Leaflet renderer would also inherit problem (1), unless it redraws on every 'zoom' event (a custom canvas or SVG layer re-projected each frame, or a forced renderer _update on zoom). So "no fix needed" holds for the rounding only, not for the vector-city path.

GridLayer._setZoomTransform ends with .round() and passes an unrounded scale to setTransform. Marker.update and Marker._animateZoom both call .round(). Renderer._updateTransform has no rounding. Polyline._projectLatlngs uses latLngToLayerPoint, and smoothFactor defaults to 1 in _simplifyPoints.

votes.corrected:
The mechanism, the visible effect, the "negligible" verdict and vector_independent=true are all right. Two magnitude numbers are wrong, and the optional fix needs a narrower scope.

Magnitude. 1 css px = 2^-(z-NZ) atlas px, with NZ=4 in maps-site/index.html. That gives 0.0156 at z10, 0.0167 at z9.9 (not 0.008; 0.008 is about z11), 0.0055 at Z_STREET 11.5, and 1 atlas px at z4.

Internals confirmed in vendor/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js:
- latLngToLayerPoint calls _round().
- Marker.update calls .round().
- GridLayer _setZoomTransform calls .round().
- Renderer _updateTransform is not rounded.

Cheap fix. None needed. Do not add the optional marker override. Dropping .round() from L.Marker.prototype.update and _animateZoom gains nothing, because tiles and overlays stay rounded and the gap between layers keeps the same bound. It also blurs divIcon glyphs at DPR 1.

- It leaves the UG3 pins alone (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask, cityCanvasSha), and determinism too, because it is render-only.
- It changes subpixel marker rects on every profile, so the desktop-identity and baseline-equality checks would see it as an undeclared change.
- It lands in maps-site/index.html while the atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) is mid-flight there.

So keep it out.

items.summary: Lifecycle: setMinZoom/setMaxZoom queue an animated setZoom in rAF that survives the following synchronous setView, so exitChart lands on the east/bottom clamp (1113 atlas px, 407 screen px on 1200x800) with the saved zoom lost and can kill a following fly, and enterChart lands in the chart's top-left quadrant; in refit the race preserves the view.

prior_record.title: setMinZoom/setMaxZoom queue an animated setZoom that fires after the synchronous setView, so chart entry/exit and resize land in the wrong place
prior_record.anchor: exitChart: `map.setMinZoom(s.minZoom); map.setMaxZoom(s.maxZoom);` then `map.setView(s.center,s.zoom,{animate:false})`; enterChart `map.setMinZoom(minZ); map.setMaxZoom(maxZ);` then setView(cb.getCenter(),minZ,...); refit `map.setMinZoom(...)`; vendored leaflet.js setMinZoom/setMaxZoom -> setZoom -> _tryAnimatedZoom (requestAnimFrame(_animateZoom))
prior_record.mechanism: Leaflet 1.9.4. When the current zoom is outside the new limit, setMinZoom/setMaxZoom call setZoom, which setView(getCenter(),limit); for |dz|<=zoomAnimationThreshold (4) _tryAnimatedZoom defers `_moveStart()._animateZoom(oldCenter,limit)` to the next frame. The app's synchronous setView({animate:false}) resets the view, map._stop() does not cancel the queued frame, and one frame later the queued animation moves to the OLD centre latlng at the clamped zoom, read in the NEW frame; moveend then _panInsideMaxBounds clamps to the nearest edge. World and chart frames share one CRS, so the old centre lands arbitrarily. Reproduced by driving vendored leaflet.js in a Node DOM shim (no browser). Also queues the stranded animation that ensureArrival has to clear.
prior_record.fires_when: exitChart whenever chart zoom at exit is below the world fitZoom (true for every image chart: chart h>137 px, all 7 DETAIL charts are 305-4200 px). enterChart when world zoom minus chart maxZ is in (0,4] (image chart maxZ ~2.8; opening a region chart from tier c ~z4.85). refit when the viewport grows taller. UI-reachable charts: Seat, Nīmlad, Far North, Home Islands, Rhusagos; Epēshu/Summarch pyramids only via ATLAS.chart() (UI routes them to flyIntoCity). Exits within a 250 ms animation also hit animating-zoom-drops-setview.
prior_record.visible_effect: On exit the world appears where the reader was, then animates to the chart's centre latlng and is pushed against the atlas edge; after 'Back to the Wide World' the saved view is not restored. On entry the chart shows its fill view for one frame then zooms to max zoom on its top-left corner.
prior_record.magnitude: Shim (1200x800): exit from the Epēshu pyramid at fill z0.65 restored world to atlas (2753,1096) instead of (1640,1095): 1113 atlas px = 407 screen px at fitZoom 2.55, on the east clamp. Entering Rhusagos (863x467) from world z5.0 settled at chart px (125,58) z2.80 instead of (431,234) z0.80: dz 2.0 (x4), offset (306,176) chart px. Plausible/unmeasured in a real browser; probe: ATLAS.chart('Seat'), then ATLAS.exitChart() and compare centre.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Never let the limit setters reach setZoom: assign map.options.minZoom/maxZoom directly, setView(...,{animate:false}), then map.fire('zoomlevelschange') (zoom-control state). Alternatively setView first with limits pre-widened, then narrow. Do not reorder setView before the range change in enterChart (_limitZoom would clamp to the old range). Apply in enterChart, exitChart and both branches of refit.
prior_record.fix_risks: No UG3-pinned function touched. Only the buggy post-frame motion goes away on desktop. Zoom-control enable/disable depends on zoomlevelschange, so keep the fire. refit sits in the mobile lanes; the Mobile 5-9 atlas lane is mid-flight, so coordinate.

votes.corrected:
The core mechanism holds. One correction: in refit it actually preserves the reader's view rather than misplacing it. There are also three wording fixes and a worse exit-then-fly case that the claim missed.

MECHANISM (confirmed by reading the vendored leaflet.js 1.9.4)
- `setMinZoom`/`setMaxZoom`: when the current zoom is outside the new limit, they fire `zoomlevelschange` and call `setZoom(limit)`.
- `setZoom` calls `setView(getCenter(), limit, {zoom: undefined})`, which goes to `_tryAnimatedZoom`. Default `zoomAnimationThreshold` is 4. The offset to the centre itself is 0. Pane elements carrying `leaflet-zoom-animated` exist. So the function queues `x(...)` (window.requestAnimationFrame) to run `_moveStart(!0)._animateZoom(oldCenter, limit, !0)`, and returns.
- The app's following `setView(..., {animate:false})` does a synchronous `_resetView`. The frame is not stored anywhere: `_stop` cancels only `_flyToFrame` and `_panAnim`, so it survives.
- When the frame runs, `_animateZoom` `_move`s to the OLD centre latlng at the limit zoom, read in whatever frame is current (the chart and the world share one `CRS.Simple`).
- 250 ms later `_onZoomTransitionEnd` calls `_moveEnd`, which fires `moveend` and runs `_panInsideMaxBounds`. `setMaxBounds` re-armed that handler, so the view is clamped against the restored bounds.

EXIT (`exitChart` in maps-site/index.html)
- It fires whenever the chart zoom at exit is below the saved world minZoom (fitZoom). At the chart's fill zoom that holds for every DETAIL chart, because all heights are 305-4200 px, above the ~137 px threshold. The difference in zoom is always ≤4, so the animated path is the one taken.
- The saved centre AND the saved zoom are both lost; the view lands at fitZoom.
- The chart centre in world px works out to (8·w, 8·h) for image charts and (2·x, 2·y) for the tile pyramids, which is always south of the atlas. So the reader ends up clamped to the bottom-middle band of the atlas, and for most charts against the east edge too. The shim figure (2753,1096) matches the east clamp at fitZoom 2.55 on a 1200×800 view.
- "Back to the Wide World" and Escape take exactly this path. `setHash` uses `replaceState`, so `restorePanel` does not re-enter `handleHash`.

WORSE CASE (traced, not measured): exit followed by a fly
- Three paths do this: `pick` from chart mode (`exitChart` then `flyTo`), `openPOI`'s "back to the city card" (`exitChart` then `flyToMarker`), and `handleHash` to a city you fly into (`exitChart` then `flyIntoCity`).
- The queued zoom-animation runs during the fly. At 250 ms `_onZoomTransitionEnd` `_move`s the view to the off-atlas chart centre. The `moveend` clamp then calls `panTo`, whose `setView` calls `_stop`, which cancels `_flyToFrame`. The fly dies and the reader rests on the clamp, not on the marker.
- `flyIntoCity` is rescued only by `ensureArrival`'s 1.7 s hard-land. `pick` and `flyToMarker` have no such fallback.
- So the claim's "stranded animation that `ensureArrival` has to clear" names the wrong thing. `_animatingZoom` clears itself at 250 ms. What is stranded is the fly.

ENTRY (`enterChart`)
- It fires when the world zoom minus the chart maxZ is in (0, 4]. Image charts have maxZ = max(minZ+2, 2), about 2.8-3.6. If the difference is above 4, the reset is synchronous and harmless.
- The chart ends at maxZ, centred on the old world centre latlng. That falls in the TOP-LEFT QUADRANT, not exactly on the corner: chart px ≤ (274,137) for image charts, ≤ (2195,1094) for the tile pyramids.
- Correction to "fill view for one frame": rAF callbacks run before the next paint, so the synchronous fill view is probably never painted. What the reader sees is a 250 ms CSS zoom transition toward the wrong spot, then the clamp pan.

REFIT (claim mislabelled)
- The mechanism does fire when the viewport grows taller. But the queued frame takes the view to the reader's OLD centre at the new min zoom. That overrides the code's own `setView(EPESHU)` or `setView(CHART.cb.getCenter())`.
- The net effect is that the reader's position is preserved, with a flicker. It does not land in a wrong place.

FIX
- The cheap fix is right for `enterChart` and `exitChart`: assign `map.options.minZoom`/`maxZoom` directly, then `setView(..., {animate:false})`, then `map.fire('zoomlevelschange')`. Keep the range change before `setView`, because `_limitZoom` clamps to the current range.
- Applied as written to `refit`, though, the fix makes `getZoom() < fitZoom` true at the check and causes a NEW jump to Epēshu or the chart centre. In both `refit` branches use `map.getCenter()` instead.
- This is a registration-independent viewport bug: a vector city would misbehave identically. It is not about art placement.

- `_tryAnimatedZoom` queues `x(function(){this._moveStart(!0, ...)._animateZoom(t, e, !0)}, this)`, where `x` is `$.call(window, ...)` = requestAnimationFrame. The default `zoomAnimationThreshold` is 4.
- `_stop` only does `r(this._flyToFrame)` and `_panAnim.stop()`, so it does not cancel the queued frame.
- `_animateZoom` and `_onZoomTransitionEnd` `_move` to `_animateToCenter`/`_animateToZoom`, then `_moveEnd`.
- `setMaxBounds` re-registers `moveend` → `_panInsideMaxBounds`. `panTo` → `setView` → `_stop` cancels `_flyToFrame`.

maps-site/index.html:
- `enterChart` calls `map.setMinZoom(minZ); map.setMaxZoom(maxZ);` and then `setView(cb.getCenter(), minZ, {animate:false})`.
- `exitChart` calls `map.setMinZoom(s.minZoom); map.setMaxZoom(s.maxZoom);` and then `setView(s.center, s.zoom, {animate:false})`, then `setMaxBounds(s.maxBounds)`.
- `refit` calls `setMinZoom` and then `setView(EPESHU or cb centre)` only if `getZoom() <` the limit.
- No `zoomAnimation` or threshold override exists in the app.

Chart data:
- data/detail-charts.json heights are 305-4200, so at the fill zoom exit always falls below fitZoom with a zoom difference under 4.
- My Epēshu arithmetic reproduces the claimed (2753,1096) east clamp: the chart centre lands at world (3914,4200), below the atlas.

Reachability:
- `setHash` uses `replaceState`, so the Back button path animates to the chart centre and clamps without flying.
- `pick`, `openPOI` back-link and `handleHash` → `flyIntoCity` chain a fly after `exitChart`. The 250 ms clamp's `panTo` kills the fly; only `flyIntoCity` has the `ensureArrival` net.

Why major, and where the claim was partly wrong:
- Severity is major: after leaving any UI chart the reader is thrown to the atlas's bottom/east clamp at fitZoom, which anyone at the table would notice.
- The claim was partly wrong on `refit` (the effect preserves the reader's position, and its own fix would regress `refit`), on the "one frame of fill view" detail, on the `ensureArrival` "stranded" wording, and on "top-left corner" (it is the top-left quadrant).
- Browser magnitude is still unmeasured; probe with `ATLAS.chart('Seat')` then `ATLAS.exitChart()` and compare the centre and zoom after 300 ms.

prior_record.title: A viewport resize at min zoom recentres the atlas on Epēshu
prior_record.anchor: refit: `fitZoom=fillZoom(); map.setMinZoom(fitZoom); if(map.getZoom()<fitZoom)map.setView(px(EPESHU[0],EPESHU[1]),fitZoom,{animate:false});` (EPESHU=[1222,1404]); refit also calls updTier; fonts.ready re-fit; 180 ms resize debounce
prior_record.mechanism: View logic. fillZoom snaps up to 0.05. When the viewport gets taller (rotation to portrait, URL bar collapse, fonts.ready reflow, window drag, devtools), fitZoom rises above the current zoom and refit sets the view to the hard-coded EPESHU constant, not the current centre. Combined with setminmax-zoom-race, setMinZoom(fitZoom) also queues an animated setZoom around the old centre, so the view flashes to Epēshu then animates to a third place (re-clamped by maxBounds); the reader's position is lost twice.
prior_record.fires_when: Resize or fonts.ready refit while zoom < new fitZoom (at or near min zoom); phones on URL-bar toggle.
prior_record.visible_effect: The atlas jumps (or flashes) to Leponnia, then slides to a centre that is neither the old one nor Epēshu.
prior_record.magnitude: Pan of |centre-(1222,1404)| up to ~1.2k-2.4k atlas-width px (about 1.2k screen px at z2.6); dz = fitZoom change, typically 0.05-0.4 (log2(h2/h1)). Shim 1200x800 to 1200x1000 from atlas (3000,800): synchronous step to (1286,1117), a 1714 atlas px flash = 795 screen px at z2.9, settling at (2751,1096) (x moved 249 px = 116 screen px where the old x was still legal).

That becomes setView(getCenter(),t), and _tryAnimatedZoom queues a requestAnimFrame `_animateZoom(oldCentre,fitZoom)` and returns true. Only after that does refit's EPESHU setView({animate:false}) _resetView synchronously to Epēshu, clamped to about (1286,1116) at z2.9. Its `_stop()` cancels only _flyToFrame and _panAnim, not the queued rAF. On the next frame, _animateZoom runs `_move(oldCentre,fitZoom)` and adds the zoom-anim CSS transition, and 250 ms later _onZoomTransitionEnd fires zoomend and moveend there. The view settles on the pre-resize centre, re-clamped by maxBounds at the new fitZoom. At a higher zoom the legal x range only gets wider, so in practice only y re-centres. The requested (3000,800) had already been clamped to about (2751,1094) before the resize. So '(2751,1096)' is the old centre, not a third place, and the old x 3000 was never legal. The flash distance is 2751-1286, about 1465 atlas px or about 683 screen px at z2.9, not 1714/795. When it fires: only a TALLER map (rotation to portrait, window drag, devtools closing; on phones the URL bar, because #app is 100dvh), while zoom is below the new fitZoom. A shorter map lowers fitZoom and only setMinZoom runs. The fonts.ready path does nothing on first load, because the view is already Epēshu, unless the reader panned before fonts resolved. Leaflet's own trackResize (default true) has usually called invalidateSize({debounceMoveend:true}) within a frame of the resize, so refit's invalidateSize is normally a no-op. The animated setView also calls clearTimeout(_sizeTimer), which cancels Leaflet's debounced moveend. Without 3D transforms (_zoomAnimated false), setMinZoom resets synchronously to the old centre and the EPESHU branch never runs. This is not a registration issue and has nothing to do with vector vs raster. Fix: drop the EPESHU setView, since setMinZoom already zooms around the current centre. Or, to kill the animation too, assign map.options.minZoom=fitZoom, fire 'zoomlevelschange', then setView(map.getCenter(),fitZoom,{animate:false}). Keep EPESHU for first load only. The fix leaves the settled position unchanged, so the 'mobile-capture baselines at min zoom change' risk is probably overstated; only the transient goes away. It should still land inside or after the Mobile 5-9 lane.

So the view settles back on the pre-resize centre, clamped at the new fitZoom. The cost is a jolt or flash of up to 250 ms, not a lost position, and certainly not 'lost twice' or a 'third place'. The claim's own numbers bear this out: (3000,800) was already clamped to x≈2751 at z2.55, so the settled (2751,1096) is the old centre. The title's claim that the view is recentred on Epēshu, and the visible effect it describes, are wrong. What is left is a subtle transient on resize.

MECHANISM (holds): in maps-site/index.html `refit` runs `fitZoom=fillZoom(); map.setMinZoom(fitZoom); if(map.getZoom()<fitZoom)map.setView(px(EPESHU[0],EPESHU[1]),fitZoom,{animate:false});`. - 1200x800 to 1200x1000: fitZoom goes 2.55 to 2.90 (dz=0.35). clamp(EPESHU) at z2.90 (scale 0.4665, hw 1286, hh 1072) is (1286, 1116). From the rightmost legal old centre (2751, 1094), the flash is about 1465 atlas px, about 683 screen px (not 1714 / 795). The view rests back at about (2751, 1094 to 1116), so the rest offset is about 0 to 22 atlas px of y re-clamp.
- General case: flash = |x_old - clamp(1222, hw_new, IMG_W-hw_new)| plus a y term of 1 to 2 hundred px or less. It is bounded by (IMG_W - hw_old) - max(1222, hw_new). That is about 1.5k atlas px on desktop widths and up to about 2.7k atlas px on narrow phones: 390x844 at z2.65 gives hw about 497, about 2670 atlas px, about 1050 screen px, about 2.7 viewport widths. vector_independent = true (pure view logic). It is neither registration nor rendering medium.

CHEAP FIX (correct, with an ordering refinement): keep the view where it is.
- Option 1: `fitZoom=fillZoom(); if(map.getZoom()<fitZoom)map.setView(map.getCenter(),fitZoom,{animate:false}); map.setMinZoom(fitZoom);`. Doing the setView before setMinZoom means getZoom() is no longer below the minimum, so no animated setZoom is queued. setView's _limitCenter applies the maxBounds clamp, and you avoid poking options.minZoom.

RISKS (corrected):
- No UG3 pins are touched: refit, fillZoom and EPESHU are outside xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask. cityCanvasSha and determinism are untouched.
- Desktop identity is NOT strictly unchanged. The fonts.ready refit runs at load whenever the container box changes. Today it re-centres on raw EPESHU, clamped at the new zoom. getCenter() would keep the old-zoom-clamped centre, e.g. y 1094 instead of 1116 in the example above. So either keep EPESHU until the first user move or zoom, or accept a few tens of px of y drift in load baselines.
- The Mobile 5-9 lane owns phone resize. docs/mobile/units.json verifies a 'fonts.ready refit no-op at the five profiles', so land this inside or after that lane and expect the min-zoom mobile-capture baselines to be re-taken.
votes.reason: The mechanism and the cheap-fix direction are right, but the effect and the magnitude are overstated. The shim started from (3000,800), which can't happen at min zoom: y is locked near 1094 and x can't exceed 2751 at z2.55. So its 'settles at a third place, position lost twice' is an artifact. In reality setMinZoom's queued animated zoom brings the view back to the old centre about 250 ms after the synchronous snap to Epēshu, so it is a transient flash of about 1.5k to 2.7k atlas px with almost no lasting displacement. The 1714 px / 795 screen px figures should be about 1465 px / 683 px. Also, 'desktop identity unchanged' ignores the fonts.ready refit at load, where getCenter() differs from re-clamped EPESHU by a few tens of px in y. items.summary: View policy: the zoom ceiling follows nearestCity of the map centre while the wheel zooms about the cursor, so aiming at an off-centre city hits the z8 wall until the centre drifts within 3r and the plan registers, then the plan pops in at overlayOpacity(z).

prior_record.title: The zoom ceiling follows the map centre while the wheel and pinch zoom toward the cursor
prior_record.anchor: wheel handler `target=Math.max(map.getMinZoom(),Math.min(map.getMaxZoom(),z+step))` + setZoomAround vs worldCityUpdate `map.project(map.getCenter(),NZ)`; ensureCityGen async (z5 tile fetch) kicked at z>6.5
prior_record.mechanism: View policy. The ceiling is chosen by nearestCity of the CENTRE and the reg only exists after ensureCityGen. Aiming the cursor at an off-centre village stops at 8 until the centre drifts within 3r and the mask lands; then registerCityOverlay -> worldCityUpdate raises the ceiling and the art pops in at overlayOpacity(z).
prior_record.fires_when: Zooming with the cursor on a city not under the centre, or before its plan is generated (z6.5-8).
prior_record.visible_effect: The zoom hits a wall at 8, then the plan pops in at partial or full opacity mid-gesture.
prior_record.magnitude: Ceiling stall dz up to cityMaxZ-8 (<=3.0); pop-in step overlayOpacity(z) up to 1.0 at z>=7.8. Probe: ATLAS.cityReg before/after a wheel sequence toward Kanae.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Choose the city by the cursor/pinch point (pass it from the wheel handler) or by nearest anchor within the viewport; call ensureCityGen in the PREWARM window (z>5.6) for every anchor in view.
prior_record.fix_risks: More tile fetches on mobile. Not pinned.

votes.corrected:
The mechanism is in maps-site/index.html. It is a view-policy fault, not a registration one, and it would happen the same way with a vector city. The wheel handler (`target=Math.max(map.getMinZoom(),Math.min(map.getMaxZoom(),z+step))`, then `map.setZoomAround(ll,target,{animate:false})`) clamps to the LIVE maxZoom and zooms toward the cursor. That call is synchronous, so zoomend/moveend run worldCityUpdate after every wheel event. worldCityUpdate picks the city with `nearestCity(cp.x,cp.y)` on `cp=map.project(map.getCenter(),NZ)`, which only returns a city within 3*footR of the CENTRE. It then sets `allowed=reg?cityMaxZ(...):Z_OPEN_MAX` (8.0), calls `map.setMaxZoom(allowed)` and runs `ensureCityOverlay((reg&&z>6.5)?near.name:null)`.

Two cases:

(A) Off-centre aim, a hard wall. The world distance from the centre to the cursor point is the screen offset divided by 2^(z-4), which is offset/16 at z8. With 3r = village 27, ruin 24, town 42 and capital 78, the zoom stops at 8 whenever the cursor sits more than about 432 / 384 / 672 / 1248 CSS px from the view centre. Being off-centre is common on desktop, since 115 of the 136 anchors are villages. The claim says the zoom waits "until the centre drifts", but at the cap nothing drifts: the handler returns early (`if(Math.abs(target-z)<1e-4)return;`), so setZoomAround, moveend and worldCityUpdate never run again. Only a pan releases it. The prewarm branch cannot help either: it also requires `near`, which is already within 3r, so its `*6` radius test never adds anything. The plan is therefore never even generated for an aimed-at, off-centre village.

(B) Centre within 3r but CITYREG not yet filled. ensureCityGen is kicked at z>6.5, or prewarmed at 5.6<z<=6.5. It is async: sampleCityMask loads z5 tiles through the same `?t=` URL as the base, which is usually a cache hit, then runs genCityCanvas plus toDataURL synchronously. Until then the cap is 8. The callback calls worldCityUpdate, which raises the cap with no user action. This wall is short and mostly bounded by the generation cost.

In both cases, once reg and near meet, ensureCityOverlay adds the overlay with `ov.setOpacity(overlayOpacity(map.getZoom()))`. At z>=7.8 that is 1.0, over a base already faded to 0.12. The result is a hard pop from ghost to full plan, with no fade.

Touch: default Leaflet TouchZoom pinches around the pinch midpoint and clamps at touchend via `_limitZoom`, bouncing back because bounceAtZoomLimits is on by default. On phone widths (half-width under about 432 px) case A rarely triggers for villages, so phones mainly hit case B.

Side effect: with dense villages, the centre's nearest anchor can be a neighbour of the target. The neighbour then sets the ceiling and its overlay shows.

Magnitudes: ceiling stall dz = cityMaxZ - 8. That is about 2.83 for a generated village (2048 px), 3.0 for a ruin, 1.3 for a generated capital, and 1.88 for Epēshu canon. The pop step is up to 1.0.

Fix: in the wheel handler, project the cursor latLng to NZ, run nearestCity there, raise setMaxZoom before clamping, and kick ensureCityGen or ensureCityGenNow for it. Also give the prewarm its own radius (6r, or the viewport) instead of nearestCity's 3r. Mobile cost: more z5 tile fetches and 2048-px generation work. None of the pinned functions change.
votes.reason: I read the whole code path in the head export of maps-site/index.html. The wheel handler clamps to getMaxZoom() and zooms around the cursor. worldCityUpdate runs on 'zoomend moveend' (setZoomAround with animate:false fires them synchronously) and chooses the ceiling with nearestCity on map.getCenter() within 3*footR. Z_OPEN_MAX is 8.0. ensureCityGen goes through sampleCityMask, an async image load of the z5 tiles, and its callback calls worldCityUpdate. ensureCityOverlay sets the opacity straight to overlayOpacity(z). The claim holds, with two corrections. First, at the cap the wheel is a no-op that returns early, so the centre never 'drifts'; only a pan releases the wall. Second, the prewarm is gated by the same centre-within-3r test, so it never prewarms an off-centre target. The wall is a hard stop at z8 over a base faded to 0.12, often hit on desktop with 115 villages (anything more than about 432 px off-centre), followed by a full-opacity pop. A reader at the table would notice it, so major. It is view policy, independent of raster vs vector.

votes.corrected:
MECHANISM: confirmed in maps-site/index.html. worldCityUpdate runs on 'zoomend moveend' and picks the city with nearestCity(map.project(map.getCenter(),NZ)) inside 3*footR. The ceiling is cityMaxZ(a,reg.w,reg.h) only once registryFor(near.name) exists, otherwise Z_OPEN_MAX=8.0. The wheel handler clamps to the live map.getMaxZoom() and calls setZoomAround(cursor). This is VIEW POLICY. It is neither registration nor a positional shift: nothing moves relative to the atlas. The effect is a stall, then a pop.

WHAT IS RIGHT AND WHAT TO CORRECT:
(1) The centre does not drift by itself once the zoom is at the wall. At z=8 the handler's `if(Math.abs(target-z)<1e-4)return` fires, so setZoomAround stops pulling the centre toward the cursor. The stall lasts until the user pans.
(2) Before the wall, the centre converges on the cursor point. At z=8 the centre sits (screen offset)/2^(8-NZ) = offset/16 world px from the cursor. The centre is captured if the cursor is on the anchor and less than 3r*16 screen px from the screen centre:
- village (r=9): 432 px
- ruin (r=8): 384 px
- town (r=14): 672 px
- capital (r=26): 1248 px
Inside those offsets the stall is transient: sampleCityMask has to land (it uses the z5 tiles, which are usually already browser-cached because the base layer draws them at z>=5), then the ceiling rises. Farther off-centre, or when a different anchor is nearer the centre, the stall is permanent until the user pans.
(3) Magnitude, recomputed with GEN_SIZE=2048 and NZ=4 (cityMaxZ = 4 + log2(mx/2r), capped at 11.5):
- village 10.83 (dz 2.83; Kanae is a village, so 2.83 there)
- town 10.19 (dz 2.19)
- ruin 11.00 (dz 3.00, the maximum)
- generated capital 9.30
- canon Epēshu 3072/52 → 9.88 (dz 1.88; it is registered at init, so it only suffers the centre-selection half of the problem)
So 'dz <= 3.0' holds. The pop-in is at full opacity: once the reg lands, ensureCityOverlay adds the overlay with overlayOpacity(8)=1. It shows no partial fade unless the user had stopped below 7.8.

VECTOR_INDEPENDENT: essentially true. Any medium gated by centre-based selection stalls the same way. One caveat: the ceiling VALUE (1 image px ≈ 1 screen px) and the async mask→canvas→toDataURL delay are raster-specific. A vector city could allow Z_STREET without waiting for an encode, but it would still need the mask for registration.

CHEAP FIX AS WRITTEN IS WRONG:
(a) Passing the cursor point from the wheel handler alone causes a snap-back. setZoomAround(animate:false) fires zoomend/moveend synchronously, so worldCityUpdate immediately re-selects by the centre and calls map.setMaxZoom(8). Leaflet's setMaxZoom then calls setZoom when the current zoom is above the new maximum, which jumps the view back out.
(b) Phone pinch goes through Leaflet TouchZoom, not this wheel listener. It is not covered and shows as a bounce at the limit.
(c) Calling ensureCityGen for every anchor in view at z>5.6 costs too much on phones. The view at z5.6 is roughly 460 world px wide and holds several anchors in Leponnia's cluster. Each one bakes a 2048² canvas plus a webp/png toDataURL, and CITYREG keeps it forever. This hits the mobile lane's phone-parity and delay-not-drop gates.

CORRECTED FIX: make worldCityUpdate itself viewport-based. Set allowed = max cityMaxZ over the registered cities whose cityBox intersects the current bounds. Keep Z_OPEN_MAX only when none intersect. Never lower the max below the current zoom while a city footprint is still in view, which removes the ease-down snap. Kick ensureCityGen (ensureCityGenNow on a deep wheel only) for at most the one or two anchors nearest the cursor or pinch focus. Keep PREWARM to the single nearest anchor on coarse pointers.

PINS: none of this touches xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask. UG3 atlas_fn_sha and cityCanvasSha are unchanged, and generation stays deterministic because only call timing changes. But the fix changes desktop behaviour in worldCityUpdate and the wheel IIFE, the same file where the atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) is mid-flight. It must be queued after Mobile 9, or written as a central unit with a desktop-identity re-capture. 'Not pinned' undersells that.

items.summary: View policy: flyToMarker, goWaypoint and flyTo(x,y,t) request max(current, tier) zoom without clamping to the destination's ceiling, so a fly started past z8 inside a city lands deep and then eases out (second stage up to dz 3.0).

prior_record.title: Flights keep deep zoom into open country, then ease out after landing
prior_record.anchor: flyToMarker / goWaypoint / flyTo(x,y,t): `Math.max(map.getZoom(),tierZoom(...))`; Leaflet flyTo does no _limitZoom
prior_record.mechanism: View policy. These flyTo calls request max(current zoom, tier zoom); Leaflet's flyTo does not clamp to maxZoom or maxBounds. Starting at z10 in a city the fly ends at z10 at the destination; moveend -> worldCityUpdate -> setMaxZoom(8) -> animated setZoom(8). If the old city's ceiling equals allowed no setMaxZoom runs and the map can rest above maxZoom.
prior_record.fires_when: Clicking a marker, waypoint, company origin, faction seat or search result while zoomed past 8 (inside a city).
prior_record.visible_effect: A two-stage motion: the fly lands deep in blank ghost country, then the map shrinks again 250 ms later.
prior_record.magnitude: Second-stage dz = start zoom - 8, up to 3.0 (x8). Probe: ATLAS.descend('Kanae') then ATLAS.fly('Epēshu') logging zoomend values.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Clamp fly targets: Math.min(Math.max(z,tier), cityAllowedAt(dest)) using the same nearestCity/registryFor rule as worldCityUpdate.
prior_record.fix_risks: Not pinned. Desktop fly endpoints change only when starting above 8.

items.summary: Input: while _animatingZoom is set (250 ms after any animated zoom) setView(...,{animate:false}) silently returns, so wheel steps and programmatic restores issued then are dropped, not caught up (0.5-1 level).

prior_record.title: While a CSS zoom animation runs, setView(...,{animate:false}) is silently ignored, so wheel input and view restores are dropped

- The window is not just 250 ms. `_tryAnimatedZoom` defers the start through requestAnimFrame (`x(function(){...this._animateZoom(t,e,!0)},this)`). A setView in that frame does apply, but the queued `_animateZoom` then overwrites it with `_move` back to the old animateToCenter/Zoom, which shows as a short jump. In total that is roughly 16 + 250 ms.
- These input-driven animations trigger it: zoomControl is on (zoomDelta .25), keyboard +/-, double-click, touch pinch end, and the setMaxZoom ease-down in worldCityUpdate (setMaxZoom calls setZoom, which animates). The wheel handler itself uses animate:false and never starts an animation, so wheel followed by wheel is safe. flyTo does not set `_animatingZoom`: setView's `_stop()` cancels a fly instead.

- One wheel detent is `step=clamp(-dy*0.0045,±1)`. That is 0.45 for dy=100 (Chrome), 0.445 for Firefox (deltaMode 1: 3*33=99), 0.54 for dy=120, and 1 for deltaMode 2.

- Mac trackpad pinch (ctrl+wheel, k=0.018) is also swallowed. At about 15 events in the window, that is roughly 0.3-1 level.

The mechanism exists as described, with small corrections.
