In the vendored leaflet 1.9.4, setZoomAround computes the centre that keeps the cursor latlng fixed and calls setView. setView runs `t=this._limitCenter(w(t),e,this.options.maxBounds)` before anything else. When the target view would cross contentBounds by more than 1 px, the centre is replaced, so the content under the cursor moves.

How far it moves: the offset is d*(1-2^-dz), where d is the cursor's distance in screen px from the edge where empty space would open. Space opens on the side away from the cursor, so the place under the cursor drifts toward and past the screen centre, toward that side. The worst case is the full view dimension, H*(1-2^-dz), not W/2. W/2*(1-2^-dz) is the case with the cursor at the screen centre: 176 px for a half-level step on a 1200 px view. A 1-level step on a 700 px view gives up to 350 px. Vertically the clamp is almost certain whenever a zoom-out reaches fitZoom, because the view then spans the whole atlas height. Summarch really is anchored at y=58: `CITY_ANCHORS['Summarch']={atlasX:523,atlasY:58,...}`. The suggested probe, cursor at the top edge at fitZoom+0.3, only shows a slide if the view is not already touching the top edge. Otherwise the top stays put and nothing moves.

1. The +/- buttons call zoomOut, then setZoom(getCenter()), which goes through the same _limitCenter. They have no cursor anchor, so what moves is the centre of the view.
2. Touch pinch takes a different path. TouchZoom._onTouchMove calls map._move with no clamp, so during the gesture the content follows the fingers and the empty space beyond the atlas edge can show. _onTouchEnd calls _animateZoom on the centre without a clamp. Only the following moveend fires `_panInsideMaxBounds`, which runs panInsideBounds and then an animated panTo, so the slide comes after release.
3. flyTo frames (_move) are not clamped either, so space beyond the edge shows during the flight and is closed by the same animated `_panInsideMaxBounds` at moveend. That part of the claim is right.

maxBoundsViscosity only affects dragging and plays no part here. This is view-level and the same for raster and vector: every layer moves together, so it causes no misregistration between the city art and the atlas.
votes.reason:
I traced the code end to end. In maps-site/index.html the wheel handler calls setZoomAround on top of setMaxBounds(contentBounds) and setMinZoom(fitZoom). In the vendored leaflet.js, setZoomAround calls setView, which applies _limitCenter, and setMaxBounds registers _panInsideMaxBounds on moveend. Summarch's atlasY:58 is confirmed.

Most of the claim is right. The parts that were partly wrong:
- The magnitude: the worst case is the full view dimension, not half of it.
- Touch pinch: no clamp during the gesture, and an animated slide after release.
- The buttons have no cursor anchor.
- The probe only works if the view is not already touching the top edge.

I rate it minor rather than major. A table reader would see the content slide when zooming out near the frame, but every map with a max-bounds limit does this, and it moves all layers together. It does not cause the art-versus-atlas registration shift the owner reports.

votes.corrected:
The mechanism is right. In maps-site/index.html the wheel handler calls map.setZoomAround(ll,target,{animate:false}), the map is created with maxBoundsViscosity:1.0, and map.setMaxBounds(contentBounds) is applied. Leaflet's setZoomAround leads to setView, which calls _limitCenter, so when the view touches the atlas frame the clamp overrides the cursor anchor. Overlays and markers move with the map, so this is a viewport slide, not a registration error: the art and the base never move relative to each other. vector_independent=true is correct.

VISIBLE EFFECT, corrected: the place under the cursor slides toward the pinned (touching) frame edge, not toward the screen centre. Take d as the screen distance from the cursor to the pinned edge, along the clamped axis. After a zoom-out of dz that point sits d*2^-dz from the edge, so the slide is d*(1-2^-dz).

MAGNITUDE, corrected:
- The slide depends on cursor position and is zero with the cursor on the pinned edge.
- With the cursor at the screen centre it is H/2*(1-2^-dz). For a 1200-px view and a half-level step that is 176 px, which is the claim's figure, but it only holds for that case.
- The maximum is the full view extent: H*(1-2^-dz), with the cursor at the opposite edge. That is about 351 px on a 1200-px view at dz=0.5.
- Wheel steps are clamped to |dz|≤1 (k=0.0045 for a wheel, 0.018 for ctrl/pinch), and target is clamped to getMinZoom.
- At min zoom (fitZoom) the handler returns early (|target-z|<1e-4), so nothing slides there. The 350 px on a 700-px map is reachable only when zooming from fitZoom+1 down to fitZoom with the cursor on the far side from the pinned edge, not "at min zoom".
- The zoom buttons (zoomDelta .25, zoom about the centre) slide H/2*(1-2^-0.25) ≈ 0.08H.

PROBE, corrected: do not put the cursor on the touching edge, because that gives zero slide. Either set the view vertically mid-frame at fitZoom+0.3 and wheel out with the cursor near the top or bottom (the only valid centre at fitZoom forces a slide of up to H*(1-2^-0.3) ≈ 0.19H), or put the cursor at the edge opposite the pinned one.

CHEAP FIX, corrected: accept it as intended. With viscosity 1.0, the anchor and the clamp cannot both hold. "Zoom around the clamped point" just moves the same slide earlier. Clamping the zoom target (stopping the zoom-out once the frame would be exceeded) changes the zoom feel, not the alignment.

bounceAtZoomLimits:false is unrelated to the bounds slide. It only stops pinch overshoot past min/max zoom, which belongs to the pinch-bounce finding. Dropping viscosity or maxBounds would bring back the parchment void.

RISKS: no UG3 pins are touched (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask are untouched; the wheel IIFE is not pinned) and there is no determinism impact. Any change to the wheel handler or the L.map options changes desktop feel (desktop identity), and those options sit in the mid-flight Mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9), so leave this alone or route it through that lane. The fix does nothing for the owner's misalignment complaint.
votes.reason:
The mechanism, the anchor and vector_independent are confirmed in the maps-site/index.html wheel handler (setZoomAround with options.zoomSnap set to 0 temporarily, maxBoundsViscosity:1.0, setMaxBounds(contentBounds)). The claim fails on three points.

1. The magnitude formula W/2*(1-2^-dz) holds only with the cursor at the screen centre. The real slide is d*(1-2^-dz), where d is the cursor's distance from the pinned edge, so it reaches the full view extent and is zero on the pinned edge. That also makes the suggested probe (cursor at the top edge) a zero-slide case whenever the top edge is the one touching.
2. The direction is toward the pinned edge, not the screen centre, and nothing slides "at min zoom" because the handler returns early there.
3. The cheap fix is muddled. Zooming around a pre-clamped point still slides, and bounceAtZoomLimits:false does not touch bounds clamping. The correct call is to accept it. It is a viewport slide, not registration, so it is irrelevant to the owner's misalignment.

items.summary: REGISTRATION (sub-pixel data): census ring markers sit 1.0 atlas px left of their printed ring centres, double-ring markers 2 px low (Hordon about 2 px, not 5), and ring-sitting anchors about (+1,+1), while Epēshu's anchor is already on its ring, so the point convention must be ruled before any snap (anchors only where a clean ring fit exists) or cityCanvasSha re-cut.

prior_record.title: Traced marker and anchor data sit ~1 atlas px off the printed ring-dot centres (tracer pixel-convention bias)
prior_record.subsystem: marks / data pixel convention (maps_markers.json, city-anchors.json, px())
prior_record.anchor: maps-site/data/maps_markers.json (Settlements, minor/lesser x,y), city-anchors.json; px(x,y)=map.unproject([x,y],NZ) (integer = pixel edge) and buildMarkers L.marker(px(c.x,c.y))
prior_record.mechanism: REGISTRATION. px() treats atlas coordinates as continuous with pixel edges at integers (matches the tile pyramid, no y-flip, measured). A ring-centroid/template fit on z5 tiles finds a consistent bias in the traced data: 120 census ('minor') markers sit median 1.00 atlas px LEFT of ring centre (dx +1.00, dy ~0.00; sd 0.05/0.04; p90 1.97; 16 of 120 >=1.5 px); the 7 wiki markers sit median 2.0 px off, mostly too LOW (Epeshu 0.0,-2.0; Summarch 0.0,-1.8; Hordon 4.8,-1.3; Ion Ephel 1.0,2.2); anchors that do sit on a ring are median 1.41 px up-left (dx +0.99, dy +1.00, 95-104 anchors; census marker y = anchor y + 1 for ~80 cities, a convention-free fact). The pattern points to the tracer's own convention (index or bbox off-by-one), not random error; the detector convention itself adds +/-0.25-0.5 px of absolute bias. Everything centred on these points inherits it: pins, overlay box, wash, mask patch, descend target, world POIs.
prior_record.fires_when: Always; legible from z~5.1-5.4 when the printed ring outgrows the 16-24 px glyph, and from ~z7 where 1 atlas px exceeds 8 screen px; grows until tier-d hides marks at 7.5.
prior_record.visible_effect: The glyph covers the printed dot at fit zoom but the printed ring peeks out on one side as you zoom, so it looks like sliding off its town (census pins drift left, Epeshu/Summarch down); pins and plans sit just up-left of the printed dot at street zoom.
prior_record.magnitude: Census 1.0 atlas px: 1.1-1.8 screen px at tier-C start (z4.13-4.87), 4 px at z6, 11.2 px at z7.49; wiki 2.0 px: 2.3-3.7 px at tier C, 8 px at z6, 22 px at z7.49 (Hordon 5.0 px: 56 px); anchors 1.0-1.4 px: 10-14 screen px at z7.3, 59-90 px at Epēshu's 9.885-z10.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Correct at the source: a one-off tool (pattern of tools/build-gazetteer.js) snapping every Settlements marker/anchor to its fitted ring centroid (or +1 on census x and hand-correct the 7 wiki markers), rewrite maps_markers.json/city-anchors.json, then regenerate gazetteer.json. Do not add a runtime +1 in px() (realms, ways and wiki markers come from other pipelines). Root-cause probe: phase-correlate a tiles/4 mosaic against PatrinorModern.png (iCloud, not in repo).
prior_record.fix_risks: Marker-only data change has no pinned source and no cityCanvasSha effect (markers do not feed the generator), but moving anchors by ~1 px changes sampleCityMask's patch origin (Math.round) and therefore every generated cityCanvasSha, needing a deliberate UG3 rebaseline. Gazetteer must be regenerated. Desktop identity at fit zoom (~2.6) is sub-pixel, though mobile-capture pixel baselines may flag it. Determinism holds.

votes.corrected:
REGISTRATION, and the data bias is real. px(x,y)=map.unproject([x,y],NZ) treats integer atlas coordinates as pixel edges. That matches the z5 pyramid: L.tileLayer has no tms or zoomOffset, and the tiles are a 2x LANCZOS upscale, so atlas continuous x maps to z5 continuous 2x. buildMarkers puts L.marker(px(c.x,c.y)) under a divIcon with iconAnchor [gc,gc]. The glyph centre is exact (16/20/22 px border-box, so gc is 8/10/11, and the tier-C scale is centre-origin), so the whole offset comes from the data.

I measured enclosed-component centroids on a z5 mosaic. The light hole for ○ and the dark core plus light gap for ◉ agree within 0.1 px. The printed rings centre on integer atlas coordinates. The offset depends on the glyph type, not on the data source:
(a) ○ rings: every census ○ marker, plus the wiki ○ markers Lepon, Clickerhall and Ion Ephel, sits exactly (-1,0), so the ring centre is marker + (1.00, 0.00). Median +1.00/0.00, p5-p95 dx 0.97-1.06.
(b) ◉ Māgosh-class rings: all 4 wiki ◉ markers (Summarch, Penthelon, Epēshu, Hordon) and all ~11 census ◉ markers (Cyrikon, Alensis City, Sepos, Tamaron, ...) sit exactly 2.0 atlas px too LOW, so the ring centre is marker + (0.00, -2.00).

Corrections to the claim: Hordon is (0,-2.0), not (4.8,-1.3). Ion Ephel is (+1,0), not (1.0,2.2). Summarch is (0,-2.0). The census set is a mixture, so the sd is not 0.05/0.04. The ">=1.5 px" outliers number about 10 and are the census ◉ markers, not tracer noise. Drāmūz, Sjefenhold and Kolens have no ring nearby.

city-anchors.json: 104 of 136 anchors sit on a ring, median (+1.00,+1.00) from it, i.e. 1.41 px up-left. The census marker y equals anchor y+1 for about 69 cities, not about 80. Epēshu's own anchor (1236.1,1415) is on its ring centre, within -0.1 px. So the "59-90 px at Epēshu's z9.885-10" figure does not apply to Epēshu. It applies to other cities near their cityMaxZ, and there the cityBox footprint error dwarfs it anyway.

The offset is a constant atlas-space offset, so its screen size grows as 2^(z-4). ○ pins: 4 px at z6, 11 px at z7.49. ◉ pins (the major cities, Epēshu included): 8 px at z6, 22 px at z7.49. Tier-d hides the marks at z7.5.

Fix: re-snap the data to the fitted ring centres: ○ +1 on x, ◉ -2 on y, anchors (+1,+1). Then regenerate gazetteer.json. Do not add a runtime px() shift. Moving anchors shifts the sampleCityMask patch origin and therefore changes cityCanvasSha, which needs a UG3 rebaseline.
votes.reason:
I traced px() in maps-site/index.html (function px, makeBase/L.tileLayer, buildMarkers with divIcon iconAnchor [gc,gc], the .mk.t-lesser CSS) and confirmed integer = pixel edge with no y-flip against the 2x LANCZOS z5 pyramid. Then I fitted ring centres on a z5 mosaic using enclosed hole and core centroids, robust to within 0.1 px.

The census ○ result (+1.00, 0.00, all 121) and the anchor result (median +1.00,+1.00 = 1.41 px, 104/136) reproduce exactly. The claim misstates the second bias. It belongs to the ◉ glyph type, not to the wiki source: every ◉ marker, wiki or census, is exactly 2 px low, and the wiki ○ markers share the census (-1,0). Its Hordon and Ion Ephel values are wrong, and so is its Epēshu anchor-magnitude example (that anchor sits on its ring).

The mechanism still exists and fires at every zoom. Rated major because the ◉ pins on the cities the table watches most (Epēshu, Summarch) sit 8 px off-centre at z6 and 22 px at z7.49, inside their printed rings. ○ pins are subtler: 4 to 11 px.

votes.corrected:
MECHANISM: confirmed. This is REGISTRATION (data), so it is vector-independent. A vector city placed at these anchors would inherit the same offset. I re-fit ring centroids on the z5 tiles with an iterated dark-ink centroid in pixel-centre convention (fit is ring centre minus point, in atlas px):
- 121 census (minor) markers: median (+0.998, -0.002), p90 |d| = 1.04. So census pins sit about 1 atlas px LEFT of the printed ring, as claimed.
- 134 anchors: median (+0.97, +0.99), median |d| = 1.41, as claimed. Cross-check: census marker y = anchor y + 1 for 71 cities (not about 80), and x is equal for 77.

WIKI / MAJOR MARKERS (corrected):
- About 2 px too LOW: Epēshu (0.0, -2.0), Summarch (0.0, -1.8), Penthelon (0.0, -2.0).
- Hordon is about (+0.4 to +0.5, -1.9 to -2.1), so |d| is about 2.0, NOT 5.0. The 4.8 px dx came from the fit locking onto the neighbouring glyph to the NE.
- Ion Ephel is about (+2.0, +1.3), |d| about 2.4.
- Lepon and Clickerhall are about +1.0 in x.
- Drāmūz, Sjefenhold and Kolens: no fit.

ANCHOR EXCEPTION: Epēshu's anchor (1236.1, 1415) sits exactly on its ring (|d| < 0.1). Its 2 px error lives only in its marker (1236, 1417). So the claimed "59-90 px at Epēshu's 9.885-z10" is wrong. The Epēshu overlay, wash and descend target are not biased by this. Use a generic town instead: an anchor at 1.0-1.4 px reaches 32-45 screen px at z9 and 59-90 at z10.

MAGNITUDE: screen px = atlas px × 2^(z-4). Unchanged and correct:
- Census 1.0 px: 1.1-1.8 at tier-C start (z4.13-4.87), 4 at z6, 11.2 at z7.49.
- Wiki 2.0 px: 2.2-3.7, 8, 22.5.
- Anchors at z7.3: 9.8-13.8.
Corrected: Hordon about 2.0 px gives about 22-24 screen px at z7.49 (not 56). Tier-D hide at Z_TIER_D = 7.5 is confirmed.

CHEAP FIX:
- Correct the data at source with a one-off tool modelled on tools/build-gazetteer.js, then regenerate gazetteer.json, which reads both files. No runtime +1 in px(), as claimed.
- Census markers: a blanket x += 1 is safe (sd about 0.05).
- Wiki/major markers: hand-correct them, or snap them to the fitted centroid.
- Anchors: snap ONLY those within about 1.6 px of a fitted ring. Do NOT apply a blanket (+1, +1) or "snap every anchor". Some anchors are off-ring by design or have no clean ring: Tamaron (+0.6 to 1.1, +3.4), Kanae (+1.4 to 3.2, +7.4), Sokundo (unstable). Moving them would shift plans away from where they were placed.

RISKS:
- cityCanvasSha hashes only Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae (mobile-capture.js), not every city.
- A 1 atlas px anchor move shifts sampleCityMask's ox/oy by 2 z5 px. That always changes the mask, so it changes the hash if any of those three moves.
- With the on-ring-only rule, those three likely do not move. Check this before claiming no UG3 effect. If any does move, a deliberate B0 rebaseline is needed.
- atlas_fn_sha is untouched, since only JSON changes.
- Land it in a gap in the mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9), not mid-lane, because UG3 compares each unit to B0 and the pixel baselines may flag pin shifts.
- Desktop at fit zoom (about 2.6) moves by less than 1 px.
- Determinism holds.
votes.reason: Mechanism, census and anchor statistics, and the 2^(z-4) magnitude arithmetic all check out against an independent ring fit on the z5 tiles. Two magnitude items are wrong. Hordon's offset is about 2 px, not 5.0 (the fit snagged on an adjacent glyph), so it is about 22-24 screen px, not 56. Epēshu's anchor sits on its ring, so the "59-90 px at Epēshu street zoom" example is false: Epēshu's error is in its marker only. The fix as worded ("snap every Settlements marker/anchor") is unsafe for anchors with no clean ring nearby (Tamaron about 3.5 px, Kanae about 7 px off). Those include the cityCanvasSha-pinned trio, so snapping must be restricted to on-ring anchors. Also, cityCanvasSha covers only Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae, not every city.

items.summary: Presentation: shared-seat faction badges are spread by 14 atlas px through px(), so the spread grows on screen (39.6 px at z5.5, 138-157 px at z7.3-7.49).

prior_record.title: Shared-seat faction badges are spread by 14 ATLAS px, so the spread grows with zoom
prior_record.anchor: buildFactionBadges: `ox=Math.cos(ang)*14;oy=Math.sin(ang)*14 ... L.marker(px(c.x+ox,c.y+oy)`
prior_record.mechanism: Presentation offset expressed in map px, not icon px: badges sharing a seat are offset by 14 world units through px(), so their screen length scales with 2^(z-4). Two shared seats: (1222,1404) x3 and (1146,1415) x2; offsets n=1 (+12.3,+6.7) and n=2 (-13.5,+3.4) atlas px.
prior_record.fires_when: pFaction pane visible at tier C (z>=~4.13-4.87) up to tier-d (7.5); every zoom change.
prior_record.visible_effect: At tier-C entry the 22-px shields still overlap; zooming in they fly apart and land on unrelated ground (the Senate shield near the Epeshu ring, others in open country), reading as shields that wander with zoom.
prior_record.magnitude: 14 atlas px = 5 px at z2.55, 16 px at z4.2 (less than the 22-px badge), 38 px at z5.5, 56 px at z6, 138-157 px at z7.3-7.49.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Keep the latlng at the seat and put the spread in the divIcon: iconAnchor [11-ox,11-oy] with ox,oy in screen px (~16 px radius); chevron/tooltip offsets unchanged.
prior_record.fix_risks: No UG3 pin (buildFactionBadges unpinned). Desktop identity changes only at tier C and above, so tier-C captures need rebaselining; Mobile lane touch targets of overlapping badges.

votes.corrected: The mechanism is real, but some details in the claim are wrong. In maps-site/index.html, buildFactionBadges keys badges by their clamped seat coordinates. Every badge after the first at the same key gets an offset, ang=(n-1)*2.3999+0.5, ox=cos*14, oy=sin*14. That offset goes into the marker LatLng through px(c.x+ox,c.y+oy), which is map.unproject([x,y],NZ=4). It is never put into the divIcon, whose iconAnchor stays fixed at [11,11]. So each badge is pinned to a fixed atlas point 14 world px from its seat. It does not move relative to the terrain. What changes with zoom is the screen distance between the badge and its seat, and between sibling badges: 14*2^(z-4) px. That is 5 px at z2.55, 16 px at z4.2, 40 px at z5.5 (not 38), 56 px at z6 and 138-157 px at z7.3-7.49. pFaction is opacity 0 at tiers a and b, and at map-tier-d (z>=Z_TIER_D 7.5) and in chart-mode. It is visible from tierZoom('c') = fitZoom+2/3*(TIER_CEIL-fitZoom) up to 7.5. With an 800-px-tall viewport that is about z4.87 (TIER_CEIL 6) or about z4.18 on retina (TIER_CEIL 5). The layout is static geometry: nothing recomputes it on zoom. "Overlap at tier-C entry" holds only near the retina threshold: at z4.87 the spread is 25.6 px, more than the 22-px badge. Data from factions.json: at seat (1222,1404) the badges are Eshbrīn (no offset), the Lektān Priesthood (+12.3,+6.7) and the Senate (-13.6,+3.4). At (1146,1415) they are the Orondēs (no offset) and Pebros's Army (+12.3,+6.7). The claim has the badges mixed up. The seat itself is about 18-19 px from the Epēshu anchor (city-anchors 1236.1,1415; marker 1236,1417). So the Lektān badge (1234.3,1410.7) is the one that lands about 4 px from the Epēshu ring. The Senate badge (1208.4,1407.4) lands about 28 px west of the anchor, outside the capital FOOT_R of 26. Pebros's Army (1158.3,1421.7) lands about 12 px from the Lepon anchor, outside the ruin FOOT_R of 8. A larger, separate offset also scales the same way: the faction seat coordinates in factions.json do not match the Epēshu anchor or marker coordinates. Each badge, including the first, is therefore registered about 18 px off the city dot, roughly 135 px off at z7. This is a registration issue in the data, and moving the spread into the icon does not fix it. The cheap fix stands: put the spread in iconAnchor (screen px), keep the LatLng at the seat, and also snap seats that name a city onto that city's anchor.
votes.reason: Confirmed in buildFactionBadges, in px() (map.unproject at NZ=4), in tierZoom and tierFor, and in the CSS pane rules for map-tier-a/b/d and chart-mode on the pFaction pane. The spread is a world-unit offset in the LatLng, not an icon-pixel offset. No zoom handler repositions the badges. The two shared seats match factions.json. Corrections: the badges do not move relative to the atlas, so this does not cause features to shift against each other. Only the badge-to-seat and badge-to-badge screen distances grow, and this is a property of the badge layout, not of the raster or vector medium. Overlap at tier-C entry happens only near the retina threshold. The 38 px figure should be 40 px. The badge that ends up near the Epēshu ring is the Lektān one, not the Senate's. The faction seat coordinates are themselves about 18 px off the Epēshu anchor, an independent registration error in the data that scales the same way. Rated minor: at z6-7.49 the shields sit visibly off their seats, over the fading-in city overlay, but they stay fixed to the ground and are hidden from 7.5 upward.

At phone tier-C zooms (~3.5) a fixed 16 px spread is larger than today's ~10 px, so those tap outcomes shift and need a central rebaseline. Schedule it outside the mid-flight Mobile 5-9 atlas lane or as one of its units, since that lane is editing maps-site/index.html.

items.summary: Presentation: POI divIcons use a 22-px box with an 11-px anchor while .poi-mk is a 26-px border-box, so every POI halo sits (+2,+2) CSS px off its point at every zoom (the claimed tooltip overlap does not occur).

prior_record.title: POI halo is 26 px but its icon box and anchor assume 22 px, so every POI ring sits (+2,+2) px off its point
prior_record.subsystem: marks / world POIs + chart POIs (icon geometry)
prior_record.anchor: buildWorldPOIs and buildPOILayer: L.divIcon({iconSize:[22,22],iconAnchor:[11,11],html:'<div class="poi-mk">'...}) vs CSS `.poi-mk{...width:26px;height:26px`; tooltip offset [0,-11]
prior_record.mechanism: Presentation error. Leaflet sizes the icon box 22x22 anchored at (11,11); the 26x26 border-box .poi-mk child is anchored at the box's top-left, so its centre is at (13,13), 2 px right and 2 px down of the latlng. The comment claims coords sit exactly on the printed badges.
prior_record.fires_when: World POIs at z>=8 near an active city and chart-mode POIs at every chart zoom; visible on hover/focus (border alpha 0 at rest, scale 1.15 about the offset centre).
prior_record.visible_effect: The hover ring is eccentric to the printed numbered badge (canon charts) or the POI point (generated plans); the badge scales with the art while the ring stays 26 px, so the mismatch reads differently at each zoom.
prior_record.magnitude: Constant (2,2) = 2.8 screen px diagonal at every zoom and DPR; POI tooltip overlaps the halo by 2 px. Badge-to-ring ratio varies as 2^(z-cityMaxZ) (Epeshu art at z8 is 0.27 of native).
prior_record.cheap_fix: In both builders use iconSize [26,26], iconAnchor [13,13] and tooltip offset [0,-13] (or set .poi-mk to 22 px).
prior_record.fix_risks: No UG3 pin. At-rest captures are pixel-identical (halo invisible); chart-mode hover captures change slightly; tap target changes slightly (Mobile lane audits target size).

votes.corrected:
The mechanism holds, but one detail about the tooltip is wrong. In maps-site/index.html, both buildPOILayer (chart mode) and buildWorldPOIs (world POIs, pane pCityPOI) call L.divIcon({className:'',iconSize:[22,22],iconAnchor:[11,11],html:'
'+p.n+'
'}). In the vendored Leaflet 1.9.4, _setIconStyles sets the outer .leaflet-marker-icon to width/height 22px with margin-left/top -11px, so that box is centred on the latlng. The child .poi-mk is width:26px;height:26px under the global `*{box-sizing:border-box}`, so it is 26 px across including its 2 px border. It is a block child with no centring, so it starts at the box's top-left and overflows right and down. Its centre is therefore (+2,+2) layer px from the point, about 2.8 px diagonal. That offset is the same at every zoom and in both modes. `.poi-mk:hover{transform:scale(1.15)}` scales about the child's own centre, which is the offset one. The ring has border alpha 0 at rest, so the error only shows on hover. The focus-visible outline (`.leaflet-marker-icon:focus-visible`) is drawn on the 22 px box, which is centred, so a keyboard-focused POI shows the outline and the ring 2 px apart. The CSS comment above .poi-mk says coords "sit exactly on" the printed badges, and this offset contradicts that. When it fires: world POIs are added only when z>=8 for the active city (the `map.getZoom()>=8` check after buildWorldPOIs, and setCityPOIVisible). Chart-mode POIs show at every chart zoom. Correction to the tooltip claim: the tooltip does NOT currently overlap the halo. With direction 'top', DivIcon tooltipAnchor [0,0], offset [0,-11] and the leaflet-tooltip-top margin-top -6px, the tooltip ends above y=-11. That is exactly where the offset ring's top edge sits (2-13 = -11). The tooltip would sit 2 px into a correctly centred ring, so the fix changes the offset to -13 along with the anchor. Fix: use iconSize [26,26], iconAnchor [13,13] and tooltip offset [0,-13] in both builders, or make .poi-mk 22 px. This is a registration bug in the icon geometry, not in the city art. It is independent of the rendering medium and does not cause any shift while zooming.
votes.reason: I checked this in the HEAD export. Both builders use iconSize [22,22] and iconAnchor [11,11] with an un-centred 26 px child, under the global border-box rule (`*{box-sizing:border-box}`). The vendored Leaflet's _setIconStyles only sizes the outer box and gives it negative margins, so the halo is off by a constant (+2,+2) px, and the hover scale happens about that offset centre. It shows only on hover or focus, and only by about 2.8 px on a 26 px ring, so it is subtle and does not shift with zoom. The tooltip-overlap part of the claim is wrong. With offset -11 plus Leaflet's -6 px margin, the tooltip now ends at the ring's top edge, -11 px (centre +2, radius 13). It would only overlap a correctly centred ring.

votes.corrected:
The mechanism and the main magnitude are right. In maps-site/index.html, buildPOILayer and buildWorldPOIs both use L.divIcon({className:'',iconSize:[22,22],iconAnchor:[11,11],html:'
'+p.n+'
'}). The CSS gives `.poi-mk{...width:26px;height:26px;...border:2px solid rgba(239,230,207,.0)}`, and the global `*{box-sizing:border-box}` makes it 26 px including the border. The child overflows the 22 px box down and to the right, so its centre sits at (+2,+2) CSS px from the latlng (about 2.83 CSS px on the diagonal). The hover scale(1.15) turns about the child's own centre, so the offset holds when hovered. That offset is 2 CSS px at every zoom. In device pixels it is 2*DPR, so it is not constant across DPR. For the badge-scale aside: the capital box is 52 world px wide over the 3072 px Epēshu art, so at z8 the art shows at 52*16/3072 = 0.27 of native, as claimed. Three corrections: (1) Tooltip. The current offset [0,-11] puts the tooltip anchor exactly at the halo's top edge. The halo spans y from -11 to +15, so the shift only pushes the bottom and right edges out. Leaflet's .leaflet-tooltip-top also adds a -6 px margin plus an arrow. So there is no "2 px overlap" caused by this bug. The fix keeps the same relationship as today: top edge -13, offset -13. (2) Focus. Keyboard focus never shows the halo, because only :hover sets the border. Focus shows the `.leaflet-marker-icon:focus-visible` outline on the 22 px outer box, and that box is centred on the point. So the only visible symptom today is the eccentric hover ring, plus a hit area that is the union of the centred 22 px box and the shifted 26 px child. After the fix the focus outline grows from 22 to 26 px. (3) Cause. This is a presentation (CSS/icon-geometry) error, not a registration error. It is fully vector-independent: a vector city would place the same divIcon the same way. The fix is correct: iconSize [26,26], iconAnchor [13,13] and tooltip offset [0,-13] in both builders. Shrinking .poi-mk to 22 px also works but changes the halo and tap size. Risks: it touches no UG3-pinned function (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask), so cityCanvasSha is unchanged. It is not generation code, so determinism is unaffected. At-rest desktop pixels are identical: transparent border, background and text. Hover, focus-outline and tap geometry change slightly. buildFactionBadges uses the same 22 px divIcon pattern and is a separate case, so leave it alone. Because the Mobile atlas lane (5-9) is mid-flight in maps-site/index.html and audits target size, sequence the edit after that lane or hand it to the lane rather than editing in parallel.

items.summary: Presentation timing: updTier runs on zoomend only while tier-d is live, so on pinch, flyTo and animated zooms the labels, lesser pins, shields and tier-C glyph scale pop in at the end (wheel zoom is effectively live).

prior_record.title: Tier A/B/C classes, atlas-labels, the tier-C glyph scale and way labels flip only on zoomend, while tier-d flips live
prior_record.anchor: map.on('zoomend',updTier) vs worldOpacityUpdate's mc.classList.toggle('map-tier-d',z>=Z_TIER_D) on 'zoom zoomend moveend'; CSS .map-tier-c .mk .glyph{transform:scale(1.14)}, .map-tier-c .way-label{display:inline-block}
prior_record.mechanism: Presentation timing. updTier runs on zoomend only. Wheel/trackpad (setZoomAround animate:false -> _resetView) fire zoomend per tick and so are effectively live; touch pinch (only 'zoom'), flyTo (one zoomend at the end) and animated button/keyboard/double-tap zooms change tier only at the end.
prior_record.fires_when: Any pinch, flyTo (search, card, #place=, waypoint, flyIntoCity) or animated zoom crossing tierZoom('b') or ('c').
prior_record.visible_effect: During the gesture or fly, settlements, lesser pins, labels, faction shields, way-label chips and the 14% glyph enlargement do not appear; they pop in (0.2 s pane fade, labels instantly) after it ends, while tier-d fades mid-gesture. Pinching out keeps labels until release.
prior_record.magnitude: Lag = gesture/fly duration (flyToMarker 0.9 s, flyIntoCity 1.4 s, button 0.25 s, pinch as long as held); pop covers glyph 22 to 25.1 px plus all labels at once.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Bind updTier to 'zoom' as well (map.on('zoom zoomend',updTier)); three classList toggles like tier-d.
prior_record.fix_risks: No UG3 pin. End state at rest unchanged. Mobile Mobile 5-9 lane and filigree R7 own label behaviour; per-frame toggles retrigger 0.2 s pane transitions mid-fly (intended).

votes.corrected:
The core claim holds; two details need correcting. In maps-site/index.html, updTier() toggles map-tier-a/b/c and atlas-labels and is bound only through map.on('zoomend',updTier). It is also called from refit(), the chart-exit restore and init. worldOpacityUpdate() toggles map-tier-d and is bound to 'zoom zoomend moveend'. Vendored Leaflet 1.9.4 timing, checked against the minified source:
(1) Wheel and trackpad-pinch. The custom wheel listener calls setZoomAround(ll,target,{animate:false}). That goes setView, then _tryAnimatedZoom returns false, then _resetView, which fires zoomstart/zoom/zoomend on every tick, so tiers update effectively live.
(2) Touch pinch. TouchZoom._onTouchMove calls map._move(...,{pinch:true}), which fires only 'zoom'. zoomend fires after release, at the end of the 250 ms snap. So tier-d follows the fingers, while the A/B/C classes and atlas-labels flip only on release. Pinching out from tier C keeps the labels until release.
(3) flyTo (flyToMarker 0.9 s, gazetteer/search revealZoom flies, flyTo(x,y,t) 1.2 s, flyIntoCity 1.4 s). Each frame calls _move(...,{flyTo:true}), which fires 'zoom', and there is a single zoomend at the end. So tier-d updates live and A/B/C/labels pop when the fly ends.
CORRECTION A: animated button, keyboard and double-click zooms (zoomDelta .25) go through _animateZoom. It calls _move(...,suppress=true), so no 'zoom' fires until _onZoomTransitionEnd, which fires 'zoom' and then 'zoomend' back to back after 250 ms. So tier-d is NOT live for these either. Both flip together at the end, and these paths have no asymmetry and no extra lag beyond tier-d's.
CORRECTION B: flyIntoCity's target is max(z, cityMaxZ-0.5), which lands at or above Z_TIER_D 7.5. At the end, the .map-tier-d rule (opacity:0!important) hides every pane the late tier-C flip would reveal. So that fly has no visible pop at the end. Its only effect is that tier-C content never appears while the fly passes from tierZoom('c') (about 4.25 to 4.9) up to 7.5.
The pop covers the 0.2 s pane fades (pSettle/pMtn/pRealm/pMinor/pLesser/pRouteLine/pRouteWp/pLane/pWay/pDistrict/pTrail/pFaction), the instant label display, the way-label chips and the glyph scale from 22 to 25.1 px. The scale is a centred transform, so nothing moves off its anchor.
This is reveal timing, not registration; vector_independent is true. Cheap fix: map.on('zoom zoomend',updTier) makes pinch and flyTo live. It does nothing for animated button zooms, which have no mid-transition 'zoom'. The van Wijk zoom-out-then-in of flyTo can make tiers flicker mid-fly. Nothing is pinned by UG3.
votes.reason: The mechanism exists as described: updTier is on zoomend only, tier-d is on the live 'zoom', the CSS selectors match, and wheel goes through _resetView with a zoomend per tick. The real live/late split shows only on touch pinch and on flyTo (flyToMarker, search and gazetteer, deep links, waypoints). Leaflet's _animateZoom fires no 'zoom' until transition end, so button, keyboard and double-click zooms flip tier-d and tiers A/B/C together after 250 ms. flyIntoCity ends at or above Z_TIER_D, which hides the late-revealed panes, so it has no end pop. Labels and pins arriving after a gesture or fly is noticeable but conventional. It is a timing pop of reveal classes with centred glyph scaling, not a positional shift or misalignment, so I rate it minor rather than major.

votes.corrected:
The mechanism holds, with corrections. In maps-site/index.html, updTier is bound by map.on('zoomend',updTier). It toggles map-tier-a/b/c and atlas-labels. worldOpacityUpdate is bound to 'zoom zoomend moveend' and toggles map-tier-d at Z_TIER_D=7.5.

Live versus end-only, per input path:
- Wheel and Mac trackpad pinch: map.scrollWheelZoom is disabled. A custom wheel handler calls setZoomAround(...,{animate:false}), which goes through _resetView and fires zoomend on every tick. Tiers are effectively live here.
- Touch pinch: Leaflet TouchZoom calls _move and fires only 'zoom' during the gesture. Tiers A/B/C wait until release; tier-d is live.
- flyTo: fires 'zoom' every frame and zoomend once at the end. Durations are flyToMarker 0.9 s, the cluster/search flyTo calls 1.2 s and 0.9 s, and flyIntoCity 1.4 s. Tiers A/B/C lag for the whole fly; tier-d is live.
- Animated button, keyboard and double-click zooms (zoomDelta .25, about 0.25 s CSS animation): _animateZoom fires no 'zoom' mid-animation. _onZoomTransitionEnd fires 'zoom' and then 'zoomend' together, and getZoom() returns the old zoom until then. Here tier-d also flips only at the end, so the claim's contrast ("tier-d flips live") is wrong for these cases. Binding to 'zoom' would change nothing for them; only a 'zoomanim' handler that reads e.zoom would.

Magnitude:
- The lag equals the gesture or fly duration, as claimed.
- The glyph change is 22 to 25.08 px (scale 1.14). Lesser glyphs go 16 to 18.2 px and mag glyphs 20 to 22.8 px. The glyph change is a 0.15 s transform transition, not an instant pop.

items.summary: Lifecycle: the async ensureCityGen callback runs worldCityUpdate with the mid-fly centre, so while z<=6.5 (about the first 0.6 s of a fly) ensureCityOverlay(null) drops the eager plan, which pops back at landing; unmeasured.

prior_record.title: The async mask callback runs worldCityUpdate mid-flyIntoCity: it can remove the eager plan or cancel the fly
prior_record.anchor: ensureCityGen callback `if(!CHART.on)worldCityUpdate();` together with flyIntoCity `ensureCityOverlay(key); // eager` and Leaflet setView -> this._stop()

Callbacks for canon cities also call worldCityUpdate.
prior_record.fires_when: flyIntoCity or #chart=City on a cold tile cache (first visit, deep link) when the mask lands before the fly ends.
prior_record.visible_effect: The art that should fade in during the descent disappears partway and pops in at landing, or the fly stops, zooms out to 8 and then jumps straight to the city at 1.7 s.
prior_record.magnitude: Unmeasured. Probe (browser): cold cache, from fit view ATLAS.descend('Sokundo'), per rAF log map.getZoom(), map.getMaxZoom(), count of '.leaflet-pCity-pane img'; repeat with tiles cached.

prior_record.fix_risks: Edits ensureCityGen/flyIntoCity only; no UG3-pinned source touched. Living-chart H2z owns fly choreography, so coordinate. Desktop identity at rest unchanged.

The mechanism is real, but the claim describes when it fires wrongly and overstates the fly-cancel branch. This is a lifecycle bug, not a registration bug, and it is the same for raster and vector cities.

Code path (maps-site/index.html):
1. flyIntoCity calls ensureCityGen(key) first, which starts the sampleCityMask z5 tile requests.
2. It then calls ensureCityGenNow(key), a synchronous 2048-square genCityCanvas plus toDataURL.
3. It then calls ensureCityOverlay(key) ("eager") and starts map.flyTo(dest, cz-0.5, {duration:1.4}) one requestAnimationFrame later.
4. When the tiles load, the ensureCityGen callback runs. For invented cities it first re-gens and hot-swaps through registerCityOverlay; canon Epēshu/Summarch skip that step. Either way it then runs `if(!CHART.on)worldCityUpdate();` using the mid-fly getZoom()/getCenter(). In Leaflet 1.9.4, flyTo's _move keeps _zoom and _lastCenter live, so these values are the mid-fly view.
5. This bypasses the author's own rule in the comment above `map.on('zoomend moveend',worldCityUpdate)`: "setMaxZoom only on zoomend+moveend (never mid-fly)".

Correction 1: the removal trigger is the zoom gate, not the 3r test. worldCityUpdate ends with `ensureCityOverlay((reg&&z>6.5)?near.name:null)`. Any callback at z<=6.5 removes the eager overlay, wash, stubs and POIs, even when the centre is already within 3r and reg exists.
- Simulated fit view to Sokundo (Leaflet's van Wijk path at 1280x800 and 390x844): the centre enters 3r at about 0.25 s, but z stays at or below 6.5 until about 0.6 s. So the vulnerable window runs from the flyIntoCity call to about 0.6 s into the 1.4 s fly.
- In the first ~0.25 s, near is null, so setMaxZoom(Z_OPEN_MAX=8) also runs. That is harmless because 1.9.4 flyTo does not apply _limitZoom to its target.

Correction 2: the callback can land before the fly starts. The tile requests are already in flight during the synchronous ensureCityGenNow work, and the fly starts one rAF later, so the callback can run at z = fitZoom. The outcome is the same removal.

Correction 3: it does not need a cold cache. Image onload is always async, so this fires on the first descend into any city whose MASKQ[key] has not been applied, warm HTTP cache included. Only a city already sampled (visited or prewarmed) is immune, because ensureCityGen returns early.

Visible effect: from about z6.8 to landing, the base fades to 0.12 with no city art, no wash and no stubs. Because CITYVIEW.name is null, show-uncharted turns on (grain plus "✶ uncharted at this scale"). The landing moveend then runs worldCityUpdate, and the overlay pops in at opacity 1. A reader at the table would see this.

Correction 4: the fly-cancel branch (setMaxZoom -> setZoom -> setView -> _stop cancels _flyToFrame) exists in the code, but it needs mid-fly z > allowed.
- It cannot fire from the fit view: z only passes 8 once the centre is within about 0.2 px of the target, so near is the target and allowed is its own cz.
- A brute-force run over anchor pairs shows it is reachable only on city-to-city descends between close neighbours, in a window of about 50-100 ms. Examples: centre between anchors at z just over 8 (Kanae->Rhup, Rēketis->Pharzeban), or passing a neighbour with a shallower cz or no reg (Hordon on the way to Maeges).
- When it does fire, maxZoom is still 8 at 1.7 s, so ensureArrival's first setView(dest,target) is clamped to z8 by _limitZoom. The landing moveend raises maxZoom, and the tries+1 retry reaches the target at about 3.4 s, not 1.7 s.
- The more common city-to-city artefact is different: a callback at z>6.5 while near is still the origin swaps the eager destination art back to the origin's overlay until landing.

Cheap fix: set a flag in flyIntoCity before the rAF and clear it on the landing moveend and in ensureArrival. While the flag is set, have the callback skip worldCityUpdate (still do washRefresh and the hot-swap). Do not use map._flyToFrame as the guard: it is never cleared after a fly finishes, so it is not a usable "pending" test.

Caveat: the timings come from simulation, not a browser probe. Real arrival depends on tile latency plus the cost of the synchronous melded gen inside the callback.

From Leaflet 1.9.4:
- flyTo's _move updates _zoom and _lastCenter on every frame.
- flyTo does not apply _limitZoom to its target.
- setMaxZoom calls setZoom when getZoom() > max; setZoom calls setView, which calls _stop() and cancels _flyToFrame.
- setView clamps through _limitZoom.

I ran a Python copy of Leaflet's flyTo maths. It shows the overlay removal reliably happens on a first descend from the fit view, through the z>6.5 gate, regardless of cache. The fly-cancel branch cannot happen from the fit view and is narrow even city-to-city. The claim's 1.7 s hard-land is clamped to z8 and the target is reached on the ~3.4 s retry.

The headline effect (art missing during the descent, the uncharted watermark, then a pop at landing) holds and would be noticed. Under the stated rubric, the claim's wrong firing condition and its fly-cancel overreach do not flip it to false.

items.summary: Timing: worldOpacityUpdate runs before worldCityUpdate changes CITYVIEW.name and the gen callback never re-toggles, so 'show-uncharted' lags one event (indefinitely if the reader is idle), in narrower cases than claimed.

prior_record.title: The 'uncharted' watermark/grain state lags one event behind the active city
prior_record.subsystem: marks / uncharted band (handler order and async plan registration)
prior_record.anchor: map.on('zoom zoomend moveend',worldOpacityUpdate) registered before map.on('zoomend moveend',worldCityUpdate); mc.classList.toggle('show-uncharted',z>6.8&&!CITYVIEW.name); ensureCityGen callback calls only worldCityUpdate
prior_record.mechanism: State timing. On moveend/zoomend worldOpacityUpdate runs first with the OLD CITYVIEW.name, then worldCityUpdate changes it, so the class is stale until the next zoom/move event. The async ensureCityGen callback registers a plan and calls worldCityUpdate without worldOpacityUpdate, so a plan arriving after the gesture leaves 'show-uncharted' on.
prior_record.fires_when: z>6.8: a drag ending inside or outside a city's 3r; any generated city whose mask lands after the reader stops (pinch, single wheel tick, #view deep link).
prior_record.visible_effect: 'uncharted at this scale' and the parchment grain sit over a freshly drawn town, or are missing in open country, until the reader nudges the map.
prior_record.magnitude: Lags one event (indefinitely if the reader does not move); grain opacity 0.6, watermark 0.92, 0.5 s fade.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Re-toggle 'show-uncharted' (or call worldOpacityUpdate()) at the end of worldCityUpdate and in the ensureCityGen callback, or register worldCityUpdate before worldOpacityUpdate.
prior_record.fix_risks: No UG3 pin; logic only (filigree owns the uncharted look). Desktop identity unchanged at rest.

votes.corrected:
The mechanism is real but narrower than claimed. This is a state-timing bug in the 'uncharted' class, not a registration or zoom-shift problem: nothing on the map moves, and vector versus raster makes no difference.

Code (maps-site/index.html):
- `worldOpacityUpdate` is the only place the class is set: `mc.classList.toggle('show-uncharted',z>6.8&&!CITYVIEW.name)`.
- Handler order: `map.on('zoom zoomend moveend',worldOpacityUpdate)` is registered before `map.on('zoomend moveend',worldCityUpdate)`.
- Only `ensureCityOverlay` (called from `worldCityUpdate`) changes `CITYVIEW.name`.
- The `ensureCityGen` callback ends with `if(!CHART.on)worldCityUpdate()` and never re-toggles the class.

Partly wrong: for zoom gestures and setView the lag self-heals within the same gesture. Vendored Leaflet 1.9.4 `_moveEnd` fires 'zoomend' and then 'moveend' back to back. So when a city's plan is already in CITYREG (canon Epēshu or Summarch, or an earlier generated plan), the sequence is: zoomend runs `worldOpacityUpdate` with the old name, `worldCityUpdate` sets the name, and moveend's `worldOpacityUpdate` then corrects the class. There is no lag after a pinch or wheel zoom in that case.

The lag survives in two cases:

(1) Pan-only moves at z>6.8. A drag, including its inertia, keyboard panning and panTo all fire only 'moveend'. The class is computed from the CITYVIEW.name of the previous view.
- Dragging into an already-registered city's 3×footR radius (`nearestCity`) leaves 'show-uncharted' on over the drawn town.
- Dragging out leaves it off in open country, but only for 6.8<z≤8. Above Z_OPEN_MAX=8, `worldCityUpdate`'s `setMaxZoom(8)` triggers Leaflet's `setZoom`, and its zoom/zoomend/moveend events re-run `worldOpacityUpdate` and fix the class.

(2) Async plan registration for procedural cities. `sampleCityMask` always resolves on Image onload, which is always async. Before that, `worldCityUpdate` sees no registry entry and calls `ensureCityOverlay(null)`, so with z>6.8 the class is turned on. When the mask lands, the callback runs `registerCityOverlay`, then `worldCityUpdate`, then `ensureCityOverlay(key)`, which sets the name and fades the plan in. The class is never re-evaluated, so the watermark and grain stay on until the next zoom or move. This fires when the gesture's last zoomend/moveend comes before the mask, which is common when the reader lands at z>6.8 near an unvisited generated town without the idle prewarm having finished. Prewarm runs only on an event at 5.6<z≤6.5 within 6×footR. Examples: a single large pinch or wheel jump, or a #view/#place deep link via setView.

`flyIntoCity` avoids this. `ensureCityGenNow` plus the eager `ensureCityOverlay` set the name before the fly.

Effect: the corner badge '✶ uncharted at this scale' (opacity .92) and the parchment grain (opacity .6) fade in over 0.5 s on a freshly drawn town, or stay missing in open country, until the next zoom or move event. That can be indefinite if the reader stops.

Cheap fix: re-run the toggle (or `worldOpacityUpdate()`) at the end of `worldCityUpdate`. That one change covers both the drag case and the ensureCityGen callback, since the callback calls `worldCityUpdate`. Alternatively, register `worldCityUpdate` before `worldOpacityUpdate` for 'moveend', but that alone would not fix the async case. Logic only, no UG3-pinned function touched.
votes.reason:
I checked this in the maps-site/index.html source and the vendored leaflet.js; I did not run it in a browser. All three anchors exist as described.

The claim is wrong for zoom gestures on cities that are already registered. Leaflet's `_moveEnd` fires 'zoomend' and then 'moveend', so the second `worldOpacityUpdate` call sees the new CITYVIEW.name and fixes the class within the same gesture.

The lag survives in two cases:
- **Pan-only moves at z>6.8.** These fire only 'moveend'. On a drag out of a city, it only applies up to z=8: above that, `setMaxZoom(Z_OPEN_MAX=8)` forces a `setZoom`, which fires the events again.
- **Plans that load late.** Generated cities register asynchronously: the mask comes from Image onload, and the `ensureCityGen` callback calls only `worldCityUpdate`, never the class toggle.

Nothing shifts or misaligns, so it does not explain the zoom-shift complaint. Even so, a wrong '✶ uncharted at this scale' badge over a freshly drawn town is visible and can stay up indefinitely, so I rated it minor rather than none.

votes.corrected:
The mechanism is real, but its reach is narrower than the claim says. The opacities in magnitude are right: in maps-site/index.html, `.show-uncharted .uncharted-grain{opacity:.6}`, `.uncharted-mark{opacity:.92}`, and both use `transition:opacity .5s`. This is not a registration or zoom-shift problem. It is UI-state timing only, and it would happen the same way with a vector city (vector_independent=true is correct).

Which events actually show the bug:
(1) A zoom gesture that ends (wheel, pinch, flyTo) heals itself. Leaflet's _moveEnd fires 'zoomend' and then 'moveend' in the same synchronous task. On zoomend, worldOpacityUpdate sees the old CITYVIEW.name and worldCityUpdate then changes it. On moveend, worldOpacityUpdate runs again with the new name, before the browser recalculates style. So no stale frame is ever painted.
(2) A pan-only drag ends with 'moveend' only. The class stays stale until the next zoom or move. This applies when z>6.8 and the drag crosses into or out of the city's active radius (once a plan is registered, the city goes active whenever it is the nearest city and z>6.5).
(3) In the async ensureCityGen callback, sampleCityMask lands, registerCityOverlay runs, then worldCityUpdate runs. That sets CITYVIEW.name, and nothing re-toggles the class. 'uncharted at this scale' and the grain stay over the new town until the reader moves the map. setMaxZoom fires zoom events only when it has to clamp the zoom down, and a newly registered plan raises the limit, so it does not rescue this case. In practice this mostly hits a city the reader reaches by pan or zoom. flyIntoCity has already set the name early through ensureCityGenNow and ensureCityOverlay.
(4) ensureArrival's "arrived" branch calls a bare worldCityUpdate() and can leave the class stale the same way. Its hard-land branch calls setView (moveend) before worldCityUpdate, so it can too.

Corrected magnitude: no visible lag for zoom gestures. For a drag end, an async plan landing after the gesture, or an ensureArrival landing, the wrong state persists until the next zoom or move, possibly forever. When it does change, it fades over 0.5 s (grain 0.6, watermark 0.92).

Corrected fix: call worldOpacityUpdate() (or just repeat the class toggle) at the end of worldCityUpdate. Every path goes through that function, including the ensureCityGen callback and both ensureArrival branches, so the callback needs no separate edit. Do not use 'register worldCityUpdate first' alone. It fixes the drag case but not the async callback or ensureArrival.

Safety: worldOpacityUpdate is idempotent. It re-applies baseOpacity, overlayOpacity and wash opacity for the same z, and the tier-d class. It returns early when CHART.on. It touches none of the functions pinned by UG3 (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask), so it cannot change atlas_fn_sha or cityCanvasSha. It does not affect determinism. Desktop identity at rest changes only in the buggy states, which is the fix itself. The one thing to manage is the mobile atlas lane: worldCityUpdate sits in maps-site/index.html, which is mid-flight, so the change goes in as a central unit after that lane releases the file, or into the lane. The filigree track owns the look of the uncharted treatment; this changes only when the class is toggled.
votes.reason: Checked against maps-site/index.html in the HEAD export. The handlers are registered in the claimed order: map.on('zoom zoomend moveend',worldOpacityUpdate) comes before map.on('zoomend moveend',worldCityUpdate). worldOpacityUpdate toggles 'show-uncharted' using z>6.8&&!CITYVIEW.name. Only worldCityUpdate, through ensureCityOverlay, changes CITYVIEW.name. The ensureCityGen callback calls only worldCityUpdate. The claim overstates how often the bug shows: Leaflet fires zoomend and then moveend in one task, so zoom gestures correct themselves through the second worldOpacityUpdate. The cases that really go stale are a pan-only drag (moveend only), the async plan callback, and ensureArrival, which the claim missed. The alternative fix (reordering the handlers) does not cover the async or ensureArrival paths. Putting worldOpacityUpdate at the end of worldCityUpdate covers every path, touches no UG3-pinned function and keeps determinism. The claim's main fix and its magnitude figures stand, so it holds with these corrections. It is cosmetic state lag, not anchoring drift.

items.summary: Presentation: the uncharted grain is a sibling of the map pane and does not follow pan or zoom, but at dot alpha about 0.02-0.05 the effect is weak; leave it.

prior_record.title: The uncharted grain is a screen-fixed pattern over a panning map
prior_record.anchor: meshedWorldInit: grain.className='uncharted-grain'; mc.appendChild(grain); CSS .uncharted-grain{position:absolute;inset:0;...background-size:6px 6px}
prior_record.mechanism: Presentation in screen px. The grain is a child of the map container (z-index 350 under the map pane 400), not of a pane, so it does not move with _mapPane and its 6-px dot pattern stays fixed; it shows through the faded base (0.12-0.36).
prior_record.fires_when: z>6.8 with no active city ('show-uncharted'), whenever the map pans or zooms.
prior_record.visible_effect: Shower-door effect: paper texture stays still while coast and roads slide and scale beneath it, so the parchment looks detached from the ground.
prior_record.magnitude: Relative motion = 100% of pan delta and 0% of zoom scale; pattern period 6 screen px.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Put the grain in a custom pane, or update background-position from map._getMapPanePos() on 'move' and background-size from 6*2^(z-z0); or keep it fixed but only for the watermark.
prior_record.fix_risks: No UG3 pin. Filigree owns texture look; desktop identity at z>6.8 changes; per-move updates are cheap.

votes.corrected: The mechanism is confirmed, with one number corrected. In meshedWorldInit (maps-site/index.html, after the registerCityOverlay('Summarch',...) call), a div with class 'uncharted-grain' is appended straight to map.getContainer(). It is a sibling of Leaflet's _mapPane, not a child of any pane. The CSS rule .uncharted-grain{position:absolute;inset:0;z-index:350;background-image:radial-gradient(rgba(90,70,40,.10) 1px,transparent 1.5px);background-size:6px 6px} gives it opacity .6 under .show-uncharted. In the vendored leaflet.css, .leaflet-pane has z-index 400, so the grain sits under the whole map pane and above the #map background (#d9cba7). Leaflet pans and zooms by transforming _mapPane and its children. The container and the grain are never transformed, so the 6-screen-px dot lattice stays still: it moves 0% with a pan and 0% with zoom scaling, while the tiles, realm fills, roads and coast above it slide and scale. The class is toggled in worldOpacityUpdate: mc.classList.toggle('show-uncharted',z>6.8&&!CITYVIEW.name). That function runs on 'zoom zoomend moveend', so the grain shows at z>6.8 whenever nearestCity() finds no anchor within 3*footR(kind) of the view centre. In practice that is most of the atlas. With no city in range, worldCityUpdate caps maxZoom at Z_OPEN_MAX=8. The grain is seen through the base tile layer. baseOpacity(z) runs from about 0.71 at z6.8 down to 0.12 at z8. The claimed range of 0.12-0.36 only covers z of roughly 7.5 to 8, so the grain's net strength grows from about 29% to 88% over z6.8-8. The dots are faint: alpha 0.10 * 0.6 is about 0.06 per 1-px dot. Panes with alpha fills above the grain (pRealm and others) also tint it. The effect is real and is not tied to raster versus vector: a vector city or base would sit over the same fixed grain. Fixes: move the grain into a custom pane under the tile layer (z-index below 200, inside _mapPane) so it moves with pans. Then either scale it, or set background-position from map._getMapPanePos() on 'move' and background-size to 6*2^(z-z0) on 'zoom'. The watermark (.uncharted-mark) is already a separate element and correctly stays screen-fixed, so leave it alone. This rule is not pinned by UG3. The texture's look belongs to the filigree track.
votes.reason: The code path exists as described. The grain is appended to map.getContainer() as a sibling of the map pane, at z-index 350 under the .leaflet-pane rule (z-index 400) in the vendored leaflet.css. Nothing transforms it, so it stays fixed on screen while _mapPane is translated and scaled. The class toggle fires as stated: worldOpacityUpdate runs on 'zoom zoomend moveend' and sets 'show-uncharted' when z>6.8 and no city is within 3 footprint radii. One detail is wrong: base opacity is 0.71 to 0.12 over z6.8-8 (Z_OPEN_MAX caps zoom at 8 with no city), not 0.12-0.36. I rate it minor, not major: each 1-px dot has about 0.06 alpha (0.10 * 0.6), and a uniform lattice has no landmarks to show the slide. A reader at the table sees a faint still texture, not an obvious misregistration, and it does not move any geography or art relative to the atlas.

votes.corrected:
Mechanism, fires_when and vector_independent=true are right: in maps-site/index.html, meshedWorldInit appends div.uncharted-grain to map.getContainer(). It sits as a sibling of .leaflet-map-pane, at z-index 350 under that pane's 400, with background-size:6px 6px. worldOpacityUpdate toggles 'show-uncharted' when z>6.8&&!CITYVIEW.name. During a pan the grain moves 0% while the ground moves 100% of the pan delta, and during a zoom it does not scale at all. The period is 6 screen px.

The visibility figure in the claim is wrong. baseOpacity(z)=1-(z-6.2)/1.8*0.88 gives about 0.71 at z6.8, 0.36 only at z≈7.51 and 0.12 from z8. So the base over the grain runs 0.71→0.12, not 0.12-0.36. The grain shows through only the transparent part of the base. Its peak alpha is the .6 class opacity × the .10 dot alpha × (1-base): about 0.018 at z6.8 and about 0.053 at z≥8. The shower-door effect is real but barely visible. It is cosmetic and plays no part in the city misalignment, because it is off whenever a city is active.

The cheap fix as written is wrong in three ways:
(1) A plain inset:0 div in a custom pane is moved with _mapPane during a pan, so it uncovers bare edges after panning. Leaflet also does not scale it during a zoom animation, because only layers that handle zoomanim are transformed. It needs a world-sized element or a GridLayer, and its pane zIndex must be below the tile pane's 200 to keep today's look of grain under the base.
(2) background-position from map._getMapPanePos() alone is only right until the first zoom, because pixelOrigin changes. Use p=map.latLngToContainerPoint(<fixed world latlng>) and background-position=(p.x mod P)px (p.y mod P)px, recomputed on 'move' and 'zoom'. For wheel zooms, also handle 'zoomanim', since the CSS-animated zoom does not fire 'move' each frame and the grain would otherwise jump at zoomend.
(3) background-size 6*2^(z-z0) has no upper bound. From z6.8 to Z_STREET 11.5 it grows to about 156 px while the 1-px dots stay 1 px, so the grain thins out until it disappears. Wrap it by octave instead: P=6*2^((z-z0) mod 1). Alternatively, anchor the position only and accept that the grain does not scale.

Safety: no UG3 pin is involved; the grain is not in xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask, and no cityCanvasSha. Determinism is untouched because no RNG is used. tools/mobile-capture.js leaves the grain out of chrome_cover because it is pointer-events:none and covers ≥90% of the viewport. That holds if it stays in the container, and an element moved inside #map .leaflet-pane is outside chrome scope anyway, so the metric survives either way. Desktop identity at z>6.8 does change, but only at ≤~5% alpha. Sequencing risks:
- The mobile atlas lane is mid-flight in maps-site/index.html, and A-U0.patch edits the neighbouring .uncharted-mark CSS, so the change must wait for that lane.
- The texture belongs to filigree ('uncharted-band softening' and 'uncharted grain' in docs/filigree/todo-inputs.json), so it should go through filigree rather than a standalone patch.
- Dropping the grain or keeping it only behind the watermark is also acceptable, given how faint it is.
votes.reason: The diagnosis is right: the grain is screen-fixed and does not follow pans or zooms. But the claim says the base over it is 0.12-0.36 when it is actually 0.71→0.12, so the effect is weaker than claimed (dot alpha about 0.02-0.05). Each proposed fix is broken: a pane-based inset:0 div leaves gaps and does not zoom-animate, _getMapPanePos goes stale after a zoom, and 2^(z-z0) sizing has no upper bound and thins the grain until it disappears. The pinned functions and determinism are safe, but the change has to be sequenced after the mobile lane and through filigree.

items.summary: Presentation: the lesser-pin proximity lens replaces the tier-C 1.14 rest scale with an inline scale starting at 1.0, so pins shrink about 12% at the 140-px ring and go stale after a zoom or pan without mouse motion.

prior_record.title: Lesser-pin proximity lens overrides the tier-C 1.14 scale (pins shrink at the 140 px ring) and goes stale after zoom
prior_record.anchor: mousemove lens IIFE (apply / LESSER.eachLayer): g.style.transform=d>=140?'':'scale('+(1+0.55*(1-d/140)).toFixed(3)+')' vs CSS .map-tier-c .mk .glyph{transform:scale(1.14)}
prior_record.mechanism: Presentation. At tier C every lesser glyph rests at scale(1.14); within 140 px of the cursor an inline transform replaces it starting at 1.0, so pins shrink 14% at the ring edge before growing to 1.55; the inline style also beats :hover. Scales are recomputed only on mousemove, so after wheel zoom, fly or keyboard pan they stay keyed to the old screen positions.
prior_record.fires_when: Tier C (pLesser visible), desktop pointer; staleness after any zoom/pan without mouse motion.
prior_record.visible_effect: Pins visibly shrink as the cursor approaches, then swell; after a wheel zoom swollen pins sit away from the cursor and normal ones under it until the mouse moves.
prior_record.magnitude: 16-px pin: 18.2 px at rest to 16.0 px at d=139 (-2.2 px, -12%); mag pins 22.8 to 20 px; max lens 1.55x; staleness until the next mousemove.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Use base = tier C ? 1.14 : 1 and scale(base*(1+0.55*(1-d/140))); re-run apply() on 'zoom' and 'move' with the last pointer position.
prior_record.fix_risks: No UG3 pin. At rest unchanged; filigree R7 may want the lens reviewed; mobile unaffected (no mousemove).

votes.corrected:
Presentation only. It does not affect registration: the scale is applied around the glyph's centre, so no pin moves off its atlas point.

Where it lives, all in maps-site/index.html:
- CSS rule `.map-tier-c .mk .glyph{transform:scale(1.14)}`, with `:hover` at scale(1.3).
- The "lesser pins swell as the cursor nears" IIFE. Its `apply()` loops over LESSER.eachLayer and sets `g.style.transform=d>=140?'':'scale('+(1+0.55*(1-d/140)).toFixed(3)+')'`.
- The pLesser pane is shown only at tier C. The rules `.map-tier-a/.map-tier-b .leaflet-pLesser-pane` set opacity 0, and so does map-tier-d. `updTier` sets map-tier-c on zoomend.

What happens:
- At rest, a lesser glyph is 16 px (20 px for mag pins; box-sizing is border-box). At tier C it scales by 1.14 to 18.2 px (22.8 px for mag).
- Inside the 140 px ring, an inline transform replaces the 1.14 class rule. It starts at 1.0 at the ring edge, so pins drop to 16 px (20 px for mag), a 12% shrink. They stay below rest size across the whole band d ≈ 104–140 px. The crossover where the lens gives back 1.14 is at d = 140·(1 − 0.14/0.55) ≈ 104 px. Closer in, pins grow to a maximum of 1.55.
- The `transition:transform .12s` on .mk.t-lesser .glyph smooths the dip, but it is still visible.
- The inline value also overrides the tier-C `:hover` scale(1.3). The border and shadow on hover still apply.
- `apply()` runs only from a mousemove listener on the container, throttled with requestAnimationFrame. mouseleave clears all the scales. Nothing re-runs it on zoom or move.

When the scales go stale (no mousemove fires):
- **Two-finger trackpad scroll.** The custom wheel handler, after `map.scrollWheelZoom.disable()`, turns non-wheelish scrolls into `map.panBy`. This is the most common case: swollen pins slide away from a still cursor and rest-size pins slide under it.
- **Keyboard pan.**
- **Fly-tos** (flyIntoCity, search, deep links).
- **Mouse wheel and pinch zoom.** These use `setZoomAround` at the cursor, so the pin directly under the cursor stays under it. Zooming in pushes the swollen ring pins outward, still swollen. Zooming out pulls in pins that should swell and leaves them unswollen.

Not affected: drag-pan, because the native mousemove still fires on the container during a drag, so the lens tracks. It is also desktop-pointer only, since touch fires no mousemove.

Fix: use `base = mc.classList.contains('map-tier-c') ? 1.14 : 1` with `scale(base*(1+0.55*(1-d/140)))`. Remember the last pointer position and re-run `apply` on map 'zoom'/'move'. Alternatively, set the inline transform to '' at d≥140 and clamp to at least base inside the ring.
votes.reason:
The code exists as the claim describes. The lens formula and the scale(1.14) CSS rule are both in maps-site/index.html. Inline style beats the class rule and :hover, so pins really are 12% below rest size in the band d ≈ 104–140 px (16 vs 18.2 px; 20 vs 22.8 for mag pins). apply() is triggered only by mousemove, so the scales go stale after zoom or pan.

1. **Wheel zoom.** It is the custom handler (setZoomAround at the cursor), so the pin under the cursor stays put. Zoom-in leaves swollen pins pushed outward, and zoom-out leaves pulled-in pins unswollen. "Normal ones under it" is wrong for zoom-in.
2. **Trackpad two-finger scroll.** The claim missed this, the most common stale case: it calls panBy with no mousemove.

Drag-pan is not stale.

Severity is minor. The effect is about 2 px, smoothed by the .12s transition, and it corrects on the next mouse motion. It moves no pin off its atlas point, so it has nothing to do with registration. It is independent of whether the cities are drawn as raster or vector.

votes.corrected:
The mechanism and visible effect are right, in maps-site/index.html (the mousemove lens IIFE `function apply()` / `LESSER.eachLayer`, versus CSS `.map-tier-c .mk .glyph{transform:scale(1.14);}` and `.map-tier-c .mk .glyph:hover{transform:scale(1.3);}`). LESSER sits in pLesser, which is visible only at tier C: tier A and tier B hide it with opacity 0, and tier D hides it with `opacity:0!important`. So whenever a lesser pin can be seen, its rest scale is 1.14.

The magnitude, recomputed: `*{box-sizing:border-box}` makes `.mk.t-lesser .glyph` 16 px with the border included. At rest it is 16x1.14 = 18.24 px. At d=139 the lens gives 1+0.55/140 = 1.0039, so 16.06 px: -2.18 px, a 12.0% drop in size (the scale falls 0.14). The mag pin goes from 22.8 to 20.08 px. The pin pops between 1.14 and 1.004 when the cursor crosses the 140 px ring, smoothed only by the 0.12 s transition. The lens is smaller than rest in the whole band 104.5 < d < 140 px (the lens equals 1.14 at d = 140x(1-0.14/0.55) = 104.5). The peak is 1.55 at d=0, which is 1.36x the rest size. The inline style does beat both :hover rules, but under the cursor the lens (up to 1.55) is already above the 1.3 hover scale, so the visible loss is small.

This is purely a size pop. transform-origin is the centre, so no pin moves: it is not a registration or anchor shift. vector_independent=true is correct, since these are DOM markers unrelated to the city raster or vector.

On staleness: a drag pan fires mousemove and refreshes the lens. Wheel zoom, flyTo/flyIntoCity, keyboard pan and a tier round-trip (C to B to C) leave the old scales in place until the next mousemove.

The fix as stated is wrong in three ways.
(a) scale(base*(1+0.55*(1-d/140))) is continuous at the ring, but it raises the peak to 1.14x1.55 = 1.767 (a 16 px pin becomes 28.3 px instead of 24.8). Use an interpolation that keeps the peak: s = 1.14 + (1.55-1.14)*(1-d/140) for d<140, else ''. The base can be the literal 1.14, because lesser pins are invisible outside tier C. If the lesser band is meant to read differently from the major glyphs, read it from the `map-tier-c` class.
(b) apply() nulls `pend`, so a re-run needs a separately stored `lastP`. Set it in mousemove and clear it in mouseleave. Hook it to `map.on('zoomend moveend', ...)` (or 'zoom move' through the same rAF throttle) and skip it when lastP is null.
(c) "mobile unaffected (no mousemove)" is not safe once a reapply is added. Phone browsers can fire compatibility mousemove on a tap, and no mouseleave follows. Pins could then re-swell around a stale tap point on every pinch or pan. Record lastP only from pointermove with e.pointerType==='mouse', or gate the whole lens on matchMedia('(hover:hover)').

The fix touches none of xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask, adds no clock token (rAF is not counted, requestIdleCallback is), and leaves determinism alone. The at-rest captures stay the same as long as no hover happens. It edits maps-site/index.html, though, so it has to be sequenced after the mid-flight Mobile 5-9 atlas lane. The lens is existing behaviour, but filigree R7 (nothing at rest; halos on hover only) should sign off on it.

The numbers check out: 18.24 to 16.06 px (-12%), mag 22.8 to 20.08 px, peak 1.55. The mechanism's "shrink 14%" is really a 0.14 drop in scale, which is 12% in size. It is a size pop with the centre fixed, not a position shift, so vector_independent is true. The proposed fix multiplies the base into the lens and so raises the peak to 1.767x, which is not "unchanged". It also ignores that apply() nulls pend, so a stored last pointer is needed. Its "mobile unaffected" claim fails once the lens is re-run on zoom and move, because a tap can fire a compatibility mousemove. There is no UG3 or determinism risk, but the edit lands in maps-site/index.html and must wait for the atlas mobile lane.

items.summary: Presentation: constant-size live glyphs and labels sit over raster-printed rings and names that scale 2^(z-4), so the printed ring and name outgrow the glyph from about z5.4-5.6 and read as two copies drifting apart; nothing is misplaced.

prior_record.title: Constant-size live glyphs and labels sit over raster-printed rings and labels that scale with zoom (reads as drift)
prior_record.subsystem: marks / base raster vs live marks
prior_record.anchor: CSS .atlas-labels .mk .lbl{display:inline} and .mk .glyph{width:22px;height:22px}; baseOpacity (base fades only from z6.2)
prior_record.mechanism: Presentation choice, working as intended. From tier C the live label (13-14 px, right of the glyph) duplicates the cartographer's printed label, which sits elsewhere and scales by 2^(z-4); the printed ring (~5-10 atlas px) outgrows the 16-24 px glyph from about z5.1-5.4. The base stays full opacity until z6.2. A vector city does not change the world-tier raster; only removing/fading the printed layer or the live labels does.
prior_record.fires_when: Tier C to z7.5, most visible z5-7.5 before the base fades.
prior_record.visible_effect: Two copies of each name drift apart as you zoom (printed one grows, left/above/below; live one stays small on the right); rings bulge from under glyphs, amplifying the 1-2 px registration errors.
prior_record.magnitude: Printed label cap height ~9 atlas px (Damoklir crop): 9 px at z4, 36 px at z6, 100 px at z7.49 vs a fixed 13-px live label; lesser ring ~6 atlas px exceeds the 16-px glyph at z5.4, capital ring ~10 atlas px exceeds 22 px at z5.1.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Hide live .lbl for points whose name is printed on the atlas (all Settlements), keeping it for hover; or scale the glyph with zoom past z5 (CSS var set on 'zoom') so it keeps covering its ring.
prior_record.fix_risks: Filigree owns the table-map look (R4 never label blocks, R7 nothing at rest), so decide there. Desktop identity at tier C changes. No UG3 pin.

votes.corrected:
The claim mostly holds, with some corrections. Nothing shifts: the glyph and the printed ring share one atlas point (L.marker at px(x,y), icon anchored at its centre), so this is a scale mismatch, not a registration error. Code path in maps-site/index.html:
- updTier runs on 'zoomend' and toggles 'atlas-labels' when tierFor(z)==='c'. Tier C starts at tierZoom('c') = fitZoom + 2*(TIER_CEIL - fitZoom)/3, with TIER_CEIL = RETINA ? 5 : 6. That is about z4.9 on a non-retina viewport 900 px tall and about z4.25 on retina.
- At tier C, '.atlas-labels .mk .lbl{display:inline}' shows a 13 px label (14 px for t-major) 5 px to the right of the glyph.
- At tier C, '.map-tier-c .mk .glyph{transform:scale(1.14)}' enlarges every glyph.
- worldOpacityUpdate toggles 'map-tier-d' at Z_TIER_D = 7.5, which hides every marker pane.
- baseOpacity is 1 up to z6.2 and then falls to 0.12 by z8.
So from tier C to z7.5 the raster's printed names and rings grow by 2^(z-4) while the live glyph and label stay a fixed screen size.

Corrections:
(1) '.atlas-labels .mk.t-lesser .lbl{display:none}' already hides the live label of all 121 traced-census lesser settlements, Damoklir included (maps_markers.json marks it minor:true). So 'two copies of each name' applies only to the 10 primary Settlements (t-set, e.g. Epēshu and Summarch, whose printed name sits left of or above the ◉) and to the 28 region, water and mountain markers. The Damoklir measurement is fine as a size scale (z5 crop: printed caps about 7-9 atlas px, ring about 6 atlas px; Epēshu ◉ about 10 atlas px), but Damoklir shows no duplicate name.
(2) The glyph sizes leave out the tier-C 1.14 scale. Real sizes: t-set 22 -> 25 px; t-lesser 16 -> 18.2 px; t-lesser.mag 20 -> 22.8 px; t-major (Major Regions, not capitals) 24 -> 27.4 px. Lesser pins also swell up to 1.55x near the cursor. Revised outgrow points: 10-px ◉ ring vs the 25-px t-set glyph about z5.3; vs the 22.8-px mag-lesser glyph about z5.2; 6-px lesser ring vs the 18.2-px glyph about z5.6.
(3) The rings 'amplifying 1-2 px errors' come from marker-coordinate error that grows by 2^(z-4). This mechanism only exposes those errors once the ring is wider than the glyph.
(4) The cheap fix is narrower than stated. Extend the existing t-lesser rule to t-set and the printed region types. But '.atlas-labels .mk-tip{display:none}' also suppresses the hover tooltip at tier C, so that rule must be relaxed too, or hidden points lose their name on hover. Lesser pins already lack a hover name at tier C today.
This is vector-independent: a vector city only replaces the pCity overlay, which fades in from z6.8. Filigree owns the decision (R4/R7). No UG3-pinned function is touched.
votes.reason: The CSS and zoom gates exist and fire as described: 'atlas-labels' is set at tier C on zoomend, labels are fixed at 13-14 px, glyphs are fixed size (x1.14 at tier C), baseOpacity holds 1 until z6.2, and map-tier-d hides markers at Z_TIER_D 7.5. Meanwhile the printed raster scales by 2^(z-4); z5 tile crops confirm the printed names and rings around Damoklir and Epēshu. The claim overstates the scope: lesser settlements, including the Damoklir example, already have their live label hidden at tier C, so duplicate names affect only the 10 primary Settlements and the region-type markers. Its glyph thresholds also leave out the 1.14 tier-C scale, so they come about 0.2 zoom early. Nothing moves relative to the anchor; the printed name and ring grow away from a fixed-size glyph and label. A reader may notice this as clutter around a few names rather than as drift, so it is rated minor.

votes.corrected: The diagnosis is mostly right, but the magnitude is a little off and the fix needs tightening. MECHANISM: right. It is a presentation (rendering) effect, not a registration error. Marker anchors do not move. Box-sizing is border-box, so iconAnchor [gc,gc] centres each glyph exactly, and the tier-C transform:scale(1.14) scales about the centre. Making the city vector does not change it; vector_independent=true holds.
