Lesser (traced-census) labels are already hidden at tier C by '.atlas-labels .mk.t-lesser .lbl{display:none}'. Lesser pins only have the ring-bulge part. MAGNITUDE (recomputed): the printed label and ring were measured on z5 tiles in maps-site/tiles/5. 'Sokundo' cap height is about 10 atlas px. The town ○ is about 6 atlas px. The Epēshu ◉ is about 9.4 atlas px. These scale by 2^(z-4), so cap height is 10 px at z4, 40 at z6 and about 113 at z7.5, against a fixed 13 px live label (14 px for t-major). At the 7.5 tier-d cutoff, baseOpacity is still about 0.36, so the printed copy is still visible when the live marks vanish. The claim's ring crossovers ignore the '.map-tier-c .mk .glyph{transform:scale(1.14)}' step-up, which is always on at tier C. The real on-screen glyph sizes are 25.1 px (t-set, 22), 27.4 (t-major, 24), 20.5 (t-minor, 18), 18.2 (lesser, 16) and 22.8 (lesser.mag, 20). The crossovers are: Settlement ◉ about 9.4 px exceeds 25.1 px at about z5.4 (claimed 5.1); lesser ○ about 6 px exceeds 18.2 px at about z5.6 (claimed 5.4); Māgosh ◉ about 9.4 px exceeds 22.8 px at about z5.3. Tier C starts at fitZoom+2/3*(TIER_CEIL-fitZoom). That is about z4.8 on a 1440-px desktop and about z4.1 on retina (TIER_CEIL 5). The effect runs to Z_TIER_D 7.5, where '.map-tier-d' hides every marker pane. CHEAP FIX: (a) Hide the live .lbl at tier C for points whose name is printed on the atlas. This must come from a per-marker 'printed' flag, not 'all Settlements', because not every wiki Settlement is confirmed to be printed. Touch has no hover, and '.atlas-labels .mk-tip{display:none}', so phones need a tap or tooltip path or the names disappear. (b) If glyphs grow with zoom, use transform:scale only, never width/height. iconAnchor gc is computed once in buildMarkers from the CSS size, so a width-based resize would move the glyph centre off its anchor and create a real (gc-w/2) px shift. The scale must also combine with the existing 1.14 tier-C scale and with the LESSER proximity lens, which writes g.style.transform inline and would override a class or variable transform. Scaling the glyph to keep covering the ring all the way to z7.5 would make badges about 80-110 px that hide the atlas. Better: cap the scale and switch the glyph to a transparent ring-hugging outline, or fade the live glyph past about z5.4. SAFETY: this is CSS and marker-UI only. It touches no UG3-pinned function (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask), leaves cityCanvasSha alone, and uses no RNG, so determinism is safe. It does change desktop identity at tier C. It edits maps-site/index.html, which the atlas mobile lane (Mobile 5-9) is changing now, so it has to queue behind that lane and pass its phone-parity checks. Filigree rulings R4 and R7 decide the label and halo policy.
votes.reason: The mechanism, the vector_independent=true call and the UG3/determinism safety all check out against maps-site/index.html. The printed sizes also check out on z5 tile crops (cap height about 10 px, ○ about 6 px, ◉ about 9.4 px). Two things fail. First, the ring crossovers leave out the always-on tier-C glyph scale(1.14), so they come out about 0.2-0.3 zoom early (5.1 should be about 5.4; 5.4 should be about 5.6). Second, the claim says 'two copies of each name', but lesser labels are already hidden at tier C. The cheap fix is also under-specified on points the claim does not mention. Resizing by width/height would move glyphs off their fixed iconAnchor and create real drift. A transform-based scale clashes with the lesser proximity lens's inline transform. Hiding labels except on hover leaves touch users with no names. 'All Settlements printed' is not verified.

items.summary: Refuted: Leaflet's built-in 6-px tooltip margins were ignored; the real gaps are 6-10 px with no overlap, and nothing changes with zoom.

prior_record.title: Marker tooltips use a fixed 12 px right offset regardless of glyph radius (8-12 px) and hover scale
prior_record.anchor: buildMarkers, buildRoute, buildOrigins, buildFactionBadges bindTooltip(...,{direction:'right',offset:[12,0]}); buildWorldPOIs/buildPOILayer offset [0,-11]; Leaflet tooltipAnchor [0,0]
prior_record.mechanism: Screen-px callout placement. A 'right' tooltip's left edge sits at latlng + offset.x; glyph radii are 8 (lesser), 9 (minor), 10 (mag), 11 (set/water/mtn/faction), 12 (major), hover scales 1.18/1.3 push past 12. The .poi-mk offset assumes 11 px but the halo is 13 px from its (offset) centre.
prior_record.fires_when: Hover at tiers A/B (marker tooltips hidden by .atlas-labels .mk-tip at tier C); POI hover at any zoom.
prior_record.visible_effect: Tooltip chips butt into or overlap larger glyphs (major, hovered) and float 4 px off small pins; constant across zoom, not a drift.
prior_record.magnitude: Gap = 12 - r*s: lesser 4 px, set 1 px, major 0 px, hovered set -1 px (overlap), POI tooltip overlaps the halo by 2 px.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Pass offset [gc+4,0] per marker class and [0,-15] for POIs, or set icon tooltipAnchor [gc,0].
prior_record.fix_risks: Hover-only, no at-rest identity change; no UG3 pin.

votes.corrected:
This is not a zoom-shift source. It is a constant, hover-only spacing variation, and the claim's arithmetic is wrong. File: maps-site/index.html, plus the vendored Leaflet 1.9.4 in vendor/leaflet@1.9.4/dist.

(1) How Leaflet places the chip. Tooltip._setPosition does pos - [subX,subY] + offset + _getAnchor(). For direction 'right', subX is 0 and subY is height/2. Marker._getTooltipAnchor returns the icon's tooltipAnchor, and for a divIcon that defaults to [0,0]. On top of that, the vendored leaflet.css adds .leaflet-tooltip-right{margin-left:6px} and .leaflet-tooltip-top{margin-top:-6px}, and .mk-tip does not override either margin. The claim missed these margins. So a 'right' chip's left edge sits 12+6 = 18 px right of the glyph centre. A 'top' chip's bottom edge sits 11+6 = 17 px above the centre. buildFactionBadges uses offset [11,0], not [12,0], which gives 17 px.

(2) Glyph radii are correct: under *{box-sizing:border-box} they are 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12 px, and gc in buildMarkers matches them.

(3) When it fires.
- `.atlas-labels .mk-tip{display:none}` is toggled with tier C in updTier. That hides every mk-tip at tier C, including the buildWorldPOIs tooltips in pCityPOI, because the city zooms are at or above tier C (TIER_CEIL is 5 or 6). So the "POI hover at any zoom" case is wrong.
- The LESSER layer (lesser and mag pins) appears only at tier C, so the lesser and mag cases never show a chip.
- The tier-C hover scale of 1.3 never coincides with a visible chip.
- The pFaction pane is hidden at tiers A and B, so faction tooltips are effectively never seen.
- pOrigin is hidden at tier A, so origin chips show only at tier B.
- Route waypoint chips bind only when the waypoint is clamped (c.clamped).
- What actually fires: buildMarkers chips for set/major/minor/water/mtn at tiers A and B (hover scale 1.18), origin chips at tier B, and chart-mode buildPOILayer chips (enterChart removes atlas-labels).

(4) Actual gaps, chip edge to glyph rim:
| Marker | At rest | Hovered (scale 1.18) |
|---|---|---|
| minor | 9 px | 7.4 px |
| set / water / mtn / origin | 7 px | 5 px |
| major | 6 px | 3.8 px |

For chart POIs, the chip's bottom edge is 17 px above centre and the .poi-mk halo radius is 13 px, so the gap is 4 px. On hover (scale 1.15) the halo reaches 14.95 px, leaving a 2 px gap. Only the faint 3 px box-shadow ring (out to about 18.4 px) overlaps the chip, by about 1.4 px.

Nothing butts into or overlaps a glyph, nothing changes with zoom, and nothing is anchored wrongly. Registration plays no part, and neither does the rendering medium: the cause is screen-space chip spacing, not atlas registration. An optional cosmetic fix is a per-class offset of [gc+2,0] or icon tooltipAnchor [gc,0] plus a smaller offset; it would only even out the 4-9 px gaps.

The fixed-offset mechanism exists: offset [12,0] on 'right' chips in buildMarkers, buildRoute and buildOrigins, [11,0] in buildFactionBadges, [0,-11] on 'top' POI chips, and tooltipAnchor defaulting to [0,0] via Marker._getTooltipAnchor. But the claim ignores Leaflet's own .leaflet-tooltip-right margin-left:6px and .leaflet-tooltip-top margin-top:-6px in the vendored leaflet.css (.mk-tip does not override them). The real chip positions are therefore 18 px and 17 px from the glyph centre, so no overlap occurs: the gaps are 4-9 px, and down to 2 px for a hovered chart POI. Several cases in the claim never fire:
- Lesser pins exist only at tier C, where `.atlas-labels .mk-tip` hides every chip.
- The 1.3 hover scale is tier-C only.
- Faction badges use [11,0] and their pane is hidden at tiers A and B.

The chips keep a constant screen offset from their markers, so they cannot cause the zoom-shift misalignment the owner reported.

items.summary: Presentation: clampToFrame insets off-frame marks by 16 atlas px, so the inset grows on screen with zoom (6 px at z2.6 to 179 px at z7.49); it does not misregister against the art.

prior_record.title: Off-frame marks rest 16 ATLAS px inside the frame, an inset that grows with zoom
prior_record.anchor: clampToFrame in maps-site/index.html (pad=pad==null?16:pad), used by buildMarkers, buildRoute (cpt and pips), buildOrigins, buildFactionBadges, flyTo; chevHtml offset 15 px (screen)
prior_record.mechanism: Presentation. Places beyond the drawn atlas are clamped to the frame with a 16-unit inset in world (atlas) px while the chevron offset is screen px; the intent ('rests at the frame edge') is screen-space but implemented in map px.
prior_record.fires_when: Clamped marks (e.g. Far North and Fell Mountains at y=-92/-93 clamped to y=16) at any zoom.
prior_record.visible_effect: At fit zoom edge marks hug the frame; zooming in they move inward and look like ordinary in-frame places with a chevron.
prior_record.magnitude: 16 atlas px = 6 px at z2.6, 16 px at z4, 64 px at z6, 179 px at z7.49.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Clamp with pad 0 in atlas px and inset the glyph via iconAnchor (screen px) toward the interior along DIR_VEC, or recompute pad = 16/2^(z-4) per zoom; same rule for route spline ends.
prior_record.fix_risks: No UG3 pin. Fit-zoom inset changes from 6 px to the chosen px (small desktop identity change at edges).

votes.corrected:
Confirmed in maps-site/index.html. `clampToFrame(x,y,pad)` sets `pad=pad==null?16:pad`. When a point lies outside 0..IMG_W x 0..IMG_H, it clamps both coordinates to [pad, IMG-pad] in atlas (world) px. In-frame points are returned untouched.

Callers that use the default 16:
- buildMarkers
- buildRoute's `cpt` (spline control points) and its waypoint pips
- buildOrigins
- buildTrails (the claim did not list this one)
- buildFactionBadges
- flyTo and goWaypoint (these only set the fly target)

Callers that pass pad 0: the route spline samples ("spline overshoot hugs the edge") and buildSeaLanes.

`chevHtml` puts the badge 15 icon (screen) px inward along DIR_VEC from the glyph centre. Under CRS.Simple with NZ=4, the 16-px inset is 16*2^(z-4) screen px:
- about 6 px at a desktop fitZoom of about 2.6 (`fillZoom` = 4+log2(vh/2188))
- 16 px at z4
- 64 px at z6
- about 179 px at z7.49

Marks vanish at Z_TIER_D=7.5, when `map-tier-d` sets the mark panes to opacity 0.

Clamped canon marks in data/maps_markers.json:
- Far North (1826,-92) and Hoarland (2088,-94), both rest at y=16
- Fell Mountains (782,-93), rests at y=16
- Moonless Lands (-174.9,1441), rests at x=16
- Party-route and origin points beyond the frame get the same treatment.

One precision: this is not a zoom shift in the registration sense. The mark is pinned to a fixed atlas point (y=16), so it stays perfectly anchored to the atlas art and never drifts against coast, river or road. Only its screen-space distance from the frame edge grows with zoom. You see it only when the frame edge is in view, which maxBounds/contentBounds with viscosity 1 lets you pan to. The rendering medium has nothing to do with it, so it is vector-independent.

The proposed fix is sound and touches no UG3 pin. Clamp with pad 0, then inset the glyph in screen px through iconAnchor along DIR_VEC (or put the pad on a zoom handler). Two cautions:
- The route `cpt` and the buildTrails endpoints must follow the same rule, or the line ends will detach from their pips.
- Corner cases (NE/NW) need a diagonal inset.
votes.reason: The code path exists as described. `clampToFrame` defaults pad to 16 atlas px, the chevron offset is a screen-px 15, and the arithmetic (16*2^(z-4)) matches every stated magnitude. Marks hide at Z_TIER_D 7.5, so z7.49 is the true maximum. The claim omits buildTrails from the callers and frames the effect as marks moving inward. In fact they hold a fixed atlas position, so nothing misregisters against the art. The issue is only that the "rests at the map's edge" cue (edgeLine) weakens: at z6+ an edge-pinned region sits 64-179 px inside the frame. That only shows when panned to the frame edge, and only for a handful of marks (Far North, Hoarland, Fell Mountains, Moonless Lands, any off-frame route, origin or faction points). It is subtle rather than something a reader at the table would read as an anchoring fault, hence minor.

votes.corrected:
The magnitude is right. pad defaults to 16 in atlas px (clampToFrame: pad=pad==null?16:pad), and screen px = 16*2^(z-NZ) with NZ=4. That gives 16*2^(2.6-4)=6.1 px, 16 at z4, 64 at z6 and 16*2^3.49=180 px at z7.49 (just under Z_TIER_D 7.5). The fit zoom is fillZoom = 4+log2(vh/2188), so the fit-zoom inset depends on the viewport: about 5 px on a 700-px-tall phone, 6 px at vh≈830 and 7.3 px at vh≈1000. Past z7.5 it keeps growing, up to 1448 px at Z_STREET 11.5.

The data example checks out: Far North (1826,-92) and Fell Mountains (782,-93) in data/maps_markers.json clamp to y=16. The chevron offset in chevHtml is 15 px in icon/screen space, measured from the glyph centre along -DIR_VEC, so it points inward.

The claim has gaps:
(a) buildTrails also uses the default pad (o and j), so the Company origin trails are affected too. The list should include it.
(b) The pad is already inconsistent today. In buildRoute, cpt and the waypoint pips use 16, but spline points use clampToFrame(...,0), and buildSeaLanes uses 0. So route and lane lines run to the frame edge while their pips rest 16 atlas px inside.
(c) This does not cause misalignment against atlas features. The mark is fixed in atlas space. Only its screen inset from the frame edge scales with zoom. It is a registration-free presentation issue, and vector_independent=true is right.

Corrected cheap fix (prefer option 1):
1. Clamp with pad 0 in clampToFrame for marks, the route cpt, trails and flyTo. Then inset each clamped glyph in screen px through the divIcon's iconAnchor: iconAnchor=[gc+u[0]*K, gc+u[1]*K] with u=DIR_VEC[dir] and K≈12-16. Moving the anchor outward along u puts the glyph K px inside the edge at every zoom. Do the same for the pips (10,10), origins (11,11) and faction badges (11,11). The faction-badge spread offsets (ox,oy) stay in atlas px and only matter for stacked seats. On diagonals, K*0.71 per axis.
2. Do not use the per-zoom pad=16/2^(z-4) option. It needs a setLatLng plus a polyline rebuild for every clamped mark on each zoomend, and during the zoom animation the marks would ride the old inset and then snap. That is itself a zoom shift.

Fix risks:
- No UG3 pin: xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask are untouched, cityCanvasSha is untouched, and nothing here uses gen RNG.
- Determinism is unaffected.
- Desktop identity changes only at the edges. Fit-zoom edge glyphs move from about 6 px to K px, and route/trail ends move by up to 16 atlas px.
- The phone side benefits most, because at a phone fit zoom (~2.3-2.4) the 16-px inset is about 5 px and a glyph can crop under the top chrome. K should account for that.
- The edit touches maps-site/index.html, which the mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) holds. Sequence it after that lane, or queue it as a unit there.
votes.reason: I recomputed the magnitudes from NZ=4 and the default pad of 16 and they match: 6.1, 16, 64 and 180 px. The mechanism also checks out: the pad is in atlas px while the chevron offset is in screen px. vector_independent=true is correct, since this is presentation and not registration. The first suggested fix (pad 0 plus a screen-px iconAnchor inset) is correct and safe: no UG3 pin is touched, determinism is unaffected, and desktop identity changes only by a few px at the edges. The claim misses that buildTrails also uses the default pad, and that route splines and sea lanes already use pad 0, so lines and their pips already disagree. The fit-zoom inset varies with the viewport (about 5-7 px). The per-zoom-pad alternative should be dropped, because re-placing marks on zoomend snaps them after the animation and adds a new zoom shift. The edit also has to be sequenced around the mobile atlas lane, which holds maps-site/index.html.

items.summary: Refuted: the spline adds at most 5.8 px; the trace itself is 20-80 px off the printed road, a fixed atlas offset that grows on screen rather than slides.

prior_record.title: Named ways, route legs and way labels ride a Catmull-Rom spline that leaves the traced vertices and the printed dotted road
prior_record.anchor: buildNamedWays: `var sm=crSpline(way.pts,16)`, label marker at px(sm[mi][0],sm[mi][1]) with .way-label{transform:translate(-50%,-50%)}; buildRoute `crSpline(ctrl,18)`; buildSeaLanes crSpline(...,16)
prior_record.mechanism: REGISTRATION of drawn geometry to the print. The traced polylines are registered to the atlas's dotted roads, but centripetal CR smoothing bulges between sparse vertices and cuts sharp traced corners. The label chip is centred on a spline vertex (index midpoint, not arc-length midpoint; 216 atlas px off the arc midpoint on the long road, a placement issue). APPR_POLYS and stubs use the raw trace, so the drawn road and the city's idea of the road disagree. Deviation from the printed dots themselves is unmeasured (probe: sample z5 tiles along the spline for the dotted pattern).
prior_record.fires_when: pWay visible (tier B line, tier C labels), legible from z>~5, until tier-d at 7.5.
prior_record.visible_effect: The inked road and its name chip slide off the printed dotted road on bends as you zoom.
prior_record.magnitude: Max deviation of any smoothed way point from the raw trace over all named ways: 5.79-5.8 atlas px ('Road that Walks with the Sun', 28 pts; 'The East-West Road' (4 pts) 3.2): 6.7 px at z4.2, 23 px at z6, 46 px at z7, 65 px at z7.49.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Draw the traced polyline directly (round lineJoin) or densify the trace so CR deviation is <0.5 px; keep crSpline only for conjectural sea lanes and the party route; place the label at the arc-length midpoint.
prior_record.fix_risks: Filigree slice B (ink) owns road styling; desktop identity at tier B/C changes slightly. Not pinned. Approach bearings already use raw points.

votes.corrected:
The code is as quoted, in maps-site/index.html. buildNamedWays draws casing, road and hit line from `crSpline(way.pts,16)`. Its label marker sits at `px(sm[mi][0],sm[mi][1])` with `mi=Math.floor(sm.length/2)`, and `.way-label` uses translate(-50%,-50%) with iconAnchor [0,0], so the chip is centred on a point of the drawn spline. buildRoute uses `crSpline(ctrl,18)` for each leg and buildSeaLanes uses `crSpline(...,16)`. buildApprPolys, which feeds APPR_POLYS and then the approach bearings and buildCityStubs, uses the raw `w.pts`. pWay shows at tiers B and C, the label only at map-tier-c, and both are hidden at map-tier-d (Z_TIER_D=7.5) and in chart-mode.

Re-measured against data/named-ways.json by running the shipped crSpline:
- Road that Walks with the Sun (28 points): max distance from the raw polyline 5.79 atlas px. 211 of 433 spline points are more than 1 px off and 100 are more than 2 px off.
- The East-West Road (4 points): 3.19 px.
- Sea lanes: up to 13.4 px (The Gulf Crossing). These are conjectural.
- Label offset from the arc-length midpoint: 216.2 and 31.1 atlas px. This is a placement choice; the chip still sits on the drawn road.
- The screen-px figures are correct at 2^(z-4): 6.7 at z4.2, 23 at z6, 46 at z7, 65 at z7.49.

The premise is false, though. The traced polylines are NOT registered to the printed dotted roads. I overlaid both traces on the z5 tiles (atlas px x2, no y-flip):
- The Sun Road trace runs along the outer Leponnia coastline, crosses the open water of the Gulf (Bēgil to Drāmūz) where nothing is printed, then cuts a straight diagonal across Rubea, where the print has no dotted road at all. The printed dotted roads run inland, roughly 20-50 atlas px away, with a different topology.
- The East-West Road trace follows the Undaukhor River, roughly 40-80 atlas px from the printed dotted road that runs from Summarch to the ford.
- Both entries say "Trace approximate" in their data, and the cards show provBlock('trace').

So the dominant REGISTRATION error is the hand trace itself, an order of magnitude larger than the spline effect. CR smoothing is a second-order effect of at most 5.8 px, sitting on a line that was never on the dots. It is also not a zoom shift. Both the spline and the raw trace are fixed in world coordinates, so nothing slides as you zoom; a fixed offset just grows in screen px like any static misregistration. The base also fades from 1 to 0.12 over z6.2-8 (baseOpacity), which further hides any comparison with the print at z7+.

The one real internal mismatch is small: the drawn road (spline) and APPR_POLYS or the stubs (raw trace) disagree by up to 5.8 atlas px where a way meets a city's approach circle.

What fixes registration is re-tracing named-ways.json onto the printed dot rows, densely enough to follow bends (sample the z5 tiles), or marking the Sun Road as conjectural where the print has no road. Drawing raw or densified points is then a cheap follow-on that removes the remaining 5.8 px. Fixing the spline alone leaves the road 20-80 atlas px off the print. This holds whatever the medium: a vector road fed the same trace misaligns the same way.
votes.reason: The code path and the spline deviation figures check out: 5.79 px max on the Sun Road and 3.19 px on the East-West Road, reproduced by running the shipped crSpline on data/named-ways.json, and the label sits at the index midpoint, not the arc midpoint. But the claimed cause, smoothing pulling the road off the printed dotted road, doesn't hold. Overlaying both traces on the z5 tiles shows the traces themselves are not on the printed dots: the Sun Road hugs the coast, crosses the Gulf by sea and cuts straight across Rubea, and the East-West Road follows the Undaukhor River 40-80 px from the dotted road. Both are marked "Trace approximate". The trace's own error is roughly 10x the spline's. Also nothing moves as you zoom: a fixed world-space offset only scales. The genuine spline-specific effect, the drawn road against the APPR_POLYS and stub raw trace, is at most 5.8 atlas px and would be hard to notice next to the much larger trace error.

votes.corrected: Mechanism holds; the visible effect, its framing as a zoom shift, and part of the fix need correcting. MAGNITUDE (recomputed by running crSpline from maps-site/index.html on maps-site/data/named-ways.json): the largest distance from a smoothed point to the raw trace is 5.79 atlas px on 'Road that Walks with the Sun' (28 pts, arc length 2304) and 3.19 px on 'The East-West Road' (4 pts). On screen that is 5.79·2^(z−4) px: 6.7 at z4.2, 23.2 at z6, 46.4 at z7 and 65.2 at z7.49. Above Z_TIER_D=7.5 the map-tier-d CSS hides pWay. Label: the index midpoint sm[floor(n/2)] is 221 atlas px along the arc from the arc-length midpoint on the Sun Road (28 px on East-West). The chip still sits on the curve (0.88 px and 2.93 px from the trace), so this is a placement choice, not misregistration. VISIBLE EFFECT, corrected: this is a FIXED offset in atlas space. It is static against the print at every zoom and only grows in proportion to the zoom, like any fixed offset. It is not a source of zoom-dependent shift. The only part that changes with zoom is Leaflet's default smoothFactor=1 simplification, which is under 1 screen px. The owner's 'things shift as we zoom' complaint is therefore not explained by this; at most it adds a constant bend error of up to ~5.8 atlas px. The error against the printed dotted road is still unmeasured. named-ways.json itself says 'Trace approximate', so the trace's own error against the print may be larger than the spline's error against the trace. Probe: sample the z5 tiles along both the raw trace and the spline. Without that probe the claim that the raw trace is better registered is unproven. vector_independent=true is right: this is drawn-geometry registration, already vector. FIX, corrected: (1) Draw the raw polyline with round lineJoin, OR densify AT RENDER TIME inside buildNamedWays only (linear subdivision before crSpline, or a smaller tension). Do NOT edit pts in named-ways.json. buildApprPolys feeds w.pts into cityApproaches (segCircleHits at radius 2.5·footR), which feeds genCityCanvas landAppr. A data edit would change the approach bearings for any city whose ring the road crosses (Tamaron lies on the Sun Road). That changes cityCanvasSha against B0, a UG3 failure, even if the code of genCityCanvas is untouched. Even collinear densification can shift the float bearings. (2) Keep crSpline for sea lanes and the party route. (3) Put the label at the arc-length midpoint. (4) Better still: re-trace the Sun Road against the z5 tiles once the probe has measured how far the trace is off the print. That is a data change, so it must be scheduled with a deliberate cityCanvasSha re-baseline in the mobile lane, not slipped in. A render-only change touches none of xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask, adds no RNG or clock use, and is deterministic. It does change the desktop look slightly at tiers B and C (road styling belongs to filigree slice B), and maps-site/index.html is held by the in-flight Mobile 5-9 lane, so it must be sequenced after that lane.
votes.reason: The constants check out (5.79/3.19 atlas px; 6.7/23.2/46.4/65.2 screen px at z4.2/6/7/7.49; label off the arc midpoint by ~221 px, not 216). But the visible effect is misdescribed: a fixed atlas-space offset scales with zoom like everything else and does not 'slide as you zoom', so it does not explain the owner's zoom shift. Its error against the printed road is unmeasured, and the trace is self-declared approximate. The fix 'densify the trace' is unsafe if it is done in named-ways.json: those pts feed APPR_POLYS, then cityApproaches, then genCityCanvas, and the change would move cityCanvasSha (UG3). The fix has to be render-only inside buildNamedWays, or a re-trace planned with a re-baseline.

items.summary: Plan core: genCityCanvas deliberately pushes a water city's core 0.07 S inland (capital 3.6, town 2.0, village 1.3, ruin 1.12 atlas px) while the mask coast stays registered; accept and record it, and do not shift cityBox.

prior_record.title: The generated town core is deliberately drawn off the anchor (away from the sea) and the market square is jittered
prior_record.anchor: genCityCanvas: `if(drawWater){cx-=sv.x*S*0.07; cy-=sv.y*S*0.07;}` and `var sq={x:cx+rr(-coreR*.12,coreR*.12), ...}`
prior_record.mechanism: Working as intended (to show more land), but it reads as a shift. For water cities the plan core is pushed 7% of the canvas inland from the canvas centre (the anchor), and the market square jitters up to +/-0.12*coreR per axis; POIs and the box stay anchor-centred. The ring dot (visible until tier-d) sits on the plan's sea side.
prior_record.fires_when: Every generated harbour/coastal (drawWater) city at z>=6.8.
prior_record.visible_effect: The town's densest blocks and market sit a little inland of the printed ◉.
prior_record.magnitude: 0.07*2r: capital 3.6, town 2.0, village 1.3, ruin 1.12 atlas px (36/19/12 screen px at z7.3; 58/31/20 at z8); square jitter up to +/-2.1 (capital), 0.87 (town), 0.37 (village) atlas px per axis.
prior_record.cheap_fix: Accept and record it, or move the shift into the overlay bounds (offset cityBox by the same vector) so the canvas core stays on the anchor; if the dot must sit in the town, move the anchor instead.
prior_record.fix_risks: Any change inside genCityCanvas changes its UG3 source hash and every generated cityCanvasSha. The bounds alternative moves world POIs and stubs, which must apply the same offset. Determinism holds.

votes.corrected:
The core of the claim holds, and the code comment says the offset is intentional: "shifted a touch off the sea so more land shows". Three details in the claim are wrong, and the proposed cheap fix would cause a misregistration. All code is in maps-site/index.html.

1. Mechanism
- In genCityCanvas, `drawWater = !!sv && (t.harbor || distPx<=25)`. Here sv is compassVec(t.sea.side). For a harbour with no charted side it is a seeded pick(COMPASS), which mask.bear replaces once the atlas mask has real water. sv is always a unit vector.
- The plan centre moves with `cx-=sv.x*S*0.07; cy-=sv.y*S*0.07` (S=GEN_SIZE 2048), away from the water.
- Everything the plan draws uses the shifted (cx,cy): the land blob, fields, gates (mkGate), the market square, the shore fallback and the POIs. The market square is `sq={x:cx+rr(-coreR*.12,coreR*.12),...}` with coreR=S*kR. For river cities the retry loop widens this to ±0.18 coreR and can push the square further off the stream.
- The canvas itself is placed by cityBox(a,S,S). That box is a 2r square centred on the anchor, so the canvas centre is the anchor dot.

2. Magnitudes (all correct)
- The shift is 0.14r world px: capital 3.64, town 1.96, village 1.26, ruin 1.12.
- On screen that is about 36/19/12 px at z7.3 and 58/31/20 px at z8.
- Square jitter per axis is 0.12·kR·2r: capital 2.12, town 0.87, village 0.37, ruin 0.46.

3. Corrections
- (a) POIs do not stay anchor-centred. addPoi uses canvas coordinates built from the shifted cx/cy/sq/gates. buildWorldPOIs and worldPOICoord map them through the same cityBox, so the roundels sit on the drawn market, quay and gate, with no mismatch between POIs and the plan. The same applies to stubs: the inner end is the real shifted gate (`a.atlasX+(gg.x-S/2)/scl`) and the outer end is anchor-radial at 1.18·footR.
- (b) The coast is not shifted when the atlas mask is present (the MK path). The water field is drawn from the z5 mask at `(a.atlasX-rW)*2-MK.ox`, which is anchor-registered. So the coast lines up with the atlas, and only the settlement composition moves inland of the dot. This is a composition offset, not a registration error. Without a mask (the synthetic shore in ensureCityGenNow before tiles are sampled), the shore is measured from the shifted cx. For an uncharted harbour the seeded compass side can also differ from the later mask.bear, so the hot-swap can move the core-shift direction and the coast together. That is a separate, deep-link-only jump.
- (c) It is not a zoom-dependent shift. The offset is fixed in world space and scales with the map. Readers notice it only during the crossfade window: z6.8 to 7.5, where the ◉ in pSettle is still visible (map-tier-d hides it from Z_TIER_D 7.5) and the overlay is at 0–0.7 opacity. The wash (washMake, 1.7× footprint) also fades the printed glyph over this band.

4. Fix
- Offsetting cityBox by the same vector is wrong. It would carry the mask-drawn coast 0.14r off the atlas coast, and this registration error is exactly what the owner is complaining about.
- Correct options: accept and record the offset; or drop the push inside genCityCanvas (cx=cy=S/2 when MK is present, letting the real coast keep buildings out of the water); or move the anchor if canon puts the dot in the town.
- Any genCityCanvas change alters its UG3 atlas_fn_sha and every generated cityCanvasSha. Determinism holds either way. This issue is independent of raster vs vector: a vector plan with the same composition offset would read the same.
votes.reason:
genCityCanvas does push the plan centre 0.07·S away from the water whenever drawWater is true, and jitters the market square by up to ±0.12·coreR. The magnitudes in the claim are correct. Three parts of the claim are wrong:
- POIs and stub gate ends use the shifted canvas coordinates, so they follow the plan rather than staying anchor-centred.
- When the atlas mask is present, the coast inside the canvas is anchor-registered from the z5 tiles. The art is therefore still registered to the atlas; only the town composition sits about 0.14r inland of the ring dot.
- The offset is fixed in world space and does not drift with zoom. It shows only in the z6.8–7.5 crossfade, while the ◉ is still on screen, and the wash softens it.

That makes it minor. The claim's "offset cityBox" fix would actively misregister the mask-drawn coast, so it is corrected above.

votes.corrected: MAGNITUDE (recomputed, correct as claimed): generated canvases are S×S (GEN_SIZE 2048), so cityBox gives hw=hh=r and 1 canvas px = 2r/S world px; sv is a unit vector (compassVec sin/cos, mask.bear normalised). Core offset = 0.07·2r = capital 3.64, town 1.96, village 1.26, ruin 1.12 atlas px; ×2^(z-4) gives about 36/19/12 screen px at z7.3 and 58/31/20 at z8. When a stream runs through (RV), the retry widens this to ±0.18·coreR (capital 3.2, town 1.3) and can push the square further, to sqN.w/2+0.22·coreR off the stream. MECHANISM CORRECTION: POIs are NOT anchor-centred. addPoi uses plan coordinates (sq, cx/cy, waterNode, gates), so the market, temple and quays POIs move with the shifted core. The stubs are mixed: the inner end (ix=a.atlasX+(gg.x-S/2)/scl) follows the shifted gate, and the outer end (a.atlasX+cos·footR·1.18) stays anchor-centred. What does stay on the anchor is the box and the MK coast. sampleCityMask/genCityCanvas draw the mask from (a.atlasX-rW)*2, so the coast and water are registered to the atlas. It only reads as a shift during the z6.8–7.8 crossfade, while the printed dot and label are still visible. vector_independent=true is right: a vector plan with the same core offset shows it too. That turns a cosmetic core offset into a real coast-misregistration of the same 1–3.6 px against the atlas, which breaks 'bend art to the atlas'. It would also need gen-only branching (cityBox also places the canon Epēshu/Summarch overlays, POIs, wash and pyramids) plus a stub inner-end offset. Correct options: (1) preferred: accept it and record it as a registration note (the coast is registered, the ◉ is atlas truth, and a ≤3.6 px inland core is within the drawn footprint); or (2) if the core must sit on the dot, change it inside genCityCanvas (drop or shrink the 0.07 shift, or apply it only when !MK, since a sampled mask already shows true land). That changes genCityCanvas's UG3 atlas_fn_sha and the cityCanvasSha of every drawWater city (and of every city if the jitter is touched). It must be a central, coordinated re-pin after the mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) lands, not done mid-lane. Determinism holds either way: the change is pure geometry and the R() draw order is unchanged if only the constant changes. Desktop identity changes visibly for harbour towns, so it needs filigree slice C sign-off. Never move the anchor: anchors are atlas data and the atlas is authoritative.
votes.reason: The magnitudes check out against FOOT_R, kR, GEN_SIZE and the 0.07/0.12 constants, and vector_independent is right. The claim fails on two points. First, its mechanism says POIs stay anchor-centred, but addPoi uses plan coordinates that move with the core; only the stub outer ends and the mask coast are anchor-registered. Second, its primary fix is harmful. Shifting the cityBox bounds would move the atlas-sampled MK coast, which is drawn from (a.atlasX-rW)*2 in genCityCanvas, off the atlas, creating a real registration error to cure a deliberate cosmetic one. Its other suggestion, moving the anchor, bends atlas data to the art. A safe fix lives only inside genCityCanvas (shrink the shift, or apply it only without a mask). That breaks the UG3 hash and the drawWater cityCanvasSha pins, so it must be re-pinned centrally after the mobile atlas lane. Otherwise, accept it as is.

items.summary: Tone, not shift: washMake's anchor-centred f=1.7 land-tone radial tints atlas sea beyond a coastal plan's own coast at 0.5-0.94 alpha in a band 0.36-0.56 r wide; any fix touches pinned washMake.

prior_record.title: The land-tone wash (1.7x box) paints over the atlas sea around coastal cities beyond the plan's own coast
prior_record.anchor: washMake `var box=cityBox(a,reg.w,reg.h),f=1.7;` and washUrl radial stops .94 @0-.5, .5 @.78, 0 @1
prior_record.mechanism: REGISTRATION/rendering. A radial wash in the sampled land hue covers 1.7*footR around the anchor, riding overlayOpacity. The plan's own content (water included) dissolves through the seeded vignette at 0.385-0.485*S radius (0.77-0.97*footR), so between the vignette and the wash fade-out the atlas sea and coast are tinted land-coloured at 50-94% alpha; the coast appears to recede and the plan's coast ends in a tan halo instead of meeting the atlas coast. (Wash and land tone are sampled from tiles/5 only, a tone mismatch under war/imperial eras.)

The mechanism exists and works mostly as claimed, with four corrections. It is a RENDERING (tint) seam, not a REGISTRATION error: the wash is centred on the anchor through the same cityBox as the plan, so nothing moves. The coast is hidden, not displaced.

Code path (maps-site/index.html):
- ensureCityOverlay calls washMake(key,reg,a) for every anchored city, canon charts included.
- washMake: `var box=cityBox(a,reg.w,reg.h),f=1.7;` builds an L.imageOverlay(washUrl(key)) over bounds of ±1.7·hw / ±1.7·hh around the anchor. It sits in pane pCityWash (z 449), just under pCity (450) and above the tile pane.
- washUrl draws a 256² radial gradient in tone tn = MASKQ[key].m.land, or LAND_TAN [198,178,128] before sampling. Stops: .94 at 0–.5, .5 at .78, 0 at 1. So the wash is elliptical when the image is not square.
- worldOpacityUpdate sets wash.setOpacity(overlayOpacity(z)), so it fades in over z6.8–7.8 (zoom 'zoom' event plus washRefresh after sampling).
- Within the wash, effective alpha ≥.94·oo out to 0.85·footR and ≥.5·oo out to 1.33·footR along each axis, reaching 0 at 1.7·footR.

1) Invented plans (genCityCanvas): the claim holds. WATER '#7fa3a0' is drawn from the atlas-sampled MK mask, so the plan's coast is registered to the atlas. The seeded destination-out vignette (v0=0.385+vw, v1=0.485+0.7vw, seven harmonics with am .012–.05) dissolves the plan at about 0.77–0.97·footR. Its exact radius wobbles with the seed. Beyond that, atlas sea under the wash is overpainted land-tan. The band is about 0.36–0.56·footR: capital 9–15, town 5–8, village 3–5 atlas px, roughly 150–240 screen px for a capital at z8.

2) Canon charts (overlay-Epeshu.jpg, overlay-Summarch.jpg) have NO vignette. They are opaque rectangles ending at exactly 1.0·hw/hh. The tan ring therefore starts at the chart's straight edge, with alpha ≈.80 there, and runs to 1.33·footR (≥.5) and 1.7 (0). That is a band about 0.33·footR wide, about 9 px for a capital, around a hard rectangle. It is not a halo at the art's own waterline.

3) Visibility is strongly damped by baseOpacity. In day theme the base fades 1→0.12 over z6.2–8, over the #map background #d9cba7, which is itself tan. So at z≥8 the atlas sea outside the wash is already about 88% tan, and the ring barely differs from its surroundings. The ring reads mainly mid-crossfade (about z7.2–7.9: base .46–.22 against wash .4–1.0) as a lighter, tan-tinted sea around the city.

In night theme only .leaflet-tile-pane is inverted. The wash (pCityWash) and plan (pCity) are not, and the map background is #0d1017. So the wash shows as a bright tan disc 1.7·footR across, laid over dark sea and land, at all z≥7.8. That is where it is most noticeable.

4) 'The shoreline seems to jump' overstates it. Nothing moves; the coast fades under a tint as the wash rises.

Confirmed side points:
- Wash tone comes only from tiles/5 (sampleCityMask uses tv('tiles/5/...')), while the war and imperial bases use tiles-war/ and tiles-imperial/. Possible tone mismatch in those eras.
- washMake is in the UG3 pin list (tools/mobile-capture.js atlas_fn_sha: xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask). washUrl is not pinned.

Fix options:
- Mask the wash with the MASKQ water mask so it is land-only. The mask patch spans 2.7·footR, which covers the 1.7·footR wash.
- Or shrink f to about 1.1–1.2. Note the wash exists to bury the magnified printed town label and dot, so shrinking f trades that away.

Either option touches washMake or washUrl and needs a central re-pin plus a filigree slice C call on the seam.

votes.corrected:
The code path is real, but the claim gets the causes, the size and the timing wrong.

Code (maps-site/index.html):
- `buildCityMask` works on the z5 patch from `sampleCityMask`. That patch is 5.4*rW z5 px square; 2 z5 px = 1 atlas px. Each pixel is classified: lum < 110 is ink and counts as no-signal; r-b <= 54 is water; anything else is land.
- `blur(wat);blur(wgt);` is a separable 5-tap box blur (radius 2 z5 px = 1 atlas px). The result is ratio-normalised, `wat/wgt >= 0.5`, and only border-connected water is kept.
- `genCityCanvas`, under `MK=(drawWater&&mask&&mask.water)`, draws the central 4rW z5 px into a 512 stage and thresholds it with `d4.data[p4]>=128?255:0`. It then smooths that to GEN_SIZE 2048, and the single field `wla`/`wAt` feeds the predicate, the fill and the rim.
- The canvas is placed through `cityBox`. The canvas is square, so it spans anchor +/- rW. The mask's source rectangle is also anchor +/- rW, and `MK.ox` is integer-rounded. So the plan and the mask are co-registered.

What actually sets the offset: only the classification. Ink is no-signal, so the 0.5 contour falls somewhere inside the coast stroke.

Measured with a PIL replica of `buildCityMask` on all 16 MK cities (repo z5 tiles):
- Distance from the mask edge to the ink centreline: median 0.3 z5 px (about 0.15 atlas px), p90 0.6, max 0.9 z5 px (about 0.45 atlas px).
- Small systematic bias toward the water side: about 0.1 atlas px.

These steps do not move the boundary:
- The blur. With ratio normalisation and a 0.5 threshold, a straight edge does not shift. The blur only rounds or erases coast features narrower than about 2.5 atlas px (thin spits, small inlets).
- The 512 stage. It is a 5x-16x upsample, and its 0.5 crossing is the mask's pixel edge.
- The 2048 smoothing. It keeps the 0.5 contour in place.
- The 8x `Math.cos(oa2)*3.5` rim. It is 3.5 canvas px, which is 0.03-0.09 atlas px (2048/(2rW) canvas px per atlas px). It is stamped outward on the land side under the fill.

Fires when:
- 16 cities pass MK. Epēshu's canon art supersedes its generated plan, so 15 generated plans are affected.
- 11 are harbours. 4 are non-harbours with a charted sea side and distPx <= 25: Lepon the Old, Rhup, Tarap, Thalbaen.
- Water fraction is 5.9-64%.

Co-visibility with the atlas coast:
- The plan is opaque inside its vignette (r < 0.385*S, after `fillRect` GREEN).
- `washMake` lays about 0.94 alpha land tone under it.
- `baseOpacity` drops to 0.12 by z8.
- Nothing above pCity redraws coast; pWater (618) holds only "Bodies of Water" labels.

So the plan coast and the atlas coast are seen together only in the `overlayOpacity` crossfade (z6.8-7.8), where the offset is 1-4 screen px. It is not "most visible at z>9", where the atlas ghost is covered.

Inland misclassification: confirmed. Many inland villages score 0.85-1.0 "water". But it never reaches a coast, because MK requires drawWater (harbor, or a sea side within distPx <= 25). It changes only `mask.land`/the wash tint, which falls back to LAND_TAN when no land pixels remain. It moves nothing.

Larger defect in the same classifier, not in the claim: the pale glow halo printed around all ink (lum about 250, r-b 36-54) also passes r-b <= 54, so it reads as water. Along a shore, the halo links the settlement ring-dot's interior and halo to the sea, and some label-glyph counters too, so the border-connected filter keeps them as sea.
- Water within 3 atlas px of the anchor: Hordon 49%, Tamaron 49%, Lepon the Old 57%, Sokundo 27%. Penthelon's 17% is probably real lake.
- Nothing in `genCityCanvas` edits `WD`/`wla` after it is built, and `g.drawImage(wla,0,0)` paints water on top. So these plans get a pond or ring about 2-3 atlas px across (roughly 250-450 canvas px) at or beside the city core, since cx,cy is pushed 0.07*S off the sea.
- This is a fidelity defect a table reader would notice. It does not change with zoom or with raster vs vector.

The cheap fix is the classifier, not skeletonising: treat bright, low-saturation pixels (the halo) as no-signal like ink, or require the sea-teal hue, then take the boundary through the no-signal band. `sampleCityMask` is UG3-pinned (cityCanvasSha), so any change needs a deliberate re-pin. Determinism holds: the mask is a pure function of the tiles.

votes.corrected:
MECHANISM (correct in kind): this is a REGISTRATION limit, and it does not depend on raster vs vector. In buildCityMask (maps-site/index.html), pixels with luminance <110 count as no-signal, and a pixel is water when `r-b<=54`. The class field is box-blurred with radius 2 z5 px, i.e. ±1 atlas px (`blur(wat);blur(wgt);`), and water is wherever the water/weight ratio is ≥0.5. So the plan's shoreline lands inside the printed coast stroke. The later stages are negligible. The 512 stage (`d4.data[p4]>=128?255:0`) samples 4rW z5 px into 512, which is 0.05–0.1 atlas px per stage px. The `Math.cos(oa2)*3.5` rim is 3.5 of the 2048 canvas px (GEN_SIZE). One canvas px is 2rW/2048 atlas px, so the whole rim is about 0.03 (village) to 0.09 (capital) atlas px wide. The claim's '0.5–0.75 half ink width' cannot be this rim.

MEASURED MAGNITUDE (Python re-implementation of buildCityMask on the real z5 tiles; offsets along tile rows, so oblique coasts read slightly high). Cities: Tamaron, Sokundo, Kanae (the three UG3 capture cities), Epēshu, Mago, Āglaz.
- The atlas coast stroke is about 4 z5 px (2 atlas px) wide at the median and 6–9 z5 px at p90, so its half-width is about 1 atlas px.
- The mask boundary sits a median 0.5–1.5 z5 px LANDWARD of the stroke centreline. The mean |offset| is 1.1–1.6 z5 px (0.55–0.8 atlas px) and p90 is 2.5–3 z5 px (1.25–1.5 atlas px).
- The bias is systematic. Anti-aliased tan-plus-ink edge pixels with lum ≥110 still pass `r-b<=54` and are classed as water.
- Corrected statement: 'typically 0.5–0.8 atlas px, tail about 1.5 atlas px, biased landward'. The claim's '<=~1 atlas px' bound is exceeded in the tail.

SCREEN PX: 1 atlas px = 2^(z-4) screen px. At z9 that is 32 px, so about 16–26 px typical and ≤48 px tail. The claim's 'z9.885 → 59 px' uses the wrong zoom: 9.885 is cityMaxZ for the CANON Epēshu image (3072 px / 52), which does not use the generated coast. Generated plans reach cityMaxZ = 4+log2(2048/2rW):
- capital 9.30 (≈39 px per atlas px)
- town 10.19 (73 px)
- village 10.83 (114 px)
- ruin 11.0 (128 px)

The harbour towns Tamaron and Sokundo, and the village Kanae, can therefore show about 40–60 px typical and 90–170 px tail at their own max zoom. Visible effect, corrected: the plan's coast rim runs inside the faint (0.12) atlas coast ghost, offset toward land rather than off it.

The inland note is accurate as a misclassification but does not affect registration. An inland city never builds MK (it needs drawWater), so a misread only skews mask.land (the GREEN surround hue) and mask.bear.

CHEAP FIX (corrected): do NOT lean on 'drop blur to radius 1'. Measured, radius 1 trims the mean |offset| only from about 1.5 to about 1.1 z5 px and lets JPEG/glyph noise through. The direct fix is to treat partially inked pixels as no-signal for the WATER class: keep `wgt` at lum ≥110, but set `wat` only when lum ≥~145 and `r-b<=54`. Measured at a 145 cutoff with radius 2 kept, the median offset becomes 0–0.5 z5 px and the mean |offset| 0.9–1.0 z5 px (about 0.5 atlas px) on Tamaron, Kanae and Epēshu; Sokundo's p90 got worse (5 z5 px), so check per city. Skeletonising the stroke to its centreline is the heavier fallback. Order of work: first run the probe (0.5 contour of MASKQ[key].m against the centreline of the lum<110 stroke) in the browser, then decide.

RISKS (corrected):
- buildCityMask is NOT one of the UG3 atlas_fn_sha pins (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask), so editing it alone does not trip a function-source hash.
- It DOES change cityCanvasSha against B0 for certain. The capture plans Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae are all harbour cities with mask coasts, and every invented plan in cityReg is hashed. It also retints mask.land, the GREEN surround of EVERY generated city, so a deliberate re-pin of B0 is required.
- The change is identical on all profiles, so the cross-profile cityCanvasSha equality and desktop/phone parity still hold. It is pure tile math, so determinism holds.
- It must not land while the atlas lane (Mobile 5–9 / MR-A) is mid-flight. Schedule it after MR-A with the re-pin. It also touches the filigree slice C coast look, so coordinate with that track.

The mechanism exists as the claim describes, but it is a mode switch, not a zoom shift. It is a REGISTRATION gap (no transform ties a chart to the atlas), and the rendering medium has nothing to do with it.

What enterChart (maps-site/index.html) does:
- It saves the view (CHART.save), calls map.removeLayer(curBase) and ensureCityOverlay(null), and adds the 'chart-mode' class.
- That class hides the world panes (pRealm, pSettle, pWay, pDistrict and the others) through the '.chart-mode .leaflet-p*-pane{display:none!important}' rules.
- It sets atZoom = def.kind==='tiles' ? def.maxz : 0 and cpx = map.unproject([x,y],atZoom). So for image charts, 1 chart px = 1 CRS unit at z0. For tile charts, 1 chart px = 1 unit at maxz=3. World markers use NZ=4.
- It then calls setMaxBounds(null), setMin/MaxZoom(fillZoomAt(def.h,atZoom), …), setView(cb.getCenter(),minZ,{animate:false}), setMaxBounds(cb) and panInsideBounds. The result is a hard cut with no animation.
- exitChart restores the saved centre and zoom exactly (zoomSnap is set to 0 while it does).
- data/detail-charts.json has no control points or transforms of any kind.

Reachability is narrower than the claim says:
- handleHash and the card's flyCity branch send anchored cities (Epēshu, Summarch) to flyIntoCity. For those two, chart mode is reachable only through ATLAS.chart.
- The card's "View the chart" button appears only for maps_markers entries whose name is a DETAIL key. That means only Far North (marker 1826,-92) and Home Islands (marker 500,2160).
- Rhusagos, Seat and Nīmlad have no marker or gazetteer entry. They are reachable only through #chart=Name or ATLAS.chart.

Correction to "region charts depict atlas geography":
- chart-Home_Islands.jpg (the Trogmunder Lands) shows islands that are not on the atlas at all. Its marker is a pointer at the bottom edge of the atlas.
- chart-Far_North.jpg shows land north of the atlas top edge (its marker is at y=-92).
- Only chart-Rhusagos.jpg overlaps the atlas, and only in its southern part (the Emphoros / Khōrgos / Garnatos / Bībūnor coasts and the lakes). Its northern half also lies above y=0.

So the cheap fix (a registered L.imageOverlay in the world frame) fits only Rhusagos. Even there it needs world bounds that extend above the atlas (negative y beyond TILE_H padding). Far North needs that same off-atlas extension. Home Islands, Seat and Nīmlad cannot be registered and should stay modal.

Chart POIs (cpx) and world POIs (worldPOICoord / buildWorldPOIs proportional through cityBox) agree only because the overlay JPG aspect ratios match the pyramids: 2863x3072 vs 3914x4200, and 3072x2859 vs 4245x3951. (overlay-Epeshu.jpg is 2863 wide, not 3072.) The two sets never show at the same time in the UI.

The fill-zoom figure depends on the viewport. fillZoomAt snaps up to 0.05, so a viewport 800 px tall gives z0.80 for Rhusagos, not z0.78.
votes.reason:
I read enterChart, exitChart, fillZoomAt, handleHash, openPlace, pick, worldPOICoord, the chart-mode CSS and data/detail-charts.json, and looked at the chart JPGs and the z2 atlas tiles.

- The frame redefinition, the hidden world, setView with animate:false and the lack of any registration data are all exactly as claimed.
- It never fires on zoom. It fires only on an explicit mode switch, and never for the two drawn city maps the owner cares about: their UI and hash routes go to flyIntoCity.
- Only two charts (Far North, Home Islands) are reachable from a card. Both depict land off the atlas, so nothing visibly misaligns. The world is hidden, not shifted.
- A reader notices the hard cut, but it is a deliberate modal. It is not a source of the zoom anchoring drift the owner reports.
- The claim overstates which charts show atlas geography, and so how widely the registered-overlay fix applies.

votes.corrected:
MECHANISM: right, and it is a REGISTRATION gap. enterChart (maps-site/index.html) sets `atZoom=def.kind==='tiles'?def.maxz:0`, places the chart at `cpx=map.unproject([x,y],atZoom)` in the world's own CRS units (which overlap the atlas's units, so the frames are simply unrelated), removes curBase, adds 'chart-mode', calls `setMaxBounds(null)`, `setMin/MaxZoom`, `setView(cb.getCenter(),minZ,{animate:false})`. No transform ties a chart to the atlas. Routing is right too: handleHash sends isFlyInCity names to flyIntoCity, and only the remaining DETAIL keys reach enterChart. From data/detail-charts.json those are Seat (building plan), Nīmlad (cosmology), and Far North, Home Islands and Rhusagos (the region charts). The overlay/pyramid agreement does check out: overlay-Epeshu is 2863x3072 and the pyramid 3914x4200, both aspect 0.932.

WHERE THE CLAIM IS WRONG OR OVERSTATED:
(1) This is not a zoom-shift source. It never fires on zoom. It is a hard cut on a click (card button, #chart=, ATLAS.chart). It belongs under zoom-through continuity (the living-chart track), not under the owner's complaint that things shift as you zoom.
(2) The magnitude is off. fillZoomAt returns `ceil((atZoom+log2(vh/h))/0.05)*0.05`, so z0.78 can never come out. For Rhusagos (h=467) on an 800px-tall viewport the result is log2(800/467)=0.777, which rounds up to z0.80. The value depends on the viewport. With a 1280x800 viewport the world tier C is fitZoom 2.22 + 2*(6-2.22)/3 = about z4.74 (TIER_CEIL 6, or 5 on retina). Zoom numbers from the two frames can't be compared, because the world is 1 atlas px = 1 screen px at z4 (NZ=4) and the chart is 1 chart px = 1 screen px at z0. Measured on screen, the scale barely changes: about 2^0.74 = 1.67 screen px per atlas px before the cut, and 2^0.80 = 1.74 screen px per chart px after. The real magnitude is a full replacement of the frame: the position, extent and ground scale are unrelated to the place's atlas footprint, and the ground scale is still unmeasured (probe: fit a transform to 3+ coast features in chart-Rhusagos.jpg against the z5 tiles).
(3) vector_independent=true is correct. A vector region chart shown in its own frame would cut the same way.
(4) The cheap fix is not cheap as written, and not exact. L.imageOverlay takes axis-aligned latLngBounds only. Control points support scale and translation and nothing more. Rotation or an affine fit needs a CSS-transformed custom layer or a CDN plugin such as Leaflet.DistortableImage. A hand-drawn region chart will probably not fit even a similarity transform. The leftover misfit is itself misregistration, and the only fix for it that keeps the atlas authoritative is to warp the art (piecewise/TPS), which is not cheap. Resolution is a second problem: a chart 863-943px wide stretched over a region's atlas extent will look soft at the zooms where it shows.

Corrected fix: for the 3 region charts only, fit a scale+translate box from control points as a first step. Report the residual in atlas px. If the residual is above a few px, either warp the art or keep the modal but animate in from the place's atlas bbox (living track owns that). Keep Seat and Nīmlad as modals.

SAFETY: no UG3 pins are touched, provided the work adds new layers and leaves xmur3/mulberry32/genCityCanvas/washMake/sampleCityMask alone. Seam-washing the new overlays needs a new function, because changing washMake breaks its source-hash pin. Determinism is unaffected (static art and data). Desktop identity changes on purpose (the card/hash path behaves differently), so the change needs owner sign-off. It edits maps-site/index.html while the mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) is mid-flight there, so queue it after that lane. Filigree R7 (nothing at rest) applies to any hover halos on the registered charts.
votes.reason: The mechanism and vector_independent are verified in enterChart, handleHash and detail-charts.json. The quoted magnitude z0.78 cannot be produced by fillZoomAt (it gives 0.80 at an 800px viewport). Comparing z numbers across the two frames is misleading, because on-screen scale barely changes. The effect is a cut on click, not a shift on zoom, so it is outside the owner's zoom-shift complaint. The 'cheap' fix overstates what L.imageOverlay can do (axis-aligned only, no rotation or affine) and leaves out the residual misfit of hand-drawn art and the softness of small images. It is safe on pins and determinism, but it changes desktop behaviour and conflicts with the in-flight mobile lane.

items.summary: Rendering: past z5 the base is a CSS-upscaled z5 ghost (co-registered across levels and eras, 0 px offset) at 0.12 under the wash, so alignment cannot be judged by eye at city zoom and registration has to happen in data.

prior_record.title: The base atlas becomes a blurred ghost past z5, so the authoritative geography cannot be checked at the zooms where the art lives
prior_record.anchor: makeBase `maxNativeZoom:RETINA?deepZoom-1:deepZoom` (z5); baseOpacity(z)
prior_record.mechanism: Working as intended. Past z5.5 the z5 tiles are CSS-scaled with no geometric error; tile levels are co-registered (phase correlation z4 vs downsampled z5 and z3 vs z4: 0.00-0.002 px; all three eras 0.00 px; 4390->4608 padding is right/bottom only so px() matches the tiles). At street zoom each z5 px is huge and the base is at 0.12 under a 0.94-alpha wash, so alignment cannot be judged against the atlas. This is why a vector city alone cannot fix 'things shift': registration must happen in data.
prior_record.fires_when: z>5.5 (tile zoom clamps to 5).
prior_record.visible_effect: A soft parchment ghost under the city with no crisp coast or roads to anchor against.
prior_record.magnitude: One z5 px = 2^(z-5) css px: 7 px at z7.8, 59 at z10.9, 90 at Z_STREET 11.5. Inter-level offset 0.00 px.
prior_record.cheap_fix: None for the shift. Vector atlas features (traced-roads, coast) drawn at deep zoom would give crisp anchors.
prior_record.fix_risks: None.

votes.corrected:
The mechanism holds as described, with a few corrections. makeBase('tiles/',5) sets maxNativeZoom:RETINA?deepZoom-1:deepZoom, maxZoom:Z_STREET and detectRetina:true. In GridLayer._setView, Leaflet 1.9.4 (vendor leaflet.js) takes tileZoom=Math.round(z), and _clampZoom caps it at maxNativeZoom. _setZoomTransform then CSS-scales that level by 2^(z-tileZoom).

(1) When it fires. On a 1x display the z5 imagery is upscaled for every z>5. At 5.5 nothing changes, because round-to-6 is clamped straight back to 5. On HiDPI, detectRetina halves tileSize to 128, adds 1 to zoomOffset, and maxNativeZoom is 4. That means URL z5 is used once z>4, the same imagery at the same scale. Either way one z5 px = 2^(z-5) css px: 7 at z7.8, ~57 at the village ceiling 10.83, 64 at z11.

(2) Z_STREET 11.5 is never reached. worldCityUpdate calls setMaxZoom with cityMaxZ = min(11.5, 4+log2(max(w,h)/(2*FOOT_R))). With GEN_SIZE 2048 that gives: villages 10.83, towns 10.19, ruins 11.0. The 3072 px canon art gives a capital 9.88 and a town 10.78. So the claim's "90 px" magnitude does not occur.

(3) HiDPI case the claim misses. detectRetina also lowers the base layer's own options.maxZoom to Z_STREET-1 = 10.5. GridLayer._pruneTiles calls _removeAllTiles whenever map.getZoom() > options.maxZoom. On HiDPI screens (phones, retina laptops), at the deepest zoom of the 115 villages and 3 ruins (and Summarch if it is a town), there is no ghost at all: the base is gone and only the page background shows. The chart-mode code ('detectRetina drops the tile layer's effective maxZoom by 1 on HiDPI', 'same rule the era bases use') applies this rule to charts, but worldCityUpdate's setMaxZoom(allowed) never applies it to the bases. This moves nothing, but it should be filed as its own claim for the mobile lane.

(4) Where the ghost can be seen. Inside cityBox the base is covered anyway: the city image reaches opacity 1 at z7.8 (overlayOpacity). washMake's radial gradient holds rgba(tone,.94) to colour-stop 0.5 of a 1.7x box (about 0.85x the box half-size), then falls to .5 at 0.78 and 0 at the edge. So the 0.12 base ghost is visible only in the fringe band outside about 0.85x the box, which is exactly where the seam is.

(5) Co-registration, checked with integer-precision phase correlation on the shipped tiles:
- z4 against 2x-downsampled z5, 3 tiles in each of the three eras: 0,0 px.
- z3 against downsampled z4, 3 tiles in each era: 0,0 px.
- Cross-era z5 (modern against war and against imperial), 4 tiles: 0,0 px.
Sub-pixel precision was not measured.

(6) Padding is right/bottom only. In the z5 tiles, content ends at x=8780 (tile 34, px 76) and y=4376, which equals 2x(4390,2188), and the top-left has no offset. So px()/map.unproject at NZ=4 matches the tiles.

Conclusion: the base introduces no geometric shift. It only stops working as a visual reference at the zooms where the city art sits. Registration has to be done in data, for example traced coast and road vectors drawn at deep zoom.
votes.reason: The mechanism exists as claimed and creates no misalignment, so severity is none. makeBase, baseOpacity (1 to 0.12 across z6.2 to z8) and the Leaflet clamp path (_setView with Math.round, then _clampZoom to maxNativeZoom, then a CSS scale transform) all behave as stated, and the tile levels and eras register at 0 px (integer precision). Partly wrong in the claim: it fires at z>5, not z>5.5. The 90 px figure at Z_STREET 11.5 never happens because the highest city ceiling is 11.0 for ruins. The ghost is mostly hidden under the opaque city image and the 0.94 wash, so it shows only in the fringe. It also misses a HiDPI case: detectRetina drops the base layer's maxZoom to 10.5, so past that zoom _pruneTiles removes the whole base layer and there is no ghost at all at village and ruin depths. That case is noticeable but moves nothing, so it belongs in a separate mobile-lane claim.

votes.corrected: Diagnosis is right: there is no geometric error. makeBase sets maxNativeZoom RETINA?4:5 with detectRetina, and baseOpacity/overlayOpacity/washUrl match the claim: base at 0.12 from z8 (about 0.22 at z7.8), wash alpha .94 out to 50% radius. vector_independent=true is also right, because the ghost comes from the base raster no matter what medium the city uses. Magnitude needs correcting. One z5 tile px = 2^(z-5) css px: 7.0 at z7.8, 59.7 (about 60, not 59) at z10.9, 90.5 at Z_STREET 11.5. But the code comment "all three eras carry sharpened z5 (2x LANCZOS + unsharp)" says z5 is a 2x upsample of the 4390x2188 atlas. The real source detail is one atlas px = 2^(z-4) css px: about 14 at z7.8, about 119 at z10.9, about 181 at z11.5. The anchoring evidence is therefore twice as coarse as the claim says. The fires_when threshold also differs on retina: the tile zoom clamps at native 4 (URL z5) above about z4.5, though the css scale of z5 content is the same 2^(z-5). Cheap fix is wrong. data/traced-roads.json is not loaded anywhere (grep traced-roads maps-site/index.html = 0). Per docs/filigree/research/q04.json and q07.json, its 46 chains are mostly mis-traces of lettering and islets that lie off the printed dotted roads (polyline #33 runs along the Mago/Tamaron label rows, with a median distance of 24 px to a road dot). Drawing it at deep zoom would give false anchors that disagree with the authoritative atlas. Corrected fix: there is no cheap fix. Crisp deep-zoom anchors need vector features re-traced from the print: dotted road dots, solid-line rivers, and the coastline from the land/water mask. That work is the planned "Traced road network" item, validated by distance-to-printed-dot. The city art is then registered to those anchors in data, bending the art to the atlas. Risks: a new deep-zoom vector layer leaves the UG3-pinned functions (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask) and cityCanvasSha unchanged only if it is added as a separate pane/layer and the wash and mask code is not edited. It still changes desktop rendering at z>6, which the mobile-review desktop-identity lens and the mid-flight atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) in maps-site/index.html will see. It also overlaps filigree ownership of road ink (the road_rust coast-road rule in density-bible) and R7 (nothing at rest). So it must be sequenced after the mobile atlas lane and routed through filigree slice B, not landed as a quick patch.
votes.reason: The mechanism (no inter-level offset, CSS-scaled ghost under a .94 wash) and vector_independent=true check out against makeBase, baseOpacity and washUrl. The magnitude counts z5 tile px, but z5 is a 2x LANCZOS upsample, so true atlas detail is 2^(z-4) css px (about 181 at Z_STREET, not 90). 59 should read about 60. The proposed fix leans on traced-roads.json, which is unloaded and shown by filigree research to be mostly label mis-traces lying off the printed roads. "Fix risks: none" ignores desktop identity, the mid-flight mobile atlas lane, and filigree ownership of road ink.

items.summary: Lifecycle: flyIntoCity's eager ensureCityOverlay(key) removes the current city's art, wash, stubs and POIs in one frame before the fly starts, leaving the 0.12 base while the fly stays above z7.8.

prior_record.title: Descending into a city drops the current city's art at the start of the flight
prior_record.anchor: flyIntoCity: `ensureCityOverlay(key); // eager: fades in DURING the descent`
prior_record.mechanism: Layer lifecycle. ensureCityOverlay removes CITYVIEW's overlay, wash, stubs and POIs synchronously before the fly; starting from deep inside another city the reader is left with the 0.12 base ghost until the arc rises above z8, while the new overlay is placed at the destination from the first frame at overlayOpacity(z).
prior_record.fires_when: flyIntoCity from z>6.8 inside another city (search, chart link, Descend).
prior_record.visible_effect: The current town vanishes before the camera moves.
prior_record.magnitude: Art opacity 1 to 0 in one frame; blank lasts while the flyTo arc stays above z7.8 (part of 1.4 s).
prior_record.cheap_fix: Keep the old overlay until the fly's zoom drops below 6.8 (overlayOpacity 0), then swap; or allow two live overlays and fade both by distance.
prior_record.fix_risks: Not pinned. Memory on mobile (2 overlays).

votes.corrected:
Confirmed, with two wording fixes and one addition. In maps-site/index.html, flyIntoCity calls ensureCityOverlay(key) ("// eager: fades in DURING the descent") synchronously. The fly itself starts one frame later inside requestAnimationFrame(function(){map.flyTo(dest,target,{duration:1.4,easeLinearity:.25})}). When CITYVIEW.name is a different city, ensureCityOverlay calls map.removeLayer on CITYVIEW.overlay, poiLayer, wash and stubs straight away; nothing fades them out. The early return `if(CITYVIEW.name===key)return;` means it only fires when you descend into a different city. It then adds the destination overlay through cityBox at ov.setOpacity(overlayOpacity(map.getZoom())), which is 1 at z>=7.8, plus a new wash. Both sit at the destination, off screen. At the start zoom (z>=8) baseOpacity is 0.12. So for at least one frame before the camera moves, the reader sees only the 12% base over the #map background #d9cba7 (night: #0d1017) and the vector panes. The art, wash, stubs and numbered POI markers are gone.

Wording fix 1: the base ghost does not end when the arc "rises above z8". It lifts as zoom FALLS below 8: worldOpacityUpdate rides the per-frame 'zoom' event and baseOpacity ramps from 0.12 at z8 to 1 at z6.2. How long the gap lasts depends on how far the van Wijk arc zooms out, which grows with distance. On long hops the dip happens early in the 1.4 s. On short hops between neighbouring cities, or when the arc stays above about z8, the ghost lasts the whole flight, until the new overlay pans in already at full opacity.

Wording fix 2: the old art's opacity drops from overlayOpacity(z) (1 at z>=7.8, partial between 6.8 and 7.8) to 0 in a single frame.

Addition: if the destination's mask has not been sampled yet, ensureCityGen's async sampleCityMask callback can land during the fly. It calls registerCityOverlay, which hot-swaps the destination overlay, and then worldCityUpdate() from a mid-flight centre. That can call ensureCityOverlay for the old or nearest city, or null, and setMaxZoom. This breaks the "never mid-fly" assumption stated in the comment on map.on('zoomend moveend',worldCityUpdate).

Triggers: the Descend button (data-descend), a #chart=City hash or link through handleHash/isFlyInCity, and ANNALS.descend, whenever another city is active at z>6.5 (art visible from z>6.8). This is about the order the layers are added and removed, not about registration, so it is independent of the rendering medium: a vector city swapped the same way vanishes the same way.
votes.reason: I read ensureCityOverlay, flyIntoCity, worldOpacityUpdate/worldCityUpdate, baseOpacity/overlayOpacity and the event bindings (zoom/zoomend/moveend). The old overlay, wash, stubs and POIs are removed synchronously before flyTo starts in the rAF. At z>=8 the base sits at 0.12, so the drawn town disappears in one frame before the camera moves. Anyone at the table would notice that. The claim's mechanism and trigger are right. Its phrase "until the arc rises above z8" is backwards: the base recovers as zoom drops below 8. On short hops the blank can last the whole flight. Separately, an async mask callback can call worldCityUpdate mid-fly.

votes.corrected:
MECHANISM (correct): this is a layer-lifecycle problem. It is not REGISTRATION and not the rendering MEDIUM. In flyIntoCity, `ensureCityOverlay(key); // eager: fades in DURING the descent` synchronously removes CITYVIEW's overlay, wash, stubs and POIs. The map.flyTo itself starts one rAF later. So the current town's art, wash, road stubs and POI markers go from full opacity to 0 in a single frame, before the camera moves. Nothing is misplaced, so this is not a source of the owner's "things shift". It is a disappearing-art flash, and vector_independent=true is right: a vector city held in the same single CITYVIEW slot vanishes the same way.

MAGNITUDE (corrected): the claim uses the wrong ramp. What the reader sees where the old town was is the base at baseOpacity(z): 0.12 for z>=8, rising back toward 1 only as z drops to 6.2. The overlayOpacity threshold of 7.8 does not matter here. The claim also has the direction backwards: the ghost lasts WHILE the arc stays at or above z8, and eases only as the arc dips below z8.

I recomputed Leaflet's flyTo arc (rho 1.42, duration 1.4 s, easeOut) for a 1366x768 viewport. Start z = 9.88, Epēshu's cityMaxZ (4+log2(3072/52)). Target 10.5 (GEN_SIZE 2048 with ruin r=8 gives cz=11, and the target is cz-0.5). Results:
- Epēshu to Lepon the Old (90 world px): the arc bottoms out at about z7.9 and stays at or above z8 for about 80% of the flight (about 1.1 s).
- 24-px neighbours (Lendānak–Phumkha): the arc never drops below about z9.4, so the ghost lasts the whole 1.4 s.
- Only long flights (about 400 px) dip below 6.2 mid-arc and get the base back.
So "part of 1.4 s" understates the common case. In practice it is roughly 1.1 to 1.4 s of a 0.12 ghost from frame 0.

FIX (corrected): variant A, "keep the old overlay until zoom < 6.8, then swap", fails on neighbour hops because the arc never crosses 6.8. No swap would happen mid-flight. The new chart would then pop in at opacity 1 when worldCityUpdate or ensureArrival runs at zoomend/moveend, which also defeats the eager fade-in.

Use the two-slot variant instead:
- Add a CITYVIEW "leaving" slot that holds the old overlay, wash and stubs. Remove its POIs at once.
- ensureCityOverlay moves the current slot into the leaving slot instead of removing it.
- worldOpacityUpdate drives both slots with overlayOpacity(z) on the existing 'zoom' events.
- Release the leaving slot on the fly's moveend, or when it leaves map bounds.
- The registerCityOverlay hot-swap (the CITYVIEW.name===key branch) must not clear the leaving slot.
- lruPut eviction removes layers it owns, so the leaving overlay must stay in the cache's recent half. It will, at size 6.

SAFETY:
- It edits none of xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask. Calling washMake is fine, so the UG3 atlas_fn_sha pins and cityCanvasSha hold.
- It adds no clock token. maps-site/index.html must stay at 1 narrow / 2 wide, so the fade can be driven only by zoom events, with no Date.now, performance.now, requestIdleCallback or timer.
- It touches no gen code, so determinism is unaffected.
- It changes desktop behaviour on purpose. It therefore cannot go inside a Mobile 5-9 unit, where the desktop-identity check would fail it, and must land in maps-site/index.html after that lane finishes.
- Memory risk is minor but real. The old image stays in the LRU either way, but keeping it attached keeps its decoded bitmap alive: about 35 MB for a roughly 3072² canon chart. That lasts only about 1.4 s, bounded by moveend.
votes.reason:
The visible effect is confirmed from source. In flyIntoCity, ensureCityOverlay(key) synchronously removes the old overlay, wash, stubs and POIs before the fly, which is kicked off one requestAnimationFrame later. vector_independent=true is right: this is layer lifecycle, not registration or medium, and it is not a shift at all, because the art vanishes rather than moves.

The magnitude is wrong. The blank is governed by baseOpacity (0.12 at z>=8, back to 1 at 6.2), not by overlayOpacity's 7.8. The claim's "until the arc rises above z8" has the direction inverted. My recomputed flyTo arcs show that a common neighbour hop (Epēshu to Lepon the Old, 90 px, z9.88 to 10.5) never goes below about z7.9 and spends about 80% of the 1.4 s at z>=8. The 24-px neighbours never go below about z9.4. So the ghost covers about 1.1 to 1.4 s, not "part of" the flight.

The first cheap fix is broken. Neighbour arcs never reach z6.8, so the swap would wait until moveend and then pop the new chart in at full opacity. The two-slot variant is the correct fix. It is safe for the UG3 pins and determinism if it is zoom-event driven with no new clock tokens. It must be sequenced after the Mobile 5-9 lane because it changes desktop behaviour. The memory risk is minor and bounded to the flight.

summaries.5-ownership: 122 of 138 anchors match a marker (121 by name, Lepon the Old by an alias the probe supplied), 40 pairs are more than 3 px apart, mostly anchors on label letters; the fix is an offline deterministic derivation with explicit overrides, not a runtime marker-wins rule, and moving the anchor fixes only the centre.

prior_record.claim: maps_markers.json (by fold(name)) matches 122 of the 138 anchors (136 in city-anchors.json plus the Summarch and Penthelon literals in meshedWorldInit). 82 of those sit within 3 px and 39 are more than 3 px apart. A 40th pair is Lepon the Old ↔ marker "Lepon" (alias match, 7.0 px). The other 16 anchors have no marker: they are the Leponnia sim towns, whose gazetteer coordinates are copied from the anchors. votes.corrected:
This is REGISTRATION, not medium. cityBox centres every footprint on CITY_ANCHORS[key], so a stale anchor misregisters a raster overlay and a vector plan by the same amount. Moving the anchor fixes only the centre. Scale and orientation of DM art inside cityBox remain unregistered. Two parts of the proposal need correcting.

(1) Do not resolve at runtime and do not apply a blanket marker-wins rule. Put the derivation in an offline deterministic tool that regenerates maps-site/data/city-anchors.json, the same pattern as tools/build-gazetteer.js, and then regenerate gazetteer.json. Markers and anchors already arrive in the same Promise.all, so runtime resolution would work technically. It would still silently rewrite canon geometry each time maps_markers changes, and it would fork the anchors from the gazetteer, which copies them.

(2) The tool must carry an explicit exception table, not just an offDot override:
- Drāmūz: the anchor is on the printed ◉ and the marker is wrong. Fix the marker; do not move the anchor.
- Penthelon: the meshedWorldInit literal is deliberately off the marker (the "wiki marker floats in the lake" comment).
- Paga and Penthelon: owner calls.

For every anchor that moves, the tool must also:
- Re-derive the anchor-relative fields (sea.side and sea.distPx, the harbor flag, the city-traits sea entry). The colour test is unreliable for 19 of the rows (region tint reads as water), so a human must confirm those.
- Move the polyline vertices that sit on the old anchors in the same edit: Summarch's party-route endpoint, and the "Road that Walks with the Sun" vertices at Drāmūz, Tamaron and Lepon the Old. Otherwise the roads detach from their towns.

Moving Tamaron changes cityCanvasSha, which hashes Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae. That breaks UG3 against B0 while the Mobile atlas lane (5-9) is mid-flight. The change must be scheduled centrally with a B0 rebaseline, not slipped into a lane. The 16 Leponnia sim towns have no marker and stay as they are. The net effect is a reviewed, generated edit of about 37 anchors plus their dependent data, not "one derivation replaces 39 hand edits".

The anchor-correction-table caveat is right that the buildCityMask colour test cannot separate gulf water from olive/grey region tint. The test is luma>=110 for weight and r-b<=54 for water; the tint reads r-b≈46-48 and gulf water ≈47. So for these 19 pairs, any number derived from sampleCityMask or buildCityMask describes tint, not coast. That covers land_frac, frac, water, bear, the living_sea_mask_rule approximation and any future tools/living-sea-mask.js. Correcting the anchors does not fix this; only a better water test does. In genCityCanvas, the mask can only shape the plan through `drawWater = !!sv && (t.harbor || distPx<=25)` and `MK=(drawWater&&mask&&mask.water)?mask:null`. Eighteen of the 19 are non-harbor in city-anchors.json, have sea:null and have no sea in city-traits.json, so sv is null, drawWater is false and MK is null. Their plans draw no coast at all, true or false. For them, the faulty mask leaks only into colour: mask.land, the average of the few pixels that read as land, which feeds LT/GREEN, and the sampled wash hue. Hemdok Laego therefore shows a landlocked plan, and "mask-true" in POLISH.md is a hollow claim, not a drawn sea. The one exception is Penthelon.
