At the marker it would read 98% water, so moving it with the test unchanged floods the plan; that matches the owner-call verdict in the table. The actionable points: (1) do not build gates or re-anchor checks on this colour test for these cities; (2) for Penthelon, and for any future town given harbor or sea data, the test must be fixed first. Possible fixes are a separate, tint-independent water source or a hue/saturation test calibrated against the region tints. Changing genCityCanvas or buildCityMask also changes the source hashes pinned by mobile UG3 (atlas_fn_sha) and cityCanvasSha, so it must be coordinated with the Mobile 5-9 atlas lane. The approach polylines in buildApprPolys (party-route.json legs plus named-ways.json pts, all classed 'land') drive the gates and road stubs of procedural cities, so any anchor that moves needs its nearby polyline points checked again. That applies only to anchors that actually move. Drāmūz is marked 'keep' (its anchor is already on the printed ◉), so its Sun Road vertex at 0.2 px is correct and not stale. The stale cases are Tamaron (anchor about 8 px N of the ◉) and Lepon the Old (about 7 px N of the ring) on the Sun Road, plus Summarch on the party route. (2) Do not snap polylines to anchors by name. The atlas is authoritative, so the Sun Road vertices (prov 'trace', 'Trace approximate') should be traced again onto the printed dotted road where it reaches the ◉. That is registration to the atlas, and the corrected anchor and the road then agree because both sit on the printed feature, not because one copies the other. The party route is a narrative path, not a road. Its second 'Summarch' point at (545,80) is offset on purpose ('offset from prior visit for clarity'), so it must stay offset. Only the first Summarch endpoint (523,58), which equals the meshedWorldInit literal, needs a decision. (3) Summarch's anchor is a source literal in meshedWorldInit (CITY_ANCHORS['Summarch']={atlasX:523,...}), not an entry in city-anchors.json, so a fix driven by the JSON misses it. For the procedural cities that move (Tamaron, Lepon the Old), the anchor and the approach polylines feed genCityCanvas through sampleCityMask and buildCityStubs, so cityCanvasSha will change for every profile. The fix must be coordinated with the mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) and re-baselined, not dropped in mid-flight. (4) The canon point stands. The Summarch (and Epēshu) charts are placed by cityBox around the anchor centre, so moving that centre to the ◉ does not register the DM chart. It needs control-point registration: chart ◉, gates and coast matched to the atlas, with the art bent to the atlas. A vector redraw placed through the same cityBox misaligns just as much (registration problem, not medium).
votes.reason: I checked the claim against the HEAD export. In party-route.json the Summarch entries are (523,58) and (545,80); the second note reads 'offset from prior visit for clarity'. meshedWorldInit hard-codes Summarch at {atlasX:523,atlasY:58}, and its canon overlay is registered through registerCityOverlay → cityBox, which centres the box on the anchor. buildApprPolys turns route legs and named-way pts into 'land' approach polylines, so polyline points that drift from an anchor do affect procedural gates and stubs. That makes the main thesis and the registration-versus-medium point correct. The claim overstates one case: in anchor-correction-table.json Drāmūz's verdict is 'keep (anchor is on the ◉)', so its vertex at 0.2 px is correct, not stale. It also proposes a by-name, same-source fix. That would wrongly collapse a deliberate narrative offset on the party route and ties roads to anchors, when both should be traced to the authoritative printed atlas features. It also leaves out two side effects: Summarch is a source literal rather than JSON data, and moving the procedural anchors changes the pinned cityCanvasSha, which collides with the mobile atlas lane now in flight.

votes.corrected: All four quotes exist verbatim (CHANGELOG 0.9.2 line 155; POLISH 'Census follow-ups'; CHANGELOG 0.9.11; docs/filigree/README.md R21), and the core facts hold. Penthelon's off-dot reason is recorded only in CHANGELOG 0.9.7, POLISH 'Lake biome' and a code comment at CITY_ANCHORS['Penthelon'] in maps-site/index.html, which says the wiki marker floats in the lake. It is not in city-anchors.json. Its anchor (1962,644) is about 112 px from the marker (1942,755), and 0.9.12 later snapped that marker to the printed double-ring, so the comment is plausibly stale. I could not check C3. Clickerhall: CHANGELOG 0.9.2 and POLISH say only 'snapped (40px) to its true printed dot' and do not say which record moved. In city-anchors.json the anchor (2577,255) sits 32.9 px from the maps_markers.json marker (2608,266). A z5 tile crop shows the anchor on the 'G' of the label 'Goblin' and the marker on the ring-dot, so the snap evidently reached the marker only (an inference). The anchor was created in 0.8.4. Hordon: the 0.8.4 anchor is 42.7 px from its marker (1124,1690), and its coordinates (1139,1730) are identical to the Maeges anchor, which is 1 px from the Maeges marker (1139,1731). R21 lists 'Hordon/Maeges anchor' as a data item. No CHANGELOG or POLISH line mentions Maeges. Narrower than the claim: 0.9.11 audited and snapped markers, 121 in total, with Hordon's double-ring measured by hand. 0.9.12 snapped five capital markers (Epēshu, Summarch, Penthelon, Hordon, Cyrikon). So these entries do not say that only Hordon's marker moved, and they never mention anchors. The count of 'other 33 far cities' is not reproducible. In city-anchors.json, 37 anchors lie more than 3 px from their Settlements marker, which is 34 once Drāmūz, Hordon and Clickerhall are removed; the count stays 37 at 5 px, and Penthelon is not in the file. Word-boundary search finds entries for Tamaron, Ion Ephel, Hemdok Laego and Cyrikon, but none gives a reason for an off-dot anchor, and the rest have no entry. Anchors carry a prov field: 32 of the 37 are prov 'trace' (the 0.9.0 census transcription, which treats the dots as the target). Their drift is therefore unexplained, not justified. 'An offDot field would carry exactly two entries' overreaches: it would hold Drāmūz (R21 marker-wrong, anchor 36.3 px from marker) and Penthelon (owner decision), and at least Hordon and Clickerhall would be unjustified drifts to fix. The lint would flag them along with about 30 more.
votes.reason: The four quotes are present and the Clickerhall, Hordon/Maeges and Penthelon facts check out against city-anchors.json, maps_markers.json, the index.html override and a tile crop. Three parts overreach. 0.9.11 and 0.9.12 snapped many markers, not 'only the Hordon marker'. '33 far cities' does not match the data: 37 anchors lie beyond 3 px, or 34 after removing Drāmūz, Hordon and Clickerhall. 'Exactly two offDot entries' leaves out Hordon and Clickerhall, which are unjustified off-dot anchors. Penthelon's override lives in index.html, not in city-anchors.json, and C3 could not be checked here.

votes.corrected: An offDot field cannot start with "exactly two entries", and a 3 px anchor-to-marker lint would fail at once. At HEAD, maps-site/data/city-anchors.json has no Penthelon key at all: Penthelon exists only in maps_markers.json, city-traits.json and location-art.json. So a Penthelon "owner decision" entry would point at an anchor that does not exist, which fits C3's finding that its reason is stale. Of the 136 anchors, 38 that have a same-name marker sit more than 3 px from it, among them Hordon 42.7 px, Clickerhall-by-Goblin-Hole 32.9, Drāmūz 36.3, Damoklir 69.1, Paga 68.6, Pontoron 67.5, Zhomphek 64.5, Philider 58.0 and Ion Ephel 31.3. Two of these are anchor errors, not reasons to sit off the dot. Hordon's anchor (1139,1730) duplicates Maeges' anchor exactly, while the Hordon marker sits on its glyph at (1124,1690). Clickerhall's anchor sits on the label, and its marker is on the ○. Both should be fixed as data items under R21, not exempted. Only Drāmūz is a documented case where the marker is wrong (R21: "marker 35 px off"). The sequence is therefore: (1) list every pair more than 3 px apart and classify each one as anchor-wrong (fix the anchor), marker-wrong (fix maps_markers, since the atlas glyph decides) or a justified exception; (2) give offDot only to the documented exceptions, which today is likely just Drāmūz until its marker is fixed; (3) only then make the 3 px lint blocking. Every fix moves art toward the printed atlas dot, never the atlas toward the art. Note that moving an anchor moves cityBox and the sampleCityMask inputs, which changes cityCanvasSha for that city. The Mobile track pins that hash, so anchor fixes must be coordinated with Mobile 5-9 and the filigree R21 queue. This is registration work. It does not depend on raster versus vector.
votes.reason: I checked the head export. The claim's history is mostly right: Penthelon's 0.9.7 reason is stale, Clickerhall moved 40 px only in maps_markers and its anchor is still 32.9 px off, and the Hordon anchor duplicates Maeges at (1139,1730) while the Hordon marker is on its glyph at (1124,1690). But applies_to_us draws the wrong conclusion. Penthelon has no entry in city-anchors.json, so it cannot carry offDot. Hordon and Clickerhall are anchor errors, not exceptions. Computed over city-anchors.json against same-name maps_markers, 38 anchors sit more than 3 px off their marker, several by 50–69 px. So a field with two entries plus a 3 px lint would flag about 37 cities on its first run, and two of the cities it relies on are the wrong kind of case. Acting on it as written would either fail the lint immediately or tempt someone to label real misregistrations as off-dot. That hides exactly the misalignment the owner is asking about. The field and the lint are worth having, but only after the pairs are triaged and the anchor fixes are coordinated with the cityCanvasSha pin.

votes.corrected: Every number in the claim matches out/three-coasts-epeshu.json, and the code quotes are real. The DEM decode is at index.html decodeEpeshuHF, the sea level at index.html `const SEA_Y = 0;`, and the mask rule at maps-site/index.html buildCityMask. The screen-px figures are consistent with atlas px * 2^(z-4). The window-wide "effectively one coast" framing does not hold. The window figures are one-directional (DEM coast to nearest print coast): rms 1.33, p50 1.03, p95 2.31, max 6.79 atlas px, which is 13 / 79 / 241 screen px rms and 67 / 401 / 1229 max at z7.3 / 9.885 / 11.5. The same JSON gives print_to_dem rms 92.87 and max 356 in the raw window. In the islet-filtered window_mainland, dem_to_print is rms 8.39 and max 54.44 at the islet group (1319,1391), and print_to_dem max is 20.32 at (1140,1740), a headland the DEM simplifies. The JSON attributes these to sea lettering, islets and the filter, but they are not shown to be zero. The narrowest supported claim: DEM-to-print agrees to about 1.3 rms (one DEM cell) over the window, with outliers from islets and print lettering. Near Epēshu (within 60 px) it is rms 1.51 and max 5.07 raw, and that max sits on an islet NNE at (1274.6,1374.5). With islets under 400 px² filled, the symmetric mainland figures are rms 1.50 and max 5.43 at (1220.75,1447.5). So the print mask and DEM are one coast to about 1.5 atlas px around Epēshu. The window-wide statement needs the one-directional qualifier and the islet/headland outliers. "Needs no reconciliation shift" is fair only near Epēshu: the best rigid shift is 1.7-1.8 px SSE, which lowers the r60 mainland sym rms from 1.50 to 1.02, and the JSON itself rules the offset "None worth correcting".
votes.reason: Figures and code quotes verify, but "one coast over the whole window" rests on the one-directional dem_to_print (n 6452). The same JSON shows window print_to_dem rms 92.87 / max 356, and, after islet filtering, window_mainland dem_to_print rms 8.39 / max 54.44 and print_to_dem max 20.3 at a SW headland. The JSON explains these as artefacts, but the claim should be limited to direction, islet filtering and the near-Epēshu mainland.

votes.corrected:
The registration target and the seam clip can be the print mask, which is what buildCityMask/sampleCityMask already produce from the z5 tiles. That keeps atlas geography authoritative. The DEM's 0 m contour agrees with it to about 1.3 DEM cells (1 cell = 800/768 = 1.04 atlas px; dem-to-print rms 1.33), so the atlas does not need a DEM-versus-print reconciliation shift. Registration bends the DM chart to the print. Neither the print nor the DEM is moved. This is a registration fact and does not depend on the medium.

Caveats:
(1) The residual is atlas-scale small, not zero. There is a systematic ~1.7 px SSE offset near Epēshu: best_translation reduces the sym rms from 1.50 to 1.02. That is ~240-310 screen px at Z_STREET 11.5. The living-chart H2z handoff from the print/chart coast to the sim's DEM coast should therefore cross-fade rather than assume the two coincide. If a nudge is wanted, it belongs on the sim side and never on the atlas side.
(2) The print mask must be used with its speck, lettering-hole and islet filtering (print-to-DEM rms 92.9 comes from sea lettering and islets). The measurements come from a PIL/numpy port of the mask, not from a browser decode.
(3) The DEM measured is the raw EPESHU_HF decode, not the W.H that genHydrology carves.
(4) Do not change buildCityMask/sampleCityMask to serve as the clip, because they are hash-pinned by Mobile UG3. Consume their output instead.
votes.reason:
The numbers match out/three-coasts-epeshu.json:
- Window dem_to_print: rms 1.33, p50 1.03, p95 2.31, max 6.79.
- r60_raw: rms 1.51, max 5.07 at (1274.58, 1374.46).
- r60_mainland: sym_rms 1.5, sym_max 5.43 at (1220.75, 1447.5).
- The screen factors are 9.85, 59.1 and 181, so 1.33 atlas px ≈ 13 / 79 / 241 screen px.

The buildCityMask quote is real. The JSON's patch_check shows that the port matches sampleCityMask's exact Epēshu patch on 99.79% of pixels.

The conclusion that print and DEM are one coast and the print is the target fits the hard rule that atlas geography is authoritative. It is also medium-independent, as the claim states. So applies_to_us mostly holds.

Two parts are overstated, and both bear on the street handoff:
- "No reconciliation shift" hides a measurable systematic offset of ~1.7 px SSE (sym rms 1.50 → 1.02 after translation), which is ~300 screen px at z11.5. That matters for H2z and the street track even though it is negligible at atlas zooms.
- The print mask is only usable with the islet and lettering filtering. Without it, print-to-DEM rms is 92.9.

Further limits: the DEM measured is the raw decode, not the carved W.H, and the mask comes from a PIL/numpy port rather than the browser. Any use of the mask as a clip must consume sampleCityMask's output without editing the hash-pinned functions.

votes.corrected:
The numbers are correct and the two-sided reading is right. Under today's cityBox the chart has 666.5 px² of land over atlas sea and 0 px² of sea over atlas land. At 0.6x+3E it is 91.1/75.3, at 0.6x+8E 39.3/106.8, at 0.8x+3E 212.4/34.6 and at 1.0x+3E 547.2/6.6. The dossier's "7-13%" covers only the land-over-sea fractions.

Practical consequences for us:
(1) A clip of the chart against the print water mask removes only land over sea. This is the buildCityMask/sampleCityMask port, and the registration target stays the atlas.
(2) Sea over land is a band where the atlas shows land but the chart shows its own water. Making the chart water transparent there is not enough. At the depths where this matters, baseOpacity is 0.12 (z>=8), so a keyed-out band would show a faint ghost, not land. That band needs a land fill: either the chart's olive countryside RGB(102,119,85) painted into keyed water that the print mask calls land, or the base kept at full opacity under the city footprint. Filling it with "atlas sea" would be wrong, because it is atlas land. The rule is: where the print mask says sea, show sea; where it says land, show land; ignore the chart's own coast.
(3) The fill colour is not as easy to key as it sounds. overlay-Epeshu.jpg is a JPG with no alpha, and only 15.5% of its pixels exactly match RGB(119,153,136). The probe needed a tolerance (L1 distance under 36, closer to the fill than to the olive), a morphological opening and hole filling. So the key must be a tolerant, deterministic canvas pass run once when the overlay is generated, or a pre-keyed PNG/WebP asset. It must not run every frame. It must stay outside the pinned functions (genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask), or cityCanvasSha and UG3 hashes will change mid-lane.
(4) Seam handling deals with leftover error. It does not replace a better fit. Both error signs are what a translate+scale fit leaves behind, and a fitted warp should shrink them before any clip or key.
The modal chart pyramid (enterChart) does not blend with the atlas base, so it does not have this seam.
votes.reason:
I checked the figures against out/three-coasts-epeshu.json (dm_art_placements.*.seam_vs_print_atlas_px2) and they match. The dossier sentence "In 7-13% of placements the art lands over atlas sea" uses land-over-sea fractions only (0.072 to 0.132), so the claim that it counted one direction is correct. The applies_to_us text is right that clipping against atlas water cannot fix sea over land, but its fix is incomplete and partly wrong.

In maps-site/index.html, baseOpacity returns 0.12 for z>=8. A transparent key would therefore expose a faded base, not land, in exactly the band where the atlas is land. "Replaced by atlas sea" puts sea where the atlas has land.

The key is also not simple. The art is a JPG with no alpha channel, and the probe's water class needed a tolerance and an opening, not an exact colour match. Any keying must also avoid the source-hash pins of the mobile atlas lane, which is mid-flight.

The direction holds: registration to the atlas comes first, then the seam is handled on both signs from the print mask. The adjustment is minor.

votes.reason: The numbers match out/three-coasts-epeshu.json (verdicts.street_handoff, dm_art_placements scale0.6_E3 and today_cityBox, dem_vs_print.window_raw). 3.57/6.84 and 6.88/18.84 are in the file. 646/1238 and 1245/3410 screen px are the file's z11.5 figures (factor 181.019). 1.33 rms x 181 = 241 px. Four problems. (1) "Registration of the chart cannot remove" contradicts the file's own wording ("only fitting the chart, or cross-fading ... does") and its dm_art_free_fit_context, where a free fit leaves the chart 1.51 rms from the DEM. That free fit sits on the search-range edge (s=0.5, dy +9). Only a policy-constrained fit is stuck near 3.6 rms. (2) "Best policy fit" is the best of six hand-picked placements (0.6/0.8/1.0 x +3E/+8E), not an optimised policy fit. The file says coast chamfer "cannot pick the policy scale". (3) The second cited quote, the genHydrology waterMask comment "1 river, 2 lake, 3 sea", is only a code legend. It does not support "the sim shows the DEM coast at SEA_Y 0". The supporting code is the later line `if(W.H[i] < SEA_Y) W.waterMask[i] = 3` with `const SEA_Y = 0`. That line reads the carved W.H, which is the very thing the figures do not model. (4) "The jump is the chart's own shape against the atlas" holds only for the chart-to-DEM residual. Any H2z handoff error is untested and would add to it. The file flags this, and the claim carries it only as a caveat.

votes.corrected: The chart coast and the sim's DEM coast really do disagree. At the best policy fit (0.6x+3E) they differ by 3.57 rms / 6.84 max atlas px, and today by 6.88 / 18.84. The DEM matches the print to 1.33 rms, so the residual is the chart's own shape, and no change of medium removes it. As H2z is specified, though, this does not show up as a "coast jump of several hundred screen px at z11.5". Two reasons. (1) Over Epēshu the atlas zoom is capped at cityMaxZ = 9.885 (setMaxZoom(cityMaxZ); 11.5 is never reached there), so any crossfade happens at 59x or less: 211 / 404 screen px at the best fit, and 406 / 1113 today. (2) The H2z target is a Street frozen-view poster (SV1-SV9 are perspective cameras via ANNALS.goto with a radius R), not a plan view registered to the atlas. The crossfade is a change of scene, and there is no coast-to-coast correspondence to jump. The handoff only becomes a measurable jump if the living track makes it a plan-registered continuity (an H1 spike, or a top-down poster placed by the S1 formula). Action: record this as a constraint on the living track's H2z/H2 unit (owner-gated, after Street 3/4). If the handoff is made plan-continuous, it should first dissolve the chart to the base tiles / print-mask coast (atlas authoritative; the DEM agrees within 1.3 px), and only then show the sim render. It must also verify the S1 atlas-to-sim transform and genHydrology's carved W.H, not the raw DEM. Change nothing in maps-site now. The real fix for the chart coast stays its registration (the fit plus a seam clip of both signs).
votes.reason: The measured residual holds: out/three-coasts-epeshu.json gives dem_vs_print 1.33 rms, and the chart is the outlier. Two things do not transfer. (a) The z11.5 screen-px magnitudes. The same file's method.screen_px notes that Epēshu's deepest atlas zoom is cityMaxZ 9.885 (maps-site/index.html cityMaxZ: Math.min(Z_STREET, NZ+log2(mx/(2*r))), so 11.5 is reached only at the handoff and not on the atlas. (b) The "jump" framing. docs/living/research-dossier.md section 5 defines H2z as a crossfade of the city overlay into the Street frozen-view poster, and docs/street/README.md section 5.1 shows those posters are perspective camera views (goto x,z,R). A perspective poster has no registered coast to jump against. The recommendation is directionally right: if a plan-continuous handoff is ever built, it should hand over on the atlas/print coast, which the DEM matches. That is consistent with "atlas authoritative" and with determinism. But H2z belongs to the living track and is owner-gated behind Street 3/4, and the S1 transform and the carved W.H are still unverified. So this is a design note for that unit, not an action for the atlas, and the "several hundred screen px every zoom-through" consequence is overstated.

votes.corrected: Both quotes exist verbatim in maps-site/index.html (cityMaxZ at its definition; "var Z_STREET=11.5, Z_OPEN_MAX=8.0, Z_TIER_D=7.5;"). Narrowest supported claim: for Epēshu (kind 'capital' in data/city-anchors.json, FOOT_R.capital=26; registerCityOverlay('Epēshu',...,{w:2863,h:3072}), so mx=3072), cityMaxZ = min(11.5, NZ + log2(3072/52)) = 9.8845 (about 9.885). worldCityUpdate calls setMaxZoom(min(Z_STREET, cityMaxZ)) whenever Epēshu is the nearest city (within 3 footprint radii, 78 px), so in the main atlas view the zoom is capped at about 9.885, not 11.5. The map's initial maxZoom is Z_STREET, a soft ceiling that worldCityUpdate narrows on zoomend/moveend, so transient excursions are possible before the first update. Screen factors relative to z4 (1 world px = 1 atlas px) are 2^(z-4): x9.85 at z7.3, x59.08 at z9.885, x181.02 at z11.5. The arithmetic is correct, but the baseline (z4) is not stated in the claim. The modal chart mode enterChart uses a separate maxZoom (tile pyramid maxz+1, or minZ+2 for image charts) and is not covered by the cityMaxZ cap. Not supported: that 11.5 'applies only to the street-view handoff'. In maps-site/index.html Z_STREET is only the soft map ceiling and the clamp in cityMaxZ and worldCityUpdate. No street-view handoff at z11.5 appears in the cited quotes or in maps-site code (the only mention of 11.5 as Z_STREET in docs is a living-track anchor list and the research dossier's 'Zoom-in 3D detail layer' row, not a handoff definition). Shift budgets over Epēshu should be quoted at z9.885; whether 11.5 is the handoff zoom needs a separate source.
votes.reason: The code and numbers check out: cityMaxZ is exactly as quoted, Epēshu is a capital with a 3072 px longest side, so the cap is 9.885 and the factors are right. The claim overreaches in one part: the cited evidence never shows that z11.5 is the street-view handoff zoom. In maps-site/index.html, Z_STREET is only a soft ceiling and clamp. The claim also omits the z4 baseline for the screen factors, the transient soft ceiling before worldCityUpdate runs, and the separate chart-mode zoom range.

votes.corrected: For today's code, quote the atlas shift budgets over Epēshu at z9.885, where the screen factor is ×59.08 (2^(9.885-4)). That is the steady-state ceiling, and the registration and stretched-raster errors of the canon overlay are largest there. Two corrections to the claim. First, 11.5 is not the street-view handoff. The atlas has no handoff in code. Z_STREET is the global ceiling: it is the initial L.map maxZoom, the maxZoom of the base tile layer, and the clamp in cityMaxZ and worldCityUpdate. The zoom-through into the street view is only the proposed living-track item H2z ("zooming from Z_OPEN_MAX toward Z_STREET"). If H2z ships, Epēshu's allowed max must rise above 9.885, and the budgets then need quoting at that new ceiling (up to 11.5, ×181), because the overlay and crossfade stay visible on the atlas up to that zoom. Second, the 9.885 ceiling depends on conditions. It holds only while nearestCity resolves to Epēshu, meaning the view centre is within 3×FOOT_R.capital = 78 world px of the anchor. Further out, the cap is Z_OPEN_MAX 8. setMaxZoom also runs only on zoomend/moveend, so a pan at depth from another city whose cityMaxZ is higher briefly shows Epēshu above 9.885. Finally, ×N is the CSS-pixel factor relative to z4. It measures how large an existing registration error looks on screen. Registration in atlas world px (cityBox and the art-to-atlas fit) is still what fixes the shift. A vector layer through the same cityBox would show the same ×59 error.
votes.reason: I checked this against the HEAD maps-site/index.html. The cityMaxZ formula is NZ+log2(max(w,h)/(2*footR)), clamped to Z_STREET. meshedWorldInit registers Epēshu through registerCityOverlay('Epēshu','art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg',{w:2863,h:3072}), and city-anchors.json gives Epēshu kind "capital" (FOOT_R 26). So cityMaxZ = 4+log2(3072/52) = 9.885. worldCityUpdate applies it with setMaxZoom ("Leaflet eases down"), and flyIntoCity flies to cz-0.5. A grep finds no handoff in the atlas; Z_STREET appears only as the initial map maxZoom, the base tile maxZoom and the clamp. The zoom-through is the H2z proposal in docs/living/research-dossier.md, and it would need Epēshu's max raised. There are also two smaller limits: the 78 px nearestCity radius (outside it the cap is Z_OPEN_MAX 8), and a brief overshoot during a pan from a neighbouring city at depth. The recommendation (budget at 9.885) is right for today but has to move with H2z. Throughout, the zoom factor scales the error on screen; it does not cause it. The fix is still registration.

summaries.2-registration: buildApprPolys classes every party-route leg as land, giving Pomos spurious gates from a 74%-sea leg; the fix is a data classification, not the renderer.
summaries.3-vector: buildApprPolys classes every party-route leg as land, so sea leg 8 gives Pomos false land gates; the fix is in the data classification, not the renderer.

prior_record.claim: buildApprPolys assigns APPR_POLYS classes per source file, not per geometry. Every party-route leg is pushed as cls 'land', and the class comes from raw pts, not the drawn spline. Leg 8 (Sepos to White Sea, 74% sea) gives the procedural village Pomos land approach bearings of 266.6° and 107.6°, with zero printed road dots in its annulus, so Pomos gets spurious gates. Leg 10 (99% sea) crosses Epēshu's 65 px circle at 314.1°. That is harmless today only because Epēshu is a canon overlay and genCityCanvas never runs for it. Leg 11 lies wholly inside Epēshu's circle (it starts 62.9 px from the anchor) and yields no bearing.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: These are wrong gate inputs that come from the data, not misplaced pixels. The fix belongs in the data (classify legs by the print sea mask or by a medium field), not in the renderer. Bearings use screen convention: 0 = E, 90 = S.

evidence.quote: P.push({pts:leg,cls:'land'}); ... ways.forEach(...P.push({pts:w.pts,cls:'land'})) ... lanes.forEach(...cls:'sea')
var appr=cityApproaches(name), landAppr=ruin?[]:appr.land, seaAppr=appr.sea;

evidence.source: out/vector-overlays-vs-print.json :: features['leg 8: Sepos -> White Sea'].appr_cities / appr_misclass
evidence.quote: Pomos feature_bearings_deg [266.6, 107.6], printed_road_bearings_deg []

votes.corrected: Claim holds as stated. Two wording notes. First, "per source file" means per data source: the party route, the named ways and the sea lanes. Second, "genCityCanvas never runs for Epēshu" holds because the canon overlay is registered first, so the guards in ensureCityGen and ensureCityGenNow skip it. It is not a hard exclusion in the generator itself.
votes.reason: Checked in maps-site/index.html at HEAD. buildApprPolys pushes every route leg as {pts:leg,cls:'land'}, every named way as 'land' and every lane as 'sea'. The leg points come from route[i].x/y and route[i].via, not from the drawn spline. genCityCanvas takes landAppr=ruin?[]:appr.land from cityApproaches, which clusters the crossings of each polyline with a 2.5×footR circle around the anchor. landAppr.forEach pushes each bearing in as a gate with appr:true, so a mislabelled leg produces real gates. ensureCityGen only generates when the city has no registration or its prov is 'invented'. ensureCityGenNow returns early if CITYREG[key] exists. Pomos is a village in data/city-anchors.json (atlasX 481, atlasY 725, prov 'trace'). The numbers match out/vector-overlays-vs-print.json. Leg 8 (Sepos to White Sea) has sea_fraction_raw 0.748, leg_medium 'sea', and Pomos with feature_bearings_deg [266.6, 107.6] against an empty printed_road_bearings_deg. The file carries an appr_misclass note for leg 8. Leg 10 has sea_fraction_raw 0.945 (0.989 on the spline), crosses Epēshu's 65 px circle at 314.1°, and its misclass note says it is harmless today because Epēshu is a canon overlay. Leg 11 has appr_cities empty and a note that it starts 62.9 px from the anchor and yields no bearing. The fix suggestion is a recommendation, not a quoted fact. The classification by data is supported, since the leg_medium field is already derived from the print water mask.

votes.corrected: These are wrong gate inputs that come from the data, not misplaced pixels. They are a registration fault of the procedural plan's gates against the print, and changing the rendering medium cannot fix them: a vector Pomos fed the same APPR_POLYS would grow the same false gates. The fix belongs where the data is classified, which is buildApprPolys in maps-site/index.html or a per-leg medium field in data/party-route.json, never in genCityCanvas or the renderer. Classify each segment, not each leg. Leg 8 is still about 26% land, so a whole-leg tag would be wrong too. Use the print sea mask, or better, stop treating party legs as roads at all, because they record the party's travels, not roadways. Land bearings should come from printed road dots or traced-roads data, and party legs should add a sea bearing only where they cross the circle over water. Party legs hit only four anchor circles: Māmīth Māgrīn on leg 5, Harney on leg 7, Pomos on leg 8 and Epēshu on leg 10 (canon, so its plan is never generated). None of the cityCanvasSha trio (Tamaron, Sokundo, Kanae) is touched, and the pinned function sources stay unchanged, so UG3 survives. The change still alters the seeded plans of Pomos, and possibly Harney and Māmīth Māgrīn, through gTarget and gate count. It edits maps-site/index.html, so it must be queued behind the Mobile 5-9 atlas lane and sequenced with filigree slice C, which owns the painted city. It is a small, real fix of minor size, not part of the anchoring fix itself. Bearings use the screen convention: 0 = E, 90 = S.
votes.reason: I checked this against HEAD. buildApprPolys pushes every party leg, built from the raw points [prev, ...via, cur], with cls:'land'. named-ways become 'land' and sea-lanes become 'sea'. cityApproaches intersects a circle of radius 2.5*footR(kind) with these polylines, and genCityCanvas turns appr.land into primary gates via mkGate(b,true). I recomputed the crossings from party-route.json and city-anchors.json. Leg 8 crosses Pomos (village, R=22.5) at 266.6° and 107.6°. Leg 10 crosses Epēshu (R=65) at 314.1°. Leg 11 gives no crossing. Epēshu is registered through registerCityOverlay as canon, so leg 10 is harmless. buildRoute draws each leg with crSpline, while the classification uses the raw points, so that part of the claim is also accurate. The diagnosis transfers: this is a classification and registration fault in the data, not a raster-versus-vector issue. Fixing it in buildApprPolys or the route data leaves the pinned sources untouched (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask). It also does not move cityCanvasSha, because none of the hashed cities are crossed by a party leg. It stays deterministic because it uses no RNG. Two refinements are needed. First, classify per segment rather than per leg. Second, consider dropping party legs as land-approach sources entirely. Also note the coordination needed with the mid-flight Mobile lane and filigree slice C, and that Pomos's seeded plan will change. The impact is one village's spurious gates (perhaps also Harney and Māmīth Māgrīn), so this is minor and not central to the owner's zoom-anchoring complaint.

items.summary: Refuted: the per-city bearing errors match the file, but 'depends entirely on the trace' overreaches the single-detection method, and re-tracing named-ways.json is not pin-safe because it changes the canvas bytes of the three cityCanvasSha cities.

summaries.1-shift: Refuted: the per-city bearing errors match the file, but 'depends entirely on the trace' overreaches the single-detection method, and re-tracing named-ways.json is not pin-safe because it changes the canvas bytes of the three cityCanvasSha cities.
summaries.2-registration: Gate-bearing errors reproduce, but the conclusion (snapping pointless, detector needed inside pinned genCityCanvas) is wrong since gates come from data.
summaries.3-vector: Gate-bearing errors against nearest printed roads were measured, but the nearest bearing may belong to another road and a re-trace is not hash-neutral.

prior_record.claim: How well gate bearings agree with printed roads depends entirely on whether the trace happens to hit the road near each city. I measured the error between each APPR land bearing (2.5 x footR circle) and the nearest printed-road bearing in the same annulus. Sokundo: 0.7° and 2.6°. Mago: 9.1° and 20.7°. Kanae: 12.4° and 43.3°. Tamaron: 9.6°, plus one 133.3° spur. Rhup: 59.5° and 162.8°. Drāmūz: 62.0°. Nhagi: 71.2° and 85.4°. Lepon the Old (a ruin, so its land approaches are ignored): 52.3° and 17.4°. Harney (leg 7): 2.5° and 57.1°. Māmīth Māgrīn: no printed road in its annulus.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: This decides stubs-unramped-and-gap and gates-ignore-atlas-roads. Snapping gates or stubs to the polyline is pointless while the polyline is 30-215 px off the ink. Snapping to printed dots would need the detector inside the hash-pinned genCityCanvas. A data-only re-trace of named-ways.json fixes the drawn line and the gate bearings together without touching any pinned function, so it should come before any snapping work. At cityMaxZ (town 10.19, village 10.83) the pWay line is hidden by .map-tier-d. The error still reaches the screen through gates and stubs: 31 px x 2^(10.19-4) is about 2.3k screen px of drift relative to the ring.

evidence.source: out/vector-overlays-vs-print.json :: features['Road that Walks with the Sun'].appr_cities
evidence.quote: Sokundo bearing_error_deg [0.7, 2.6]; Kanae [12.4, 43.3]; Tamaron [133.3, 9.6]; Rhup [59.5, 162.8]; Drāmūz [62.0]; Nhagi [71.2, 85.4]
var Rr=2.5*footR(a.kind) ... if(angDelta(arr[i],out[k].a)<0.25)

votes.corrected: Supported (numbers and code quotes verified): out/vector-overlays-vs-print.json (features[] with name 'Road that Walks with the Sun', plus 'leg 7: Siege of the Seat -> Sepos' for Harney and 'leg 5: Fell Mountains -> Summarch' for Māmīth Māgrīn) records, per city, the angle between each APPR land bearing (2.5 x footR circle) and the nearest bearing of DETECTED printed road dots in the annulus [R-4,R+4]. Errors in degrees: Sokundo 0.7/2.6; Mago 9.1/20.7; Kanae 12.4/43.3; Tamaron 133.3/9.6; Rhup 59.5/162.8; Drāmūz 62.0; Nhagi 71.2/85.4; Lepon the Old 52.3/17.4 (a ruin, and genCityCanvas uses landAppr=ruin?[]:appr.land, so these are ignored); Harney 2.5/57.1; Māmīth Māgrīn has no detected printed-road dots in its annulus (not 'no printed road'). The first row, Epēshu (25.4/48.2), is omitted from the claim's list. Agreement is good at Sokundo and Harney's first gate and poor at most other cities. The data fit 'the trace misses the printed road near several cities', but they do not show it 'depends entirely' on the trace. Several large errors are forced pairings: where a city has one detected printed bearing (Tamaron, Rhup), the second gate is compared against that same road. The tool's own method note says the nearest dot may belong to a different road. Harney's anchor is also 18 px off its printed ring (cross_ref). Whole-feature figures for the Road that Walks with the Sun: normal-band median 31.3 px, p90 64.6, max 98.2; nearest-dot euclid max 215.7; 45% of samples have no dot in band; 44% of the raw polyline lies over water mask. So '30-215 px off the ink' mixes a median with a maximum. The 31 px x 2^(10.19-4) = about 2.3k screen px figure is the median line offset of the whole road projected to town cityMaxZ (the file's own 2285). It is not the displacement of a gate. Gates sit on a circle of 2.5 x footR (35 px for a town) and inherit angular error, so a gate's displacement is bounded by about 2R. pWay is hidden by .map-tier-d (opacity 0 above Z_TIER_D 7.5), as stated. Not supported as written: a data-only re-trace of named-ways.json touches no pinned function source, but it changes gate bearings and so the genCityCanvas output for Tamaron, Kanae and Sokundo, which are the three plans cityCanvasSha hashes. Mobile gate UG3 requires cityCanvasSha to equal B0, so the re-trace needs a deliberate baseline re-cut. It also does not cover cities whose approaches come from party-route.json legs (Harney, Māmīth Māgrīn) or sea-lanes.json.
votes.reason: Every cited number matches the JSON, and both code quotes exist in maps-site/index.html (2.5*footR(a.kind), angDelta(...)<0.25). The CSS hiding of pWay and the cityMaxZ values of 10.19 and 10.83 also check out. The claim overreaches in five places. 'Depends entirely on the trace' is too strong, because the method uses a single printed-dot detection and the nearest-dot pairing is forced where only one printed road is found. 'No printed road' should read 'no detected dots'. Epēshu's 25.4/48.2 is dropped from the list. The 2.3k screen-px 'drift' applies a whole-feature median line offset to gates, which only inherit angular error. The data-only re-trace is not free under the mobile gates, because it changes cityCanvasSha for the three hashed cities (Tamaron, Sokundo, Kanae) against the B0 baseline that UG3 requires. The Harney anchor's own 18 px offset from its printed ring is a second cause of its error.

votes.corrected:
The measurement holds. The per-city errors match out/vector-overlays-vs-print.json (Road that Walks with the Sun appr_cities; leg 5 gives Māmīth Māgrīn no printed road; leg 7 gives Harney 2.5 and 57.1; leg 8 gives Pomos no printed road). Epēshu (25.4 and 48.2) is left out correctly: it is a canon chart and buildCityStubs skips charts whose prov is not 'invented'. In maps-site/index.html the generated-plan gates come from data: genCityCanvas calls cityApproaches, which reads APPR_POLYS, and buildApprPolys fills that from the route legs, named-ways.json and the sea lanes. The step landAppr.forEach(...mkGate(b,true)) makes the gates, and the stubs are gate to 1.18*footR in atlas coordinates. So this is a REGISTRATION fix that bends the data to the atlas. The rendering medium does not matter: a vector plan would inherit the same wrong bearings.

Doing a data-only re-trace of named-ways.json (and of the route vias that feed APPR_POLYS) before any snapping is the right order. Keep the bearings that are already good (Sokundo 0.7°/2.6°, Harney's 2.5° leg).

It is not pin-neutral, though. It leaves xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask untouched, but it changes their OUTPUT. cityCanvasSha hashes Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae, and all three sit on this road. UG3 requires cityCanvasSha equal to B0, so the re-trace fails UG3 while the atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) is in flight. It must either wait until the lane closes or ship as a declared, owner-approved B0 re-baseline of cityCanvasSha. It also changes every invented plan near the road (all gates, street layout, POIs), so treat it as a deliberate regeneration.

Snapping does not need a detector inside genCityCanvas. Bearings detected from the print can be precomputed offline as data, for example a gates or approach field per anchor. The canvas hash would change in the same way.

The drift figure is wrong. 31 px is the median lateral offset over the whole polyline, and 45% of it is at sea or has no ink in the band. What reaches the screen is the gate or stub bearing error: a chord of about 2*1.18*footR*sin(θ/2) world px at the plan edge. For a town at θ≈10° that is about 2.9 px, or about 210 screen px at z10.19. For Rhup or Nhagi at θ≈60-85° it is about 13-18 px, or about 1-1.5k screen px at z10.83. The ink it is compared against is the base print at 0.12 opacity under the wash. The pWay line is hidden at Z_TIER_D=7.5, not just at cityMaxZ.
votes.reason: The data is right and so is the order (fix the registration data first, don't snap to a bad polyline). But the claim that this is safe for the pins because no pinned function is touched is wrong. The gates are derived inside genCityCanvas through cityApproaches/APPR_POLYS, so re-tracing named-ways.json changes the canvas bytes of exactly the three cities that cityCanvasSha pins (Tamaron, Sokundo, Kanae, all on this road). That breaks UG3 while the Mobile 5-9 atlas lane is mid-flight. The claim that snapping needs a detector inside the pinned function is also false: precomputed bearing data works. And 31 px × 2^6.19 ≈ 2.3k mixes up the whole-road lateral offset (half of it at sea) with the angular gate error at the plan edge, which is what reaches the screen.

items.summary: The North Coast Packet sea lane crosses the Paerāndas islets for 26-27 px (raw/spline); the South Lane's land run is only 12 px raw / 5 px spline, not 35 px; lane endpoints sit up to 60 px from anchors; fix by moving or splitting a vertex in sea-lanes.json.

summaries.1-shift: The North Coast Packet sea lane crosses the Paerāndas islets for 26-27 px (raw/spline); the South Lane's land run is only 12 px raw / 5 px spline, not 35 px; lane endpoints sit up to 60 px from anchors; fix by moving or splitting a vertex in sea-lanes.json.
summaries.2-registration: The North Coast Packet crosses 26-27 px of islet land, and the South Lane overruns only 12 px raw / 5 px spline (not ~35); fix in sea-lanes.json.
summaries.3-vector: The North Coast Packet crosses 26-27 px of land at the Paerāndas islets and the South Lane only 12 px raw / 5 px spline beyond its port allowance (not ~35), small data fixes in sea-lanes.json.

prior_record.claim: Sea lanes. The Gulf Crossing and the Strait Run stay on print water beyond their ports (longest land run 1-2 px). The North Coast Packet crosses land for 27 px at x1311-1336, y~1398 (the Paerāndas islets), on both the raw and spline geometry. The South Lane's last ~35 px (x1487-1525, y~1820) run over land into Kardunash, beyond the port allowance (1.35 x footR plus the endpoint-to-anchor distance). Lane endpoints sit 13.7-60 px from their anchors (Gulf Crossing to Hordon 60.1 px, both Epēshu-side ends 17.9 px).
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: These are small REGISTRATION errors: lanes are drawn into the islets and onto a land approach, at most 27 px, which is 108 px on screen at z6 and 266 px at z7.3. Both lanes feed APPR_POLYS seaAppr for the quay bias of Sokundo, Kanae, Tamaron, Mago, Drāmūz and Kardunash. Moving two or three vertices fixes them. No rendering change is involved.

evidence.quote: land_length_px 42, longest_land_run_px 27, line_ink_crossings 10, crosses_land true
land_length_px 12, longest_land_run_px 12, crosses_land true

votes.corrected: Gulf Crossing (longest land run beyond ports: raw 1 px, spline 0) and Strait Run (2 px both) stay on print water. The North Coast Packet crosses land for 26 px on the raw geometry and 27 px on the spline, at x1311-1336, y~1398 (the Paerāndas islets). The South Lane has only 12 px of land beyond the port allowance on the raw geometry (longest run 12 px, total 12 px) and 5 px on the spline (total 7 px). The ~35 px stretch at x1487-1525, y~1820 is the whole approach into Kardunash and includes the port allowance. Lane endpoints sit 0.2-60.1 px from their anchors: South Lane 0.2 px (Drāmūz) and 0.4 px (Kardunash), Mago 13.7, Strait Run 16.3 and 27, both Epēshu-side ends 17.9, Hordon 60.1.
votes.reason: I checked out/vector-overlays-vs-print.json and the buildCityMask water test in maps-site/index.html. The buildCityMask quote is present (`if(r*0.299+gc2*0.587+b*0.114>=110){wgt[i]=1;if(r-b<=54)wat[i]=1;}`). The quoted figures for North Coast Packet spline (land_length_px 42, longest run 27, ink crossings 10) and the screen-px values (108 at z6, 265.9 at z7.3) also match. Three parts overreach. (1) The 27 px run holds on the spline only. The raw longest run is 26 px, and the raw land total is 31. (2) The South Lane "last ~35 px beyond the port allowance" is not supported. land_check_raw gives land_length_px 12 and longest_land_run_px 12, and the spline gives 5 and 7. The ~35 px figure comes from the file's location note, which describes the whole approach and includes the port exclusion (excluded radius about 19 px). The claim's own cited quote shows 12, not 35. (3) The endpoint-to-anchor range "13.7-60 px" is wrong. The South Lane endpoints are 0.2 px (Drāmūz) and 0.4 px (Kardunash) from their anchors, so the true range is 0.2-60.1 px. The conclusion that these are small registration errors fixable by moving a few vertices still stands, with the South Lane error smaller than stated. I did not check the claim's list of six quay-bias cities against the code. The data file lists Sokundo, Kanae, Tamaron and Mago for the North Coast Packet and Drāmūz and Kardunash for the South Lane.

votes.corrected: This is a small REGISTRATION error in data, and it is fixed only in maps-site/data/sea-lanes.json. The lanes are prov "invented", so bending them to the print is allowed. No rendering change is needed: a vector or raster lane drawn through the same points sits on land either way. Three corrections. (1) The North Coast Packet overrun is right: the longest land run is 27 px on the spline and 26 px on the raw line. That is about 108 screen px at z6 and about 266 px at z7.3. It comes from the segment through vertex [1320,1398]. Rerouting that vertex around or between the Paerāndas islets fixes it. The crossing lies outside every approach circle (2.5 x footR, with Epēshu R=65 reaching only about x1301), so it changes nothing in seaAppr or any city plan. It is purely the drawn line. The Epēshu-side segment's bearing would move slightly, but Epēshu uses DM art. (2) The South Lane is overstated. Beyond the port allowance it has 12 px of land on the raw line and 5 px on the spline, not about 35 px. Its endpoints sit on the anchors: Drāmūz 0.2 px and Kardunash 0.4 px. They are not 13.7-60 px off. The overrun comes from the lane running to Kardunash's dot, which the anchor data puts 14 px inland (sea side W). The fix is to end the lane at the shore, about 14 px W of [1525,1820]. The endpoint-to-anchor range of 13.7-60.1 px is true only for Mago (13.7), Tamaron (16.3), Epēshu (17.9) and Hordon (60.1). (3) The South Lane edit changes Kardunash's seaAppr bearing, because cityApproaches uses segCircleHits on a 35 px circle. That changes Kardunash's genCityCanvas plan and so the mobile UG3 cityCanvasSha baseline. Hand it to the mobile atlas lane, or schedule it after that lane with a re-baseline. Do not land it during Mobile 5-9.
votes.reason: I checked this against the HEAD export. The claim and its framing (registration, a data fix, no medium change) carry over to our stack. Lanes come from sea-lanes.json, and buildApprPolys feeds them in as 'sea' polylines. I recomputed which cities each lane enters, and the claim's list (Sokundo, Kanae, Tamaron, Mago, Drāmūz, Kardunash) matches; Epēshu and Hordon are also entered. The z6 and z7.3 screen figures are correct. The facts need fixing. The out json gives 12 px raw and 5 px spline for the South Lane, not about 35 px. Its endpoints sit 0.2 and 0.4 px from the Drāmūz and Kardunash anchors. The claim also leaves out two things. The islet fix is display-only and touches no approach. The Kardunash fix changes genCityCanvas output, so it collides with the cityCanvasSha pin while the mobile atlas lane is in progress.

items.summary: Refuted: the district rings have no printed counterpart, but an owner-flagged POLISH ruling says they were traced from dotted road lines and are to be relabelled or retired, not re-registered, and Azrāken lies over the strait, not mostly over the Marble Gulf.

summaries.1-shift: Refuted: the district rings have no printed counterpart, but an owner-flagged POLISH ruling says they were traced from dotted road lines and are to be relabelled or retired, not re-registered, and Azrāken lies over the strait, not mostly over the Marble Gulf.
summaries.2-registration: District rings have no printed border, but the proposed remedy is wrong; the project already treats them as approximate traces.
summaries.3-vector: District-ring measurements are sound, but the proposed remedy contradicts the POLISH ruling to relabel or retire the rings with the road network.

prior_record.claim: Minor-region (district) borders have no printed counterpart. The print draws no district boundary class, only spaced lettering, which I checked on a Leponnia crop. Their rings sit a median 7.5-34.9 px from the nearest river, coast or graticule ink. A large share of each ring lies on print sea: Lamor 51%, Aura-Hōth Hanath 51%, Azrāken 41%, Pēshunor 36%. 80% of Azrāken's eroded interior reads as water, so that district is drawn mostly over the Marble Gulf.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: These cannot be registered to print ink because none exists. The 'trace' provenance is misleading. The right anchor is the coast (clip rings to the land mask) plus rivers. These rings do not feed APPR_POLYS.

evidence.quote: Azrāken ring_sea_fraction 0.414, interior_water_fraction 0.8; Sūs Gimilīn nearest_line_ink median 34.9; printed_class NONE
properties {'prov': 'trace'} on all 7 features
L.polygon(latlngs,{color:'#6a5c48',weight:1.2,opacity:.85,dashArray:'2 5',...pane:'pDistrict'})

votes.corrected: The print draws no district boundary class. On a Leponnia crop (tiles z5, rings overlaid) the regions Lamor, Pēshunor, Dranimos, Rhoshkhon, Sūs Gimilīn, Azrāken and Aura-Hōth Hanath are spaced lettering only, and the dotted lines join settlements as roads. The 7 rings in maps-site/data/minor-regions.geojson all carry prov 'trace'. They are rough polygons drawn by buildDistricts as a dashed L.polygon on pane pDistrict with no crSpline. Per out/vector-overlays-vs-print.json, their median distance to the nearest river, coast or graticule ink is 7.5 px (Lamor) to 34.9 px (Sūs Gimilīn). The share of each ring lying on print sea is Lamor 0.51, Aura-Hōth Hanath 0.509, Azrāken 0.414 and Pēshunor 0.362. For Azrāken, 0.8 of the eroded interior reads as water. That is expected rather than an error, because canon (wiki-places 'The White Sea' and 'Leponnia') makes Azrāken a sea-strait region of the White Sea between Leponnia and Horat. The ring sits over the Azrāken strait, not the Marble Gulf, which is a separate region. These rings cannot be registered to print ink because no printed boundary exists. The anchors available are the coast (clip land-regions to the land mask) and rivers. The geojson note ('Approximate trace of the atlas' dotted border') contradicts the print, where the dotted ink is roads.
votes.reason: The numbers match: the 7.5 to 34.9 px median range, the sea fractions 51, 51, 41 and 36 percent, Azrāken at 0.8 interior water, prov 'trace' on all 7 features, and the buildDistricts code. The 'no printed district boundary' claim also holds on my own crop of the z5 tiles with the rings overlaid. The 'feeds_APPR_POLYS: false' flag is in the JSON, but I did not check that APPR_POLYS is built from other sources (buildApprPolys). The claim overreaches in one place: 'drawn mostly over the Marble Gulf' is wrong. The crop shows the Azrāken label and ring over the strait south of Hordon, and the Marble Gulf is the separate water labelled GULF to its north. The wiki lists Azrāken and Marble Gulf as distinct regions of the White Sea, and says the Azrāken divides Leponnia from Horat. The 80 percent water figure is therefore canon-consistent. The claim also leaves out that the geojson note says 'Approximate trace of the atlas' dotted border', which conflicts with the 'no printed counterpart' reading, and the 'trace is misleading' wording is an interpretation. The 'checked on a Leponnia crop' evidence is only an assertion in the method text, but my own crop confirms it.

votes.corrected: The facts check out, but the remedy is wrong. All 7 features in maps-site/data/minor-regions.geojson carry prov 'trace' and the note "Approximate trace of the atlas' dotted border". buildDistricts draws them as dashed L.polygon in pane pDistrict, and buildApprPolys only reads route, ways and lanes, so they do not feed APPR_POLYS. The project already knows what these rings are. POLISH.md (the road-network item, cited as POLISH.md:13 in docs/filigree/research-dossier.md and todo-inputs.json) records a USER FLAG: the "District borders" layer traced dotted lines as boundaries, but per the cartographic key "they are ROADS (relabel/retire the layer when the network ships)". So 'trace' is not invented provenance. It is a misread of road dots, and the fix is already queued under the road-network and filigree data prerequisites. Clipping the rings to a land mask and snapping them to rivers would make up district boundaries that the authoritative atlas never draws. Registration means bending art to existing atlas ink, and here there is nothing to bend to. The only land mask in code (sampleCityMask/buildCityMask) is hash-pinned by the mobile track and is known to read inland realm tints as water, so it is the wrong clip source anyway. What fits the project: (1) correct the provenance/note to "misread road dots, no printed boundary"; (2) retire or relabel the layer when the traced road network ships, as POLISH.md says, and keep the minor regions as the canon lettering/markers (maps_markers has 7 Minor Regions; Lamor and Pēshunor are regions, not towns); (3) until then, at most show them on hover only, in line with filigree R7. The district layer is a tier-C toggle hidden in chart mode and tier D. It has nothing to do with the owner's city-zoom shifting, which comes from cityBox placement (registration) and not from the rendering medium.
votes.reason: The measurements are sound. The print has no district boundary class, a large share of each ring lies on print sea, and the rings stay out of APPR_POLYS (checked in buildApprPolys and buildDistricts in maps-site/index.html). The applies_to_us remedy does not carry over. POLISH.md already holds an owner-flagged ruling: these rings were traced from dotted ROAD lines (dotted = roadways in the user-confirmed key), and the layer is to be relabelled or retired when the road network ships, not re-registered. Moving them to the coast and rivers would put invented boundaries on top of an authoritative atlas that draws none. The only land mask available is the pinned sampleCityMask, which misreads inland tints as water. The overlay also has no bearing on the city-zoom anchoring the owner asked about.

evidence.quote: var drawWater = !!sv && (t.harbor || distPx<=25); ... var MK=(drawWater&&mask&&mask.water)?mask:null;
over_half_water_not_harbor: Mishimbril 0.997, Sārūmeron 1.0, Permūr 0.99 ...

votes.corrected: Claim holds as stated. Minor wording: the quote from the out file is a truncated list of 71 entries (70 inland plus Lepon the Old, which has a sea entry). The "none exceeds 0.8" part for the 16 drawWater anchors is not stored in the out JSON for the harbor ones; it is supported by my recomputation.
votes.reason: Quote 1 exists verbatim in genCityCanvas in maps-site/index.html (HEAD): "var drawWater = !!sv && (t.harbor || distPx<=25);" and "var MK=(drawWater&&mask&&mask.water)?mask:null;". buildCityMask contains the water test `if(r-b<=54)wat[i]=1`, and keeps only border-connected water. Quote 2 exists in out/vector-overlays-vs-print.json under side_check_buildCityMask.over_half_water_not_harbor: Mishimbril 0.997, Sārūmeron 1.0, Permūr 0.99. The realm medians match: Eastern Patrin 0.999 (n9), Umbadic 0.99 (n3), Alensic 0.862 (n8), Pheropic 0.569 (n2). The list has 71 entries, and one is Lepon the Old, which has a sea entry; the other 70 have none. Counting from city-anchors.json, 115 anchors have neither harbor nor sea.side, so "70 of 115" is right. The same file gives exactly 16 anchors that satisfy harbor or (sea.side and distPx<=25), where distPx defaults to 8 when absent. I re-implemented buildCityMask from the z5 tiles. It reproduced Permūr 0.99, Mishimbril 0.997 and Lepon the Old 0.627. All 16 qualifying anchors came out at 0.644 or below (Tamaron 0.644, Lepon 0.627, Sokundo 0.573), so none exceeds 0.8. Without drawWater, mask only supplies the land hue: LT=(mask&&mask.land)||LAND_TAN in genCityCanvas, and the land tone in the wash code (q.m.land||LAND_TAN). sampleCityMask and buildCityMask exist and are pinned, so "flag, not fix" is consistent.

votes.corrected: This is a latent trap for any future registration step that trusts mask.water away from the coast, such as clipping, snapping or warping inland plans to the atlas. Today it only shows up as colour. When most of a patch is misread as water, mask.land is averaged from the few pixels left (or falls back to LAND_TAN). So the LT/GREEN surround and the wash re-tone of tinted-realm inland cities are biased too, not just correctly taken from the atlas. Any registration work must use a classifier that tells realm tints from sea (for example, require border water to connect to a charted sea or harbor entry, or test hue and not only r-b) before trusting mask.water inland. Pin scope: only sampleCityMask is source-hashed under UG3 atlas_fn_sha (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask). buildCityMask is not in that list. It is still pinned through the output: cityCanvasSha hashes the invented-plan data URLs (Tamaron, Sokundo, Kanae, plus any registered invented plan) against the baseline and across profiles, so any change to buildCityMask that moves a land hue breaks UG3. Changing it therefore needs the mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) to re-baseline; flag it now, don't fix it. Anchor-to-ring offsets (Harney 18 px, Stony Ford 23 px) are a separate registration matter for out/anchor-correction-table.json. Neither the bad mask nor its fix moves any anchor or cityBox, so the mask does not cause the zoom shift the owner sees.
votes.reason: Checked against HEAD maps-site/index.html. buildCityMask sets wat[i]=1 when r-b<=54 on any bright pixel, then keeps water connected to the patch border. genCityCanvas sets drawWater = !!sv && (t.harbor || distPx<=25) and MK=(drawWater&&mask&&mask.water)?mask:null. Elsewhere the mask feeds only LT=(mask&&mask.land) and the wash tone (MASKQ[key].m.land at the top of the wash code), plus mask.bear for a harbor whose sea side is uncharted. So the claim's account of the impact is right: cosmetic today, a trap for inland registration later. The out/vector-overlays-vs-print.json side_check_buildCityMask data matches the numbers quoted (for example Lepon the Old, which does draw water, reads 0.627, under 0.8). The claim misses one thing: with 99% read as water, mask.land comes from leftover pixels, so even the hue is skewed. One correction is needed in applies_to_us. tools/mobile-capture.js source-hashes only sampleCityMask, not buildCityMask (its list is ['xmur3','mulberry32','genCityCanvas','washMake','sampleCityMask']). buildCityMask is pinned indirectly by cityCanvasSha, which hashes invented plan data URLs against the baseline. "Flag, not fix" still holds while the mobile atlas lane is mid-flight. Registration and rendering are separate here. This is a registration-input defect; neither a vector nor a raster city fixes it. It matters only if a registration step trusts the mask inland, and it does not explain today's cityBox zoom shift.

items.summary: Refuted: q08-c08 is a DEM-versus-chart-coast discrepancy measured through cityBox, but 'the only quantified registration error' is not shown, and an anchor move would also invalidate it.

summaries.1-shift: Refuted: q08-c08 is a DEM-versus-chart-coast discrepancy measured through cityBox, but 'the only quantified registration error' is not shown, and an anchor move would also invalidate it.
summaries.2-registration: q08-c08 measured DEM vs chart through cityBox, and any placement change, including an anchor move, stales it.
summaries.5-ownership: Refuted: q08-c08 measures the chart coast against the sim DEM, not the atlas, so it is not a registration baseline and moves under any placement change.

prior_record.claim: Only one chart-vs-atlas registration error is quantified anywhere in the bible chain: q08-c08 and density-bible city_grain.contour_hill.gap. It was measured through the cityBox mapping, so a canon translate+scale override (b) invalidates it directly. An anchor move does not, because Epēshu is within 3 px of its marker.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: After a (b) override these residuals must be measured again. They are also the baseline for judging whether registration improved.

evidence.quote: The DEM coast does not follow the chart coast in the southern half of Q1 ... sits 1.0 and 0.8 atlas px ... the transform looks right and the gap is in the DEM's own sea/land line
a clip to the chart coast (the DEM shore runs up to 10 atlas px off in the south)

votes.corrected: Both quotes exist (docs/filigree/research/q08.json q08-c08 and docs/filigree/density-bible.json city_grain.contour_hill.gap, whose 'up to 10 atlas px' rounds the 10.4 figure). The narrowest supported claim: q08-c08 measures a sim-DEM versus chart-coast discrepancy in Epēshu's chart quadrant Q1. The DEM first reaches land 0.8-1.0 atlas px from the chart coast in the north, and 3.8-10.4 atlas px east of it in the south. The chart pixels were mapped to atlas coordinates through the cityBox(anchor, capital r=26) formula (q08-c01). The source itself says the northern agreement within one DEM cell means 'the transform looks right and the gap is in the DEM's own sea/land line'. So this is a DEM sea/land error, not a chart-vs-atlas registration error. It is a medium-confidence finding, not high. The 'only one quantified anywhere' wording is not shown: q05-c13 quantifies Epēshu's marker as 2.2 atlas px off the printed ring centre, and the density-bible punch list notes the Drāmūz marker 35 px off its anchor. Neither is chart-vs-atlas, but the sweep was not exhaustive. A canon translate+scale override changes the cityBox chart-to-atlas mapping, so these DEM-vs-chart residuals would have to be re-measured. An anchor move of about 2 px (anchor 1236.1,1415 vs marker 1236,1417) shifts the box by that much, which is the same size as the 0.8-1.0 px northern residuals, so the claim that an anchor move does not invalidate them is unsupported. The residuals cannot serve as a baseline for 'did registration improve', because the source attributes the gap to the DEM, not to the transform.
votes.reason: The quotes are real, and the cityBox dependence is real (q08-c01 gives the formula). The claim overreaches in three ways. It labels a DEM-coast discrepancy a 'registration error' when q08-c08 says the transform looks right. 'Only one quantified anywhere' is not demonstrated. The anchor-move immunity does not follow, because a roughly 2 px shift is comparable to the 0.8-1.0 px residuals. The source also rates c08 'medium' confidence, not 'high'.

votes.corrected: q08-c08, and the density-bible city_grain.contour_hill.gap figure that copies it, were measured through cityBox. q08 gives the mapping as anchor 1236.1,1415, capital r=26, overlay 2863x3072, so atlas 1211.87..1260.33 x 1389..1441, 80.77 chart px per atlas px, and scan rows at atlas y = 1389+cy/4200*52. Any change to that placement makes the numbers stale. That includes a canon translate+scale override (b), and it includes an anchor move too: cityBox centres the box on atlasX/atlasY, so moving the anchor shifts the chart against the DEM by exactly that amount. A shift of up to 3 px is larger than the 0.8-1.0 px northern agreement. Re-measure after either change, using the same q08 scan as a regression check. Do not use this residual as the yardstick for registration. It measures the DEM against the chart, not the authoritative PatrinorModern print against the chart. q08 itself says the transform looks right and that the 3.8-10.4 px southern gap lies in the DEM's own sea/land line. Minimising it would bend the canon chart onto the DEM's wrong southern shore. The density-bible already prescribes the fix: clip relief to the chart coast. Judge registration against the print's ink coast, rivers and dotted roads (as q10 does for rivers with its within-3-px-of-print-ink test, A.rivers_overlap), and check the northern 1 px agreement as a sanity floor.
votes.reason: The claim is partly right. q08.json shows the measurement went through cityBox ("Epēshu's world footprint is cityBox(anchor 1236.1,1415; capital r=26; overlay 2863x3072) = atlas x 1211.87..1260.33, y 1389..1441"), so an override (b) does make it stale. I also found no other chart-vs-atlas offset quantified in docs/filigree, docs/living or docs/research. q05-c20's "misregistered trace" is road data against the print, and q09's registration check is DEM cell against wiki anchor. Two parts are wrong, though. (1) "An anchor move does not invalidate it" is backwards. In maps-site/index.html, cityBox computes x0:a.atlasX-hw and y0:a.atlasY-hh, so any anchor edit translates the whole chart. A shift of up to 3 px is larger than the 0.8/1.0 px northern residual. (2) Using this number as "the baseline for judging whether registration improved" breaks the rule that the atlas is authoritative. The residual is DEM against chart, and q08-c08 says "the transform looks right and the gap is in the DEM's own sea/land line" (and q08 lists that gap as unexplained). Optimising toward it would fit the canon art to a derived DEM's faulty southern shore. It is also mislabelled as a "chart-vs-atlas registration error". The better baselines are the print's coast, river and road ink, together with the bible's existing clip-to-chart-coast rule. Severity is medium: following the advice as written could push an override (b) in the wrong direction, but the re-measure step itself is sound.

items.summary: Refuted: the footprint-derived numbers (48.46x52, 80.77, 10.336 vs live 9.885) are right, but the Q1 window and hex overlaps move under an anchor move too, so the scenario split is wrong.

summaries.1-shift: Refuted: the footprint-derived numbers (48.46x52, 80.77, 10.336 vs live 9.885) are right, but the Q1 window and hex overlaps move under an anchor move too, so the scenario split is wrong.
summaries.2-registration: The stale-number scenarios were misattributed: a seam clip changes none, and an anchor move shifts the Q1 window.
summaries.5-ownership: Refuted: numbers right, scenario split wrong; an anchor or translate-only move shifts the Q1 window, the 9.885 vs 10.336 gap already exists at HEAD, and 10.336 stays valid as a chart scale constant.

prior_record.claim: Several footprint-derived numbers in Filigree 1 research change under (b) and stay put under (a) and (c): the 48.46x52 footprint, 80.77 chart px per atlas px, the Q1 atlas window and its hex overlaps, and the 10.336 cityMaxZ. Scale also shifts every proxy sampling zoom by log2(scale). The live cityMaxZ for the Epēshu overlay is 9.885 (3072-px registration), while q03 computed 10.336 from the 4200-px detail chart.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: These are stale under any Epēshu override. Filigree 2 must decide which cityMaxZ its sampling zooms use.

evidence.quote: footprint box of 48.46x52.0 atlas px (FOOT_R capital 26), so 80.77 chart px = 1 atlas px, and cityMaxZ = 4 + log2(4200/52) = 10.336
return Math.min(Z_STREET,NZ+log2(mx/(2*r)));
registerCityOverlay('Epēshu','art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg',{prov:'canon',w:2863,h:3072,

votes.corrected:
The numbers and quotes check out, but the scenario attribution overreaches. Verified at HEAD:
- q03 q03-c05 says "footprint box of 48.46x52.0 atlas px (FOOT_R capital 26), so 80.77 chart px = 1 atlas px, and cityMaxZ = 4 + log2(4200/52) = 10.336".
- q08 q08-c01 gives cityBox = x 1211.87..1260.33, y 1389..1441 (48.46x52) for overlay 2863x3072.
- maps-site/index.html cityMaxZ is `Math.min(Z_STREET,NZ+log2(mx/(2*r)))`, and meshedWorldInit calls registerCityOverlay('Epēshu',...,{w:2863,h:3072}).
- I recomputed the live value: 4+log2(3072/52) = 9.885, against q03's 10.336 from the 4200-px chart. So q03's cityMaxZ is already stale by 0.45 zoom levels without any override.

The cited sources only support the baseline numbers and the stale 10.336. None of them defines or tests scenarios (a), (b) or (c). Those come from the placement-consumers research, which says: "Footprint-size numbers move only under (b) with scale ≠1 (sampling zooms shift by log2(s)); the Q1 window moves under any translation."

Narrowest supported claim: the footprint size (48.46x52), the 80.77 chart px per atlas px and the cityMaxZ change only if a canon override rescales the Epēshu box (scale ≠1). Proxy sampling zooms then shift by log2(scale). These stay put under anchor moves, translation-only overrides and seam clips (a, c).

The Q1 atlas window (origin 1211.87,1389.0 plus chart px/80.77) and its hex overlaps also move under any translation. That includes (a), an anchor move, and a translate-only (b), so they do not "stay put under (a)". A seam clip (c) leaves them unchanged.

cityMaxZ currently reads FOOT_R and the overlay w/h, not the box, so an override changes it only if cityMaxZ is also changed to read the override scale. Filigree 2 should take 9.885 as the live baseline, not 10.336.
votes.reason: The quotes exist and the arithmetic is right (9.885 vs 10.336, 48.46x52, 80.77). The claim says the Q1 window and its hex overlaps stay put under (a), but the Q1 origin is derived from the anchor box, so it moves under any anchor move or translation. The cited evidence also never defines or tests (a)/(b)/(c), and only the placement-consumers research covers them.

votes.corrected:
These numbers do not all go stale "under any Epēshu override". The definitions below come from out/placement-consumers.json.
(1) A seam clip (c) changes none of them. A clip hides pixels and does not move the box.
(2) An anchor move (a) leaves the 48.46x52 footprint, the 80.77 ratio and the cityMaxZ unchanged. It shifts the Q1 atlas window and its hex overlaps (84.3% in F10) by the move vector. That only matters if the registration item actually moves the Epēshu anchor, and Epēshu sits in the within-3px set with no move verdict, so this is conditional.
(3) An override that only translates the overlay changes the Q1 window and the hex overlaps but none of the size numbers. A scale override changes all of them, and every proxy sampling zoom moves by log2(scale).
(4) The 9.885 vs 10.336 gap already exists at HEAD with no override at all. maps-site/index.html cityMaxZ takes reg.w/h from the 2863x3072 overlay, and worldCityUpdate setMaxZoom clamps the world view to 4+log2(3072/52)=9.885. The 4200-px chart is shown only in modal enterChart, which has its own zoom frame (atZoom=def.maxz).
(5) 10.336 is wrong as a cap but still correct as a scale constant. The overlay and the chart share the cityBox footprint and the same aspect (2863/3072 ≈ 3914/4200). So on screen, one chart-feature px still equals 2^(z-10.336) screen px, and q03's arterial thresholds (z8.34, z9.34) still hold in the world view. What is stale is q03-c05's instruction to sample P1 at z10 and z10.34: Leaflet cannot reach those zooms in the world view. They are past the 9.885 cap that would apply unless a registration scale or a vector city raises it.
Filigree 2, which has not frozen its gates yet, should sample at or below the live cityMaxZ, or keep 10.336 only as the chart-px scale constant. Registration (a/b) is what moves these numbers. Moving to a vector city placed through the same cityBox changes none of them. Rebase cost falls only on the frozen Filigree 1 artefacts (q03, q08, the density bible).
votes.reason:
I checked the facts against the HEAD export.
- The code defines cityMaxZ as Math.min(Z_STREET,NZ+log2(mx/(2*r))).
- meshedWorldInit registers Epēshu with w:2863,h:3072, and the image file really is 2863x3072. That gives a live cap of 4+log2(3072/52)=9.885.
- q03-c05 and q08-c01 are quoted correctly: 10.336 comes from the 4200-px chart, and the footprint is 48.46x52.
- The claim's own split is mostly right, with two exceptions. Under (a), the Q1 window and hex overlaps move if the Epēshu anchor moves, which placement-consumers.json marks conditional. Under (b), a translate-only override leaves the size, the ratio and the cap unchanged.
applies_to_us ("stale under any Epēshu override") contradicts the claim itself, since (c) and a translate-only (b) leave most of the numbers alone. It also misplaces the cityMaxZ issue: the 9.885/10.336 gap is a mismatch that exists at HEAD regardless of any override. The constant 10.336 is still valid for chart-px-to-screen-px scale because the overlay and the chart share the footprint and aspect. What actually breaks is q03's z10/z10.34 sampling, which sits above the live 9.885 cap. Acting on the claim as worded could lead Filigree 2 to throw out a valid scale constant, or to think the problem only appears once an override lands.

items.summary: Refuted: the cell arithmetic holds, but the read-only DEM probe shows no window hex changes class under the anchor moves, so no density-bible amendment is needed.

summaries.2-registration: A probe shows no window hex changes ground class under the anchor moves, so no bible amendment is needed.
summaries.5-ownership: Refuted: the cell moves are right but no window hex is reclassified, so the bible's calibration counts are unchanged and no amendment is needed.

prior_record.claim: The bible's ground classification reads city-anchors.json points inside 32-px hexes, so anchor moves (a) can reclassify window hexes. The in-window moves change cells as follows: Hordon 35,54 to 35,52; Gehon Or 47,38 to 48,39; Gehon Iepīr enters the window at 46,38. Tamaron and Lepon the Old keep their cells. Sheet one is untouched. (b) and (c) do not affect this.
