evidence.quote: Anchor tests read maps-site/data/city-anchors.json atlasX,atlasY inside the hex's half-open bbox with no margin
the whole window grid (676 hexes, cells 33-58 x 38-63) as open_sea 241, open_ground 201, coast 120, no_dem 51, hill 45, islets 12, settlement 3, ruin 1, river_town 1, painted_city 1

votes.corrected:
The cell arithmetic is right, but the conclusion that the anchor moves can reclassify window hexes is not supported. Running the read-only probe on the HEAD export shows no window hex changes class. Hexes are 32 atlas px, so cell = floor(coord/32).

Cell moves, from anchor-correction-table.json against city-anchors.json:
- Hordon [1139,1730] -> [1124,1690]: cell 35,54 -> 35,52.
- Gehon Or [1512,1247] -> [1540,1261]: cell 47,38 -> 48,39.
- Gehon Iepīr [1466,1186] -> [1483,1217]: cell 45,37 -> 46,38. 45,37 is outside the window grid (cells 33-58 x 38-63), so it "enters the grid". Cell 46,38 is not in the DEM window, because its centre y 1232 is below 1240.
- Tamaron (51,48) and Lepon the Old (35,44) keep their cells.
- Sheet one is untouched: its bbox 1216,1376..1760,1664 covers cells 38-54 x 43-51, and the only anchor in it that is flagged to move is Tamaron, which stays in cell 51,48.

Probe results for the affected cells (node tools/filigree-dem.js):
- 35,54: land_frac 0.95, so coast (Test 7). The anchor test (Test 9) comes later and never fires.
- 35,52: land_frac 0.81, so coast.
- 47,38: centre outside the DEM window, so no_dem (Test 1).
- 48,39: land_frac 0, so open_sea (Test 2).
- 46,38: no_dem.

Test 9 (settlement) runs only after the coast and hill tests, so the anchor never decides the class of any of these hexes. The window calibration counts (open_sea 241, open_ground 201, coast 120, no_dem 51, hill 45, islets 12, settlement 3, ruin 1, river_town 1, painted_city 1) should not change from these moves, and no bible amendment is triggered. The claim's "depends on a DEM probe that has not been run" is resolved by this run. Cell 35,54 still holds the Maeges anchor at the same coordinates, 1139,1730, which no row moves.

The evidence does not define what "(b) and (c)" are, so "(b) and (c) do not affect this" could not be checked.
votes.reason: The quotes exist and the cell arithmetic checks. Sheet one is unaffected, and the Tamaron and Lepon the Old cells are unchanged. The claim overreaches in saying the moves can reclassify window hexes. Probing the five affected hexes shows each is decided by an earlier test, namely no_dem, open_sea or coast, so the calibration counts do not change.

votes.corrected:
No bible amendment is needed, and the DEM probe the claim was waiting on has now been run. The anchor moves in (a) change no ground class in the window. Both calibration lines in docs/filigree/density-bible.md stay exactly as they are: sheet one's 153 hexes, and the 676-hex window (open_sea 241, open_ground 201, coast 120, no_dem 51, hill 45, islets 12, settlement 3, ruin 1, river_town 1, painted_city 1).

Why, using the B-02 order (no_dem and open_sea are tested before any anchor test, and coast and hill before settlement):
- Gehon Iepīr moves to (1483,1217), which is cell 46,38. That hex's centre is (1488,1232), and `--at` returns h null because the window starts at y 1240. So the hex is no_dem by Test 1, with or without the anchor. In fact the whole of row 38 is no_dem.
- Gehon Or moves from 47,38 to 48,39. Cell 47,38 is no_dem (centre (1520,1232), h null). Cell 48,39 is open_sea: `--bbox 1536,1248,1568,1280` gives land_frac 0. Both tests come before any anchor test, so the hexes keep their classes. The new point also probes as sea (`--at 1540,1261` gives h -44.3). That is a registration issue for the anchor-correction step, not a filigree count change.
- Hordon moves from 35,54 to 35,52. Cell 35,54 keeps the Maeges anchor at the same coordinates (1139,1730), and it is coast anyway (land_frac 0.95). Cell 35,52 has land_frac 0.81, so it is coast by Test 7, before Test 9 (settlement). It is coast with or without the anchor.
- Tamaron stays in 51,48, and Lepon the Old stays in 35,44, so the ruin count stays 1. Sheet one (B-55, x1216-1760 by y1376-1664, cells 38-54 by 43-51) has no hex change.
- Test 3 uses detail-charts names and Test 4 uses Aldorūs. Neither of those anchors moves.

The one real impact downstream is on placement, not counts. Once Hordon's anchor leaves Maeges' dot, Test 9 and town_name instances that are placed at an anchor follow the new coordinates. The cell is still classed coast, so this changes no six. Any future anchor move should re-run this check as a gate (the B-02 tests, scripted with tools/filigree-dem.js), not be assumed to cause a bible amendment.

Fixing it means re-cutting B0/R1, because the gate says cityCanvasSha must equal B0. The cause is that genCityCanvas and sampleCityMask both read CITY_ANCHORS[key].atlasX/atlasY, and mobile-capture hashes only cityReg entries with prov 'invented' and a data: URL (Tamaron, Sokundo, Kanae). "Owner Q6" appears in no source doc and in the dossier only as the table's own phrase. The B0/R1 rebaseline requirement is a reasonable inference from "equal to B0", not a stated procedure.

Tamaron is one of the three cities the capture descends into, and sampleCityMask samples the z5 tiles at ox/oy, which are derived from atlasX/atlasY. A seam clip (c) keeps UG3 and UG7 only under three conditions. First, it is applied at display time, for example as a CSS clip-path or mask on the existing L.imageOverlay in pCity and on the wash overlay in pCityWash, not on the pane, which also holds the road-stub polylines. Second, the clip path is computed in a new non-pinned function from the already-returned mask. Third, it adds no pane. Baking the clip into the canvas or the data URL breaks cityCanvasSha even from a new helper outside the five pinned functions. Code inside genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask also breaks atlas_fn_sha. A new pane breaks UG7. Even a display-only clip changes atlas shots, so it must be a declared change. It belongs to filigree slice C (painted city, pooled edges), not a standalone patch. It only hides pixels across the seam and does not fix misregistration.

The claim's list of placements that break the hash is incomplete. Any clip written into the invented city's data: URL breaks cityCanvasSha, even from a new helper that touches none of the five pinned functions. Only a display-time clip is safe: a CSS clip-path or mask on the overlay's , plus the pCityWash overlay. It must be on the element, not the pane, because pCity also holds the road-stub polylines. 2. Calling the CSS clip simply "should be done" overstates it. - The clip still changes atlas screenshots, so it needs declared change keys. - It falls in filigree slice C's ownership (pooled city edges). - placement-consumers.json notes that a clip "hides pixels; it does not move the box". So it is a seam cosmetic. It is not the registration fix the owner's misalignment needs. **Status of (b).** "Canon overlays are never hashed" is true: Epēshu and Summarch are canon and fail the prov filter. votes.corrected: In docs/mobile the ten names (Penthelon, Damoklir, Paga, Pontoron, Zhomphek, Philider, Permūr, Hordon, Līrider, Dargan) appear in two forms. Both come from the wiki markers, and neither comes from maps-site/data/city-anchors.json or the CITY_ANCHORS literals. (1) baseline.json lists each as a "button:<name> — …" control with "marker": true. Hordon has a second control, "Hordon Mopher", and Līrider has "Līrider Hana". (2) The docs/mobile/captures/*.json tap-fixture records mention some of them, either as tapped glyph names (e.g. "name": "Zhomphek") or as "opened": "#place=Hordon|Penthelon|Pontoron|Dargan" card hashes from marker taps, mostly wrong-card ("outcome": "other") taps. The tap fixture (the TAP_VIEWS loop in tools/mobile-capture.js) taps the .glyph centre of marker glyphs from window.__mc.glyphs(), with views centred only on the Epēshu marker or the whole map. tapAtZoom is called only for Epēshu, and none of the ten is Epēshu. Marker latlngs are set from the marker data (m._mk, tools/mobile-capture.js and maps-site/index.html around MREF), not from CITY_ANCHORS. So moving a city-anchors.json entry changes no id, glyph position or tap target for these ten. A change to a marker position would not alter the button ids either, but it would shift glyph rects and tap coordinates. The claim's wording is wrong in two places. The names are not "only" button ids, because they also appear in capture tap records and "opened" hashes. The fixtures are not "centred on" these markers. Drāmūz is not one of the ten, and nothing was verified about it here.
votes.reason: The substantive conclusion holds. Both evidence quotes exist in the HEAD export. The Damoklir baseline entry reads "w": 16, "h": 16, "marker": true, and all ten have marker:true controls. The tapAtZoom line is verbatim. Markers are positioned independently of CITY_ANCHORS, so anchor moves leave these ids and tap targets unchanged. The wording overreaches in two ways. First, the names also appear in docs/mobile/captures/*.json tap records and #place= hashes, not only as button ids. Second, the quoted tapAtZoom fixture is used only for Epēshu, and TAP_VIEWS centres only on Epēshu or the whole map, so fixtures are not centred on the ten markers. The Drāmūz marker-fix contrast is an unverified extension.

votes.corrected: Only half right. Moving an anchor leaves the marker-derived mobile control ids alone, and it leaves the tapAtZoom/TAP_VIEWS fixtures alone, because both read window.ATLAS.find(n)._mk.getLatLng() or glyph rects, never CITY_ANCHORS. A marker fix such as Drāmūz does change those (controls.json and rebase-1.json carry "button:Drāmūz — settlements" and "#place=Drāmūz"). But anchor moves are not free of mobile rebases. Two of the ten worst off-dot names, Kanae and Sokundo (anchors-off-print.json summary.over_3px), and Tamaron from the correction table are exactly the three cities that mobile-capture.js descends into to hash cityCanvasSha. sampleCityMask(key) samples the mask window from CITY_ANCHORS[key].atlasX/atlasY, and cityBox/genCityCanvas build from the anchor too, so any move of these anchors changes cityCanvasSha. UG3 (docs/mobile/gates.md, README) requires cityCanvasSha to equal B0 on all five profiles (baseline.json holds cd1b54cc... for the dpr>1 class and 098da2e4... for desktop 1x). So moving Kanae, Sokundo or Tamaron needs a central, owner-approved B0 rebase of cityCanvasSha. Land it as its own unit outside the Mobile 5-9 atlas lane, or after it, so no in-flight unit fails UG3. The other off-dot names (Sjefenhold, Kolens, Shengo, Ūmak-nūs-Ion, Ītor Hāspira, Pomos, Ishin, Pish) need no mobile rebase, apart from any overlay-bounds change that shows up in a tap view's elementsFromPoint stack.
votes.reason: The evidence quoted is correct as far as it goes. Control ids and tap fixtures are keyed on wiki markers: tapAtZoom and setTapView use ATLAS.find(n)._mk.getLatLng(), and the ids are "button:<marker name> — <layer>". So a marker fix like Drāmūz would show up there and an anchor move would not. The claim says the ten names appear in docs/mobile "only" as button ids and that "moving these anchors needs no mobile control or tap-fixture rebase". That is too broad, because it leaves out the third place the mobile track pins placement: the cityCanvasSha determinism pin. mobile-capture.js runs ATLAS.descend over ['Tamaron','Sokundo','Kanae'] and hashes the seeded plans. sampleCityMask reads CITY_ANCHORS[key].atlasX/atlasY to choose which z5 tile window becomes the land/water mask, and that mask feeds genCityCanvas. Kanae and Sokundo are both in the ten-worst list (over_3px in out/anchors-off-print.json), and Tamaron is in out/anchor-correction-table.json. Moving any of them changes cityCanvasSha against B0 and fails UG3 on every profile, including in the Mobile 5-9 atlas lane that is mid-flight. A downstream-consumer audit that tells the owner the moves are rebase-free would set up a gate failure. The registration fix itself is still correct: it bends anchors to the atlas rings. It just has to be sequenced and paired with an explicit cityCanvasSha rebase. This is a placement (registration) issue, not a rendering-medium one: a vector city would hash or pin the same anchor-derived mask.

votes.corrected:
The claim mostly holds, but it needs some sharpening.

**LV5 and LV6 (Living fixture views).** Living 1 has not frozen anything yet. In the HEAD export, docs/living/gates does not exist, and the Living 1 POLISH item and the sea-mask item are both unchecked. So registration that lands before Living 1 adds no re-freeze cost to the living track. If registration lands after Living 1, the cost is still small: delete docs/living/gates/views.json and view/ and re-freeze (README §5.1).

What each change does to LV5/LV6:
- They resolve from the Epēshu anchor plus a zoom rule.
- (a), moving an anchor, changes the LV5/LV6 focus only if the Epēshu anchor itself moves. Epēshu is in the within-3 px set of anchor-correction-table.json and has no move verdict.
- (b), a canon translate+scale override, and (c), a seam clip, keep the focus. They change only the pixels the stills capture.
- LV6 also depends on cityMaxZ, so if (b) changes the box size, re-check LV6.

**The sea-mask check (`--check`).** It is a separate item, blocked by Filigree 4 and by Mobile 9 and 14, so it will probably run after registration anyway. As written, the Done-when cannot pass whichever anchors move:
- In the colour test, only 14 of the 38 in-scope anchors pass at the anchor. At the marker it is 21 of 38.
- 16 anchors fail at both positions.
- 19 pairs carry a colour test the table itself marks unreliable.
- Harbor anchors with `sea:null` (for example Ion Ephel) leave `distPx` undefined.

So the item's own threshold or scope needs amending, for example a reliable-pair subset and a default `distPx`. Moving anchors to the printed ○ improves the pass rate but does not fix the check.

**Rendering medium.** Neither consumer is affected by raster versus vector on its own terms. Registration is what changes them.

1. LC7 is owner-gated and applies only 'inside the Epēshu window'. Tamaron and Lepon the Old are outside it, so the zoom-through does not depend on their anchors.
2. POLISH.md describes 'Sim ↔ atlas continuity' as 'matching deep-link vocabulary both ways (sim #goto= ↔ atlas #chart=)'. That is hash vocabulary, not coordinate agreement, so it does not 'rely on' anchor agreement.
3. No cited source shows that a Tamaron or Lepon sim edit moves the Street baselines. The Street frozen views are Epēshu street views. The UG3 fingerprint shift is a plausible inference from changed routes and distances, not something a source states.

Also, q13-c02 says the transform is valid only for seed 'epeshu'.

votes.corrected: The coordinate match is real, but nothing reads it while the apps run. q13-c02's transform (1060+g*800/768, 1240+g*800/768) gives Tamaron grid 574,296 -> 1657.9,1548.3, the same as city-anchors.json. So the two apps agree today, but only because the numbers happen to line up. The sim never reads city-anchors.json, the atlas never reads the sim's gridX/gridZ, and the cross-links between them use place names: LC7 and "Sim ↔ atlas continuity" both go through #s=epeshu&goto=<place> (applyGotoFromHash / gotoSettlement), and POLISH describes continuity as "matching deep-link vocabulary". The LC7 zoom-through also covers only the Epēshu window. So moving an atlas anchor to sit on the printed ring (registration bends the anchor to the atlas: Tamaron's ring is at about 1658.8,1554.1 per q07, 6 px off the anchor) can be done in maps-site only. It breaks no link and does not touch UG3, cityCanvasSha inputs other than the anchor, or the Street baselines. What changes is that the sim's settlement then sits a few px away from the atlas ring on terrain (EPESHU_HF over the same [1060,1860)x[1240,2040) window) that otherwise matches. Record that drift per city (e.g., in q13 or the gazetteer) and do not fix it as a side effect. Moving the sim to match is a separate, optional central task: it rebases the B0 simDays fingerprint for epeshu and the Street baselines, and it only matters for Epēshu, whose anchor already matches the sim. Do not make anchor moves wait on it. The cityLabels part is correct: they are dx/dz offsets in sim world units around s.x/s.z, so the atlas does not consume them.
votes.reason: I checked the facts in the HEAD export. Tamaron grid 574,296 maps to 1657.9,1548.3, matching city-anchors.json. Lepon the Old 1146.5,1420.2 matches too. cityLabels are offsets in sim space. Simulated positions would change the fingerprint (agent routes and departDay are in it). Where the claim goes wrong is the coupling. "Moving an anchor either breaks sim-atlas agreement that LC7 and continuity rely on, or forces a sim edit" is a false dilemma. LC7 and "Sim ↔ atlas continuity" land by place name (goto=<place>, POLISH line "matching deep-link vocabulary"), not by coordinate. LC7 is limited to the Epēshu window, so neither Tamaron nor Lepon is involved. No code in maps-site uses the sim transform; only the offline tools/filigree-dem.js does. So anchor registration fixes can be made in the atlas alone (correctly, the atlas is authoritative) with no Street or mobile-sim rebase. A sim edit stays an optional, separately scheduled choice. Its rebase cost is real but is not caused by anchor moves. If the claim's applies_to_us were followed as written, atlas registration fixes would wait on sim and baseline rebases they don't need.

votes.reason: Claim says no doc or tool holds a Summarch coordinate literal and that every 523/542 hit is a substring of something else. Grep of the HEAD export disproves this. maps-site/data/factions.json line 69 has "seat": {"label":"Summarch","x":523,"y":58}. maps_markers.json (x 542, y 52) and gazetteer.json (x 542, y 52) both hold Summarch with those coordinates. factions.json is consumed by atlas code (flyTo on f.seat), so 523,58 is not confined to meshedWorldInit. The first evidence quote (CITY_ANCHORS['Summarch']) exists and the A-U11 quote exists, but the claim overreaches them.

votes.corrected: Moving Summarch's anchor is not a one-literal change, and it is not free for every track except the A-U11 shot. In the HEAD export, the literal 523,58 appears in three places: maps-site/index.html meshedWorldInit (CITY_ANCHORS['Summarch']={atlasX:523,atlasY:58,...}), maps-site/data/factions.json (the Allhammers seat: "seat": { "label": "Summarch", "x": 523, "y": 58 }) and maps-site/data/party-route.json ("name": "Summarch", "x": 523, "y": 58). The atlas loads both JSON files (getJSON('data/factions.json') and getJSON('data/party-route.json')). factions.json drives the faction-seat badges (clampToFrame(f.seat.x,f.seat.y)) and the 'show on the map' fly-to (flyTo(f.seat.x,f.seat.y,'c')). The 542 hits are not just substrings either. maps-site/data/maps_markers.json (x 542, y 52, mag true) and maps-site/data/gazetteer.json (x 542, y 52) hold Summarch's wiki marker, and tools/build-gazetteer.js generates the gazetteer, so it must be regenerated rather than hand-edited. To move the anchor, first decide which point the atlas art supports: the wiki marker (542,52), the current anchor (523,58), or a newly registered point. Then update CITY_ANCHORS, factions.json and party-route.json together, or derive the seat and the route point from the anchor. Leave the wiki marker alone unless the atlas shows it is wrong. After that, re-take the mobile A-U11 max-zoom shot and confirm that the faction-seat badge and the party-route line still sit on the city.
votes.reason: I checked the claim against the HEAD export and it is wrong on its own evidence. The literal 523,58 is not only in meshedWorldInit. It is also in maps-site/data/factions.json and maps-site/data/party-route.json, and the atlas loads and draws both of them (seat badges, seat fly-to, party route). The claim also says every 542 hit is a substring, but maps_markers.json and gazetteer.json both hold Summarch's own wiki marker at (542,52). That puts the canon marker 19 px from the anchor, which is itself relevant to the registration question. If the anchor moved under this claim, the Summarch city overlay would shift while the faction seat badge and the party-route point stayed at the old spot. That is exactly the kind of zoom misalignment the owner complained about. So the claim's applies_to_us conclusion, that the fix is cheap and the only cost is A-U11, does not hold. The A-U11 cost and the rule that the atlas wins over art still apply.

votes.corrected: tools/build-gazetteer.js adds a city-anchors.json entry only when no marker has the same folded name (fold = NFD, strip diacritics, lowercase), and the result is written to maps-site/data/gazetteer.json. Of the 33 anchors, about 29 have no same-named marker, so they reach gazetteer.json from the anchor loop (checked: Sokundo, Kanae, Mago, Aldorūs, Pharzeban, Lepon the Old). Only Epēshu, Tamaron and Drāmūz are shadowed by markers, so moving any anchor-only entry changes gazetteer.json. 'Lepon the Old' is anchor-only: the marker is named 'Lepon' (x1145, y1427) and the anchor 'Lepon the Old' (1146.5, 1420.2), so the names differ and both appear as separate gazetteer entries (Lepon, Settlements; Lepon the Old, ruin). Moving that anchor therefore changes gazetteer.json. Both B-19 and B-40 in docs/filigree/density-bible.json cite gazetteer.json. Regenerate with node tools/build-gazetteer.js after moving any anchor-only anchor.
votes.reason: Confirmed: the add() dedupe logic, the Lepon / Lepon the Old entries, and q12-c02 (F11: 1 marker, 1 anchor, 2 gazetteer entries). B-19 and B-40 both mention the gazetteer. The claim overreaches on 'None of the top-10 off-dot names reach gazetteer.json through it': no top-10 off-dot list is cited, and most anchors (Sokundo, Kanae, Mago, Aldorūs, Pharzeban and others) are anchor-only and do enter the gazetteer through the anchors loop. It holds only if the top 10 are all marker-shadowed, and only three anchors are. The Lepon reasoning is also garbled: it reaches the gazetteer because its anchor name differs from the marker name, not because the marker is named 'Lepon'.

votes.corrected:
Mostly right, but the wording needs fixing. tools/build-gazetteer.js, in the add() function, adds markers first. It adds an anchor only when no marker has the same fold()ed name. At HEAD, 119 anchors are shadowed by a marker and only 17 reach gazetteer.json through the anchor path: Sokundo, Kanae, Mago, Aldorūs, Rēketis, Āglaz, Mīth Mirdānak, Pharzeban, Sardil, Perōna, Tarap, Thalbaen, Medem, Shengo, Kardunash, Rhup and Lepon the Old.

'Lepon the Old' gets in because its folded name ('lepon the old') does not equal the marker's ('lepon'). The marker does not cause it. The gazetteer therefore holds two entries for one place: Lepon (Settlements, 1145,1427, from the marker) and Lepon the Old (ruin, 1146.5,1420.2, from the anchor).

Corrected rule: after any city-anchors.json edit, regenerate the gazetteer with `node tools/build-gazetteer.js`, as CLAUDE.md already requires for anchor or marker edits. Regenerating is sufficient only for the 17 anchors that have no same-name marker. For the 119 shadowed anchors, moving the anchor never changes gazetteer.json. The gazetteer keeps the marker's coordinates, so the two now disagree. Regenerating cannot fix that, so either move the marker too or record the split as intended. The same applies to alias pairs like Lepon / Lepon the Old: moving the anchor separates the pair. Check B-19's ranked naming and B-40's Elder Chart name sourcing against the regenerated file.

All of this is downstream bookkeeping for REGISTRATION (where the anchor sits). It has nothing to do with whether the city layer is raster or vector. Anchor moves must also follow the atlas (bend data to the atlas, never the reverse).
votes.reason:
The code confirms the claim's mechanism: `if(seen.has(key)) return` in add(), with markers.forEach running before the anchors loop. Running the fold against HEAD data gives 17 anchors that are not shadowed and 119 that are, and Lepon the Old is one of the 17. The density bible confirms that B-19 and B-40 consume gazetteer.json. However, the claim says Lepon the Old gets in 'because its marker is named Lepon'. That is backwards: it gets in because the names differ after folding.

The recommended action is correct and safe. It is deterministic, has no runtime cost, does not touch the mobile pins or genCityCanvas, and is already policy in CLAUDE.md. It is incomplete in one way: for most anchors, which are marker-shadowed, regenerating has no effect, and moving the anchor silently splits the anchor from the gazetteer's coordinates. That case needs its own handling. Severity is minor because this is index hygiene, not the root cause of the zoom misalignment, which is cityBox registration.

votes.corrected: All four quotes exist and read as stated, but the claim leaves out that A-U2 has not landed. At HEAD, unit A-U2 is status "failed" after 3 attempts, and maps-site/index.html still has the relative tierZoom (fitZoom + range/3 and 2*range/3, with TIER_CEIL=RETINA?5:6). There is no Z_TIER_B or Z_TIER_C. docs/mobile/captures/A-U2.json is a measurement of the rejected candidate, not of shipped code. The candidate's tiers (a/b/c/d) are {desktop 2.35/3.4/4.2/7.5, iphone13 1.9/3.4/4.2/7.5, pixel7 2.4/3.4/4.2/7.5, landscape 0.7/3.4/4.2/7.5, desktop2x 2.6/3.4/4.2/7.5}. The b, c and d values are identical on all five profiles, so the candidate does remove the tier spread; `a` varies by design. The failure was UG8 on desktop: the epeshu_z4.55 tap-fixture counts went 269 to 270, 187 to 189, 165 to 166 and 22 to 23. The accept file expected those keys unchanged, although the unit's own acceptance text says they should be declared. The fly-target caveat is correct. HEAD revealZoom is Math.max(map.getZoom(), tierZoom(t)). The old formula gives the 1x desktop B 3.5667 and C 4.7833. Owner answer q1=a (docs/mobile/owner-answers.json) pins B/C to the desktop2x values 3.40/4.20. A-U2's own acceptance says "desktop flyTo targets unchanged" while also accepting the earlier 1x reveal, so it contradicts itself. Pinning to 4.20 also changes the phone fly targets: iphone13 C 3.9667 to 4.20, pixel7 4.1333 to 4.20, landscape 3.5667 to 4.20. Desktop2x is unchanged at 4.20. The citations do not support "the only pending atlas unit that fixes tier-thresholds-viewport-dpr", and "the dossier's tier-thresholds cheap fix is redundant" cannot be checked from them. The label "tier-thresholds-viewport-dpr" appears nowhere in the head repo, and no other unit in docs/mobile/units.json (A-U3, A-U10) carries a tier fix. The narrowest supported claim is that A-U2 is the only unit in the mobile units file that targets the viewport- and DPR-dependent tier thresholds. It is failed and unlanded, and if re-cut with owner answer a it would make b, c and d identical on all profiles.
votes.reason: The quotes and the fly-target arithmetic check out against docs/mobile/captures/A-U2.json, units.json, owner-answers.json and the revealZoom/tierZoom code. The claim overreaches on status and scope. state.json marks A-U2 failed (UG8 tap-fixture drift), HEAD still has the relative tierZoom, and the capture is of an unlanded candidate. The "listed shift source" and "dossier" are not in the cited sources.

votes.corrected: A-U2 is not pending. docs/mobile/state.json records it as "failed" after 3 attempts, and that left A-U3 and A-U4 "skipped". The tiers in docs/mobile/captures/A-U2.json (b 3.4, c 4.2 and d 7.5 on all five profiles; `a` varies with minZoom) come from the failed attempt's build, atlas_sha e2fd37cc. They do not come from HEAD (4f9757bf), where tierZoom still derives from fitZoom and the RETINA TIER_CEIL. At HEAD the spread therefore stays: desktop C is 4.7833 and iphone13 C is 3.9667. The attempt failed on exactly the 1x-desktop epeshu_z4.55 tap-fixture deltas (270/189/166/23 vs 269/187/165/22). units.json A-U2 acceptance itself tells the run to declare these deltas, so the fix is to re-run A-U2 with those keys declared in its accept file. It does not need a separate tier change. The dossier row tier-thresholds-viewport-dpr already says "do not build it separately", so no cheap fix is pending that A-U2 would make redundant. The flyTo caveat is real. revealZoom, flyTo and the line-1209 fly all use max(z, tierZoom('c')), so the 1x-desktop fly target from minZoom drops from 4.7833 to 4.20. That contradicts "desktop flyTo targets unchanged" but matches owner answer q1=a ("1x desktops reveal earlier"). The acceptance line should say "desktop2x flyTo targets unchanged". Phone targets move later, not earlier: iphone13 goes 3.97→4.20, pixel7 4.13→4.20 and landscape 3.57→4.20. For the owner's ask, tier thresholds are PRESENTATION: they change which marks show and at what zoom, not where anything sits. Landing A-U2 fixes none of the REGISTRATION misalignment between the atlas and the city art (cityBox/FOOT_R), and none of the raster-vs-vector medium question. Leave it to the mobile lane (Mobile 5 re-run). The anchoring work should not count it as an alignment fix.
votes.reason: I checked the claim against the HEAD export. Some figures are right. In captures/A-U2.json, tiers b/c/d are identical on all 5 profiles. tiers_derived for desktop gives C 4.7833, and revealZoom = max(getZoom(), tierZoom(t)), so the flyTo tension with owner answer q1=a is real. Three framings are wrong. (1) Status: state.json has A-U2 "failed", attempts 3, failing UG8 on desktop tap_fixture deltas that units.json says should have been declared. The capture comes from a non-HEAD atlas_sha, and HEAD tierZoom still uses fitZoom, so nothing has "landed" and A-U3/A-U4 are blocked. (2) "The dossier's cheap fix is redundant": the dossier row already defers to A-U2 ("do not build it separately"), so there is nothing to retire. (3) Relevance to the ask: tier thresholds decide which marks show, not where they sit. They are not a registration source for the atlas-to-city-art misalignment, and they have nothing to do with raster vs vector. The phone fly-target change is a later reveal (3.97/4.13/3.57 → 4.20), so it is not the same change as the earlier reveal on 1x desktop. Acting on it is correct only as a mobile-lane re-run. The anchoring work should neither duplicate it nor count it as an alignment fix.

prior_record.claim: A-U11 is the only atlas unit that hot-swaps an overlay URL: a 720 px preview, then the same full plate. No unit changes overlay bounds. Bounds stay exact if the registerCityOverlay literal w/h are kept, as the spec requires. The swap mechanism is unspecified. evidence.quote: after load the full image is the same file and the final shot equals R1 at max zoom; registerCityOverlay literal kept
if(CITYVIEW.name===key){CITYVIEW.name=null;ensureCityOverlay(key);} // hot-swap if viewing
CITYREG[key]={url:url,w:w,h:h,prov:opts.prov||'invented'

votes.corrected: Within docs/mobile/units.json, A-U11 is the only unit that touches overlay art (only unit matching overlay/cityBox/registerCity/CITYREG/imageOverlay). It adds 720 px previews and requires "after load the full image is the same file ... registerCityOverlay literal kept". No unit changes cityBox bounds. The swap mechanism is unspecified. If it is a second registerCityOverlay call, then: bounds come from cityBox(a,reg.w,reg.h) rebuilt after overlayCache.delete, so they stay exact only if the literal w/h are kept. The hot-swap line sets CITYVIEW.name=null and calls ensureCityOverlay, which removes the overlay, POI layer, wash and stubs and then rebuilds them. That is the same path as the runtime synthetic-to-melded swap in ensureCityGen. Omitting opts would reset prov to 'invented' and null provText, poiRef, pois and stubs. Wording nuance: "tears down" means tear down and rebuild, not permanent loss. "Only unit" is scoped to units.json, because the runtime synthetic-to-melded swap already hot-swaps URLs in code.
votes.reason: Verified in HEAD export. The units.json A-U11 acceptance quote is verbatim. registerCityOverlay contains the CITYREG assignment with opts.prov||'invented', overlayCache.delete(key), and the "hot-swap if viewing" line. ensureCityOverlay removes the overlay, POI layer, wash and stubs, then recreates them with washMake, buildCityStubs and buildWorldPOIs. The Epēshu canon registration quote is verbatim. ensureCityGen and ensureCityGenNow use the same registerCityOverlay hot-swap path. No other unit in units.json mentions overlay or bounds, and no unit text specifies how the swap is done. The only imprecision is "tears down" versus tear down and rebuild, and the "only unit" scope.

votes.corrected: Holds with a sharper consequence. A-U11 (Mobile 6, defect A7) is the only mobile unit that touches the city overlay. Its acceptance pins the full file and "registerCityOverlay literal kept", so the bounds stay cityBox(a, reg.w, reg.h) whatever pixel size the 720 px preview has. Registration is untouched by A-U11; it only changes which raster sits inside the same box. The anchor work therefore does not need to wait on A-U11 for alignment. A per-city cityBox override or a registered transform lands in cityBox/ensureCityOverlay, and the preview and the full plate both inherit it, provided the swap keeps the existing L.ImageOverlay. What does need coordinating is the swap mechanism. Ask A-U11 to swap with the Leaflet 1.9.4 ImageOverlay.setUrl() on the cached overlay (overlayCache/lruPut entry) after the full image's onload. It should not call registerCityOverlay a second time. A second call deletes the cache, re-runs ensureCityOverlay (tearing down and rebuilding wash, stubs and POIs, which flickers at max zoom), and without opts it resets prov to 'invented' and drops pois/poiRef/stubs. A canon seam mask must read CITYREG[key].prov, not the overlay URL or natural size. Any swap crossfade belongs to the living/filigree tracks, not to the registration fix. A seam mask built inside washMake changes a source-hash-pinned function (UG3 atlas_fn_sha), so it has to go into the pin manifest centrally after the Mobile 5-9 lane lands. That timing, not A-U11 itself, is the real sequencing constraint.
votes.reason:
The code backs every factual part of the claim, read from the HEAD export of maps-site/index.html and docs/mobile:
- registerCityOverlay always runs overlayCache.delete(key). When the city is being viewed it sets CITYVIEW.name=null and calls ensureCityOverlay, which removes and rebuilds the overlay, wash (washMake), stubs (buildCityStubs) and POIs (buildWorldPOIs).
- Missing opts gives prov 'invented' and null pois/poiRef/stubs.
- The canon literals are w:2863,h:3072 for Epēshu and w:3072,h:2859 for Summarch.
- In docs/mobile/units.json, A-U11 is the only unit whose text mentions overlays or bounds. Its mechanism is unspecified: the brief, inputs/brief.md row A7, says only "swap to the full image on load, or cut the overlay into the tile pyramid".
- ensureCityOverlay derives the bounds only from cityBox(a, reg.w, reg.h), so a preview with a different pixel size keeps the box exact.

Where the original applies_to_us goes wrong:
- It treats the cityBox override as something that must "attach where A-U11's swap passes". Registration is decided in cityBox/ensureCityOverlay, and A-U11 does not change bounds, so the two are orthogonal. They only collide if the swap rebuilds the overlay.
- It names the wrong ordering constraint. The real one is the UG3 source-hash pin on washMake and the mid-flight atlas lane.
- It leaves the swap mechanism open when an in-stack answer exists: Leaflet 1.9.4 ImageOverlay.setUrl.

None of this breaks determinism (no gen code changes) or the rule that DM art is canon.

items.summary: Refuted: the UG3 gate mechanics are right, but the cited sources do not show the off-dot or sea-side faults or the no-shared-code assertion.

summaries.1-shift: Refuted: the UG3 gate mechanics are right, but the cited sources do not show the off-dot or sea-side faults or the no-shared-code assertion.
summaries.2-registration: The pinned-hash quotes are real, but the claim's sequencing conclusion did not hold (detail truncated in the check text).
summaries.3-vector: The claimed independence of registration fixes from A-U units and the 'wrong sea sides' were not shown by the cited sources.
summaries.5-ownership: Refuted: gate mechanics right, but 'shares no code with any A-U unit' and 'wrong sea sides' were not shown; data fixes still change the hashed plan inputs.

prior_record.claim: The registration cheap fixes (anchors, trait sea.side, marker snaps, gates) do not share code with any A-U unit. They collide with the lane only through gates: UG3 cityCanvasSha hashes the invented plans of Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae, which are off-dot and have wrong sea sides. Canon cities are excluded, so the Summarch literal and the Epēshu override do not trip it.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: anchor-on-label, trait-sea-side-vs-atlas, marker-anchor-pixel-bias and gates-ignore-atlas-roads land after G9 with an owner-approved rebaseline.

evidence.quote: for (const n of ['Tamaron', 'Sokundo', 'Kanae']) {
if (!e || e.prov !== 'invented' || !/^data:/.test(e.url || '')) continue
cityCanvasSha is equal to B0 **and equal across all five profiles**

votes.corrected: The three quotes are real. In tools/mobile-capture.js the city-canvas determinism step loops `for (const n of ['Tamaron', 'Sokundo', 'Kanae'])` calling ATLAS.descend, then hashes the `data:` URL of each ATLAS.cityReg entry whose `prov === 'invented'`. docs/mobile/gates.md UG3 requires "cityCanvasSha is equal to B0 and equal across all five profiles". Epēshu and Summarch are registered with prov 'canon' (image URLs 'art/overlay-*.jpg'), so they are skipped. The hashed plans come from genCityCanvas, which reads the anchor atlasX/atlasY and the trait sea.side. So changing those anchors or sea sides for any invented city whose plan is registered would change cityCanvasSha and fail UG3 unless B0 is rebaselined. Narrowest supported claim: the hash covers the invented plans (not only the three named, as the hash includes every invented entry in cityReg after the descents), and canon cities are excluded. Not supported by the cited evidence: (a) that Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae are "off-dot" with "wrong sea sides" (no cited source says so; city-anchors.json only lists sea sides E, WSW and E), and (b) that registration fixes "do not share code with any A-U unit" (nothing cited was checked against the A-U unit file targets). The "land after G9 with owner-approved rebaseline" step is a recommendation inferred from UG3, not a stated rule.
votes.reason: The gate mechanics (the three-city loop, invented-only data-URL hash, UG3 equal to B0 and across profiles, canon cities skipped) are confirmed in code. The claim overreaches the cited quotes on two points: the cities being off-dot with wrong sea sides, and the no-shared-code assertion about A-U units. Neither is shown by any cited source.

votes.corrected: These are registration fixes; the rendering medium is untouched. Sequence them all after G9 (Mobile 9 passed), when maps-site/index.html is no longer held. (1) Data-only fixes: anchor-on-label edits to atlasX/atlasY in maps-site/data/city-anchors.json and sea.side fixes in maps-site/data/city-traits.json. They change no pinned function, but they change the inputs to the invented plans. sampleCityMask builds its window from a.atlasX/atlasY, and genCityCanvas reads t.sea.side and distPx. So cityCanvasSha for Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae moves, and the UG3 equality with B0 fails until the owner approves a B0 rebaseline. The byte change also leaves maps-site/data/offline-manifest.json stale, which build-offline-manifest.js --check catches and G9/G14 re-check, so regenerate it with --atlas in the same change. Land them in one central change before the sim lane's G14, or have G14 compare against the rebased B0, because UG3 also runs there. (2) Marker-anchor-pixel-bias snaps are code changes in the divIcon marker code that A-U3, A-U4 and A-U5 edit. They also break those units' invariants ("glyphs never move", "marker glyph rects equal R1"). So they need their own unit after G9 that declares that change and re-takes the R1/final glyph-rect references; this is more than a UG3 rebaseline. (3) The gates-ignore-atlas-roads fix touches tools/mobile-capture.js and the accept files. That is central tooling, so do it centrally with no agent and no lane unit. Canon cities (Epēshu, Summarch) stay out of cityCanvasSha because the hash skips anything that is not prov 'invented' with a data: URL. Their registration is a separate step: overlay bounds/affine work in cityBox, which is not pinned.
votes.reason: Partly verified at HEAD. The UG3 capture walks Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae and hashes only reg entries with prov 'invented' and a data: URL. So canon Epēshu and Summarch overlays are excluded, which is correct. Anchor and sea-side edits do move cityCanvasSha: sampleCityMask derives its tile window from a.atlasX/atlasY, and genCityCanvas uses t.sea.side and distPx; city-traits.json has Tamaron E, Sokundo WSW, Kanae E. I did not verify the claim that these sides are wrong against the atlas, and I did not check whether the three dots are off. Two parts of the claim are overstated. First, it says the fixes "do not share code with any A-U unit" and collide "only through gates/UG3". Marker snaps would edit the same L.divIcon marker code that A-U3, A-U4 and A-U5 touch, and they contradict those units' acceptance terms ("glyphs never move", "marker glyph rects equal R1"). Second, any byte change to maps-site data makes the A-U7 offline manifest stale (tools/build-offline-manifest.js compares the per-file bytes record). --check then fails, and G9/G14 re-check it. So the collisions are wider than the one cityCanvasSha gate. The applies_to_us direction ("after G9 with owner-approved rebaseline") is right but incomplete: it also needs the manifest regenerated, the marker glyph-rect references re-taken by a declared unit, G14 coordination because UG3 also runs on the sim lane, and the gate-tool fix done centrally.

items.summary: Refuted: glyph-moving fixes conflict with A-U3/A-U4 only when made inside a mobile unit, only two of the four named fixes move glyphs, and 'only after G9' is stronger than the gates support.

summaries.1-shift: Refuted: glyph-moving fixes conflict with A-U3/A-U4 only when made inside a mobile unit, only two of the four named fixes move glyphs, and 'only after G9' is stronger than the gates support.
summaries.2-registration: Glyph-moving fixes conflict with A-U3/A-U4 as a sequencing and rebase cost, not a rule that they must wait for G9.
summaries.5-ownership: Refuted: gates score against the reference in force and rebase() re-takes it after a non-mobile edit, so glyph-coordinate fixes do not conflict with A-U3/A-U4 outside a mobile unit.

prior_record.claim: Fixes that move glyphs conflict with A-U3/A-U4 acceptance: marker-anchor-pixel-bias, route-faction-coords-off-town, faction-spread-in-map-px and clamp-pad-map-px. Route/faction is the sharpest case, because A-U3 fixes the Lektān badge stacked on Epēshu (A2) without moving it.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: These four sources can only land after G9.

evidence.quote: glyphs never move (no badge offset): marker glyph rects equal R1
marker glyph rects equal R1 (map-region shot diff <= 0.5% by the metrics.md section 7 function)
if(n){var ang=(n-1)*2.3999+0.5;ox=Math.cos(ang)*14;oy=Math.sin(ang)*14;}

votes.corrected: Both acceptance quotes are real and say what is cited. A-U3 says "glyphs never move (no badge offset): marker glyph rects equal R1". A-U4 says "marker glyph rects equal R1 (map-region shot diff <= 0.5% ...)". A-U3 also fixes A2 (Epēshu z4.55 tap opened the Lektān card) by a tap resolver and chooser, not by moving glyphs. That differs on purpose from the A2 text in docs/mobile/inputs.json, which says "Offset faction badges from their seat glyph". The narrowest supported claim is this: any change that shifts a marker or badge glyph on the atlas would fail the A-U3/A-U4 "glyph rects equal R1" checks, and UG8 (desktop identity) for every unit in the lane unless the unit declares the changed keys. Two cited mechanisms exist in maps-site/index.html. Faction badges sharing a seat get a 14 map-px spread (buildFactionBadges: ox/oy from ang=(n-1)*2.3999+0.5). clampToFrame uses a 16 map-px pad. Nothing in the cited evidence supports the other two named fixes (marker-anchor-pixel-bias, route-faction-coords-off-town). The four slugs appear nowhere in the repo, so they would need their own evidence. "Can only land after G9" overreaches. G9 is the central gate that closes the atlas lane before Filigree 2. The acceptance files do not forbid glyph moves after A-U4. They forbid undeclared moves in units that score against R1, and a later unit can declare changed keys. G9 is a sensible scheduling choice, not something the evidence forces.
votes.reason: Quotes 1 and 2 verified exactly in docs/mobile/units.json (A-U3 and A-U4 acceptance). Quote 3 verified in buildFactionBadges. The sources support only two of the four named fixes (faction spread and clamp pad, both in map px) as glyph-moving. Nothing supports marker-anchor-pixel-bias or route-faction-coords-off-town. "Only after G9" is a stronger sequencing claim than the units.json acceptance, UG8 and G9 definitions support.

votes.corrected:
The conflict is real, but it is a sequencing and rebase cost, not a rule that the fixes must wait for G9. The fixes are marker-anchor-pixel-bias, route-faction-coords-off-town, faction-spread-in-map-px and clamp-pad-map-px. They are registration fixes for glyphs, so they move marker rects.

Inside a mobile unit they are forbidden. A-U3 says "glyphs never move (no badge offset): marker glyph rects equal R1". A-U4 says "marker glyph rects equal R1 (<= 0.5%)". Every later atlas unit's UG8 desktop identity is also scored against the current reference. So no mobile implementer may bundle them.

The plan has a sanctioned path for non-mobile app edits in docs/mobile/README.md: "may run when no mobile atlas unit holds maps-site/index.html; if it lands mid-lane, references are rebased before the next atlas unit". After G9, "any later non-mobile change to it triggers the rebase rule" against the Filigree 2 baseline sha. So the fixes can land:
(a) between atlas units, as a central non-mobile commit with an R1/tap-fixture rebase (costly mid-flight, not recommended), or
(b) preferably after G9, before Filigree 2 stamps its baseline, or folded into filigree slice B ink. Filigree owns glyph placement on the table map.

In every case the A-U3 tap fixture must be re-run after the move: wrong_card = 0 and the 22 px chooser pairs. Moved glyph centres change which pairs fall within 22 px. If A-U3 has not landed yet, A2 (Lektān on Epēshu) is still open.

On route/faction: A-U3 deliberately fixes A2 with a tap resolver. It overrides the inputs.json A2 suggestion to "offset faction badges". buildFactionBadges in maps-site/index.html offsets only the 2nd and later badges at a shared seat (`if(n){var ang=(n-1)*2.3999+0.5;ox=Math.cos(ang)*14;...}`), so the first badge sits exactly on the seat dot. A spread fix that also offsets the first badge would undo that ruling. It needs an explicit decision to supersede A-U3's "no badge offset", not just a later slot.

items.summary: Once A-U7 lands, a coarse-pointer zoom-button press steps 0.5 zoom (overlay 0.5, base about 0.244 per press, crossfade in 2 presses) and a press during an animated zoom loses 0.5; desktop is unchanged.

summaries.1-shift: Once A-U7 lands, a coarse-pointer zoom-button press steps 0.5 zoom (overlay 0.5, base about 0.244 per press, crossfade in 2 presses) and a press during an animated zoom loses 0.5; desktop is unchanged.
summaries.5-ownership: Once A-U7 lands (Mobile 8), one zoom-button press on coarse pointers is 0.5 zoom (overlay ramp in 2 presses, base about 0.244 per press, a press during animation lost); these are spec-derived figures for the buttons only, desktop unchanged.

prior_record.claim: A-U7 changes the magnitude of the zoom-step sources on coarse pointers. One press steps 0.5 zoom, so the overlay changes 0.5 per press, the base about 0.244 per press, and the overlay ramp takes 2 presses (fine pointers still take 4). A press dropped during an animated zoom loses 0.5. Desktop is unchanged.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: New figures for opacity-steps-on-animated-zoom, animating-zoom-drops-setview and crossfade-double-image on touch. These are derived from the spec, not measured.

evidence.quote: function overlayOpacity(z){if(z<=6.8)return 0;if(z>=7.8)return 1;return z-6.8;}
coarse: one zoom-button press changes zoom by 0.5; fine pointers keep today's step
zoomSnap:0,zoomDelta:.25,wheelPxPerZoomLevel:80,wheelDebounceTime:20,

votes.corrected: Holds as a spec-derived claim, with three limits. (1) A-U7 is a planned unit in docs/mobile/units.json. Its acceptance reads "coarse: one zoom-button press changes zoom by 0.5; fine pointers keep today's step"; at HEAD the map still has zoomDelta:.25 and no coarse branch. (2) The 0.5 step applies only to the +/- zoom-button presses, not to wheel or pinch zoom. The per-press figures hold only while the zoom sits inside the ramp: overlay 6.8-7.8 gives 0.5 per press (2 presses, against 4 at 0.25), and base 6.2-8 gives 0.5*0.88/1.8 = 0.244 per press. (3) The dropped-press part is not in the cited quotes. It follows from the vendored Leaflet 1.9.4 (maps-site/vendor/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js): while _animatingZoom is true, _tryAnimatedZoom returns without starting a zoom, and _zoom only updates when the animation ends. A press during an animated zoom is therefore ignored and loses its whole delta (0.5 on coarse). Desktop being unchanged follows from the fine-pointer acceptance line.
votes.reason: All four quotes exist at HEAD. overlayOpacity returns z-6.8 between 6.8 and 7.8, baseOpacity is 1-(z-6.2)/1.8*0.88, the L.map options include zoomSnap:0,zoomDelta:.25, and the A-U7 acceptance line is verbatim. The arithmetic checks out (0.5 step, 0.244 base per press, ramp 2 presses vs 4). The Leaflet dropped-press behaviour was verified in the vendored source. I did not run it in a browser. The overreach is minor: the claim does not say the step applies only to the zoom buttons, and the drop behaviour is not covered by any cited quote.

votes.corrected: These are spec-derived figures for the zoom buttons only. They apply once A-U7 lands (Mobile 8, not built at HEAD). On coarse pointers one button press is 0.5 zoom. That moves overlay opacity by 0.5 and base opacity by 0.244. The 6.8 to 7.8 overlay ramp takes 2 presses (4 at today's zoomDelta .25). A press made while Leaflet's zoom animation is running is dropped, which loses 0.5. Because zoomSnap is 0 and the start zoom is fractional, one press can land anywhere inside the ramp. Pinch and wheel are continuous and are not affected, and pinch is the main way to zoom on touch. None of this is measured. It is a timing and crossfade item for the mobile and living tracks, not a registration item: cityBox placement is unchanged, so overlays shift exactly as they do now.
votes.reason: I checked the arithmetic against HEAD and it is correct. overlayOpacity is linear over 6.8 to 7.8, so 0.5 per press and 2 presses at 0.5 (4 at zoomDelta .25). baseOpacity has a slope of 0.88/1.8 = 0.489 per zoom unit, so about 0.244 per half-step. Leaflet 1.9.4's Control.Zoom._zoomIn calls map.zoomIn(options.zoomDelta), so the button step is the zoomDelta the coarse-pointer change would alter. The claim about dropped presses also holds: zoomIn goes to setZoom and setView, and _tryAnimatedZoom starts with "if (this._animatingZoom) { return true; }", so a press during the animation does nothing. The map also already works around a stranded _animatingZoom flag ("clear a stranded zoom-anim flag, else _tryAnimatedZoom makes setView silently no-op"). The units.json acceptance text for A-U7 says exactly "coarse: one zoom-button press changes zoom by 0.5; fine pointers keep today's step", and desktop is unchanged. Three caveats belong in applies_to_us. First, A-U7 is pending (run "Mobile 8"), so these are future figures and nothing in the tree matches them yet. Second, the change covers button presses only; pinch and wheel zooming (zoomSnap 0) keep their continuous ramps. Third, it changes how coarsely the crossfade is sampled, not where the overlay sits. Seam misalignment comes from cityBox registration, and this unit does not touch it. So acting on it as a note for mobile and living-chart planning is right, but it is no evidence for an anchoring fix.

summaries.1-shift: A-U9 replaces the fixed 64% sheet with peek/half/full stops, so the +0.32H phone offset for panel-covers-fly-target goes stale and should be computed from the settled sheet geometry at open; the HEAD figures themselves are derived, not sourced.
summaries.5-ownership: A-U9 replaces the fixed 64% sheet with peek/half/full stops and a shared CSS variable, so the panel fly-target offset should be computed from the sheet's settled geometry, after A-U9 lands; the per-stop figures were derived, not measured.

prior_record.claim: A-U9 makes the dossier's +0.32H phone offset for panel-covers-fly-target stale. That figure comes from the fixed 64% sheet, which A-U9 replaces with peek / half / full stops and a shared CSS variable. Derived per stop on iphone13 (map 509 px): a 140 px peek leaves the target clear (offset about +0.14H), half needs +0.25H, and full covers it. The desktop −170 px still holds.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: The panBy offset should read the live sheet stop and variable, not a constant. Land it after A-U9 (Mobile 8).

evidence.quote: #panel{top:auto;left:0;right:0;bottom:0;width:auto;max-width:none;height:64%;
.panel-open #jbar{left:12px;bottom:calc(64% + 10px);}   /* ride above the bottom sheet */
jbar never intersects the sheet at peek or half (the shared CSS variable replaces calc(64% + 10px))
the A-U1 closed-sheet checks still hold; desktop side panel identical to R1

votes.corrected: All four quotes exist in the HEAD export. The mobile #panel rule is `height:64%`, and the jbar rule is `.panel-open #jbar{left:12px;bottom:calc(64% + 10px);}`. A-U9's acceptance says "peek height 100-140 px ... half = 50% ... full" and "jbar never intersects the sheet at peek or half (the shared CSS variable replaces calc(64% + 10px))". So the narrowest supported claim is this. Today's mobile sheet is a fixed 64% bottom sheet. A-U9 (Mobile 8) replaces it with peek (100-140 px), half (50%) and full stops, and replaces the jbar calc with a shared CSS variable. Any panel-covers-fly-target offset derived from the fixed 64% sheet would therefore have to be recomputed per stop. The per-stop figures are the claim's own arithmetic, not sourced. The arithmetic is internally consistent: 0.64/2 = 0.32H, 140/2/509 = 0.14H, and 0.5/2 = 0.25H of the map height. Three inputs are not in the cited sources or anywhere in the HEAD tree, so they stay unverified. First, the "dossier's +0.32H" figure: grep for 0.32 finds only unrelated weather rolls. Second, the desktop "-170 px" panBy offset: the only 170 is `.panel-open #jbar{left:calc(50% + 170px)}`, and there is no panBy offset in the flyTo, goWaypoint or flyIntoCity code. Third, the iphone13 map height of 509 px: the only 509 in the captures is the `h` of a region entry, not a map or stage rect. A-U9 also does not state what "half = 50%" is a percentage of (map or viewport). Also, no current code applies any offset for the open panel, so the "+0.32H" is a recommendation from elsewhere, not existing behavior. "Stale" and "desktop -170 px still holds" should be dropped or marked as unverified.
votes.reason: The cited quotes are present, but the claim's key figures (the dossier's +0.32H, the desktop -170 px, the 509 px map height) are not in any cited or findable source in HEAD, so the claim overreaches its evidence. Only the 64% fixed sheet and A-U9's peek/half/full plus shared-variable replacement are supported.

votes.corrected: The claim is right, with three refinements. (1) Base the offset on the sheet's resolved geometry, not on a constant or a raw CSS-variable string. At the moment the card opens, take the stop it is opening to, then compute dy = (mapH - visibleH)/2 from #panel's settled height. The rect has to be the settled one, because the transform transition runs .28s. Measured geometry also covers the A-U8 landscape side-sheet case, where the sign flips, without a second code path. (2) The offset is needed only where the sheet covers the target. On iphone13 (map 509 px) a 140 px peek leaves the target 114.5 px clear, so +0.14H there just re-centres the view and can be skipped. Half (sheet top at the centre) needs +0.25H, which is about 127 px. Full covers the target whatever the pan, so either don't fly into full or drop to half first. (3) Apply the same offset to the ensureArrival dest so the hard landing agrees with the fly. On desktop the panel is 340 px on the left (#panel width:340px), so panBy -170 px x still holds. That code is unchanged by A-U9 ("desktop side panel identical to R1"). Timing: land this after A-U9 (Mobile 8), in a central gap and not inside the mid-flight atlas lane. It does not touch the UG3-pinned functions. It is a UI-occlusion fix, not registration: it moves where the camera centres and never where art or geometry sits relative to the coast, rivers or roads.
votes.reason: Checked against HEAD and it holds. The mobile #panel is absolute inside #stage, alongside #map, with height:64%. So the open sheet covers 0.64 x 509 = 326 px of the iphone13 map. The visible band's centre sits 163 px (0.32H) above the map centre, which confirms +0.32H as the HEAD figure. A-U9's acceptance in docs/mobile/units.json does replace that fixed 64% with peek 100-140 px / half 50% / full and a shared CSS variable, so a hard-coded 0.32H goes stale once it lands. The per-stop numbers are right: peek 140 gives (509-369)/2 = 70 px, which is 0.1375H, and the target clears the sheet top by 114.5 px. Half gives 127 px (0.25H), with the target exactly on the sheet edge. Full covers it. The desktop -170 is half of the 340 px left panel, and A-U9 leaves the desktop panel untouched. The claim needs three refinements. First, at peek no offset is needed because the target is already clear; that case is cosmetic. Second, read the settled panel rect rather than parsing the variable, which also handles the A-U8 landscape case (C8). Third, flyIntoCity with poiN=0 calls closePanel(), so the offset matters only for POI flies, where openWorldPOI runs on moveend, and for the search, waypoint and card flies (flyTo, revealZoom sites) that open the sheet. This is UI occlusion, not registration, so it does nothing for the owner's misalignment. It is a small, correct mobile-correctness item to sequence after Mobile 8.

items.summary: Refuted: A-U10's lower coarse-portrait minZoom is owner-gated and not in HEAD, the deltas need the stage height, and its interaction with bounds-clamp and exitChart is broader than claimed.

summaries.1-shift: Refuted: A-U10's lower coarse-portrait minZoom is owner-gated and not in HEAD, the deltas need the stage height, and its interaction with bounds-clamp and exitChart is broader than claimed.
summaries.2-registration: A-U10 is owner-gated and not in HEAD, and the bounds-clamp effect worsens inside the band, not only at the edges.
summaries.5-ownership: Refuted: the minZoom drops reproduce only with capture stage heights, and the bounds-clamp extension and 'setMinZoom inert' claims were unsupported.

prior_record.claim: A-U10 lowers coarse-portrait minZoom to fitWidthZoom, by about 1.39 levels on iphone13 and 1.81 on pixel7 (estimated from HEAD constants). This extends the zoom range where bounds-clamp-slides-anchor applies, and makes the setMinZoom half of setminmax-zoom-race mostly inert on phones. Desktop is unchanged.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Keep the dossier's 'exitChart only, not refit' fix separate from A-U10's refit and fillZoom edits.

evidence.quote: coarse + portrait: minZoom = min(fillZoom, fitWidthZoom)
map.setMinZoom(s.minZoom); map.setMaxZoom(s.maxZoom);
var NZ=4, IMG_W=4390, IMG_H=2188, TILE_W=4608, TILE_H=2304;

votes.corrected: A-U10 (docs/mobile/units.json, owner-gated on q2, depends on A-U2/A-U8, not yet in the HEAD code) specifies that on coarse + portrait minZoom = min(fillZoom, fitWidthZoom), with desktop minZoom identical to R1. At HEAD, fillZoom() is IMG_H-based (4+log2(vh/2188)) and exitChart restores the saved s.minZoom/s.maxZoom. Lowering minZoom to fit-width means roughly 1.4 to 1.5 zoom levels on iphone13 and roughly 1.75 to 1.8 on pixel7, depending on the map stage height (about 509-553 px on iphone13). Those figures come from the harness viewport and measured share_visible, not from the cited constants alone. Whether this widens a "bounds-clamp-slides-anchor" zone or makes the setMinZoom half of a "setminmax-zoom-race" inert is the dossier's own inference. Neither term, nor the mechanism, appears in the repo, so it is unverified here.
votes.reason: The three quotes exist verbatim at HEAD. A-U10's acceptance in docs/mobile/units.json says "coarse + portrait: minZoom = min(fillZoom, fitWidthZoom)", and desktop minZoom is stated identical to R1. exitChart contains "map.setMinZoom(s.minZoom); map.setMaxZoom(s.maxZoom);". The constants line "var NZ=4, IMG_W=4390, IMG_H=2188, TILE_W=4608, TILE_H=2304;" is present in maps-site/index.html. The claim overreaches in four ways. First, the 1.39/1.81 figures are not derivable from the cited constants, because they need the map stage height. 1.39 matches a stage of about 509 px (the harness notes 390x509 z1.9), but 518 or 553 px gives about 1.41 to 1.51. The measured share_visible of 0.360 (iphone13) and 0.292 (pixel7) gives log2(1/share) of about 1.47 and 1.78, so 1.81 is slightly high. Second, "bounds-clamp-slides-anchor" and "setminmax-zoom-race" are not found anywhere in the HEAD repo or docs. The claim that A-U10 extends the first and makes half of the second inert is therefore unverifiable from the cited sources. Third, "mostly inert" is inference. exitChart still restores s.minZoom, which would now be the lowered value on phones. Fourth, A-U10 is a planned unit gated on owner answer q2, with a deferral path. The claim reads as if it were in effect, but it is not implemented at HEAD.

votes.corrected:
The deltas are right. A-U10 (units.json: "coarse + portrait: minZoom = min(fillZoom, fitWidthZoom)") lowers the world floor from fillZoom to 4+log2(vw/IMG_W). On iphone13 (390 px wide, fill 1.90) that is 0.51, a drop of about 1.39. On pixel7 (412 px wide) it is about 0.59, a drop of about 1.8. Desktop is unchanged.

Bounds-clamp-slides-anchor gets worse in that band, not only at the edges. Between fitWidth and fill the viewport is taller than contentBounds (maxBoundsViscosity 1.0), so Leaflet's _limitCenter centres the vertical axis. Every pinch or wheel zoom in that band therefore slides the anchor vertically. A-U10 should own and accept this; the dossier's "mostly accept" was rated for edge cases only.

The setMinZoom half of setminmax-zoom-race does NOT become inert on phones. enterChart opens every chart at minZ=fillZoomAt(def.h, atZoom). For the two city charts that is about 0.00 (Epēshu, maxz 3, h 4200) and about 0.05 (Summarch) on iphone13, and about 0.46 for Epēshu on pixel7. On iphone13 Seat, Nīmlad, Rhusagos and Home Islands also open below 0.51. All of these sit below the lowered floor, so the default path (open a chart, then Back) still has exitChart's map.setMinZoom(s.minZoom) queue an animated setZoom that races the following setView.

Keep the dossier's exitChart-only fix: set options.minZoom/maxZoom directly, setView with animate:false, then fire 'zoomlevelschange'. Do not apply it to refit. It also changes: on exit, recompute the world floor with A-U10's rule instead of restoring the CHART.save snapshot, which already goes stale after a rotation inside chart mode at HEAD. So the fix depends on A-U10's floor function and should land after Mobile 6, in its own central atlas edit. It should not be folded into A-U10's refit/fillZoom changes, and should not be dropped as "mostly inert".
votes.reason:
Checked against the HEAD export.

- **Numbers.** fillZoom/fillZoomAt use a 0.05 ceil snap. Constants are NZ=4, IMG_W=4390, IMG_H=2188, and contentBounds=px(0,0)..px(IMG_W,IMG_H). The capture profiles are iphone13 390x664 (map height about 510, so fill 1.90, matching the dossier) and pixel7 412 wide. These give fitWidth 0.51 and 0.59, which reproduces the claim's 1.39 and about 1.81.

- **Bounds-clamp extension.** Correct, and understated. Below fill the content is shorter than the viewport, so Leaflet's _rebound centres the vertical axis. Zoom-about-point then slides vertically everywhere in the letterbox band, not only at the edges.

- **"Mostly inert" is wrong.** detail-charts.json gives Epēshu tiles maxz 3, h 4200; enterChart opens at minZ = maxz + log2(vh/h). That puts Epēshu at about 0.00 and Summarch at about 0.05 on iphone13, and Epēshu at about 0.46 on pixel7. Seat, Nīmlad, Rhusagos and Home Islands also open below 0.51 on iphone13. All are below the A-U10 floor, so exitChart's setMinZoom still triggers Leaflet's animated setZoom on the most common enter-then-Back path.

- **The proposed action.** "Keep the exitChart fix separate from A-U10's refit/fillZoom edits" is right on sequencing and scope: A-U10 is in the mid-flight Mobile 6 lane, and refit must not get the direct-options trick. But it misses two things. First, the fix stays needed on phones. Second, it must take A-U10's floor rule (recompute on exit rather than restore the snapshot), so it lands after A-U10.

- **Medium vs registration.** This is a lifecycle/gesture issue. It is independent of raster vs vector, and does not touch the pinned functions (genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask).

items.summary: Refuted: TILES_V and manifest rules apply to raster byte changes and D7 is not in HEAD, and the A-U11 same-file conflict was unsourced in that claim.

summaries.1-shift: Refuted: TILES_V and manifest rules apply to raster byte changes and D7 is not in HEAD, and the A-U11 same-file conflict was unsourced in that claim.
summaries.2-registration: Only raster byte changes need a TILES_V bump; data JSON edits do not, so 'every registration item' overreached.
summaries.3-vector: Only raster byte changes need a TILES_V bump; 'any data JSON edit' was too broad and the A-U11 same-file conflict unsourced.
summaries.5-ownership: Refuted: TILES_V bumps are needed only for changed raster bytes under tiles/, charts/ or art/, D7 is not in HEAD, and anchors, control points, bounds overrides and CSS masks need none.

prior_record.claim: Art and data changes face cache and manifest gates once D5 and D7 are in place. Any change to the art bytes (a feathered plate, a re-cut plate, a regenerated preview) needs a TILES_V bump. Any data JSON edit after D7 needs the manifest regenerated. The pre-feathered-alpha variant of canon-hard-edge-seam conflicts with A-U11's 'same file' rule; the CSS-mask variant does not.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Every registration or art plan item must include a TILES_V bump and manifest regeneration.

evidence.quote: --check [--atlas|--sim] -> exit 1 when a listed raster changed and TILES_V did not (or the manifest is stale).
`var TILES_V=1` present; every request under tiles/, tiles-war/, tiles-imperial/, charts/, art/ carries ?t=1
node tools/build-offline-manifest.js --atlas --check passes

votes.corrected: Once D5 (TILES_V and ?t= on rasters) and D7 (maps-site/data/offline-manifest.json) land, the repo's own checker (tools/build-offline-manifest.js --check --atlas, required to pass by D7 and G9) fails when any raster under tiles/, tiles-war/, tiles-imperial/, charts/ or art/ (jpg/png/webp/gif/avif, so a re-cut plate or a regenerated preview such as art/overlay-*-720.jpg) changes while the TILES_V literal in maps-site/index.html does not. It also fails when the manifest is stale. The manifest lists every maps-site file, including data JSON, by path and byte size, so a data JSON edit that changes its byte size makes the manifest stale and it must be regenerated with --atlas. The check compares sha256 only for rasters, so a same-size data edit would not trip it. If TILES_V moved, --check returns 0 with a 'regenerate' notice and does not run the stale test. The sentence that the pre-feathered-alpha variant of 'canon-hard-edge-seam' conflicts with A-U11's 'same file' rule while the CSS-mask variant does not is NOT supported: the string 'canon-hard-edge-seam' (and 'hard-edge', 'feather') appears nowhere in the HEAD export. A-U11's only 'same file' text is 'after load the full image is the same file and the final shot equals R1 at max zoom; registerCityOverlay literal kept'. Applying that to feathered plates is the claimant's inference.
votes.reason: The three quotes are exact: the tools/build-offline-manifest.js header; the D5 acceptance line about var TILES_V=1 and ?t=1 on tiles/, tiles-war/, tiles-imperial/, charts/ and art/; and the G9 acceptance line about --atlas --check passing. The check code supports the TILES_V-bump rule for art rasters and the manifest-regeneration rule for byte-size changes. The final sentence about canon-hard-edge-seam variants conflicting with A-U11 has no source: the finding is not in the repo and the evidence list cites none, so that part overreaches. The 'any data JSON edit' wording is also too broad, because the check detects only size-changing data edits (no sha256 for non-rasters).

votes.corrected: Only plan items that change RASTER BYTES under maps-site/tiles/, tiles-war/, tiles-imperial/, charts/ or art/ (a re-cut or feathered overlay-Epeshu.jpg/overlay-Summarch.jpg, a re-tiled chart pyramid, a new PNG plate) need a TILES_V bump; such items must also rerun tools/art-previews.js so the A-U11 720 px previews match the new plate, and keep the registerCityOverlay literal. Note TILES_V is one global (tv() and the tile URLs in maps-site/index.html), so a bump re-fetches every tile on repeat visits: batch art re-cuts into one bump. Registration fixes that live in data or code (city-anchors.json anchors/control points, a cityBox/affine replacement, a vectorized city layer drawn at runtime, genCityCanvas/sampleCityMask output) change no raster bytes and need no TILES_V bump. After D7 lands (sw.js + maps-site/data/offline-manifest.json; not in HEAD yet), ANY edit under maps-site/ (data JSON included) needs `node tools/build-offline-manifest.js --atlas` regenerated so --check passes; this is a one-command chore, not a design constraint. The 'same file' clause of A-U11 is a mobile-unit acceptance about the preview-then-full load sequence, not a ban on later art changes; a pre-feathered (alpha, hence PNG) plate is a new raster that needs a TILES_V bump, new previews and a re-baselined R1 shot, whereas a CSS/canvas mask leaves the bytes and the gates untouched, which is why the mask variant is the cheaper choice.
votes.reason: The mechanism is real. In HEAD, D5 has already landed: maps-site/index.html has `var TILES_V=1;function tv(u)`, and tiles, charts and art carry ?t=. tools/build-offline-manifest.js check() exits 1 when the sha256 of a raster under RASTER_DIRS changed without a TILES_V change, and also when the manifest is stale. Data JSON files are listed by byte size, so a JSON edit makes the manifest stale. D7 is not in HEAD yet: there is no maps-site/sw.js or data/offline-manifest.json, and check() skips quietly when no manifest exists unless --atlas is passed. The applies_to_us rule is wrong because it is too broad. Registration is the real fix for misalignment, and it lives in anchor data (city-anchors.json) and placement code (cityBox). A vector or procedural city layer is drawn at runtime and changes no raster bytes. None of these need a TILES_V bump. Requiring one would make every repeat visitor re-download every tile for nothing, because tv() applies a single global version to all rasters. That cost hits the mobile repeat_visit budget. The rule also leaves out a real obligation: a re-cut overlay must regenerate the A-U11 720 px previews (tools/art-previews.js). Manifest regeneration after D7 is needed for any edit under maps-site/, not just plan items, and it takes one command. The A-U11 conflict is overstated. Its 'same file' clause says that after the preview loads, the full image is the same file and the shot matches R1. That is an acceptance check for the mobile unit, not a permanent freeze on the art. A feathered plate is allowed, but it costs a bump, new previews and a re-baselined shot. A mask-based variant avoids all three.

votes.corrected: The claim's numbers hold as stated. Qualify them as counts from a recording-stub run of the verbatim generator with a synthetic half-sea mask and nearest-neighbour resampling. Expect roughly 5-15% shift against the real tile-sampled coast. Epēshu is a counterfactual capital, since canon art ships and ensureCityGen only generates when !reg||reg.prov==='invented'. The "buildings are 85-90% of features" line in applies_to_us should read about 77-92%. Village Kanae is 77% (549 of 715) and ruin Lepon is 92% (1324 of 1437). Capital, town and trait-less village are all about 90%.
votes.reason:
I compared every number in the claim against generated-plan-vector-budget.json (headlineSingleCity) and all match.
- Capital Epēshu (half-sea): 1864 buildings; 28 lanes (9 streets + 19 alleys); 9 roads; 558 raw wall segments in 10 runs; 8232 core vertices; 2065 features and 8462 vertices; GeoJSON 405,527 B (59,862 gzip); delta-int at 0.25 px 25,514 B (21,535 gzip).
- Town Tamaron: 1223 buildings, 25 lanes, 7 roads, 288 wall segments in 4 runs, 5374 core vertices, 1360 features, 5560 vertices; GeoJSON 266,903 B (37,001 gzip); delta-int 16,783 B (14,062 gzip).
- Village Kanae: 549 buildings, 19 lanes, 7 roads, no wall, 715 features, 2581 vertices; GeoJSON 132,419 B (16,701 gzip); delta-int 8,178 B (6,898 gzip).
- Trait-less Feldspar (all-land mask): 602 buildings, 668 features, 2640 vertices.
- Ruin Lepon the Old: 1324 buildings, 0 lanes, 1 road, 1437 features, 5555 vertices; GeoJSON 276,278 B (35,448 gzip); delta-int 17,046 B (13,644 gzip).

The three code quotes exist in maps-site/index.html at HEAD and support the structural parts of the claim.
- `var maxLanes=({capital:80,town:52,village:26})[t.kind]||42` is present.
- `var step=({capital:15,town:16,village:17,ruin:20})[t.kind]||16;` is present.
- `if(ruin) for(var by=cy-landR; ... // ruins keep the scattered infill (Lepon stays byte-identical) — NOT lane-graphed` is present, which supports "ruins skip the lane graph" and 0 lanes.

These quotes only confirm the lane cap and the ruin behaviour. The counts themselves rest on the JSON, which the JSON's own caveats mark as approximate. I did not re-run the stub.

The one overreach is in applies_to_us, not in the claim's figures. Its "85-90%" building share ignores Kanae (77%) and Lepon (92%).

votes.corrected: These numbers are the rendering-medium cost for one GENERATED city plan only (the 136 genCityCanvas cities: 17 towns, 116 villages, 3 ruins). They do NOT cost the owner's main case, the DM-drawn canon maps (overlay-Epeshu.jpg, overlay-Summarch.jpg). Epēshu here is a counterfactual run of the generator, so its "capital" row says nothing about vectorizing the canon art. That cost is in dm-chart-vector-budget. They are also not REGISTRATION: the geometry is placed by the same cityBox/footR mapping genCityCanvas uses (scl=S/(2*footR)), so a vector city emitted this way misaligns with the atlas coast, rivers and roads exactly as the raster does. Alignment needs a separate registration step that bends the plan to atlas features. Buildings are about 77-92% of vector-worthy features (Kanae 77%, Epēshu/Tamaron/Feldspar 90%, Lepon 92%), so the building representation sets the cost. Merging per class and style (L.polygon MultiPolygon, allowed by R4/R7) turns 500-2,100 per-feature paths into 11-30 paths per city. Frame time is unmeasured and has to come from a P11 browser sweep over N, zoom (fade band about z7.8 vs Z_STREET 11.5) and smoothFactor. The counts come from a draw-call stub on a synthetic mask, about 5-15% off, and are not comparable to cityCanvasSha/UG3. Emitting vectors must not edit the hash-pinned genCityCanvas/xmur3/mulberry32 while the mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) is mid-flight. Any emitter has to sit beside them and consume the same seeded stream, so determinism is kept.
votes.reason: I checked every count in the claim against out/generated-plan-vector-budget.json (headlineSingleCity) and they match. The three quoted literals (maxLanes, step, the ruin-infill comment) are verbatim in the HEAD maps-site/index.html. The method is sound: it ran the verbatim generator block, Math.random/Date.now were trapped and never fired, and two runs gave the same op log. applies_to_us is broadly correct, but it is incomplete and slightly wrong in three ways. (1) The "85-90%" share is off: from the claim's own numbers, Kanae is 549/715 = 77% and Lepon is 1324/1437 = 92%. (2) It calls this the cost of "the owner's vector-city idea" without saying that the owner's emphasis is the drawn canon city maps. This budget covers only generated plans, and its capital row is a counterfactual because Epēshu ships canon art and ensureCityGen never generates it. (3) It leaves out the registration distinction the evidence file states itself: vector geometry placed through cityBox misaligns exactly as the raster does. It also omits the practical constraints: no frame time was measured, the counts are stub/synthetic-mask numbers not comparable to cityCanvasSha, and the genCityCanvas source hash is pinned while the mobile lane is mid-flight. Using these numbers as an input to size a generated-city vector layer is correct for the project. Treating them as evidence that vectors fix the misalignment, or as the cost of the canon-art cities, would not be.
