votes.corrected:
Mostly right that these map-wide totals are not a shipping cost. Only one city overlay is live at a time (ensureCityOverlay removes the previous one), and the inputs are already shipped: city-anchors.json, CITY_TRAITS, the approach polylines and the z5 tiles. So a client-side vector plan could be built on demand, and the cost that matters is the per-city build and draw time on the mobile frame budget (a median of about 700 to 1,000 features, at most about 1,570 features and 6,249 vertices for Sjefenhold), not 18.4 MB or 0.99 MB.

The stated reason is wrong, though. A plan is not a pure function of the city name. genCityCanvas(name,t,a,mask) seeds R with xmur3(name), but the output also depends on four other inputs:
- t from traitsFor(key): CITY_TRAITS or the anchor's kind/harbor/sea.
- the anchor a.
- the land/water mask from sampleCityMask, which decodes z5 JPEG tiles on a canvas.
- cityApproaches(key), which returns empty arrays without caching when APPR_POLYS has not loaded yet.

There are also two variants of every plan. ensureCityGenNow first registers a maskless plan for flyIntoCity, and the melded plan replaces it once the tiles arrive. So the inputs, and the stage at which the vectors are taken, must be fixed or you get a different plan.

Emitting vectors also means refactoring genCityCanvas so it returns geometry instead of drawing straight to the canvas. That function is pinned by source hash (UG3 atlas_fn_sha and cityCanvasSha, which differs across DPR classes today), and the atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) is mid-flight. So the vector emitter must sit beside it and leave the pinned function untouched, or be scheduled with that track.

Building on the client leaves alignment as it is. The plan is still placed through cityBox, so a vector plan misaligns exactly as the raster one does. Only registration to the atlas coast, rivers and roads fixes that.

The canon cities Epēshu and Summarch are out of this budget either way, because they are DM art.

So 'a pure function of the city name' is false. 'Built on the client, nothing ships' only holds if those inputs and the timing are fixed. votes.corrected:
This is about the rendering medium only, not registration. Placed through cityBox, or through genCityCanvas's own scl=S/(2*footR(kind)) mapping as the budget does, a vector plan misaligns with the atlas coast, rivers and roads exactly as the raster does. A registration step has to bend the plan to the atlas first.

For the 136 generated cities (17 towns, 116 villages, 3 ruins), one plan is live at a time. worldCityUpdate passes the nearest city to ensureCityOverlay, which removes the previous overlay, wash, stubs and POI layer. That makes the budget per city:
- Real generated cities: about 500-1,570 features and 1.9k-6.3k vertices (village median 690, town median 997, ruin max 1,570).
- Counterfactual capital: 2,065 features and 8.5k vertices. This case does not exist today, because Epēshu and Summarch ship DM canon art and are never generated. A vector Epēshu or Summarch would mean tracing or registering DM art, which this budget does not cover.

The counts are uncertain by about 5-15%. They come from a stub replay with synthetic masks, and circles are counted as one vertex.

pCity currently has no renderer set, so its paths (buildCityStubs) use Leaflet's default SVG renderer. Leaflet's SVG _initPath creates one path per layer. Merging by class and style into multipolygon L.polygon layers gives 11-29 paths per city at the same vertex count. If you merge, set smoothFactor about 0 so _simplifyPoints does not collapse the tiny building rings, and use fill rule nonzero.

R4 (never label blocks) and R7 (nothing at rest; halos only on hover) do not forbid the merge. They also do not say blocks need no hit target. That is an inference, and the owner asked for an "interactive" drawn city.

If per-building hover or click is wanted, there are two options:
- Keep the merged SVG paths and hit-test the generated geometry with a small seeded-free JS spatial index on mousemove, drawing the one halo as its own path.
- Use per-feature layers on an explicit renderer L.canvas({pane:'pCity'}), passed as each layer's renderer.

The geometry must come from a sibling emitter that leaves genCityCanvas, xmur3, mulberry32, washMake and sampleCityMask byte-identical (UG3 atlas_fn_sha and cityCanvasSha pins), coordinated with the Mobile 5-9 atlas lane and with filigree slice C, which owns the city look.

No frame times exist yet. P11 times SVG-merged against L.canvas, separating animation frames (CSS transform only) from the end-of-gesture zoomend/moveend task plus worldCityUpdate, on iPhone 13, Pixel 7 and desktop. Nothing should ship before that.

votes.corrected: In Leaflet 1.9.4 (maps-site/vendor/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js) the vector renderer only CSS-transforms its container on zoomanim (_onAnimZoom) and zoom (_onZoom). On zoomend it calls _project() on every layer the renderer holds, not only the on-screen ones. On moveend Renderer._update fires "update", which runs _updatePaths and so each layer's _update (_clipPoints, _simplifyPoints, _updatePath). The atlas map uses zoomSnap:0, zoomDelta:.25, wheelPxPerZoomLevel:80 and wheelDebounceTime:20 (maps-site/index.html), so a wheel or pinch gesture that completes a zoom ends in zoomend then moveend work that scales with the vertex count. The claim's "2.6k-8.5k vertices" figure and "per-frame" cost are not supported by any cited evidence. No cited source or doc in the HEAD export gives those counts, so they are a budget estimate. The zoomend and moveend cost is not measured.
votes.reason: All four quotes exist verbatim at HEAD. The code paths hold: the renderer's getEvents binds moveend to _update and zoomend to _onZoomEnd, and _onZoomEnd re-projects every layer. The Polyline _update quote is per-layer and is only reached through the renderer's "update" event, which the evidence did not show (I confirmed it with `this.on("update",this._updatePaths,this)`). Three parts overreach. (1) "2.6k-8.5k vertices of the city on screen" has no source, and I found none in docs/. (2) "of the city on screen" understates the cost, because _project covers all layers in the renderer and clipping only happens afterwards on moveend. (3) "every wheel or pinch gesture" is a simplification, since a gesture that does not complete a zoom change does not fire zoomend. The atlas sets no preferCanvas, so it uses the default SVG renderer. The claim stays at default holds=false because of the unsupported vertex figures; the mechanism itself is correct.

votes.corrected: Mostly right, with three changes. (1) The cost is not limited to the vertices on screen. Renderer _onZoomEnd calls _project() on every layer in that renderer, and Polyline _project runs _projectLatlngs over the whole geometry; clipping only happens later, in _update. So the zoomend cost scales with every vertex loaded into the renderer, including off-screen and not-yet-faded cities. Only the moveend clip/simplify/rebuild and the Canvas _redraw are bounded by the view. (2) moveend also fires at the end of a plain pan or drag, so every drag ends in a full path rebuild too, not only zooms. With zoomSnap 0 and wheelDebounceTime 20, one long wheel gesture produces several animated-zoom completions, not just one. A wheel batch that arrives while _animatingZoom is set makes _tryAnimatedZoom fall through to a reset, which fires viewreset and runs Renderer _reset: _project plus _update on every layer. (3) The 2.6k-8.5k vertex count belongs to a proposed vector city. HEAD has only about 12 small L.polyline/polygon/circleMarker calls, so today this is a budget for something not yet built. Corrected applies_to_us: if a vector city layer is adopted, P11 (or whatever unit sets its budget) should time the gesture-end hitch, meaning zoomend plus moveend: _project over all loaded city vertices, then clip, simplify and _updatePath/_redraw. Time it on the mobile profiles for wheel steps, pinch release and drag release, not only the animation frames, which stay CSS transforms. Cap vertices per renderer: give the city its own renderer/pane, and remove or skip non-nearest cities instead of hiding them with opacity. None of this changes registration. A vector city placed through cityBox misaligns exactly as the raster does; this is purely a budget for the rendering medium.
votes.reason: I checked the code paths against the vendored maps-site/vendor/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js. Renderer getEvents maps zoom to _onZoom, moveend to _update and zoomend to _onZoomEnd, and adds zoomanim to _onAnimZoom. Both _onAnimZoom and _onZoom only call _updateTransform, which is a CSS transform. _onZoomEnd loops over the renderer's layers calling _project(). Renderer _update fires 'update', which runs _updatePaths, which calls each Polyline _update (_clipPoints, _simplifyPoints, _updatePath); Canvas _updatePaths also calls _redraw. maps-site/index.html has 'zoomSnap:0,zoomDelta:.25,wheelPxPerZoomLevel:80,wheelDebounceTime:20,'. Pinch (TouchZoom _onTouchMove) calls map._move, which fires 'zoom', so the CSS transform applies there too, and the projection happens at touchend. So the claim's core holds, and timing the end of the gesture is correct and useful for the mobile per-frame budget. It understates the cost in two ways. Projection covers all of the renderer's vertices, not only those on screen. And pans and mid-animation wheel resets also trigger rebuilds. It is also only applicable if a vector city is adopted, since HEAD has almost no vector paths. This is a performance budget about the rendering medium and does nothing for registration/alignment. 'P11' is not defined anywhere in the HEAD docs, so I am treating it as a proposal ID from this research run.

genCityCanvas(name,t,a,mask) in maps-site/index.html returns no plan. It creates its own canvas with document.createElement('canvas') and paints imperatively. Several branches choose geometry, and so how many R() draws are spent, by reading back rasterised bands with getImageData on canvases drawn with imageSmoothingEnabled=true (the s4 and wla water bands and the RVD/RD river bands). (b) Fork the generator into a vector twin. The R() stream and the predicates then drift apart over time, so raster and vector disagree.

The stub's op-log sha and draw counts must not stand in for either. Vector output fixes crispness and interactivity only. A fitted transform is kept as data next to city-anchors.json, never computed at runtime from random input. It starts as a similarity or affine fit. If the residuals on a hand-drawn DM map stay above about 1 world px, it moves to a piecewise or thin-plate warp. The warp always bends the art to the atlas, never the atlas to the art.

I checked the claim against the HEAD export and the principle holds for our stack.

- **Frame:** the frame is real. NZ=4, and BASES shares makeBase(...,5) across the modern, war and imperial tile sets.

The corrections are small:
1. One affine fit may not be enough for hand-drawn DM art. Allow a piecewise or thin-plate warp when the control-point residuals are high.
2. The modal chart pyramids (enterChart) need the same transform.
3. Procedural cities already sample the atlas mask, so their transform is the identity.
4. True vector geometry should be native polylines or canvas strokes in atlas coordinates, not an svgOverlay.

In the repo, C13 in docs/living/todo-inputs.json is an unrelated mobile-build hold item, and neither "ckan" nor "VL4" appears in the docs. The claim also asserts that ckan is blocked and that VL4 and C13 are disputed 1/2. No cited source and no repo doc supports either (no "ckan" or "VL4" in docs, and C13 is an unrelated mobile hold). The "no client-side hit-test" and "10 px tolerance for identify" wording leans on constant names and comments, not on the identify code itself. Inverse-project the tap to atlas px, then query a seeded or canon footprint list placed by the same registration transform as the art. Use a tolerance in CSS px, converted to atlas px at the current zoom, never a fixed atlas-px radius (swisstopo uses 10 px, which is a screen tolerance). So a lookup is only as right as cityBox, and it moves when cityBox is replaced by a fitted per-city transform. Audit: a debug-only swipe or clip comparison at a fixed zoom, behind a URL flag or in tools/, never shipped and never touching genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask, which are pinned by UG3 hashes. Only REGISTRATION, meaning replacing cityBox's FOOT_R box with a transform fitted to atlas features that bends the art to the atlas, does that. The rendering medium (raster or vector) does not. summaries.2-registration: swisstopo's 2D-to-3D hand-off transfers view state (centre, height from resolution, top-down pitch), which maps to carrying an atlas-px centre and scale through the Epēshu atlas-sim transform.

prior_record.claim: swisstopo 2D-to-3D hand-off [registration]. The viewer transfers view state, not a picture. The Cesium camera starts at the 2D centre, with a height computed from the 2D resolution and canvas width, at a top-down pitch. Leaving 3D sets the 2D centre to the camera target. C12 survived 2/2.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: For the living track's H2/H2z zoom-through, carry an atlas-px centre and a scale through the existing Epēshu atlas-sim transform. This is a separate problem from the cityBox overlay.

evidence.quote: calculateHeight(store.getters.resolution, viewer.canvas.clientWidth) ... pitch: -CesiumMath.PI_OVER_TWO

votes.corrected: swisstopo's web-mapviewer CesiumCamera.vue hands off view state, not a picture. When no camera position is already stored (for example from the URL), initCamera() flies the Cesium camera to the 2D centre (store.getters.centerEpsg4326). Its height comes from calculateHeight(store.getters.resolution, viewer.canvas.clientWidth), which cameraUtils.js defines as resolution*width/(2*tan(PI/6)). Its pitch is -PI_OVER_TWO (top-down), and its heading is the negated 2D rotation. If a camera position already exists, that position is used instead. On unmount (leaving 3D), setCenterToCameraTarget picks a ray through the canvas centre against the globe and dispatches setCenter with that target converted to the 2D projection. The centre is only updated if the pick hits the globe (the defined() guard).
votes.reason: The raw file was fetched (HTTP 200). The cited text is present, but the quote is stitched from two separate spots (the calculateHeight(...) argument and the pitch line) and omits that the fallback branch only runs when no camera position is stored. Neither calculateHeight nor setCenterToCameraTarget is quoted. The "leaving 3D sets the 2D centre to the camera target" half of the claim rests on onBeforeUnmount/setCenterToCameraTarget, which the quote doesn't cover. calculateHeight's formula is in cameraUtils.js, not the cited file. I checked cameraUtils.js and it matches the "height from 2D resolution and canvas width" wording. The "C12 survived 2/2" tag is an internal label and could not be checked from the source. The applies_to_us recommendation is the proposer's inference and not something the source states.

votes.corrected:
REGISTRATION, sim hand-off only. This applies to the living track's H2/H2z units and only inside the Epēshu window. The atlas-to-sim transform already exists in index.html (the EPESHU_HF comment block): atlas px = (1060,1240) + grid·800/768, and gridToWorld(i) = (i/(N-1) - 0.5)·W_SIZE. It is valid only for atlas px [1060,1240]..[1860,2040], so outside that window there is nothing to hand off to.

What to carry: the planned H2 link carries only a place name (sim/#s=epeshu&goto=<place>&street=1). Following swisstopo, it should also carry the atlas-px centre plus a scale. The scale comes from the Leaflet zoom: in CRS.Simple with NZ=4, the resolution is 2^(4-z) atlas px per CSS px. Convert that to world metres through 800/768 and CELL, then set the camera height to res_world·canvasWidth / (2·tan(fov/2)). This is the analogue of Cesium's calculateHeight. Start top-down, then tilt.

For H2z, the Street frozen-view poster must be rendered from the camera this mapping gives at the crossfade zoom. Otherwise the crossfade itself shifts. The poster's footprint must also cover the same atlas-px box the map shows at that zoom. The crossfade starts from the cityBox-placed Epēshu overlay, so if that overlay's registration has not been fixed first, a registered poster will show the cityBox error at the seam. Crossfade from the base instead, or fix the overlay first.

Going back (sim to atlas) needs a new atlas hash key for view state. Today setHash only writes #place= and #chart=. The new keys belong to the living H2 link unit. They only move the camera: they are not seed or generation inputs, so determinism and the mobile pins (genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask, cityCanvasSha) are untouched. Like the rest of H2 they wait for street=1 (Street 3/4).

The claim is right that this does not fix the cityBox overlay misalignment.
votes.reason:
This mostly transfers. Grounding I checked: the transform it relies on is real. The index.html EPESHU_HF comment and docs/filigree/research-dossier.md give atlas = (1060,1240) + grid·800/768. The dossier cross-checks it at Aldorūs: the sim grid gives 1448.5/1527.5 against the anchor's 1448.6/1527.5. The H2 link in docs/living/research-dossier.md carries only goto=<place>. The sim reads goto= (applyGotoFromHash). The atlas hash has no centre or zoom key: setHash writes only #place= and #chart=.

Why the swisstopo approach fits: handing over view state (centre plus a height worked out from resolution and canvas width) rather than a picture is the correct registration idea for H2/H2z, and it needs no new library.

What the claim leaves out, all supplied in the corrected text:
1. The transform only works inside the window [1060,1240]..[1860,2040].
2. It says nothing about how a Leaflet zoom becomes a camera height.
3. H2z ends in a frozen poster, not a live camera, so the poster has to be rendered from the mapped camera or the crossfade will shift.
4. Crossfading from the cityBox-placed overlay would show the overlay's own misregistration. So the claim is right that this does not fix cityBox, but wrong to call it fully separate: the two meet at the H2z seam.
5. Going back to the atlas needs a new hash key, and the whole thing is gated on street=1 (Street 3/4).

Constraints: carrying the view moves only the camera, so seeded determinism and the mobile pins are untouched. It also does not bend the atlas to fit the art.

items.summary: The best Tokyo candidate uses one metric frame with 256 m tiles, and 3D Tiles parent-child transforms preserve registration that was authored in rather than creating it.

summaries.1-shift: The best Tokyo candidate uses one metric frame with 256 m tiles, and 3D Tiles parent-child transforms preserve registration that was authored in rather than creating it.
summaries.2-registration: The Tokyo candidate and 3D Tiles keep detail in one parent-relative frame; the chain preserves registration authored in and does not create it.
summaries.4-references: The candidate Tokyo repo uses one metric frame with 256 m tiles and 3D Tiles nests child transforms in the parent frame, which preserves registration authored in but never creates it; cityBox is a parent-relative transform whose translation and scale are assumed, not fitted.

prior_record.claim: Tokyo streamed city [registration]. The best candidate, github.com/jeantimex/tokyo, is not confirmed as the post. It uses one metric frame with its origin at the centre of the area and 256 m tiles. In 3D Tiles each tile's transform maps into its parent's frame, and child content lies inside the parent's bounding volume. The chain preserves registration that was authored in; it does not create it. C11 is disputed 1/2, and 'cannot move content' is an inference.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: A city detail level should be a child of the atlas frame: atlas px plus one fitted transform. cityBox is a parent-relative transform, but its scale comes from FOOT_R, not from the art.

evidence.quote: World frame: metres, x east, y up (Tokyo Peil height), z south; the origin is the area's centre.
each tile has a bounding volume completely enclosing its content, and the content for child tiles are completely inside the parent's bounding volume.

votes.corrected: Claim holds as written. Verified: jeantimex/tokyo README states "World frame: metres, x east, y up (Tokyo Peil height), z south; the origin is the area's centre" and "one 256 m tile". The 3D Tiles spec (README.adoc) says each tile has a bounding volume "completely enclosing its content, and the content for child tiles are completely inside the parent's bounding volume". The spec also says the tile `transform` maps "from the tile's local coordinate system to the parent tile's coordinate system", and the top-down traversal post-multiplies child and parent transforms. That transform sentence is in the same file but is not among the cited quotes. The statements that the chain "preserves, does not create" registration and that 'cannot move content' is an inference, and the C11 vote, are the claim's own caveats, not source text. The post is correctly marked as not confirmed (streamed-streets.md says the same). The cityBox/FOOT_R remark checks out against maps-site/index.html: cityBox takes its half-size from footR(a.kind), with FOOT_R={capital:26,town:14,village:9,ruin:8}, and ignores what the art depicts.
votes.reason: Both cited quotes were fetched and found verbatim. Each supports the claim as scoped: one metric frame centred on the area with 256 m tiles, and child content enclosed by the parent. The parent-frame transform statement is present in the spec file. The claim marks its own inferences and its unconfirmed provenance. The cityBox/FOOT_R statement matches the HEAD code.

votes.corrected: REGISTRATION, not medium. The principle transfers: a city detail level should be a child of the atlas frame, meaning atlas px plus one stored transform per city. The claim's point that a parent/child chain only preserves registration that was authored in, and never creates it, is the key lesson for us. In maps-site/index.html, cityBox(a,w,h) is the only parent-to-child transform. Every call site uses it: the POI layers through reg.poiRef, washMake bounds and the pCity L.imageOverlay. It is not a fitted transform. It centres the box on the anchor dot (translation is assumed, not fitted), takes the scale from FOOT_R[kind] (capital 26, town 14, village 9, ruin 8) times the image aspect (scale is assumed, not fitted), and has no rotation. Two cases follow. (1) Procedural plans: sampleCityMask samples the z5 land/water mask in a window around the same anchor, sized by footR, so genCityCanvas coast and water are registered to the atlas by construction, up to z5 resolution. Little drift is expected there. (2) The DM canon art (overlay-Epeshu, overlay-Summarch and the charts used by enterChart) is stretched into the FOOT_R box, so nothing ties its coast, rivers or roads to the atlas. That is where the misalignment comes from. The action is per-city data, e.g. an optional fit {tx,ty,s,theta} or a 3+ point control-point similarity/affine in city-anchors.json. It is fitted once by matching art features (shoreline, river mouth, gate/road exits) to atlas px, and the art bends to the atlas, never the atlas to the art. cityBox and cityMaxZ fall back to FOOT_R when no fit exists, and POIs and the wash use the same fit. Caveat: L.imageOverlay only takes axis-aligned bounds, so a rotation needs a canvas or CSS-transform overlay, or vector geometry transformed in code. Translation plus scale alone fits the existing overlay. A vector city drawn through the unfitted cityBox would misalign in exactly the same way. Vector rendering brings crispness, interactivity and shared road vertices, not alignment. cityBox, cityMaxZ and the anchor JSON are not in the UG3 pin set (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask), so this does not touch pinned sources, and the fit is static data, so determinism holds. Sequence it after the atlas lane of mobile (Mobile 5-9) and agree it with filigree slice C, which owns the city look. 3D Tiles, octrees and streaming do not apply to a two-level Leaflet raster. Tokyo is an unconfirmed source, so it gives the framing and is not a template.
votes.reason: I checked the HEAD export, maps-site/index.html. Line 834 defines FOOT_R. cityBox (`function cityBox(a,w,h){var r=footR(a.kind)...`) returns a box centred on a.atlasX/atlasY with half-size from footR times the aspect, and has no offset, scale-from-art or rotation term. Every overlay, wash and POI call site uses it, and cityMaxZ also derives from footR. So applies_to_us is right that cityBox is the parent-relative transform and that its scale is not taken from the art. It is incomplete in three ways. (a) The translation is also assumed: the box is centred on the dot, and the art's centre need not match the dot. (b) It does not separate procedural plans from DM art. sampleCityMask samples the tile mask in a window sized by the same footR around the anchor, so procedural plans are registered by construction, and the real misalignment is the canon raster art. (c) It does not mention that L.imageOverlay cannot rotate. The 3D Tiles evidence supports only the general rule that a chain preserves registration and does not create it. Streaming and bounding-volume machinery does not transfer to a two-level Leaflet CRS.Simple map. The fix is per-city fitted data plus a cityBox fallback. It is deterministic, touches no pinned function, and fits the single-file constraint. The claim holds, with sharpening.

items.summary: Bay Atlas's stack is unverified owner's brief; the only transferable point is that layers authored in one frame stay anchored, and for the atlas that frame is CRS.Simple atlas px.

summaries.1-shift: Bay Atlas's stack is unverified owner's brief; the only transferable point is that layers authored in one frame stay anchored, and for the atlas that frame is CRS.Simple atlas px.
summaries.2-registration: Bay Atlas's stack is unverified owner's brief; if right it stays anchored because all data share one vector-tile frame, which is a principle, not proof.
summaries.3-vector: Bay Atlas's stack is unverified (owner's brief); only the one-frame principle transfers, and 'density is a property of the medium' must not be read as vectorising fixes the shift.
summaries.4-references: Bay Atlas's stack is unverified (owner's brief); the vector-tile spec only shows the frame comes from shared source coordinates, so the one-frame principle transfers while 'density is a property of the medium' is rejected.
summaries.5-ownership: Owner's brief only: Collison's Bay Atlas stack is unverified; the transferable principle is one authoring frame (CRS.Simple atlas px), and vectors in that frame are registered only if authored against it.

prior_record.claim: OWNER'S BRIEF (not a verified web fact): Patrick Collison's 29 Sep 2026 post wants to 'wallow in cartographic filigree'. His demo, Bay Atlas, draws the Sonoma coast in a style after swisstopo. The stack the brief attributes to it (MapLibre GL + PMTiles + Mapzen terrain + OSM) is unverified. If that stack is right, it stays anchored because everything is OSM data in one vector-tile grid whose decoder already knows the frame (VL7 survived 2/2). Its density is a property of the medium.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: The filigree look the owner admires rests on data authored in one frame. For the atlas that frame is CRS.Simple atlas px.

evidence.quote: Everything below about post text, replies, Bay Atlas visuals and the Azlen flyover is **owner's brief**. It has not been re-verified as a web fact.
| Bay Atlas = MapLibre + PMTiles + Mapzen terrain + OSM | **Unverified.**
A Vector Tile SHOULD NOT contain information about its bounds and projection.

votes.corrected: Owner's brief only (unverified as web fact): Collison's 29 Sep 2026 post says he wants to "wallow in cartographic filigree", and the demo, Bay Atlas, draws the Sonoma coast in a style after swisstopo. Bay Atlas's stack (MapLibre + PMTiles + Mapzen terrain + OSM) is unverified; no repo was found. The Mapbox Vector Tile spec (2.1, section 3) does say "A Vector Tile SHOULD NOT contain information about its bounds and projection" and that the decoder is assumed to know the bounds and projection. That is a general property of the vector-tile format, not evidence about Bay Atlas. Nothing read supports "it stays anchored" for Bay Atlas, "its density is a property of the medium", or "VL7 survived 2/2".
votes.reason: Two quotes check out. The dossier (docs/filigree/research-dossier.md section 1) says the post material is "owner's brief" and "has not been re-verified as a web fact". docs/research/cartographic-filigree.md lists "Bay Atlas = MapLibre + PMTiles + Mapzen terrain + OSM" as "Unverified". The raw.githubusercontent.com Mapbox spec fetched live contains the third quote, and the sentence after it says the decoder is assumed to know the bounds and projection. Two things fail. First, findings.json is not in the HEAD export, and no VL7 or "survived 2/2" text turned up in the docs, so the cited VL7 record cannot be verified. Second, the claim's second half reasons from the unverified Bay Atlas stack. The spec supports only a general point about vector tiles. It does not show that Bay Atlas is built on OSM vector tiles, that its density comes from the medium, or that it stays anchored, so those parts overreach. The claim is hedged ("if that stack is right"), so the overreach is mild.

votes.corrected:
Partly transfers, and only as a principle. The Bay Atlas stack is unverified (cartographic-filigree.md: "Unverified. No repo was found"), so it cannot be cited as proof. What carries over is the general point: things stay anchored when every layer is authored in one coordinate frame. For the atlas that frame is CRS.Simple atlas px (1 world px = 1 PatrinorModern px at NZ=4, with no y-flip against the z5 tiles).

Two corrections. (1) REGISTRATION: this is what fixes our misalignment. In an OSM-style stack, layers line up because all the data shares one source coordinate system (lat/lon from survey). It is not because the data is vector tiles. Our city layers do not share the frame. The DM's canon art (overlay-Epeshu.jpg, overlay-Summarch.jpg) and genCityCanvas plans are placed by cityBox(a,w,h): a FOOT_R[kind] box centred on the anchor dot, sized to the image aspect, with no tie to the coast, rivers or roads. So adopting the principle means fitting each city to the atlas with ground-control points (a coast or harbour point, river crossings, gate and road ends matched to atlas px), using an affine fit or a light warp that bends the art to the atlas. It never means moving atlas geography to suit the art. (2) RENDERING MEDIUM: reject "density is a property of the medium". Swiss and OSM density comes from rich data. A vector city placed through the same cityBox misaligns exactly as the raster does. Going vector is worth it only after registration, where it brings crispness past the stretched image, interactivity, and road vertices shared with the atlas roads.

Any vector layer must stay a pure function of the seed. It must not change the pinned genCityCanvas, sampleCityMask or washMake hashes (UG3 atlas_fn_sha, cityCanvasSha) while the Mobile 5-9 atlas lane is in flight. Its look stays with the filigree slice C, under R4 (never label blocks) and R7 (nothing at rest).
votes.reason: The applies_to_us line is right as far as it goes: the anchoring principle, everything in one frame, holds whatever Bay Atlas actually uses, and our frame really is CRS.Simple atlas px (NZ=4, 1 world px = 1 atlas px). It is incomplete in a way that could mislead the build. The claim says the anchoring comes from 'one vector-tile grid' and that 'density is a property of the medium'. That invites the conclusion that vectorizing the city fixes the shift. It does not. The vector-tile spec quote (a tile SHOULD NOT contain bounds or projection) shows the frame comes from shared source coordinates, not from the vector format. Our shift comes from cityBox in maps-site/index.html (`function cityBox(a,w,h){var r=footR(a.kind)`, with `FOOT_R={capital:26,town:14,village:9,ruin:8}`): it sizes the art from a radius chosen by kind and the image aspect, not from what the art depicts. That is a registration gap and is independent of the medium. The stack attribution is also unverified (confidence low; the dossier marks it owner's brief), so the claim should stand as a generic principle rather than evidence from Bay Atlas. Acting on the corrected form is correct for this project: register to atlas px with control points, bend the art to the atlas, then optionally vectorize, all deterministic and respecting the mobile hash pins and the filigree rulings.

votes.corrected: Azlen's flyover is an aesthetic reference, not an anchoring technique. It is the owner's brief (low confidence, not re-verified) and it shows a camera moving over one authored sheet, so it has nothing to register. What transfers is the medium: a painted city with block grain, park voids, ocher arterials and fog (filigree slice C, R4, R7). It gives us no method for alignment. Our atlas holds at least two pictures: the PatrinorModern sheet, and the city art placed by cityBox (FOOT_R[kind] around the anchor dot, aspect-fit, whatever the art depicts). The chart pyramids and the sim street view (H2z) add more. These behave like one sheet only once the city is in atlas px. The two cases differ. (a) The procedural plans (genCityCanvas) are already partly painted in atlas px, because sampleCityMask reads the land/water mask from the z5 tiles around the same anchor. Their residual drift comes from the extent the mask covers versus the cityBox extent, and from the road stubs, not from the medium. (b) The DM canon maps (overlay-Epeshu.jpg, overlay-Summarch.jpg) are dropped into a box sized by footprint class, so their coast, rivers and gates never meet the atlas. These need registration: control points matched to atlas coast, river and road features, then a fitted affine or thin-plate warp of the art into atlas px. The warp is baked offline and committed, so the DM art is bent to the atlas and the atlas is never moved. Doing this in the medium the art already uses (raster) fixes alignment. Moving to vector adds crispness, interactivity and shared road vertices, but a vector city placed through the same cityBox misaligns the same way. Any change to genCityCanvas, sampleCityMask or washMake trips the mobile pins (UG3 atlas_fn_sha, cityCanvasSha) and has to be sequenced with the atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) and filigree slice C.

That fix is REGISTRATION, which means fitting the city art and geometry to the atlas coast, rivers and roads. A Mapbox-style exhibit (camera pose plus layer toggles) is a RENDERING and narrative pattern only. Registration matters only where a target sits inside a city. votes.corrected: Supported: (1) Leaflet 1.9.4 CRS.Simple guide says to find the right bounds by "measuring how many pixels there are between the 0 and 1000 coordinates, and extrapolating". It does not say "not from approximate bounds", which is the claim's gloss. (2) @allmaps/transform 1.0.0-beta.53 README table: straight = translation+scale, 2 GCPs; helmert 2; polynomial/polynomial1 3; thinPlateSpline 3, "exact" at GCPs. The README transforms geometries and shows image distortion; raster warping is done by the separate @allmaps/render package using the same transformer, so "rasters and vectors alike" is not stated in this quote. (3) Leaflet 1.9.4: Map.latLngToLayerPoint does project(...)._round(), and ImageOverlay._reset places the image from the rounded NW and SE corners. That means up to about 0.5 px of position error and about 1 px of size error at rest. The Map.js quote alone supports only the rounding, so ImageOverlay._reset must be cited with it. (4) StreetView3DOverlay README: the Street View parameters "have been established by trial-and-error. This means that both the position and orientation of the ferris wheel is not very precise." It also says the method is imprecise because panorama distortion is non-uniform. That supports "hand-tuned placement in a Street View overlay was imprecise", not a general rule. NOT supported: the claim that the Azgaar-to-Watabou link and TownGeneratorOS "work in their own frames and are never registered to the world map". The cited Model.hx line (`var sa = Random.float() * 2 * Math.PI;` in buildPatches) is only a random start angle for the Voronoi patch spiral around the origin. It shows TownGeneratorOS builds in a local frame with no geo input, but it says nothing about Azgaar, the Watabou link, or registration. Narrowest supported claim: Leaflet advises measuring known coordinates and extrapolating to get image bounds; Allmaps offers straight/Helmert (2 GCPs), polynomial1 (3) and TPS (3, exact at GCPs) transforms; Leaflet ImageOverlay adds roughly 1 px rounding; a hand-tuned Street View overlay was self-described as not very precise. Drop or separately source the Azgaar/Watabou/TownGeneratorOS never-registered statement.

votes.corrected: Port the method, not the libraries, but only for the two canon overlays. Fit an offline, deterministic transform from overlay px to atlas px for art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg and art/overlay-Summarch.jpg, using control points the DM's art shares with the atlas (coast, river mouths, road gates). Store it as data per city, with its residual in atlas px, and swap it in for cityBox wherever registerCityOverlay entries have prov:'canon'. Procedural cities need no fit. sampleCityMask already reads their land/water mask from the z5 atlas tiles around the same anchor and footR, so genCityCanvas plans are registered to the atlas by construction. Their bounds, cityCanvasSha and the UG3-pinned functions stay as they are. Try translation plus uniform scale first, because it maps directly onto L.imageOverlay's axis-aligned LatLngBounds. Use Helmert only if the residual calls for it. Its rotation cannot be shown by L.imageOverlay, so it needs either a CSS-transformed custom layer or an image rotated once offline. Rotation is a similarity, so it does not bend the art, but the owner should agree to it. TPS warps canon art and needs an owner ruling. Every consumer of cityBox for a canon city must read the same stored transform, or the art and its pins will separate. That means the POI reprojection through poiRef, the pCityWash wash bounds, the cityMaxZ zoom cap and the seam fade. The enterChart modal draws in its own chart frame and needs no fit. The edit lands in maps-site/index.html, so schedule it after the mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9).
votes.reason: The claim mostly holds for this project; the corrections are about scope. Checked in the HEAD export, maps-site/index.html. cityBox(a,w,h) centres every overlay on the anchor and sizes it only from footR(kind) and the image aspect, so canon art is not registered to any atlas feature. Fitting from measured shared points, as Leaflet's CRS.Simple guide and Allmaps recommend, is the correct cure. It is deterministic and offline, keeps the atlas authoritative, and does not touch xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask. The applies_to_us text has three gaps. (1) It does not limit the fit to the canon overlays. The procedural plans are already atlas-registered, because sampleCityMask draws tiles/5 around atlasX/atlasY with the same footR, and refitting them would shift the bounds the mobile pins capture. (2) 'Then Helmert' overlooks that L.imageOverlay only takes axis-aligned bounds, so any rotation needs a custom layer or an offline-rotated image. (3) cityBox has several consumers: POI layers via poiRef, the wash bounds (f=1.7), cityMaxZ and the overlay itself. Applying the fit to only one of them would create a new misalignment. The ~1 px _round claim and the remark that Watabou/TownGeneratorOS are unregistered are accurate but carry little weight. The real error in our stack is cityBox's footprint guess, measured in world px at z4 and magnified far more at Z_STREET, not Leaflet rounding. The rest of the claim is fine as stated: the enterChart modal works in its own chart-px frame, and the rendering medium stays a separate question from registration.

The shipped atlas does not use this figure. maps-site/index.html sets `var MI_PER_NATIVE=600/723; // 600 Imperial (Cyrikon) mi ≈ 723 native px` (updScale reads it through px()), which gives 0.830 mi/px. The live scale bar therefore reads about 9% short. It also spells the name 'Cyrikon', but the plate says 'Cyrikoi'. How the claim applies to us: (1) Change the MI_PER_NATIVE literal to 600/659 and fix the spelling. This is a one-constant change, not generated code, so seeded determinism is not affected. It is also not one of the UG3-pinned functions (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask) and does not change cityCanvasSha. Still, maps-site/index.html is being edited by the Mobile 5-9 lane, so this goes into a central or queued unit, not a live edit. (2) A scale does not fix the anchoring the owner asked about. Anchoring is a registration problem: where art sits against the coast, rivers and roads. A scale only checks size. It gives a canon way to sanity-check the arbitrary FOOT_R footprints (a capital's 26 px half-size is about 24 mi, so a 47 mi-wide city box) and to size a registered city layer, raster or vector, if the DM's city maps carry their own scale. It does not choose where the art is placed. That still needs control points matched to atlas features, with the art bent to the atlas and never the reverse. (3) We use CRS.Simple and one flat constant, which follows the plate's own convention of a single printed bar. 'The projection looks conic, so the bar drifts' is an unverified guess, not a measured fact. Record it as an open question and do not build a per-latitude correction now. (4) River-Measures are optional canon flavour for chronicle prose or a second bar. They fit the bronze-age voice, but filigree R7 (nothing shown at rest) governs whether a second bar is ever drawn.
votes.reason: I checked the claim against the tiles. The 'Sārmathic River-Measures' bar beneath it spans about 1190 z5 px, so the claim's numbers and its z5 = 2x geometry (35x18 tiles) are correct. The claim's 'applies_to_us' misses that the atlas already ships a scale bar with a different constant: MI_PER_NATIVE=600/723, labelled 'Cyrikon', in maps-site/index.html, used by updScale. That constant is about 9% off canon. So the finding is a real canon correction, and a small, determinism-safe one, but it must be coordinated with the mid-flight mobile atlas lane. Registration (where art sits against the coast, rivers and roads) is what fixes the shift, and that is true whether the city layer is raster or vector. The 'conic projection drift' caveat is speculation. Under CRS.Simple and the plate's single printed bar, one flat constant is correct for now.

items.summary: The code constant MI_PER_NATIVE=600/723 (0.830 mi/px) differs ~9% from the printed bar and is undocumented; the dissent notes it is not an anchoring question since insets are symbol-scaled.

prior_record.claim: The atlas code uses a different constant from the printed bar: MI_PER_NATIVE=600/723 = 0.830 mi/px, vs 0.910 measured from the printed bar (about 9.7% smaller). The code comment says '600 Imperial (Cyrikon) mi ≈ 723 native px'; the printed bar spans about 659 atlas px. The origin of 723 is not documented anywhere in the repo (grep finds only the comment and the CHANGELOG line 'Cyrikon-miles scale bar').
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Any scale-aware design (true-scale vector city, scale bar inside the city view) needs one ruled constant; the two candidates differ by ~10%. See open questions.

evidence.quote: var MI_PER_NATIVE=600/723; // 600 Imperial (Cyrikon) mi ≈ 723 native px
1318 z5 px / 2 = 659 atlas px for 600 mi

votes.corrected: Verified in the repo: maps-site/index.html contains `var MI_PER_NATIVE=600/723; // 600 Imperial (Cyrikon) mi ≈ 723 native px`, so the code constant is about 0.830 mi per native px. Native px are atlas px at NZ=4, because px() is map.unproject([x,y],NZ). The constant feeds updScale. CHANGELOG.md lists "Cyrikon-miles scale bar". A grep of the HEAD export for the whole word 723, MI_PER_NATIVE and "Cyrikon mi" finds only that one comment; the other 723 hits are base64 data in the sim index.html and the lexicon data. lexicon/research/dm-rulings.md item 8 and docs/research/atlas-structure.md also list the map scale as an open DM question, so no documented origin for 723 exists. Not verified: the printed bar's 659 atlas px (1318 z5 px / 2) and the 0.910 mi/px (about 9.7% difference). They rest on a "measure in C05" that is not a repo file or a fetchable source, and the HEAD repo has no measurement of the bar. Narrowest supported claim: the code uses 600 mi = 723 native px (0.830 mi/px) with no documented origin, and the DM has never ruled the atlas scale. The comparison with a 659 px printed bar is an unconfirmed measurement that needs re-measuring from the atlas or tiles.
votes.reason: The first evidence item (code comment) and the CHANGELOG line are confirmed, and the claim that no doc explains 723 holds. The second evidence item, the 659 px / 0.910 mi/px printed-bar measurement, cites a measurement in another claim (C05) and cannot be checked against any repo source or URL. The "about 9.7% smaller" figure and the "two candidates differ by ~10%" conclusion therefore rest on an unverified number, and the claim stays unconfirmed under the default-false rule.

votes.corrected: The facts are right, but the claim is not about anchoring, and the choice of constant is not really an open question. (1) Re-measured from the z5 tiles: the printed "Imperial (Cyrikon) Miles" bar runs from its 0 tick to its 600 tick over z5 x 112.5 to 1430.5 in the crop, which is 1318 z5 px = 659 atlas px. That gives 0.910 mi per atlas px. The code uses MI_PER_NATIVE=600/723 = 0.830. In maps-site/index.html, updScale measures px(0,0) to px(1000,0) at NZ=4, so "native px" means atlas px and the two numbers are in the same unit. The bar on screen is therefore about 9.7% too long, and it understates distances by about 8.8%. 723 does not match the second printed bar either: 600 Sārmathic River-Measures span 595 atlas px. (2) The printed atlas bar is DM canon, and atlas geography is authoritative, so the ruling should be MI_PER_NATIVE = 600/659 (about 0.910). Ask the owner only to confirm that 723 was not a deliberate DM figure. The change is one line in the scale-bar block ("scale bar (Cyrikon miles)"). It touches no seeded or pinned function (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask) and nothing in cityCanvasSha. It only has to be scheduled outside the mobile atlas lane's hold on maps-site/index.html. (3) It has no bearing on the shifting the owner sees (REGISTRATION). cityBox sizes overlays from FOOT_R in world px, not miles, so changing this constant moves nothing, for raster or vector cities alike. It also does not give a true-scale vector city its scale, which needs metres per atlas px. That needs two more unknowns: how long a Cyrikon mile is in metres, and how long a league is. The better evidence for city scale is each city art's own fit to coast and river features (for example, Summarch's own scale bar). It belongs on the list as a small, separate fix to the scale bar's correctness, not as an input to anchoring.
votes.reason: I checked against the HEAD export and a tile measurement. The code line and comment are as quoted ("var MI_PER_NATIVE=600/723"). Neither the repo nor the docs give a source for 723: docs/filigree/todo-inputs.json says "scale unchecked", and atlas-structure.md says the bar "needs the units-per-league calibration". I stitched the z5 tiles at x 0-7, y 16-17 and found the printed bar's tick columns. The Imperial bar measures 0 to 600 = 1318 z5 px = 659 atlas px, which confirms C05's 0.910 mi/px against the code's 0.830 (723/659 = 1.097). The claim's applies_to_us is broadly right that any scale-aware feature needs one ruled constant. It is wrong in two ways. First, it leaves the choice open when the project's own rule (atlas art is canon) settles it in favour of the printed bar. Second, it implies the constant matters for the vector-city or anchoring work. Registration is set by cityBox and FOOT_R, not by miles, and a city's metric scale needs a conversion from miles to metres that does not exist yet. Acting on it is correct and cheap: a one-line constant change with no determinism or pin impact. It is low severity and does not touch the misalignment problem.

items.summary: Canon distance figures are verbatim in the wiki snapshot, but their 'inconsistency' is an inference and they do not bear on anchoring.

prior_record.claim: Canon text states scales only in leagues, miles and km, never per atlas px, and its units are inconsistent. Mountain Wall page: '900 kilometers (186 leagues)' gives 4.84 km = 3.0 mi per league. Lepon page: 'twenty leagues west of Epēshu' and 'roughly fifty miles ... as the crow flies' (plus thirty miles on foot) gives 2.5 mi per league. Sun Road page: 1000 leagues = 560 (Drāmūz to Cyrikon) + 440 (imperial extension). Other figures: Tungril 1300-1400 miles; Alensis 90x60 leagues; Empheros ~300 leagues east-west; Sargāzat 85 leagues; Longdale 35 leagues.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: The wiki snapshot (51 pages) is the only canon source reachable; the live wiki was blocked by the egress proxy (403 CONNECT), so the Map-of-the-Wide-World page and contentIndex.json were not read.

evidence.quote: The mountain range is about 900 kilometers (186 leagues) in length

LocationNorthwestern shore of Leponnia, twenty leagues west of Epēshu ... Its ruins are roughly fifty miles west of present-day Epēshu as the crow flies, but traveling on foot adds an additional thirty miles

evidence.source: wiki-places.json (Road that Walks with the Sun)
evidence.quote: a thousand leagues in length ... originally ran 560 leagues from Drāmūz to Cyrikon ... the Empire added 440 leagues

votes.corrected: All cited quotes and figures exist verbatim in maps-site/data/wiki-places.json (the 51-page snapshot) and the arithmetic checks out. The claim holds only as a statement about that snapshot, and the inconsistency is an inference, not canon's own statement. Narrowest supported form: in the 51 snapshotted wiki pages, distances are given in leagues (10 mentions), miles, and kilometres (once, Mountain Wall), plus some feet (heights) and a 'day journey'. No page mentions pixels or an atlas px scale. The one canon pair that fixes a ratio is Mountain Wall '900 kilometers (186 leagues)', about 4.84 km (3.0 mi) per league. Lepon pairs an infobox 'twenty leagues west of Epēshu' with prose 'roughly fifty miles ... as the crow flies', which implies 2.5 mi per league. That second ratio is an inference from loosely worded figures (an infobox rounding or a different measure), not a stated canon conversion. Sun Road: 560 + 440 = 1000 leagues, confirmed. Other figures confirmed: Tungril 'about 1300–1400 miles', Alensis 'roughly 90 leagues from east to west and 60 leagues from north to south', Empheros 'some three hundred leagues' east to west, Sargāzat '85 leagues from end to end', and 'Longdale (35 leagues long)' (on the Mountain Wall page; there is no Longdale page). Whether live-wiki pages, Map-of-the-Wide-World or contentIndex.json state a map scale is unverified.
votes.reason: Every quote was found in wiki-places.json and the numbers reconcile. Three things go beyond the evidence. (1) 'Never per atlas px' and 'only leagues, miles and km' are absence claims over a 51-page snapshot, and the claim's own applies_to_us says the live wiki was unreachable. (2) The snapshot also uses feet and a 'day journey'. (3) The 2.5 mi per league figure comes from mixing an infobox location with crow-flies prose, so calling the units 'inconsistent' is an inference. One attribution slip: Longdale's 35 leagues sits on the Mountain Wall page, not a Longdale page.

votes.corrected: The quotes are accurate. I checked each one against the HEAD snapshot maps-site/data/wiki-places.json (51 pages): Mountain Wall '900 kilometers (186 leagues)', Lepon 'twenty leagues west of Epēshu' / 'roughly fifty miles ... additional thirty miles', Sun Road 1000 = 560 + 440, Tungril 1300–1400 miles, Alensis 90x60 leagues, Sargāzat 85 leagues, Longdale 35 leagues. These figures still do not help the owner's anchoring problem. City overlays drift because of REGISTRATION: cityBox(a,w,h) places the art as a FOOT_R[kind] box centred on the anchor dot, whatever the image actually shows. The fix is control points tied to atlas features (coast, rivers, roads near the city), with the DM atlas authoritative. A canon league scale cannot serve as that control. It is internally inconsistent (about 3.0 mi/league from the Mountain Wall page, 2.5 from the Lepon page, roughly 17% apart). It is also far too coarse: the Lepon the Old–Epēshu anchor pair in city-anchors.json is about 89.75 atlas px for '20 leagues', which is about 4.5 px per league, while the error to fix is a few atlas px of offset and stretch inside a 26-px capital box. The RENDERING MEDIUM is unaffected either way. The safe use is a scale bar, a distance readout, or a sanity check on FOOT_R footprints. Calibrate one constant from atlas anchor pairs, label it as approximate, and never bend atlas geography to fit a canon distance. The live wiki being unreachable (the Map-of-the-Wide-World Leaflet config, contentIndex.json) is a provenance caveat, not applicability. Those Leaflet markers only repeat atlas pixel positions and would add no scale.
votes.reason: The factual content of C07 checks out in the snapshot, so the inventory is correct. Its applies_to_us field doesn't say how the claim applies to the stack, though. It only notes the wiki was unreachable, and someone could read the inventory as offering a league-to-px scale for city alignment. That would be wrong. The canon units disagree by about 17% (2.5 vs 3.0 mi/league). A league works out to about 4.5 atlas px (Lepon the Old to Epēshu, 89.75 px for 20 leagues), which is far coarser than the few-px registration error between cityBox overlays and atlas features. Canon distances also have to give way to the atlas, never the reverse. For the anchoring fix the claim doesn't carry over: registration comes from atlas-feature control points, not from text scales. The figures are only useful for an approximate scale bar or a check on footprint sizes, with no effect on determinism, the mobile pins or any track.

items.summary: Atlas distances agree with canon prose only to order of magnitude (Sun Road 1704-1870 mi vs 560 leagues; Lepon-Epēshu 74-82 mi vs 50 mi); the atlas governs, and the holding check names MI_PER_NATIVE as that scale, but this section keeps the constant as an owner question.

prior_record.claim: The atlas and the text agree on order of magnitude but not tightly. The traced Sun Road (data/named-ways.json, Drāmūz to the vertex at (2600,1862), 2054 atlas px) is 1704 mi at the code's 0.830 mi/px = 568 leagues at 3 mi (1.4% off canon's 560), but 1870 mi = 623 leagues (11% over) at the printed bar's 0.910. Lepon-Epēshu anchors are 89.75 atlas px apart = 74 mi at 0.830 or 82 mi at 0.910, versus canon '50 miles' (or 20 leagues = 60 mi): 24-63% over.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Atlas geography is authoritative (constraint), so the atlas bar governs; but canon prose cannot be used to refine it beyond about ±25%. The Sun Road trace is hand-approximated ('Trace approximate') and ends about 190 px south of the Cyrikon anchor, so treat the 1.4% as luck.

evidence.quote: Lepon the Old atlasX 1146.5, atlasY 1420.2; Epēshu atlasX 1236.1, atlasY 1415 -> distance 89.75 px

votes.corrected: Verified: (a) named-ways.json 'Road that Walks with the Sun' (prov 'trace', note ends 'Trace approximate') starts at [1335,1734]; its polyline length to the [2600,1862] vertex is 2053.9 px. (b) maps-site/index.html MI_PER_NATIVE=600/723=0.830 mi/px (a 'Cyrikon miles' bar, 600 Imperial mi ≈ 723 native px), so 2054 px ≈ 1704 mi. (c) Lepon the Old (1146.5,1420.2) and Epēshu (1236.1,1415) are 89.75 px apart, ≈74 mi at 0.830. (d) Canon: wiki-places.json Sun Road page says 'originally ran 560 leagues from Drāmūz to Cyrikon'; Lepon page says 'twenty leagues west of Epēshu'; factions.json says Lepon is 'some fifty miles from the city'. (e) The vertex (2600,1862) is about 193 px from the Cyrikon anchor (2573,1671). Narrowest supported claim: at the code's 0.830 mi/px and an ASSUMED 3 mi/league, the trace is about 568 leagues, 1.4% over 560, and Lepon-Epēshu is about 74 mi, about 24% over 60 mi (20 leagues) and about 49% over 'fifty miles'. NOT supported: the 'printed bar's 0.910' value (no 0.91 scale appears anywhere in the repo, so the 1870 mi / 623 leagues / 11% and 82 mi / 63% figures have no cited source) and the 3 mi/league conversion (no repo or wiki text states it). The repo itself marks the atlas scale as unchecked and an open DM question (lexicon/research/dm-rulings.md item 8; docs/filigree/todo-inputs.json 'scale unchecked'), so agreement 'on order of magnitude' is only conditional on those unsourced assumptions. The trace also does not end at Cyrikon, so the 1.4% is not a like-for-like comparison with canon's Drāmūz-to-Cyrikon length.
votes.reason: The arithmetic, the polyline length, the anchor distance and the canon quotes (560 leagues, twenty leagues, fifty miles) all check out. But the 0.910 mi/px 'printed bar' and the 3 mi/league factor appear in none of the cited evidence or anywhere in the repo, and the repo records the atlas scale as unchecked. The half of the claim that rests on 0.910 (11% over, 82 mi, 63% over) is therefore unsupported, and the 560-league match mixes an unverified league length with a trace that stops short of Cyrikon.

votes.corrected:
The atlas is authoritative, so the code's scale MI_PER_NATIVE=600/723 (about 0.830 mi/px; maps-site/index.html, "// ---- scale bar (Cyrikon miles) ----") governs. Canon prose only confirms the order of magnitude and should not be used to retune it. Here are the checks against the repo copy.

(a) The figures hold. The Sun Road polyline in named-ways.json measures 2053.9 px from Drāmūz to the (2600,1862) vertex. Lepon the Old and Epēshu are 89.75 px apart.

(b) The "printed bar 0.910" figure is not attested anywhere in the repo. The code comment says the 600/723 value is itself the bar reading, so 0.910 should be dropped or re-measured on PatrinorModern.png before anyone cites it.

(c) The comparison depends on how long a league is, and that is not defined anywhere in the repo or the wiki mirror. Canon actually contradicts itself here. The Lepon page in wiki-places.json gives both "twenty leagues west of Epēshu" and "roughly fifty miles west ... as the crow flies, but traveling on foot adds an additional thirty miles". Those two figures imply a league of 2.5 mi, not 3.
- At 2.5 mi per league the Sun Road comes to 1704 mi = 682 leagues, which is 22% over canon's 560.
- So the "1.4% off" result is an artefact of assuming 3 mi per league, as well as of the hand-traced line ("Trace approximate"). That line ends about 191 px south of the Cyrikon anchor at (2573,1671).

(d) The distance between anchors is a crow-flies distance, so the right canon figure is 50 mi. That makes the 74 mi result about 48% over. The 80 mi on-foot figure is a path length and does not apply.

Net effect: canon and the atlas agree only to within about ±25-50%, and the atlas wins.

This has no bearing on the zoom-anchoring and registration problem. MI_PER_NATIVE feeds only the scale bar. City placement uses cityBox/FOOT_R in world px, which fixes art to the anchor regardless of miles. So neither registration nor a raster-versus-vector choice should depend on this scale, and no change is called for beyond correcting the scale bar's label or comment if 0.910 turns out to be real.
votes.reason:
I recomputed both distances from the repo data and they match: 2053.9 px and 89.75 px. The canon figures (560 leagues; fifty miles or twenty leagues) are quoted correctly from wiki-places.json. The claim's applies_to_us conclusion is right in direction: the atlas governs, prose can't refine the scale, and the 1.4% match is luck. But it has three problems:
- It cites a "printed bar 0.910" that appears nowhere in the repo. The code's 600/723 comment says that value is the bar reading.
- It assumes 3 mi per league with no source. Canon's own 20 leagues = 50 miles implies 2.5 mi, which turns the 1.4% into 22% over.
- It mixes in the 60 mi figure instead of the crow-flies 50 mi.
On the owner's alignment ask, this finding has no effect on registration: MI_PER_NATIVE is used only by the scale bar, and cityBox sizes cities in world px. It is low severity: information only, with no build action.

items.summary: Summarch's chart has a printed 0-500 m bar (1.819 pyramid px/m; chart ~2334x2172 m); the dissent limits it to sizing within the chart and the street track, never sizing the city in atlas px.

prior_record.claim: The Summarch chart carries its own printed metre scale bar (0m / 250 / 500), the only quantitative scale of any city in the repo. Measured on the z3 chart pixels, ticks at x=138, 592.5, 1047.5, so 500 m = 909.5 chart px = 1.819 px/m (0.55 m/px). The whole chart therefore depicts about 2334 x 2172 m (2.3 x 2.2 km); the outer wall ring is about 0.86 km across (about 2.7 km round, eyeballed from the downscaled chart). The chart's cartouche is titled 'Sun's March'.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: This is the only anchor for a true-scale city. It can be used to size a Summarch vector layer in metres and, via C05, in atlas px.

evidence.source: charts/summarch/3 stitched, row y=435 baseline, ticks

evidence.quote: legend: 'Sun's March' / 'om 250 500' scale bar; walled ring about 330 of 900 thumbnail px wide

votes.corrected: The Summarch chart (maps-site/charts/summarch, native 4245x3951 per maps-site/data/detail-charts.json, all at z3) has a printed bar labelled 0m / 250 / 500 under the cartouche "Sun's March". Stitching the z3 tiles, I measured the labelled ticks at x=138, 592.5 and 1047.5, so 500 m = 909.5 px = 1.819 px/m (0.55 m/px). The chart covers about 2334 x 2172 m. The walled ring is about 0.86 km across (my measure: about 1570 px = 863 m) and about 2.6-2.7 km round (eyeballed). It is the only DM-drawn city chart in the repo with a printed metre scale bar. The Epēshu chart has none. Do not read it as the only metric scale anywhere, because the sim works in metres (W_SIZE = 9000 m) and keeps its own terrain grid.
votes.reason: I stitched the z3 tiles (17x16 tiles, cropped to 4245x3951) and scanned the bar row. Row y=435 is the baseline, with long ticks at x=138, 592-593 and 1047-1048, plus minor ticks at 365-366 and 821. The labels read "0m", "250" and "500", and the cartouche reads "Sun's March". The arithmetic holds: 909.5/500 = 1.819 px/m, 4245/1.819 = 2334 m and 3951/1.819 = 2172 m. A crop of the wall shows a closed ring about 1570 px (about 863 m) wide and about 1420 px tall, giving a perimeter of about 2.6-2.7 km. The claim's "330 of 900 thumbnail px" is consistent with that. The Epēshu chart (4 tiers, 3914x4200) has a numbered legend but no scale bar. The only overreach is "the only quantitative scale of any city in the repo". It is true only for the drawn chart art, since index.html uses metres for sim geometry. The wall size is eyeballed, as the claim already says.

votes.corrected: The bar is real and useful, but only inside the chart. It gives a scale within the Summarch chart (about 1.82 chart px per metre). That is enough to size buildings, lanes and walls consistently in a Summarch vector layer drawn in chart or metre space, to keep that layer's proportions faithful to the DM's art, and to give the street track true metres for its 3D view. It must NOT be used to size the city in atlas px. The atlas's own scale (MI_PER_NATIVE=600/723 in maps-site/index.html, about 1.34 km per atlas px) would make the whole 2.3 km chart about 1.7 atlas px wide. Today the footprint is about 28 atlas px (FOOT_R.town=14 in cityBox), roughly 16 times larger. Settlement ring-dots on PatrinorModern are symbols, not true-scale city sizes. So the zoom into a city needs a deliberate scale break. Wherever the city sits on the atlas, its outer scale is set by registration: control points that tie the chart's gates, roads, river and wall to the atlas's dotted roads, solid rivers and coast near anchor (523,58). The art bends to the atlas, never the reverse, and a metric conversion can't stand in for those control points. The metre scale handles the city's inside; registration handles where it lands. Also, the world scale bar is already hidden in chart mode (updScale returns early when CHART.on). Any metre readout for the city view would be a separate, chart-local bar.
votes.reason: The measured scale itself is plausible: ticks at 138, 592.5 and 1047.5 give 454.5 px per 250 m, and the chart is 4245x3951 (matching DETAIL['Summarch'] in registerCityOverlay). I did not re-measure the pixels. What's wrong is the applies_to_us step "and, via C05, in atlas px". The atlas carries its own scale: MI_PER_NATIVE=600/723, about 0.83 mi or 1.34 km per atlas px, from the Cyrikon-mile scale bar in updScale. At that scale a 2.33 km city is about 1.7 atlas px wide, smaller than its own settlement ring-dot. The current cityBox footprint is about 28 px for a town (FOOT_R town 14), about 37 km at atlas scale. The atlas is symbolic at city level, so sizing the vector layer by true metres would collapse the city instead of aligning it. Acting on the claim would also swap one fixed sizing rule (FOOT_R) for another (metres) while leaving registration out. That is exactly the gap behind the owner's misalignment. Fitting the chart to atlas features (roads, river, wall, gates) is what fixes the shift; the metre scale does not. Where the bar does transfer: proportions inside the chart for a vector Summarch layer (building and lane widths, the wall ring of about 0.86 km) and real metres for the street track. One more point: it is the only metric source for one city, so it can't set a general scale for procedural cities, which would need their own ruling. It doesn't touch the determinism or pin constraints, since it is a data constant, not generated code.

items.summary: Summarch's 2.33 km chart in a 28 px box is a ~17.6x linear exaggeration of the printed scale (true size ~1.6-1.8 atlas px); the arithmetic holds but the conclusion that a tighter footprint cannot help overreached.

prior_record.claim: True-scale vs drawn-scale: Summarch's chart (2.33 x 2.17 km) is placed in a 28.0 x 26.1 atlas px box. At the printed bar (0.910 mi/px) that box is 25.5 x 23.7 mi = 41 x 38 km, a linear exaggeration of about 17.6x (about 16x at the code's 0.830). In true scale the whole Summarch chart would be only about 1.6-1.8 atlas px across (2334 m / 1.46 km per px at 0.910; 1.75 px at 0.83). A 52 atlas px Epēshu box is 48.5 x 52 px = 44 x 47 mi = 71 x 76 km at 0.910 (65 x 70 km at 0.830); Epēshu's chart has no bar, so its own exaggeration is unknown.
prior_record.confidence: high for Summarch arithmetic, low for any Epēshu factor
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Answers the owner's question: yes, a city drawn 28-52 atlas px wide is exaggerated by about an order of magnitude and a half relative to the printed scale. A tighter footprint would not make the art line up, because the chart's coast and rivers were drawn at city scale, not traced from the atlas.

votes.corrected:
The arithmetic holds; the "applies_to_us" conclusion and two phrases overreach.

Verified:

votes.corrected:
The counts are right. data/city-anchors.json has 136 keys: village 115, town 17, ruin 3, capital 1. 111 carry prov 'trace' (102 villages and 9 towns). 11 have harbor:true and 117 have sea:null. meshedWorldInit hard-codes Summarch and Penthelon, giving 138 anchors at runtime.

Every one of those 138 anchors can get a seeded plan, but only when the map is near it. ensureCityGen runs for the nearest city once zoom passes 6.5, and worldCityUpdate pre-warms it in idle time from zoom 5.6. ensureCityGenNow does the same for flyIntoCity. genCityCanvas then draws the plan using the atlas land/water mask from sampleCityMask, and registerCityOverlay registers it as prov 'invented'. Only Epēshu and Summarch have canon plan art (art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg and art/overlay-Summarch.jpg, plus the charts/ pyramids). The loc-*.jpg files, including loc-Penthelon and loc-Lepon, are illustrations, not registered plans.

Every overlay, canon or generated, goes through the same cityBox. That box is the FOOT_R square at the anchor dot. So the registration fix has two parts:
(a) Epēshu and Summarch each need their own art-to-atlas transform (control points on the coast, rivers and roads) instead of cityBox.
(b) The 136 generated plans need their mask sampling and road stubs (sampleCityMask, buildCityStubs) to use the same frame as the overlay bounds.

Vectorising the plans would not fix alignment on its own. Any change to genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask also changes the pinned hashes (UG3 atlas_fn_sha, cityCanvasSha) and runs into the Mobile atlas lane that is still in progress.
votes.reason:
I recounted the anchors in the HEAD copy of maps-site/data/city-anchors.json and every number in the claim matches. In maps-site/index.html, meshedWorldInit adds the Summarch and Penthelon anchors and registers the only two canon overlays, Epēshu and Summarch, with prov 'canon'.

traitsFor falls back to the anchor's kind, harbor and sea when data/city-traits.json has no entry. That file covers only 27 names, so 111 anchors run on defaults, and every anchor can still get a plan. Plans are built on demand, not up front: ensureCityGen near zoom (from worldCityUpdate) and ensureCityGenNow when flying in. They are built only when no canon entry exists (the check `!reg||reg.prov==='invented'`).

So applies_to_us is right in substance but too loose in three places:
1. Plans are built lazily, one nearest city at a time. They are not all made in advance, which matters for the mobile per-frame budget.
2. Those plans already sample the atlas coastline through sampleCityMask, so part of their registration comes from the atlas. That helps them line up, but only if the overlay bounds come from the same frame.
3. "Only 2 have drawn art" is correct for city plans, but art/loc-*.jpg also holds location illustrations (Penthelon, Lepon and others) that must not be mistaken for plans to register.

Acting on it is correct if the inventory sets the scope: two canon overlays that need their own per-art registration transforms, plus 136 seeded plans whose fit depends on cityBox and the mask frame matching. It is wrong if it is read as "vectorise 138 cities". That fixes the rendering medium, not registration, and it would touch the pinned genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask hashes.

votes.corrected:
The facts mostly hold, with one correction. Summarch and Penthelon are not in city-anchors.json at all. They are hardcoded in meshedWorldInit (maps-site/index.html): CITY_ANCHORS['Summarch']={...kind:'town'} and CITY_ANCHORS['Penthelon']={...kind:'village'}. So the ◉ glyph class (maps_markers mag:true) and FOOT_R[kind] really are out of step: Penthelon gets r9 and Summarch gets r14, while Epēshu gets r26. Ten of the 15 ◉ cities (Alensis City, Sepos, Līm Haub, Bōlkhar, Gizalīs, Ākat, Kurūgnon, Nub-Nefer, Men-Nehet, and others) have no anchor, so they have no city view at all. That is a coverage and inventory gap, not a misalignment.

What it means for the owner's ask: the class-to-glyph mismatch is a sizing and inventory inconsistency. It is not the cause of the drift on zoom, and fixing it does not align anything. A size bucket keyed to the ◉ class is still cityBox: a box centred on the dot that ignores what the art shows. A vector or raster Summarch scaled to a 'major' bucket would still miss its coast, rivers and roads. The fix that matters is registration: give each city its own fitted bounds, or a transform from 2+ control points matched to atlas coast, river and road features, stored as data per city. That bends the art to the authoritative atlas. footR/FOOT_R would then only be the fallback for procedural plans.

"No size at all" is not an option. L.imageOverlay and cityMaxZ (NZ+log2(mx/(2r))) both need an extent. Re-classing kinds also changes cityBox, cityMaxZ and the fr*6 nearest-city radius. If a kind feeds traits for genCityCanvas, it could also move the pinned cityCanvasSha (UG3) while the atlas Mobile lane is mid-flight. So any re-class must be a deliberate, separately gated data change. Painted-city footprint sizing also falls under the filigree slice C ruling.
votes.reason: Checked in the head export. maps_markers.json has exactly 15 entries with mag:true. city-anchors.json has kinds capital 1, town 17, village 115, ruin 3. Among the ◉ cities only Epēshu (capital), Hordon, Cyrikon (prov:'trace') and Tamaron (town) are in it. Summarch (town, r14) and Penthelon (village, r9) are injected in code in meshedWorldInit. Bōlkhar and 9 other ◉ cities have no anchor. FOOT_R={capital:26,town:14,village:9,ruin:8} and cityBox centre the box on the anchor with half-size footR(kind), whatever the art shows. So the inventory mismatch is real (the evidence wrongly says Summarch and Penthelon are in city-anchors.json). But the claim's applies_to_us treats footprint class as the lever that matters. It is not the cause of the zoom drift. Under the task's own distinction this is a size bucket, not registration: a ◉-sized cityBox misaligns exactly as the current one does, raster or vector. "No size" cannot work, because imageOverlay bounds and cityMaxZ need r. Acting on it as written would trigger re-classing churn: cityMaxZ, the nearest-city radius, possibly the traits that feed genCityCanvas and so the pinned cityCanvasSha. It would not fix alignment. The correct follow-up is per-city registered bounds or a control-point transform, plus an inventory note that 10 ◉ cities have no city view.

votes.corrected: The inventory is accurate. city-traits.json holds flavour and generator steers keyed by name, and no geometry or registration. A future geometry file belongs beside it, not inside it. The atlas already has an atlas-px vector precedent: data/traced-roads.json (polylines in atlas px) and the pts of data/named-ways.json. The missing piece is per-city REGISTRATION: control points that map DM chart px to atlas px. data/chart-pois.json, for example, is in chart-image px (Epēshu POI 1 at x 788, y 2095). Today every placement goes through cityBox/FOOT_R. So the right refinement surface is a new data/city-geometry.json (or a registration block per city) authored in atlas px, with these rules: (1) it snaps road ends and gates to traced-roads/named-ways vertices and the coast to the atlas (bend the art to the atlas, never the reverse); (2) it carries DM-chart control points or a fitted affine, so overlay-Epeshu/Summarch and the chart POIs sit in atlas coordinates; (3) it is hand-authored or generated offline from the seed, never by Math.random at runtime. A vector city authored in a cityBox-local frame would misalign exactly as the raster does. The medium only adds crispness, interactivity and shared vertices. Small gaps in the inventory: the field list leaves out hinterlandOf and river (Kolens 'through', Ion Ephel 'beside'), and sea.distPx is a scalar steer, not a footprint. Kind steers extent only indirectly, through FOOT_R in code.
votes.reason: I checked this against the HEAD export with node. There are 27 non-_readme keys, and the counts match: capital 1, town 9, village 14, ruin 3. The names match too. The _readme quote is verbatim. Epēshu is wall:true, harbor:true with sea {side:SSW, distPx:10}. Summarch is wall:true, harbor:false, sea:null. Neither entry has coordinates or an extent. maps-site/index.html loads the file only into CITY_TRAITS (getJSON('data/city-traits.json')) for cards and generator steers. Its geometry comes from city-anchors.json plus cityBox/FOOT_R. The applies_to_us is directionally right: a separate geometry file in atlas px is the right home, and it keeps prov-tagged flavour apart from geometry. But it implies a geometry file alone fixes alignment, and that blurs registration with the rendering medium. Alignment only improves if the file is registered to atlas features (traced-roads.json and named-ways already supply atlas-px road vertices to snap to) and carries chart-to-atlas control points for the DM art and chart-pois (which are in chart px). Placing the file through cityBox would leave the shift in place. Adding a data file does not touch the hash-pinned functions (genCityCanvas, sampleCityMask, washMake), so it is compatible with the mobile pins. Any change to genCityCanvas to consume it would break cityCanvasSha and must be coordinated with the mobile lane and with filigree slice C.

The counts (19 and 9), the x/y ranges, the named coordinates, the 'd' field on every POI and the wikiSlug on Winehall and The Seat all match the file. The chart frames match detail-charts.json and the fallbacks in maps-site/index.html. The footprint-transform claim is confirmed in index.html (poiRef, worldPOICoord, buildWorldPOIs).
