votes.corrected: The inventory is accurate. maps-site/data/chart-pois.json has Epēshu 19 (x 246-3782, y 121-3835) and Summarch 9, every entry has a 'd', and only Winehall and The Seat carry a wikiSlug. The POIs live in chart pixel space and are mapped in two different ways. (1) Chart mode (enterChart → buildPOILayer) places them with cpx = map.unproject([x,y],atZoom) in the chart's own frame. That is independent of the atlas, so footprint changes cannot move them there. (2) World mode (buildWorldPOIs / worldPOICoord) places them through cityBox(a,reg.w,reg.h) with fractional poiRef normalisation (p.x/poiRef.w*box.fw). The overlay JPGs (2863x3072, 3072x2859) have the same aspect ratio as the charts (3914x4200, 4245x3951), so the fractions carry over. In world mode the POIs therefore inherit the overlay's misregistration exactly. A vector redraw of them would not fix that. They are also not the only vector data tied to city plans: procedural cities emit their own pois and road stubs from genCityCanvas/buildCityStubs. For our stack this means any registration fix has to replace cityBox with ONE shared per-city transform used by the overlay bounds, buildWorldPOIs and worldPOICoord, so the art and the POIs cannot drift apart. The POIs carry no atlas coordinates (wiki-places has their lore only, and they are not in maps_markers), so they cannot serve as atlas ground-control points by themselves. A few edge features can be candidate tie points to atlas features when fitting that transform: the Road That Walks with the Sun (3782,1738) as the eastern road exit against traced-roads.json, Bangeph Rock in the bay and Mount Mastery over the harbour against the atlas coast. The fit bends the art to the atlas, never the reverse. Chart-mode POIs need no change.
votes.reason: I checked against the HEAD export. Counts, ranges, names, the 'd' descriptions and the wikiSlug holders all match chart-pois.json. The applies_to_us is half right. World-mode POIs do ride cityBox through poiRef fractions (worldPOICoord, buildWorldPOIs), so they move with the footprint and are misaligned the same way the raster is; that is a registration problem, not a rendering one. Chart-mode POIs use cpx in the chart frame and never touch the footprint. Procedural cities also carry pois and stubs, so "only vector-ish data" is wrong. The practical takeaway the claim leaves out: whatever registration replaces cityBox (a per-city similarity or affine fitted to coast, river and road ties) must be one function shared by the overlay and the POIs. The POIs' beyond-the-walls entries can help fit it, but they cannot anchor it alone because they have no atlas coordinates. This is low severity: it is inventory plus an incomplete implication, and acting on it as corrected stays inside the determinism and pin constraints (no change to pinned genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask is needed).

In index.html, W_SIZE=9000 and N=768. buildEpeshuMapData's comment gives the atlas window px [1060,1240]..[1860,2040]. That makes sim-to-atlas a pure affine map: atlasX = 1060 + gridX*800/768 and atlasY = 1240 + gridZ*800/768. The scale is the same on both axes (11.25 m per atlas px), with no rotation. So any geometry the sim or the street track generates for Epēshu (streets, building footprints, roads) can be projected into atlas px with no fitting. A vector or procedural city layer drawn from that geometry would line up with the anchors and coast. The DM raster still goes through cityBox with FOOT_R 26, which is placed by size alone. A uniform 100x-plus compression does not shift anything, because an affine scale keeps relative positions. What misaligns is cityBox placing the art by size and centre, not the sim's scale. H2z (docs/living research-dossier) is not a continuous camera zoom across that scale gap. It crossfades the city overlay into the Street frozen-view poster and then offers a page hop (H2). For the zoom-through, the only canon raster is Epēshu. It is a capital, so footR is 26 and the box is 52 world px; overlay-Epeshu.jpg is registered at 2863x3072. That gives cityMaxZ = 4+log2(3072/52) ≈ 9.885, where 1 atlas px is about 59 CSS px. Summarch has no entry in city-anchors.json, so its art appears only in the modal chart (enterChart), not in the zoom-through. Procedural plans are GEN_SIZE 2048, so their cityMaxZ is 4+log2(2048/28) ≈ 10.19 for a town and ≈ 10.83 for a village, not 9.88. worldCityUpdate clamps setMaxZoom to cityMaxZ, so 'past z9.88' cannot be reached at Epēshu. The real crispness gap is HiDPI: at cityMaxZ one image px covers DPR device px, so phones see a 2-3x upscale from about cityMaxZ-1 onward. The other gap is that the 3072px overlay is a downsample of the larger chart source (DETAIL ref 3914x4200). To be crisp, the deep end needs either the existing chart pyramid wired into the zoom-through (a tile layer clipped to the footprint) or vector geometry. Vector cost must fit the mobile per-frame budget, and genCityCanvas/sampleCityMask must stay untouched (they are pinned by UG3). Neither medium fixes where the art sits. Placement comes from cityBox (anchor centre plus FOOT_R half-size scaled to the image aspect). Only a registration transform (control points that bend the art to the atlas coast, rivers and roads) fixes the shift.

The formulas and the Epēshu numbers check out: 3072/52 = 59, and z ≈ 9.885. The key point also holds: rendering medium (raster or vector) and registration are separate problems, and cityBox placement is the cause of the misalignment. Four details are overstated. (1) 'Every overlay' uses the Epēshu number, but procedural 2048px plans have different cityMaxZ values (about 10.19 for a town, 10.83 for a village). items.summary: 136 of 138 overlays are seeded genCityCanvas plans registered to the coast via the z5 mask; the dissent says the claim overstates their registration, since rivers and roads are not registered to the print.

prior_record.claim: Procedural cities (136 of the 138 anchors) use a seeded plan: genCityCanvas, with a mask sampled from the z5 tiles (sampleCityMask) and stubs from buildCityStubs, registered with prov:'invented', w/h of the generated canvas. These do carry atlas registration for the coast (the mask) and the road entries (stubs), because they are drawn from atlas tiles; the DM charts do not.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: The only registration machinery that exists is on the invented plans; the canon charts are the ones with no registration.

votes.corrected: 136 of the 138 city overlays (the 136 data/city-anchors.json entries minus Epēshu, plus the two code-added anchors Summarch and Penthelon, minus the canon Epēshu and Summarch) are generated by genCityCanvas(key,t,a,mask) and registered in ensureCityGen/ensureCityGenNow with prov:'invented', w/h = the generated canvas (GEN_SIZE square), pois, poiRef and stubs. Two atlas-derived inputs feed them. (1) The coast comes from a land/water mask that sampleCityMask builds from the z5 tiles, and it applies only when the sampled patch has at least 2.5% water (mask.water); otherwise a synthetic compass shoreline is used. (2) The gate and stub bearings come from cityApproaches, which intersects atlas road and sea-lane vector polylines (APPR_POLYS, built by buildApprPolys from party route legs, named ways and sea lanes) with a 2.5x footprint circle. The stubs are not drawn from tiles. Both inputs only shape what is painted inside the canvas: the canvas is still placed through the same cityBox footprint, so this is shaped content, not a registration transform. The DM charts (prov:'canon', Epēshu and Summarch) carry no stubs and no mask.
votes.reason: The quoted registration call exists, in ensureCityGen and ensureCityGenNow in maps-site/index.html. The count holds: 136 anchor keys plus Summarch and Penthelon gives 138, with the 2 canon registrations leaving 136 procedural. The mask is sampled from z5 tiles by sampleCityMask, buildCityStubs returns null for non-invented overlays, and the canon registrations pass no stubs. The claim overreaches in two places. First, it says the stubs are drawn from atlas tiles, but they come from vector polylines (route legs, named ways, sea lanes) through cityApproaches and APPR_POLYS. Second, it says these cities carry atlas registration, but the mask and stubs only shape the generated content, while placement still uses the cityBox footprint. The mask also applies only when the patch holds real water.

votes.corrected: Mostly right, but it overstates how much registration the procedural plans carry. The 136/138 count checks out: the 136 entries in city-anchors.json plus the two anchors added in meshedWorldInit (Summarch, Penthelon), minus the two canon charts Epēshu and Summarch. Canon charts are registered only through cityBox (the anchor dot plus the FOOT_R box, fit to the image aspect). Nothing ties them to the atlas coast, rivers or roads, and buildCityStubs returns null unless prov is 'invented'. So all of the misalignment the owner sees on the drawn city maps is a REGISTRATION problem with those two charts. The fix is per-chart control points (for example a similarity or affine fit from chart features to atlas pixels) that bend the art to the atlas. Changing the medium from raster to vector would not fix it. For the procedural plans, registration is partial and comes from two separate mechanisms. (1) Coast: sampleCityMask reads the z5 tiles, and genCityCanvas redraws the mask's central 4rW (z5 px) onto the canvas. Because the plan is square, that window equals the cityBox, so the coast lines up pixel for pixel by construction. It only applies when drawWater && mask.water (a harbor, or sea.distPx<=25) and only after the tiles arrive; the ensureCityGenNow fallback without a mask uses the synthetic compass shoreline. (2) Roads: the stubs do NOT come from the tiles. cityApproaches takes the bearings at which vector polylines cross a circle of 2.5×footR: party route legs, named ways and sea lanes. Gates sit on the plan's own gate ring, whose centre moves toward the water, and the stub runs from the gate to 1.18×footR along that bearing. That matches road direction, not road position, and nothing snaps to the atlas's dotted roads. Streets and blocks inside the plan have no registration at all. Rivers come from traits data (t.river), not from the atlas. What follows for us: the invented plans are already generated in the atlas frame, so turning them into vectors mainly brings crispness and interactivity, plus the option of real shared road vertices in place of bearing-only stubs. Any vector or raster rebuild must keep the pinned genCityCanvas, sampleCityMask and washMake hashes (UG3) and seeded determinism.
votes.reason: I checked this against maps-site/index.html. The parts that hold: ensureCityGen and ensureCityGenNow register genCityCanvas output as prov:'invented'; the canon overlays for Epēshu and Summarch are registered in meshedWorldInit with no stubs and no mask; buildCityStubs bails out when reg.prov!=='invented'; and cityBox(a,w,h) is the only thing that places either kind. The coast claim also holds: in genCityCanvas, g4.drawImage(mcv,(a.atlasX-rW)*2-MK.ox,...,4*rW,4*rW,...) puts the sampled tile mask in exactly the footprint frame. The part that does not hold is the claim that the road entries are 'drawn from atlas tiles'. The stubs come from cityApproaches/segCircleHits over APPR_POLYS, which buildApprPolys fills from route legs, named ways and sea lanes. They give a bearing only: mkGate puts each gate on a ring of radius gr around a centre moved toward the water (cx-=sv.x*S*0.07), so the stub's position is not tied to where the atlas road actually runs. Coast registration is also conditional (drawWater && mask.water) and asynchronous. The overall conclusion is right for this project: canon charts have no registration, and invented plans have partial registration by construction, which separates the registration problem (canon charts need control points) from the medium question (vector for crispness, interactivity and shared road vertices). It just needs the stub mechanism and the conditions above corrected so nobody assumes the procedural roads already line up with the atlas roads.

items.summary: Epēshu has 0 strict identifiable ties; today's placement misses by tie rms 8.0 px, fits beyond translation+scale overfit, coast matching is multimodal, and a policy-chosen translate+scale override (tie rms 5.3-8 over 0.83-1.0x, 0-5 px E) plus a seam clip is recommended.

ties.feature: T1 west-shore knee W of the city centre (atlas: westmost point of the shore W of the ring, where the coast turns from SW-running to S-running / art: Necropolis of the Founders (1) knee)
ties.note: Same morphology on both sides (convex knee on the waterfront at the latitude of the centre). The atlas knee is about 9 px from the ring edge, though, and that gap is drafting clearance around the symbol, so the position is only good to a few px.

ties.feature: T2 eastmost water reach N of the centre (atlas: foot of the headland's W shore where it meets the E-W shoulder / art: the bay's smooth eastward bulge near Temple of Thobrauk (5))
ties.note: The atlas shows a sharp corner where the art shows a gentle bulge, so the along-shore position is ambiguous by about 400 art px. This is the sector where the shapes disagree most: north of y~1404 the atlas shore steps east to x~1240, while the art waterfront stays around x 580-870 art (1222-1227 atlas at today's placement).

ties.feature: T3 east road (atlas: dotted road from the ring, at its bend from E to SSE / art: Road That Walks with the Sun (15) where it leaves the frame)
ties.note: The road identity is good: it is the sun-ward road to Pēshunor and the only eastern exit on both maps. The point is not: the art point is a frame-edge exit and the atlas point is a bend, so this is really a cross-track (line) constraint. The atlas road dots are about 2.5 px apart. Today's placement already puts the art road within about 1-2 px of the atlas road's E-running segment.

ties.feature: T4 south road (atlas: dotted road leaving the ring due S at x~1240 and turning SW just below the box / art: double-line SSE trunk east of Old Quarry Lot (16) at the frame bottom)
ties.note: The directions differ (atlas S then SW, art SSE). It is a frame-edge exit, and which of the art's several southern lanes is the atlas road is a judgement call.

ties.feature: T5 settlement ring centre / Epēshin Forum (7)
ties.note: This is a symbol convention, not geography: the ring marks the city and the forum is its civic centre. The ring's radius is about 4.5 px plus stroke, and the atlas coast is drafted to clear it.

s=0.014020 (0.828x today), rot=+5.4 deg, t=(1222.85,1391.81). Gains only 0.2 px over translation+scale. LOO held-out rms 9.89, max 15.53. Rotation is unsupported.

fits.params: A=[[0.01133,-0.00165],[0.00115,0.01701]], t=(1226.78,1387.07); singular scales 1.010x and 0.673x today (anisotropic). LOO held-out rms 19.91, max 38.42, so this is overfitting. TPS was skipped: there are 0 high-confidence ties (6 needed).

fits.params: s=0.031 (1.83x today). Fits T1/T5 to 1.5 px and throws the road ties 23-43 px off. This scale is the ring-to-shore clearance artifact (12.8 atlas px on the atlas vs 413 art px), not geography.

fits.params: 1.01x today, rot 0, centre (1238.5,1433.5): 18.5 px SOUTH of the anchor, IoU 0.737. The waterfront hugs the shore W of the ring and the SE water finger, but the Forum lands at (1229,1434) on the narrows, about 20 px from the ring. Ridge at this scale: translations within 0.03 IoU span cx 1236.5-1240, cy 1431.5-1436. Grid: 36 scales (0.3-2.0x) x 21 rotations (+/-30 deg) x translations within +/-25 px. 14 entries above 0.6x lie within 0.02 IoU of the best, spanning 0.61-1.04x and -18..+30 deg, so the objective is multimodal and flat.

prior_record.implied_scale: The repo has no ground calibration: I searched docs/research, maps-site/index.html and index.html and found no km-per-atlas-px or scale bar (atlas-structure.md lists the scale bar as needing a units-per-league calibration). So the scale can only be expressed relative to today's box, and the atlas does not pin it down. The 5 ties give 0.83x, but that is unstable (LOO worse than today). The two medium ties give 1.8x, which is the symbol-clearance artifact. The coast-shape matches give 0.32x, 0.55x and 1.01x as separate, equally good modes. Matching coast features therefore does not demand a markedly larger or smaller footprint than FOOT_R=26; it is compatible with anything from ~0.3x to ~1.0x. Separately, as a guess kept out of the recommendation: the art's house fills (about 12-16 art px per lot) suggest roughly 1 m per art px, so about 2.9 x 3.1 km. If Epēshu-Lepon (~91 atlas px) were about a day's walk, an atlas px would be ~0.3 km and the true city ~10 atlas px across, about 0.2x today. That would make the drawn ring and FOOT_R a symbol exaggerated ~5x, and the 0.32x coast mode the nearest thing to true scale. That guess is unverified.
prior_record.recommended_transform: Use translation + uniform scale only: what cityBox already is, turned into an explicit per-city registration override (centre dx,dy and radius or scale in city-anchors data) instead of 'FOOT_R[kind] centred on the dot'. Choose the parameters by stated policy, not by fitting, because the atlas does not constrain them. The policy: (1) the printed ring falls inside the art's built-up area, near the Forum; (2) the art waterfront meets the atlas shore at the ring's latitude (T1); (3) the sun-ward road (T3) stays on the atlas's eastern dotted road. Around today's values (scale 0.83-1.0x, centre shifted 0-5 px E) this cuts tie rms from 8 to about 5 px and coast chamfer from 9.3 to about 5.8 px. Rotation (5.4 deg, 0.2 px gain), affine (LOO 19.9 px) and TPS (no high-confidence ties) are rejected. The conflict in the NW sector, where the art's Eelwynd quarter and upper waterfront sit over atlas sea by ~12-15 px, cannot be removed by any similarity that keeps the ring inside the city. It must be handled at the seam: clip or fade the canon art against the atlas water mask (sampleCityMask-style), so art is bent to the atlas, never the atlas to art. Registration and rendering medium are separate questions. Registration is what fixes the misalignment. A vector city placed through the same box would misalign exactly as the raster does. A vector or procedural layer generated FROM the atlas land/water mask and road stubs would not have the NW conflict, because its coast and roads would share the atlas geometry. The canon raster will always carry it.
prior_record.notes: Image size: the task text says 3072x2863, but the file is 2863 wide x 3072 tall, and registerCityOverlay('Epēshu','art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg',{w:2863,h:3072}) agrees with the file. Today's box therefore comes from cityBox(a,w,h) with r=26 and mx=3072: half-sizes 24.231 x 26, box (1211.87,1389)-(1260.33,1441), 0.016927 atlas px per art px. The anchor comes from city-anchors.json; Epēshu has no code override (only Summarch and Penthelon do). image_px values are in overlay-art px, not the poiRef 3914x4200 frame. No river lies within ~50 px of the box (the solid line SE of the box is outside it). The atlas has no north road, and the art shows no east coast. What the atlas offers at city scale is a generalized, hand-wiggled coast drawn with a ~2 px stroke and wiggles of ~3-5 px, a ring symbol ~9 px across with coast clearance drafted around it, and two dotted roads with ~2.5 px dot spacing. Only 2 ties are genuinely point-identifiable (T1, T5, both medium); T2-T4 are a smooth bulge and frame-edge exits. Findings: today misses by tie rms 8.0 px (max 12.9) and coast chamfer 9.3 px (max 20). The dominant visible error is the art claiming land over atlas sea NW of the ring. Tie fits look better in-sample (5.0-5.3 px), but their leave-one-out error is worse than today's, so 5 weak ties cannot choose a better transform. Coast-shape matching is multimodal, with good fits at 0.32x, 0.55x and 1.01x scale, and every mode puts the ring outside the city. The art's single gently curved waterfront fits many stretches of the atlas coast, which proves the atlas is too simple at this scale to register a city chart against. The conclusion is that FOOT_R is an exaggerated city symbol rather than true-scale geography: the canon chart is an inset whose placement is a policy choice, and seam reconciliation (clip or fade against atlas water) has to absorb the leftover ~12-15 px. Registration and rendering medium stay separate: registration (where geometry sits relative to coast, roads and the ring) fixes the misalignment, while the medium (raster vs vector) only buys crispness, interactivity and shared road vertices. Rotation, affine and TPS are not justified by the data. Files from this run in crops_dir: sbs_ctx{3x,8x,20x}.png (atlas | art in today's box), blend_ctx*.png (50% blend), atlas_ctx*_box.png, atlas_grid_zoom14.png (gridded atlas), art_grid.png, art_crop_{east,south,promontory}.png, art_water_mask.png/.npy, atlas_water_mask_halfpx.png/.npy, ties_today.png, ties_ties_trans_scale.png and ties_pair.png (tie residual vectors plus art coast), fit_today.png, fit_iou_*.png and fit_pair_{A,B}.png (coast-mode overlays), fits_ties.json, fit_mask_iou.json, fit_mask_summary.json, ties_report.json. The prev_run/ subfolder holds an earlier run's outputs; I moved them aside and did not use them as evidence. No browser, server, git or repo writes; reads only from the HEAD export.

- Translation + uniform scale: rms 5.25, max 6.84; leave-one-out rms 9.13, max 12.58.

votes.corrected:
My recount gives identifiable_n = 0 strict point features. T1 can count as a partial x-only constraint, which makes it 1 at most. The analysis said 2. Per tie, re-rendered from the z5 tiles and overlay-Epeshu.jpg (2863x3072, which confirms the file size):
- T1: not the same feature. The atlas point (1223.3,1412) is the westmost point of a ~10 px promontory that the coast draws around the ring symbol, turning about 90 deg from WSW to SSE (drafting clearance). The art point (462,1560) is a small bump at the Necropolis, under 1 atlas px, turning about 30 deg from SSW to S. The art coast has no promontory and no SE inlet. It only works as a latitude-matched shore point, which fixes x and leaves y loose.
- T5: a symbol convention (ring = Forum 7), not a geographic feature. It is a policy choice and should not be counted as a tie.
- T2: corner versus gentle bulge, ambiguous along the shore, low confidence. The pairing is the right concept.
- T3 and T4: the road identities are right. T3 is the sun-ward road and the only east exit. T4 is the art's only road reaching the bottom edge, the double-line SSE trunk at about x 1390-1410, and the atlas has only one south road. Both art points are frame-edge exits paired with atlas points that are not the same point: a bend for T3, and today's box bottom edge for T4. They are cross-track or line constraints, not point ties. Treated as points, their along-track part is fake: T3 alone pulls the right edge in by ~4.8 px.

So the 0.83x scale from the 5-tie fit, and its "tie rms 8 to 5", are artifacts of mis-posed ties, not a scale the ties imply. When I refit with T3 and T4 as line constraints, the result depends on which atlas segment T3 is tied to:
- the SSE segment past the bend gives 0.61-0.73x
- the E-running segment gives 0.69-1.03x
- either way the centre lands about 3-6 px E and 0-2 px N of the anchor.

So the ties do not pin scale, which strengthens the analysis's own conclusion. I recomputed coast chamfer independently from my own atlas sea mask, with the ring and road-dot holes filled:
- today: 9.47 rms / 21.5 max (analysis: 9.30/19.96)
- the 0.825x fit: 5.46 (analysis: 5.80)
- mode C: 2.37 (analysis: 1.54)
- today's water IoU: 0.377 (analysis: 0.362)

votes.corrected: REGISTRATION diagnosis, narrowed to what the sources show. In maps-site/index.html (HEAD export), px(x,y) is `map.unproject([x,y],NZ)`. The base tile layer's bounds (px(0,0)..px(TILE_W,TILE_H)) and the city overlay's bounds (`L.latLngBounds(px(box.x0,box.y0),px(box.x1,box.y1))`) both go through it under L.CRS.Simple. The overlay box comes from cityBox, which centres a box of half-size FOOT_R[kind] on the anchor and aspect-fits the image into it, whatever the image depicts. So the overlay shares the base's coordinate frame and does not drift with zoom. Any misfit is therefore a fixed offset or scale error in world px (set by the anchor dot, FOOT_R and the aspect-fit), and the screen shows it magnified by 2^(z-4). The factor is 1 at z4 (2 px of misfit is 2 screen px), 16 at z8 (32 px) and 2^7.5, about 181, at Z_STREET 11.5 (about 360 px, not 300). Leaflet 1.9.4 ImageOverlay._reset builds its bounds from map.latLngToLayerPoint, which calls project(...)._round(). That rounds each corner by at most 0.5 layer px, which is negligible beside these errors. The sources do not measure the actual misfit: the "2 world px" is an illustrative figure, not a measured one. Placing a vector city through the same cityBox keeps the same placement error, so the medium does not fix registration. A better registration, meaning a placement transform or per-city control points fitted to atlas features (coast, rivers, road entries), is what changes it. The sources do not show that a plain offset or scale transform is sufficient, only that registration is where the fix lives.

A rotated, skewed or piecewise (rubber-sheet) warp would have to be baked into the image or drawn by a custom canvas layer, never by moving the atlas. Do not edit the pinned functions (genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask): keep the canon transform in cityBox's caller or in the anchor data. A vector layer placed through the same cityBox carries exactly the same error. Vector rendering only adds crispness, interactivity and road vertices shared with the atlas once registration is fixed.

items.summary: Minimum GCPs: straight 2, Helmert 2, affine 3, projective 4, polynomial 2 six, polynomial 3 ten, TPS 3 (Allmaps) or 10+ (QGIS); usable transforms are capped by L.imageOverlay's axis-aligned box.

prior_record.claim:
Transform types and the minimum GCPs each needs:
- straight (translation and uniform scale): 2
- Helmert/similarity (adds rotation; shape and angles kept): 2
- affine/polynomial 1 (adds shear; straight and parallel lines kept): 3
- projective (perspective): 4
- polynomial 2: 6
- polynomial 3: 10
- thin-plate spline (TPS): 3 in Allmaps; QGIS says 'technically 10, usually more'.
GDAL fits up to order 2 automatically and warns that order 3 is unstable.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Yes, as the menu. Every one of these is a small linear solve (about 10 lines for Helmert or affine least squares; a dense (n+3)^2 system for TPS) that fits inline in one file. They are deterministic and need no seed.

evidence.quote: `helmert` | Helmert transformation or 'similarity transformation' | Applies translation, scaling and rotation. Preserves shapes and angles. | 2
`thinPlateSpline` | Thin Plate Spline transformation or 'rubber sheeting' (with affine part) | ... Transformation is 'exact' at GPCs. | 3
It technically requires a minimum of 10 GCPs, but usually more to be successful.
Note that 2nd order requires at least 6 GCPs, and 3rd order requires at least 10 gcps. If nReqOrder is 0 the highest order possible (limited to 2)
three control points that are collinear (one the same line) only count as two linearly independent points

votes.corrected: Same table as claimed, with one change. Collinear points count as fewer independent points. GDAL: gdal_crs.cpp states order 2 needs at least 6 GCPs and order 3 at least 10. When the order is left at 0 it picks order 2 only with 6 or more GCPs (order 1 below that), and never picks order 3. The source comment says "for now we avoid 3rd order since it is unstable". That is a developer code comment, not a warning shown to users, so "GDAL warns that order 3 is unstable" overreaches. Say instead: GDAL's auto order selection is capped at 2 (needs at least 6 GCPs, else 1), with a source comment calling order 3 unstable.

The Allmaps README table (beta.53) gives helmert 2, polynomial 3, polynomial2 6, polynomial3 10, thinPlateSpline 3, projective 4, straight 2, and has the collinear-points sentence. The auto-selection also depends on GCP count: order 2 needs 6 or more GCPs, otherwise order 1. The rest of the claim holds.

votes.corrected: Yes, as a reference menu. The counts are correct as sourced: Allmaps lists 3 GCPs for TPS because its TPS includes an affine part, QGIS says 10 or more, and GDAL auto-fits at most order 2. The solves are small and deterministic, use no seed, and fit inline. Two limits apply to us. (1) The render path caps which transforms we can use. L.imageOverlay (cityBox in maps-site/index.html, also used by enterChart) only places an axis-aligned box: translation plus per-axis scale. Helmert rotation, affine shear, projective and TPS cannot go through it. A raster needs a one-time warp into a canvas. Affine can use ctx.setTransform. Projective and TPS need a triangle-mesh warp, or a CSS matrix3d on the overlay img, which must survive Leaflet's own translate3d positioning. Vector geometry takes any of these transforms per vertex at no extra cost, but the vertices still need the same fitted transform. (2) GCP supply caps which transforms are sensible. A city has only a few reliable atlas features (coast or harbor points, river mouths or crossings, road entries), and some of those may be collinear. With so few points, Helmert (2+) or affine (3+) is the realistic choice, fit by least squares with residuals reported. Polynomial 2/3 and TPS would overfit; TPS is exact at the GCPs, so it bakes in any picking error. Use TPS only for DM canon art with many well-spread GCPs (Epeshu, Summarch). Project constraints: fit art to atlas, never the reverse. Do the warp after genCityCanvas, never inside it: genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask are hash-pinned (UG3 atlas_fn_sha), and cityCanvasSha must not change. Warp once per city and cache the result, never per frame, to stay inside the mobile frame budget.

A vector layer avoids that limit but still needs the fitted transform. With the few GCPs a city offers, only Helmert or affine is well-posed, so higher orders and TPS are risky unless a city has many well-spread GCPs. items.summary: Over-determined Helmert/affine/polynomial fits average noise with residuals, while TPS interpolates exactly (RMS always 0); prefer Helmert or affine, scoped to the two canon overlays.

prior_record.claim: Over-determined fits behave differently by type. With more than the minimum GCPs, Helmert, affine and polynomial fits are least-squares: each GCP gets a residual, and noise in any one point is averaged out. TPS has no residuals. It passes exactly through every GCP, so one misplaced click bends the art locally and its RMS is always 0. The standard remedy is a smoothing term, which turns TPS back toward a least-squares polynomial.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Yes. Our GCPs will be few and noisy (see R6), which is exactly the case where TPS hurts. Prefer Helmert or affine. If TPS is ever used, add smoothing or restrict it to the coast band.

evidence.quote: In contrast, TPS will precisely match all specified GCPs, but may introduce significant deformations between nearby GCPs with registration errors.
In all of the algorithms except TPS, if more than the minimum GCPs are specified, parameters will be fitted so that the overall residual error is minimized.
The interpolant perfectly fits the data when this is set to 0. For large values, the interpolant approaches a least squares fit of a polynomial

votes.corrected: All three quotes exist verbatim and support the core of the claim. QGIS 3.34 docs: in every transformation except TPS, if more than the minimum GCPs are given, parameters are fitted to minimise overall residual error, which helps against slightly imprecise clicks (the fit then matches GCPs only approximately). TPS "will precisely match all specified GCPs, but may introduce significant deformations between nearby GCPs with registration errors". SciPy RBFInterpolator: smoothing 0 fits the data perfectly, and for large values the interpolant approaches a least-squares fit of a polynomial of the specified degree. Not supported by the cited sources: (a) "its RMS is always 0" — neither source says it. It is a mathematical corollary of exact interpolation, not a cited fact, and QGIS does not report a TPS RMS. (b) "standard remedy" — SciPy only shows that a smoothing parameter exists. QGIS's TPS has no smoothing option, so adding smoothing means leaving QGIS. (c) The smoothing limit is only approached "for large values", and the polynomial is of the chosen degree (SciPy's thin_plate_spline default degree is 1, which is affine). (d) "noise is averaged out" overstates QGIS's wording ("minimize the impact of registration errors"). Narrowest supported claim: with more than the minimum GCPs, non-TPS fits are least-squares and only approximately match each GCP, whereas TPS matches every GCP exactly, so a mis-clicked GCP deforms the art locally. A TPS smoothing parameter, where one exists (SciPy RBFInterpolator), trades exactness for a fit that approaches a polynomial least-squares fit as it grows.
votes.reason: Quotes verified against the QGIS 3.34 georeferencer.rst and SciPy _rbfinterp.py (smoothing parameter docstring). The mechanism claims hold. The claim overreaches on "RMS is always 0" (inference, in neither source), "standard remedy" (QGIS offers no TPS smoothing, SciPy only documents the parameter), and "noise is averaged out" (QGIS says "minimize the impact").

votes.corrected:
Yes, with limits. The claim is generic georeferencing fact and it transfers. Applied to us, it only touches REGISTRATION (where the art sits). It has nothing to say about the rendering medium (raster or vector).

(1) Scope. It applies only to the two DM canon overlays, overlay-Epeshu.jpg and overlay-Summarch.jpg, plus their chart pyramids. Procedural plans (genCityCanvas) need no GCP fit: sampleCityMask samples the land/water mask from the z5 tiles inside the same cityBox, so their water already sits on the atlas water by construction.

(2) Noise. Our GCPs are few and coarse. cityBox squeezes a roughly 3000 px drawing into a 52-world-px box (FOOT_R capital 26). At that size the atlas shows only a few resolvable features (coast, river mouth, road exits), each accurate to about 1 to 2 world px, which is about 60 to 120 art px. That is the noisy, sparse case where exact interpolation is dangerous. So the default is: Helmert (4 parameters) for each canon overlay, and affine only when there are 4 or more well-spread GCPs. Check the fit with per-GCP residuals and leave-one-out error, never with TPS's RMS, which is always 0.

(3) Residuals need redundancy. With exactly the minimum number of points (2 for Helmert, 3 for affine) every type passes exactly through them and has no residuals. Collect more than the minimum.

(4) Leaflet. L.imageOverlay only takes axis-aligned bounds. A rotation or shear has to be applied either as a CSS matrix transform on the overlay element (vanilla, inline, no plugin) or as a deterministic canvas pre-warp. Plain scale plus translate fits into the existing bounds.

(5) Local warps. TPS stays an opt-in for one specific problem: a measured local mismatch (for example the coast) that persists after the global fit. Use it only with smoothing or a few hand-checked control points. It bends the art to the atlas, never the reverse. A pure-JS smoothing TPS is feasible, but it is a per-pixel warp and must be computed once and cached, never per frame.

(6) Constraints. Store the fit as authored GCP JSON (e.g. in city-anchors.json) and solve it with plain arithmetic. That keeps it deterministic and leaves the pinned functions untouched (genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask, cityCanvasSha). Coordinate the change with the mobile atlas lane, which is mid-flight in maps-site/index.html.
votes.reason:
The claim is accurate and well sourced. QGIS documents that TPS passes exactly through every GCP while the other types are least-squares, and scipy documents that smoothing moves an RBF toward a least-squares polynomial fit. The "prefer Helmert/affine" advice also suits our stack. In maps-site/index.html, cityBox(a,w,h) places each overlay as an axis-aligned square of half-size footR(kind) centred on the anchor. The canon art is about 3000 px drawn into 52 world px, so atlas control points are sparse and coarse relative to the art. One bad click under TPS would visibly bend DM canon art.

applies_to_us needs four corrections. (a) The fit only matters for the two canon DM overlays: procedural plans already line up with atlas water, because sampleCityMask samples the mask inside the same cityBox. (b) With only the minimum number of GCPs nothing has residuals, so the least-squares advantage needs redundant points. A sound check is leave-one-out error, not TPS RMS. (c) L.imageOverlay is axis-aligned, so any rotation or affine fit needs a CSS matrix transform or a cached canvas warp. (d) The "coast band" TPS idea is vague. Keep it as an opt-in, smoothed, cached local warp, and keep the fit outside the pinned functions so the hash pins and the in-flight mobile lane are unaffected.

None of this fixes misalignment by switching the medium. A vector city placed through the same cityBox would misalign exactly as the raster does.

items.summary: QGIS, Map Warper and gdalwarp report per-GCP residuals and RMS; leave-one-out is standard statistics, not a cited tool feature; commit GCPs as data with a node residual/LOO gate.

prior_record.claim: How the tools report error. QGIS lists per-GCP residuals and RMS errors, in pixels or map units. Map Warper computes per-GCP error and an overall map error. gdalwarp -refine_gcps iteratively drops outliers, for polynomial fits only, with tolerance in pixel units when there is no projection. For TPS, residual RMS is always 0 and tells you nothing, so a held-out check is needed: leave one GCP out, fit, measure its miss, repeat. No reachable primary source documents leave-one-out for a georeferencing tool, so this part is the standard statistical method applied here, not a cited feature.
prior_record.confidence: high for QGIS/GDAL/Map Warper reporting; medium for leave-one-out (inferred, no tool doc reachable)
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Yes. Commit GCPs as data and have a node tool print per-GCP residuals and RMS (in atlas px, and in screen px at z8 = x16) plus leave-one-out misses. Use that as the acceptance gate for each canon city's registration.

evidence.quote: an image of the residuals and a list with all GCPs and their RMS errors.
# map gets error attibute set and gcps get error attribute set
Note that GCP refinement only works with polynomial interpolation. The tolerance is in pixel units if no projection is available

votes.corrected: Holds as written, with one note on sourcing. All three quotes were fetched (HTTP 200) and are verbatim. QGIS 3.34 georeferencer.rst says the report includes "an image of the residuals and a list with all GCPs and their RMS errors", and its settings say residual units are pixels or map units. Map Warper map.rb has the comment "map gets error attibute set and gcps get error attribute set", and gcps_with_error calls ErrorCalculator::calc_error, which returns per-GCP errors plus a map_error stored in @error. gdalwarp.rst says "GCP refinement only works with polynomial interpolation. The tolerance is in pixel units if no projection is available, otherwise it is in SRS units", and describes -refine_gcps as eliminating outliers until minimum_gcps remain or none are found. The TPS claim "residual RMS is always 0" is not stated in any cited quote. The QGIS doc supports it only indirectly: "TPS will precisely match all specified GCPs" (an exact interpolator, so residuals at the GCPs are zero by construction), and the line before it says the residual-minimising fit applies "in all of the algorithms except TPS". Cite that sentence for the TPS point and treat the zero-RMS conclusion as an inference from it. The claim already labels leave-one-out as the standard statistical method with no tool citation, which is accurate: neither the QGIS doc nor gdalwarp.rst mentions leave-one-out or cross-validation. Minor: the QGIS quote supports a per-GCP RMS list in the PDF report. It does not say outright that the list also shows per-GCP residuals in pixels.
votes.reason: All three cited sources are reachable and the quotes exist verbatim, and each supports the reporting claim it is attached to. The TPS zero-residual point rests on the QGIS statement that TPS exactly matches all GCPs, an inference from that sentence and not a quoted fact. The leave-one-out part is correctly disclaimed as not a documented tool feature. The only edits are sourcing precision: cite the QGIS TPS sentence, and note the report lists per-GCP RMS errors.

votes.corrected: Yes, with limits. This is about registration only: it measures where the art sits relative to atlas features. It does nothing for the rendering medium, and a vector city placed through the same cityBox needs exactly the same gate. Store each canon city's GCPs as committed data, for example a maps-site/data JSON keyed like city-anchors.json, with each pair as image px to atlas px. Pick the points on features that both the DM art and PatrinorModern clearly show: coast inflections, river mouths and bends, and where dotted roads leave the town. Write a read-only node tool in tools/ that prints, for each GCP, the residual and the RMS. Report them in atlas px and also in screen px at z8 (x16, since NZ=4) and at the deepest zoom the city actually reaches (cityMaxZ / Z_STREET 11.5, about x180). Score the residuals under the model the page actually draws. Today that model is cityBox through L.imageOverlay: axis-aligned bounds, with translate and per-axis scale only, so no rotation or shear. If you want a richer fit (similarity, affine or TPS), first ship a way to display it, either an image pre-warped offline into the atlas frame or a mesh/canvas warp. Otherwise the reported error will not match what users see. Report leave-one-out misses as standard statistics, not as a cited tool feature. They mean something only with enough points: at least 3 for the 4-parameter box model, more for affine, and many more for TPS. A canon city footprint is only about 52 atlas px wide (capital r=26), so expect few usable GCPs per city. Set the pass threshold in atlas px, no tighter than the precision of picking a point on the atlas, which is about 1 atlas px or 16 screen px at z8. The gate covers only the DM canon art: overlay-Epeshu, overlay-Summarch and the chart pyramids in detail-charts.json. Procedural genCityCanvas cities have no GCPs. They take their registration from sampleCityMask over the atlas tiles, so they need a different check. The tool must stay offline. It must not touch the pinned functions (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask), cityCanvasSha or the mobile per-frame budget, and the atlas never moves to fit the art.
votes.reason: The general approach transfers. It is offline tooling, adds no runtime cost, is deterministic, and fits the existing tools/*.js read-only node style (tools/living-drift.js, street-drift.js). It also matches the project rule that registration bends the art to the atlas. The x16 conversion at z8 is right for NZ=4. The claim as written misses four things specific to our stack. (1) The runtime cannot display a fitted transform. cityBox(a,w,h) in maps-site/index.html builds an axis-aligned box from the anchor dot and FOOT_R[kind], and the page draws it with L.imageOverlay(reg.url,cb,...), which takes bounds only. So residuals have to be computed under that box model, unless a pre-warp or mesh-warp step ships too. The TPS and leave-one-out discussion only matters once the display can show a richer warp. (2) GCPs will be few per city because the canon footprints are small (26/14/9/8 world px radius). That makes leave-one-out unstable and puts a floor on the threshold set by atlas resolution (about 1 atlas px, which is 16 screen px at z8 and about 180 at Z_STREET 11.5). (3) The gate applies only to the DM canon overlays and chart pyramids (overlay-Epeshu.jpg, overlay-Summarch.jpg, detail-charts.json entries), not to procedural cities. (4) No GCP data exists in the repo yet: there is no GCP or residual data in maps-site/data or tools. The anchors only record atlasX/atlasY, kind, harbor and sea, so the data and the tool are both new work. The cited facts about QGIS, Map Warper and gdalwarp are consistent with their quoted sources and are not load-bearing here.

items.summary: Tie supply is limited by the atlas (52 px footprint, coarse features only), ruling out polynomial 2+ and TPS; the GCP-count estimate is superseded by the measured tie work, and the traced-roads aside was struck.

prior_record.claim: Our GCP supply is limited by the atlas, not the art. At z4 (1 world px = 1 atlas px) Epēshu's footprint is only about 52 atlas px across. Expect 4-8 GCPs with about ±1 atlas px error each. That points to Helmert (4 parameters), or affine (6) if residuals show squash along one axis. Polynomial 2+ and TPS are ruled out.
