(3) The leaflet-zoom-animated class plus transition applies to the discrete animated-zoom path (Map._animateZoom adds leaflet-zoom-anim and fires 'zoomanim'); there ImageOverlay sets a CSS transform via _animateZoom, and a custom element needs BOTH the class and its own zoomanim handler that sets the transform, so the class alone is not sufficient. (4) The cost contrast with a canvas warp on 'zoom' and the 'mobile budget rules it out' conclusion are the researcher's inference, not shown by the quotes; also _reset resizes via width/height (layout), not a pure transform.
votes.reason: Quotes verified in the HEAD leaflet.css and leaflet-1.9.4.tgz source. But the claim conflates two paths: flyTo only calls _move per frame (zoom event -> ImageOverlay._reset) and never adds leaflet-zoom-anim or fires zoomanim, so the CSS transition/class is irrelevant to fly-ins. 'Must carry leaflet-zoom-animated' overreaches, since a zoomanim handler setting the transform is also required. The O(1) vs per-pixel cost comparison is unsupported inference. flyIntoCity/ensureArrival do use map.flyTo (verified in maps-site/index.html).

votes.corrected: Yes, with corrections. The performance point holds. flyIntoCity and ensureArrival call map.flyTo, the marker and journey fly helpers call flyTo, and touch pinch calls _move with pinch:true. All of these fire 'zoom' on every frame, so ImageOverlay._reset (zoom:this._reset) runs once per frame. The atlas already uses that frame: map.on('zoom zoomend moveend',worldOpacityUpdate) in maps-site/index.html calls only setOpacity. That is O(1) per frame and should stay that way. Any registration warp must therefore be baked once: a pre-warped plain overlay (R12), or a CSS matrix on a wrapper (R8). It must never be a CPU re-sample of pixels on 'zoom', which would blow the mobile per-frame budget. If R12 bakes the warp inside genCityCanvas, it changes the pinned cityCanvasSha and the UG3 atlas_fn_sha, so it must be coordinated with the mobile lane (Mobile 5-9). Doing the warp as a separate post-pass outside the pinned functions avoids that. Corrections: (1) The CSS class alone does not keep a custom element in step. The leaflet-zoom-animated transition only applies during the animated zoom (wheel, double-click or button zoom under zoomAnimationThreshold, which goes through _tryAnimatedZoom), and the element also needs a 'zoomanim' handler that sets its transform, as ImageOverlay._animateZoom does. A custom R8 wrapper must replicate both the zoomanim handler and the zoom/viewreset _reset. flyTo and pinch bypass the CSS transition entirely and run purely through the per-frame 'zoom' _reset. (2) 'O(1)' covers the JavaScript only. _reset resizes the element every frame, so the browser re-rasterizes it every frame. For a large JPEG overlay that cost is bounded. For a vectorized city in L.svgOverlay or another resized SVG, it grows with path count on every frame of a fly. Leaflet's own L.SVG/Canvas renderers avoid this by applying a transform mid-zoom and redrawing only on zoomend. A vector city layer should follow that pattern or be pre-rasterized. (3) None of this fixes registration. A cheap overlay placed through cityBox still misaligns. What fixes it is the transform bake, not the per-frame mechanism.
votes.reason: Checked against the HEAD export. maps-site/index.html calls map.flyTo in flyIntoCity, flyToMarker and flyTo, and binds worldOpacityUpdate to the live 'zoom' event. leaflet.css has the .leaflet-zoom-anim .leaflet-zoom-animated transition. The evidence quotes match Leaflet 1.9.4 behaviour (flyTo calls _move each frame, which fires 'zoom', which runs ImageOverlay._reset). So the conclusion holds for us: no runtime CPU warp, and the warp must be baked or done with a CSS matrix or GPU. The claim overstates the role of the CSS class. That class plus the transition only cover the animated zoom path (wheel, double-click, buttons), and only when a zoomanim handler sets the transform. flyTo and pinch skip the transition and rely on the per-frame _reset. Saying 'O(1)' also leaves out the browser re-rasterizing a resized SVG or vector element every frame, which matters for the owner's vectorized-city idea. It also leaves out that baking the warp into genCityCanvas would break the mobile cityCanvasSha and atlas_fn_sha pins. These gaps refine the claim rather than overturn it, so holds=true at minor severity.

items.summary: Allmaps stores GCPs, transform type and mask in IIIF Georeference Annotations and renders via WebGL2; not a runtime dependency, but its data shape and algorithms are worth borrowing; the fly-in conflict was overstated.

prior_record.claim:
How Allmaps works:
- Data model: a IIIF Georeference Annotation stores GCPs as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection. Each GCP is a Point in WGS84 with a resourceCoords [x,y] property; an optional transformation {type: polynomial|thinPlateSpline, options:{order}} and an SVG selector for the mask sit alongside.
- Rendering: WebGL2 triangulates the mask, back-projects the viewport to fetch IIIF tiles, and draws each triangle at its forward-transformed spot.
- Plugins: Leaflet, OpenLayers and MapLibre.
- Algorithms: @allmaps/transform gives results (nearly) identical to GDAL's.
- Leaflet plugin limits: it ships ESM-only with bare imports, assumes WGS84 GCPs and Web Mercator (proj4), needs IIIF tile sources, and the README sets zoomAnimationThreshold: 1 because multi-level zoom animation is unsupported.
prior_record.confidence: high on what Allmaps does; medium on its incompatibility with CRS.Simple (projection defaults verified; not tried)
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Not as a runtime dependency: it needs a build, IIIF tiles and a geographic CRS, and conflicts with our fly-in animations. Worth borrowing are the data shape (GCP list of art px to atlas px plus a transformation type plus a mask polygon, as a committed JSON per canon city) and its algorithms as the reference implementation to port inline.

evidence.quote: A GeoJSON Feature Collection where each GCP is stored as a GeoJSON Feature with Point geometry and a `resourceCoords` property

The area inside the resource mask is rendered in the viewport, triangle by triangle, using the cached tiles. The location of where to render each triangle is computed using the forward transformation built from the GPCs.
The transformation algorithms of this package correspond to those of **GDAL** and the results are (nearly) identical.
// Zoom animations for more than one zoom level are // currently not supported by the Allmaps plugin for Leaflet zoomAnimationThreshold: 1
import { lonLatProjection, webMercatorProjection } from "@allmaps/project"; ... projection: webMercatorProjection
import { WebGL2Renderer } from "@allmaps/render/webgl2";

votes.corrected: Supported (all six quotes exist verbatim): (1) IIIF Georeference spec: GCPs are a GeoJSON FeatureCollection of Point Features (WGS84) each with properties.resourceCoords [x,y]; an optional `transformation` object on that collection with type polynomial (options.order 1-3) or thinPlateSpline (no options); the mask is an SvgSelector on the annotation's target, not part of the FeatureCollection. (2) @allmaps/render WebGL2: the resource mask is triangulated, the viewport is transformed back to resource coords to fetch IIIF tiles, and each triangle is drawn at its forward-transformed position from the GCPs. (3) Plugins exist for Leaflet, OpenLayers and MapLibre. (4) @allmaps/transform: algorithms correspond to GDAL's with (nearly) identical results. (5) The @allmaps/leaflet README sets zoomAnimationThreshold: 1, commenting that zoom animations of more than one level are not currently supported. (6) @allmaps/render's Viewport defaults to webMercatorProjection (uses proj4), and the Leaflet WarpedMapLayer builds its Viewport with that default, reading center and scale through map.options.crs.project; it needs georeferenced IIIF images (served by an IIIF image server) as its source. Not supported / to drop or soften: "ships ESM-only" -- the Leaflet README says "works in browsers and in Node.js as an ESM or an UMD module" (the beta.55 tarball itself contains only dist/index.js with exports ./dist/index.js and bare imports of leaflet and @allmaps/render/webgl2, so say "the published tarball contains only ESM with bare imports; the README claims a UMD build I did not find"). "Assumes ... Web Mercator" is true of the Viewport default only; that CRS.Simple would break is inference (the plugin projects through the map's own crs, so under CRS.Simple the viewport would be in map units but still labelled Web Mercator), untested -- consistent with the claim's own medium confidence. "Conflicts with our fly-in animations" is not established by the README: the caveat concerns multi-level zoom animation (setZoom/zoomIn animated transforms); our flyTo calls (map.flyTo in maps-site/index.html) are Leaflet's frame-by-frame moves, and whether the layer redraws correctly through them was not tested. The applies_to_us recommendation (not as a runtime dependency; borrow the GCP + transformation type + mask polygon data shape and port the algorithms) rests on build/IIIF/CRS needs, which are supported, so it stands without the fly-in clause.
votes.reason: Core facts are verified against the IIIF spec and the @allmaps render, transform and leaflet package files. Three parts overreach: "ESM-only" is contradicted by the README (ESM or UMD), Web Mercator is only the Viewport default and its CRS.Simple incompatibility is inferred, and "conflicts with fly-in animations" is an untested inference from a multi-level-zoom-animation caveat. Mask SvgSelector placement ("alongside" the transformation) is also loose, since it sits in the annotation target.

votes.corrected:
Not as a runtime dependency. @allmaps/leaflet ships ESM-only with bare imports, so it needs a build. It assumes WGS84 GCPs and Web Mercator, which clashes with L.CRS.Simple. It needs IIIF tile sources, and its WebGL2 renderer draws a triangulated mesh every frame, which costs the mobile per-frame budget. The fly-in conflict is overstated. flyIntoCity and flyToMarker use map.flyTo, which Leaflet animates with a per-frame loop and not through zoomAnimationThreshold. It is not a primary blocker.

Borrow two things, both for REGISTRATION only:
(1) The data shape, as a committed JSON per DM canon art: a GCP list of art px [x,y] to atlas px, a transformation type (affine/polynomial order 1-2 or thin-plate spline) and a mask polygon in art px. This covers overlay-Epeshu.jpg, overlay-Summarch.jpg and the charts/epeshu and charts/summarch pyramids used by enterChart. GCPs sit on atlas features such as coast, river mouths, road exits and walls, so the art bends to the atlas.
(2) The solve, ported as a small pure function or run offline. @allmaps/transform can run inside a node tools/ script as a dev dependency, like build-gazetteer.js.

Do NOT port the per-frame triangle renderer into the page. Bake the warp offline into a deterministic atlas-frame image (and re-tile the chart pyramid) with exact atlas bounds. Those bounds replace the cityBox/footR box for canon cities only. The page cost stays one L.imageOverlay. Any future vector city layer traced from DM art is pushed through the same transform, so raster and vector register identically.

Procedural cities (genCityCanvas, sampleCityMask, buildCityStubs) are already drawn in the atlas frame and need no GCPs. Leave those pinned functions (UG3 atlas_fn_sha, cityCanvasSha) untouched. Land the change after the Mobile 5-9 atlas lane releases maps-site/index.html.
votes.reason:
The overall verdict transfers: no runtime dependency; borrow the GCP, transform and mask data shape and the transform algorithms. It respects "atlas authoritative" (GCPs bend art to the atlas), and it targets REGISTRATION, which is the real cause of the misalignment. Today cityBox in maps-site/index.html places each overlay as a box of footR(kind) around the anchor, whatever the image shows. A vector city placed through that box would misalign the same way.

Three corrections:
(a) The animation conflict is mis-cited. The atlas flies in with map.flyTo (flyIntoCity, flyToMarker, flyTo in maps-site/index.html), which Leaflet drives frame by frame and not through zoomAnimationThreshold. The real blockers are the ESM build, the Web Mercator/WGS84 projection, IIIF tile sources, and the WebGL2 cost on mobile.
(b) "Port its algorithms inline" invites porting the runtime mesh renderer. For one vanilla file with a mobile budget, the right move is an offline, deterministic bake in tools/ (or porting only the transform solve). That yields a pre-warped image plus exact atlas bounds, so the page still uses a single L.imageOverlay.
(c) Scope it to the DM canon art: the two overlay JPGs and the chart pyramids that enterChart builds with L.imageOverlay. Procedural plans are generated in atlas coordinates and are covered by pinned hashes, so they should not be touched.

Nothing in the repo uses Allmaps or GCPs yet (no hits in docs/research/accurate-mapping.md or the data files), so this would be new committed data per canon city.

items.summary: The offline GDAL pre-warp route overreached: Map Warper works in EPSG:4326 with alpha, and the route applies only to canon overlays.

prior_record.claim: The offline route keeps the runtime a plain L.imageOverlay. Fit GCPs once, then resample the art into a new axis-aligned image whose bounds are the warped quad's bounding box in world px. gdal_translate -gcp attaches pixel-to-target pairs and gdalwarp warps with -order 1-3 or -tps. Without an SRS, tolerances are in pixels, so atlas world px can serve as target coordinates. Map Warper runs exactly this pipeline server-side. ImageMagick 6.9.12 is available locally and its -distort covers Affine, ScaleRotateTranslate (SRT), Polynomial and Shepards control-point warps.
prior_record.confidence: high on tool behaviour; medium on the exact command line for a no-SRS, y-down target (not run)
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Yes, and it fits best. It is a build artifact (committed image plus GCP JSON), so the seeded runtime and the hash-pinned functions are untouched (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask, cityCanvasSha), and nothing changes per frame. The cost: the warped image gains empty corners, which need parchment fill or an alpha format (JPG has no alpha), and both canon overlays and the chart pyramids under charts/epeshu and charts/summarch must be re-cut if those should line up too.

evidence.quote: -gcp <pixel> <line> <easting> <northing> [<elevation>] Add the indicated ground control point to the output dataset.

-order <n> order of polynomial used for warping (1 to 3). The default is to select a polynomial order based on the number of GCPs. ... -tps Force use of Thin Plate Spline transformer based on available GCPs.
when "p1" transform_option = " -order 1 " ... when "tps" transform_option = " -tps "
command = ["#{GDAL_PATH}gdal_translate", "-a_srs", "EPSG:4326", "-of", "VRT", src_filename, "#{temp_filename}.vrt", gdal_gcp_array]
Affine AffineProjection ScaleRotateTranslate SRT Perspective ... Polynomial ... Shepards

votes.corrected: All five quotes check out, but two sentences overreach them. What the evidence supports: gdal_translate -gcp attaches GCPs to a dataset, and gdalwarp can resample with -order 1-3 or -tps. Map Warper runs a similar GCP, VRT and gdalwarp pipeline server-side, but it georeferences in EPSG:4326 (lon/lat, via -a_srs and -s_srs), not in a no-SRS pixel space. Its gdalwarp call also adds -dstalpha and COMPRESS=JPEG, so it emits an alpha channel. The pixel-unit statement is documented only for gdalwarp -refine_gcps ("The tolerance is in pixel units if no projection is available, otherwise it is in SRS units"). The -et and other tolerances are not covered, and none of the cited quotes supports the broader claim. Using atlas world px as an SRS-less target frame is therefore an untested design inference, not a documented behaviour. ImageMagick 6.9.12-98 is installed and lists Affine, ScaleRotateTranslate/SRT, Polynomial and Shepards. Of these, Polynomial and Shepards (and Affine, given 3 or more point pairs) take control-point pairs. SRT takes explicit scale, rotate and translate parameters, not control points.
votes.reason:
Verified by fetching the cited sources.

Supported:
- gdal_translate.rst has "-gcp <pixel> <line> <easting> <northing> [<elevation>]: Add the indicated ground control point to the output dataset", followed by "may be provided multiple times".
- gdalwarp.rst has the -order text ("order of polynomial used for warping (1 to 3). The default is to select a polynomial order based on the number of GCPs") and -tps ("Force use of Thin Plate Spline transformer based on available GCPs").
- maps_controller.rb has the case "p1" -> " -order 1 " ... "tps" -> " -tps ".
- map.rb line 691 matches the gdal_translate -a_srs EPSG:4326 -of VRT quote, apart from a trailing .flatten.
- convert -list distort on ImageMagick 6.9.12-98 lists Affine, AffineProjection, ScaleRotateTranslate, SRT, Perspective, Polynomial and Shepards.

Overreach:
1. "Without an SRS, tolerances are in pixels, so atlas world px can serve as target coordinates" has no cited quote. The only matching doc sentence is the one under -refine_gcps, which is narrower than "tolerances", and the doc says nothing about using arbitrary pixel space as a target frame.
2. "Map Warper runs exactly this pipeline" is not supported. map.rb line 709 shows gdalwarp with -s_srs EPSG:4326, -dstalpha, -dstnodata none and -co COMPRESS=JPEG, so the target frame is lon/lat, not world px. The command also shows no resampling to a bbox in world px and no explicit -t_srs. Only the GCP, VRT and gdalwarp shape matches.
3. Listing SRT among "control-point warps" is loose. The practical conclusion still stands (offline resample, committed image, runtime unchanged), but the exact no-SRS y-down command line is unverified, as the claim itself notes.

votes.corrected: Partly. This is a REGISTRATION fix, and only for the two canon overlays (art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg and overlay-Summarch.jpg). It does not apply to the procedural genCityCanvas plans: those are drawn at runtime against the sampleCityMask land/water mask inside cityBox, so their misfit comes from the footprint box and the mask, not from un-warped art. Fitting GCPs offline (art px to atlas world px, y-down, no SRS) and resampling to an axis-aligned image does keep the overlay a plain L.imageOverlay. It also keeps the seeded and hash-pinned code byte-identical and adds no per-frame cost. It also obeys the rule that the art bends to the atlas. But the tooling and the runtime claims are wrong. (1) GDAL is not installed in this container; only ImageMagick 6.9.12 is. So the working route is `convert -virtual-pixel` with a parchment background and `+distort Affine|Polynomial|Shepards` using the GCP pairs, and +distort's viewport gives the bbox offset. Otherwise GDAL becomes a new offline dependency. (2) The runtime is not untouched. In maps-site/index.html, cityBox(a,w,h) sets the overlay bounds in ensureCityOverlay. It is also called by the canon POI reprojection (the two `cityBox(a,reg.w,reg.h),pr=reg.poiRef` sites), by cityMaxZ, and inside the pinned washMake. So the build must emit per-city bounds (world px bbox plus scale) in a committed JSON file, and cityBox/cityMaxZ must read it. The canon POIs (in DETAIL poiRef frames, 3914x4200 and 4245x3951, which differ from the overlay pixel sizes) must go through the same GCP transform, or the pins drift off the warped art. Making cityBox read the override keeps washMake's source hash but changes the wash bounds it returns. Treat that as a change in behaviour that the Mobile UG3 lane must accept, and land it only when the atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) is not holding maps-site/index.html. (3) The chart pyramids under charts/epeshu and charts/summarch do NOT need re-cutting. enterChart is a modal view in the chart's own pixel frame (map.unproject at the chart's maxz, the base removed), so it never overlays the atlas. (4) The empty corners can be filled with parchment in the JPG; washMake's radial wash already hides the seam.
votes.reason: The offline GCP-warp idea transfers. It is registration done at build time, it does not touch determinism, and the art is bent to the atlas. But the applies_to_us text gets four things wrong. (a) It leans on gdal_translate/gdalwarp, but `which` finds no GDAL here, only /usr/bin/convert. (b) It says nothing in the runtime changes. In fact cityBox (maps-site/index.html) sets the bounds in ensureCityOverlay, the canon POI reprojection (reg.poiRef), cityMaxZ and the hash-pinned washMake, so registered bounds and a POI transform must be wired into the file the Mobile atlas lane is editing. (c) It says the chart pyramids must be re-cut. enterChart shows them in their own unprojected pixel frame with the base removed, so they never align to the atlas. (d) It implies coverage of city overlays in general, but the procedural genCityCanvas plans are not pre-drawn art and cannot be warped offline.

items.summary: Whatever replaces cityBox must be one record read by every placement consumer (overlay bounds, POIs, wash, cityMaxZ, fly targets); cityMaxZ repeats the box maths itself, and washMake must get geometry through reg/a fields.

prior_record.confidence: high on the code; the claim that washMake's body is in the pin set comes from the task brief, not checked here
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Yes. Introduce a per-city registration record {gcps, type, params} and a forward/inverse pair. The 2-3 cityBox consumers call the forward transform. The pinned functions keep their signatures.

evidence.quote: var ll=px(box.x0+(p.x/pr.w)*box.fw, box.y0+(p.y/pr.h)*box.fh);
var box=cityBox(a,reg.w,reg.h),f=1.7;
// real charts (canon) — Epēshu's 19 POIs reproject through the footprint transform.
`transformer.transformToGeo()` to transform geometries from 'resource' space to 'geo' space, and `transformer.transformToResource()` to transform from 'geo' space to 'resource' space.

votes.corrected:
Code facts verified at HEAD (maps-site/index.html). The cited quotes are exact, and the @allmaps/transform README (v1.0.0-beta.53) does name transformToGeo/transformToResource as the two directions, but it only shows that such an API exists. Verified:
- cityBox(a,w,h) is a centred aspect-fit square of half-size footR(kind) around the anchor.
- worldPOICoord and buildWorldPOIs both map POI pixels through box.x0/y0/fw/fh, which is the same mapping used for the overlay bounds.
- washMake calls cityBox(a,reg.w,reg.h) and builds its rectangle from a.atlasX/atlasY plus box.hw/hh times 1.7.
- buildCityStubs draws reg.stubs as world-px segments with no box mapping, and only for prov==='invented'. Canon charts have no stubs.
- washMake is in the UG3 atlas_fn_sha pin set (tools/mobile-capture.js lists xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask).

Corrections:
1. There are four cityBox call sites, not "2-3": worldPOICoord, buildWorldPOIs, washMake and ensureCityOverlay (the overlay bounds). footR is also used independently in cityMaxZ, the nearest-city test, and genCityCanvas / sampleCityMask.
2. The stubs are not independent of the box. genCityCanvas (also pinned) bakes them in world px as a.atlasX + (gate - S/2)/scl and a.atlasX + cos(ang)*footR*1.18, so they implicitly assume the identity footprint (centred on the anchor, radius footR). A non-identity registration for an invented city would move the art and POIs but not the stubs, and the stubs cannot be edited without changing the pinned genCityCanvas hash. The claim's "do not (derive from cityBox)" is literally true but understates this coupling. The practical answer is that procedural cities stay identity-registered, because their raster is generated inside that box, and only canon charts (Epēshu, Summarch) get a non-identity registration.
3. "Wash and bounds use the transformed quad" overreaches. L.imageOverlay and washMake take an axis-aligned LatLngBounds, so a Helmert rotation or general affine cannot be shown as a quad without pre-warping the raster, or a plugin or canvas layer.
4. "Changed geometry should reach washMake through reg/a fields" is workable only because washMake's geometry comes from the unpinned cityBox(a,reg.w,reg.h). Its signature and call pattern must therefore be preserved.
votes.reason: The code quotes are exact and the single-transform design logic is sound. But the claim says 2-3 cityBox consumers where HEAD has 4 call sites. It omits that the pinned genCityCanvas bakes stub coordinates from the anchor and footR, so stubs assume identity registration. It also implies a transformed quad can be used for bounds, which Leaflet's axis-aligned imageOverlay and washMake's latLngBounds cannot do without pre-warping the raster. The Allmaps quote shows only that forward and inverse methods exist, not that this design is required.

votes.corrected: Yes, but only for the canon art, and the plan needs four fixes. (1) Scope: fit GCP registration (Helmert or affine, from DM-chart px, i.e. reg.poiRef/DETAIL space, to world px) only for the canon overlays Epēshu and Summarch. Invented plans are already registered by construction. sampleCityMask reads the land/water mask from a footR square around the anchor. genCityCanvas emits reg.stubs in world px with the same frame inline (scl=S/(2*footR), a.atlasX+(g-S/2)/scl). Both functions are hash-pinned. So for invented plans the transform must stay exactly cityBox (the identity case). Otherwise the plan, its stubs and its mask come apart, and fixing that would mean editing pinned code. (2) Consumers: the full list is the overlay bounds in ensureCityOverlay, worldPOICoord, buildWorldPOIs, washMake, cityMaxZ (deepest-zoom scale) and arguably nearestCity's radius. That is more than "2-3". POIs and any vector city vertices use the forward transform. (3) The raster: L.imageOverlay only takes axis-aligned latLngBounds, so it cannot apply a rotated or sheared inverse. Either pre-warp the static canon JPG offline with the same parameters and place it by the warped quad's AABB (preferred: no new runtime code, no per-frame cost, and the art bends to the atlas), or write a small custom CSS-matrix overlay layer (no plugin/framework). Leave chart mode (enterChart) in its own image space. (4) The pins are by source hash, so pinned bodies cannot change at all; keeping their signatures is not enough. cityBox itself is not pinned. washMake only builds an AABB radial wash centred on a.atlasX/atlasY with hw/hh from cityBox(a,reg.w,reg.h). So feed it a derived anchor/reg (centroid, AABB-matching w/h), or make cityBox registration-aware for canon keys. Do not edit washMake. The wash needs only the quad's centroid and AABB, not the quad itself. Registration is what fixes the drift. A vector city placed through the old cityBox would drift exactly as the raster does.
votes.reason: The core point holds. At HEAD, maps-site/index.html sends the overlay bounds (ensureCityOverlay), the POIs (worldPOICoord, buildWorldPOIs: px(box.x0+(p.x/pr.w)*box.fw,...)) and the wash (washMake: var box=cityBox(a,reg.w,reg.h)) through cityBox. One shared forward transform is the right fix for POIs drifting off the art, and it is a registration fix, not a medium fix. Four details in applies_to_us need correcting. (a) reg.stubs do not call cityBox, but genCityCanvas computes them with the same footR frame inline (var scl=S/(2*footR(a.kind)) ... a.atlasX+(gg.x-S/2)/scl), and sampleCityMask samples tiles in that same frame. Both are UG3-pinned (docs/mobile/README.md: diff touches none of xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask; cityCanvasSha unchanged). So invented plans must keep the identity/cityBox mapping, and GCP registration only makes sense for the canon art (Epēshu, Summarch), which has no stubs anyway. (b) There are more cityBox consumers than "2-3": cityMaxZ and the overlay bounds also depend on the box scale. (c) L.imageOverlay is axis-aligned, so the raster cannot simply be given the inverse. It needs an offline pre-warp (fits no-build, adds no per-frame cost, bends the art to the atlas, not the atlas to the art) or a small custom CSS-transform overlay. (d) "Pinned functions keep their signatures" understates the pin: it hashes the whole body. washMake can only follow through its inputs (a.atlasX/Y, a.kind, reg.w/h) or through the unpinned cityBox it calls. Its output is an axis-aligned radial blob, so it can only take the transformed quad's centroid and AABB. The evidence quotes are accurate (buildWorldPOIs, washMake, and the 'real charts (canon)' comment in meshedWorldInit).

items.summary: A vector city transforms vertex by vertex through the same registration, so it aligns only as well as that registration; vectors add crispness and shared vertices, but traced-roads.json is not loaded by the atlas.

prior_record.claim: REGISTRATION versus MEDIUM for the 'vectorized city' idea. Vector geometry is transformed vertex by vertex, using the same GCP transform as the raster; Allmaps adds midpoints so lines stay smooth under non-linear transforms. A vector city therefore aligns only as well as its registration. What vectors add is crispness past the stretched bitmap (cityMaxZ caps zoom at native resolution) and road vertices shared with the atlas road graph, which can then meet with no seam. They do nothing for a placement error. L.svgOverlay in 1.9.4 inherits ImageOverlay's axis-aligned bounds, but an inner <g transform> can carry an affine, the same nesting as in R8.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Yes. Do registration first and render the vector city through that registration, so its road vertices snap to traced-roads at the gates. The filigree slice C 'city' owns the look, with R4 (no block labels) and R7 (nothing at rest).

evidence.quote: For lineStrings and polygons the transform options can be used to **refine** the geometry during transformation as needed, i.e. add extra midpoints to assure sufficiently smooth results.
export var SVGOverlay = ImageOverlay.extend({ _initImage: function () { var el = this._image = this._url;
// native resolution sets the city's own deepest zoom (1 image px ≈ 1 screen px).

votes.corrected: All three quotes exist and support the core claim, but two sub-claims have no cited evidence and one is slightly overstated. Supported: (1) Allmaps transform README, "For lineStrings and polygons the transform options can be used to **refine** the geometry during transformation as needed, i.e. add extra midpoints to assure sufficiently smooth results." The same README says Allmaps renders maps with a GCP Transformer, so vector features and the raster can share one transform. Refinement is opt-in: maxDepth defaults to 0, so midpoints are added only when options are set, and the README does not say "non-linear" in that sentence. (2) Leaflet 1.9.4 SVGOverlay is ImageOverlay.extend(...) and sets this._image = this._url. ImageOverlay._reset sizes and positions the element from the NW/SE corners of this._bounds, so an SVG overlay is placed as an axis-aligned box. (3) maps-site/index.html cityMaxZ carries the comment "native resolution sets the city's own deepest zoom (1 image px ≈ 1 screen px)". The code is Math.min(Z_STREET, NZ+log2(mx/(2*r))), so the zoom cap at native resolution is confirmed. Narrowest supportable claim: vector geometry run through the same GCP transform is registered exactly as well as the raster (placement error is untouched), and a vector layer would lift the cityMaxZ resolution cap. Not supported by the cited evidence: (a) that an inner <g transform> carries an affine inside an L.svgOverlay (standard SVG behaviour, but none of the three quotes show it, and R8 is not in the HEAD export, so the 'same nesting as R8' link is unverified); (b) that vector road vertices shared with the atlas road graph 'meet with no seam' (a design inference, not evidence). maps-site/data/traced-roads.json exists at HEAD, but maps-site/index.html does not load it.
votes.reason: The Allmaps midpoint quote, the SVGOverlay source and the cityMaxZ comment are all real, and the registration-vs-medium argument stands on them. The claim overreaches in its tail: the <g transform> affine and 'same nesting as R8' are uncited and R8 is not checkable at HEAD, and 'no seam' with the traced-roads graph is inference, since the atlas does not yet load that file. Allmaps midpoint refinement is also opt-in (maxDepth defaults to 0).

votes.corrected:
Partly. The registration-versus-medium split is correct for us, so register first. A vector city placed through cityBox (maps-site/index.html, function cityBox: anchor-centred, FOOT_R-sized, aspect-fit) misaligns exactly as the raster does. Vectors only bring crispness past cityMaxZ, interactivity, and road vertices that can be shared.

The road-snapping part does not hold as written. maps-site/data/traced-roads.json is not loaded by maps-site/index.html. The density bible (blazed_paths, B-16) and the research dossier both say its 46 chains are "mostly lettering and islets", lie off the printed dotted road, and "cannot feed it before the Traced road network item". Today the only road geometry at a city's edge is the invented buildCityStubs segments. So gate vertices must snap to a road graph re-traced from the print dots (the POLISH "Traced road network" item), not to the current traced-roads.json.

Scope:
(1) The canon cities, Epēshu and Summarch, keep the DM art (overlay-*.jpg and the chart pyramids) as the canon image. The fix there is a GCP or affine fit of that art to the atlas coast, rivers and roads. That fit bends the art, never the atlas. A vector layer over them would be a traced, registered companion, not a replacement.
(2) For procedural cities, genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask are pinned by source hash (UG3 atlas_fn_sha / cityCanvasSha) while the Mobile 5-9 atlas lane is in flight. A vector city has to be a new seeded function placed beside them. Their sources stay untouched until the owner re-pins.
(3) The SVG DOM costs too much for full building fabric on the mobile per-frame budget. Prefer L.canvas, or an svgOverlay with a few aggregated paths. In 1.9.4 L.svgOverlay inherits ImageOverlay's axis-aligned bounds, so any rotation or shear has to go in an inner <g transform>.
(4) The look belongs to the filigree slice C 'city' (painted city, pooled edges), under R4 (never label blocks) and R7 (nothing at rest; halos on hover only). The zoom-through into the 3D street view belongs to the living track (H2z), and Epēshu streets and buildings to the street track.
votes.reason:
The technical claim checks out against the HEAD export. cityBox places every overlay by anchor and footprint with no feature registration. The cityMaxZ comment confirms that native resolution caps the zoom. Vector geometry moved through the same transform inherits the same error, while Allmaps-style refinement only keeps lines smooth.

The weak point is applies_to_us. It tells the city's road vertices to snap to traced-roads.json at the gates. That file is not loaded by maps-site/index.html; grep finds no consumer. docs/filigree/density-bible.md and research-dossier.md also record that its chains lie off the printed road and must wait for the Traced road network item, so following the advice as written would fix the seam onto wrong geometry.

applies_to_us also leaves out several constraints. The DM art stays canon and is fitted to the atlas, not swapped for vectors. The pinned genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask must stay untouched during Mobile 5-9. The mobile per-frame budget rules out a heavy SVG. Ownership splits between filigree slice C and the living H2z zoom-through.

The direction is right: register first, then render vectors through that registration. So the claim holds with a corrected application.

items.summary: Art px and CRS.Simple world px both run y down, so fits need no axis flip; LatLng and north-up GDAL frames must stay out of the fit.

prior_record.claim: Axis handedness. Pixel art (y down) against geographic space (y up) needs an axis flip for coupled transforms such as Helmert. Our art px and CRS.Simple atlas world px both run y-down, so a Helmert fit from art px to atlas world px needs no flip. Mixing in Leaflet lat/lng (y up) or a GDAL north-up geotransform would bring the flip back.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Yes. Fit in world px (y down) and convert to LatLng only through px(). For a gdalwarp pre-warp, check the sign of the output's y axis (open question).

evidence.quote: For some transformations, like the Helmert transformation, the transformation of x- and y- coordinates are computed jointly (they are said to be 'coupled') and the difference matters.
function px(x,y){return map.unproject([x,y],NZ);}

votes.corrected: Claim stands as stated. Narrowest form: a Helmert fit between two y-down pixel planes (art px and atlas world px) needs no flip. The flip only matters when one side is y-up, such as Leaflet lat/lng or a north-up GDAL geotransform.
votes.reason: Source 1: I fetched the @allmaps/transform 1.0.0-beta.53 tarball. Its README Handedness section has the quote nearly verbatim: "For some transformations, like the Helmert transformation, the transformation of x- and y- coordinates are computed jointly (they are said to be 'coupled') and the difference matters." The same section says typical pixel coordinates with the origin at top-left are left-handed (y down) and that equirectangular (lon, lat) is right-handed (y up). It also says differentHandedness should be true when the two spaces differ, e.g. image pixels against lon/lat. So the claim's first half is supported. Source 2: maps-site/index.html in the HEAD export has `function px(x,y){return map.unproject([x,y],NZ);}` under `L.map('map',{crs:L.CRS.Simple,...})`, with `NZ=4`. The y-down convention for atlas world px is supported by the code. `contentBounds=L.latLngBounds(px(0,0),px(IMG_W,IMG_H))` puts the origin at the top-left, and the off-frame clamp marks `y<0` as 'N' and `y>IMG_H` as 'S'. cityBox builds `y0=atlasY-hh` and `y1=atlasY+hh`, and the image overlay bounds come from px(), so art px and atlas px share one orientation. The claim's recommendation to fit in world px and go through px() is consistent with the code. Two limits. First, the repo doesn't show the DM art px convention directly. The y-down reading rests on image pixels being top-origin, which is standard. Second, the GDAL part is not evidenced by either source, but the claim marks it as an open question and a check, so it does not overreach.

votes.corrected: Yes, with one more source of y-up coordinates to watch. Fit Helmert (or affine) control points from art px to atlas world px, where both axes run y-down. Atlas world px are what city-anchors.json atlasX/atlasY and cityBox() use. Convert the result to LatLng only through px(x,y)=map.unproject([x,y],NZ). Under CRS.Simple that gives lat=-y/16 and lng=x/16, so it is a flip plus a scale and must never enter the fit. Two inputs bring y-up back, and each must be converted to y-down before fitting. (1) Control points taken from the wiki's Leaflet world map, whose markers use lat = pixels from the BOTTOM edge: use y = 2188 - lat. (2) A GDAL north-up geotransform from a gdalwarp pre-warp: check the sign of its y axis (open question). A Helmert fit across mixed handedness does not fail loudly. A similarity transform cannot represent a reflection, so the fit returns a plausible-looking rotation with large residuals. An affine fit absorbs the flip as a negative determinant. Either way, assert that the fitted determinant is positive and the residuals are small. This is only the sign convention for the registration step. It fixes nothing by itself and applies the same way to raster or vector city layers. Run the fit offline in a tool, or once at load as a pure function of fixed control points. Never run it per frame, and leave the pinned genCityCanvas/sampleCityMask/washMake unchanged.
votes.reason: Checked against the HEAD export. maps-site/index.html builds the map with crs:L.CRS.Simple and defines `function px(x,y){return map.unproject([x,y],NZ);}`. cityBox(a,w,h) works directly on a.atlasX/a.atlasY in image px, y-down, and city-anchors.json stores y-down atlas px (Epēshu atlasY 1415 of 2188). Art images are y-down too. So a Helmert fit from art px to atlas world px has matching handedness and needs no flip, which makes the claim correct. The allmaps point is also right: only coupled transforms such as Helmert are sensitive to handedness. The claim's applies_to_us leaves out the most likely real-world trap. The project's own canon note (CLAUDE.md) says the wiki Leaflet markers put lat in pixels from the BOTTOM edge. If those markers are reused as ground control points, they are y-up and need y = 2188 - lat first. The corrected text adds this, a determinant/residual check, and that px() also scales by 1/16 (it is not a pure flip). It also says this is registration bookkeeping, separate from the raster-vs-vector choice. Acting on it is correct, carries little risk, and conflicts with none of the determinism, mobile-pin or track constraints, as long as the fit runs offline or once at load.

items.summary: Generated plans are registered to the coast by construction: the sampleCityMask frame and the cityBox frame agree exactly; GCP registration is needed only for the canon overlays.

prior_record.claim: Procedural city plans are partly registered by construction. sampleCityMask reads the land/water mask from the z5 tiles around the anchor, and genCityCanvas draws onto it. GCP georeferencing is therefore mainly needed for the two DM-drawn canon overlays (Epēshu and Summarch) and their chart pyramids. One thing to check: the mask is sampled over ±1.35·footR, while the plan is placed through cityBox at ±footR.
prior_record.confidence: medium (the mapping from mask to canvas inside genCityCanvas was not traced)
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Yes. Scope GCP registration to the canon art. For procedural plans, verify once that the mask frame and the cityBox frame agree, without touching the pinned genCityCanvas or sampleCityMask.

evidence.quote: var ox=Math.round((a.atlasX-1.35*rW)*2),oy=Math.round((a.atlasY-1.35*rW)*2), n=Math.round(5.4*rW);
registerCityOverlay('Summarch','art/overlay-Summarch.jpg',{prov:'canon',w:3072,h:2859,

votes.corrected:
Both quotes exist in maps-site/index.html at HEAD, and the claim holds with these limits.

Procedural plans are registered to the atlas coastline only. This applies when the city is a harbour or its sea distance is 25 px or less (`drawWater`), and the sampled patch holds at least 2.5% water (`mask.water`). Otherwise `genCityCanvas` uses only the mask's land hue and bearing. Rivers (`traits.river`) and roads (`buildCityStubs`) are not registered to the atlas by this mechanism, so I make no claim about them.

The frame check the claim flags is already answered in the code. `sampleCityMask` covers ±1.35·footR atlas px, which is n = 5.4·footR z5 px. `genCityCanvas` then cuts the central 4·footR z5 px, which is ±footR atlas px. The call is `g4.drawImage(mcv,(a.atlasX-rW)*2-MK.ox,(a.atlasY-rW)*2-MK.oy,4*rW,4*rW,0,0,512,512)`. The generator canvas is square (`GEN_SIZE` 2048, returned as w=h=S). `cityBox` makes a square ±footR box for a square image. So the mask frame and the cityBox frame agree, and the extra 0.35·footR is padding. The one offset is `cx -= sv.x*S*0.07` for harbours. That shifts the drawn land centre, not the mask sampling.

The canon claim is also right: Epēshu and Summarch are registered with `prov:'canon'` and image files, and they go through the same `cityBox`. I did not trace the chart pyramids (`enterChart`), so that part rests on the project guide only.
votes.reason: Quote 1 is at `sampleCityMask` (ox/oy/n with 1.35 and 5.4). Quote 2 is the `registerCityOverlay('Summarch','art/overlay-Summarch.jpg',{prov:'canon',w:3072,h:2859,` line. Tracing `genCityCanvas` shows the mask is cropped to the central ±footR and is drawn through a square canvas into `cityBox`, so the open check resolves in the claim's favour. The claim overreaches slightly in implying general registration. The mask drives only the coast, only when drawWater is true and at least 2.5% of the patch is water, and at z5 resolution (2 px per atlas px, blurred and thresholded). The claim is also hedged on exactly the point I traced, so I mark it as holding.

votes.corrected: Yes, with the open check now resolved. In the HEAD export of maps-site/index.html, the mask frame and the cityBox frame already agree. sampleCityMask samples an n=5.4·rW px z5 patch starting at (atlasX−1.35·rW)·2. genCityCanvas (the MK branch) then crops exactly the central 4·rW z5 px, which is 2·rW world px, with g4.drawImage(mcv,(a.atlasX-rW)*2-MK.ox,(a.atlasY-rW)*2-MK.oy,4*rW,4*rW,0,0,512,512). That is the same square as cityBox(a,S,S) (hw=hh=footR) for the square GEN_SIZE canvas. The extra 0.35·rW is only margin, and the Math.round on ox/oy cancels out because the crop uses the unrounded anchor minus the rounded origin. So the one-time check is a measurement with no code change, and the pinned genCityCanvas and sampleCityMask stay untouched. Scope GCP or affine registration to the two canon overlays: registerCityOverlay('Epēshu',…) and ('Summarch',…), their POI reprojection, and the charts/epeshu and charts/summarch pyramids used by enterChart. Do it through new registration data (control points to a transform that replaces cityBox for prov:'canon'), bending the art to the atlas. For procedural plans the registration is only partial, and the job description should say so. (1) The coast is atlas-registered only when drawWater && mask.water. Otherwise the synthetic compass shoreline is used, and ensureCityGenNow shows a plan with no mask until the melded one hot-swaps in. (2) Roads are matched by bearing only: cityApproaches takes the angles where atlas road polylines cross a circle of 2.5·footR, so the roads are not shared vertices. (3) traits.river draws a synthetic watercourse that is not sampled from the atlas river. A vector re-render of these plans through the same cityBox would keep exactly this registration. It would add crispness, not alignment.
votes.reason: I checked the claim's open question in the code, and it holds. sampleCityMask uses ox=round((atlasX−1.35rW)·2) and n=5.4rW. genCityCanvas crops source rect ((atlasX−rW)·2−ox, …, 4rW, 4rW), which is the ±rW world-px square, the same as cityBox for a square S×S canvas (hw=hh=footR(kind)). So for procedural plans the coast is registered by construction, and the GCP effort belongs with the DM-drawn canon overlays placed by cityBox (overlay-Epeshu.jpg 2863x3072, overlay-Summarch.jpg 3072x2859) and their chart pyramids. That fits the rules that the atlas is authoritative and that the pinned hashes stay unchanged: canon registration can be new data plus a bounds transform for prov:'canon'. The claim overstates one thing: "registered by construction" covers only the water mask, and only for coastal or harbor cities. Roads match by bearing only (cityApproaches), rivers are synthetic, and the deep-link fallback starts with no mask. Its other parts are correct. Severity is minor because the recommendation's direction is right and needs no pinned-code change.

votes.corrected: Claim holds as stated. Static, offline measurement (browser_run false) of the water class of overlay-Epeshu.jpg placed via cityBox (capital FOOT_R 26, centre 1236.1,1415) against the print-tile coast mask and the DEM 0 m contour. Chart-to-print: rms 8.48, p95 16.89, max 21.05 atlas px, mean vec (4.34,4.39) SE. Print-to-chart in box: rms 14.93, max 33.62. Chart-to-DEM: rms 6.88, max 18.84. Screen px (atlas px x 2^(z-4)): 83.5 at z7.3, 501 at z9.885, 1535 at z11.5. Caveats to carry: 'SE' is the direction of the nearest-point mean vector in atlas coordinates (y down), not a verified chart shift; the print-to-chart figures are box-limited and not comparable across box sizes; the chart-coast extraction is a colour-class heuristic.
votes.reason: Checked against out/three-coasts-epeshu.json (dm_art_placements.today_cityBox): art_to_print rms 8.48/p50 6.62/p95 16.89/max 21.05, print_to_art_in_box rms 14.93/max 33.62, art_to_dem rms 6.88/max 18.84, mean_vec dx 4.34 dy 4.39 SE, screen-px 83.5/501/1535 all match, and the screen-px factors equal 2^(z-4). The verdicts block calls the DM chart the outlier, with DEM-to-print at 1.33 rms and print vs DEM within 1.3-1.5 rms. Repo quotes verified in head/maps-site/index.html: function cityBox(a,w,h){var r=footR(a.kind),mx=Math.max(w,h); is at line 1894; var FOOT_R={capital:26,town:14,village:9,ruin:8}; is at line 834; registerCityOverlay('Epēshu','art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg',{prov:'canon',w:2863,h:3072, is at line 3083. city-anchors.json has Epēshu as capital at atlasX 1236.1, atlasY 1415, matching the method's centre and box. The applies_to_us line (a vector city through the same cityBox carries the same error) is restated in the file's key_distinction.

votes.corrected:
This is a registration error, not a rendering-medium one. The atlas print mask and the DEM shore agree with each other to about 1.3-1.5 atlas px rms. Under today's cityBox (capital FOOT_R 26, which puts the 2863x3072 chart in the box [1211.9,1389]-[1260.3,1441]), the DM chart's coast is 8.5 px rms off and sits SE. It also lays about 666 px2 of land over atlas sea and never puts sea over land.

Any city layer whose coast comes from the chart carries the same 8.5 px rms error if it is placed through the same cityBox. That covers a raster image, a vectorization traced from overlay-Epeshu.jpg, and POIs reprojected through the footprint. A vector or procedural plan whose coast comes from the atlas mask (sampleCityMask/buildCityMask) does not carry it. So the cure is to fit the chart to the atlas through a per-city registration, with the atlas fixed and the art moved. A medium change does not cure it.

Fitting on the coast alone cannot set the scale. The free fit is multimodal and lands on the edge of the search range (s=0.5, about +10 px south). The registration therefore needs control points such as the road, river and harbor ties on the atlas, not just a coast chamfer.

Screen figures: 84 px at z7.3 and 501 px at z9.885 (Epēshu's cityMaxZ, the deepest the atlas zoom reaches today) are real. The 1535 px at z11.5 only applies if the H2z zoom-through takes Epēshu past cityMaxZ, or at the sim street handoff.
votes.reason:
All the figures check out against out/three-coasts-epeshu.json under dm_art_placements.today_cityBox: art_to_print 8.48/6.62/16.89/21.05, print_to_art_in_box 14.93/33.62, art_to_dem 6.88/18.84, mean vector (4.34,4.39) SE. The screen factors 2^(z-4) are 9.849, 59.077 and 181.02, which give 83.5, 501 and 1535.

The code matches the claim. In maps-site/index.html, cityBox does hw=r*w/mx and hh=r*h/mx around a.atlasX/atlasY. FOOT_R capital is 26. The Epēshu anchor is (1236.1,1415,capital). registerCityOverlay('Epēshu', w:2863, h:3072) is there. cityMaxZ gives 4+log2(3072/52)=9.885.

"Outlier" is justified: dem_vs_print mainland is about 1.3-1.5 px rms, against the chart's 8.5. The main conclusion holds: this is registration, and the medium does not change it. Fixing it by moving the art to the atlas is correct for the project, since atlas geography is authoritative.

Three refinements:
(1) "A vector city carries the same error" is true only for a vector traced from or keyed to the DM chart. A vector or procedural plan built from the atlas mask is aligned by construction.
(2) z11.5 is not reachable at Epēshu in the atlas today, because setMaxZoom is capped at cityMaxZ 9.885. That figure matters only for H2z, the zoom-through and street handoff.
(3) Coast chamfer alone cannot pick the registration. The free fit sits on the search edge and is multimodal, so the fix needs atlas control points.

Other caveats: the measurement is static (a PIL JPEG decode and a colour-class water mask, not a browser run). Registering the chart also changes poiRef reprojection. A per-city transform record need not touch the pinned genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask, but it must not edit those functions, or it breaks the mobile track's source-hash pins.

votes.corrected: Holds, with scope limits. B-38's "DEM shore runs up to 10 atlas px off" came from q08-c08, which scanned atlas y = 1389+cy/4200*52. That is the today's-cityBox frame (capital FOOT_R 26, box y 1389-1441). So it measured the DEM against the DM chart as cityBox places it. q08-c08 itself blamed the DEM and rated its confidence medium; the later three-coasts-epeshu.json run overturns that. Within about 60 atlas px of Epēshu, the DEM coast sits 1.3-1.5 atlas px rms from the atlas print-mask coast (p95 2.3-2.7, mainland max 5.4). The chart sits 8.5 px rms from the print, and 6.9 px rms from the DEM, under today's cityBox. At the best policy fit (0.6x, +3E), the registered chart is still 3.6 px rms from the print and from the DEM. It errs both ways: land over atlas sea 91 px2, sea over atlas land 75 px2. Clipping to the print mask lines up with the DEM to about 1.4 px. Caveats: (a) that 1.4 px is DEM-coast-to-print-coast distance near Epēshu. It is not a measured result of clipping contours. (b) It uses the raw DEM, not the genHydrology-carved W.H. (c) The window-wide DEM-to-print rms of 8.4 is an islet-merge artefact, and there is a 20 px headland simplification 339 px away. (d) The art-fit numbers use overlay-Epeshu.jpg, while q08-c08 used the Q1 mosaic (4200 chart px tall).
votes.reason: All four quotes exist in the cited sources. q08-c08 has the 1.0/0.8 vs 3.8/7.0/10.3/10.4 px figures and the scan ref. B-38 has the clip-to-chart-coast text, and its density-bible row says "up to 10 atlas px off". three-coasts-epeshu.json has today_cityBox vs_dem mean_vec dx 2.5, dy 3.52, bearing 144.6 SE. The numbers match the file's own b38 verdict. The 3.57-3.58 rms, the 91/75 px2 seam and the DEM-to-print rms of 1.33-1.5 (r60 mainland 1.36) all check out. The attribution to today's cityBox follows from 1389+cy/4200*52 matching the cityBox [1389,1441] and FOOT_R capital 26. The claim's wording is nearly the file's verdict text, so it needed only the scope limits above, not a rewrite.

votes.corrected: B-38's clip reference should be the atlas print mask (buildCityMask/sampleCityMask water class), not the DM chart's own coast. The DEM shore (EPESHU_HF_URI raw decode) agrees with the print to about 1.33-1.5 atlas px rms, so the two can be treated as one coast with no reconciliation shift. This is a REGISTRATION fix to the reference, not a medium change: vector or raster contours clipped to a cityBox-placed or translate+scale-registered chart still sit 3.6 px rms (0.6x+3E) to 6.9 px rms (today) off the atlas coast. Condition: a print-mask clip is only right if slice C also makes the painted chart obey the print coast. Its land over atlas sea gets clipped, and its sea over atlas land (75 px2 at 0.6x+3E) is made transparent or filled with atlas sea, as seam_both_signs says. If the chart keeps its own coast on screen, print-clipped contour hair falls on painted chart water, and DEM-clipped relief gets cut where the chart's land runs out over sea. In that interim case, clip contours to the intersection of print-mask land and chart land. Filigree owns this: write it up as a proposed amendment to B-38 in the slice C spec (with the q08-c08 reading reclassified as chart-vs-DEM under cityBox), not as an atlas-lane edit. The 0.6x+3E fit is an exploratory policy point that nobody has adopted. The DEM is the raw decode without genHydrology carving.
votes.reason: The numbers check out against the sources. q08-c08 scanned along atlas y = 1389+cy/4200*52, which is the cityBox span 1389-1441 at 80.77 chart px per atlas px. So it measured the DEM against the chart as placed by today's cityBox, not against the atlas. three-coasts-epeshu.json gives DEM-to-print at 1.33 rms over the window and 1.36-1.51 within 60 px. At 0.6x+3E it gives art_to_dem 3.57 rms and print seams of 91/75 px2 (both signs). Today's art_to_dem mean_vec is 2.5/3.52 at 144.6 deg, matching the quoted evidence. The claim fits the stack because the atlas is authoritative and registration bends art to the atlas. It is also cheap: the print mask is already built deterministically by buildCityMask/sampleCityMask, so no new pinned function changes and there is no per-frame cost beyond a clip path. The gap in applies_to_us is that it leaves out what is visibly underneath. B-38 clipped to the chart so relief would not cross painted water. Switching to the print mask is correct only when the chart's own sea/land is also brought to the print coast. Otherwise contours land on painted sea, which breaks filigree's look. This belongs to the filigree track (slice C), so the recommendation is a proposed amendment to the bible, not a direct edit.

summaries.3-vector: The patch check compared the numpy port with itself, and its figures are close to but neither equal to nor independent of the dossier's.

Coast chamfer rms 9.3, max ~20 ... Policy placements score chamfer 3.7-3.9 at 0.6-0.7× and 6.35 at 1.0×

votes.corrected: The quoted sentences exist, and the file's figures are near the dossier's but do not equal them. Verified: out/three-coasts-epeshu.json method.patch_check says the numpy port on sampleCityMask's exact Epeshu patch agrees with the window mask on 99.79% of pixels with a 0.0 px coast offset. Today's cityBox gives art_to_print rms 8.48 and max 21.05 (dossier: coast chamfer rms 9.3, max ~20). The 0.6x, +3E placement gives rms 3.58 (dossier: 3.7-3.9 at 0.6-0.7x). Corrections: (1) patch_check compares the numpy port with itself on two windows. It does not run the real browser sampleCityMask/buildCityMask (the file notes PIL JPEG decode, not the browser's). It shows the patch crop does not change the mask. It does not show the port equals the code. (2) The figures are close but not equal, and were not derived independently of the dossier's method. 8.48 against 9.3 is about 9% lower. 3.58 sits just below the dossier's 3.7-3.9 range. The dossier's 1.0x figure is a refit placement and the file's 8.48 is the unshifted cityBox, so the two are different quantities. (3) The 3.58 is the best policy fit (0.6x, +3E) and is the only 0.6x placement scoring that low. The 0.6x, +8E placement scores 4.82. (4) Chamfer direction matters: only art_to_print is comparable across placements, and this file reports that direction. Supportable claim: the file's numbers corroborate the dossier's ranking and rough magnitudes (today about 8.5-9 rms and 20-21 max; a 0.6x policy placement about 3.6-3.9 rms). They should be cited beside the dossier's with the method difference stated, not treated as interchangeable, and the file's own values should be used where the file's placements are meant.
votes.reason: Both quotes are present (the dossier quote splices lines 41 and 122). The overreach is in the framing: 'independently match' and 'without re-deriving' are too strong. 8.48/21.05 versus 9.3/~20 and 3.58 versus 3.7-3.9 are close but differ, and the dossier's 1.0x figure of 6.35 differs from the file's 7.21 and 5.88. patch_check shows only port-versus-port consistency across two windows, not agreement with the real JS code.

votes.corrected: Use the three-coasts-epeshu.json figures as their own baseline, and do not quote them next to the dossier's numbers as if the two came from one measurement. They agree only roughly: today's placement measures 8.48 rms here against the dossier's 9.3, and the 0.6x/+3E policy placement measures 3.58 here against the dossier's 3.7-3.9. That rough agreement corroborates the same conclusions: the DM chart, not the atlas, is the coast outlier; a translation plus uniform scale override chosen by policy beats today's cityBox; and a seam clip is needed. When a figure is quoted, name its direction and reference: art_to_print, one-sided, coast points within 40 art px of the frame dropped, PIL JPEG decode of the z5 tiles. The print_to_art direction (14.93 today) is not comparable across box sizes. The patch_check shows only that the numpy port is self-consistent between sampleCityMask's 140 px patch and the larger window. It is not a check against the browser's buildCityMask (static_only true, browser_run false). The P4 browser crossfade baseline in screen px is still the number to use for acceptance. All of this concerns REGISTRATION. The rendering medium plays no part in these figures: a vector Epēshu placed through the same cityBox would score the same 8.48.
votes.reason:
The claim's figures are copied correctly. In out/three-coasts-epeshu.json, dm_art_placements.today_cityBox.vs_print.art_to_print gives rms 8.48 and max 21.05, and scale0.6_E3 gives 3.58. method.patch_check gives the 99.79% / 0.0 px result. The dossier's (b) Registration section gives 9.3 / ~20 and "3.7-3.9 at 0.6-0.7x, 6.35 at 1.0x".

Three problems with saying the numbers can be used side by side without re-deriving:

1. "Checks out against the code" overstates the check. The file says static_only true and browser_run false. The 99.79% agreement compares the numpy port with itself: run on the sampleCityMask patch versus run on the bigger window. It does not compare the port with the browser's buildCityMask, which decodes JPEGs differently.

2. The two sources measure chamfer in ways that are not shown to be the same. This file uses one direction (art_to_print), its own colour classifier for the art's water, and drops points within 40 px of the frame. The dossier's "coast chamfer" does not state a direction or a reference. The direction matters a great deal: for the same placement, print_to_art_in_box is 14.93 while art_to_print is 8.48. So a match "within ~1 px" could be partly coincidence.

3. The policy comparison is not like for like. The dossier's 3.7-3.9 spans 0.6-0.7x with the centre at +3..+6 E. This file's 3.58 is a single placement (0.6x, +3E). The dossier's 6.35 at 1.0x is never re-checked here.

The figures support the same direction and roughly the same size of error, which is enough to corroborate the conclusions. They are not interchangeable baselines. Acceptance for any per-city override inside cityBox should come from one consistent run, preferably the P4 browser crossfade measured in screen px. This is a minor issue: no wrong code change follows from it, only possible mixing of numbers in docs or gates. It is about REGISTRATION; the raster-versus-vector choice does not change these figures.

items.summary: Realm polygons sit a median 3.5-5.4 px from the printed wash edge, showing the vector medium registers well when traced against a clear edge.

summaries.2-registration: Realm polygons sit a median 3.5-5.4 px from the printed wash edge, showing the vector medium registers well when traced against a clear edge.
summaries.3-vector: Hand-traced realm rings sit a median 3.5-5.4 atlas px from the printed wash edge for six realms, showing that the vector medium registers well when traced against a clear printed edge.

prior_record.claim: Realm borders are the best-registered layer. The print draws realms only as colour washes, with no border line. The polygon ring's distance to the printed wash edge has a median of 3.5-5.4 px for Cyrikon, Sārmathi, Alensic, Wall, Eastern Patrin and Pheropic (p90 10.8-22.5, max 20.9-59.9; IoU 0.57-0.85). Umbadic (median 8.5, p90 32.2) and Regimen (median 9.9, p90 62.1) are low-confidence measurements. The print's green tint spreads across Emphēros beyond the polygon, and Regimen is printed as hatching that a colour classifier misses.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: This shows the KEY DISTINCTION in reverse. The same vector medium registers to within a few px when it was traced against an unambiguous printed edge, which shows that the medium does not cause drift. Realms do not feed APPR_POLYS. At z7.3 the median is still 34-53 screen px, so wash fills visibly overshoot coasts. Realms are drawn on raw rings with no spline.

evidence.quote: Kgd. of Cyrikon (3.5, 11.1, 20.9) IoU 0.697; Alensic (3.5, 16.5, 52.4) IoU 0.805; Kgd. under the Wall (3.6, 17.9, 35.6) IoU 0.848; Umbadic (8.5, 32.2, 60.0) confidence low
ring.map(function(c){return px(c[0],c[1]);}) ... L.polygon(latlngs,{color:col,weight:1.5,opacity:.7,fillColor:col,fillOpacity:.22,pane:'pRealm'})

votes.corrected: Verified numbers: the print draws realms only as colour washes with no border line. For the realm rings (L.polygon on raw rings via px(), no spline, pane pRealm, fillOpacity .22, not in APPR_POLYS), distance to the nearest edge of the printed wash has median 3.5-5.4 atlas px (Cyrikon 3.5, Sārmathi 3.5, Alensic 3.5, Wall 3.6, Pheropic 3.5, Eastern Patrin 5.4). p90 is 10.8-22.5 and max 20.9-59.9. IoU of polygon against the print tint is 0.57-0.85 (Pheropic 0.57, Sārmathi 0.60, Cyrikon 0.70, Eastern Patrin 0.70, Alensic 0.81, Wall 0.85). Umbadic (8.5, 32.2) and Regimen (9.9, 62.1) are marked low confidence, because the green tint spreads across Emphēros beyond the polygon and Regimen is printed as hatching the colour classifier misses. At z7.3 the six medians are 34.5-53.2 screen px. Narrowest supported claim: for six realms the traced rings sit within a median of about 3.5-5 atlas px of the classifier-defined wash edge, with fit that is only moderate (IoU 0.57-0.85, max up to 60 px). Drop three overreaches. (1) 'Best-registered layer' is not shown: Umbadic (8.5) and Regimen (9.9) are no better than Lamor (7.5) and party-route leg 6 (7.9), and the six good realms are compared against a soft, classifier-defined edge, not a drawn line. (2) 'Unambiguous printed edge' contradicts the source's own caveats: Alensic's wash is close to sea colour, Eastern Patrin's coast edges rely on luminance, and Pheropic's interior is 60% water-coloured. Cyrikon's polygon is only 76% on print tint. (3) 'Shows the medium does not cause drift' is an inference the data does not test: there is no raster comparison, and the source's own key_distinction says vector geometry mis-registered at the source misaligns exactly as a raster would. The identical 3.5 median across four realms may be a measurement floor from the r=4 blur, which the source does not state. The source supports only that these realm rings were traced closely enough to the washes.
votes.reason: All numbers and both code facts check out against out/vector-overlays-vs-print.json and maps-site/index.html (buildRealms, buildApprPolys). The interpretive framing overreaches: 'best-registered layer', 'unambiguous printed edge' and 'medium does not cause drift' are not supported, and the source's per-realm caveats and its key_distinction cut against them.

votes.corrected: Mostly right, with one clause that the data does not support. As evidence, the claim shows the KEY DISTINCTION from the other side. Hand-traced vector rings in the same L.CRS.Simple px() frame land a median of about 3.5-5.4 world px from an unambiguous printed edge. So the vector medium does not cause drift, and the city misalignment comes from REGISTRATION (cityBox/FOOT_R placement). A vector city plan placed through cityBox would drift just as the raster does. Checks against maps-site/index.html: buildRealms maps raw ring coordinates through px() with no crSpline, so raw and spline stats are identical. APPR_POLYS is built only from the route, named ways and sea lanes, never from realms. The screen-px arithmetic is right: 3.5-5.4 x 2^(7.3-4) is about 34-53 screen px at z7.3. Caveats: (1) The metric is the unsigned distance to the edge of the classified colour wash. It is not a signed overshoot and not a distance to the coast, so the claim that wash fills visibly overshoot coasts is unsupported. Drop it or measure signed sea-side overlap. (2) Six realms share an identical 3.5 px median, which looks like a measurement floor from the r=4 z5-px blur and opening, so 'within a few px' is resolution-limited. (3) Registration at realm scale does not show registration at city scale: 3.5 px is 13-40% of FOOT_R (9-26). (4) The pRealm pane is hidden at map-tier-d (Z_TIER_D=7.5) and in chart-mode, so realms overlap the city fade only between z6.8 and 7.5. Acting on this claim means no work on realms. Use it only as the argument that city fixes belong to registration, done by bending art to the atlas. Any future retrace of the realm rings is low priority, and the Emphēros tint and the Regimen hatching need a better measurement before anyone retraces against them.
votes.reason: Checked against the HEAD export and out/vector-overlays-vs-print.json. buildRealms maps raw rings through px() with no spline. Every realm row has feeds_APPR_POLYS:false and identical raw and spline stats, and buildApprPolys takes only the route, ways and lanes. The z7.3 screen-px figures check out arithmetically, and realms are still visible there because Z_TIER_D is 7.5. The 'overshoot coasts' clause is unsupported: the method measures the unsigned distance from each ring sample to the edge of the classified wash, not a signed overlap onto sea. The applies_to_us text also leaves out context that limits relevance. pRealm is hidden at tier D and in chart mode. The repeated 3.5 px median is probably a measurement floor. Realm-scale accuracy does not carry over to the city footprint scale. Its core inference, that the medium is not the cause and registration is, still transfers and fits the project's constraints, so the claim holds with these corrections.

items.summary: A bible edit does re-open the Filigree 1 gate, but the rest (registration numbers in city_grain, a free POLISH-only route) did not hold.

summaries.2-registration: A bible edit does re-open the Filigree 1 gate, but the rest (registration numbers in city_grain, a free POLISH-only route) did not hold.
summaries.3-vector: A density-bible .json edit re-opens the Filigree 1 gate, but a .md-only edit does not, and a POLISH-only item is invisible to Job 2 and does not gate Job 3.
summaries.5-ownership: Refuted: a density-bible.json edit does break the Job 1 to Job 2 chain, but a POLISH-only item is not honoured by Job 2 (it never enters the spec, Job 3 gates only on roads, census and rivers) and a 'Filigree data —' title holds Street 3.

prior_record.claim: Any edit to docs/filigree/density-bible.{md,json} re-opens the Filigree 1 gate. That includes adding a 'Filigree data — city art registration' row to its prerequisites, or rewriting the city_grain registration numbers. The item can be queued without amending the bible: put it only in POLISH.md, above Filigree 3 per R21, and Job 2 honours it.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: This decides the sequencing. Amending the bible means a Filigree 1 re-integration before Filigree 2. Queuing the item in POLISH.md only costs nothing on the filigree gate.

evidence.quote: "id": "G1.1", "desc": "bible files exist + validator ok" ... "threshold": "ok && failures=[] && validator sha256 = integrator sha256 (64-hex) for both bible files"
When the gate already passed on a bible that re-hashes, a rerun returns `pass:true` without re-running
an item is skipped if POLISH.md already has "Filigree data — <item>"

votes.corrected: Verified: editing docs/filigree/density-bible.json breaks the Job 1 to Job 2 chain. Job 1 treats the gate as "already passed" only when the gate is pass and both bible files re-hash to the shas recorded in gates/1-research.json (md_ok/json_ok in filigree-1-research.js, README section 2 "When the gate already passed on a bible that re-hashes..."). Job 2 preflight compares sha256 of density-bible.json with the gate's artifacts entry (bible_sha_ok) and in full mode dies with "gates/1-research.json is not pass, or the bible changed since" (filigree-2-plan.js, G2.0). Job 1 rejects force, so the only route is a full Job 1 re-integration (delete the gate or resume:false). Adding a prerequisites row or rewriting city_grain numbers in the .json would therefore need that re-run. Two parts of the claim go beyond the evidence. (1) Only the .json sha is checked by Job 2. A .md-only edit makes Job 1 re-run (md_ok false) but does not trip Job 2's preflight, and mobile-build only checks that the gate exists and passes, not that it re-hashes. (2) "Job 2 honours it" is unsupported. The cited line (design/workflow-2-plan.md, filigree-2-plan.js prereq_unqueued) only dedups entries of the spec's /prerequisites, which come from the bible's prerequisites, against POLISH.md titles, so as not to insert duplicates. A POLISH-only "Filigree data — city art registration" item that is not in the bible or spec /prerequisites is simply ignored by Job 2: it is not read into the spec and is not checked as a prerequisite. Job 3 blocks only on the "Traced road network" and "Census second pass" titles (R11), and an unchecked "Filigree data —" item only affects Job 3 check-off. Narrowest supported claim: a .json bible edit forces a full Filigree 1 re-run before Job 2 can run (a .md edit re-opens only Job 1's own re-hash test). A POLISH.md-only item above Filigree 3 (R21) costs nothing on the gate, but it will not feed the sheet spec or block Job 3 unless it is also in the bible prerequisites or its title is added to Job 3's prerequisite check.
votes.reason: The gate and re-hash evidence is real and supports the first half (the .json case), but "any edit to .md or .json" overstates it because Job 2 checks only the .json sha. "Job 2 honours it" overreaches: the cited line is only a dedup of bible-derived prerequisites, and a POLISH-only item is ignored by Job 2 and does not gate Job 3.

votes.corrected:
Half right. The first half holds. Job 2's preflight compares the sha256 of density-bible.json with the hash recorded in gates/1-research.json "artifacts" (bible_sha_ok). Criterion G2.0, "preflight chain: Job 1 passed, bible unchanged", then fails, so any bible edit means a Filigree 1 re-run or re-integration before Filigree 2. That includes adding a prerequisites row. (city_grain holds no registration numbers today, only B-33..B-38 grain, park, arterial, fog and contour notes.) Mobile-build only checks that gate 1 exists and passes, not the bible hash, so the mobile lane is not held by a bible edit.

The second half is wrong. Job 2 does not "honour" a POLISH-only item. Its prereq_unqueued and polish_inserts logic only skips duplicates of entries already in the bible's /prerequisites. An item that exists only in POLISH.md is invisible to Job 2: it does not enter the sheet spec or any unit, and no slice depends on it. Job 3's prerequisite gate (R11) checks only "Traced road network", "Census second pass" and rivers.json. So a POLISH-only "Filigree data — city art registration" item does not stop slice C from painting the city through the unregistered cityBox placement. It is not free either. The street workflows' hold (ST15, HOLD_TASK in street-1..4) holds Street 3 while any line matching "- [ ] **Filigree data —" is open. That title prefix therefore blocks the street track until the item is checked.

Correct sequencing:
- If the goal is no gate churn, queue it in POLISH.md as a standalone atlas or registration item outside the "Filigree data —" prefix (unless holding Street 3 is intended). Place it before Filigree 3 slice C. Then hand it to Job 2 by an explicit note or ruling, or accept that slice C must be re-pointed afterwards.
- If slice C must be gated on registration, that needs a bible prerequisite, with Job 1 re-integration, or a Job 3 prereq change. Neither is free.
- Either way, registration (per-city control points against the atlas coast, rivers and roads) is the fix. Vector versus raster is not.
votes.reason:
Checked against the HEAD export.
- First half verified: filigree-2-plan.js sets bible_sha_ok from the bible hash recorded in gate 1's artifacts, and G2.0 fails when chainOk is false. The README confirms that a rerun returns pass:true only "on a bible that still re-hashes".
- Second half fails on the downstream consumers. filigree-2-plan.js line `prereq_unqueued` covers only the "item" of /prerequisites entries. polish_inserts only adds those entries, so Job 2 never reads an arbitrary POLISH item. filigree-3-build.js `missingPre` / `reqOk` gate only on roads, census and rivers, so a POLISH-only item does not gate slice C.
- The street workflows' HOLD_TASK greps every open "Filigree data —" line, and ST15 holds Street 3 while one is open. Queuing under that prefix therefore has a real cost on another track.
- So "costs nothing on the filigree gate" is true only in the narrow G1.1/G2.0 sense. The claim that "Job 2 honours it" is false, and the real effect is that registration is not enforced on slice C.

summaries.2-registration: Chart POIs, wash and fly targets are placed through cityBox, so an override on overlay bounds alone would split art from halos; the override must be one record read by all consumers.

prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Any override must live in one function that cityBox, cityMaxZ, buildWorldPOIs and worldPOICoord all read. Mobile A-U11 also requires the 'registerCityOverlay literal kept'.

votes.corrected: Both quotes exist verbatim. buildWorldPOIs and worldPOICoord both place POIs through cityBox(a,reg.w,reg.h), and ensureCityOverlay builds the imageOverlay bounds from the same cityBox. The POLISH.md "Epēshu roundel doubling" entry says the 19 POI coords were corrected to the printed badge centres and the live markers are invisible hover halos over the print. So a registration override applied only to the overlay bounds would move the printed badges and leave the halos behind. Two precisions on applies_to_us. (1) cityMaxZ does not call cityBox. This is about the rendering medium (raster or vector), not registration. Scale-aware level of detail (LOD) makes a vector city legible, but it does nothing for alignment. If the plan is still placed through cityBox, it misaligns exactly as the raster does.

What holds in maps-site/index.html: canvas px per atlas px is GEN_SIZE/(2*footR). GEN_SIZE is 2048 and FOOT_R is {capital:26,town:14,village:9,ruin:8}, which gives 39.4, 73.1, 113.8 and 128. Buildings are rr(5,11) canvas px (placeBld). Screen px per atlas px is 2^(z-NZ) with NZ=4. In the overlayOpacity band (z6.8 to 7.8), a town building is about 0.5 to 1 screen px at z6.8 and about 1 to 2 px at z7.8. Village and ruin buildings are smaller still. A capital building is about 1.8 to 3.9 px at z7.8. So per-feature vector geometry gets Douglas-Peucker simplification at smoothFactor:1, and 1px strokes swamp sub-2px footprints. The raster just downsamples. The current fade band is about 1 to 2 px per building, so a raster hand-off (or no building geometry at all) below about z8 is right.

Hundreds of buildings should not be separate L.polygon objects, given the mobile per-frame budget. They belong in one seeded canvas draw (or a single renderer) with screen-space LOD: blocks or a fill below about z8, footprints above. The pinned genCityCanvas raster can be the low-zoom LOD, so its cityCanvasSha and atlas_fn_sha pins stay untouched. Any new vector path must take its seed from xmur3/mulberry32 the same way.

None of this applies to the DM-drawn canon plans for Epeshu and Summarch. Those stay raster unless they are traced.
