It will also catch the numeral badges, the legend box and the compass, which must be masked. Expect blocks or approximate footprints, not 1:1 houses.

(3) Tracing is not registration. Traced coordinates are image px. They line up with the atlas only after a GCP fit that bends the art to atlas features (coast, river, roads). Fed through cityBox(a,w,h), whose box size comes from FOOT_R[kind], vector footprints misalign exactly as the raster does now. Hand-traced skeleton lines double as GCP and seam evidence, but the fix is the warp, not the medium.

(4) Runtime fit. Around 17k polygons as Leaflet SVG/canvas layers would break the mobile per-frame budget. Under R4 (never label blocks) and R7 (nothing at rest) they add almost nothing interactive. The building grain should stay raster (the DM art warped, or tiles rendered from the vectors). Vectors should be limited to the skeleton plus a few hover features.

Tracing must be an offline tools/ step (like tools/build-gazetteer.js) emitting static JSON: no runtime tracing, no build, and nothing touching the pinned genCityCanvas/sampleCityMask hashes. Slice C "city" belongs to the filigree track and the Epēshu streets/buildings to the street track, so the traced data should feed both rather than fork them. The 10 s per footprint figure is an unsourced estimate, as the claim itself says.
votes.corrected: Partly. Effort split is right: do not hand-digitize every building. Hand-trace only the skeleton: coast, river, walls and gates, main roads, districts and fields (tens to low hundreds of features). Use those lines as the GCP/seam evidence for a warp that bends the art to the atlas, since tracing alone does not register anything. Before any tracing, ask the DM whether the Watabou city-generator links/seeds or GeoJSON exports for Epēshu and Sun's March still exist (both maps look like Watabou output); if so, take vectors from there. Otherwise auto-trace (Potrace / colour quantization) gives block-level or approximate footprints, not 1:1 houses: the JPEGs and thin shared-wall outlines merge houses, and the badges, legend and compass must be masked. Run it as an offline tools/ step that emits static JSON. Keep the building grain raster (warped art or tiles rendered from the vectors) to stay within the mobile budget and R4/R7. Vectors are for the skeleton and a few hover features. Coordinate with filigree slice C and the street track.

items.summary: Leaflet clips and simplifies every path on each renderer update (moveend/zoomend, not every frame), SVG makes one element per path while Canvas uses one canvas, so ~17k separate SVG polygons is not phone-safe.

prior_record.claim: Leaflet re-clips and Douglas-Peucker-simplifies every Polyline/Polygon on each update. The default SVG renderer gives each path its own DOM element. The Canvas renderer draws all paths into one <canvas> and batches redraws. About 17k L.Polygon footprints in SVG is not phone-safe.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Yes, within the mobile per-frame budget. Options: (a) a dedicated L.canvas() renderer for pane pCity, with footprints shown only past cityMaxZ-1. (b) Use vectors as the registration substrate only: warp in atlas px, then rasterize offline to a per-city atlas-frame tile pyramid like charts/epeshu. Vectors give alignment, raster gives delivery, and interactive hit-testing runs on a small vector subset (roads, districts, POIs). Precedent: buildCityStubs already draws L.polyline in atlas px (px(s.x0,s.y0)) into pCity with no cityBox.

evidence.quote: How much to simplify the polyline on each zoom level. More means better performance and smoother look, and less means more accurate representation.
Allows vector layers to be displayed with <canvas>. Inherits Renderer.

votes.corrected: Verified against Leaflet v1.9.4 source (not the two quoted lines): Polyline._update runs _clipPoints (LineUtil.clipSegment against the renderer bounds; Polygon uses PolyUtil.clipPolygon) and _simplifyPoints (LineUtil.simplify at smoothFactor) on every update. The renderer calls _update on moveend/viewreset/zoomend. The `noClip` option skips clipping. The SVG renderer's _initPath creates one path element per layer inside a shared <g>. The Canvas renderer draws every layer into one <canvas> and coalesces redraws through _requestRedraw/requestAnimFrame. Clipping and simplification happen in Polyline/Polygon before the renderer, so L.canvas() saves DOM nodes, not that per-update geometry work. The two cited quotes support only: smoothFactor ("How much to simplify the polyline on each zoom level...") and "Allows vector layers to be displayed with <canvas>... Inherits Renderer" (the source has markdown link syntax and backticks around those words). The "~17k L.Polygon footprints is not phone-safe" figure and verdict have no source. The only repo count found is ~13,669 building fills in Epēshu chart quarter Q1 (docs/filigree/research/q08.json), and no phone benchmark exists. Treat it as an unmeasured engineering estimate to be measured on the Mobile capture profiles. The precedent holds: buildCityStubs in maps-site/index.html draws L.polyline([px(s.x0,s.y0),px(s.x1,s.y1)]) into pane pCity without cityBox. Those are line stubs, not polygon footprints, so it shows atlas-px placement only, not polygon scale.
votes.reason: The Leaflet mechanics (re-clip and Douglas-Peucker on each update, one SVG path element per layer, one canvas with rAF-batched redraw) are correct per the v1.9.4 source, and the quotes exist. The quotes alone don't establish the DOM-per-path or batching claims, though. The "17k polygons not phone-safe" conclusion is unsupported: no 17k figure or benchmark appears in the repo (nearest is 13,669 fills in Epēshu Q1). The claim also omits that Canvas does not avoid the clip/simplify cost.

votes.corrected:
Partly. The Leaflet facts are right. In v1.9.4, Polyline._update clips the points to the renderer bounds and Douglas-Peucker simplifies them (smoothFactor) on every renderer update. That happens on moveend/zoomend, not every frame. During a pinch the pane is CSS-transformed. The atlas sets no preferCanvas and no renderer (see `L.map('map',{crs:L.CRS.Simple`), so every vector it draws today, the buildCityStubs polylines included, is an SVG path. The "17k footprints" figure has no source. Only one city is ever live (CITYVIEW holds one overlay plus its stubs), so the real count is one city's buildings.

The recommendation, corrected:

(a) Draw building footprints through a dedicated L.canvas({pane:'pCity'}) renderer, shown only past about cityMaxZ-1, with interactive:false. Leaflet's Canvas renderer hit-tests by looping over every layer on each mousemove, and it redraws the whole padded viewport on each update. So footprints stay non-interactive, and hover/click goes to a small separate set: roads, districts and POIs. Hover halos only and no block labels, per filigree R7 and R4.

(b) Is the more correct path. Do the registration in atlas px: warp the DM art, the vectors and the stubs to atlas features such as coast, river, gate and road. Then deliver raster, like charts/epeshu. Vectors give the alignment, raster gives the delivery.

Limits on (b):
- Canon DM art (overlay-Epeshu, overlay-Summarch) is bent to the atlas by the warp, never redrawn as vectors.
- Procedural cities stay runtime genCityCanvas output. An offline bake would replace a function pinned by the mobile track (UG3 atlas_fn_sha, cityCanvasSha) while Mobile 5-9 is mid-flight. Any change to the generator or its placement has to wait for that lane or go through it.

The cited precedent needs a correction. buildCityStubs does draw L.polyline in atlas px into pCity without calling cityBox. But each stub's inner end comes from the gate's canvas position scaled back by scl=S/(2*footR(kind)), which is the same anchor-centred footR box as cityBox. So the stubs inherit the cityBox registration error. They are a precedent for the medium (atlas-px vectors), not for registration.
votes.reason:
The Leaflet mechanics hold for v1.9.4: clipping and simplifying run per update, SVG makes one DOM element per path, Canvas draws to one batched canvas. The atlas uses the default SVG renderer: L.map has no preferCanvas or renderer option. The main recommendation is the right fit for this project: register in atlas px and deliver raster, with a small vector set for interaction. It keeps the line between registration and medium, and it respects mobile cost. Three corrections are needed:
1. Leaflet's Canvas renderer is not free for interaction. Its hover hit-test loops over all layers on every mousemove, so footprints must be interactive:false. This also matches R7 (hover halos only) and R4 (never label blocks).
2. The "17k" count is unsourced. Only one city is live at a time.
3. The precedent is misread. The buildCityStubs inner endpoints are mapped through scl=S/(2*footR(kind)), the same box as cityBox. So the stubs show atlas-px vector drawing, not independent registration, and they misalign the same way the overlay does.

Constraints the claim leaves out:
- Canon DM art is warped to the atlas, never replaced.
- Procedural cities can't be baked offline or have genCityCanvas changed while the mobile pins (atlas_fn_sha, cityCanvasSha) and the Mobile 5-9 lane hold.

items.summary: Traced-chart byte estimates reproduced only within ~10% for Epēshu and not for Summarch; superseded by G0-19 and G7-3.

prior_record.claim: Measured lower bound on file size: Epēshu's 17,323 building blobs as axis-aligned rectangles weigh 2.14 MB as GeoJSON (233 KB gzipped). As a delta-encoded integer array they weigh 172 KB (52 KB gzipped). Summarch's 3,769 weigh 473 KB / 55 KB gz as GeoJSON and 45 KB / 16 KB gz as delta ints. For comparison, overlay-Epeshu.jpg is 2.17 MB and the charts/epeshu pyramid is 6.6 MB. TopoJSON's shared arcs and quantized delta encoding cut GeoJSON by about 80% and store each shared road vertex once.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Yes. Real traced outlines would run about 1.5-3x the rectangle bound (estimate). A quantized, delta-encoded atlas-px city of a few hundred KB still undercuts the raster and pyramid. With no build step, use a hand-rolled flat int array with an inline decoder rather than the topojson-client library.

evidence.source: maps-site/art/overlay-*.jpg (measured: bbox per blob, json.dumps + gzip)
evidence.quote: Epeshu 17323 delta-int bytes 172059 gz 51862 | geojson bytes 2143168 gz 232978
TopoJSON is substantially more compact than GeoJSON, frequently offering a reduction of 80% or more even without simplification.
geometries in TopoJSON files are stitched together from shared line segments called *arcs*.

votes.corrected: Measured lower bound (bounding rectangles per building blob, my re-run of the method reproduces it within about 10%): Epeshu's roughly 17k blobs weigh about 2.1-2.4 MB as GeoJSON (about 230 KB gzipped). As a delta-encoded integer array they weigh about 170 KB (about 51 KB gzipped). Summarch's figures are of the same shape but unreproduced. For comparison, overlay-Epeshu.jpg is 2.17 MB (2,171,695 bytes, confirmed) and the charts/epeshu pyramid is 5.9 MB (5,904,620 bytes across 370 files), not 6.6 MB; 6.6 MB is the disk-block figure from du -s. The TopoJSON README says TopoJSON is "frequently" 80% or more smaller than GeoJSON even without simplification, and that geometries are stitched from shared arcs. That is the library's general claim. It was not measured on our data, and the rectangle figures above are not TopoJSON output.
votes.reason: Both TopoJSON quotes are verbatim in the README at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/topojson/topojson/master/README.md. They read "substantially more compact than GeoJSON, frequently offering a reduction of 80% or more even without simplification" and "stitched together from shared line segments called arcs". overlay-Epeshu.jpg is 2,171,695 bytes (2.17 MB, matches). Two points overreach. (1) The charts/epeshu pyramid totals 5,904,620 bytes over 370 jpg files, so 6.6 MB is wrong; du -s reports 6664 KB because it counts disk blocks. charts/summarch is 3,163,046 bytes. (2) The blob counts and the per-blob method are undocumented anywhere in the repo (no "17323" or "3769" in docs or tools), so they are not checkable from the repo. I could only re-derive them roughly. Connected components of tan building-colour pixels in overlay-Epeshu.jpg gave about 17.0k blobs, 2.37 MB / 231 KB gzipped as GeoJSON, and 168 KB / 50.6 KB gzipped as delta ints. That agrees with the claim in order of magnitude and ratio, so the Epeshu numbers are plausible. The Summarch numbers were not reproduced. The "about 80% cut" is TopoJSON's own marketing figure and says "frequently". It was not measured here, and the claim's "store each shared road vertex once" is an inference from the arcs description rather than something the README quote states.

votes.corrected: Partly, and only as a payload footnote. Download size is not what limits a vector city, and it does nothing for alignment. (1) REGISTRATION vs MEDIUM: these numbers say a vector layer would be small. They say nothing about whether it lines up. Encoded in "atlas px" through today's cityBox(a,w,h) (anchor plus FOOT_R scaled to the image aspect), a vector Epēshu misaligns exactly as the JPG does. The coordinates must first come from a fitted warp of overlay pixels to atlas features (coast, rivers, roads), which bends the art to the atlas. (2) The real cost on mobile is drawing, not bytes. 17,323 Leaflet polygons (SVG or a Canvas renderer) are redrawn on every zoom and pan. That needs a measured per-frame budget, plus culling, a zoom gate or merged batched paths, before anyone calls it cheap. (3) The comparison is skewed. The 370-tile charts/epeshu pyramid is 6.6 MB on disk (5.9 MB in raw bytes), but Leaflet fetches only the tiles in view, so its per-view cost is far below that. (4) TopoJSON's "about 80%" and shared arcs apply to adjacent polygons and road networks, not to separate building rectangles (each sits alone, so there are no shared arcs). Keep shared vertices for the road/edge graph, which the filigree slice C "pooled edges" work already owns, and treat buildings as plain delta-int rectangles or rings. (5) "Blobs" are connected components of the raster. They include glyphs, hatching and wall fragments, so they need cleaning and a check against the DM art (the art is canon) before they count as buildings. The 1.5-3x outline multiplier is an unverified estimate. (6) A hand-rolled inline int-array decoder is the right fit for one file with no build. The data is static, so determinism and the xmur3/genCityCanvas/sampleCityMask/cityCanvasSha pins are untouched, as long as the procedural path is not replaced inside the mobile lane while Mobile 5-9 are running. City rendering belongs to filigree slice C (rulings R4 and R7 apply).
votes.reason: The measured file sizes check out. overlay-Epeshu.jpg is 2,171,695 bytes, and the charts/epeshu pyramid is 6.6 MB by du -sh (5.9 MB in raw bytes, 370 tiles). So "a few hundred KB of vector undercuts the raster" is roughly true for bytes. But applies_to_us draws the wrong conclusion for this project in four ways. First, it treats download size as the deciding factor. The owner's problem is anchoring (registration), and a vector city put in place through cityBox shifts exactly as the raster does; only a fitted overlay-to-atlas warp fixes that. Second, it ignores the mobile cost of drawing about 17k Leaflet polygons on every frame. Third, it compares against the whole pyramid, but tiles load only for the current view. Fourth, it carries TopoJSON's shared-arc savings over to separate building rectangles, which share no arcs; the saving applies only to the road/edge graph. The inline-decoder and no-library advice is sound. Static data does not threaten determinism or the source-hash pins, but the work belongs to filigree slice C, not the mobile lane that is mid-flight.

items.summary: The procedural-city literature was seen only via search summaries, and coast-conditioned generation in the base frame already exists in sampleCityMask/genCityCanvas.

prior_record.claim: Classic procedural city pipelines produce vectors directly in the base map's frame, conditioned on its land/water image. Parish and Müller grow streets from input image maps (land-water boundary, density). Chen et al. 2008 design a tensor field from a water map so streets follow the shore. Watabou's MFCG builds seeded Voronoi wards, walls, gates and streets.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Yes, for the invented cities. Emit roads, wards and footprints as atlas-px arrays from the sampled mask and approach bearings, then rasterize or draw. Registration comes by construction. MEDIUM: vectors add crispness and a shared road graph. Fidelity to DM art does not apply, because these cities have no canon map.

evidence.quote: From various image maps given as input, such as land-water boundaries and population density, the system generates a system of highways and streets
The pipeline begins with topographical water and park maps ... users design a tensor field that is then used to generate a road network.
Voronoi.build( points ) ... voronoi = Voronoi.relax( voronoi, toRelax ) ... Random.reset( seed )
implement the queue, not the grammar — and the image maps condition growth, they don't replicate exact street plans.

votes.corrected: Parish & Müller (SIGGRAPH 2001) take image maps such as land-water boundaries and population density as input and generate highways and streets (seen only via a search-engine summary; history.siggraph.org was blocked on direct fetch). Chen et al. (SIGGRAPH 2008) start from topographical water and park maps, and the user designs a tensor field that generates the road network (search summary only; the oregonstate PDF was blocked). The sources do not say the tensor field is derived from the water map or that streets follow the shore. Watabou's TownGeneratorOS Model.hx builds seeded Voronoi patches with relaxation, wards, a curtain wall with gates and streets (confirmed in raw source). It takes no land/water image and has no coast or river flag; its only environment flags are random booleans (plazaNeeded, citadelNeeded, wallsNeeded). Our repo's docs/research/town-generation.md confirms that the image maps "condition growth, they don't replicate exact street plans." That doc also says its Watabou-internals claims did not survive verification, and it flags the Parish-Müller L-system as functionally a priority-queue growth. The pipelines produce street networks conditioned on constraint maps. That registration against a given base map is "by construction" holds only if our own code samples the atlas mask into the generator, which is our design and not something the sources show.
votes.reason: Sources 1 and 2 (history.siggraph.org, oregonstate PDF) were unreachable on direct fetch (egress blocked). The wording of their quotes appears only in WebSearch summaries. Beyond that, the claim overreaches in three places. (a) "Tensor field from a water map so streets follow the shore" is not in the quote, which says only that the pipeline begins with water and park maps and the user designs the tensor field. (b) The umbrella "conditioned on its land/water image" does not apply to Watabou's MFCG: Model.hx has no image or water input, only random flags and seeded Voronoi. (c) "Vectors directly in the base map's frame" is the project's inference, not something the sources state. Verified: the Model.hx lines (Voronoi.build, Voronoi.relax, Random.reset(seed) guarded by seed>0, walls, gates, streets) and the town-generation.md quote (it reads "implement the queue, not the grammar — and the image maps condition growth, they don't replicate exact street plans.").

votes.corrected: Partly, and mostly already built. The literature summary is accurate: Parish & Müller condition growth on image maps, Chen/Esch/Wonka/Müller/Zhang 2008 design tensor fields from water maps, and Watabou's MFCG uses seeded, relaxed Voronoi. But for our invented cities, the "registration by construction" this claim proposes already exists in maps-site/index.html. sampleCityMask reads the z5 tiles around the anchor (atlas px x2). buildCityMask keeps only border-connected sea and returns its bearing. genCityCanvas maps that mask into the 2048 canvas with the same square footprint cityBox uses (drawImage from (atlasX-rW)*2-MK.ox, scl=S/(2*footR)), takes land approaches from APPR_POLYS through cityApproaches, and buildCityStubs draws its stubs in ATLAS coords. An invented plan is square, so its cityBox equals its footprint exactly. Emitting the same geometry as atlas-px vectors would therefore not add registration. Any remaining invented-city misfit comes from three sources: mask fidelity (2 z5 px per atlas px, sea only), rivers not being in the mask (the 'riverine watercourse' backlog note in genCityCanvas), and approaches being bearings rather than shared road vertices. These are REGISTRATION-input gaps: richer conditioning maps (rivers and road polylines from the atlas) fix them in either medium. Vectors are a RENDERING-MEDIUM gain only: crisp past cityMaxZ, hit-testable, and a road graph that can share vertices with the atlas roads. Two limits on acting: (1) The owner's complaint is about the canon cities (Epēshu, Summarch: DM art placed by cityBox), and this method does not touch them. Those need art-to-atlas registration (control points), not generation. (2) Any change to genCityCanvas or sampleCityMask breaks the UG3 pins (atlas_fn_sha, cityCanvasSha) while the mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) is mid-flight, and it overlaps filigree slice C (the painted city) and R4/R7. So defer it to a post-Mobile-9, filigree-coordinated unit that adds a separate seeded vector emitter beside the pinned canvas (same xmur3/mulberry32 seed, no clock), rather than rewriting the canvas.
votes.reason: The facts in the claim hold, but its applies_to_us treats something already implemented as if it were new. In the HEAD maps-site/index.html, genCityCanvas is already conditioned on the atlas: sampleCityMask/buildCityMask supply sea and bearing, cityApproaches/APPR_POLYS supply approach bearings, and the plan is drawn in the cityBox frame (scl=S/(2*footR)). buildCityStubs already emits atlas-px road stubs. "Registration comes by construction" is therefore already true for invented cities, and switching to vectors would only change the medium. The remaining invented-city gaps (low-resolution, sea-only mask; no rivers; approaches are bearings, not shared vertices) are registration-input problems. The claim also skips the owner's main misalignment case, the canon DM-art cities, which this method cannot fix. Acting now would also edit functions pinned by UG3 during the in-flight mobile atlas lane and overlap filigree slice C, so the recommendation has to be gated and additive, not a rewrite.

items.summary: The mobile UG3 pins and filigree slice C ownership of the four city functions are confirmed, so a runtime vector emitter must be a new sibling function on its own stream and wait for the atlas lane; offline tracing touches no pin.

prior_record.claim: Determinism and ownership constraints on a vector emitter (code/docs). The mobile track pins xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask by source hash (UG3), plus cityCanvasSha, while its atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) is mid-flight. Filigree slice C owns registerCityOverlay, genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask for the painted city with pooled edges.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Yes. A runtime vector generator must be a new sibling function seeded from its own xmur3(name+'|vec') stream, so the pinned functions and cityCanvasSha stay byte-identical. Otherwise it waits for the atlas lane and Filigree C. Offline tracing (committed JSON regenerated by a tools/ script, like build-gazetteer.js and pgd2lexicon.js) is deterministic for free and leaves the site free of any build step.

evidence.quote: | painted city, pooled edges | `registerCityOverlay`, seeded `genCityCanvas`, `washMake` (print-hue wash), `sampleCityMask` (land/water mask) | the four `function` names |
var seed=xmur3(name)(),R=mulberry32(seed);

votes.corrected: Both quotes exist verbatim. The README row (docs/filigree/README.md, section 7 "Reuse map", row "painted city, pooled edges") and the genCityCanvas line `var seed=xmur3(name)(),R=mulberry32(seed);` both match. The mobile pinning is confirmed. UG3 in docs/mobile/gates.md says "the diff touches none of xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask, and cityCanvasSha is equal to B0 and equal across all five profiles". tools/mobile-capture.js hashes those five functions into R.atlas_fn_sha and sets R.cityCanvasSha. POLISH.md has Mobile 4 checked and Mobile 5-9 unchecked, so the atlas lane is mid-flight. The README row says only that the city feature in the Filigree plan reuses those function names, and the table is headed "Reuse map (what already exists)". It does not assign them to slice C or give Filigree ownership, and the README never names slice C in that row. Narrowest supported claim: the Filigree track plans to reuse registerCityOverlay, genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask for its painted city with pooled edges, and slice C (city) gates G3.C1-C9 cover that city. The "owns" wording comes from the owner brief, not from this source. Two further nuances. cityCanvasSha is not currently equal across all profiles, because docs/mobile/README.md says desktop 1366x768@1 differs from the dpr>1 profiles. registerCityOverlay is named in the Filigree reuse row but is not among the five functions UG3 hashes. The "applies_to_us" recommendation (a sibling function with its own xmur3(name+'|vec') stream) is the researcher's inference, not something the sources state.
votes.reason: Quotes and the UG3 and cityCanvasSha pinning are verified. The claim overreaches on "Filigree slice C owns": the cited README row is a reuse map, not an ownership assignment. It also glosses over the fact that registerCityOverlay is not hash-pinned and that cityCanvasSha already differs on the 1x desktop profile.

votes.corrected: Mostly yes, with three corrections. (1) The pins are as stated. tools/mobile-capture.js hashes xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask (R.atlas_fn_sha) and cityCanvasSha. Gate UG3 in docs/mobile/gates.md requires that "the diff touches none of" them, that cityCanvasSha equals B0, and that the maps-site/index.html clock-token count stays at 1 narrow and 2 wide. So a runtime vector emitter must be a new sibling function on its own stream, for example xmur3(name+'|vec'). It must call none of the pinned functions and change none of them; if it needs the land/water mask, it either reads the result sampleCityMask already returns or uses its own reader. It must add no Math.random or Date tokens, and its output must not depend on DPR or viewport. Profile equality is already fragile: canvas text hinting at dpr 1 is a known split. (2) "Otherwise it waits" understates the hold. Any runtime emitter edits maps-site/index.html, which the atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) is changing mid-flight. Filigree slice C owns the painted city look and the pooled edges whatever the new function is called. So even a sibling waits for the lane to land and has to be scheduled as, or after, Filigree slice C. It must also follow R4 (no block labels) and R7 (nothing at rest). (3) Offline tracing in a tools/ script that writes committed JSON, the way build-gazetteer.js and pgd2lexicon.js work, is the cleanest route for the DM canon maps (Epeshu, Summarch). It is deterministic, needs no build step in the site, and leaves the pinned functions alone. But determinism and ownership do not settle alignment. Traced or generated vectors placed through cityBox (FOOT_R box centred on the anchor) misalign exactly as the raster does. The tool must bake registration into the JSON: control points fitted to atlas coast, rivers and roads, bending the art to the atlas. The JSON also needs a regenerate-don't-hand-edit rule.
votes.reason: I checked the evidence at HEAD and it is accurate. docs/filigree/README.md lists the slice C row word for word. genCityCanvas contains "var seed=xmur3(name)(),R=mulberry32(seed);". tools/mobile-capture.js pins those five functions by source hash and computes cityCanvasSha. UG3 forbids touching them and fixes the maps-site/index.html clock tokens at 1 narrow and 2 wide. So the core advice holds: put new vector code in a sibling function on its own stream, or emit it offline into committed JSON. Three gaps remain. Being a sibling function does not get around the hold, because maps-site/index.html is being changed by the atlas lane and Filigree slice C owns the city look and pooled edges. The claim leaves out the clock-token count, the DPR-independence requirement and R4/R7. And the claim is only about determinism and ownership. The registration step (fitting to atlas features rather than cityBox) is what actually fixes the misalignment, and the offline tool has to carry it.

items.summary: Tracing or chart-matched generation gives exact shapes, not placement, so it is not a registration precedent.

prior_record.claim: The Pompeii CGA work is the precedent for chart-matched generation: real 2D footprints fix the layout and rules extrude massing. Parcel subdivision (Vanegas 2012) does not guarantee buildable lots and needs a repair pass. Straight-skeleton roofs are a solved primitive.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Yes, across tracks. Traced, registered canon footprints and a road graph for Epēshu could become the shared input for the atlas city sheet and the sim's street view (the street track owns s.streets and Epēshu's {name:'Epēshīn Forum'} / {name:'Wood Quay'}). The living track's zoom-through (H2z) would then cross between apps on one geometry. Tracing settles the 'exact reproduction vs conditioning' question the town digest left open: footprints are reproduced exactly, and only massing and roofs are generated.

evidence.quote: demonstrated by **rebuilding Pompeii from its historical 2D plan** — the direct academic precedent for "generate a 3D settlement matching a known 2D chart"
**Refuted (0-3):** the claim that the parcel stage *guarantees* buildable lots
the virtual rebuilding of the archaeological site of Pompeii as a case in point

votes.corrected: The repo digest docs/research/town-generation.md says: (a) Müller et al. 2006 CGA shape grammars demonstrated by "rebuilding Pompeii from its historical 2D plan" (the digest's own gloss: real footprints constrain layout, probabilistic rules extrude massing); (b) the claim that Vanegas 2012 parcel subdivision "guarantees" buildable lots was refuted (0-3), and the digest recommends keeping a rejection/repair pass after subdivision; (c) the straight skeleton is a solved primitive for hip roofs (CGAL extrude_skeleton, a WASM wrapper exists; the digest calls it cheap in JS only for convex quads). The Pompeii work is a precedent for generating 3D massing on a known 2D plan, but the "2D plan fixes the layout" detail rests only on the digest, not on a source I could open. The SIGGRAPH page was blocked, and the ACM abstract found by search says only "virtual rebuilding of the archaeological site of Pompeii as a case in point", with no mention of footprints or a 2D plan. The repair pass is the digest's recommendation, not Vanegas's own finding. The applies_to_us sentence that tracing "settles" the exact-reproduction-vs-conditioning question overreaches: the digest lists that question as open (Open questions, "Exact reproduction of a known 2D chart ... vs. conditioning"). Footprint reproduction is a proposed design choice, not something the evidence settles.
votes.reason: The two repo quotes exist verbatim in docs/research/town-generation.md and support their sub-claims. The third source, history.siggraph.org/?p=113547, was unreachable (egress blocked). Its text matched only through a web search that returned the ACM abstract of Müller 2006, and that abstract does not mention a 2D plan or footprints. The sub-claim that footprints are fixed rests only on the digest's gloss. The claim that tracing settles the open question contradicts the digest's own open-questions section, which lists it as unresolved. The straight-skeleton and Vanegas-repair sub-claims hold, with the digest's caveats (the repair pass is a recommendation; skeleton roofs are cheap only for convex quads in JS).

votes.corrected: Partly, and only for the two cities that have DM charts (Epēshu, Summarch). The literature summary is accurate: CGA rebuilt Pompeii from its 2D plan, Vanegas 2012 parcels need a repair pass, and straight-skeleton roofs are a solved primitive (docs/research/town-generation.md). The cross-track promise does not follow from it. (1) Tracing gives exact shapes, not placement. Traced footprints and roads are aligned to the DM chart, not to the atlas. Dropped through cityBox(a,w,h) with FOOT_R, they misalign exactly as overlay-Epeshu.jpg does now. They line up only after a separate registration step: control points on coast, river and road ends, fitted to atlas pixels at z4, which bends the vector to the atlas and never the reverse. "Registered" in the claim names that step without supplying it. (2) "One geometry across apps" does not exist today. The sim's Epēshu is the heightfield realm EPESHU_HF on a gridX/gridZ frame, and its labels use dx/dz offsets (buildEpeshuMapData, {name:'Epēshīn Forum', dx:0, dz:-15}). Nothing maps that frame to atlas pixels. A shared footprint set would need its own sim-grid↔atlas transform, and the sim terrain/coast agreeing with it. That is H2z continuity work owned by the living track. (3) Putting traced footprints into s.streets/s.buildings is new sim data. That is a scope change for the street track, whose contract says no new sim state (SG1.12/SG2.9), and it would shift that track's sim fingerprint. It needs a ruling from the owner and the street track, not a research inference. (4) Tracing settles exact reproduction versus conditioning only by choosing it, and only for charted cities. Every other city stays procedural (genCityCanvas, whose source hash is pinned by mobile UG3). The open question about vectorizing the chart into a primary road graph and generating secondary streets is still open for those. (5) On the atlas, a traced vector sheet brings crispness past the stretched image, interaction and shared road vertices. It must also respect filigree slice C and rulings R4 and R7. Roofs and massing are sim-only and must fit the mobile per-frame budget. Use the precedent as a long-term input format: registered canon vectors for the two charted cities. It is not a fix for the shifting or an agreed shared geometry.
votes.reason: The research facts hold, but applies_to_us goes too far. It treats tracing as if it solved alignment and as if it gave one geometry across both apps. Tracing fixes shape, not registration: a traced city placed through cityBox shifts exactly as the raster does. The sim's Epēshu sits on its own heightfield grid (EPESHU_HF, gridX/gridZ, dx/dz labels), and no transform links that grid to atlas pixels. Feeding traced data into s.streets would also break the street track's "no new sim state" contract. And the precedent only covers the two DM-charted cities, so the open question in the town digest stays open for the procedural ones.

items.summary: Watabou's MFCG has had a GeoJSON export since devlog 0.7.3 (not final), and both canon charts look like MFCG output, so the DM should be asked for seeds or exports before any tracing; authorship is an inference.

prior_record.claim: Watabou's Medieval Fantasy City Generator can export its city as GeoJSON (since devlog 0.7.3), driven from the URL by export=png|svg|json on Arcana builds. The Summarch art has MFCG's look (scale bar, compass, towered wall, hatched fields, numbered-ward legend).
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Maybe. If the DM made Summarch (or Epēshu) in MFCG and still has the seed or permalink, the canon vectors already exist, exact with no tracing. They would only need the V4 warp into atlas px. MFCG authorship is my inference from the image and must be confirmed with the owner.

evidence.quote: Export to JSON (to GeoJSON to be exact) is added for those who want to tinker with data created by MFCG, instead of images.

votes.corrected: Watabou's Medieval Fantasy City Generator gained a GeoJSON export in devlog 0.7.3 ("Export to JSON (to GeoJSON to be exact) is added for those who want to tinker with data created by MFCG, instead of images"). The same devlog added a URL parameter "export" with values png, svg and json, which makes the generator export the map right after creating it. The developer called the export not final and was unsure about keeping GeoJSON. Whether the Summarch or Epēshu art was made in MFCG is not evidenced. It is an unverified visual inference with no cited source, and the repo does not settle it.
votes.reason: The watabou.itch.io devlog URL is egress-blocked, so I could not open it directly and the quote is not verified from the primary page. A WebSearch result for the devlog title reproduced its contents. That paraphrase supports the GeoJSON export in 0.7.3, the quoted sentence, and the export=png|svg|json parameter. The claim overreaches in three ways. (1) "On Arcana builds" has no support in the cited quote or the search paraphrase. The paraphrase mentions no Arcana builds, so that qualifier should be dropped. (2) The Summarch art having MFCG's look (scale bar, compass, towered wall, hatched fields, numbered-ward legend) has no source. The only repo mentions of MFCG, in docs/research/town-generation.md and docs/street/research-dossier.md (row V6), say nothing about Summarch. The first says "no verified claims on their internals survived". (3) The "canon vectors already exist" implication depends on that unconfirmed authorship, and the entry's own applies_to_us already says it must be confirmed with the owner. Confidence stays low.

votes.corrected:
Maybe. It is worth one question to the DM, but it is not a plan yet. Both canon city maps look like Watabou's MFCG. maps-site/art/overlay-Summarch.jpg ("Sun's March") has the framed legend with a 0/250/500 m scale bar, the numbered ward discs, the towered wall, hatched fields and the compass rose. overlay-Epeshu.jpg has the same legend box, numbered dark discs and building texture. If the owner confirms they were made in MFCG and still has the permalink (size + seed + options, see dossier V6 in docs/street/research-dossier.md), an offline GeoJSON export gives buildings, walls, roads, rivers and fields as vectors, with no tracing.

Caveats that must ride with it:
(1) Only the GeoJSON export is attested, and only by a blocked search snippet. The `export=png|svg|json` URL parameter on Arcana builds is unverified.
(2) A seed may not reproduce the same city in today's MFCG if the generator changed after the DM made the map. The DM may also have edited the image afterwards (custom names, colours). Any re-export must be overlaid on the canon jpg and checked before it counts as canon. The jpg stays the authority.
(3) This changes the rendering medium, not registration. The export is in MFCG's own local frame. Placing it through cityBox (FOOT_R box centred on the anchor) misaligns exactly as the raster does. It still needs the V4 control-point warp that bends the city to the PatrinorModern coast, rivers and roads (never the atlas to the city). Pooling with the atlas's own road vertices is a separate step.
(4) It must be a one-time tool output: a vendored data file, generated and not hand-edited, like gazetteer.json. MFCG never runs at runtime. That keeps the no-build rule and seeded determinism, and it leaves the pinned genCityCanvas/sampleCityMask/cityCanvasSha untouched.
(5) The look, rendering and per-frame cost of thousands of building polygons on mobile belong to filigree slice C and the mobile lane. Use a canvas renderer, simplify, and keep rulings R4 (no block labels) and R7 (nothing at rest). The street track could reuse the same Epēshu footprints.
(6) It applies only to the two DM cities. Procedural cities stay on genCityCanvas.
votes.reason: The visual evidence for MFCG authorship is strong. Summarch has MFCG's legend box with scale bar, numbered ward badges, towered wall, hatched field strips and compass. Epēshu has the same legend and badge style. The repo's own dossier (V6) records that Watabou links reproduce from size + seed. So "Maybe, confirm with the owner" is the right call, and it fits the stack as an offline, vendored, deterministic data import. Two things the claim understates. First, it is a medium change, not a registration fix: a vector city still needs the V4 warp to sit on the atlas and is no better aligned under cityBox. Second, getting the same city back from a seed depends on the MFCG version and on any edits the DM made afterwards, so the export must be checked against the canon jpg. The export URL parameter is unverified, and mobile and filigree ownership apply. I tightened applies_to_us with these points rather than rejecting it.

items.summary: Order the work: register the canon art first (fixes the shift in any medium), then trace, then a sibling vector emitter for invented cities after the mobile lane closes; the original effort and byte figures are superseded by G0-19 and G7-3.

prior_record.claim: Synthesis: comparison of approaches by fidelity to DM art, effort, determinism and size. (1) Raster as-is through cityBox: full fidelity, zero effort, deterministic, 2.2 MB; misregistered (V2/V3). (2) The same raster registered by GCP/TPS, warped offline into an atlas-frame pyramid: full fidelity, hours of GCP picking, deterministic, size unchanged. This fixes the anchoring with no vectorizing. (3) Auto-traced plus hand-traced primaries, warped per vertex: near-full fidelity for footprints, about a day per city of tooling and cleanup, deterministic (committed), about 0.2-0.6 MB raw. This adds interactivity, crisp zoom and a shared road graph. (4) Procedural vectors in the base frame: no fidelity to canon art (fine for invented cities), registered by construction, seeded, tiny.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Yes. Recommended order: GCP registration of the canon art first (it removes the shift whatever the medium), then trace (3) for Epēshu and Summarch, then a vector sibling emitter (4) for invented cities after the mobile atlas lane closes.

evidence.quote:
"path": "charts/epeshu",
  "w": 3914,
  "h": 4200,
  "maxz": 3,
*Exact* reproduction of a known 2D chart (vectorize the chart into a primary road graph Citygen-style, generate only secondaries?) vs. conditioning.

votes.corrected: Supported by the evidence: both quotes exist. detail-charts.json has "Epēshu" as a tiles chart (path charts/epeshu, w 3914, h 4200, maxz 3) and Summarch as 4245x3951, maxz 3. docs/research/town-generation.md lists "Exact reproduction of a known 2D chart (vectorize the chart into a primary road graph Citygen-style, generate only secondaries?) vs. conditioning" under "Open questions the dive could not settle". The raster in approach (1) is about 2.2 MB only for overlay-Epeshu.jpg (2,171,695 bytes). overlay-Summarch.jpg is 1.28 MB, and the chart pyramids are 6.6 MB (epeshu) and 4.0 MB (summarch). The narrowest claim the evidence supports: the DM art exists as large rasters (an overlay plus a tiled chart pyramid), and tracing it into a primary road graph is a documented but unresolved idea in the repo's research. The four-way comparison is the author's own judgment, not sourced. Its effort figures ("hours of GCP picking", "about a day per city"), the 0.2-0.6 MB vector size, and the fidelity and determinism ratings for approaches (2)-(4) have no cited evidence. Neither quote mentions GCP/TPS registration, auto-tracing or warped vectors. Treat them as estimates. "Misregistered (V2/V3)" rests on other claims.
votes.reason: Both quotes exist (the JSON one with different whitespace only), but they support only the chart dimensions and an open research question. The comparison table's effort, size and fidelity numbers are unsourced estimates. The 2.2 MB size fits Epēshu only (Summarch is 1.3 MB, chart pyramids 4-6.6 MB). The town-generation quote is explicitly listed as unsettled, so it cannot back a claim that tracing works.

votes.corrected: Yes, with corrections. Do the work in this order. (a) REGISTRATION first. Pick GCPs/TPS on the two canon overlays (art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg, art/overlay-Summarch.jpg), using atlas features: coast, river mouths, and road entries at the walls. Warp each overlay offline into the atlas frame and commit the result as a deterministic asset. This removes the shift whatever the medium, and it bends the art to the atlas, never the atlas to the art. Expect only a handful of GCPs per city: the atlas carries few features inside a 52-px capital footprint. The warp also resamples the canon art, so "full fidelity" in practice means "near-full". The size figure needs fixing: 2.2 MB is Epēshu alone. Both overlays come to about 3.45 MB. The modal chart pyramids (charts/epeshu 6.6 MB, charts/summarch 4.0 MB) are viewed in their own frame through enterChart and are not part of this fix. (b) Tracing (3) for Epēshu/Summarch is a MEDIUM upgrade only: crisp zoom, interactivity, a shared road graph. It is not an anchoring fix, and its vertices must go through the same warp. Its look belongs to filigree slice C "city" (rulings R4: no block labels; R7: nothing at rest, halos on hover only). The Epēshu streets and road graph have to be reconciled with what the street track already owns. It also needs a mobile per-frame cost check for thousands of footprints. The estimates of "a day per city" and "0.2-0.6 MB" are guesses nobody has verified. (c) For invented cities, (4) does not fix registration. genCityCanvas already builds from sampleCityMask, which reads the z5 base tiles around the anchor in the atlas frame, so the procedural cities are already registered at roughly mask resolution. A vector sibling emitter only brings crispness. It must be a new function that leaves the pinned genCityCanvas/sampleCityMask/washMake/xmur3/mulberry32 hashes and cityCanvasSha untouched, and it waits until the mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) closes.
votes.reason: The synthesis transfers to our stack. Its key point is correct and verified: cityBox(a,w,h) centres a fixed FOOT_R box on the anchor whatever the image shows, so registration (GCP/TPS warp of the canon art) is what removes the shift, and a vector city placed through cityBox would misalign just as the raster does. Offline warps and committed traces keep generation deterministic and need no build step. The applies_to_us ordering is right. It needs corrections in four places. (1) The size figure: 2.2 MB is overlay-Epeshu.jpg only. Summarch adds 1.28 MB, and the separate chart pyramids (10.6 MB, modal enterChart) are out of scope. (2) Option (4) is presented as gaining registration "by construction", but procedural cities are already sampled in the base frame by sampleCityMask, which reads the z5 tiles at 1.35*footR around atlasX/atlasY. For them, vectorizing is a crispness gain only. (3) It leaves out who owns what. Filigree slice C owns the painted city look (R4/R7), the street track owns the Epēshu streets/buildings that a shared road graph would have to match, and the mobile per-frame budget limits how much vector geometry we can draw. (4) The pins: any emitter must sit beside the source-hash-pinned functions (genCityCanvas, sampleCityMask, washMake), not inside them, and only after Mobile 5-9. The effort and size estimates for (3) are unverified.

items.summary: Panel-offset logic for fly targets should derive the uncovered rect from the open sheet's measured geometry, not a device class; the +211 px landscape figure is unsupported.

summaries.3-vector: Panel-offset logic for fly targets should derive the uncovered rect from the open sheet's measured geometry, not a device class; the +211 px landscape figure is unsupported.
summaries.5-ownership: If A-U8's landscape right-side sheet (at most 50% wide) applies to #panel, the fly-target offset flips sign (up to about +W/4); panel offset logic should take the sheet side from measured geometry, not a device class.

prior_record.claim: If A-U8's landscape right-side sheet (at most 50% wide) also applies to #panel, the landscape offset flips from −170 px to about +W/4 (+211 px at 844 px). This is unconfirmed.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Panel-offset logic must take the sheet side from geometry, not from a device class.

evidence.quote: landscape 844x340: drawer is a right-side sheet <= 50% wide, no horizontal overflow
A landscape phone (>640 px wide) gets the desktop drawer
/* ---- side panel drawer ---- */

votes.corrected: The three quotes exist, but they do not support the numbers. A-U8 acceptance requires "landscape 844x340: drawer is a right-side sheet <= 50% wide, no horizontal overflow". Brief A16 describes the defect as "A landscape phone (>640 px wide) gets the desktop drawer", and the fix is "In landscape use a right-side sheet capped at 50% width". The "side panel drawer" CSS comment sits directly above #panel. Together these show the drawer being moved to a right-side sheet in landscape is #panel itself, so the "if it also applies to #panel" condition is effectively resolved, not open. What the sources support: in landscape the sheet moves from the left to the right of the map, so any horizontal compensation for the open panel (the visible-centre shift) must change sign and size with it. A sheet capped at 50% shifts the visible centre by at most W/4, which is 211 px at 844 px only if the sheet is exactly 50% wide. The "-170 px" and "+211 px" figures appear in none of the cited sources and are the author's own arithmetic. At HEAD the only 170 px offset is the CSS `.panel-open #jbar{left:calc(50% + 170px)}`, which is half the 340 px panel width. The other compensation is the 346 px margin on `.panel-open .leaflet-top.leaflet-left` and `.leaflet-bottom.leaflet-left` (in the `.panel-open .leaflet-top.leaflet-left,.panel-open .leaflet-bottom.leaflet-left` rule, which carries the 346px safe-area calc). I found no JS pan-offset logic for #panel. The step "flips from -170 to about +W/4" is therefore an inference, not a quoted fact. The conclusion that panel-offset logic should take the side from geometry (the panel's measured side and width) is reasonable, but the sources do not state it.
votes.reason: The three quotes are present at HEAD (units.json A-U8 acceptance, brief A16, the CSS comment at maps-site/index.html). None of them states the -170 px or +211 px offsets. At HEAD the only 170 px is the CSS `.panel-open #jbar{left:calc(50% + 170px)}` (half of the 340 px #panel). The other compensation is the 346 px margin on `.leaflet-top.leaflet-left` and `.leaflet-bottom.leaflet-left` under `.panel-open`. I found no JS pan-offset logic for #panel. The claim also overreaches in treating "applies to #panel" as uncertain: A16's "desktop drawer" is #panel, so the sheet applies to it. And "<= 50% wide" gives a shift of at most W/4, not "about +W/4". The claim does label itself unconfirmed, so the overreach is mild.

votes.corrected: Mostly right as stated, with three refinements. (1) Derive the fly-target offset from the open sheet's measured layout relative to the map container (map.getContainer()), not from a device class or media-query flag: delta = mapCentre − centre of the uncovered rect. A left 340 px panel gives [−170, 0], which stays identical to R1 on desktop. A right sheet of width S gives [+S/2, 0], so at most +W/4 ≈ +211 px at 844 px wide. A bottom sheet gives [0, +sheetH/2] at the chosen stop. Measure with offsetLeft, offsetTop, offsetWidth and offsetHeight (or the .open/stop layout), not with getBoundingClientRect during the 0.28 s transform transition, and not while the closed sheet is translated off-screen. (2) Which shape #panel takes in landscape is genuinely open. A-U8's "landscape 844x340: right-side sheet ≤ 50% wide" may mean the new A4 table drawer, not #panel. A16 alone (extend the mobile query to max-height:500px) would make #panel a bottom sheet, which gives a vertical offset and no sign flip. Pin this in A-U8/A-U9 (Mobile 6/8) before anyone codes an offset. (3) This is viewport framing for flyIntoCity/ensureArrival (setView must also land on the offset target). It is neither registration nor rendering medium, so it fixes none of the owner's zoom misalignment, and it belongs to the mobile lane, not the anchoring work.
votes.reason: This was checked against the HEAD export. Today #panel is a 340 px left drawer (`#panel{...left:0;...width:340px;max-width:86vw`) on every viewport wider than 640 px, including the 844x340 landscape profile. So −170 holds there today, and the dossier's panBy sign (desktop delta [−170, 0]) is consistent. The geometry for a right sheet capped at 50% is also right: the uncovered centre sits S/2 left of the map centre, so delta is +S/2 ≤ +W/4 = +211 at 844 px. The "unconfirmed" label is correct, and the reason is that A-U8 is ambiguous. Its acceptance line speaks of "drawer", and its title and A4 define a new "table drawer" (era/layers/Groups/Company/journey). A16, which A-U8 also owns, is about #panel getting the desktop drawer, and its fix (extending the width-only @media (max-width:640px) query) would make #panel a 64%-height bottom sheet. That outcome needs a vertical offset, not a sign flip. Taking the side from geometry covers all three outcomes and keeps desktop identical to R1, so applies_to_us is sound. It needs two precision fixes: transform-free measurement (#panel animates via transform) and the sheet stop A-U9 opens at. It also needs a scope note. This only frames the fly target clear of the card. It does not change where art or vector cities sit relative to the coast, rivers or roads, so it does nothing for the registration problem the owner raised. It is mobile-lane work (Mobile 6/8 are mid-flight), and it touches no pinned function (xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask).

votes.corrected:
Applies, but only as a method, and only to the two DM canon charts. Epēshu (overlay-Epeshu.jpg) and Summarch (overlay-Summarch.jpg) are the only drawn charts. Today they are placed by cityBox(a,w,h) in maps-site/index.html, which centres the image on the anchor dot at FOOT_R.capital = 26 world px and fits it to the image's aspect ratio. Nothing ties that box to the coast or to roads, so this is a registration fix, not a change of rendering medium. A vector city placed through cityBox would be off by exactly the same amount.

The fix: pick a few control points where the table actually checks the fit, such as the coastline (Epēshu's sea lies SSW, about 10 px away), river mouths, and the gates where the dotted roads arrive. Fit a low-order transform with art moving to atlas, never the reverse: a similarity transform with 4 parameters, or an affine one if there are at least 4 well-spread points. Don't use a rubber-sheet warp, because the atlas has only about 52 px of detail across a capital and DM art is canon. Report the leftover error per point in atlas px.

That error has to be judged at the zooms where it shows. In the overlay fade (z6.8-7.8) one atlas px is about 7-14 screen px; at Z_STREET 11.5 it is about 180 screen px. So "small" means small at the crossfade, and the base map has to stay hidden past it.

Stack notes:
- L.imageOverlay takes only axis-aligned bounds. A rotation or shear has to be either baked offline into the overlay JPG and the charts/ pyramid (a stored canon asset; this keeps runtime cost and determinism unchanged), or applied with a CSS transform on the overlay element.
- The POIs and enterChart currently reproject through the footprint transform. They must use the fitted transform instead, or the POIs will drift off the art.
- Store the transform as data, e.g. control points plus fitted parameters per city next to city-anchors.json. Don't hand-tune the box.
- cityBox and cityMaxZ are not pinned functions. But the atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) is mid-flight in the same file, so schedule this after it.

Procedural cities don't need control points. genCityCanvas already samples the atlas land/water mask through sampleCityMask and the same box, so they are registered by construction. Their only gap is that the footprint scale is arbitrary.

The Siegfried figures (0.7 mm, 35 m, ten points) don't transfer as a target. Treat them as precedent only; the transform swisstopo uses is still unverified.
votes.reason:
The direction is right. The atlas is authoritative, and the misalignment comes from cityBox: a centred, kind-sized square that ignores what the image depicts. Fitting control points on the coast, river mouths and road gates, then reporting the leftover error, is the correct registration fix, and it matches the owner's complaint about drawn city maps not anchoring.

The original note was too vague in five ways:
1. Scope. Only the two canon charts need fitting; procedural plans are already aligned to the atlas mask.
2. Leaflet limits. An image overlay can't rotate or shear, so the transform has to be baked into the image offline or applied with a CSS transform.
3. Transform choice. A similarity or affine fit, not a warp, is what respects DM art as canon.
4. The leftover error has to be read at each zoom level. A 1 atlas px error is about 180 screen px at street zoom.
5. POIs and chart mode reuse the footprint transform and have to move with the fit. The edit also has to wait for the mobile atlas lane that is mid-flight in the same file.

The Siegfried tolerance numbers are low-confidence search summaries and have no counterpart in our project.

items.summary: Allmaps' transform ladder (straight/Helmert 2 GCPs, polynomial1 3, polynomial2/3 6/10, TPS 3 exact at GCPs) ports as an offline fit tool, scale+translate first, Helmert pre-warped with alpha, TPS only on an owner ruling; registerCityOverlay needs a bounds override honoured by cityBox and cityMaxZ, and the library itself does not fit CRS.Simple.

prior_record.claim: [registration] Ways to register an image to a base, ranked by how much they bend it. A straight transform (2 control points) moves and scales. Helmert (2) adds rotation and keeps shapes and angles. Polynomial1 (3) adds shear. Polynomial2/3 (6/10) bend. A thin-plate spline (3+) is 'exact at GCPs' rubber-sheeting. Allmaps applies these in the browser with WebGL2 on georeferenced (EPSG:4326/3857) maps and needs zoomAnimationThreshold:1. Covered by: new (accurate-mapping.md covers vectorising scans, not image-to-base transforms).
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: The method ports; the library does not. It needs WebGL2, a projected CRS, IIIF, a beta dependency chain and a build, against our CRS.Simple, single-file, no-build atlas, and it conflicts with the custom wheel zoom. The fit is an offline node tool (alongside tools/build-gazetteer.js): fit Helmert or polynomial1 from DM-chart px to atlas px, write a pre-warped JPG plus axis-aligned bounds, then registerCityOverlay unchanged. This is deterministic and costs nothing per frame. Helmert keeps the DM's drawing exactly; TPS bends canon art, which needs an owner ruling.

Say instead that the layer takes Georeference Annotations (IIIF) and projects them to geographic positions. The repo-coverage note holds: docs/research/accurate-mapping.md has nothing on Helmert, polynomial or TPS transforms or georeferencing. The 'applies_to_us' text about a build, a beta chain and conflict with CRS.Simple is the author's inference, not something the sources state.

votes.corrected:
The method transfers but the library does not. Allmaps needs WebGL2, a georeferenced CRS (EPSG:4326 or 3857), IIIF, a beta dependency chain and a build. Our atlas is CRS.Simple, one file, no build, with a custom wheel handler (map.scrollWheelZoom.disable() plus the 'wheel' listener in maps-site/index.html).

The fix is REGISTRATION, not medium. Add an offline node tool next to tools/build-gazetteer.js. It fits a transform from DM-chart pixels to atlas pixels using ground control points on atlas features (coast, river mouths, road gates). Try the transforms from least bending to most:
(a) Straight transform, or Polynomial1 with no shear. This needs only new axis-aligned bounds: no resampling and no new image.
(b) Helmert. Use it only if the fitted rotation is not negligible. Write a pre-warped image. It must be PNG or WebP with alpha, not JPG, because rotation leaves empty corners.
(c) TPS or Polynomial2/3. These bend canon art, so they need an owner ruling.

The overlay path does NOT stay unchanged. Bounds come only from cityBox(a,w,h), which uses footR(kind) centred on the anchor. cityMaxZ, the POI layer, the wash and worldCityUpdate all call cityBox. So registerCityOverlay needs an opts.bounds override that cityBox and cityMaxZ honour. The canon POIs (reprojected via poiRef 'through the footprint transform') must go through the same fitted transform, or they drift off the corrected art.

Scope:
- This applies to the two canon overlays, overlay-Epeshu.jpg and overlay-Summarch.jpg.
- The modal enterChart pyramids live in their own chart space and are unaffected.
- Procedural cities (genCityCanvas plus sampleCityMask) already sample the atlas mask inside cityBox, so they are registered by construction. Do not touch the pinned genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask, or cityCanvasSha.

The result is deterministic, costs nothing per frame, and keeps the atlas authoritative. A vector city placed through the unchanged cityBox would misalign exactly as the raster does today.
votes.reason:
Verified in the HEAD export, maps-site/index.html.
- Bounds are cityBox(a,w,h) = footR(a.kind) centred on a.atlasX/atlasY, scaled to the image aspect. Every consumer calls cityBox: the POI layers (two sites with reg.poiRef), the wash at f=1.7, and the nearest-city path. registerCityOverlay takes no bounds option. So "registerCityOverlay unchanged" is wrong: a fitted transform's bounds have no way in without an opts.bounds or cityBox override.
- Canon POIs are reprojected through that same footprint (comment: "Epēshu's 19 POIs reproject through the footprint transform"; poiRef DETAIL w/h). They must get the fitted transform too, or the markers detach from the corrected art.
- A Helmert rotation cannot be shown by an axis-aligned L.imageOverlay without resampling. A JPG pre-warp leaves opaque corners, so it needs alpha. When rotation is negligible, a 4-parameter scale+translate fit is just new bounds and touches no pixels at all. That is the least-bending option, and it should be tried first.
- The library rejection is correct: CRS.Simple, no build, single file, the custom wheel zoom (scrollWheelZoom disabled plus our own wheel listener), and the beta WebGL2/IIIF stack.
- The offline node tool is the right shape: deterministic, no per-frame cost, atlas authoritative. The TPS-needs-an-owner-ruling caveat is right too.
- Scope needed narrowing: procedural cities already sample the atlas mask inside cityBox, so they are registered by construction. The pinned genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask are untouched. The enterChart pyramids are modal and use their own chart coordinates.
The core recommendation holds; only the "unchanged" detail and the missing POI and alpha handling needed correcting.

items.summary: Leaflet corner plugins (Rotated: 3 corners; DistortableImage: 4 corners via CSS) show runtime registration without WebGL, but the cheapest step is a control-point-registered axis-aligned box, with a ~40-line _reset/_animateZoom subclass or offline pre-warp only if rotation or shear remains.

prior_record.claim: [registration] Leaflet-native runtime registration exists without WebGL. L.ImageOverlay.Rotated places an image by three corners (affine: rotate and skew). Leaflet.DistortableImage places it by four corners (perspective, CSS3 matrix3d), with a README claim that it handles 100+ images on a smartphone. Covered by: new.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Usable as a pattern of about 40 lines (a CSS matrix from 3 corners, re-applied on zoomanim/zoomend the way ImageOverlay does). Vendoring either plugin conflicts with single-file/no-framework, and Rotated is untested on 1.9.4. Prefer pre-warping offline (C7), which keeps the plain axis-aligned ImageOverlay; use corners at runtime only if the owner wants the DM art left unresampled.

evidence.quote: whereas `L.ImageOverlay.Rotated` is defined by **three** points (the `L.LatLng`s of the top-left, top-right and bottom-left corners of the image). The image will be rotated *and* skewed ... This plugin has been tested only with Leaflet 1.0.0-beta and 1.0.0-rc1.
allows for perspectival distortions of images, client-side, using CSS3 transformations in the DOM ... It can handle over 100 images smoothly, even on a smartphone

"Affine" is an inference from three points, not README wording. Every quote is verbatim: the three-point definition, "rotated and skewed", the 1.0.0-beta/rc1 test caveat, "perspectival distortions ... CSS3 transformations in the DOM", and "over 100 images smoothly, even on a smartphone". The four-corner placement is supported by the getCorners() API in the README. I confirmed matrix3d by downloading the 0.21.9 tarball: src/util/DomUtil.js and the dist bundle both build matrix3d(). The only gaps are matrix3d and "affine", which are not README text, and the smartphone figure is a self-reported README claim.

votes.corrected: This is a REGISTRATION fix, not a rendering one. The pattern transfers, the plugins do not, and the claim's runtime-corner step is premature. (1) Cheapest first: maps-site/index.html already places every city layer through `cityBox(a,w,h)`. That covers the overlay in the worldCityUpdate path, the wash in `washMake` (`var box=cityBox(a,reg.w,reg.h),f=1.7`) and the POIs in buildWorldPOIs and its sibling. A plain axis-aligned L.imageOverlay can already show separate x/y scale plus an offset. So give the canon art (overlay-Epeshu.jpg, overlay-Summarch.jpg) a per-city registered box, solved from two or more ground control points against the atlas coast, river and roads, in place of the FOOT_R square. The wash, POIs and overlay then follow with no edit to the pinned `washMake`/`genCityCanvas`/`sampleCityMask` source, and cityCanvasSha does not change. (2) Only if the leftover error after that shows rotation or shear, use a three-corner affine. Do this by pre-warping offline (C7), which keeps the axis-aligned ImageOverlay, or with a small in-file ImageOverlay subclass of roughly 40 lines. That subclass must override `_reset` and `_animateZoom`, because Leaflet 1.9.4 writes the image transform itself with DomUtil.setTransform. The same affine must also be applied to the POI marker mapping, the wash bounds and the road stubs. A new image-px-to-atlas function shared by every cityBox consumer is required, or the markers drift off the art. (3) Do not take either plugin. Leaflet is self-hosted under vendor/leaflet@1.9.4, so loading from a CDN is not the objection. The objection is that Rotated was only tested on Leaflet 1.0 betas, and DistortableImage is an editing UI with handles, toolbars and extra dependencies, so its '100+ images on a smartphone' claim says nothing about our case of one overlay at a time. A four-corner perspective warp also adds nothing for top-down hand-drawn art. (4) Scope: the seeded procedural cities are drawn from a mask sampled out of the z5 tiles inside the same box, so they are already registered to the atlas and need no corners. Only the DM canon maps and their enterChart chart pyramids do. (5) Timing: maps-site/index.html is held by the in-flight mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9), so this must be queued after it. Any warp bends the art to the atlas, never the atlas to the art.
votes.reason: The claim is right that the stack can register art without WebGL, and right to reject vendoring either plugin. The ~40-line CSS-matrix pattern is technically sound on Leaflet 1.9.4, as long as it overrides _reset and _animateZoom, since ImageOverlay sets its own transform during zoom animation. It gets three things wrong or leaves them out. First, it skips the zero-new-mechanism step. cityBox ignores what each image depicts, and a plain bounds overlay can already apply separate x/y scale and an offset, so control-point-registered per-city boxes come first and may be all that is needed. Second, cityBox has several consumers: the overlay, washMake's wash bounds and the POI placement in buildWorldPOIs and its sibling. A corner-placed overlay that does not share one transform with all of them would leave the POIs and wash misaligned against the art. Registering through the box needs no edit to washMake's pinned source, which matters for the UG3 atlas_fn_sha pin. Third, it does not say that only the DM canon art and chart pyramids need this, since the procedural cities are generated from the tile mask inside the box. Minor factual tweak: Leaflet is self-hosted under vendor/, so the reason not to vendor is plugin age and its editing-UI dependencies, not a CDN or single-file rule as such. Timing: maps-site/index.html is mid-flight in the mobile atlas lane.

items.summary: L.svgOverlay extends L.ImageOverlay and is placed by the same bounds box, so a vector city through cityBox keeps the raster's offset (an SVG letterboxes unless preserveAspectRatio is none), while L.polyline/L.polygon in atlas px are placed per vertex.

prior_record.claim: [medium] A vector city placed through cityBox misaligns exactly as the raster does. L.svgOverlay extends L.ImageOverlay, so it shares the same bounds-box positioning and _animateZoom scaling. Vectors only give crispness, interactivity and shared vertices. They do not fix registration. Covered by: new (source-confirms the task's key distinction).
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Any 'vectorized city layer' must be authored in atlas-px coordinates, or pass through the same registration transform as C5/C7, before it reaches Leaflet. Dropping an SVG export of the DM chart into cityBox gives a crisp image at the same misplacement.

evidence.quote: export var SVGOverlay = ImageOverlay.extend({ _initImage: function () { var el = this._image = this._url; ...

votes.corrected: Leaflet 1.9.4 SVGOverlay extends ImageOverlay and overrides only _initImage, so it inherits ImageOverlay's _reset (sizes and positions the element to the projected bounds box) and _animateZoom (scales the element from _bounds). An SVG overlay therefore sits wherever its bounds box puts it, as a raster does. A vector city given the same cityBox bounds (cityBox is in maps-site/index.html and sizes the box from FOOT_R[kind] and the image aspect) inherits the same registration error. Vectors improve crispness, interactivity and shared vertices, and do not change registration. The last two benefits are the claim's own inference and are not in the quoted source. "Exactly" is slightly strong. An SVG with a viewBox and the default preserveAspectRatio is fitted inside the box (letterboxed), where a raster is stretched to it. Set preserveAspectRatio="none", or match the box aspect to the viewBox, to get identical placement. A vector layer built from Leaflet vector layers (L.polygon, L.polyline) in atlas-px coordinates is positioned per vertex and does not go through a bounds box.

The quoted text matches (the quote was elided with "..."): SVGOverlay = ImageOverlay.extend({_initImage...}). ImageOverlay's _animateZoom uses this._bounds and _reset sets position and size from the bounds, and SVGOverlay does not override either. cityBox and FOOT_R exist in the head export of maps-site/index.html. The source confirms the shared-mechanics part. The statements that vectors give only crispness, interactivity and shared vertices, and that misalignment is "exactly" the same, are design inference, not source text. The viewBox/preserveAspectRatio letterboxing difference and the per-vertex vector alternative narrow the claim slightly.

votes.corrected: Holds, with sharper wording. The atlas positions every city image through `L.imageOverlay(reg.url, cb, …)`, where `cb` comes from `cityBox(a,w,h)`. That function centres a `footR(kind)` box on `a.atlasX/atlasY` and scales it to the image's aspect ratio. It does not look at what the image shows. `L.svgOverlay` extends `ImageOverlay` and takes the same `LatLngBounds`, so an SVG or vectorised export of the DM chart (overlay-Epeshu / overlay-Summarch) or of `genCityCanvas` placed through `cityBox` keeps exactly the same offset. Only the stretching blur goes away. Vectors help registration only when their coordinates are already registered. Two ways to get there: (a) author the geometry as `L.polyline`/`L.polygon` in atlas-px latlngs, which Leaflet projects vertex by vertex and which can share vertices with atlas roads, coast and rivers; or (b) use one `svgOverlay` whose `viewBox` is in atlas px and whose bounds equal that `viewBox` extent exactly, after the DM art has been bent to the atlas by the C5/C7 control-point transform. Registration always bends the art to the atlas, never the atlas to the art. Neither `ImageOverlay` nor `svgOverlay` drifts during zoom; `_animateZoom` stays consistent with the bounds. The 'shift' the owner sees comes from what `cityBox` assumes about the image's contents, plus the cross-fade between base and city layers (`baseOpacity`/`overlayOpacity`) showing two different geometries at once.
