items.summary: Refuted: Leaflet vector re-projection is real, but atlas-px geometry is not 'the medium that lines up', because buildCityStubs already inherits cityBox via scl=S/(2*footR) and alignment needs registration first.

prior_record.claim: [both] Geometry authored in map coordinates stays registered and sharp at any zoom. L.polyline/L.polygon in a Renderer are re-projected from full-precision latlngs at each zoomend (Renderer._onZoomEnd then _project), CSS-transformed only during the animation, and simplified in screen px (smoothFactor 1.0). This is Leaflet's equivalent of MapLibre vector overzoom ('Data from tiles at the maxzoom are used when displaying the map at higher zoom levels') and of filigree's 'style separate from geometry'. Covered by: partly (living dossier 'Renderer.js' pattern and filigree dossier §9 'Style separate from geometry'); the overzoom equivalence is new.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Applies. buildCityStubs already draws atlas-px polylines in pane pCity, so the pattern is shipped. A vector city (streets, walls, quays as atlas-px paths, with a road stub sharing its end vertex with the traced atlas road) is the medium that lines up and stays crisp past the z5 overzoom. Cost: preferCanvas or a single L.canvas per city to respect the mobile frame budget (web-performance.md), and hover-only halos and no block labels (filigree R4/R7). City-look ownership stays with filigree slice C.

evidence.quote: _onZoomEnd: function () { for (var id in this._layers) { this._layers[id]._project(); } }
// @option smoothFactor: Number = 1.0 // How much to simplify the polyline on each zoom level.
maxzoom: "Maximum zoom level for which tiles are available, as in the TileJSON spec. Data from tiles at the maxzoom are used when displaying the map at higher zoom levels."
**Style separate from geometry.** This is the Vectormap instinct.

votes.corrected: [both] Geometry authored as atlas-px latlngs in a Leaflet vector layer stays registered to the atlas and is redrawn crisply at rest after each zoom. Renderer.getEvents binds zoomend to _onZoomEnd, which calls each layer's _project() from the stored latlngs. During zoom, Renderer._onZoom and _onAnimZoom only CSS-transform the renderer container via _updateTransform (so it is scaled, not sharp, mid-animation). Polyline._simplifyPoints runs LineUtil.simplify on the projected pixel parts with tolerance smoothFactor, default 1.0, so simplification is in screen px. The three quotes are verbatim in Leaflet v1.9.4 Renderer.js and Polyline.js. The MapLibre line is verbatim in the v8 style spec (maxzoom doc), but it describes tiled vector data being reused above the tile maxzoom. Leaflet vectors are not tiled, so calling this 'Leaflet's equivalent of MapLibre overzoom' is the dossier author's analogy (both keep geometry resolution-independent), not something either source states. The filigree dossier quote 'Style separate from geometry. This is the Vectormap instinct.' is real (docs/filigree/research-dossier.md, the bullet under '## 9. Readers vs navigators (v2)'). Its sub-bullets are about data JSON versus rendering and hot-swappable registerCityOverlay, not Leaflet re-projection. Repo check: buildCityStubs in maps-site/index.html draws two L.polyline per stub with px() latlngs in pane 'pCity', only when reg.prov==='invented' and reg.stubs exist. These are straight two-point segments, not a vector city. maps-site/index.html has no preferCanvas or L.canvas, so the canvas-renderer cost note is a recommendation, not shipped.
votes.reason: The Leaflet mechanics are confirmed against the v1.9.4 source (fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com): Renderer._onZoomEnd calls _project on every layer, _onAnimZoom and _onZoom apply a CSS transform through _updateTransform, and Polyline._simplifyPoints uses smoothFactor 1.0 as a pixel tolerance. The MapLibre maxzoom text exists verbatim in v8.json. The filigree dossier quote exists. The 'Renderer.js' pattern in the living dossier is real but is about a registered overlay canvas (10% pad, CSS transform on zoomanim, redraw on moveend), so 'partly covered' is fair. The claim overreaches in three places. First, 'Leaflet's equivalent of MapLibre vector overzoom' is an analogy: the MapLibre quote concerns tile availability and no source ties it to Leaflet vector layers. Second, 'sharp at any zoom' holds only at rest, because the renderer is scaled by CSS during zoom. Third, the filigree 'style separate from geometry' quote is about data versus rendering, not zoom re-projection. Narrowing to the verified mechanics leaves the recommendation intact: it supports atlas-px vector geometry staying registered, but it says nothing about how city art is registered to the atlas, which is the real alignment issue.

votes.corrected:
Partly applies. The Leaflet mechanism is real and transfers to our stack. L.polyline/L.polygon latlngs keep full precision; the renderer CSS-transforms them during the zoom animation and re-projects them on zoomend. Geometry authored in atlas px (px(x,y) under CRS.Simple, NZ=4) therefore draws crisp at Z_STREET 11.5, where the z5 base and the cityBox-stretched image go soft. The applies_to_us text overclaims in three places.

(1) The claim that the pattern "is shipped" needs a qualifier. buildCityStubs (maps-site/index.html) does draw atlas-px polylines in pane pCity, but only for reg.prov==='invented'; canon charts get none. Each stub is a 2-point line. Its inner end is the canvas gate mapped back through scl=S/(2*footR(a.kind)), which is the same footR/cityBox registration the raster uses. Its outer end is a synthetic point at footR*1.18 along the gate angle. It is not a shared vertex with the traced atlas road (buildNamedWays). So the medium is shipped, but registration is not.

(2) "Is the medium that lines up" is wrong. REGISTRATION fixes misalignment: anchoring streets, walls and quays to atlas coast, river and road features, with the art bent to the atlas. The RENDERING MEDIUM only buys crispness past the overzoom, interactivity, and the possibility of shared vertices. A vector city placed through cityBox misaligns exactly as the raster does. Acting on this needs a registration step first: control points from DM art or generated plan to atlas features, a fitted transform, and stub and road endpoints snapped to the exact atlas road vertex. Only then do you vectorize. Once registered, the same transform also fixes the raster canon overlays.

(3) The MapLibre "maxzoom overzoom" equivalence is loose. Leaflet has no tiled, quantized vector source. Better wording: geometry is re-rasterized per zoom instead of resampled. "Style separate from geometry" (filigree dossier §9) is the correct analogy.

Constraints:
- Epēshu and Summarch are DM-drawn canon. A vector city there must be traced from, or registered to, the DM art. It cannot replace that art with procedural geometry.
- Procedural vector cities must come from the seeded gen. The genCityCanvas, sampleCityMask and washMake hashes (UG3 atlas_fn_sha) and cityCanvasSha are pinned mid-flight (Mobile 5-9), so add new functions beside them rather than editing them.
- The map today uses the default SVG renderer (no preferCanvas). Use one L.canvas renderer per active city, in a declared pane, to stay within the mobile frame budget.
- Filigree R4 (never label blocks) and R7 (nothing at rest; halos on hover only) apply.
- Filigree slice C owns the city look. Living H2z owns the zoom-through into the 3D street view.

L.map has no preferCanvas set, so it uses the SVG default; the canvas-renderer cost note is valid. The MapLibre tiled-overzoom analogy does not match Leaflet's untiled latlng model. items.summary: Tokyo's single metric frame and 3D Tiles' parent-relative transforms with nested bounding volumes preserve registration authored into the parent frame but do not themselves guarantee a refinement swap cannot move content; a city detail level should be atlas px plus one fitted transform.

prior_record.claim: [registration] Streamed 3D cities stay anchored because every tile lives in one frame. The Procedural-Tokyo candidate uses a single metric frame with its origin at the area centre and 256 m tiles. In 3D Tiles, each child's transform is relative to its parent and its content lies inside the parent's bounding volume, so a refinement swap (REPLACE) or overlay (ADD) cannot move content. Covered by: partly (streamed-streets.md and street dossier S2-S6/V1 cover SSE refinement and REPLACE/ADD; the frame and transform property are new).
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Analogy for the atlas. A city detail level should be a child of the atlas frame (atlas px, plus a registration transform per C7), not a separately fitted picture. Each finer level then nests inside the coarser one, the way tier D nests in the base. Street-level LOD itself stays with the street track.

evidence.quote: World frame: metres, x east, y up (Tokyo Peil height), z south; the origin is the area's centre. ... Tiles are 256 m squares meshed in Web Workers.

The `transform` property is a 4x4 affine transformation matrix ... that transforms from the tile's local coordinate system to the parent tile's coordinate system. ... each tile has a bounding volume completely enclosing its content, and the content for child tiles are completely inside the parent's bounding volume.
refine by screen-space error `geomErr·H/(2d·tan(fov/2)) > ~16 px`

votes.corrected: All three quotes are verified verbatim. The Tokyo README (github.com/jeantimex/tokyo) states a single world frame (metres, x east, y up, z south, origin at the area's centre) and 256 m tiles meshed in Web Workers. The 3D Tiles spec states that a tile's `transform` maps its local coordinates to its parent's coordinate system, and that each tile's bounding volume encloses its content with child content inside the parent's bounding volume. The spec also defines REPLACE (children render in place of the parent) and ADD (parent and children render together). docs/research/streamed-streets.md carries the screen-space-error rule. What the sources support is: tiles share one coordinate frame (Tokyo) or a parent-chained transform with nested bounding volumes (3D Tiles), and these are spatial-containment conventions a tileset author must satisfy. They do not by themselves guarantee that a refinement swap cannot move content. Fine-level geometry registering with coarse-level geometry depends on how the data was authored, which is why 3D Tiles carries a geometric error. Neither source says Tokyo's single frame or the 3D Tiles transform chain is the reason the cities stay anchored. That is an inference, and the two sources describe different mechanisms: Tokyo has one flat frame, while 3D Tiles composes per-tile transforms. The 'new' flag against the street dossier was not checked beyond finding that streamed-streets.md has the SSE rule.
votes.reason: Quotes exist and match, but the claim that a refinement swap 'cannot move content' and that a single frame is why streamed cities stay anchored goes beyond what the sources state. The spec guarantees a transform chain and bounding-volume containment, not content registration across levels. The 'applies to us' analogy is reasonable but is the authors' inference.

votes.corrected:
Analogy for the atlas, and it is mainly about registration. The 3D Tiles nesting rule (each child has a parent-relative transform and its content stays inside the parent's bounding volume) keeps a level-of-detail swap from moving content only because the content was registered to the parent frame when it was made. The rule does not do any registering itself. We already have one frame: CRS.Simple world px, which equals atlas px at NZ=4. The city overlay is already a parent-relative transform: cityBox in maps-site/index.html applies a uniform scale and translate about the anchor. The fault is how that transform's parameters are set. The scale comes from FOOT_R[kind] and the image's aspect ratio, not from matching what the image shows to atlas features. Rendering the city as vectors through the same cityBox would misalign in exactly the same way.

The cases differ:
- Procedural plans are already children of the atlas frame by construction. sampleCityMask reads the z5 tiles over the anchor ± 1.35·footR, so their coast and water are registered.
- The DM canon art (overlay-Epeshu.jpg, overlay-Summarch.jpg) is the "separately fitted picture". It needs a per-image registration transform (C7) fitted from control points matched between the art and the atlas: coast, river mouths, road entries. The atlas is fixed and the art bends to it.
- enterChart's modal charts live in their own image-pixel frame (cpx at atZoom). They are not a child of the atlas at all, so they should stay a separate mode or be given the same transform.

Practical limits:
- L.imageOverlay takes only axis-aligned bounds. A transform with rotation or shear means hand-written code: a CSS matrix on the overlay element or a canvas pre-warp. A plain bounds fit only covers scale plus translate.
- Hand-drawn art may need a piecewise warp, not a single affine.
- Vector geometry takes any transform cheaply. It is also where pooled road vertices can be shared with the atlas, but only after registration.

Keep changes outside the pinned functions:
- Put the transform in a data table beside city-anchors.json and apply it in cityBox and the overlay code.
- Do not edit genCityCanvas, sampleCityMask or washMake, so UG3 atlas_fn_sha and cityCanvasSha stay valid.
- Coordinate with Mobile 5-9, which is mid-flight in maps-site/index.html.

"Tier D nests in the base" is accurate only in this sense: tier D is a zoom reveal in the same world-px frame. Street-level LOD and the zoom-through into 3D (H2z) stay with the street and living tracks.
votes.reason:
The analogy carries over, and "child of the atlas frame plus a registration transform per C7" is the right direction. As written, though, the claim suggests the nesting invariant is what anchors content and that adding a frame and transform is new. We already have both. CRS.Simple gives us one world frame, and cityBox is a transform relative to the parent (scale and translate about atlasX/atlasY). It shifts things because its scale comes from FOOT_R and the image aspect ratio, not from features in the art. In 3D Tiles, content stays put on refinement only because it was authored in the parent frame. Nesting keeps that registration intact but does not create it.

The corrected text adds:
- Procedural plans are already registered through sampleCityMask.
- The DM art is where control-point registration is needed.
- The enterChart modal is a separate frame.
- Leaflet's imageOverlay only takes axis-aligned boxes.
- A vector layer does not fix the offset without registration.
- The pinned function hashes must not change (UG3).

None of the corrections reverses the recommendation, so the claim holds with minor corrections.

items.summary: map.geo.admin.ch hands 2D to 3D as view state (centre, height from resolution and canvas width, top-down, only when no camera is stored) and returns only the ray-cast centre; for H2/H2z this means carrying an atlas-px centre and scale through the Epēshu atlas-sim transform, separate from the cityBox fix.

prior_record.claim: [registration] A 2D-to-3D hand-off stays anchored when it transfers the view state, not the picture. map.geo.admin.ch starts its Cesium camera at the 2D centre, with a height computed from the 2D resolution and canvas width and a top-down pitch. On leaving 3D it ray-casts the camera target and makes that point the new 2D centre. Cesium's own 2D-to-3D morph lerps camera vectors in stages. Covered by: partly (living dossier §2 Cesium SceneTransitioner; §5 H1/H2/H2z); the geoadmin camera transfer is new.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Applies to H2/H2z (owned by the living track). The atlas-sim transform already exists inside the Epēshu window, atlas = (1060,1240) + grid·800/768 (cartographic-filigree.md), so #goto can carry an atlas-px centre plus a zoom-to-camera-radius mapping, and the reverse lands the atlas on the sim's focus. Outside the window there is no sim frame. The poster crossfade (H2z) must be registered with the same transform or it will drift like StreetView3DOverlay (C14).

votes.corrected: map.geo.admin.ch's CesiumCamera.vue (read raw, packages/mapviewer/src/modules/map/components/cesium/CesiumCamera.vue on develop) hands state across the 2D/3D boundary, not an image. (a) Only when no camera position is already stored (for example from the URL), initCamera flies to Cartesian3.fromDegrees(centerEpsg4326[0], centerEpsg4326[1], calculateHeight(resolution, canvas.clientWidth)) with pitch -PI_OVER_TWO and heading from the 2D rotation. calculateHeight in cameraUtils.js is (resolution*width)/(2*tan(PI/6)). (b) On onBeforeUnmount, setCenterToCameraTarget() calls getPickRay at the canvas centre, then globe.pick, then dispatches setCenter with the point projected from WGS84. It transfers only the centre. It does not transfer zoom or resolution back to 2D, and the camera-to-2D height inverse (calculateResolution) is not used on exit. Cesium's SceneTransitioner.morphFrom2DTo3D divides the duration by 3 and runs staged morphs (ortho-to-perspective, then Columbus-view-to-3D, then morphTime). The camera vectors go through columbusViewMorph, a Cartesian3.lerp commented 'Just linear for now', driven by a QUARTIC_OUT-eased time, so 'linearly lerped' is loose. The docs/living/research-dossier.md §2 row and the cartographic-filigree.md line 'atlas = (1060,1240) + grid·800/768' both exist as cited.
votes.reason: I read the raw source, so the WebFetch-summary caveat no longer applies. The geoadmin quotes (centre-based destination, calculateHeight from resolution and canvas width, top-down pitch, ray-cast target set as the new centre) are all present and support the claim. Three qualifiers are needed. The 2D-to-3D start applies only when no camera position is already stored. The 3D-to-2D return carries the centre only, not the zoom, so 'transfers the view state' is slightly broader than the code. The Cesium morph is staged (three stages) with eased lerps, not purely linear. The repo-side facts (the dossier §2 row and the Epēshu atlas-to-sim transform at EPESHU_HF) are verified. I did not check the C14 StreetView3DOverlay drift reference or the H2z wording in this pass.

votes.corrected:
Applies, narrowed. This is about REGISTRATION of the atlas-to-sim hand-off (H2, and H2z in the living track). It does not fix the misalignment the owner reported: cityBox puts the overlay on a FOOT_R box, and that stays a separate registration problem whatever the medium. Only the view-state half transfers. The atlas and the sim are separate pages with separate engines, so Cesium's staged in-engine morph (SceneTransitioner) has no counterpart here.

The transform is real and checks out against the data. In index.html, N=768 and gridToWorld(i)=(i/(N-1)-0.5)*W_SIZE with W_SIZE=9000. The mapping is atlas=(1060,1240)+grid*800/768. So one affine atlas-px to sim-metres map (about 11.7 m per atlas px) exists for the Epēshu window [1060..1860]x[1240..2040]. But it lives only in docs and implied data. Zoom mapping: at atlas zoom z, one screen px = 2^(4-z) atlas px. Convert that to metres per px, then to the sim's CAM altitude/tFromAlt using the sim FOV, the canvas width and the pitch at that t. The geoadmin formula assumes a top-down camera; the sim's orbit camera is not top-down.

Reverse direction: no ray-cast is needed, because CAM.focus is already the ground target. Map focus x,z through the inverse transform to the atlas centre and pick a zoom from altitude.

Outside the Epēshu window there is no sim frame. Fall back to the name-based #goto, or no link at all.

The H2z poster is a perspective frozen view. No planar transform can register it to the top-down atlas beyond the single transferred focus point. Anchor the crossfade on that point (or use a top-down sim render), and do not promise full-frame alignment (compare the StreetView3DOverlay drift, C14). Determinism and the mobile per-frame budget are unaffected: this is camera state carried in the hash, not generation.
votes.reason:
The core idea transfers: hand over the view state (centre plus scale), not the picture. The atlas-to-sim affine transform is confirmed in the data (Epēshu grid 169,168 maps to anchor 1236.1,1415 in city-anchors.json), and the sim's CAM.focus/flyTo/tFromAlt make both directions straightforward.

4. A perspective poster can only be anchored at the focus point, not "registered with the same transform".

The Cesium morph does not apply, because the atlas and sim are separate pages and engines.

items.summary: StreetView3DOverlay's trial-and-error placement is self-described as 'not very precise' and js-three anchors its origin near the content because float32 holds about 7 digits; the lesson is to fit control points and report a residual, and the precision issue applies only to a WebGL layer, not Leaflet's float64 2D layers.

prior_record.claim: [registration] Placing 3D or detail content over 2D imagery without real registration drifts. StreetView3DOverlay's author says registration is imprecise and was tuned by trial and error. Google's js-three uses a fixed anchor origin because float32 holds about 7 digits. Covered by: covered (docs/living/research-dossier.md §2).
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Warns against H1 (three.js inside the atlas) and against hand-nudging the bounds until it looks right. Registration must come from control points with a residual reported. At z11.5 one atlas px is about 181 screen px, so a per-city local origin matters for any canvas or GL detail layer.

evidence.quote: StreetView3DOverlay: three.js model over Street View imagery. The author says registration is imprecise and was tuned by trial and error, so 3D drifts on 2D imagery

The README of rbejar/StreetView3DOverlay says its Street View panorama parameters "have been established by trial-and-error", that the ferris wheel's "position and orientation ... is not very precise", and that "the distortion in the panoramic images is not uniform". The README of googlemaps/js-three says GPU position math "use[s] float32 numbers, which limits the possible precision to about 7 decimal digits", and that the anchor (lat/lng/altitude of the world-space origin) should be set close to where objects are placed. Narrowest supported claim: a 3D overlay on Street View panoramas was placed by hand-tuned parameters and is imprecise because panorama distortion is non-uniform, and js-three uses a caller-chosen local anchor origin near the content because float32 GPU positions hold about 7 digits. The wording "drifts" and the general rule that detail content over 2D imagery drifts without registration are the dossier's inference, not the author's statement: the README speaks of imprecision, not drift under zoom. "Fixed anchor origin" should read "a single local anchor origin chosen near the scene". The z11.5 figure of about 181 screen px per atlas px is the project's own arithmetic in applies_to_us and no cited source supports it.
votes.reason: The dossier quotes are present and both GitHub READMEs back the core facts: trial-and-error imprecise registration, and float32 limiting precision to about 7 digits with a local anchor. The claim overreaches in three places. It generalizes to "drifts", where the source says only "not very precise" because panorama distortion is non-uniform. It calls js-three's anchor "fixed", but the README says to set it near the content. And the 181 px/px figure has no cited source. The dossier's own vote record for js-three is conf/unverif, but the primary README resolves that. The claim as written is not fully supported, though the correction needed is small.

votes.corrected: REGISTRATION, not medium: this is the core lesson for us. Anything drawn on top of the atlas drifts unless its placement comes from fitted control points. Today cityBox(a,w,h) in maps-site/index.html centres a box on the anchor and sizes it from FOOT_R[kind]. Nothing in that ties the box to the coast, rivers or roads of the art, so it has the same flaw as StreetView3DOverlay's trial-and-error tuning. Fix it by fitting a similarity or affine transform per city from control points on DM art (coast, river mouths, road exits) matched to the same features on PatrinorModern. Store that transform as data next to city-anchors.json and report its RMS residual in atlas px. Never hand-nudge bounds, and never move the atlas to fit the art. A vector city layer placed through cityBox would misalign in exactly the same way. The transform data is plain data, so seeded determinism and the pinned hashes of genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask are unaffected, provided the fit stays outside those functions. It is also a further caution on H1, which is already owner-gated and lists "3D-on-raster drift (StreetView3DOverlay)" among its costs in research-dossier.md. PRECISION (narrow it): the float32 / anchor-origin point applies only to a WebGL layer such as H1. At Z_STREET 11.5, 1 atlas px is 2^7.5, about 181 screen px, and the world is about 834k px wide. Leaflet already keeps imageOverlay, SVG and its Canvas renderer stable at that size, because it draws relative to pixelOrigin in float64 JS. A 2D canvas detail layer therefore needs no special origin handling, as long as it draws through Leaflet's layer points. A per-city local origin is required only if GL vertex data is ever used. Also note that the js-three row in the dossier is marked unverified at the source.

Saying a per-city local origin "matters for any canvas" is wrong for our stack. Leaflet 1.9.4 renders overlays, SVG and Canvas relative to pixelOrigin in float64, so only a WebGL layer (H1, which is gated) has the float32 problem. Precision does not cause today's shift; registration does. The 181 px figure is correct (2^(11.5-4)).

It removes curBase and clamps setMaxBounds to the chart. The meshed world instead places art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg (2863x3072) and overlay-Summarch.jpg with cityBox(a,w,h). The frames are not fully unrelated, though. The pyramid (detail-charts.json Epēshu 3914x4200, maxz 3) and the overlay are the same art at the same aspect. The canon POIs are stored once in chart px and reach the meshed overlay through registerCityOverlay's poiRef scaling. It replaces cityBox and the poiRef scaling for the meshed overlay and its POIs. Because the chart px space is shared, that one record also gives the modal chart an exact link back to the atlas (for example, Back returns to the registered spot, and the chart can show an atlas-frame locator).

It also cannot be done by re-pointing the existing pyramid as a bounded L.tileLayer. Those tiles are cut on the chart's own grid (origin at chart 0,0, power-of-two levels up to maxz 3). The registered placement is generally a non-power-of-two scale with a non-tile-aligned offset, and with control points also a warp. A plain L.tileLayer cannot express that, and L.imageOverlay cannot rotate. So if one frame is wanted, the plan needs either an offline, deterministic re-cut of the art on the atlas tile grid at roughly z8 to z10.2 (52 world px holds 3914 chart px, about 75x, so the native level is NZ+6.2, which is below Z_STREET 11.5), or a custom GridLayer that transforms the chart tiles. A registration fix that never touches zoom would still be blocked, and an edit landed right after Mobile 8 would still break the Mobile 9 lane review's reference.
(2) The cause is wrong. A-U7 changes the button increment on touch, plus tile idle and offline-manifest handling. Registration is cityBox placement and the fade bands, which are independent of the zoom increment. Tying (a) to A-U7 mixes up input stepping with anchoring.

items.summary: Epēshu and Summarch are registered as plain images with w/h (registerCityOverlay stores no control points or georeference), placed only by cityBox, and their POIs are reprojected linearly into the same box; a vector layer placed the same way would misalign the same way.

prior_record.claim: (b) The DM-drawn charts are registered to the atlas only through cityBox: Epēshu and Summarch go in as plain images with w/h. Their POIs are reprojected linearly into the same box, with no control points tying them to the print.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: REGISTRATION gap for the canon charts. A vector layer placed through this same box would misalign the same way.

evidence.quote: registerCityOverlay('Epēshu','art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg',{prov:'canon',w:2863,h:3072,
return px(box.x0+(p.x/pr.w)*box.fw, box.y0+(p.y/pr.h)*box.fh);

votes.corrected: Holds as stated. In maps-site/index.html, registerCityOverlay('Epēshu','art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg',{prov:'canon',w:2863,h:3072,poiRef:...,pois:...}) and the matching Summarch call (w:3072,h:2859) register plain images. registerCityOverlay stores only {url,w,h,prov,provText,poiRef,pois,stubs} and has no georeference or control-point fields. The overlay's placement comes only from cityBox(a,w,h): the anchor dot plus footR(kind), aspect-fit to w/h. Both worldPOICoord and buildWorldPOIs compute px(box.x0+(p.x/pr.w)*box.fw, box.y0+(p.y/pr.h)*box.fh), which is a pure linear scale and offset into that box. A grep of maps-site/index.html finds no GCP, georeference, affine or homography code (the only 'control point' hit is a Catmull-Rom comment). Nuance: the POI coordinates are in the modal chart's pixel space (poiRef = DETAIL['Epēshu'] 3914x4200, DETAIL['Summarch'] 4245x3951), not in the overlay image's own space. The linear mapping is only correct because the aspect ratios agree (2863/3072 ≈ 0.932 ≈ 3914/4200, and 3072/2859 ≈ 1.074 ≈ 4245/3951). The code assumes this and does not check it.
votes.reason: Both quotes exist verbatim in maps-site/index.html (registerCityOverlay at the Epēshu call, and the POI reprojection line inside worldPOICoord and buildWorldPOIs). Reading cityBox, registerCityOverlay and the POI code confirms that placement and POI positions are linear maps into the anchor-centred box. A search turned up no control-point or warp registration code. The claim is slightly loose in that the POIs come from the chart's own pixel space (poiRef), but that does not change the conclusion.

votes.corrected: REGISTRATION gap for the canon charts, verified at HEAD. The only placement Epēshu and Summarch get is cityBox: a box centred on the anchor, with half-size footR(kind) (capital 26 / town 14 world px) fitted to the image's aspect. No control points tie the art to the atlas's coast, rivers or roads. Epēshu's anchor comes from data/city-anchors.json (1236.1, 1415). Summarch's anchor is hand-coded in maps-site/index.html (CITY_ANCHORS['Summarch']={atlasX:523,atlasY:58,kind:'town'...}). In both cases the box is only a size guess, not a fit to the print. POIs are mapped linearly from poiRef (the chart-pyramid size, DETAIL w/h 3914x4200 and 4245x3951) into the same box by worldPOICoord and buildWorldPOIs. So the POIs inherit any misfit in the overlay exactly. Chart mode (enterChart) sits in its own pixel space (map.unproject at def.maxz) and is never registered to the atlas. A vector layer placed through this same cityBox would misalign the same way, so changing the medium does not fix this. The fix is a per-chart fit, stored as data, for the canon entries only. Use 3 or more control points picked on the chart and on the atlas (coast, river mouths, road gates) to fit a north-up scale+translate, or a similarity or affine transform. Then compute the overlay bounds and the POI transform from that fit instead of footR. This bends the art to the atlas, as the rule requires. It is a pure function of data, so determinism holds. It does not need to touch genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask or cityCanvasSha, so the mobile pins are safe. Plain L.imageOverlay only takes axis-aligned bounds, so scale+translate fits it directly. Rotation or affine would need a CSS-matrix overlay or canvas resampling, and that should be weighed against the mobile per-frame budget. Timing: maps-site/index.html is mid-flight in Mobile 5-9, and filigree slice C owns the city look, so this lands as a data and transform change coordinated with those tracks.
votes.reason: Both quotes are verified in the HEAD export's maps-site/index.html. There are no control-point, affine or warp fields in the code or in city-anchors.json. The image sizes are consistent (Epēshu JPEG is 2863 wide x 3072 tall, matching the registered w/h). One nuance: Summarch's anchor is hard-coded in index.html, not in city-anchors.json, but it still goes through cityBox. The applies_to_us framing is correct and keeps registration separate from the rendering medium. Acting on it is correct for this project, under these conditions: the fit is data-driven, the atlas stays authoritative, nothing pinned by hash is touched, and the work is coordinated with the Mobile atlas lane and filigree slice C.

items.summary: Misregistration is largest in the two canon charts (and modal chart pyramids), which only cityBox places; seeded plans use the z5-tile mask from sampleCityMask, but that mask shapes the plan only where the patch holds real sea (drawWater and mask.water), so procedural plans are not registered by construction in general.

prior_record.claim: (b) The seeded plans already fit the atlas coast: sampleCityMask builds a land/water mask from the z5 base tiles, and genCityCanvas spans the central part of that patch. The canon charts get no such fit, and the bible says Epēshu comes from the canon chart, never the generator.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Misregistration is concentrated in the two canon charts (plus the modal chart pyramids). Procedural towns are registered by construction at z5 resolution.

evidence.quote: im.src=tv('tiles/5/'+tx+'/'+ty+'.jpg');
// mask px (z5, canvas spans the central 4rW of the 5.4rW patch)
Epēshu is drawn from the canon chart, never the generator

votes.corrected: All three quotes exist and the first two support the mechanism. In maps-site/index.html, sampleCityMask loads z5 base tiles ('tiles/5/'+tx+'/'+ty+'.jpg') into a patch of 5.4*rW z5 px, and buildCityMask thresholds it into a water mask. genCityCanvas draws the central 4*rW z5 px of that patch, which equals the cityBox footprint of 2*rW atlas px. The mask only shapes the plan when the patch holds real sea (MK is set only if drawWater and mask.water, i.e. at least 2.5% water). Inland and non-coastal seeded plans therefore get no atlas fit beyond that, and the mask covers land/water only (colour thresholds, no rivers or roads). ensureCityGen replaces a registration only when prov==='invented'. The two canon charts (registered with prov 'canon' for 'Epēshu' and 'Summarch') are placed only through cityBox, which centres a box on the anchor with half-size footR(kind) and no coast fitting. The density-bible quote ("Epēshu is drawn from the canon chart, never the generator", row B-33) is about block density and source of the built fill. It is not a statement about registration, so it does not support "canon charts get no such fit". That part rests on the code. Narrowest supported claim: seeded coastal plans get their shoreline from the z5 atlas mask, while canon charts get no coast fit. This does not show that procedural towns are "registered by construction", nor that misregistration is "concentrated" in the canon charts, because inland plans, rivers and roads are not fitted and the evidence never measured where misregistration sits.
votes.reason: The quotes are real and the mask mechanism is correctly described. The claim overreaches in two places. The bible quote is about block density, not registration. "Registered by construction" and "misregistration concentrated in the canon charts" go beyond coast-only, sea-in-patch-only fitting, and the evidence contains no measurement of where misregistration sits.

votes.corrected: The REGISTRATION gap is largest in the two canon charts (overlay-Epeshu.jpg and overlay-Summarch.jpg, plus the modal chart pyramids under charts/epeshu and charts/summarch). They are placed only by cityBox, a FOOT_R box centred on the anchor dot, so nothing ties their coast, rivers or roads to the atlas. Fixing that means bending the art to the atlas, for example with a control-point fit per chart. It does not mean regenerating Epēshu, because the density bible (B-33) says Epēshu is drawn from the canon chart, never the generator. Seeded plans are registered only partly, and only for the coast. In genCityCanvas the coast comes from the z5 sampleCityMask patch. drawImage crops the central 4rW z5 px, which is exactly the 2r world-px cityBox square, so that coast lines up by construction. That holds only when all of these are true: drawWater is on (harbor, or sea distPx<=25), the mask reads water (frac>=0.025), and the tiles have loaded. Before the tiles load, ensureCityGenNow on a deep link registers the synthetic compass shoreline and hot-swaps it later. Inland towns never use the mask. Even when the coast is registered it is coarse: 2 mask px per world px, so a capital is about 104 mask px stretched to GEN_SIZE, and the water/land split is a colour threshold in buildCityMask. Rivers are not registered at all. In traits.river mode 'through' the flow bearing is R()*2π, and in 'beside' it follows the sea vector; neither is fitted to the atlas's solid-black rivers. Roads are registered only by bearing. Gates come from the land-approach route legs, and buildCityStubs ends each stub at 1.18·footR along that bearing, not on a vertex of a drawn atlas road. So a rebuild in a vector medium would still need the same per-feature registration work for seeded towns' rivers and roads, and for inland towns, as the canon charts need. The z5 mask idea is reusable only for seeded coasts, and any change to genCityCanvas, sampleCityMask or washMake breaks the UG3 atlas_fn_sha and cityCanvasSha pins, so it has to be coordinated with the mobile atlas lane and with filigree slice C.
votes.reason: The quoted code is accurate, and the main point carries over to our stack. sampleCityMask loads z5 tiles over a 5.4rW patch, and genCityCanvas draws the central 4rW of it, which matches the cityBox 2r world square. The canon charts get only cityBox, and density-bible B-33 forbids generating Epēshu. So it is right that the canon charts are where the REGISTRATION work matters most. But "procedural towns are registered by construction" overstates it. (1) The mask drives the coast only when drawWater is on and mask.water is set; inland towns, and deep links before the tiles load (ensureCityGenNow), get the synthetic shoreline. (2) Rivers are seeded: R()*2π, or the sea-vector bearing for 'beside' mode. Nothing fits them to the atlas's black river lines. (3) Roads match only by bearing: buildCityStubs stops at 1.18·footR on the gate angle and shares no vertices with the atlas roads. (4) The mask is coarse (z5, colour-threshold water). Acting on the claim as written would tell us to fix only the canon charts and leave the seeded towns' river and road misalignment in place. A rebuild in a vector medium would not fix that either. Anything that touches the coast-fit code also has to respect the UG3 and cityCanvasSha pins.

F10 holds the Epēshu anchor
the frozen `gates/hexes.json` and `gates/hex/*.jpg` are skipped, never regenerated

items.summary: Changing an anchor or FOOT_R changes the seeded canvas via sampleCityMask's patch and genCityCanvas's crop, so canon registration should be a separate per-city transform applied where cityBox/cityMaxZ place the overlay, leaving the inputs to the pinned generator unchanged.

prior_record.claim: (b) Moving an anchor or a FOOT_R value changes the seeded canvas: sampleCityMask centres its patch on the anchor with radius footR, and genCityCanvas scales by footR. That changes cityCanvasSha and fails UG3.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Registration must leave FOOT_R and the anchors untouched.

evidence.quote: var a=CITY_ANCHORS[key],rW=footR(a.kind);
var scl=S/(2*footR(a.kind)), stubs=[];
cityCanvasSha is equal to B0 **and equal across all five profiles**

votes.corrected: All three quotes exist in HEAD. Changing a city's anchor or its FOOT_R value changes the seeded canvas through sampleCityMask, because that function builds its patch from the anchor and footR(a.kind): ox,oy = (atlasX or atlasY - 1.35*rW)*2 and n = 5.4*rW. The patch's mask supplies the sampled land hue and, for water cities, the coast. genCityCanvas then reads the mask again with a crop based on rW and the anchor, via drawImage((a.atlasX-rW)*2-MK.ox, ...). The hash the capture tool uses (R.cityCanvasSha) covers the data-URL canvas of only Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae, so UG3 fails only if such a change alters one of those three canvases (the gate also requires the diff to leave the five named functions untouched). The cited line `var scl=S/(2*footR(a.kind))` does not support the claim that the canvas scales by footR. scl is used only to build the stubs (atlas-coordinate road stubs), and the stubs are not part of the hashed canvas. The "fails UG3" step is also conditional, since it depends on those three cities and on a change that actually alters their canvases.
votes.reason: The sampleCityMask quote and the gates.md quote are accurate (maps-site/index.html sampleCityMask; docs/mobile/gates.md UG3). The genCityCanvas scl quote only feeds stubs (the stubs block, via `var scl=`). The hashed canvas depends on footR and the anchor through the mask patch and the mask crop inside genCityCanvas (`var WD=null,wAt=null,rW=footR(a.kind)` and the drawImage at (a.atlasX-rW)*2-MK.ox), which the cited evidence does not show. tools/mobile-capture.js hashes only Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae, so the UG3 failure is scoped to those cities. The practical conclusion that registration must leave FOOT_R and the anchors alone while the mobile atlas lane is mid-flight is sound. The wording overreaches the quoted lines.

votes.corrected: The mechanism is real but narrower than the claim says. Registration should not fix misalignment by editing FOOT_R or by moving anchors to match the art. It should fit the canon art to the atlas with a separate per-city transform or bounds (for example a control-point fit), applied where cityBox/cityMaxZ place the overlay, so the inputs to genCityCanvas and sampleCityMask stay unchanged. While the mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) is in flight, UG3 also forbids any edit to FOOT_R or to the anchor or kind of an invented city in the capture set: that set is Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae, plus any invented city left in cityReg. Correcting an anchor that is wrong against the atlas ring-dot is allowed under the rule "bend art to the atlas". It just has to wait until after the lane, or be declared as a deliberate re-baseline of B0 cityCanvasSha. Canon-art cities (Epēshu, Summarch) are not in cityCanvasSha. Data edits never trip the atlas_fn_sha source pins.
votes.reason:
The quotes check out in maps-site/index.html. In sampleCityMask, `var a=CITY_ANCHORS[key],rW=footR(a.kind);` sets the z5 tile patch (ox and oy from atlasX/Y minus 1.35*rW, n=5.4*rW). genCityCanvas sets `rW=footR(a.kind)` for the mask mapping, and buildCityStubs uses `scl=S/(2*footR(a.kind))`. So the anchor and FOOT_R do feed the seeded procedural canvas, and changing them changes its pixels.

The claim overreaches in three ways:
(1) tools/mobile-capture.js hashes only cityReg entries with `prov === 'invented'` and a data: URL. It descends into Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae and hashes every invented city then in cityReg. The DM canon overlays (overlay-Epeshu.jpg, overlay-Summarch.jpg), which are where the visible misalignment matters, are not in cityCanvasSha. Moving their anchors or registering them does not fail UG3.
(2) atlas_fn_sha hashes function source only. Editing city-anchors.json or the FOOT_R table changes no pinned source, so that part of UG3 is not affected.
(3) "Must leave untouched" is wrong as a permanent rule. B0 is a gate baseline for the mobile lane. After the lane, or with a declared re-baseline, an anchor correction toward the atlas ring-dot is legitimate and fits the authority rule.

The useful takeaway still holds. Registration is a placement problem: cityBox places every overlay through footR(a.kind) whatever the image shows. The right fix is a separate per-city registration transform used only for overlay placement, not a reuse of FOOT_R. That leaves both seeded generation and the pins alone. A vector city placed through the same cityBox would misalign in the same way.

items.summary: UG3's atlas_fn_sha hashes only xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask, so a change confined to cityBox or registerCityOverlay leaves it intact; this is a blind spot in the gate, not a safe route to plan around.

prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Registration shipped default-on must declare the city-zoom regions in an accept file.

evidence.quote: Metrics equal the reference except the unit's declared keys; shots differ ≤ 0.5% outside the declared regions

votes.corrected: UG8 (docs/mobile/gates.md) requires desktop (1366x768@1, 1440x900@2) metrics to equal the reference except the unit's declared keys, and shots to differ by at most 0.5% outside the declared regions. Regions are rectangles listed under `mask` in the unit's accept file (docs/mobile/metrics.md). The gate is therefore real, and an accept-file `mask` is the mechanism for declaring regions. The cited quote does not support "moving the canon overlays is a declared-region change". The desktop atlas shots are 1-contents, 2-whole-chart, 3-layers and 4-place-card, taken in tools/mobile-capture.js. The place-card shot is taken at minZoom+2.6, about z4.6, well below the overlay fade-in (overlayOpacity returns 0 for z<=6.8 in maps-site/index.html). The city-zoom `ATLAS.descend` step comes after all atlas shots and feeds only the cityCanvasSha hash. So no UG8 shot shows a city overlay, and re-registering overlays at city zoom would leave every UG8 shot unchanged. It would need no shot mask unless the change also moves pixels in those four views (base, markers or wash). The gates it would touch are the UG3 cityCanvasSha and the declared-keys metric rule. Narrowest supported claim: UG8 fails a unit whose desktop shots differ by more than 0.5% outside accept-file `mask` rectangles. No current UG8 shot reaches city zoom, so city-overlay registration alone does not require declaring city-zoom regions. Adding city-zoom shot views (via `shot_views`) would be a separate choice.
votes.reason: The gates.md quote exists and states the 0.5% rule, but the claim's inference overreaches. The capture tool's shot list (contents, whole-chart, layers, place-card at about z4.6) never views an overlay (opacity 0 at z<=6.8), so moving canon overlays is not a declared-region change under UG8, and the applies_to_us advice to declare city-zoom regions is unsupported.

votes.corrected: UG8 is a gate on Mobile-track units only. mobile-build runs it through tools/mobile-capture.js --accept against B0. Registration work would be an atlas or filigree item, not a Mobile unit, so it gets no Mobile accept file and UG8 never scores it. Even if it did, none of the baseline's atlas desktop shots show a city overlay, so moving the overlays changes no UG8 pixels and there is no region to declare. The four desktop/desktop2x atlas views are 1-contents, 2-whole-chart, 3-layers and 4-place-card (the place card is taken at minZoom+2.6). The overlay only fades in at z6.8-7.8. The real cross-track duty is different. Registration must not touch xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask, and must not change cityCanvasSha (UG3 atlas pins). It must not call createPane (UG7). It must not land in maps-site/index.html while the Mobile 5-9 atlas lane is mid-flight. After it lands, the central session re-takes B0 or R1, or a later Mobile unit lists the changed metric keys in declared_change_keys (for example a tap_fixture view), instead of masking regions. A city-zoom shot would change almost the whole frame, and --lint-accept rejects any mask covering more than 35% of the viewport, so a region mask could not cover it anyway.
votes.reason:
The quote is accurate. docs/mobile/gates.md UG8 says "shots differ ≤ 0.5% outside the declared regions", and tools/mobile-capture.js gateResults adds 'UG8.<surface>.<profile>.shot_diff' when sd.diff > 0.005. Declared regions are the accept file's `mask` rectangles (metrics.md section 'Declared regions are rectangles in the accept file (mask)'). The conclusion drawn from it fails on three counts.
(1) Scope. UG1-UG11 are the per-unit gates of the mobile-build loop, scored by `--accept` on Mobile units. Registration of the canon overlays is atlas work owned by the filigree and atlas side, with no Mobile accept file. The gate does not bind it.
(2) No shot sees it. Per docs/mobile/baseline.json, the atlas shots on every profile are 1-contents, 2-whole-chart, 3-layers and 4-place-card. tapAtZoom('Epēshu', 2.6) puts the card shot far below where overlayOpacity fades the pCity overlay in (z6.8-7.8). A change to cityBox bounds or to the overlay registration leaves every UG8 pixel identical. Note that TAP_VIEWS includes 'city_z6.15' for the tap fixture, but that records glyph taps, not overlay pixels.
(3) Masks can't do it. A city-zoom view would differ over nearly the whole frame. lintAccept rejects any mask with rect w*h > 0.35*viewport, so 'declare the city-zoom regions' is not even expressible. The project's real mechanism for an intended change is declared_change_keys or a re-baseline (B0/R1) done centrally.
The binding constraints for registration are the UG3 atlas pins (genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask, cityCanvasSha) and UG7 (no createPane), plus sequencing behind the Mobile 5-9 lane. Acting on the claim as written would add pointless accept-file ceremony and miss those real pins.

items.summary: Mobile 6's A-U11 requires the final max-zoom shot to equal R1 and the registerCityOverlay literal to be kept, so changing the canon overlay calls or their placement collides with it until A-U11 has passed; it is a sequencing rule, not a permanent ban.

prior_record.claim: (b) Mobile 6's unit A-U11 (720 px overlay previews) pins the overlay's final shot to R1 and keeps the registerCityOverlay literal. Moving the overlay before A-U11 lands would collide with its acceptance.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Registration waits until after Mobile 6 at minimum, and in practice after Mobile 9.

evidence.quote: after load the full image is the same file and the final shot equals R1 at max zoom; registerCityOverlay literal kept

Moving the Epēshu/Summarch overlay, or changing their registerCityOverlay('Epēshu','art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg',{prov:'canon',w:2863,h:3072,...}) calls (for example to add control points), would break that acceptance. votes.reason: The quote is checked against the HEAD export: A-U11's fourth acceptance line in docs/mobile/units.json pins the final shot to R1 and keeps the registerCityOverlay literal. docs/mobile/state.json shows R1 as a pinned baseline and the item still at Mobile 5, so the lane is open. items.summary: Filigree and street scripts and mobile UG4 check the flag-1 literals 'function registerCityOverlay', 'function washMake', 'function sampleCityMask' and 'function genCityCanvas' (among others) by indexOf, so any rework adds code and never renames them.

prior_record.claim: (b) The filigree scripts anchor on the literals of the four city functions (flag 1), and UG4 requires every flag-1 anchor to resolve. Renaming or removing them throws "anchor lost".
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Any registration or vector rework keeps those four function names.

evidence.quote: ['maps-site/index.html', 'function registerCityOverlay', 1]
Every flag-1 anchor of the eight scripts is found.

votes.corrected: The claim holds as stated. In .claude/workflows/filigree-2-plan.js, the ANCHORS table lists ['maps-site/index.html', 'function registerCityOverlay', 1], plus 'function washMake', 'function sampleCityMask' and 'function genCityCanvas', all flagged 1. The same table also holds other flag-1 literals, such as 'function xmur3', 'function mulberry32', 'var Z_STREET=', 'function worldOpacityUpdate' and 'window.ATLAS=', so the four city functions are only a subset. A flag-1 literal that is not found makes anchorsLost() non-empty, and the script then calls die('anchor lost: ...'), which throws an Error. The other three filigree scripts (1, 3 and 4) have the same die('anchor lost') check. docs/mobile/gates.md row UG4 reads "Every flag-1 anchor of the eight scripts is found.", and mobile-build.js says to keep every flag-1 literal ("add, never rename"). One nuance: the match is on the literal text 'function <name>', so what breaks is renaming or removing that declaration text.
votes.reason: Both quotes exist verbatim in the HEAD export. The first is at filigree-2-plan.js line 112 (the ANCHORS table, flag 1). The second is in docs/mobile/gates.md under UG4. The four city functions are all present as flag-1 anchors (washMake, sampleCityMask and genCityCanvas at line 113). die() throws an Error, and the 'anchor lost' check also appears in the other filigree scripts. All four functions are also defined in maps-site/index.html.

votes.corrected: Any registration or vector rework keeps the four declaration literals 'function registerCityOverlay', 'function washMake', 'function sampleCityMask' and 'function genCityCanvas' in maps-site/index.html. All eight filigree and street scripts plus the mobile UG4 gate check these with String.indexOf. The rule for these scripts is add, never rename. A rework goes into new functions or into non-pinned code such as cityBox, registerCityOverlay's body and worldCityUpdate. The bodies of genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask are also frozen: UG3 atlas_fn_sha says the diff touches none of them, and cityCanvasSha must stay equal to B0. Changing that pinned code needs an owner-approved re-pin coordinated with the mobile atlas lane, not a silent edit.
votes.reason:
Verified in the HEAD export, and the claim is correct.

1. **The anchors exist as described.** Every filigree script (filigree-1..4-research/plan/build/review.js) has an ANCHORS list. It includes ['maps-site/index.html','function registerCityOverlay',1], 'function washMake', 'function sampleCityMask' and 'function genCityCanvas', all with flag 1. `anchorsLost` keeps the flag-1 entries whose literal was not found. The preflight then calls `die('anchor lost: ...')`, which appears in all four filigree scripts and the street scripts.

2. **UG4 enforces them.** docs/mobile/gates.md UG4 says "Every flag-1 anchor of the eight scripts is found." mobile-build.js tells implementers to "add, never rename", and mobile-review.js treats a broken flag-1 anchor as a blocker.

3. **Two refinements to applies_to_us.**
   - The check is a plain String.indexOf on the declaration literal. Only the `function X` text has to survive; the check does not inspect the body.
   - The body constraint is stricter than the claim implies. UG3 says "the diff touches none of xmur3, mulberry32, genCityCanvas, washMake or sampleCityMask", and captures pin the atlas_fn_sha source hashes. cityCanvasSha must also equal B0 on all five profiles. So keeping only the names is not enough: three of the four functions are frozen in content too.

4. **What that means for the alignment work.** The registration fix (bending art to the atlas through control points or an affine/TPS fit in place of the FOOT_R box) has to live in new functions or in non-pinned code: cityBox, registerCityOverlay's body, worldCityUpdate. A vector city layer should likewise be a new, added function.

5. **Clarifications.** The anchor check fires only when a workflow's preflight runs, not on page load. Mobile 5-9 is mid-flight, so any edit to the pinned code must wait for or coordinate with that lane.

items.summary: R21 and B-32 give a process carrier for a registration item (recorded and queued above the job it blocks), but R21 names three items today and a 'Filigree data —' title has side effects, so it is a queueing route, not a fix.

prior_record.claim: (b) On the filigree side the natural carriers for a chart-to-print mismatch are R21 and B-32 (data truth): such contradictions are recorded and queued directly above the job they block.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Registration fits as a data-truth item that blocks Filigree 3's city slice. This is an interpretation: R21 names three specific items today.

evidence.quote: recorded and queued directly above the job they block; canon notes are never edited by these jobs
Named layers are built only from data that matches the print

votes.corrected: Both quotes exist. README R21: "recorded and queued directly above the job they block; canon notes are never edited by these jobs". density-bible B-32: "Named layers are built only from data that matches the print". Together they support this much: the filigree track records data contradictions between canon or notes and the print, queues them above the filigree job they block, and never edits canon notes. R21 names exactly three items (Aldorūs "out of sight of the sea" vs sea 77 px NE, Drāmūz marker 35 px off, Hordon/Maeges anchor), and B-32 repeats the same three. Neither mentions chart-to-print or registration mismatch, and neither mentions the city slice. B-32 says what waits is Job 3 slice B (named things from data), not slice C (city). So the claim that R21 and B-32 are the "natural carriers" for a chart-to-print mismatch, and that it blocks Filigree 3's city slice, is the proposer's inference, not something the sources say. Narrowest supportable form: the filigree docs set a precedent for queueing data contradictions directly above the job they block. Adding registration to that process would be a new R21 item or ruling, and which slice it blocks would be a new decision.
votes.reason: The quotes are real and the procedure claim is accurate. The "natural carrier" claim overreaches: R21 and B-32 cover only three named data contradictions and tie slice B, not the city slice, to the data-truth wait. The proposer's own applies_to_us text already concedes this is an interpretation.

votes.corrected:
It partly applies, as a process carrier and not as a fix. Both quotes are accurate. docs/filigree/README.md R21 ("recorded and queued directly above the job they block; canon notes are never edited by these jobs") and density-bible.md B-32 ("Named layers are built only from data that matches the print") do give a valid way to queue a city-art REGISTRATION item. It would be a central, hand-queued POLISH entry, "- [ ] **Filigree data — city art registration (Epēshu, Summarch)**", placed directly above "Filigree 3 · Implementation → the table map". The density bible's "Blocks" column ("the earliest slice that cannot be built without the item (R11, R21)") would name slice C city as the slice it blocks. Slices A ground and B ink are unaffected.

Four caveats change what that means:
(1) R21 is a closed list today: the Drāmūz marker, the Hordon/Maeges anchor and the Aldorūs sea note. Those are canon DATA that contradicts the print. The city misfit is mostly a CODE/geometry defect: cityBox centres a box of FOOT_R[kind] half-size on the anchor, whatever the art depicts. Calling it "data truth" is an interpretation. The data part is narrower: per-city control points or a transform beside city-anchors.json, which the owner or the central session adds.
(2) The automated route is Job 2's polish_inserts, which takes only items from its /prerequisites section. Filigree 2 has not run (there is no docs/filigree/gates/2-plan.json). Until it does, someone has to queue the item by hand. Job 2 skips an item only when the exact title "Filigree data — <item>" is already in POLISH.md, so the hand-queued title has to match that form.
(3) Queueing changes no alignment. Slice C's gates (README G3.C1–C9: pins, labels, fog, pooled-edge band) do not test registration. Slice C reuses registerCityOverlay, genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask, which sit on whatever bounds cityBox gives. The item therefore needs its own acceptance test, for example the art's coast, river and gate points within N atlas px of the print. It also has to bend the art to the atlas, never the atlas to the art.
(4) The fix has to work through overlay bounds or a transform, without changing canvas bytes. The mobile track pins genCityCanvas, washMake and sampleCityMask by source sha (UG3), and pins cityCanvasSha. Its atlas lane (Mobile 5–9) is also mid-flight in maps-site/index.html, so the item must not run beside it.

Switching the medium to a vector city does not help unless it uses the same registration. A vector city placed through cityBox misaligns exactly as the raster does.
votes.reason:
Checked in the HEAD export:
- R21 is in README §9 and B-32 in density-bible.md and .json. The README §10 row reads "Data items Jobs 1–2 find (R21: …) | the job they block".
- workflow-2-plan.md defines polish_inserts as "Filigree data — …" items placed directly above Filigree 3. Filigree 2 is unchecked in POLISH.md, and gates/ holds no 2-plan.json.
- The density bible says Blocks is the earliest slice that cannot be built without the item.

So the carrier exists and can name slice C, and the claim's own hedge ("an interpretation") is correct. What it overstates:
- R21 lists three print-vs-data contradictions. The city misfit sits mainly in cityBox placement logic, not in contradictory canon data.
- The only automated insert path, Job 2, has not run. The item would be queued by hand.
- Queueing fixes nothing. Slice C's gates (G3.C1–C9) don't measure registration, so the item needs its own acceptance test.
- It must respect the mobile sha pins (genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask, cityCanvasSha) and the in-flight Mobile 5–9 lane. That is why the fix has to go through bounds or a transform rather than canvas changes.

It transfers as a way to queue and sequence the work, not as an alignment fix, so it holds with corrections.

items.summary: Refuted: B-38 chooses between the sim DEM shore and the chart coast, not the print, so it does not conflict with atlas authority as stated (later superseded by gap-coasts tc-6).

prior_record.claim: (b) The bible's B-38 clips the city contours to the chart's own coast where the DEM shore disagrees, and records a gap of up to 10 atlas px. That treats the chart as truth on the city sheet, which is in tension with the rule that the atlas is authoritative.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Once the chart is registered to the print, B-38's chart coast and the atlas coast converge. Changing B-38 itself means re-integrating the bible (Path B).

evidence.quote: smoothed, and clipped to the chart's own coast where the DEM shore disagrees with it.
(the DEM shore runs up to 10 atlas px off in the south)

votes.corrected: Both quotes exist in docs/filigree/density-bible.md. B-38 (the Sheet-spec row at "| B-38 | contour hills |") says the city-sheet contour hills are taken from the DEM, smoothed, and "clipped to the chart's own coast where the DEM shore disagrees with it". The ground-truth row ("| contour_hill | B-38 |") records that "the DEM shore runs up to 10 atlas px off in the south". The supported claim is narrower: the bible resolves a DEM-versus-chart coast mismatch on the contour layer in favour of the chart's coast, with an observed offset of up to 10 atlas px in the south. The bible never compares the chart coast with the atlas coast, and it never says the atlas is wrong or the chart authoritative. The gap is between the DEM shore and the chart. Whether this conflicts with "atlas is authoritative" is the reviewer's inference, not something the bible states. It only matters if the DEM shore is the atlas coast, or if the chart coast is itself off the atlas. This is not established by the cited text, and the chart is DM-drawn canon.
votes.reason: Both quotes are present and the factual part (clip to the chart coast, DEM shore up to 10 atlas px off in the south) is accurate. The claim overreaches in two places. It calls the 10 px gap one between the chart and the atlas, but the bible measures the DEM shore against the chart. It also says the clip "treats the chart as truth ... in tension with" atlas authority, which the bible does not state. That conflict is inferred and unverified. No part of the cited text links the DEM shore or the chart coast to the atlas coast.

votes.corrected: B-38 does not conflict with the rule that the atlas is authoritative, so it should not be changed and needs no Path B re-integration. The two coasts B-38 chooses between are the sim's DEM shore and the chart's coast. The sim DEM is the heightfield embedded as index.html :: const EPESHU_HF_URI and read through tools/filigree-dem.js; density-bible.md calls it "the probe on the raw decode". The PatrinorModern print is not part of that choice. The sim DEM is derived data, not canon, so it should lose to drawn ink either way. The "up to 10 atlas px" figure is a DEM-versus-chart gap, not an error in the chart's position on the atlas. B-38 is a consistency rule for drawing the city sheet: contour hair must not run into water on the painted chart the reader is looking at. If registration later warps the chart onto the print coast, the clip should use the coast of the registered chart, so it follows the chart and the print with no change to the rule. Registration fixes misalignment. Rendering the contours as raster or vector has no effect on it. The open question belongs to registration, not to B-38: after the chart is warped, does any remaining chart-versus-print gap matter? If one is still visible, the fix is to register the chart better, not to edit the bible.
votes.reason: B-38 in density-bible.md says the contours are "clipped to the chart's own coast where the DEM shore disagrees with it". The contour_hill row explains the gap as "the DEM shore runs up to 10 atlas px off" the Epēshu chart coast. Here "DEM" means the sim heightfield sampled by tools/filigree-dem.js, which density-bible.md defines as "dem = the probe on the raw decode"; the bible defines print ink on the PatrinorModern crop as a different source. So B-38 never ranks the chart above the atlas print. It ranks drawn chart ink above a derived sim heightfield. That fits the owner's rule that DM art is canon and does not break the rule that the atlas is authoritative. The claim's applies_to_us has two problems. First, it says the chart coast and the atlas coast "converge" after registration, which mixes up the DEM shore with the atlas coast; the DEM gap could remain even then. Second, it says B-38 needs Path B re-integration, and nothing needs re-integrating. Acting on the claim by rewriting B-38 to clip to the DEM or the print would put contours on water in the painted chart and churn a rule from the filigree track that the owner already ruled on, for no gain in alignment.

items.summary: 'Region-chart zoom-through' is an open evaluate item gating F3-D (bible lettering) for region MapArt; city registration should be a reusable placement primitive that item can adopt later, not scoped together with it.

prior_record.claim: (b) The queued "Region-chart zoom-through" owns footprint-anchoring of the REGION charts only (not the cities). It is the sibling of city registration, and the bible lists it as blocking F3-D.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: City registration should share its placement mechanism with this item, or be scoped together with it.

evidence.quote: **Region-chart zoom-through** — evaluate footprint-anchoring the REGION MapArt
| Region-chart zoom-through | F3-D | open |

votes.corrected: Both quotes exist verbatim. POLISH.md has an open item, "Region-chart zoom-through", which says to "evaluate footprint-anchoring the REGION MapArt (Rhusagos, Relkor…) at mid zooms the way cities anchor at street zooms; keep modal where the geometry doesn't fit". docs/filigree/density-bible.md, in its Prerequisites table, lists "Region-chart zoom-through | F3-D | open". F3-D is "city grain, plates and the final gate". The bible's wording is that the item "blocks" the earliest slice that cannot be built without it. The narrowest supported claim: an open POLISH item asks to evaluate footprint-anchoring region MapArt at mid zooms, modelled on how cities anchor at street zooms, and the density bible lists it as a prerequisite that blocks filigree slice F3-D. The evidence does not support three parts of the claim. (1) "Owns ... only (not the cities)": the item says "evaluate", so it is a scoped evaluation and not an owner of a build. It concerns region MapArt, but nothing in the text excludes cities or assigns them elsewhere. A grep of POLISH.md finds no separate city-registration item. (2) "Sibling of city registration": the item only uses city anchoring as an analogy ("the way cities anchor"). It does not say it shares a mechanism with city registration or that the two are related items. (3) The "owner of region anchoring" framing is the lens's inference, not something the sources state.
votes.reason: The two quotes are accurate and the F3-D blocking status is confirmed. The claim overreaches in "owns ... only (not the cities)" and "sibling of city registration". The POLISH item only says "evaluate" region-chart footprint-anchoring, using the way cities anchor as an analogy. It says nothing about owning region anchoring or excluding cities.

votes.corrected: City registration should be built as a reusable placement primitive in maps-site/index.html (anchor/control-point fit that replaces the cityBox footprint box, so art is bent to the atlas coast, rivers and roads) which the "Region-chart zoom-through" item can later adopt for the REGION MapArt. Do not scope the two together: the region item is only an "evaluate" entry that gates filigree slice F3-D, and tying the city fix to it would hold the owner's city misalignment fix behind the filigree queue. Its own wording, footprint-anchoring "the way cities anchor at street zooms", is a warning, not a model to copy. Done through today's FOOT_R box, region art would misalign the same way the cities do, whether it is raster or vector. Fixing registration first and sharing that mechanism avoids building the error twice.
votes.reason: The facts check out at HEAD. POLISH.md has "- [ ] **Region-chart zoom-through** — evaluate footprint-anchoring the REGION MapArt (Rhusagos, Relkor…) at mid zooms the way cities anchor at street zooms; keep modal where the geometry doesn't fit". The density-bible.md Prerequisites table lists "| Region-chart zoom-through | F3-D | open |". docs/living/research-dossier.md also says to specify the zoom-through handoff "together with" this item. So "region only, sibling of city registration, blocks F3-D" is accurate. The applies_to_us line is half right. Sharing the mechanism is right, because the item copies city anchoring, and city anchoring today is the cityBox/FOOT_R footprint box, which ignores what the image shows. That box is the cause of the shift the owner reports, so a region copy of it would inherit the misalignment. "Or be scoped together" is wrong for this project. The region item is an open "evaluate" prerequisite owned by the filigree queue (slice F3-D), while city registration is an atlas fix to the city overlays the owner asked for directly. Bundling them would put the city fix behind filigree gating and widen its scope across tracks. The right order: build registration as a primitive that bends art to the authoritative atlas, then let the region item adopt it. A long-press (Leaflet 600 ms) shows the name only and opens no card. Faded or tier-hidden glyphs, including any during the z6.8-7.8 overlayOpacity crossfade, never take a tap. Glyph centres are anchored to registered geometry (the printed badges or atlas features), not to cityBox placement. Registration, not the medium, keeps those 22 px hits on target. Making each vector building or street a tappable target would turn a dense city into a near-constant chooser. Any per-building hit layer is therefore a new filigree ruling the owner must sign off, not something R7 already allows.

items.summary: A vector city should take its road-to-gate tie points from the atlas's traced approaches (cityApproaches feeding mkGate); agreement with the sim's s.entries has not been measured and only the atlas side applies now.

prior_record.claim: City gates and road entries are a further surface where the apps must agree. The atlas generator opens gates where its approach bearings meet each city (Route continuity, done). The sim derives s.entries from where W.roads cross 0.92 R. Agreement between the two has not been measured.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Parts (b) and (c): road-to-gate tie points are shared vertices that a vector city should take from the traced road network, and the sim's entries should match them. That REGISTRATION needs measuring; this report does not claim they agree today.

if(entry) s.entries.push({x:entry.x, z:entry.z});

Its one measured example is Tamaron's Sun-Road gate, which points at Epēshu within 3.6 degrees, so "exactly" is the log's wording and not a measured claim for every city. In index.html, registerRoadEntries pushes `s.entries.push({x:entry.x, z:entry.z})`. The entry is the first road point (from-end) or last road point (to-end) lying beyond 0.92*s.R from the settlement centre. It runs for generated roads and for new village roads. The atlas side is maps-site/index.html buildApprPolys and the "per-city approach bearings" block. Its input polylines are party route legs, named ways and sea lanes, and the bearing is where each one crosses a 2.5x-footprint radius around the anchor. The sim's W.roads are A* roads it generates itself (roadAstar then chaikin), not those atlas polylines. So the two sides use different data and different crossing radii, and I found no measured comparison of atlas gates against sim s.entries in docs, POLISH.md or tools at HEAD. Narrowest supported claim: the atlas opens gates at approach bearings from route, way and lane polylines. The sim derives s.entries from its own A* road crossings at 0.92R. Their agreement is unmeasured, and for non-canon seeds the two networks are independent.

The claim hedges that agreement is unmeasured, and a search of the HEAD docs, POLISH.md and tools found no such measurement. votes.corrected:
Only part (b) applies, and only on the atlas side. When a vector city is built, it should take its road-to-gate tie points from the traced world polylines. The atlas already does this: in maps-site/index.html, cityApproaches(name) supplies landAppr, and `landAppr.forEach(function(b){gates.push(mkGate(b,true));})` turns each approach into a primary gate. A vector plan should reuse these as shared vertices. Like any other geometry, they are only as well registered as the anchor-to-art transform that places the city. Today that transform is cityBox, not the gates.

Part (c), matching the sim's s.entries to the atlas gates, does not apply to this alignment problem and should not be a work item here. The sim builds its road network independently. In index.html, genRoads runs roadAstar as a nearest-connected spanning tree over its own heightfield, then adds one loop road between the first two towns. The settlement grid points (gridX/gridZ) come from buildEpeshuMapData, which carries no roads. registerRoadEntries then takes the first point past s.R*0.92. So the two apps do not share a road graph, a set of approach bearings, or a city plan. The sim's Epēshu is planStreetsFor spokes, not the DM art or genCityCanvas. "Measuring agreement" would therefore compare two unrelated networks. Making them agree would mean feeding atlas roads into CUSTOM_MAP_DATA and changing W.roads, which would shift every sim fingerprint. That work belongs to the living track (the H2z zoom-through hand-off) and the street track (Epēshu streets), not to the atlas registration fix. At most, add a note for the living track that entries may need an atlas-px to sim-grid transform at the zoom-through seam.

In index.html, W.roads come from genRoads, which runs roadAstar over the sim's own cost grid and links each settlement to its nearest already-connected settlement. They do not come from the atlas world polylines, and CUSTOM_MAP_DATA (buildEpeshuMapData) supplies no roads. registerRoadEntries simply takes the first road point past s.R*0.92, and planStreetsFor builds the sim town from those entries, independently of the atlas art. Expecting the sim's entries to match the atlas gates assumes a shared road network and coordinate frame that do not exist. Forcing them to match would change sim roads, which conflicts with determinism and the street and living tracks' ownership. It also does nothing for the owner's complaint, which is about atlas zoom alignment. At most it is a later continuity check for the living track's H2z hand-off.
