prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Part (c), sim side: putting a sim street plan on DM-chart geometry should be queued like LC17: owner-ruled, after Street 4 and the street hold, keeping existing rng draws.

evidence.quote: A world-generation change to #s=epeshu re-baselines every frozen fingerprint (mobile, street, living), so it is never a default

votes.corrected: LC17 (the sim dragon) is open and owner-gated (docs/living/rulings.json: "gated": true, overrides {} and confirmed [] are empty), and its "why" reads "A world-generation change to #s=epeshu re-baselines every frozen fingerprint (mobile, street, living), so it is never a default; it edits index.html, so it waits for Street 4 and the street hold; any build keeps the pick(dR, …) draw". Precedent only: a change to Epēshu street planning (planStreetsFor runs inside world gen with the seeded R) would be a world-generation change and, by this rule, should be queued the same way. That extension is an inference from the ruling, not something the ruling says about streets.
votes.reason: The quote is verbatim in docs/living/rulings.json (LC17 "why"). LC17 is gated: true, and overrides and confirmed are empty, so it is open. The "Street 4 and the street hold" wait is in the same text. The one stretch is that LC17 is about the dragon, not streets; applying it to re-planning Epēshu's streets is the claim's own inference. It is reasonable, because planStreetsFor(s, R) is called from the world-gen code in index.html, but the ruling does not name streets.

votes.corrected: Part (c), sim side, registration rather than medium: laying the sim's Epēshu street plan onto DM-chart geometry changes #s=epeshu world generation, so it follows the LC17 path. It is an owner-gated "later" item (never a default) that edits index.html, so it waits for Street 4 to pass and the street hold to clear (docs/street/README.md §1.3) and runs when no mobile-build is live. It records the re-baseline it causes for each consumer (docs/mobile/baseline.json B0, captures/R1.json, final.json, docs/street/gates/baseline.json and the frozen SV1-SV8 views, maps-site/living/traffic.json) and never hand-edits them. It belongs to the street track's ownership of Epēshu's streets and buildings (ST2/ST12, the street-data anchors `s.streets.push` and `{name:'Epēshīn Forum'`), not the living track. Unlike LC17, "keep the existing rng draws" is not enough. planStreetsFor(s, R) and the later building and lane growth (tryGrowBuildings, the `s.streets.push({pts:lane` path) all draw from the shared W.rng.gen stream, and geometry-dependent rejection sampling changes how many draws are taken. The build must still consume Epēshu's original planStreetsFor draws, then lay the chart plan and its lots from a separate keyed stream (makeStream-style, keyed on W.seed and 'epeshu-plan'). That way tamar1374 and every other Leponnia settlement stay identical. Only Epēshu's own fingerprint (nDwell → pop/prosperity) moves, and it is identical on a double run. The DM chart has to be registered to the atlas-derived EPESHU_HF coast and river first (art bends to the atlas). This item does not block or fix the atlas-side cityBox misalignment, which is separate and does not wait on it.
votes.reason: Verified in the HEAD export. In docs/living/rulings.json, LC17's "why" contains the quoted text verbatim, and it also requires waiting for Street 4 and the street hold and keeping the pick(dR, …) draw. docs/living/design/polish-entries.md P2 lists the same blockers and the re-baseline consumers. Epēshu's streets are generated, not drawn: buildEpeshuMapData supplies only gridX/gridZ, labels and pop, and genTownPlans → planStreetsFor(s, R = W.rng.gen) lays the spokes and rings. Changing that changes world gen and the sim state, so the precedent transfers. Two corrections. (1) The LC17 trick of "keep the existing draw" is a single pick(). Street layout shares W.rng.gen across all settlements, and building and lane growth uses geometry-dependent draws. Preserving the draws alone would not keep the rest of the realm stable, so a consume-then-keyed-stream approach is needed. (2) Ownership: Epēshu's streets and buildings are the street track's (ST2, ST12, the street-data anchors and the frozen SV views keyed on Epēshu labels). It should be queued as a street-owned, owner-gated item, not filed under living. The registration-versus-medium point also needs saying: a sim plan on the chart only helps if the chart is first registered to the atlas-derived heightfield. It does not address the atlas overlay drift, which is a cityBox registration problem on the atlas side.

prior_record.claim: LC4 (creatures) is open but untouched by this ask.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: None of parts (a)-(d); it stays a living-track owner question.

evidence.quote: Whales of the Loon Sea move only where Living 1 resolves a canon placement

votes.corrected: LC4 (creatures) is still open in the living track. In docs/living/rulings.json, overrides is {} and confirmed is [], and the file describes LC4 as an "owner-gated addition, never default". The cited quote ("Whales of the Loon Sea move only where Living 1 resolves a canon placement...") is verbatim in the LC4 text, so creatures stay off or canon-backed by default. votes.reason: The quote exists verbatim in the LC4 text of docs/living/rulings.json. The "open" half is supported: overrides is {}, confirmed is [], and the about text calls LC4 owner-gated, with no default addition. The cited quote concerns only whale placement and does not bear on "untouched by this ask", so that half is unsupported inference. The inference is plausible: todo-inputs.json notes the Loon Sea has no atlas coordinates, and city-overlay registration would not change that. It still goes beyond what the quote shows.

votes.corrected: None of parts (a)-(d). LC4 is unconfirmed (docs/living/rulings.json: confirmed [], overrides {}), so its default stands: canon-backed movers only, whales only where Living 1 places the Loon Sea, Lugal one still mark, invented creatures absent (LC_GATED in the living scripts). Neither city registration (bending city art and geometry to the atlas coast, rivers and roads) nor the rendering medium (a raster overlay or a vector city layer) creates, moves or places a creature, and neither touches the sim's W.dragon or its whale chronicle line in index.html. LC4 stays a question for the owner of the living track. The registration work must not add creature marks, and it does not resolve the Loon Sea placement, because the atlas data holds none.
votes.reason: Verified in the HEAD export. docs/living/rulings.json lists LC4 among the owner-gated additions ("LC4, LC7 and LC17 are owner-gated additions, never defaults"), and the file has confirmed [] and overrides {}, so the ruling is open with its default in force. The quoted evidence matches the LC4 text, which is mirrored byte for byte in LC_RULINGS in docs/living/design/workflows/living-*.js and in build/living-config.js. The owner's ask is about anchoring city art to the atlas when zooming (registration) and about possibly replacing the stretched image with a vector city layer (rendering medium). Neither involves creatures. The atlas has only a "Whale" name token in a word list in maps-site/index.html, with no creature movers. On the sim side the only whale is a chronicle event in index.html, and the dragon is W.dragon, which LC4 says must never be named Lugal. A city layer or registration change touches neither of these. Treating LC4 as out of scope is therefore correct, and keeping it a living-track owner question respects track ownership. One nuance: "open" means no confirmation or override has been recorded yet. It does not mean undecided behaviour, because the default (invented creatures absent) applies until the owner rules.

items.summary: 'Region-chart zoom-through' queues footprint-anchoring of region MapArt and keeps the modal view where geometry does not fit; one registration method (tie points, low-order fit, RMS residual as the fit/modal test) should serve both rather than copying the city FOOT_R box.

prior_record.claim: The 'Region-chart zoom-through' POLISH item already queues the same footprint-anchoring question for region MapArt (Rhusagos, Relkor), keeping a modal view where the geometry does not fit.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Part (b): a REGISTRATION method chosen for city charts (tie points instead of a FOOT_R box) should be shared with this item rather than solved twice.

evidence.quote: evaluate footprint-anchoring the REGION MapArt

votes.corrected: POLISH.md has an unchecked item, "Region-chart zoom-through", whose text reads: "evaluate footprint-anchoring the REGION MapArt (Rhusagos, Relkor…) at mid zooms the way cities anchor at street zooms; keep modal where the geometry doesn't fit." It queues anchoring region MapArt on the map at mid zooms in the way city overlays are anchored, and keeps the modal chart view where the geometry doesn't fit. It does not mention tie points or any specific registration method. It also says "the way cities anchor", so it assumes the current cityBox/FOOT_R footprint model. Any shared registration method is a recommendation built on top of this item, not something the item states.
votes.reason: The quote is present verbatim at POLISH.md, line 543 of the HEAD export. The "(Rhusagos, Relkor…)" and "keep modal where the geometry doesn't fit" parts appear in the following lines. The claim's wording "the same footprint-anchoring question" is a mild interpretive gloss. The item describes footprint-anchoring modelled on city anchoring, not a registration method. The claim's "already queues" is accurate (the item is `- [ ]`). The item is not in a sim-specific section; it concerns atlas MapArt charts. The claim does not assert sim-side ownership, so nothing else is overreached.

votes.corrected: Part (b), with corrections. Use ONE REGISTRATION method for both: tie points matched between chart art px and atlas px (coast, river mouths, road junctions, settlement dots), fitted per chart as a low-order transform (affine; a piecewise or TPS warp only where needed), stored as data, and checked by RMS residual. The residual is also the test for the item's own "keep modal where the geometry doesn't fit". Do NOT carry over the city method the item names ("the way cities anchor at street zooms"). That method is cityBox/FOOT_R, a square box from the anchor's kind that ignores what the art shows. It is the mechanism behind the misalignment, and region charts have no anchor or FOOT_R in the first place. The scope is narrower than the claim says. DETAIL (maps-site/data/detail-charts.json) registers only Far North, Home Islands and Rhusagos as "REGION CHART" images. Relkor has an art file (art/chart-Relkor.jpg) but no detail-chart entry, so it would have to be registered before it can be anchored. Sharing the method means coordinating with the tracks that already depend on this item, not solving it centrally. The filigree density-bible marks it as blocking F3-D, and the living dossier says to specify the H2z handoff "together with Region-chart zoom-through". It is atlas-only. The sim's mapArt (CUSTOM_MAP_DATA.mapArt / #mapArtToggle in index.html) is a different thing and has no stake here. The RENDERING MEDIUM (raster vs vector) is a separate question; changing it fixes nothing for region charts.
votes.reason: Verified in the HEAD export. POLISH.md has the unchecked item "Region-chart zoom-through — evaluate footprint-anchoring the REGION MapArt (Rhusagos, Relkor…) at mid zooms the way cities anchor at street zooms; keep modal where the geometry doesn't fit", and the quote matches. So the claim and the "share, don't solve twice" direction hold. Tie-point data is deterministic (no RNG). It changes none of the pinned functions (genCityCanvas, washMake, sampleCityMask, xmur3, mulberry32; cityBox is not pinned). It bends art to the authoritative atlas and fits Leaflet image overlays in CRS.Simple world px. Three points need correcting. (1) The item literally asks to copy the city footprint approach (cityBox in maps-site/index.html: anchor ± footR(kind) scaled to the image's aspect). That approach is the misregistration itself, so sharing it as written would repeat the bug for regions. What should be shared is tie-point REGISTRATION, which is separate from the raster vs vector medium. (2) Relkor is not in detail-charts.json; only Far North, Home Islands and Rhusagos are REGION CHART entries. (3) The item has owners already: docs/filigree/density-bible.json lists it as blocking F3-D, and docs/living/research-dossier.md ties the H2z handoff spec to it. Coordinate through those tracks, and keep it apart from the sim's unrelated mapArt.

items.summary: overlay-Epeshu.jpg is portrait 2863x3072 (the brief had it swapped), the same aspect as the 3914x4200 chart chart-pois.json is indexed in, so one chart-to-atlas transform moves overlay, POIs and any chart-derived vector together.

prior_record.claim: overlay-Epeshu.jpg is portrait, 2863x3072 (measured from its JPEG SOF header), not 3072x2863 as the brief states. It has the same aspect as the 3914x4200 Epēshu city chart that chart-pois.json is indexed in (a 1/1.367 downscale). The atlas registers it with w:2863, h:3072 and poiRef 3914x4200.
prior_record.applies_to_us_proposed: Orientation correction for parts (b) and (c): the overlay, chart tiles and POIs share one frame. So a single chart-to-atlas registration (for example an affine transform fitted to tie points) would move overlay, POIs and any vector city derived from the chart together.

evidence.quote: registerCityOverlay('Epēshu','art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg',{prov:'canon',w:2863,h:3072,

votes.corrected: overlay-Epeshu.jpg is portrait 2863x3072 (JPEG SOF header measured: width 2863, height 3072), not 3072x2863. Its aspect (0.93197) matches the 3914x4200 Epēshu chart in detail-charts.json (0.93190), a ~1/1.367 downscale. maps-site/index.html registers it with w:2863,h:3072 and poiRef {w:eref.w,h:eref.h}, where eref = DETAIL['Epēshu'] (3914x4200). chart-pois.json coordinates reach x=3782, y=3835, which exceed the overlay's pixel size and fit the 3914x4200 frame. "Share one frame" is inferred from the aspect match and the POI reprojection, not from a pixel comparison of overlay against chart. Also, Summarch is registered as 3072x2859, so the brief's 2859x3072 for Summarch is likewise wrong, which is outside this claim.
votes.reason: I confirmed each fact against the HEAD export. The registerCityOverlay literal reads w:2863,h:3072. The SOF header gives 2863x3072. detail-charts.json has Epēshu as kind tiles, w 3914, h 4200. poiRef is taken from DETAIL['Epēshu'], and the POI coordinates fit that frame. The one overreach is that the aspect-ratio match only suggests the overlay and chart show the same content, so I flagged it as inference.

votes.corrected:
Holds, with scope. Everything the claim measures checks out. The SOF header of maps-site/art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg gives height 3072 and width 2863, so the image is portrait and has no EXIF orientation tag. The registerCityOverlay('Epēshu',...) call in maps-site/index.html passes w:2863,h:3072 and poiRef taken from DETAIL['Epēshu']. In data/detail-charts.json that entry is w 3914, h 4200. The brief has the two dimensions swapped. overlay-Summarch.jpg really is 3072x2859, and the code registers it that way.

I also checked that the overlay and the chart are the same picture, not just the same shape. I stitched level 1 of charts/epeshu (256 px tiles at 1/4 scale), cropped it to 3914x4200/4, downscaled it and the overlay to 200x215, and compared them. The correlation is 0.998, and the best offset across ±4 px is 0,0. So the overlay is the chart image at lower resolution, and chart-pois.json coordinates map into it by simple scaling. worldPOICoord and buildWorldPOIs already do that scaling through p.x/pr.w * box.fw, using the same cityBox as the overlay. Today the overlay and the POIs therefore move together, and they are misplaced together.

Corrected applies_to_us: one chart-frame-to-atlas transform, fitted to tie points (coast, river mouths and road exits on the canon chart, matched to the same features on PatrinorModern), would replace cityBox for Epēshu. It would place three things at once: the meshed-world overlay, the 19 POIs, and any vector city traced in chart coordinates. Fitting it to atlas features is what fixes the misalignment. This is a registration fix, not a rendering-medium fix: a vector city that still went through cityBox would sit exactly as wrong as the raster does.

Limits:
(1) The transform applies only to the meshed-world overlay pane (pCity/pCityPOI). The modal chart mode (enterChart) shows the chart on its own with the atlas base removed, so it needs no registration.
(2) L.imageOverlay can only use an axis-aligned box. A transform with only scale and offset (4 parameters) drops straight into the existing bounds. A transform with rotation or skew needs the overlay drawn with a CSS matrix or onto a canvas, written inline in the file (no plugin dependency).
(3) It does not carry over to the sim. The sim's Epēshu streets belong to the street track and are not in the chart frame, so they only line up if that track also adopts the chart-to-atlas transform.
(4) It covers only the two canon cities, each fitted separately; Summarch needs its own tie points. Procedural cities (genCityCanvas, which the mobile track pins) have no chart frame. This change leaves the pinned functions untouched; cityBox is not in the pinned set.
votes.reason: The facts check out against the HEAD export: the JPEG SOF gives 2863 wide by 3072 tall, the code registers w:2863,h:3072 with poiRef 3914x4200, and stitched chart tiles correlate 0.998 with the overlay at zero offset, so they share one frame. A single affine transform per canon city is the right fix and keeps the atlas authoritative. applies_to_us overstates the reach, though. It covers only the atlas overlay, POIs and chart-traced vectors for the canon cities, not chart mode or the sim's street-track Epēshu. It also leaves out that a transform with rotation or skew needs a CSS or canvas transform written inline, because L.imageOverlay bounds are axis-aligned only.

owner_questions.text: Anchor verdict table. The audit now reads 45 move / 2 keep / 4 owner calls over the 51 audited anchors of 138 (it replaces the earlier 37/1/2; the other 87 already sit on a printed ring). The two keeps mean different things: Drāmūz (its anchor is on the printed ◉; its marker, 35 px S in open water, is the record to fix) and Sjefenhold (an uncharted canon place kept off-dot with an explicit reason). Under this table Hordon and Clickerhall are anchor errors, not exemptions. The table would be derived by an offline deterministic tool against a reviewed by-name exception table, with no runtime marker-wins rule and no distance-only snap. Choose: (a) approve as stated; (b) approve with changes to named rows; (c) hold it until the census second pass has landed.

Penthelon. Its marker (1942,755) sits on the printed ◉, but moving the anchor there drowns the plan: the r−b≤54 colour test reads the olive region tint as water (about 2% land at the ring against about 61% at the current anchor 113 px N), and the 0.9.7 off-dot reason is stale. Choose: (a) move it together with a non-colour land/water source (inked coast or the filigree DEM), which touches the UG3-pinned sampleCityMask path and so atlas_fn_sha and cityCanvasSha; or (b) keep it off-dot with a fresh, stated reason.

Paga and Drāmūz. Paga: both its anchor and its marker are off the print, and the printed ○ is near (2074,809); re-snap both records there, or name another target? Drāmūz: fix the marker (35 px S in open water) and keep the anchor, or treat it differently?

The remaining owner calls and keeps. Kolens (uncharted; no printed river or ring under it) and Ūmak-nūs-Ion: move, keep, or rule each separately? Sjefenhold: keep off-dot with an explicit reason, or move?

Point convention, to be ruled before any cityCanvasSha B0 re-cut (G0-3 makes it a precondition). Choose: (a) ring centre (pixel-centre detector); (b) census-marker convention, ring −(1,0); (c) today's anchor convention, ring −(1,1). Each gives a different sampleCityMask window, plan, hash and gate set; Tamaron's sea approaches are [319.3,1.6] at the ring centre against [317.7,113.6,3.5] at ring −(1,1). In the same ruling: are the trio's sea fields re-measured in the same edit, or explicitly frozen? The ruling also settles Summarch's ring point, (542.0,50.0) by the detector against (541.75,49.75) by the earlier tie fit.

cityCanvasSha B0 rebaseline for the hashed trio, Tamaron ◉ (1659,1554), Sokundo ○ (1478.0,1450.0) and Kanae ○ (1523.0,1490.0) (anchors, sea.side and road bearings), after OQ5 and a crop check of the Sokundo and Kanae rings. Choose: (a) approve one re-cut landing at the Mobile 9 lane boundary; (b) approve it as a declared rebase at another point; (c) do not move the trio yet.

Summarch. Move the literal (523,58) to the printed ring as a translation only, keeping FOOT_R 14 and north-up? The target is (541.75,49.75) by the tie fit or (542.0,50.0) by the ring detector, depending on OQ5. Which records move with it: the meshedWorldInit literal, the factions.json Allhammers seat, party.json, and the party-route.json (523,58) waypoint? The second visit at (545,80) is offset on purpose. The DM's river runs north of the ring while the atlas river runs on its other side (canon has the Stony River girdling the southern flank). Choose: redraw the river, move the ring, or accept the mismatch.

Epēshu placement policy. Given: the atlas decides placement and the sim follows later as a separate item. The evidence: the print coast favours 0.6x of today's box with the centre +3 px E (3.58 atlas px rms), but that is the bottom of the policy range and a free fit runs to the edge of its search box, so coast shape cannot decide it (the holding check on G0-15 suggests picking within about 0.6-0.8x); the sim's hand-placed label spread favours about 1.0x (rms-radius ratio 1.12, or 0.94 without Fairy Arch) and its built-up extent favours 1.0x or more (1.53-1.63x). Choose: (a) the scale, anywhere in roughly 0.6-1.0x (centre shifts +3 to +8 px E were tested); (b) which chart point sits on the printed ring: the Forum, the harbour mouth, or the built-up centroid; (c) whether the atlas fabric is a drawn symbolisation with no metric scale (the chart's drawn density cannot match the sim's metric lots; they differ about 4-7x linear).

Epēshu seam band 2: chart sea over print land, about 75 px² at 0.6x+3E. Band 1 (chart land over print sea) is handled by the print-land clip plus a sea fill in pCityWash. Choose for band 2: (a) make it transparent; (b) key the chart's flat sea fill out so the atlas land shows; (c) fill it with land tone; (d) keep the base opaque under the footprint (G8-6 [D] found this is one global opacity, with only about 6% showing through the wash).

Canon art bending. Choose the limit for the DM's Epēshu and Summarch charts: (a) scale plus translate only (new axis-aligned bounds, no resampling); (b) also rotation by Helmert, which keeps shapes but needs a PNG or WebP pre-warp with alpha or a custom overlay subclass; (c) also warps (TPS, polynomial2/3). Only translate plus uniform scale was tested, and one coast-band warp was measured and rejected (G0-11).

Modal chart. Should enterChart over charts/epeshu and charts/summarch read the same stored chart-px-to-atlas-px transform (for example so Back returns to the registered spot), or stay in its own chart-px frame, which leaves two POI transforms?

Registration audit. Should the swipe or opacity override (base and overlay forced to opacity 1, at about z7-8) ship behind a URL debug flag in maps-site, or stay tools-only? R7 forbids showing it at rest.

Lifecycle policy. May worldCityUpdate stop lowering maxZoom below the current zoom (no automatic ease-down), with catchment hysteresis? This changes desktop feel, and the living chart's H2z zoom-through builds on it. Nobody owns this unrequested camera move today. Choose: (a) ride with the registration item's lifecycle fixes; (b) its own item; (c) leave it as the intended soft ceiling.

Ownership and queueing of the registration work. None of these is owned by the filigree, living, street or mobile tracks today: the per-city record, the anchor data, the print-coast ring and sea fill (seam-clip data), the plan-river consumer, and road re-traces with a per-leg medium field in party-route.json. Choose: (a) a standalone atlas registration item (a new POLISH item beside filigree slice C, no density-bible edit) that reaches Filigree 2 through a README §7 row; (b) an amendment to slice C; (c) another home. Also: should the canon skeleton trace (coast/water, Summarch's wall ring, Epēshu's hinterland edge) sit with it, with a full-building or chart-conditioned fabric as its own later item gated on OQ17 and OQ18? Is holding Street 3 wanted (a POLISH title starting 'Filigree data —' does that)?

Road data. Re-trace the Road that Walks with the Sun and the sea-lane vertex [1320,1398] onto the printed ink now (data-only, but it changes generated gates and so cityCanvasSha), or wait for POLISH 'Traced road network'?
Mile constant. Choose: the printed bar (659 atlas px = 600 mi, 0.910 mi/px) or MI_PER_NATIVE=600/723 (0.830 mi/px, origin undocumented).

DM masters. Both canon charts look like Watabou MFCG output. Does the DM hold higher-resolution or vector masters, such as MFCG seeds or permalinks or GeoJSON exports, for Epēshu and Summarch? The proposal is to ask before any tracing; tracing finds no street network in the charts, because the lanes are unpainted ground.

What the vector idea is for. The DM raster is 1 texel per CSS px at Epēshu's cityMaxZ 9.885, so on phones it goes soft from z8.3 (DPR 3) and z8.885 (DPR 2), and flyIntoCity lands at 0.471 texels per device px on an iPhone 13. Choose: (a) crispness only, which a higher-resolution registered raster also delivers; or a drawn, interactive city as (b) a vector layer replacing the chart, (c) vector under the chart as hit geometry only, or (d) vector only past the chart's native zoom.

Hit-testing. The city has nothing at rest (R7), no block labels (R4) and a 22 CSS px tap resolver (FM4). Should it carry building or block hit-testing at all? If yes, choose: a coordinate lookup through the registration transform, or vector paths. The prototype's drawTrace draws POI discs at rest, which R7 forbids.

LC7 and a 2D in-atlas city. Confirm or override LC7 (the sim is the only 3D; no WebGL in maps-site; H2z crossfades into a Street poster). If confirmed, any vector city is a 2D Leaflet layer and the prototype's three.js mode stays out of the atlas. Separately, since LC7 asks only about 3D/WebGL: should a 2D in-atlas detailed city be built at all, and should it, or the raster overlay (today 'the city overlay'), be the H2z crossfade source?

How far the sim follows. Choose any of: (a) move the sim's Epēshu cityLabels toward the registered chart POIs before Street 1 (costs frozen-view fixtures SV1/SV3/SV6/SV8, not the fingerprint, by code reading); (b) leave planStreetsFor alone until an LC17-class ruling; (c) treat sim adoption of chart geometry for Epēshu, which re-baselines the whole #s=epeshu world through W.rng.gen (buildings, great houses, flora, chronicle), as a separate owner-gated item after the street hold, or never. Keep the sim out of the first cut?

Canon district names and deep links. Should the sim adopt the chart's canon spellings ('Marble Quarter', 'Thūkīn Amphitheatre', 'The Fairy Arch')? Should 'Sim ↔ atlas continuity' add cityLabels targets to #goto= so that LC7's 'Epēshīn Forum' step lands?
First Epēshu control point. Use the Blue Temple of Thobrauk / Wood Quay pair? To be shared, the sim would have to place the temple first.

View-state hash keys. May the living track's H2/H2z link add atlas hash keys for view state (an atlas-px centre plus a scale)? Today setHash writes only #place= and #chart=, and the sim's applyGotoFromHash reads only a name.

measure_probes.text: Common setup for every probe. Run in a later session, after Mobile 5 lands, on a HEAD copy (an exact export of the committed repo) served by the probing session's own static server on a free port other than 8544, written below as http://localhost:<port>/. Never use port 8544, never run tools/mobile-capture.js, and never run beside a mobile capture (it holds a global lock). Throwaway pages and edited copies go in a mktemp -d directory served by that same server. Profiles: desktop 1366x768@1, desktop2x 1440x900@2, iphone13 390x664@3 touch, and pixel7 where noted (4x CPU throttle where noted). Atlas: load http://localhost:<port>/maps-site/?v=<fresh-int> and wait for window.ATLAS.ready; handles ATLAS.map, ATLAS.descend(name,poi), ATLAS.chart(name,poi), ATLAS.exitChart(), ATLAS.fly(name), ATLAS.cityReg, ATLAS.cityAnchors. Sim: load http://localhost:<port>/?v=<fresh-int>#s=epeshu and wait for window.ANNALS.ready.

setMaxZoom ease-down (desktop, iphone13). ATLAS.descend('Kanae'), wait for moveend, then ATLAS.map.panBy([1800,0],{animate:false}). Repeat with a drag at z9 from Epēshu into open sea. Log getZoom(), getMaxZoom(), getCenter() and a timestamp on every zoomend/moveend for 3 s. Fail on any zoom change >0.05 without input. Expected today: about 2.3 dz (Kanae) and 1.885 (Epēshu).

Synthetic-to-melded swap (desktop, iphone13). With cache disabled, load #chart=Sokundo&poi=1. Per rAF, log getZoom(), the count of '.leaflet-pCity-pane img' and ATLAS.cityReg['Sokundo'].url. Record the POI latlng at fly start against worldPOICoord after landing. Take overlay-only shots before and after the swap. Report the POI move in atlas and screen px and the coast rotation in degrees.

Crossfade residuals in screen px (desktop, iphone13). Centre on Epēshu (1236.1,1415), Summarch at both the printed ring (541.75,49.75; the detector gives 542,50) and the literal (523,58), Sokundo and Damoklir. Shoot each at z7.1, 7.3, 7.5, 7.8 and at the city's own cityMaxZ, once with pCity and pCityWash hidden and once with the tile pane hidden. Pick coast and road edges and report chamfer rms/max in screen px and in atlas px (divide by 2^(z−4)). Static estimate for Epēshu: about 7.7-8.5 atlas px rms (8.48 atlas px chart-to-print ≈ 84 screen px at z7.3). Target after registration: ≤2 screen px at z7.3.

Hordon/Maeges end state (desktop). Load #chart=Maeges cold. For 6 s log getZoom(), getMaxZoom(), the overlay src, and every setView call via a wrapper, so the ensureArrival retries at 1.7, 3.4 and 5.1 s show up. Expected: a 2.33 dz yank to 8, Hordon's plan appearing, then an unanimated snap to about 10.19. With Hordon pre-registered: a 0.14 ease only.

exitChart clamp (desktop 1200x800). At fitZoom record getCenter(), then ATLAS.chart('Epēshu') and ATLAS.exitChart(). Repeat with 'Seat'. Log the centre after zoomend. About 1113 atlas px east today; pass ≤1 px. Also exit, then ATLAS.fly('Kanae'), and log whether the fly completes.

Mid-fly mask callback (desktop, iphone13). Cold cache, ATLAS.descend('Sokundo') from the fit view. Per rAF log getZoom(), getMaxZoom() and the '.leaflet-pCity-pane img' count. Fail if the count drops to 0 mid-fly.

ensureArrival hijack (desktop, iphone13). ATLAS.descend('Epēshu'), then inject a synthetic drag at t=300 ms. Log moveend times and zoom at 1.7, 3.4 and 5.1 s. Fail on any jump after the drag. Expected today: a single teleport of about 4.7 levels.

#view boot cap (desktop; settles the disputed view-hash-lossy). Load cold #view=1236,1415,9.5, then #view=542,50,10.5, then a generated ruin at 11. Log getMaxZoom() inside the first worldCityUpdate (before handleHash) and after landing, plus the landed zoom and centre against the request. This decides whether every link deeper than 8 lands at 8 (Epēshu included) or Epēshu keeps 9.885.

Generation jank (pixel7, iphone13, at 4x CPU throttle). Scripted pinch onto an ungenerated town with a PerformanceObserver('longtask'). Report the count and duration of tasks >50 ms. Also time the overlay 'load' of overlay-Epeshu.jpg on Fast 3G against getZoom(); that part belongs to A-U11.

Vector cost, only if a vector form is chosen (iphone13, pixel7 at 4x CPU throttle, desktop). Build a throwaway page with Leaflet 1.9.4 CRS.Simple. Load synthetic city layers at both ladders: N = 300 / 1,000 / 3,000 and 5,000-30,000 features (1.9k-30k vertices), and the measured sizes 700 / 1,000 / 2,100 / 6,279 / 7,758 features at 2.6k / 8.5k / 23k / 29k vertices. Draw each two ways: SVG merged by class (9-30 L.polygon multipolygons, 3-level arrays, fillRule:'nonzero') and L.canvas({pane:'pCity'}), each with smoothFactor 0 and the default. Run a flyIntoCity-like flyTo from z6 to z9.4 and a scripted two-finger pinch. Use PerformanceObserver('longtask') and per-rAF timestamps. Report animation-frame ms and the single end-of-gesture task (zoomend _project plus moveend _update) separately, at z7.8 and at the city's cityMaxZ (z9.885 for Epēshu). Pass if no frame exceeds ~10-15 ms and the end task stays under 50 ms.
Retina base dropout (desktop2x, iphone13). At z>10.5 over a village, a ruin and Summarch, log the base tile layer's visible tile count and opacity during zoom, and screenshot the plan and wash edge.

Seam in both directions after registration (desktop, iphone13). Once a per-city record exists, at z7.3 and z9.885 over Epēshu, measure the overlay's land-over-sea and sea-over-land area against the print water mask in screen px, then divide by 2^(z−4). Static targets at 0.6x+3E: 91 and 75 atlas px². Pass when the chosen clip and sea fill (an L.imageOverlay in pCityWash, zIndex 2) hide both bands.

clip-path on a Leaflet ImageOverlay (iphone13/WebKit, pixel7, desktop 1366x768@1). Apply a throwaway percent clip-path: polygon() from the islet-filled print-land ring (try DP0.5 and DP0.25) to the Epēshu pCity through the className option or a class rule. Centre on (1236.1,1415) at z7.3 and z9.885. Screenshot with the tile pane hidden and with the pCity pane hidden. Check that land-over-sea is hidden, that both seam bands are handled, that there is no hairline at the clip edge, that the clip stays crisp at 9.885, and that it tracks the img through a button zoom (CSS transform), a pinch and flyIntoCity / ATLAS.descend('Epēshu') (per-frame _reset and _animateZoom transform writes). Log rAF frame times during the fly with and without the clip. If the clip fails, test an inline SVG data-URI mask-image with -webkit-mask-image as the fallback.

Fill tone (G8-4). At 0.6x+3E, with the clip and a sea-toned L.imageOverlay in pCityWash at zIndex 2, sample screen RGB inside the clipped band 1 and compare with the print sea mean [159,152,117]; target ΔE well under the measured wash 14.1. Repeat after a forced washRefresh to confirm the fill stays above the wash.

River crossings (desktop). For the 18 generated plans with a printed river within 2.5·FOOT_R (G0-7), shoot at z7.8 and cityMaxZ with pCity shown and hidden, and record whether the plan hides or contradicts the printed river. Repeat after any anchor move.

Chart-conditioned build time on phones (pixel7 and iphone13, also at 4x CPU throttle). Load prototypes/epeshu-chart.html, call build() with seed 'epeshu' 5 times, and run the build (growRibs, extractBlocks, makeParcels, footprint) under PerformanceObserver('longtask'), recording performance.now() deltas and longtask entries. Node v22 baseline: about 1.2 s (1,177-1,375 ms). Decide whether a port can build off the gesture path (idle callback after moveend, cached) or must ship static output.

DPR crispness (desktop2x 1440x900@2, iphone13). ATLAS.descend('Epēshu'). Take device-pixel screenshots of the .leaflet-pCity-pane img at z8.3, 8.885, 9.385 and 9.885, centred on (1236.1,1415). Measure the edge-gradient width in device px across a building outline. Confirm softness begins at z8.3 on DPR 3 and z8.885 on DPR 2.

Era check (desktop). Switch setEra among modern, war and imperial with the Epēshu overlay and clip at z7.8. Confirm the overlay, clip and POIs do not move. Record the wash tone mismatch on war and imperial (expected ΔG≈29, ΔB≈21 in Leponnia) as a colour item, not a registration item.

Leaflet rounding at rest (desktop, iphone13). ATLAS.fly('Epēshu'), then map.setZoom(7.37,{animate:false}). Read the getBoundingClientRect corners of the .leaflet-pCity-pane img and compare them with map.latLngToContainerPoint of the cityBox corners (x 1211.87-1260.33, y 1389-1441 via px()). Do the same for a tile img's position against latLngToContainerPoint of its tile corner. Pass at ≤1 screen px. Repeat per rAF during ATLAS.fly from the fit view and log the maximum.

Debug swipe audit (desktop, iphone13). Centre on Epēshu (1236.1,1415) and on Summarch (541.75,49.75). At z7.0, 7.5 and 8.0 run curBase.setOpacity(1) and CITYVIEW.overlay.setOpacity(1), set style.clipPath='inset(0 50% 0 0)' on the overlay img, and take a screenshot. Pick coast and dotted-road edges on both sides of the clip line. Report the offset in screen px, and divide by 2^(z−4) for atlas px. Baseline for Epēshu: 8.48 atlas px rms chart-to-print, about 84 screen px at z7.3.

H2z camera mapping (gated on street=1, Street 3/4). From atlas z=9.885 centred on (1236.1,1415), compute res = 2^(4−z) atlas px per CSS px, convert to metres through 800/768 and CELL, and set the sim camera height to res·canvasWidth/(2·tan(fov/2)), top-down, at the focus mapped by atlas=(1060,1240)+grid·800/768. Render the sim, overlay it on the atlas crop of the same CSS size, and report the focus-point offset and the coast offset in atlas px.

Sim fingerprint under a cityLabels move (own-sim S13 is code reading only). Load the sim at http://localhost:<port>/?v=<fresh-int>#s=epeshu, wait for window.ANNALS.ready, run ANNALS.simDays(400) and record JSON.stringify(ANNALS.stats()). Repeat against a throwaway copy of index.html in the mktemp directory, with every Epēshu cityLabels dx/dz in buildEpeshuMapData shifted by +20 m. Pass: identical stats. Also log the flyTo targets for 'Epēshīn Forum', 'Whitestreet', 'the Marble Quarter' and 'Wood Quay' in both builds to show which frozen-view poses (SV1, SV3, SV6, SV8) move.

Atlas gates vs sim s.entries (own-sim S22, never measured). Atlas: load maps-site/?v=<int>, wait for ATLAS.ready, ATLAS.descend('Tamaron') (then Epēshu-window cities such as Lepon the Old), and read the gate bearings that cityApproaches/mkGate produce. Sim: load #s=epeshu, find the same settlement in ANNALS.world.settlements, and convert each s.entries {x,z} to a bearing from the settlement centre (sim −z = north). Report the per-gate angular difference in degrees and any unmatched gates on either side. No pass bar yet; record as baseline.

cityCanvasSha by point convention (G0-3's hash differences are inferred, not recomputed). Desktop profile. For each of Tamaron, Sokundo and Kanae at the HEAD anchors: ATLAS.descend(name), wait for moveend, sha256 ATLAS.cityReg[name].url in the page. Then set ATLAS.cityAnchors[name] in turn to the ring centre (Tamaron ◉ 1659,1554; Sokundo ○ 1478.0,1450.0; Kanae ○ 1523.0,1490.0), ring−(1,0) and ring−(1,1). For each, delete the cityReg entry and its cache, descend again, re-hash, and log the gate and sea sets. Pass: confirms whether the three conventions give three different hashes, and which sea sets appear (expected Tamaron [319.3,1.6] at the ring centre vs [317.7,113.6,3.5] at ring−(1,1)).

open_questions.theme: Shift mechanics still unmeasured
open_questions.text: view-hash-lossy: the two checks disagree on the boot cap. Does maxBounds clamp the boot centre away from every anchor, giving a cap of 8 everywhere, or does Epēshu keep 9.885? Probe P9 decides it.

open_questions.theme: Shift mechanics still unmeasured
open_questions.text: Hordon/Maeges: is the cold-path end state (snap back to about 10.19 on Hordon's plan) reached within the first ensureArrival retry on real networks, or does the view sit at z8 until 3.4-5.1 s? (P5)

open_questions.theme: Shift mechanics still unmeasured
open_questions.text: Which share of the observed shift is cityBox placement, setMaxZoom auto-zoom-out, or the nearest-city overlay swap? Not measured (task 19, after Mobile 5; P1, P4).

open_questions.theme: Shift mechanics still unmeasured
open_questions.text: How large are the Epēshu and Summarch misfits against the PatrinorModern coast, rivers and roads under cityBox, in world px and degrees of rotation, measured in a browser (POLISH 'Anchoring: measure shift budget', task #19; P4, R2)? Pick coast and road features on the atlas and on the overlay and report per-feature offsets. That decides whether a straight fit with a better scale is enough, or whether Helmert, affine or piecewise warping is needed.

open_questions.theme: Anchors and point conventions
open_questions.text: Sokundo and Kanae targets: the G0-2 detector finds clean ○ rings 5.81 and 7.45 px from their anchors, but the marker-bias dissent's local fit found Kanae off-ring and Sokundo unstable. A crop check is needed before the trio is re-cut.

open_questions.theme: Anchors and point conventions
open_questions.text: Summarch ring centre: (542.0,50.0) from the G9 pixel-centre detector and the ◉ marker −(0,2) rule, against (541.75,49.75) from the earlier tie-point fit. The 0.25-px gap is most likely a convention difference, settled by the G0-3 ruling (OQ5).

open_questions.theme: Anchors and point conventions
open_questions.text: Was the Summarch anchor (523,58) vs printed glyph (542,52) offset deliberate (shoreline fit) or drift from the 'snap to printed ◉' pass? Same for Penthelon (113 px).

open_questions.theme: Anchors and point conventions
open_questions.text: G0-3: the per-convention cityCanvasSha differences are inferred from sampleCityMask's rounding, not recomputed (probe G0-3).

open_questions.theme: Anchors and point conventions
open_questions.text: canon C15: the checks say eight and ten ◉ cities have no anchor; the named list implies nine. This needs a recount.

open_questions.theme: Anchors and point conventions
open_questions.text: gap-consumers C11: the checks give about 29 against 17 anchors reaching gazetteer.json through the anchor path. The second check's named list of 17 is used.

open_questions.theme: Anchors and point conventions
open_questions.text: Were the Shengo and Rhup anchors re-snapped in city-anchors.json after the sim grid coordinates were fixed? If so, the sim gridX/gridZ need regenerating from the anchors.

open_questions.theme: Anchors and point conventions
open_questions.text: After the anchors move, how many generated plans gain or lose printed-river crossings, and do Aldrakhar, Iet Ford, Bash Dargis and Stony Ford change class as G0-10 predicts? (P15)

open_questions.theme: Canon charts: orientation, scale, control points, bending
open_questions.text: Is the DM Epēshu chart north-up? The tie fits reject rotation, but the chart carries no compass (Summarch's chart does). The atlas projects it unrotated into cityBox; the sim's hand-placed labels and landmarks fit no single similarity transform of the chart, and some sim district offsets would match the POIs better under a different rotation.

open_questions.theme: Canon charts: orientation, scale, control points, bending
open_questions.text: Do the canon charts need rotation at all? Only translate plus uniform scale was tested (tc-4). A rotation would force either an offline pre-rotated plate (TILES_V bump, A-U11 conflict) or a warp, which was measured and rejected in G0-11.

open_questions.theme: Canon charts: orientation, scale, control points, bending
open_questions.text: True and display scale: should the Epēshu chart be ruled to a true scale (the DM never gives it one; the Summarch bar, 1.82 px/m, could suggest a house scale but is not evidence for Epēshu)? Is the DM-drawn city art meant to be at true scale relative to the atlas at all? Should the canon city stay an exaggerated inset (about 10-16x the atlas scale) whose rim is fitted onto the atlas coast, roads and river, or should the zoom-through shift scale continuously? That needs the length of the Cyrikon mile (MI_PER_NATIVE is in Cyrikon miles).

open_questions.theme: Canon charts: orientation, scale, control points, bending
open_questions.text: Control points: which chart pixel should sit on the atlas ring-dot (cityBox centres the whole DM image on the anchor, not on a charted landmark such as the Forum or the harbour mouth; the owner/DM must name them)? Which atlas features can serve as GCPs inside or next to each canon footprint: coast inflections in the z5 mask, the harbour mouth, river lines and the Summarch river crossings, dotted-road exits or road entries in traced-roads.json, the ring-dot? Is the ring-dot the city centre or a symbol, and can the DM say what it marks? 'Traced road network (USER FLAG)' is still unchecked in POLISH.md, and traced-roads.json has no points within 60 px of Epēshu.

open_questions.theme: Canon charts: orientation, scale, control points, bending
open_questions.text: Is the DM chart's straight western sea edge an artistic simplification, so the chart must be fitted to the atlas coast, or does it encode a harbour shape the atlas lacks? The atlas is authoritative either way, but the fit's tolerance depends on the answer.

open_questions.theme: Canon charts: orientation, scale, control points, bending
open_questions.text: How much may canon DM art be bent to fit the atlas? Helmert/straight keep the drawing exactly; polynomial1 shears it; TPS/polynomial2+ rubber-sheet it (rubber-sheeting seems unwelcome). This needs an owner ruling (OQ10), since registration bends art to the atlas and the atlas is never moved.

open_questions.theme: Canon charts: orientation, scale, control points, bending
open_questions.text: Does the Epēshu painting's depicted extent (walls, quays, coast) match the FOOT_R capital box of about 48x52 atlas px, or should control points on coast, river and dotted-road gates set the box? This needs the in-browser shift measurement.

open_questions.theme: Canon charts: orientation, scale, control points, bending
open_questions.text: Is a wall drawn on the Epēshu chart? Three files disagree; the wall-ring strain figures for an Epēshu warp (G0-14) rest on a wall traced by eye while sibling files say no separable wall is drawn, so they stay on hold.

open_questions.theme: Canon charts: orientation, scale, control points, bending
open_questions.text: Are overlay-Epeshu.jpg and the z3 charts/epeshu pyramid the same art? q08 reports a mean RGB difference of 13.6 and left it unsettled.

open_questions.theme: Canon charts: orientation, scale, control points, bending
open_questions.text: Does the live wiki's Epēshu page (it has a 'Map' heading in the snapshot) or the Map-of-the-Wide-World page state a scale or embed the Epēshu chart with a bar? The wiki host was unreachable through the egress proxy, so contentIndex.json and the Leaflet config were not read.

open_questions.theme: Canon charts: orientation, scale, control points, bending
open_questions.text: Does the DM hold higher-resolution masters or vector sources (MFCG seed, permalink or GeoJSON export; Inkarnate, Wonderdraft or Illustrator originals) for the Epēshu and Summarch charts? The 3914x4200 and 4245x3951 pyramids are the best on disk and do not look vectorised from a line source; their original size (before the 0.73 overlay downscale) is unknown. Were the charts made in Watabou's MFCG or another generator? A GeoJSON export would replace all tracing (OQ17).

open_questions.theme: Canon charts: orientation, scale, control points, bending
open_questions.text: If the canon overlay is ever pre-warped: should the chart pyramids (charts/epeshu, charts/summarch) used by enterChart stay unwarped as the DM's original (probably yes, since chart mode is its own modal CRS, but POIs must then use two different transforms)? Output format: JPG with parchment-filled corners, or WebP/PNG with alpha? It interacts with washMake's seam and the mobile byte budget.

open_questions.theme: Canon charts: orientation, scale, control points, bending
open_questions.text: Should cityMaxZ, which repeats the footR/aspect maths instead of calling cityBox, be folded into the single override function, or keep its own copy reading the same record?

open_questions.theme: Canon charts: orientation, scale, control points, bending
open_questions.text: Should one registration record per city (control points from chart px to atlas px) drive the meshed-world overlay, the chart POIs and the modal chart pyramids together, or should modal chart mode (enterChart, its own chart-px frame) stay modal as the Region-chart item allows ('keep modal where the geometry doesn't fit')? Ownership spans filigree slice C, the living H2z poster and the Mobile atlas lane (OQ11).

open_questions.theme: Canon charts: orientation, scale, control points, bending
open_questions.text: Which source governs Epēshu's interior: the DM-drawn city chart (overlay-Epeshu / charts/epeshu / chart-pois) or the sim's seeded plan? 'Atlas geography is authoritative' does not settle it, because the PatrinorModern print has no interior. Today the two disagree by 103-489 m per district.

open_questions.theme: Seam, delivery and the filigree route
open_questions.text: Does the evenodd fill-rule of clip-path polygon() work on iOS Safari 15? MDN BCD has no entry for it. The single islet-filled ring avoids the question but loses islets (P14).

open_questions.theme: Seam, delivery and the filigree route
open_questions.text: A-U11's swap mechanism is unspecified in docs/mobile/units.json: setUrl (a bounds override is then independent of the swap) or a second registerCityOverlay call (tears down wash, stubs and POIs)? If it re-runs registerCityOverlay, the canon clip, the fill and the override must survive overlayCache.delete and the prov reset.

open_questions.theme: Seam, delivery and the filigree route
open_questions.text: Should registration of the canon charts ship default-on as a base-atlas data fix (declared UG8 regions, a rebase after Mobile 9), or behind filigree=1 as part of slice C? R18 only governs the table map.

open_questions.theme: Seam, delivery and the filigree route
open_questions.text: B-38 clips city contours to the chart's own coast, which treats the canon chart as truth, while the stated constraint makes the print authoritative. Should the owner rule that registration supersedes B-38's chart-coast clip? Changing B-38 means re-integrating the bible (Path B) before Filigree 2.

open_questions.theme: Seam, delivery and the filigree route
open_questions.text: Slice letters: the bible's prerequisites table says F3-C is the fiction stack and F3-D the city; the Filigree 2 script and POLISH say C is the city and D the stack. Which should a registration prerequisite cite?

open_questions.theme: Seam, delivery and the filigree route
open_questions.text: The README §7 route into Filigree 2: own-atlas v2's holding check names three limits, and only the first (live read at run time) is visible in the check text; limits (2) and (3) are unknown. Does anything gate or hash a README §7 edit (any workflow preflight that sha-checks docs/filigree/README.md)? None was found among the items, but it was not verified directly.

open_questions.theme: Seam, delivery and the filigree route
open_questions.text: When Filigree 2 runs relative to Mobile 9 determines whether registration costs a Filigree 2 rebase; filigree-2-plan.js never re-reads state.json, so nothing checks this automatically.

open_questions.theme: Rivers, roads and scale constants
open_questions.text: Who supplies plan-usable rivers? 18 generated plans plus Epēshu sit near a printed river, and no item owns the consumer. It should queue after Mobile 9/14 with an atlas_fn_sha rebase.

open_questions.theme: Rivers, roads and scale constants
open_questions.text: Which mile constant governs: the printed bar (659 atlas px per 600 mi = 0.910 mi/px) or MI_PER_NATIVE=600/723 (0.830)? 723 is undocumented; the printed bar is measurable on the tiles. The traced Sun Road favours 0.83 (568 vs 560 leagues) only if a league is exactly 3 mi (OQ16).

open_questions.theme: Rivers, roads and scale constants
open_questions.text: What is a league? Mountain Wall implies 3.0 mi (900 km = 186 leagues); Lepon implies 2.5 mi (20 leagues = 50 mi). Is a Cyrikoi mile equal to an English mile at all, and what is a River-Measure (about 1.11 mi on the printed bar)?

open_questions.theme: Rivers, roads and scale constants
open_questions.text: Should the sim's epeshu roads follow the atlas's traced roads (atlas authoritative), at the cost of changing the seeded world and its determinism fingerprint?

open_questions.theme: Rivers, roads and scale constants
open_questions.text: Who owns a shared traced road graph used by both the atlas city sheet (Filigree C) and the sim street view (street track)? Is its source of truth the art-px trace or the atlas-px warp?

open_questions.theme: Vector city: tracing, generation, cost, ownership
open_questions.text: Can a street layer for the canon charts come from the negative space of the ground class (Epēshu 5,089 polygons / 105,656 vertices at DP 1) or from a centreline graph via thinning (AutoTrace -centerline or a skeletonize step on the thin white or grey road strokes)? Both are unmeasured (G0-20), as is how cleanly badge and legend in-filling restores the building fabric beneath.

open_questions.theme: Vector city: tracing, generation, cost, ownership
open_questions.text: Why do V8 (17,323 Epēshu blobs ≥12 px on overlay-Epeshu.jpg) and G4/G0-20 (23,184 on the charts/epeshu/3 pyramid) differ? The source-resolution explanation is an inference; the check text is truncated.

open_questions.theme: Vector city: tracing, generation, cost, ownership
open_questions.text: Could the canon city charts be traced to footprints (blocks, quays, walls) to give hover hit geometry while the DM art stays the painted surface? accurate-mapping.md's U-Net plus watershed pipeline is unproven on a single hand-drawn chart; interactive tracing in a tool step may be the realistic path.

open_questions.theme: Vector city: tracing, generation, cost, ownership
open_questions.text: genCityCanvas exposes no geometry. Should a vector form of generated plans re-implement the plan in a sibling function, or refactor the pinned function under an owner-approved atlas_fn_sha/cityCanvasSha rebaseline? If slice C draws the procedural towns as vectors, cityCanvasSha (a hash of the invented data: canvases) becomes null and fails UG3 in every later capture-gated run: should the vector layer sit beside the raster registration (keeping the data: URL) or replace it, with the baselines re-taken after Mobile 9/14?

open_questions.theme: Vector city: tracing, generation, cost, ownership
open_questions.text: Pre-existing: cityCanvasSha differs on the 1x desktop (likely canvas text hinting). Any generator-touching vector work inherits that per-class comparison.

open_questions.theme: Vector city: tracing, generation, cost, ownership
open_questions.text: Does the prototype's zero-area-building defect have causes beyond the own-stamp repair path? About 87 remain after clearing the stamp.

open_questions.theme: Vector city: tracing, generation, cost, ownership
open_questions.text: Per-frame cost of a Canvas-renderer city of N footprints (N = 300 / 1,000 / 3,000) during a flyIntoCity descent and a pinch on the iphone13/pixel7 profiles: nothing in web-performance.md or docs/mobile measures it, and SwiftShader fps is ungated (P11). Where does the Canvas-renderer cutoff sit for about 17k footprints against an offline-rasterised atlas-frame pyramid? That comparison was noted as needing tools/mobile-capture.js after Mobile 5-9; it was not measured here and is outside this phase's probes.

open_questions.theme: Vector city: tracing, generation, cost, ownership
open_questions.text: Should vectors appear only after moveend (raster stays the in-flight surface) or be redrawn per 'zoom' frame by a custom layer? Leaflet's Renderer CSS-scales during animation (VL9). This belongs to the living-chart track (H2z) and needs its decision.

open_questions.theme: Vector city: tracing, generation, cost, ownership
open_questions.text: Should the atlas adopt preferCanvas:true globally, as web-performance.md recommends, or a pCity-only L.canvas renderer? Global adoption touches every pane while the mobile atlas lane (Mobile 5-9) is mid-flight.

open_questions.theme: Vector city: tracing, generation, cost, ownership
open_questions.text: Does a vector city fit filigree slice C (painted city, pooled edges) and R4/R7? Vectors may need to be invisible hit geometry plus hover halos rather than a new visible style; that is filigree's call. Does a vector Epēshu traced from the canon chart count as 'drawn from the canon chart' (B-33) and accepted print under R5, or does the owner need to rule on tracing and warping canon art?

open_questions.theme: Vector city: tracing, generation, cost, ownership
open_questions.text: Who owns an atlas vector city and a shared city generator? Filigree slice C owns genCityCanvas, registerCityOverlay, washMake and sampleCityMask (by the README §7 reuse map) under mobile sha pins; living may not touch them (LC12); street may not write maps-site (ST1), leaving the link to 'Sim ↔ atlas continuity'. Is it a slice-C amendment (Filigree 2 re-run) or a new track or item, and does it get a pane despite the UG7 / Filigree 2 pane freeze?

open_questions.theme: Vector city: tracing, generation, cost, ownership
open_questions.text: Is the 'one geometry for atlas and sim' goal wanted at all, given that the fabric's scale cannot be shared (only the trace and the transform can)? Should a single Epēshu plan file (streets, quays, gates, the Blue Temple footprint) be the shared source both apps read, so the atlas vector city and the sim's 3D streets share vertices? If so, which track writes it?

open_questions.theme: Sim, living and cross-app identity
open_questions.text: Already open: LC7 — is a page change into the sim acceptable as the 'transitive layer', or must the zoom stay in the atlas? First exhibit (default: the Epēshīn Forum)? This ask partly answers it and should be put back to the owner with an in-atlas 2D vector city named as an option (OQ20).

open_questions.theme: Sim, living and cross-app identity
open_questions.text: Does H2z's crossfade source become the vector city instead of the raster overlay, and should the poster or a sim top-down view be shot from a pose derived from the atlas frame (R3), so the hand-off is geometrically aligned rather than a name-keyed cut?

open_questions.theme: Sim, living and cross-app identity
open_questions.text: Already open: LC17 — the sim's dragon in #s=epeshu: rule (a), (b) or (c). It matters here only as the precedent and queue for any #s=epeshu world-gen change.

open_questions.theme: Sim, living and cross-app identity
open_questions.text: Already open: LC4 — which creatures move. Not affected by this ask.

open_questions.theme: Sim, living and cross-app identity
open_questions.text: If the DM chart governs, may the sim's cityLabels and extraLandmarks be re-registered to it? This is fingerprint-safe by code reading but moves Street SV1/SV6 (and SV3/SV8), so it is cheapest before Street 1 freezes views. May the sim's Epēshu street plan be rebuilt on chart geometry? That is a world-gen change with an LC17-style re-baseline, after Street 4 (OQ21).

open_questions.theme: Sim, living and cross-app identity
open_questions.text: Unmeasured sim facts: the simDays(400) fingerprint invariance under a cityLabels move (own-sim S13) is code reading (probe S13); agreement between atlas gates (cityApproaches/mkGate) and the sim's s.entries (own-sim S22) has never been measured (probe S22).

open_questions.theme: Sim, living and cross-app identity
open_questions.text: One canonical district and landmark name list (article and spelling: 'Marble Quarter' vs 'the Marble Quarter', 'Amphitheatre' vs 'Amphitheater', 'The Fairy Arch' vs 'Fairy Arch'), so goto and chart links and a shared vector city can match by name. Should 'Sim ↔ atlas continuity' grow from name vocabulary to district-level targets (goto=<district>, cityLabels resolution) and a shared coordinate contract, given that LC7's default exhibit 'Epēshīn Forum' is ignored by the sim's goto today (OQ22)?

open_questions.theme: References and tools that could not be verified here
open_questions.text: How does swisstopo georeference its historical Dufour/Siegfried sheets (per-sheet control points, transform type, rubber-sheeting, the LV03 to LV95 shift)? The swisstopo georeferencing pages and Heitzler et al. (e-Perimetron 13(2)) are egress-blocked, so upstream registration is still an inference and VL3 rests on search summaries.

open_questions.text: Does the Siegfried figure (a 0.7 mm / 35 m average deviation over ten points, 1888 guidelines) actually appear in Heitzler et al., e-Perimetron 13(2)? So far it comes only from a search summary.

open_questions.theme: References and tools that could not be verified here
open_questions.text: Does ch.swisstopo.zeitreihen use the generic OpenLayersWMTSLayer component, and does the viewer crossfade between sheets (unread in the geoadmin code)? Is DEFAULT_FEATURE_IDENTIFICATION_TOLERANCE (10 px) passed to the identify backend, and is the light base map (ch.swisstopo.leichte-basiskarte_world.vt) mounted as a VECTOR layer?

open_questions.text: Were the era tile sets (tiles-war/, tiles-imperial/) themselves registered to the modern atlas, or only cut on the same grid? (G9 shows their ink matches modern within 1 atlas px at every anchor.)
